Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No. 5.
questions.explanation: Prospects will hinge 'foremost', that is above all, on the pandemic.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series. ABC_FG_JK_MOPQ_TUV_Y
questions.explanation: The series is the alphabet with every fifth letter (D, I, N, S, X) left out: ABC E FG H JK L MOPQ R TUV W Y. The blanks take E, H, L, R and W.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘FUTURE’ is written as ‘IXWXUH’ and ‘ISLAND’ is written as ‘LVODQG’. How will ‘JERSEY’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places forward: FUTURE → IXWXUH and ISLAND → LVODQG. So JERSEY → MHUVHB.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the given statements. Statements: All Grapes are Berries. Some Berries are Juices. All Juices are Sodas. Conclusions: (I) Some Berries are Grapes. (II) Some Sodas are Berries.
options: Both the conclusions (I) and (II) do not follow
questions.explanation: All grapes are berries, so some berries are grapes (I). Some berries are juices and all juices are sodas, so those berries are sodas: some sodas are berries (II). Both follow.

questions.text: Each of the letters in the word ‘DARKEN’ is arranged in the English alphabetical order. How many letters are there in the English alphabetical series between the letter which is second from the left end and the one which is third from the right end in the new letter-cluster thus formed?
questions.explanation: DARKEN in alphabetical order is A D E K N R. The second from the left is D and the third from the right is K; between them come E, F, G, H, I and J: six letters.

questions.text: ‘Conceal’ is related to ‘Disclose’ in the same way as ‘Identical’ is related to ‘________’. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word.)
questions.explanation: 'Conceal' and 'disclose' are opposites; the opposite of 'identical' is 'distinct'.

questions.text: Select the number that will come in the place of the question mark(?), if ‘+’ and ‘ – ‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged 11 ÷ 8 – 78 × 6 + 37 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 11 × 8 + 78 ÷ 6 − 37 = 88 + 13 − 37 = 64.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. 3 — 20 — 5; 4 — 17 — 3 NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: In each set, first × third + 5 = second: 3 × 5 + 5 = 20 and 4 × 3 + 5 = 17. Likewise 9 × 8 + 5 = 77.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (16, 7, 112) (8, 12, 96)
questions.explanation: In each set the third number is the product of the first two: 16 × 7 = 112 and 8 × 12 = 96. Likewise 15 × 8 = 120.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’; ‘A − B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’; ‘A × B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’ and ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the father of B’. Based on the above, how is I related to H if ‘B + R × I − T ÷ H’?
questions.explanation: B is the mother of R, R is the wife of I, I is the brother of T and T is the father of H. So I is the brother of H's father: H's father's brother.

questions.text: Four letter-clusters have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the letter-cluster that is different. Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter cluster
questions.explanation: In PRUZ, MORW and XZCH the letters move +2, +3, +5 (Z wraps round to C). ORTU moves +3, +2, +1, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: The second number in the given number pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number pairs except one. Find that odd number pair. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In 23 : 25, 35 : 36 and 13 : 16 the second number is the next perfect square above the first (5², 6², 4²). 44 is not a perfect square, so 34 : 44 is the odd pair.

questions.text: Two sets of numbers are given below. In each set of numbers, certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number result(s) in the second number. Similarly, certain mathematical operation(s) on the second number result(s) in the third number and so on. Which of the given options follows the same set of operations as in the given sets? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 48 – 50 – 46 – 52; 37 – 39 – 35 – 41
questions.explanation: In each set the steps are +2, −4, +6: 48 → 50 → 46 → 52 and 37 → 39 → 35 → 41. Likewise 26 → 28 → 24 → 30.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 176,167,156,147,136, ?
questions.explanation: The differences alternate −9 and −11 (176, 167, 156, 147, 136), so the next is 136 − 9 = 127.

questions.text: Which of the four options will replace the question mark (?) in the following series? FX32, EV38, DT44, CR50, ?
questions.explanation: First letters run F, E, D, C, so next is B; second letters move back two (X, V, T, R), so next is P; the number rises by 6 (32, 38, 44, 50), so next is 56: BP56.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘÷’ and ‘–‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘+’ are interchanged? 7 + 4 ÷18 – 3 × 2 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 7 × 4 − 18 ÷ 3 + 2 = 28 − 6 + 2 = 24.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? QGMW, VCPU, AYSS, ? , KQYO
questions.explanation: Letter by letter the clusters move by fixed steps: first letters +5 (Q, V, A, F, K), second −4 (G, C, Y, U, Q), third +3 (M, P, S, V, Y) and fourth −2 (W, U, S, Q, O). The missing term is FUVQ.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘D’ is coded as ‘16’, ‘B’ is coded as ‘4’ and ‘T’ is coded as ‘400’. How will ‘H’ be coded in the same language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is coded as the square of its place in the alphabet: D (4) = 16, B (2) = 4 and T (20) = 400. So H (8) = 64.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘bright colour rainbow’ is coded as ‘mq bj st’ and ‘sunny bright day’ is coded as ‘nv bj fm’. How is ‘bright’ coded in that language?
questions.explanation: 'bright' is the only word in both sentences and 'bj' the only code in both, so bright = bj.

questions.text: At the 36th National Games, Hashika Ramchandra won six gold medals in which of the following sports?
questions.explanation: Karnataka's Hashika Ramchandra won six gold medals in swimming at the 36th National Games, held in Gujarat in 2022, and was named the best female athlete.

questions.text: Which state in India was the most transformed by the Green Revolution?
questions.explanation: The Green Revolution's high-yielding wheat and rice, with irrigation and fertilisers, transformed farming most in Punjab, followed by Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh.

questions.text: Which of the following ports was developed as a Satellite port to relieve the pressure at the Mumbai port?
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru Port at Nhava Sheva was developed as a satellite port to relieve the congestion at Mumbai port.

questions.text: Who among the following was the shortest-serving Prime Minister of India?
questions.explanation: Gulzarilal Nanda was acting Prime Minister twice, for 13 days each time: after Nehru's death in 1964 and after Shastri's in 1966.

questions.text: In the context of Mathura school of Art, during which of the following periods were a number of sculptures of Brahmanical deities, such as Kartikeya, Vishnu and Kubera carved?
questions.explanation: Mathura's sculptors of the Kushana period carved many images of Brahmanical deities, among them Kartikeya, Vishnu and Kubera, besides Buddhist and Jain ones.

questions.text: In which of the following situations does the government run a deficit budget?
options: When the government expenditure and revenue both are zero.
When the government revenue exceeds expenditure.
When the government expenditure equals revenue.
When the government expenditure exceeds revenue.
questions.explanation: A budget is in deficit when the government's expenditure exceeds its revenue.

questions.text: Tsang Po and Jamuna are other names of which river?
questions.explanation: The Brahmaputra is known as the Tsangpo in Tibet and the Jamuna in Bangladesh.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following groups/parties was started in San Francisco, United States of America during the Indian National Movement?
questions.explanation: The Ghadar Party, formed in 1913 by Indians in North America, had its headquarters in San Francisco.

questions.text: Which of the following organisations is NOT a winner of the $100,000 cash prize as ‘Best Small Business: Good Food for All’, announced by the United Nations for providing inspiring, diverse and impactful solutions in improving access to healthy and sustainable food?
options: Oorja Development Solutions India Private Limited
questions.explanation: Edible Routes, Oorja Development Solutions and Taru Naturals were the three India-based enterprises among the 50 winners announced in 2021, ahead of the UN Food Systems Summit. Patanjali was not one of them.

questions.text: ‘Castling’ is related to which of the following sports?
questions.explanation: Castling is a chess move in which the king and a rook move in the same turn.

questions.text: What is the cost of the ‘Nand Baba Milk Mission’ scheme launched by the Uttar Pradesh state government in 2023 to provide milk producers the facility of selling their milk at a reasonable price in villages through dairy co-operative societies?
questions.explanation: Uttar Pradesh's Nand Baba Milk Mission, launched in 2023, has a budget of ₹1,000 crore over five years.

questions.text: In the context of vernier calliper, an internal jaw is used to measure:
options: the length correct up to 1 mm
the length of a rod and diameter of a sphere
the internal diameter of a hollow cylinder and pipes
questions.explanation: The internal (upper) jaws of a vernier calliper fit inside a hollow object to measure its internal diameter; the external jaws measure lengths and outer diameters, and the depth rod measures depth.

questions.text: If a bar magnet is hung from a string, in which direction does its north pole point?
questions.explanation: A freely suspended bar magnet lines up with the Earth's magnetic field, its north pole pointing (roughly) to geographic north.

questions.text: Fugdi dance is associated with which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Fugdi is a folk dance performed by women in Goa and the Konkan region.

questions.text: The concept of ‘Independence of judiciary’ in the Indian Constitution is taken from the Constitution of:
questions.explanation: Independence of the judiciary, judicial review and Fundamental Rights were borrowed from the US Constitution.

questions.text: Umayalpuram K Sivaraman is an eminent musician associated with which of the following musical instruments?
questions.explanation: Umayalpuram K. Sivaraman is a Carnatic mridangam maestro.

questions.text: Rottela Panduga or the Roti Festival is celebrated in which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Rottela Panduga is held every year at the Bara Shaheed Dargah in Nellore, Andhra Pradesh.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Belur Math was founded by which of the following social reformers in British India?
questions.explanation: Swami Vivekananda founded Belur Math, near Kolkata, as the headquarters of the Ramakrishna Math and Mission.

questions.text: Which of the following parts of the mountain will receive the most rainfall from moisture-laden winds?
questions.explanation: Moist winds forced up the windward slope cool and drop their rain there; the leeward side lies in the rain shadow.

questions.text: Which singer from Assam was posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2019?
questions.explanation: Bhupen Hazarika, Assam's celebrated singer and composer, was awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 2019.

questions.text: Medini Rai of Chanderi, Hasan Khan of Mewat and Mahmud Lodi joined Rana Sanga with their forces to fight against which of the following Mughal rulers?
questions.explanation: They joined Rana Sanga against Babur at the Battle of Khanwa in 1527.

questions.text: Which writ is issued by a high court or supreme court when a lower court has considered a case going beyond its jurisdiction?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives prohibition, which a higher court issues to a lower court or tribunal to stop it exceeding its jurisdiction while the case is still before it. Certiorari is also issued for excess of jurisdiction, but to transfer a case or quash an order already made.

questions.text: As per the UNDP, the rank of Sri Lanka in the Human Development Index (2022) is:
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 73. In UNDP's Human Development Report 2021/22, released in 2022, Sri Lanka ranked 73rd, though out of 191 countries, not 189; the 2020 report, which ranked 189, put it 72nd.

questions.text: The side BC of ∆ABC is produced to a point D. If AC = BC and ∠BAC = 70°, then find the value of 2.5∠ACD − 1.5∠ABC.
The marked price of an electronic watch in a store is ₹15,620 and it is available at a discount of 27%. What is the price (in ₹, to the nearest tens) that a customer pays if he buys from the store?
questions.explanation: ₹15,620 × 0.73 = ₹11,402.60, which is ₹11,400 to the nearest ten.

questions.text: The five-digit number 45yz0 is divisible by 40. What is the maximum possible value of (y + z)?
questions.explanation: Ending in 0, the number is divisible by 5; it is divisible by 8 when yz0 is, that is when the two-digit number yz is a multiple of 4. The largest digit sum of such a yz is 8 + 8 = 16 (88; 89, 98 and 99 are not multiples of 4).

questions.text: If a ∶ b = c ∶ d = e ∶ f = 5 ∶ 7, then what is the ratio (3a + 5c + 11e) ∶ (3b + 5d + 11f)?
questions.explanation: a = 5b/7, c = 5d/7 and e = 5f/7, so 3a + 5c + 11e = (5/7)(3b + 5d + 11f). The ratio stays 5 : 7.

questions.text: Varun and Raju, working together, can complete a job in 40 hours whereas Varun alone can complete the same job in 50 hours. The number of hours required by Raju to complete the job alone is:
questions.explanation: Raju does 1/40 − 1/50 = 1/200 of the job an hour, so alone he takes 200 hours.

questions.text: What principal would amount to ₹21,420 in 2 years at the rate of 9.5% p.a. simple interest?
questions.explanation: In 2 years at 9.5% the interest is 19% of the principal, so 1.19P = ₹21,420 and P = ₹18,000.

questions.text: A thief takes off on his bike at a certain speed, after seeing a police car at a distance of 250 m. The police car starts chasing the thief and catches him. If the thief runs 1.5 km before being caught and the speed of the police car is 70 km/h, then what is the speed of thief’s bike (in km/h)?
questions.explanation: Starting 250 m behind, the police car covers 1.75 km while the thief covers 1.5 km. Their speeds are in the ratio 1.75 : 1.5 = 7 : 6, so the thief rides at 70 × 6/7 = 60 km/h.

questions.text: The sum of two consecutive even numbers is 174. Find the smaller number.
The central angle of a sector is 80° and whose length is 96π. What is the radius of the circle?
Simplify the following expression. (60 + 64 ÷ 4 of 4) × {1000 ÷ ((10 of (3 + 2)) × 2 of 5)} − 28 + (100 × 3 of 3).
questions.explanation: 'Of' is worked before ÷ and ×: 64 ÷ (4 of 4) = 4, so the first bracket is 64; (10 of 5) × (2 of 5) = 500, so the braces give 1000 ÷ 500 = 2; and 100 × (3 of 3) = 900. Then 64 × 2 − 28 + 900 = 1000.

questions.text: Half litre of a solution contains 15% of alcohol. To change the alcohol concentration to 50%, find the quantity of alcohol to be mixed.
questions.explanation: Half a litre holds 75 ml of alcohol. Adding x ml: (75 + x)/(500 + x) = 1/2, so 150 + 2x = 500 + x and x = 350 ml.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'atrocious'.

questions.text: Identify the error in the given sentence. My colleague always works latest than me.
questions.explanation: A comparison with 'than' needs the comparative: 'works later than me', not the superlative 'latest'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Loud enough to be heard.
questions.explanation: 'Audible' means loud enough to be heard; 'audacious' means bold.

questions.text: Identify from the given options the word which is similar in meaning to the following word. Munificent
questions.explanation: 'Munificent' means very generous: 'magnanimous'. 'Miserly' is its opposite.

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. P) once said Q) a wise man R) that action speaks S) louder than words
questions.explanation: 'A wise man (Q) once said (P) that action speaks (R) louder than words (S).'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Just bite the ______ and tell him the truth.
questions.explanation: To 'bite the bullet' is to face something difficult or unpleasant with courage.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the opposite meaning of the underlined word. In front of the big screen, this behaviour is generally considered “taboo”.
questions.explanation: Something 'taboo' is forbidden or socially unacceptable; its opposite is 'acceptable'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. “Verity” is a good virtue for human life.
questions.explanation: 'Verity' means truth.

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. Founding father / is / of / New Historicism / Greenbalt / considered / the.
options: Greenbelt is the founding father of New Historicism considered.
Greenbalt is considered the founding father of New Historicism.
The founding father of New Historicism is considered Greenbalt.
The founding father is considered Greenbalt of New Historicism.
questions.explanation: Subject, verb, then complement: 'Greenbalt is considered the founding father of New Historicism.' (The critic is Stephen Greenblatt; the paper spells it 'Greenbalt'.)

questions.text: Select the most appropriate verb / verb phrase to fill in the blank. The team ________________ the championship before their star player got injured.
questions.explanation: Of two past actions, the earlier takes the past perfect: the team 'had won' before the player got injured.

questions.text: Select the correct ANTONYM of the underlined word to fill in the blank and complete the following sentence. He is always “active” in a party but _______ in the class.
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'active' is 'inert': inactive, sluggish.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can rectify the incorrectly spelt word in the following sentence. In our quest for power, we often fail to acknowlege the existence of other people.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'acknowledge'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Money collected from people for a cause.
questions.explanation: A fund is money collected or set aside for a particular purpose.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. Bincy’s mother “kept her cards close to her chest”.
options: Kept her plans and thoughts hidden
Informed that all the cards must be kept safe
Kept her purse and money by herself
questions.explanation: To 'keep one's cards close to one's chest' is to keep one's plans and thoughts secret.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the following sentence in active voice. The issue has been successfully resolved by the customer care team.
options: The customer care team has successfully resolved the issue.
The issue has successfully resolved the customer care team.
The customer care team successfully resolves the issue.
The customer care team successfully resolved the issue.
questions.explanation: The present perfect passive 'has been resolved' becomes the active 'has resolved', with the team as the subject.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I like bread made up of corn __________.
questions.explanation: Ground grain is 'flour'; 'flower' sounds the same but means something else.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A.He remembered her as she once was – an eager, glowing girl. B.He had not seen her for nearly thirteen years. C.Mr. Satterthwaite went to meet her. D.And now he saw – a Frozen Lady.
questions.explanation: C introduces the meeting, B says how long it had been, A recalls the girl she once was and D contrasts it with what he now sees: CBAD.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the following sentence in passive voice. Gill scored 3 centuries in Tata IPL 2023
options: 3 centuries had been scored by Gill in Tata IPL 2023.
3 centuries were scored by Gill in Tata IPL 2023.
3 centuries has been scored by Gill in Tata IPL 2023.
3 centuries were being scored by Gill in Tata IPL 2023.
questions.explanation: The simple past 'scored' becomes 'were scored' in the passive, plural to agree with '3 centuries'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Insert
questions.explanation: To 'insert' is to put something in; its opposite is 'remove'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Carcass
questions.explanation: A 'carcass' is a dead body: a 'corpse'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Social media companies (1)______ claim that they promote democracy and are dedicated to the empowerment of ordinary individuals. The assertion (2)______ entirely unfounded. Recent history shows how (3)______ citizens have been mobilised against totalitarian regimes on social networking sites. Starting from MeToo to Black Lives Matter, digital networks (4)______ indispensable in bringing together critical voices against social and political (5)______ .

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.explanation: The companies 'frequently' make this claim; 'never' and 'seldom' would contradict the assertion the passage goes on to weigh.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Social media companies (1)______ claim that they promote democracy and are dedicated to the empowerment of ordinary individuals. The assertion (2)______ entirely unfounded. Recent history shows how (3)______ citizens have been mobilised against totalitarian regimes on social networking sites. Starting from MeToo to Black Lives Matter, digital networks (4)______ indispensable in bringing together critical voices against social and political (5)______ .

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
questions.explanation: 'The assertion may not be entirely unfounded': the passage goes on to give evidence for it. The other options leave out the verb 'be'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Social media companies (1)______ claim that they promote democracy and are dedicated to the empowerment of ordinary individuals. The assertion (2)______ entirely unfounded. Recent history shows how (3)______ citizens have been mobilised against totalitarian regimes on social networking sites. Starting from MeToo to Black Lives Matter, digital networks (4)______ indispensable in bringing together critical voices against social and political (5)______ .

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
questions.explanation: 'Common citizens', ordinary people, have been mobilised against totalitarian regimes.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Social media companies (1)______ claim that they promote democracy and are dedicated to the empowerment of ordinary individuals. The assertion (2)______ entirely unfounded. Recent history shows how (3)______ citizens have been mobilised against totalitarian regimes on social networking sites. Starting from MeToo to Black Lives Matter, digital networks (4)______ indispensable in bringing together critical voices against social and political (5)______ .

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
questions.explanation: 'Digital networks have been indispensable': the present perfect for a run of events up to now.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Social media companies (1)______ claim that they promote democracy and are dedicated to the empowerment of ordinary individuals. The assertion (2)______ entirely unfounded. Recent history shows how (3)______ citizens have been mobilised against totalitarian regimes on social networking sites. Starting from MeToo to Black Lives Matter, digital networks (4)______ indispensable in bringing together critical voices against social and political (5)______ .

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
questions.explanation: Critical voices are brought together against social and political 'injustice'.

questions.text: Four letter-clusters have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the letter-cluster that is different. Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter cluster.
questions.explanation: In YWA, JHL and OMQ the letters move −2, then +4 (W + 4 wraps round to A). LJO moves −2, then +5, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: 624 is related to 160 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 448 is related to 116. To which of the following is 528 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each number is divided by 4 and 4 is added: 624 ÷ 4 + 4 = 160 and 448 ÷ 4 + 4 = 116. Likewise 528 ÷ 4 + 4 = 136.

questions.text: What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘+’ and ‘×‘ are interchanged and ‘−’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 95 − 19 × 4 + 6 ÷ 16 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 95 ÷ 19 + 4 × 6 − 16 = 5 + 24 − 16 = 13.

questions.text: 80 is related to 99 following certain logic. Following the same logic, 0 is related to 3. To which of the following numbers is 35 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each number is one less than a square and is related to one less than the next square: 80 = 9² − 1 → 10² − 1 = 99 and 0 = 1² − 1 → 2² − 1 = 3. So 35 = 6² − 1 → 7² − 1 = 48.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 2736 × 8 – 55 + 105 ÷ 2 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 2736 ÷ 8 + 55 − 105 × 2 = 342 + 55 − 210 = 187.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? FHVQ, IJSO, LLPM, ONMK, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move +3 (F, I, L, O, so R); second letters +2 (H, J, L, N, so P); third letters −3 (V, S, P, M, so J); fourth letters −2 (Q, O, M, K, so I): RPJI.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. WEL: DVO :: FOR: ULI :: SDX:?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite in the alphabet (A ↔ Z, B ↔ Y and so on): WEL → DVO and FOR → ULI. So SDX → HWC.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘open the door’ is coded as 'wu ko tn' and ‘door is solid’ is coded as ‘ko gk mb’. How is ‘door’ coded in the given language?
questions.explanation: 'door' is the only word in both sentences and 'ko' the only code in both, so door = ko.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that, when sequentially placed from left to right in the blanks below, will complete the letter series. _ V D W Y _ D W Y V _ W Y _ D _
questions.explanation: With Y, V, D, V, W in the blanks the block YVDW repeats: YVDW YVDW YVDW YVDW.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’; ‘A − B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’; ‘A × B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’ and ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the father of B’. Based on the above, how is 4 related to 1 if ‘4 × 3 − 2 − 1’?
questions.explanation: 4 × 3: 4 is 3's wife. 3 − 2 and 2 − 1: 3 is 2's brother and 2 is 1's brother, so 3 is 1's brother. 4 is 1's brother's wife.

questions.text: The position of how many letters will remain unchanged if all the letters in the word MOLTEN are arranged in English alphabetical order?
questions.explanation: MOLTEN in alphabetical order is E L M N O T. Compared with M O L T E N, no letter keeps its place.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘VTPM’ is coded as ‘37’ and ‘CGNK’ is coded as ‘73’. How will ‘MVLC’ be coded in the same language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite (A ↔ Z) and the positions are added: VTPM → E, G, K, N = 5 + 7 + 11 + 14 = 37 and CGNK → X, T, M, P = 24 + 20 + 13 + 16 = 73. MVLC → N, E, O, X = 14 + 5 + 15 + 24 = 58.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 672, 677, 686, 699, 716, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 5, 9, 13, 17, rising by 4 each time, so the next is 21: 716 + 21 = 737.

questions.text: Three of the following number-pairs are alike in some manner and hence form a group. Which number-pair does not belong to that group? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In 8 – 100, 6 – 64 and 9 – 121 the second number is the square of the first plus 2 (10², 8², 11²). For 12 that would be 14² = 196, not 225, so 12 – 225 is the odd one.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter cluster in the same way as the second letter cluster is related to the first letter cluster and the fourth letter cluster is related to the third letter cluster. IMPROVE : RPMIEVO :: HISTORY : TSIHYRO :: JOURNEY : ?
questions.explanation: The word is split after its fourth letter and each part is reversed: IMPR OVE → RPMI EVO and HIST ORY → TSIH YRO. So JOUR NEY → RUOJ YEN: RUOJYEN.

questions.text: Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some cups are glasses. No glass is a stone. All stones are metals. Conclusions: I. All cups can never be stones. II. No cup is a metal. III. All metals can never be glasses.
options: Only II and III conclusion follow
Only I and III conclusion follow
All I, II and III conclusion follow
questions.explanation: The cups that are glasses cannot be stones, so all cups can never be stones (I). The stones are metals that are not glasses, so all metals can never be glasses (III). A cup that is not a glass may still be a metal, so II does not follow.

questions.text: In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (96, 29) (112, 33)
questions.explanation: In each pair the second number is a quarter of the first plus 5: 96 ÷ 4 + 5 = 29 and 112 ÷ 4 + 5 = 33. Likewise 188 ÷ 4 + 5 = 52.

questions.text: In this question, three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All phones are TVs. Some TVs are big. Some big are cars. Conclusions: I.Some TVs are phones. II.Some big are TVs. III.All big are cars.
options: Only conclusions II and III follow.
Only conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: All phones are TVs, so some TVs are phones (I); some TVs are big, so some big are TVs (II). Some big are cars does not make all big cars, so III does not follow.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which of the following places did Mahatma Gandhi, along with other Indians, establish the Natal Congress to fight against racial discrimination?
questions.explanation: In 1894 Gandhi founded the Natal Indian Congress in Durban, South Africa, to fight discrimination against Indians there.

questions.text: Yakshagan is a folk dance of which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Yakshagana is the dance-drama of coastal Karnataka.

questions.text: What is the unit of specific resistance?
questions.explanation: Specific resistance (resistivity) is ρ = RA/l, so its unit is ohm × m²/m: the ohm metre (Ω m).

questions.text: UPSC is a Constitutional Body to conduct examinations for appointments to the services of the Union and the services of the State, respectively, under Article ________.
questions.explanation: Article 320 sets out the functions of the Public Service Commissions, the first being to conduct examinations for appointments to the services of the Union and of the States.

questions.text: The Tripartite struggle happened among the Palas, the Pratiharas and the _______.
questions.explanation: The Palas of Bengal, the Gurjara-Pratiharas and the Rashtrakutas of the Deccan fought a long three-way struggle for control of Kannauj.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Guru Ghasidas led which of the following movements to improve the social condition of leather workers in British India?
questions.explanation: Guru Ghasidas founded the Satnami movement in central India (present-day Chhattisgarh), working among the leather workers to improve their social status.

questions.text: Subansiri, Jia Bharali, Dhansiri and Puthimari are the major tributaries of which river?
questions.explanation: The Subansiri, Jia Bharali, Dhansiri and Puthimari are tributaries of the Brahmaputra in Assam.

questions.text: The first Indian Olympic Games was hosted by which of the following cities?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Lahore, where lists of the National Games place the first Indian Olympic Games, their forerunner, in 1924. Some accounts put the games of February 1924, which picked India's team for the Paris Olympics, in Delhi instead.

questions.text: Which law states that endothermic animals from cold climates have smaller extremities or appendages than closely related species from warm climates?
questions.explanation: Allen's rule: warm-blooded animals of colder climates have shorter limbs, ears and tails than their relatives in warm climates, so they lose less heat.

questions.text: What gave a major impetus to the cotton textile industry in India after Independence?
options: Export of raw cotton to England
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the Swadeshi movement, whose call to boycott British goods in favour of Indian ones gave the cotton mills a major boost. That was in the early 1900s, though, before Independence; after it, Partition hurt the industry, as much of the cotton-growing land went to Pakistan.

questions.text: Pushyabhuti dynasty, after Prabhakarvardhana, strengthened its position in the regions of Punjab and Haryana after defeating which of the following dynasties?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the Hunas. Banabhatta's Harshacharita hails Prabhakarvardhana, Harsha's father, as 'a lion to the Huna deer': his wars against the Hunas in the north-west strengthened the Pushyabhutis of Thanesar in Punjab and Haryana.

questions.text: Which type of well-managed industry was established in India at the time of independence?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives steel and cotton: the cotton textile mills and the Tata Iron and Steel Company (1907) were India's longest-established large industries at Independence. Sugar and cement mills also existed by then, so the question is loosely worded; electronics had barely begun.

questions.text: Each of the following statements includes two terms. In three cases, the two terms mean the same as each other. In which of the following cases do the two terms NOT mean the same as each other?
options: The base period and the reference period
Changes in real GDP and the GDP deflator
Nominal GDP and GDP at current prices
Real GDP and GDP at constant prices
questions.explanation: Nominal GDP is GDP at current prices, real GDP is GDP at constant prices, and the base period is also called the reference period. The GDP deflator is a price index (nominal GDP ÷ real GDP), not a change in real GDP.

questions.text: Vishu festival is celebrated in which of the following states?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Kerala and Tamil Nadu. Vishu, the Malayalam new year in mid-April, is Kerala's festival and is also kept in neighbouring parts of Tamil Nadu such as Kanyakumari; the Tulu-speaking coast of Karnataka marks the same day as Bisu, so Kerala and Karnataka is arguable too.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding water remaining colder in an earthen pot (matka)?
options: The water oozes out through the pores in an earthen pot.
Environmental water vapour enters the pot through pores.
Water gets evaporated at the surface of the earthen pot.
questions.explanation: Water seeps out through the pot's pores and evaporates from its surface, taking heat from the water inside. Water vapour from the air does not enter the pot.

questions.text: In February 2023, BVR Subrahmanyam was appointed as the ________.
questions.explanation: BVR Subrahmanyam was appointed CEO of NITI Aayog in February 2023.

questions.text: Which of the following is a key focus area of the ‘Amrit Dharohar’ scheme launched by the Prime Minister Narendra Modi on World Environment Day, 2023?
options: Preservation of ancient Indian heritage sites
To promote values of local communities in conserving wetland ecosystem
questions.explanation: Amrit Dharohar, announced in the 2023-24 Budget and launched in June 2023, covers India's Ramsar wetlands: it promotes their unique conservation values, with local communities, through wise use and ecotourism.

questions.text: Which of the following states suffers from ‘Loo’?
questions.explanation: The Loo is the hot, dry wind that blows over north-western India, including Rajasthan, in May and June.

questions.text: The National Youth Policy 2014 defines youth as population between the ages of ________ and _________.
questions.explanation: The National Youth Policy 2014 defines youth as people aged 15 to 29.

questions.text: Which television channel presents the IMMIES Awards every year with an aim to reward the best talent in the Indian music industry?
questions.explanation: The IMMIES (Indian Music Awards) are presented by MTV India.

questions.text: At which Olympic games did Abhinav Bindra win the gold medal?
questions.explanation: Abhinav Bindra won the 10 m air rifle gold at Beijing 2008, India's first individual Olympic gold.

questions.text: Which of the following options best describes the primary cause of the per capita income decline?
options: Decline in the gross domestic product
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives population growth: per capita income is national income divided by population, so it falls when the population grows faster than income. (A fall in GDP would lower it too.)

questions.text: Which of the following organisations is associated with the development of the web version: e-GOPALA application?
options: National Institute of Agricultural Extension Management
questions.explanation: e-GOPALA, an app and portal for dairy farmers covering breeding, animal health and nutrition, was developed by the National Dairy Development Board.

questions.text: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions about the ‘Promotion of educational and economic interests of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and other weaker sections’?
questions.explanation: Article 46, a Directive Principle, asks the State to promote the educational and economic interests of the weaker sections, especially the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

questions.text: Pandit Ram Narayan was associated with which of the following musical instruments?
questions.explanation: Pandit Ram Narayan made the sarangi a solo concert instrument.

questions.text: Ram’s income is 2.5% more than Shyam’s income. By what percentage is Shyam’s income less than Ram’s income?
questions.explanation: Shyam's income is less by 2.5/(100 + 2.5) × 100 = 2.43…% of Ram's.

questions.text: Find the volume of a cone having base radius 3.5 cm and height 18 cm.

A shopkeeper has a fault of 100 g in a 3 kg weight. He sold 3 kg of potatoes to Charu using the same faulty weight for ₹46. The cost price of the potatoes for the seller was ₹12 per kg. How much profit (in ₹) did he earn on the potatoes?
questions.explanation: A 3 kg weight 100 g short weighs out only 2.9 kg, which cost him 2.9 × ₹12 = ₹34.80. He sold it for ₹46: a profit of ₹11.20.

questions.text: A tank is filled in 45 minutes by two pipes, A and B. Pipe B fills the tank twice as fast as A. How much time (in minutes) will pipe A alone take to fill the tank?
questions.explanation: If A fills x of the tank a minute, B fills 2x, so 3x = 1/45 and x = 1/135: A alone takes 135 minutes.

questions.text: How much rice of ₹4 per kg should be mixed to 15 kg of rice of ₹10 per kg, so as to make a mixture worth ₹6.50 per kg?
questions.explanation: By alligation the ₹4 and ₹10 rice are mixed in the ratio (10 − 6.5) : (6.5 − 4) = 3.5 : 2.5 = 7 : 5. With 15 kg of the ₹10 rice, 15 × 7/5 = 21 kg of the ₹4 rice is needed.

questions.text: Find the value of the unknowns: x + 1.5y + 2z = 5.5; x + 5y + 7z = 15; 3x + 11y + 13z = 25
questions.explanation: Subtracting the first equation from the second gives 3.5y + 5z = 9.5; subtracting three times the first from the third gives 6.5y + 7z = 8.5. These give z = 4 and y = −3, and then x = 5.5 + 4.5 − 8 = 2.

questions.text: In a triangle PQR, ∠P + ∠Q = 84°. Find the value of ∠R.
questions.explanation: The angles of a triangle add up to 180°, so ∠R = 180° − 84° = 96°.

questions.text: The monthly incomes of A, B and C are in the ratio 2 : 9 : 3 and their expenses are in the ratio 3 : 9 : 5. If A’s saving is half of his total income, then savings of A, B and C are, respectively, in the ratio of:
questions.explanation: Take incomes 2k, 9k, 3k and expenses 3m, 9m, 5m. A saves half his income: 2k − 3m = k, so k = 3m. Savings are 6m − 3m, 27m − 9m and 9m − 5m: 3 : 18 : 4.

questions.text: If the altitude from two vertices of a triangle to the opposite sides are equal, then the triangle will be:
questions.explanation: Area = ½ × side × altitude to it, so equal altitudes from two vertices mean the sides they fall on are equal: the triangle is isosceles.

questions.text: An article costs ₹1,000 for a salesman. He fixes its marked price as ₹1,500. He sells it to a customer at a discount of 20%. He gives a further discount of 10% for each cash payment. Find the percentage of loss or gain that the salesman makes on sale.
questions.explanation: ₹1,500 less 20% is ₹1,200, and a further 10% off leaves ₹1,080. On a cost of ₹1,000 that is a gain of 8%.

questions.text: In a circular race of 1600 m in length, Bhaskar and Vinay start with speeds of 27 km/h and 45 km/h starting at the same time from the same point. When will they meet for the first time on the track when running in the opposite directions and the same direction, respectively?
questions.explanation: 27 km/h = 7.5 m/s and 45 km/h = 12.5 m/s. In opposite directions they close the 1600 m at 20 m/s: 80 seconds, or 1 minute 20 seconds. In the same direction the faster gains 5 m/s: 320 seconds, or 5 minutes 20 seconds.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Customary
questions.explanation: 'Customary' means usual or habitual; its opposite is 'unusual'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined part of the following sentence. The playwright has faced “many ups and downs” in his literary career, which spanned for almost 30 years.
questions.explanation: 'Ups and downs' are a mixture of good and bad times.

questions.text: Select the word segment that can substitute the bracketed word segment correctly and complete the sentence meaningfully. We will have to (put the meeting away) as the Director is not well.
questions.explanation: To 'put off' a meeting is to postpone it; to 'put away' is to store something.

questions.text: Complete the sentence with the most appropriate set of ANTONYMS of the highlighted word. . ‘Grisly’. The other day Jimmy behaved _______ with Jammy and that was quite _______ for me.
questions.explanation: 'Grisly' means horrifying or gruesome; its opposites 'pleasantly' and 'comforting' fit the blanks.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. How have they been ordered by the minister?
options: How has the minister ordered them?
How did the minister order them?
How have the minister ordered them?
How had the minister ordered them?
questions.explanation: The present perfect passive 'have been ordered by the minister' becomes the present perfect active, with 'has' to agree with 'the minister': 'How has the minister ordered them?'

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. (A) to become severely seasick (B) a world tour, but he was (C) a nervous flyer and tended (D) he wanted to go on
questions.explanation: 'He wanted to go on (D) a world tour, but he was (B) a nervous flyer and tended (C) to become severely seasick (A).'

questions.text: Select the correct meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence. Lucy’s conceited conduct with her colleagues has left her “high and dry”
questions.explanation: To be left 'high and dry' is to be left helpless, without help or support.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. He was / bad injured / in the / last match.
questions.explanation: The participle 'injured' needs an adverb: 'He was badly injured in the last match.'

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the sentences in the correct logical sequence to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. a. This figure is predicted to climb as the percentage of Americans residing in rural areas falls by an average of 1.6% annually. b. The United Nations reports that India’s urban population is growing at a rate of 1.1 percent annually, while the country's rural population is shrinking at a rate of 0.37 percent annually. c. While 82% of Americans live in urban settings, only 30% of Indians do so. d. It's still a considerably smaller percentage of the Indian population than it is in the US that resides in urban areas.
questions.explanation: b gives the UN's figures for India, d says India's urban share is still far below the US's, c gives the numbers (82% against 30%) and a says the American figure will climb: b, d, c, a.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Study of flying airplanes
questions.explanation: Aviation is the flying of aircraft; astronomy is the study of the heavens, alchemy was medieval chemistry and acoustics is the science of sound.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate homophone to fill in the blank. The _____ of the flowers spread everywhere when they bloom.
questions.explanation: A 'scent' is a pleasant smell; 'cent' and 'sent' sound the same but mean something else.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'convenient'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in brackets to fill in the blank. She __________ requested him to pay the bills. (persistently)
questions.explanation: 'Persistently' means continuing without letting up: 'continuously'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Astute
questions.explanation: 'Astute' means shrewd and clever; its opposite is 'stupid'.

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. (a) one of the primary obstacles encountered (b) is the risk of sample contamination (c) during the analysis of controlled dangerous substance (CDS) (d) from improper handling and collecting methodologies (e) proof bloodstain patterns and DNA evidence
questions.explanation: 'One of the primary obstacles encountered (a) during the analysis of controlled dangerous substance (CDS) (c) proof bloodstain patterns and DNA evidence (e) is the risk of sample contamination (b) from improper handling and collecting methodologies (d).'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Coy
questions.explanation: 'Coy' means shy and reluctant to be noticed; its opposite is 'extroverted'.

questions.text: Select the correct spelling of the word that means ‘to replace’.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'supersede'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. A famous company conducted the workshop for its customers.
options: The workshop were conducted by a famous company for its customers.
The workshop was conducted by a famous company for its customers.
The workshop is conducted by a famous company for its customers.
The workshop had been conducted by a famous company for its customers.
questions.explanation: The simple past 'conducted' becomes 'was conducted', singular to agree with 'the workshop'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select ‘No substitution’. The chief guest concluded his speech as “he requested” to stop by the organisers.
questions.explanation: The organisers made the request, so the passive is needed, in the past tense like 'concluded': 'as he was requested to stop by the organisers'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. My sister and I / work very hard / nevertheless my brother does not do / any task assigned to him.
options: nevertheless my brother does not do
questions.explanation: 'Nevertheless' is an adverb and cannot join two clauses; the contrast needs 'but' or 'whereas': 'My sister and I work very hard, but my brother does not do any task assigned to him.'

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Global warming is a major problem. The result will be the problems created by the rising temperatures of the Arctic region. As a result of global warming, (1)_________ in rainfall and plant distribution affect the migration patterns, feeding behaviour, and breeding preferences of numerous bird species. The increase in the temperature may also alter ocean currents, which may alter the (2)__________ ecology as a whole. Greenhouse gas emissions are responsible for the ongoing melting of the Arctic. This will result in a (3)__________loop since greenhouse gases trap the heat in the atmosphere and the additional emissions may (4)__________ the global warming process. Now, the only way to reverse the harm is for every person to be environmentally sensitive. This may offer us hope that we will be able to leave a green planet to our future generations, who presently appear to face (5)__________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Changes, 'alterations', in rainfall and plant distribution affect the birds' migration and breeding.

questions.explanation: Ocean currents shape 'marine' ecology.

questions.explanation: Melting releases more gases, which trap more heat and cause more melting: a self-reinforcing 'vicious' loop.
