The rise in global temperature (1)__________ already occurred is leading to extreme weather events that bring (2)__________ heat waves and droughts, devastating floods and increasingly powerful hurricanes and tropical storms. The combination of these factors means the impact on human health is increasing and is (3)__________ accelerate. But there is room for hope, particularly if governments take action now to (4)__________ the pledges made at Glasgow in November 2021 and to go further in resolving the climate crisis. WHO is (5)__________ governments to lead a just, equitable, and fast phase out of fossil fuels and transition to a clean energy future.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Extreme weather brings 'intense' heat waves, in line with 'devastating floods' and 'increasingly powerful hurricanes'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The rise in global temperature (1)__________ already occurred is leading to extreme weather events that bring (2)__________ heat waves and droughts, devastating floods and increasingly powerful hurricanes and tropical storms. The combination of these factors means the impact on human health is increasing and is (3)__________ accelerate. But there is room for hope, particularly if governments take action now to (4)__________ the pledges made at Glasgow in November 2021 and to go further in resolving the climate crisis. WHO is (5)__________ governments to lead a just, equitable, and fast phase out of fossil fuels and transition to a clean energy future.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: The impact 'is likely to accelerate': 'likely' takes 'to', while 'barely', 'rarely' and 'hardly' do not fit before 'to'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The rise in global temperature (1)__________ already occurred is leading to extreme weather events that bring (2)__________ heat waves and droughts, devastating floods and increasingly powerful hurricanes and tropical storms. The combination of these factors means the impact on human health is increasing and is (3)__________ accelerate. But there is room for hope, particularly if governments take action now to (4)__________ the pledges made at Glasgow in November 2021 and to go further in resolving the climate crisis. WHO is (5)__________ governments to lead a just, equitable, and fast phase out of fossil fuels and transition to a clean energy future.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: To 'honour' a pledge is to do what one promised. 'Keep the pledges' would also be good English, but SSC's key gives 'honour', the more formal collocation.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The rise in global temperature (1)__________ already occurred is leading to extreme weather events that bring (2)__________ heat waves and droughts, devastating floods and increasingly powerful hurricanes and tropical storms. The combination of these factors means the impact on human health is increasing and is (3)__________ accelerate. But there is room for hope, particularly if governments take action now to (4)__________ the pledges made at Glasgow in November 2021 and to go further in resolving the climate crisis. WHO is (5)__________ governments to lead a just, equitable, and fast phase out of fossil fuels and transition to a clean energy future.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: To 'call on' someone to do something is to urge them formally to do it. ('Calling for governments to lead' can also be said, but SSC's key gives 'calling on'.)

questions.text: ‘RX-21’ is related to ‘UU-11’ in a certain way. In the same way, ‘PM-39’ is related to ‘SJ-29’. To which of the following is DP-17 related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: The first letter moves 3 forward, the second 3 back and the number falls by 10: RX-21 → UU-11 and PM-39 → SJ-29. So DP-17 → GM-7.

questions.text: Select the triad in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the given triads. (8, 9, 7), (24, 13, 35) (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: In each triad, twice the first number minus the second gives the third: 2 × 8 − 9 = 7 and 2 × 24 − 13 = 35. Likewise 2 × 17 − 11 = 23.

questions.text: Select the number from the given options to complete the series. 32, 36, 44, 56, 72, ___
questions.explanation: The differences are 4, 8, 12, 16, rising by 4 each time, so the next is 20: 72 + 20 = 92.

questions.text: Three of the following four options are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which is the one that does NOT belong to that group? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In the others, twice the first number plus the third gives the middle one: 2 × 58 + 23 = 139, 2 × 23 + 38 = 84 and 2 × 89 + 34 = 212. But 2 × 12 + 99 = 123, not 122.

questions.text: 61 is related to 18 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 213 is related to 38. To which of the following is 509 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each first number is a cube minus 3, and the second is the square of the same number plus 2: 61 = 4³ − 3 gives 4² + 2 = 18, and 213 = 6³ − 3 gives 6² + 2 = 38. 509 = 8³ − 3, so 8² + 2 = 66.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘LIGHT’ is coded as ‘25709’ and ‘SIGHT’ is coded as ‘97065’. What is the code for ‘S’ in that language?
questions.explanation: I, G, H and T are in both words, as are 0, 5, 7 and 9 in both codes. The letter left in SIGHT is S and the digit left in its code is 6, so S = 6.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. LOI: QTN :: VES:AJX :: AND: ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 5 places forward, wrapping round after Z: LOI → QTN and VES → AJX. So AND → FSI.

questions.text: The position of how many letters will remain unchanged if each of the letters in the word ‘DELIGHT’ is arranged in the English alphabetical order?
questions.explanation: DELIGHT in alphabetical order is D E G H I L T. D, E and T stay in the same places: three letters.

questions.text: If A is the sister of B, C is the daughter of A, D is the sister of A and E is the brother of C. How is D related to E?
questions.explanation: E is C's brother, so C's mother A is E's mother too. D is A's sister, so D is E's mother's sister.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'PUPIL' is written as '162116912' and 'PURGE’ is written as '16211875'. How will 'PURSE' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is written as its place in the alphabet: P = 16, U = 21, R = 18, S = 19, E = 5. So PURSE is 162118195.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘−’ are interchanged? 20 + 4 ÷ 2 × 3 − 6 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 20 ÷ 4 + 2 − 3 × 6 = 5 + 2 − 18 = −11.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series. _TUVTR_WU_UXVN_Y
questions.explanation: With S, U, P, U in the blanks the series reads STUV TRUW UPUX VNUY: the first letters run S, T, U, V, the second T, R, P, N (back 2), the third is always U and the fourth runs V, W, X, Y.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of numbers. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 33 : 340 48 : 490
questions.explanation: The second number is ten times the first plus 10: 33 × 10 + 10 = 340 and 48 × 10 + 10 = 490. Likewise 63 × 10 + 10 = 640.

questions.text: Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All spoons are forks. All forks are knives. No knife is a spatula. Conclusions: I. Some knives are spoons. II. No fork is a spatula. III. Some spoons are spatulas.
options: Only conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: All spoons are forks and all forks are knives, so all spoons are knives and some knives are spoons (I). No knife is a spatula, so no fork is a spatula (II), and no spoon is one either, so III does not follow.

questions.text: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series to make it logically complete? TGO, VIN, XKM, ZML, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move 2 forward (T, V, X, Z, B), second letters 2 forward (G, I, K, M, O) and third letters 1 back (O, N, M, L, K): BOK.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 125 ÷ 5 + 1809 × 9 – 14 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 125 × 5 − 1809 ÷ 9 + 14 = 625 − 201 + 14 = 438.

questions.text: Four letter-clusters have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the one that is different. The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter cluster
questions.explanation: In UTW, NMP and CBE the letters move 1 back, then 3 forward. LKM moves 1 back, then 2 forward, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some Mirrors are Decoratives. No Decorative is a Plant. All Plants are Trees. Conclusions: (I) Some Mirrors are Plants. (II) Some Decoratives are Trees.
questions.explanation: The mirrors are linked to plants only through decoratives, and no decorative is a plant, so I need not follow. Nothing says whether any decorative is a tree, so II need not follow either.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who founded the Arya Samaj in Mumbai in 1875?
questions.explanation: Swami Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in Bombay in 1875, calling for a return to the Vedas.

questions.text: Who is considered the highest law officer of the state in India?
questions.explanation: Article 165 provides for an Advocate General in each state, appointed by the Governor, as the state's highest law officer. The Attorney General (Article 76) is the highest law officer of the Union.

questions.text: In which state of India is the Tadoba National Park located?
questions.explanation: Tadoba National Park, part of the Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve, is in Chandrapur district, Maharashtra.

questions.text: What is the primary benefit offered to businesses in Special Economic Zones (SEZs)?
questions.explanation: SEZs offer their units tax and duty concessions, such as duty-free imports and income-tax breaks, to promote exports.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: Rivers and sea water are considered as fresh water.
Pond water and sea water are considered as fresh water.
Rivers, creeks, lakes, ponds, and streams are all freshwater habitats.
questions.explanation: Rivers, creeks, lakes, ponds and streams hold fresh water; sea water is salt water, a marine habitat.

questions.text: Which of the following countries will host the ICC men’s Cricket World Cup in the year 2031?
questions.explanation: In November 2021 the ICC named India and Bangladesh joint hosts of the 2031 Men's Cricket World Cup.

questions.text: Which of the following terms is related to football?
questions.explanation: A bicycle (overhead) kick is a football move; LBW, overs and third man belong to cricket.

questions.text: AR Rehman, Gulzar and _____ won the 52nd annual Grammy Award for the best motion picture song ‘Jai ho’.
questions.explanation: Tanvi Shah, who wrote and sang the Spanish lines of 'Jai Ho', shared the Grammy with A R Rahman and Gulzar.

questions.text: The Working Group under the chairmanship of __________ in the year_________ proposed a new intermediate monetary aggregate to be referred to as NM2.
questions.explanation: The RBI's Working Group on Money Supply chaired by Dr Y V Reddy reported in 1998; it proposed new monetary aggregates, with NM2 as the intermediate one.

questions.text: Classical Sarod player, Amjad Ali Khan was awarded ____________ in 2001 by the Government of India.
questions.explanation: Sarod maestro Amjad Ali Khan received the Padma Vibhushan, India's second-highest civilian award, in 2001.

questions.text: By which National Waterways (NW) of India, are the delta channels of Mahanadi and Brahmani rivers and East Coast Canal connected?
questions.explanation: National Waterway 5 joins the East Coast Canal with the Brahmani-Kharsua river system and the delta channels of the Mahanadi, in Odisha and West Bengal.

questions.text: According to the Census of India 2011, which group of Union Territories has the highest density of population?
options: Delhi, Chandigarh and Daman and Diu
Lakshadweep, Daman and Diu and Puducherry
Lakshadweep, Daman and Diu and Chandigarh
questions.explanation: In the 2011 census Delhi, Chandigarh and Puducherry were the three most densely populated Union Territories.

questions.text: Identify an example of plasma as a state of matter.
questions.explanation: In a neon sign an electric current ionises the gas into a glowing plasma. Freon is a gas, blood a liquid and dry ice a solid.

questions.text: Which fundamental duty applies to you when you see your college friends start fighting with the canteen person when he passed a few anti-religious statements?
options: To value and preserve the rich heritage
To promote harmony and spirit of brotherhood
To protect and improve our natural environment
To develop the scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry
questions.explanation: Article 51A(e) asks every citizen to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood, transcending religious, linguistic and regional diversities.

questions.text: Which Article deals with the election of the President?
questions.explanation: Article 54 provides for the election of the President by an electoral college; Article 66 covers the Vice-President's election.

questions.text: Who among the following Indian cricketers were named the Wisden’s cricketer of the year in the 2022 edition of the Almanack?
options: Surya Kumar Yadav and Axar Patel
questions.explanation: Rohit Sharma and Jasprit Bumrah were among Wisden's five Cricketers of the Year in the 2022 Almanack.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a physical change?
options: Heating of iron rod to red hot
questions.explanation: Curdling of milk is a chemical change: acid coagulates the milk's proteins, and the change cannot be reversed. The other three change only the temperature or state of the substance.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who is called the father of Local Self-Government in India?
questions.explanation: Lord Ripon's resolution of 1882 laid the foundation of local self-government in India.

questions.text: By which of the following methods do red algae reproduce?
questions.explanation: Red algae usually reproduce vegetatively by fragmentation; they also reproduce by spores and sexually.

questions.text: By what name is the festival of Makar Sankranti celebrated in Assam?
questions.explanation: In Assam Makar Sankranti is celebrated as Magh (Bhogali) Bihu, the harvest festival; Pongal is Tamil Nadu's name for it.

questions.text: Which of the following Constitution Amendment Bills is related to the provision of modifying the list of Scheduled Caste in Tamil Nadu?
options: The Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order Amendment Act, 2013
questions.explanation: The Bill modified Tamil Nadu's list of Scheduled Castes, grouping seven castes under the common name Devendrakula Velalar.

questions.text: Mahendravarman I who wrote Mattavilasa-prahasana is related to which of the following ruling dynasties?
questions.explanation: Mahendravarman I, the Pallava king of Kanchi, wrote the Sanskrit farce 'Mattavilasa Prahasana'.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: When was the All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) established?
questions.explanation: The AITUC was founded in Bombay on 31 October 1920, with Lala Lajpat Rai as its first president.

questions.text: Which of the following is responsible for the red colour of beetroot?
questions.explanation: Betanin, a betalain pigment, gives beetroot its red colour. Lycopene colours tomatoes, curcumin turmeric and beta-carotene carrots.

questions.text: Raziya Sultan was the first and only female ruler of the Sultanate, who ascended the throne in:
questions.explanation: Iltutmish's daughter Raziya ascended the throne of Delhi in 1236 and ruled until 1240.

questions.text: Find the greatest value of ‘k’ in a 6-digit number 6745k2 such that the number is divisible by 3.
questions.explanation: The digit sum 6 + 7 + 4 + 5 + k + 2 = 24 + k must be a multiple of 3, so k is 0, 3, 6 or 9. The greatest is 9.

questions.text: One pipe can fill a tank 6 times faster than another pipe. If both the pipes together can fill the tank in 40 minutes, then in how many minutes will the slower pipe alone be able to fill the tank?
questions.explanation: If the slower pipe fills 1 part a minute, the faster fills 6, together 7. The tank holds 7 × 40 = 280 parts, so the slower pipe alone takes 280 minutes.

questions.text: What conclusion can be drawn about the solution of the following system of linear equations in two variables: 3x + 2y = 7 2x + 3y = 7
questions.explanation: 3/2 ≠ 2/3, so the two lines cross at exactly one point: the unique solution x = 1, y = 1.

questions.text: The marked price of a revolving chair is ₹15,000. It is available on two successive discounts of 20% and 12%. What is its selling price (in ₹)?
The radius of a circle is 12.5 cm and the length of one its chords is 11 cm. What is the distance of the chord from the centre? (correct to one decimal place)

In an election between two candidates, 80% of the voters cast their votes, out of which 4% votes were declared invalid. A candidate got 15,360 votes which were 80% of the valid votes. Find the total number of votes.
questions.explanation: Valid votes = 15,360/0.8 = 19,200, which is 96% of the votes cast: 20,000. These are 80% of the voters, so there were 25,000 votes in all.

questions.text: PQ is the diameter of a circle with centre A. M is a point on the circumference of the circle. If m∠MAP = 110°, then find the value of m∠MQA.
The volume of a right circular cylindrical box of radius 30cm is 600cm³. Find the height of the box.
Triangle XYZ is an isosceles triangle with sides XY = XZ. If the measure of angle Y is 80°, what is the measure of angle X?
In how much time (in years, rounded off to 2 decimal places) will ₹10,800 amount to ₹24,800 if invested at simple interest at the rate of 15.5% per annum?
In what ratio, sugar costing ₹78 per kg be mixed with sugar costing ₹46 per kg such that by selling the mixture at ₹75 per kg there is a gain of 20%?
questions.explanation: For a 20% gain the mixture must cost 75/1.2 = ₹62.50 per kg. By alligation, ₹78 sugar : ₹46 sugar = (62.5 − 46) : (78 − 62.5) = 16.5 : 15.5 = 33 : 31.

questions.text: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 100 m. The thief starts running and the policeman chases him. If the speed of thief and policeman are 21 km/h and 23 km/h, respectively, then how far will the thief have to run before he is over taken?
questions.explanation: The policeman gains 2 km/h, so he closes the 100 m (0.1 km) in 0.05 hours. In that time the thief runs 21 × 0.05 = 1.05 km = 1050 m.

questions.text: A, B and C invested money in a business such that 2 times A's share, 4 times B's share and 6 times C's share are all equal. If they earned ₹44,000, find the share of A.
Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank. We need to __________ a solution to this problem before it gets worse.
questions.explanation: To 'come up with' a solution is to think of or produce one.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom for the given group of words. A time when money might unexpectedly be needed
questions.explanation: Money saved 'for a rainy day' is kept for a time when it may unexpectedly be needed.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Mr. Adhil “called back but he wasn’t able to” find the scooter part he needed.
options: called down but he wasn’t able to
called up to but he wasn’t able to
called off but he wasn’t able to
called around but he wasn’t able to
questions.explanation: To 'call around' is to telephone several people or places, as when searching for a part; to 'call back' is only to return a call.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word from the following sentence. Barren "Can you believe how much traffic there is today?", grumbled Tom, glancing at the congested road ahead.
questions.explanation: 'Barren' means bare or empty; its opposite is 'congested', crowded and full.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the following sentence. It was difficult to accommodate the “avariciousness” of the people.
questions.explanation: 'Avariciousness' is greed; its opposite is 'generosity'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word..
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'measurement'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined word segment in the given sentence. A “herd of cattle” consists of related females, cubs, and a small number of adult males.
questions.explanation: Related females, cubs and a few adult males make up a 'pride of lions'; cattle have calves, not cubs.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Maverick
questions.explanation: A 'maverick' is an independent-minded, unconventional person, as is a 'bohemian'. The other three are opposites.

questions.text: Identify the error in the given sentence. Camels tend to move slowly than other domestic animals in the plains.
questions.explanation: A comparison with 'than' needs the comparative: 'move more slowly than other domestic animals'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A person who does not believe in God
questions.explanation: An atheist is a person who does not believe in God.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. I saw a shabby looking man living in the “cavity” of a mountain.
questions.explanation: A 'cavity' is a hollow, a 'hole'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. This is a clear example of “conflict” of egos.
questions.explanation: A 'conflict' of egos is a 'clash' of egos.

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. P) her face Q) I have R) for a year S) not seen
questions.explanation: 'I have (Q) not seen (S) her face (P) for a year (R).'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence. Instead of confusing others, let us “call a spade a spade” in front of the audience.
questions.explanation: To 'call a spade a spade' is to speak plainly and truthfully.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'necessary'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. It is nothing “else your pride which makes” you say such a thing.
options: else but your pride which make
else but your pride which makes
questions.explanation: The idiom is 'nothing else but', and 'pride' takes the singular 'makes': 'It is nothing else but your pride which makes you say such a thing.'

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A.The door of the flat was ajar. B.The taxi stopped. C.Mr. Satterthwaite flung himself out and raced up the stone stairs to the second floor like a young athlete. D.He pushed it open, and the great voice welcomed him.
questions.explanation: The taxi stops (B), Mr Satterthwaite runs up the stairs (C), finds the door ajar (A) and pushes it open (D): BCAD.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. He has written a best-selling novel.
options: A best-selling novel has been written by him.
A best-selling novel was written by him.
A best-selling novel was being written by him
A best-selling novel would have been written by him.
questions.explanation: The present perfect 'has written' becomes 'has been written' in the passive.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. He wrote an inspiring speech for the event.
options: An inspiring speech was written by him for the event.
An inspiring speech was being written by him for the event.
An inspiring speech has been written by him for the event.
An inspiring speech is written by him for the event.
questions.explanation: The simple past 'wrote' becomes 'was written' in the passive.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word in the given sentence. This building is “colossal” and it can hold a village’s population in it.
questions.explanation: 'Colossal' means extremely large.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The mathematician Federico Ardila-Mantilla grew up in Colombia, an (1) ______________ student but gifted in math. He was failing most of his classes at his high school in Bogotá when someone (2) _______________ him to apply to MIT. He had not heard of the school. To his surprise, he got in, and he went on scholarship. Mathematically, he did well. One of his professors, an acid-tongued theoretician known to (3) ____________ his audience to a herd of cows, routinely tucked ‘open’ math problems into homework assignments, without telling the students. These had never been solved by anyone. Ardila solved one. He went on to receive his bachelor’s and Ph.D. in math from MIT. But his academic experience was also one of isolation. Part of it had to do with his own (4) _____________. Part of it was cultural. As a Latino, he was very much in the minority in the department, and he did not feel comfortable in American mathematical spaces. No one had tried to explicitly (5) ______________ him, yet he felt alone. In math, collaborating with others opens up new kinds of learning and thinking. But in his nine years at MIT, Ardila worked with others only twice.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1
questions.explanation: He was failing most of his classes: an 'indifferent' student, though gifted in math.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’; ‘A – B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’; ‘A x B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’ and ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the father of B’. Based on the above, if M + Q – R + K – Y, then how is M related to Y?
questions.explanation: M + Q: M is Q's mother, and Q – R: Q is R's brother, so M is R's mother. R + K: R is K's mother, and K – Y: K is Y's brother, so R is Y's mother. M is Y's mother's mother.

questions.text: Four letter-clusters have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the letter-cluster that is different. Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter cluster.
questions.explanation: In MPS, TWZ and DGJ the letters move +3, then +3. KNP moves +3, then +2, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the following equation correct? 29 × 145 + 5 − 640 ÷ 15 = 216
Which number will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 14 − 45 × 5 + 6 ÷ 3 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 14 + 45 ÷ 5 − 6 × 3 = 14 + 9 − 18 = 5.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series. LM_O_NPMRO_KU_TI
questions.explanation: With N, O, R, P in the blanks the series falls into blocks of four, LMNO ONPM RORK UPTI: first letters move +3 (L, O, R, U), second +1 (M, N, O, P), third +2 (N, P, R, T) and fourth −2 (O, M, K, I).

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of numbers. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 11 : 1331 9 : 729
questions.explanation: The second number is the cube of the first: 11³ = 1331 and 9³ = 729. Likewise 7³ = 343.

questions.text: Select the word pair that best represents a similar relationship to the one expressed in the pair of words given below. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Cessation : Beginning
questions.explanation: 'Cessation' (an end) is the opposite of 'beginning', as 'enormous' is of 'miniscule' (tiny). None of the other pairs are opposites.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 5, 10, 17, 26, 37, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 5, 7, 9, 11, so the next is 13: 37 + 13 = 50. (The terms are 2² + 1, 3² + 1, … 7² + 1.)

questions.text: In this question, three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All necklaces are squares. Some squares are circles. No circle is a ring. Conclusions: I.No square is a ring. II.No ring is a circle. III.Some squares are necklaces.
options: Only conclusions I and III follow.
Only conclusions II and III follow.
questions.explanation: All necklaces are squares, so some squares are necklaces (III). No circle is a ring, so no ring is a circle (II). Only some squares are known to be circles, so a square could still be a ring: I does not follow.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘TERRAIN’ is written as ‘VETTAIP’ and ‘TRAFFIC’ is written as ‘VTAHHIE’. How will ‘MOTOR’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Consonants move 2 places forward and vowels stay: TERRAIN → VETTAIP and TRAFFIC → VTAHHIE. So MOTOR → OOVOT.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? HKPT, JLNS, LMLR, ?, POHP
questions.explanation: First letters move +2 (H, J, L, N, P), second +1 (K, L, M, N, O), third −2 (P, N, L, J, H) and fourth −1 (T, S, R, Q, P): NNJQ.

questions.text: Select the word pair that best represents a similar relationship to the one expressed in the pair of words given below. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Scissors : Paper
questions.explanation: Scissors are used to cut paper, as an axe is used to cut wood.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of numbers. (317, 202) (438, 323) (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is 115 less than the first: 317 − 115 = 202 and 438 − 115 = 323. Likewise 402 − 115 = 287.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word.) Pig : Piglets :: Deer : ?
questions.explanation: A piglet is a young pig, and a fawn a young deer. A foal is a young horse and a pup a young dog; the young of a few large deer, such as elk, are also called calves, but 'fawn' is the general word.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘IFF’ is coded as ‘21’ and ‘ARB’ is coded as ‘21’. How will ‘CAW’ be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: The code is the sum of the letters' positions: I + F + F = 9 + 6 + 6 = 21 and A + R + B = 1 + 18 + 2 = 21. So CAW = 3 + 1 + 23 = 27.

questions.text: The position(s) of how many letters will remain unchanged if all the letters in the word ‘ASTEROID’ are arranged in English alphabetical order?
questions.explanation: ASTEROID in alphabetical order is A D E I O R S T. Compared with A S T E R O I D, only A, first in both, keeps its place.

questions.text: The second number in the given number-pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) is/are followed in all the number-pairs, except one. Find that odd number-pair. (NOTE: The relation should be found without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits)
questions.explanation: In 13 : 182, 25 : 650 and 23 : 552 the number is multiplied by the next one (13 × 14, 25 × 26, 23 × 24). 18 : 306 is 18 × 17, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: 22 is related to 176 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 32 is related to 256. To which of the following is 48 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: The second number is 8 times the first: 22 × 8 = 176 and 32 × 8 = 256. So 48 × 8 = 384.

questions.text: Which types of gametes are found in Spirogyra?
questions.explanation: In Spirogyra the fusing gametes are alike in size (isogamous) and have no flagella (non-motile).

questions.text: Which Article mentions the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?
questions.explanation: Article 148 provides for a Comptroller and Auditor General of India, appointed by the President.

questions.text: According to the Census of India 2001, which of the following is the main reason that Indian men migrate?
questions.explanation: By NCERT's reading of the 2001 Census, work and employment was the main reason men migrated (38%); for women it was marriage.

questions.text: Identify the INCORRECT pair regarding motion and their examples?
options: Periodic motion – Hands of a clock
Oscillatory motion – Earth moving around the sun
Translatory motion – A ball falling from the cliff
Rotatory motion – blades of a fan
questions.explanation: The Earth's revolution round the Sun is periodic motion, not oscillatory: an oscillation is a to-and-fro movement, like a pendulum's. The other three pairs are correct.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Where was the 1912 session of the India National Congress held in Bihar?
questions.explanation: The Congress met at Bankipore (Patna) in 1912, under the presidency of R. N. Mudholkar.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which year was the temple entry movement started by Bhimrao Ambedkar?
questions.explanation: NCERT dates the temple entry movement Ambedkar started, in which his Mahar caste followers took part, to 1927.

questions.text: N. Rangasamy sworn in as the Chief Minister of Puducherry in May 2021. What is the name of the party he formed?
questions.explanation: N. Rangasamy founded the All India N.R. Congress in 2011, after leaving the Indian National Congress.

questions.text: Who among the following is the first Indian to win gold at Junior World Weightlifting Championship in May 2022?
questions.explanation: Harshada Sharad Garud won the women's 45 kg gold at the 2022 Junior World Weightlifting Championships in Heraklion, Greece: India's first gold at the event.

questions.text: Who among the following dancers was the first one from the state of Odisha to be conferred the Padma Vibhushan Award?
questions.explanation: The Odissi guru Kelucharan Mohapatra received the Padma Vibhushan in 2000, the first person from Odisha to do so.

questions.text: Which gas is evolved when iron and water react?
questions.explanation: Iron reacts with steam to form iron oxide and hydrogen: 3Fe + 4H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + 4H₂.

questions.text: Sankalp Gupta is associated with which of the following events?
questions.explanation: Sankalp Gupta, from Nagpur, is an Indian chess grandmaster.

questions.text: About what percentage of passenger traffic is carried by roads in India?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 87%: the government's National Road Transport Policy puts about 87% of India's passenger traffic on land (road and rail together) on the roads. Other sources give figures between 85% and 90%.

questions.text: Which of the following classes includes the family of turtles?
questions.explanation: Turtles and tortoises are reptiles (class Reptilia), along with snakes, lizards and crocodiles.

questions.text: Some of the talas invented by ____________ include Trimukhi, Panchamukhi, Saptamukhi and Navamukhi.
questions.explanation: The Carnatic musician M. Balamuralikrishna devised a new tala system whose basic types are Trimukhi, Panchamukhi, Saptamukhi and Navamukhi.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding Fundamental Rights?
options: The Fundamental Rights are mentioned in constitution from article 12 to 35.
Fundamental Rights can be enforced by Law.
Fundamental rights are derived from the Britain Constitution.
questions.explanation: India's Fundamental Rights were borrowed from the US Constitution's Bill of Rights, not Britain's. They are in Part III (Articles 12 to 35), are enforceable in the courts, and Article 21 protects the right to life.

questions.text: Rudrankksh Patil is associated with _________.
questions.explanation: Rudrankksh Patil is a shooter; he won the 10 m air rifle title at the 2022 ISSF World Championship.

questions.text: Under which scheme are collateral free loans of up to ₹10 Lakh extended by the Member Lending Institutions (MLIs) in India?
questions.explanation: Under the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (2015), Member Lending Institutions (banks, NBFCs and microfinance institutions) give collateral-free loans of up to ₹10 lakh to small businesses.

questions.text: Which of the following group of months is the coldest in North India?
questions.explanation: December and January are the coldest months in northern India, in the cold weather season that runs from mid-November to February.

questions.text: Which of the following was NOT one of the basic attributes of Ashokas' Dhamma?
questions.explanation: Ashoka's Dhamma was a moral code for ordinary people: non-violence, tolerance of all sects and respect for elders, meant also to hold his vast empire together. It did not ask for celibacy.

questions.text: Which ocean is encircling the continent of Antarctica and extends northward to 60 degrees south latitude?
questions.explanation: The Southern Ocean surrounds Antarctica and extends north to 60° south latitude.

questions.text: Harmonium player, Tulsidas Borkar, was awarded with the ___________ in 2016.
questions.explanation: Pandit Tulsidas Borkar, the Goan harmonium player, received the Padma Shri in 2016.

questions.text: The 'Make in India' initiative primarily focuses on which sector?
questions.explanation: Make in India, launched in 2014, aims to make India a global manufacturing hub.

questions.text: The real name of Babur, the founder of Mughal dynasty in India was:
questions.explanation: Babur, who founded the Mughal dynasty after the First Battle of Panipat (1526), was born Zahir-ud-din Muhammad.

questions.text: Which of the following States have enacted the Cattle Preservation Act, 2021 in July- August 2021 to regulate slaughter and transport of cattle and proposed an amendment in December 2021 to allow inter-district transportation of cattle for agricultural and animal husbandry except in districts sharing international border?
questions.explanation: Assam passed its Cattle Preservation Act in August 2021, and in December 2021 amended it to allow cattle to be moved between districts for farming and animal husbandry, except in districts on the international border.

questions.text: Which of the following festivals observed in Assam is majorly celebrated by Vaishnavites?
questions.explanation: Doljatra (Doul Utsav), Assam's Holi, is centred on the Vaishnavite satras, above all Barpeta Satra.

questions.text: A man buys 10 kg of wheat at a rate of ₹26/kg. The wheat is mixed with 6 kg of other good quality of wheat to get a mixture at a price of ₹35/kg. The price of good quality wheat per kg (in ₹) is:
questions.explanation: 10 × 26 + 6x = 16 × 35 = 560, so 6x = 300 and the good wheat costs ₹50/kg.

questions.text: Ghanshyam is thrice as old as Akash. 10 years ago, Ghanshyam was four times as old as Akash. What is the difference between their current ages (in years)?
questions.explanation: With Akash's age a, 3a − 10 = 4(a − 10), so a = 30 and Ghanshyam is 90. The difference is 60 years.

questions.text: On dividing a number by 55, we get 28 as the remainder. On dividing the same number by 11, what is the remainder?
questions.explanation: The number is 55k + 28. 55k is divisible by 11, and 28 = 2 × 11 + 6, so the remainder is 6.

questions.text: Two goods trains 132 m and 108 m in length are running towards each other on parallel tracks. The first train is running at a speed of 32 km/h and the second at a speed of 40 km/h. How much time will they take to cross each other after meeting?
questions.explanation: Running towards each other, the relative speed is 32 + 40 = 72 km/h = 20 m/s. Crossing covers both lengths, 132 + 108 = 240 m, so it takes 240/20 = 12 s.

questions.text: What is the length (in cm) of each side of a cube if the volume of a cube is 13,824 cm³?
The radii of two concentric circles are 26 cm and 10 cm. If the chord of the greater circle is a tangent to the smaller circle, then find the length of that chord.
questions.explanation: The point of contact is the chord's midpoint, so half the chord = √(26² − 10²) = √576 = 24 cm and the chord is 48 cm.

questions.text: If the mean proportional between p and q is 12, then the possible values of p and q, respectively, are:
questions.explanation: The mean proportional is √(pq) = 12, so pq = 144. Of the pairs only 24 × 6 = 144.

questions.text: Vipul spends 30% of his monthly income on rent, 60% of the remaining on groceries, and 40% of the remaining on others. If he saves ₹7056 in a month, then how much (in ₹) does he spend on groceries?
questions.explanation: After rent 70% of the income is left; groceries take 60% of it (42% of the income), leaving 28%; others take 40% of that, leaving 16.8% saved. Income = 7,056/0.168 = ₹42,000, so groceries = 0.42 × 42,000 = ₹17,640.

questions.text: A cell phone is available for Rs.600 or for Rs.300 cash down payment together with Rs.360 to be paid after two months. Find the rate of interest charged under this scheme.
questions.explanation: Paying ₹300 down leaves ₹300 owed, and paying ₹360 for it two months later is ₹60 interest on ₹300 for 2 months. Rate = (60 × 100)/(300 × 2/12) = 120% a year.

questions.text: An article is sold for ₹747 after successive discounts of 17% and x%. If the marked price of the article is ₹1,600, what is the value of x?
questions.explanation: After 17% off, 1,600 × 0.83 = ₹1,328. Then 747/1,328 = 0.5625, so the second discount is 43.75%.

questions.text: A person purchased a table and a sofa for ₹28,000. He sold the sofa at a profit of 10% and the table at a profit 15.25%. If his total profit was 13%, then the difference between the cost price of the sofa and the table (in ₹) is:
questions.explanation: With the table costing T: 0.10(28,000 − T) + 0.1525T = 0.13 × 28,000 = 3,640, so 0.0525T = 840 and T = ₹16,000. The sofa cost ₹12,000; the difference is ₹4,000.

questions.text: Let C be a circle with centre O and PQ be a minor arc on C. Let R and S be two points on the major arc of PQ on C. If PQ subtends an angle 80° at O, find ∠PRQ and ∠PSQ, respectively.
questions.explanation: An arc subtends at any point on the rest of the circle half the angle it subtends at the centre. R and S both lie on the major arc, so ∠PRQ = ∠PSQ = 80° ÷ 2 = 40°.

questions.text: Select the correct spelling to fill in the blank. Definitions of _________ are subjective to various interpretations.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'sovereignty'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Foment
questions.explanation: To 'foment' is to stir up or encourage trouble; of the options, 'regulate' (to control or keep in check) is the nearest opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Hostile
questions.explanation: 'Hostile' means unfriendly or aggressive; its opposite is 'friendly'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word. At times, David behaves in a very “obdurate” manner to kids.
questions.explanation: 'Obdurate' means stubbornly refusing to change: 'obstinate'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the following sentence. Sachin Tendulkar was an “indispensable” member of the Indian cricket team in his days.
questions.explanation: 'Indispensable' means absolutely necessary: 'essential'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment in which the article has been used INCORRECTLY. Master Sam / is a heaviest / boy in / grade twelve.
questions.explanation: A superlative takes 'the': 'is the heaviest boy in grade twelve'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. He was given a reward for his contribution by the Governor.
options: For his contribution, he was rewarded by the governor.
The governor gave him a reward for his contribution.
Rewarded by the governor, as he contributed along.
questions.explanation: The agent, the Governor, becomes the subject and 'was given' becomes 'gave': 'The governor gave him a reward for his contribution.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words Anything pertaining to cats
questions.explanation: 'Feline' means relating to cats; 'canine' is dogs, 'bovine' cattle and 'taurine' bulls.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence. Rahul won the extempore competition. He is lucky to be blessed with the “gift of the gab”.
questions.explanation: The 'gift of the gab' is a talent for speaking fluently and persuasively.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the sentences in the correct logical sequence to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. a. It regulates the operation of all body organs and protects the body and mind from becoming unbalanced as a result of negative circumstances and unhealthy lifestyles. b. It only requires frequent practice of the proper body motions and breathing techniques. c. The physical benefits of yoga can be enjoyed for a lifetime without risk or injury. d. It regulates the relationship between the body, the intellect, and the spirit.
questions.explanation: c names the subject, yoga, and its benefits; b says all it requires; d and a then say what it regulates, from the link between body, intellect and spirit to the working of the organs: c, b, d, a.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Cascade
questions.explanation: A 'cascade' is a small waterfall, or water falling in stages.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. We have to say little in this matter.
options: In this matter, little is to be said.
Little has to be said in this matter.
In this matter, little must be said.
Little had to be said in this matter.
questions.explanation: 'Have to say' becomes 'has to be said', agreeing with the new subject 'little': 'Little has to be said in this matter.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Positive self-talk “have a great affect” on one’s self-worth.
questions.explanation: The singular subject 'self-talk' takes 'has', and the noun is 'effect' ('affect' is the verb): 'has a great effect'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Sharat is always ______ about showing up for work because he believes that tardiness gets us nowhere.
questions.explanation: 'Tardiness' is lateness, so someone who thinks it gets us nowhere is 'punctual'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. That which is no longer in existence
questions.explanation: 'Extinct' describes what no longer exists, such as a species that has died out.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. I had “not only helped her by” giving hints but also with providing her links.
questions.explanation: 'Not only' should stand just before the first of the two things joined, matching 'but also': 'helped her not only by giving hints but also with providing her links'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Nina has not yet learned how to “straighten up and fly right”.
options: be professional in flying the aircraft
forget the wrongdoings of the others
improve her absurd behaviour and act seriously
remember the past and prepare for the future
questions.explanation: To 'straighten up and fly right' is to stop behaving badly and act responsibly.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Deepak is studying B.tech. at IIT Delhi to become the engineer.
questions.explanation: Becoming one of a profession takes the indefinite article: 'to become an engineer', not 'the engineer'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Dealing with things in a practical and sensible way
questions.explanation: 'Pragmatic' means dealing with things practically and sensibly; a 'stoic' endures hardship without complaint and a 'cynic' distrusts others' motives.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'attempt'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option, in the questions that follow, to fill in each blank. A dance which is created or choreographed and performed according (1)___________ the tenets of the Natya Shastra is called a classical dance. The two broad (2)____________ of classical dancing are the tandava and the lasya. Power and force are typical of the tandava; grace and delicacy of the lasya. Tandava is (3)_______________ with Shiva, and lasya with Parvati. Dance which is pure movement is called nritta, and dance which is (4)_______________ in nature is called nritya. A dancer, in the classical tradition, has to have years of training before he or she can begin to perform on the stage. The four main (5)_____________ of classical dancing in India are : Bharat Natyam, Kathakali, Manipuri, Kathak .Bharat Natyam is the oldest and most popular dance-form of India.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Performed 'according to' the tenets: the phrase always takes 'to'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option, in the questions that follow, to fill in each blank. A dance which is created or choreographed and performed according (1)___________ the tenets of the Natya Shastra is called a classical dance. The two broad (2)____________ of classical dancing are the tandava and the lasya. Power and force are typical of the tandava; grace and delicacy of the lasya. Tandava is (3)_______________ with Shiva, and lasya with Parvati. Dance which is pure movement is called nritta, and dance which is (4)_______________ in nature is called nritya. A dancer, in the classical tradition, has to have years of training before he or she can begin to perform on the stage. The four main (5)_____________ of classical dancing in India are : Bharat Natyam, Kathakali, Manipuri, Kathak .Bharat Natyam is the oldest and most popular dance-form of India.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Tandava and lasya are the two broad 'aspects', or sides, of classical dancing.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option, in the questions that follow, to fill in each blank. A dance which is created or choreographed and performed according (1)___________ the tenets of the Natya Shastra is called a classical dance. The four main (5)_____________ of classical dancing in India are : Bharat Natyam, Kathakali, Manipuri, Kathak .Bharat Natyam is the oldest and most popular dance-form of India.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Tandava is 'associated' with Shiva, and lasya with Parvati.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option, in the questions that follow, to fill in each blank. A dance which is created or choreographed and performed according (1)___________ the tenets of the Natya Shastra is called a classical dance. Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: Pure movement is nritta; dance that expresses meaning, 'interpretative' in nature, is nritya.

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option, in the questions that follow, to fill in each blank. A dance which is created or choreographed and performed according (1)___________ the tenets of the Natya Shastra is called a classical dance.
