Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Bharat Natyam, Kathakali, Manipuri and Kathak are 'schools', or styles, of classical dance.

questions.text: 7 is related to 40 by certain logic. Following the same logic, 5 is related to 16. To which of the following is 9 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each number is related to its square minus 9: 7² − 9 = 40 and 5² − 9 = 16. So 9² − 9 = 72.

questions.text: 64 is related to 4 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 216 is related to 6. To which of the following is 729 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: Each number is related to its cube root: 64 = 4³ and 216 = 6³. 729 = 9³, so 9.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series. B_DE_GDGBK_IB_DK
questions.explanation: With C, B, D, O in the blanks the series splits into BCDE, BGDG, BKDI, BODK: the first and third letters stay B and D, the second moves +4 (C, G, K, O) and the fourth +2 (E, G, I, K).

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘ZCJV’ is coded as ‘YBIU’ and ‘GKMD’ is coded as ‘FJLC’. How will ‘EYOR’ be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one place back: ZCJV → YBIU and GKMD → FJLC. So EYOR → DXNQ.

questions.text: Q is the mother of T. R is the husband of P. S is the father of Q. T is the brother of P. How is P related to S?
questions.explanation: T is P's brother and Q is T's mother, so Q is P's mother, and S is Q's father. P has a husband, R, so she is S's daughter's daughter.

questions.text: Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-clusters are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which is the one that DOES NOT belong to that group? (Note: The odd man out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter-cluster.)
questions.explanation: In HKI, MPN and RUS the letters move +3, then −2. QUR moves +4, then −3, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: In this question, three statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusion(s) logically follows/follow from the statements. Statements: All grains are cereals. Some cereals are fruits. No fruit is a vegetable. Conclusions: I. All cereals can be vegetables. II. All grains are fruits.
options: Neither Conclusion I nor II follow.
Both Conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: The cereals that are fruits can never be vegetables, as no fruit is a vegetable, so I does not follow. All grains are cereals, but nothing links grains to fruits, so II does not follow either.

questions.text: In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (26, 114) (47, 198)
questions.explanation: The second number is four times the first plus 10: 26 × 4 + 10 = 114 and 47 × 4 + 10 = 198. Likewise 15 × 4 + 10 = 70.

questions.text: Select the word pair that best represents a similar relationship to the one expressed in the pair of words given below. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Love : Harmony
questions.explanation: Love brings harmony, as peace brings bliss: in both pairs a positive state leads to a related, happy one. Rage and cool are opposites, and calm : sad and anger : excitement do not pair a state with the good it brings.

questions.text: The position of how many letters will remain unchanged if each of the letters in the word ‘SIGNATURE’ is re-arranged in the English alphabetical order from left to right?
questions.explanation: SIGNATURE in alphabetical order is A E G I N R S T U. Only G, the third letter, stays in its place.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question marks (?) in the given series? 61, ?, ?, 73, 79, 83, 89
questions.explanation: The series is consecutive prime numbers: 61, 67, 71, 73, 79, 83, 89.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘BLEACHERS’ is coded as ‘63’ and ‘ABACAS’ is coded as ‘42’. How will ‘FIZZY’ be coded in the same language?
questions.explanation: Each word's code is 7 times its number of letters: BLEACHERS has 9 (9 × 7 = 63) and ABACAS 6 (6 × 7 = 42). FIZZY has 5: 5 × 7 = 35.

questions.text: Which number will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 7 ÷ 5 − 30 × 6 + 4 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 7 × 5 + 30 ÷ 6 − 4 = 35 + 5 − 4 = 36.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 1604 × 4 + 87 – 16 ÷ 16 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 1604 ÷ 4 − 87 + 16 × 16 = 401 − 87 + 256 = 570.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Botany : Plants : : Conchology : ?
questions.explanation: Botany is the study of plants; conchology is the study of shells.

questions.text: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series to make it logically complete? JAL, MDO, PGR, SJU, ?
questions.explanation: Every letter moves 3 places forward each time: J, M, P, S, V; A, D, G, J, M; L, O, R, U, X. The next cluster is VMX.

questions.text: Three of the following numbers are alike in a certain way and one is different. Pick the odd one out. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: 829, 643 and 821 are prime numbers. 237 = 3 × 79, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Gangubai Hangal belonged to the ________.
questions.explanation: Gangubai Hangal, the Hindustani vocalist from Karnataka, was a leading singer of the Kirana gharana.

questions.text: In India, Teachers’ Day is celebrated annually on September 5 to mark the birthday of:
questions.explanation: Teachers' Day marks the birthday of Dr Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, philosopher, teacher and India's second President, born on 5 September 1888.

questions.text: Which of the following articles of the Indian constitution deals with the parliament and it's proceedings?
questions.explanation: Articles 79 to 122 (Part V, Chapter II) deal with Parliament. Articles 12 to 35 are the Fundamental Rights, 36 to 51 the Directive Principles and 51A the Fundamental Duties.

questions.text: Which of the following Rajiv Gandhi National Sadbhavana Awards was conferred on Ustad Amjad Ali Khan?
questions.explanation: The sarod maestro Ustad Amjad Ali Khan received the 21st Rajiv Gandhi National Sadbhavana Award, given for promoting communal harmony and national integration.

questions.text: The Pratiharas who first had their capital at Bhinmal gained prominence during the rule of:
questions.explanation: Nagabhata I raised the Gurjara-Pratiharas to power in the 8th century and pushed back Arab raids from Sindh. Kanishka was a Kushana king, Devapala a Pala king and Nagarjuna a Buddhist philosopher.

questions.text: In which state of India is the Chandra Prabha Wildlife Sanctuary located?
questions.explanation: The Chandra Prabha Wildlife Sanctuary is in Chandauli district, Uttar Pradesh, near Varanasi.

questions.text: Which Committee identified the existence of legal provisions for implementation of some of the Fundamental Duties?
questions.explanation: The Justice Verma Committee on Fundamental Duties (1999) pointed to existing laws that already enforce some of them, such as the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971.

questions.text: Which of the following is a correct statement?
options: National Income is NNP at FC.
National Income is GDP at MP.
National Income is GNP at FC.
National Income is NDP at MP.
questions.explanation: National income is the net national product at factor cost: GNP at market prices less depreciation and net indirect taxes.

questions.text: The final match of IPL 2023 was hosted by which of the following cities?
questions.explanation: The IPL 2023 final, in which Chennai Super Kings beat Gujarat Titans, was played at the Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad.

questions.text: Which among the following is NOT a classification criterion of drugs?
questions.explanation: Drugs are classified by pharmacological effect, by drug action, by chemical structure and by molecular target. 'Behavioural condition' is not one of these criteria.

questions.text: What is iGOT launched by the Government of India in April 2020?
options: Online portal for social security schemes
Online training portal for COVID-19 management
Online portal for scholarships to single girl child
questions.explanation: iGOT (Integrated Government Online Training), launched on the DIKSHA platform in April 2020, trained frontline workers in COVID-19 management.

questions.text: The _________ portal is a platform provided by the Govt. of India for famers to attain any information related to agriculture.
questions.explanation: The Farmers' Portal (farmer.gov.in) is the agriculture ministry's one-stop source of information for farmers, from seed varieties and pests to weather advisories, credit and insurance.

questions.text: The name of the strait between the Pacific and Arctic oceans, separating the Chukchi Peninsula of the Russian Far East from the Seward Peninsula of Alaska, is the:
questions.explanation: The Bering Strait links the Pacific and Arctic oceans and separates Asia (Russia) from North America (Alaska).

questions.text: ‘Ungalil Oruvan’ (One Among You) is the autobiography of which of the following chief ministers?
questions.explanation: 'Ungalil Oruvan' is the autobiography of Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M.K. Stalin; its first part was released in 2022.

questions.text: What happens when two forces act in the opposite directions on an object?
options: The net force acting on the object is the total of the two forces.
The net force acting on the object is the difference between the two objects.
The net force acting on the object is the sum of the two objects.
The net force acting on the object is the difference between the two forces.
questions.explanation: Forces acting in opposite directions partly cancel, so the net force is their difference, in the direction of the larger force.

questions.text: The first Indian woman to hold the Under-20 World Wrestling Championship is _________.
questions.explanation: In 2022 Antim Panghal won the 53 kg title at the Under-20 World Wrestling Championships, the first Indian woman to become a U-20 world champion.

questions.text: Which industrial policy marked the beginning of liberalisation in the Indian industry, reducing the restrictions on private companies?
questions.explanation: The New Industrial Policy of 1991 abolished licensing for most industries and opened the economy to private and foreign investment.

questions.text: Which of the following is a saturated hydrocarbon?
questions.explanation: Propane, C₃H₈, fits the alkane formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂: it has only single bonds, so it is saturated. C₂H₄ (ethene) has a double bond and C₆H₆ (benzene) is unsaturated; C₄H₈ is usually butene, though its ring isomer cyclobutane is saturated.

questions.text: Who among the following famous badminton players won Swiss Open 2022?
questions.explanation: PV Sindhu won the women's singles title at the Swiss Open in March 2022.

questions.text: The Kuchipudi dance belongs to which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Kuchipudi, a classical dance named after a village in Krishna district, belongs to Andhra Pradesh.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: With reference to Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, consider the following statements. a) He protested child marriage and polygamy. b) Due to his efforts, the first Hindu Widow Remarriage Act, 1856, was introduced. c) He was primarily known for his scholarship in Persian language. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Vidyasagar campaigned against child marriage and polygamy, and his efforts led to the Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856. He was a Sanskrit scholar, not a Persian one, so c is wrong.

questions.text: A large number of words are derived from the word ‘Go’ meaning cow. A wealthy person was known as ________ in Vedic times.
questions.explanation: Cattle were the chief measure of wealth in Vedic times, so a rich man was a 'gomat', one rich in cows. 'Gotra' came to mean lineage and 'gaveshana' (a search for cows) a search or inquiry.

questions.text: What was India's annual exponential growth rate as per the 2011 Census?
questions.explanation: Census 2011 put India's average annual exponential growth rate for 2001-2011 at 1.64%, down from 1.97% in 1991-2001.

questions.text: Which of the following districts of India is an example of an industrial district?
questions.explanation: SSC's key follows the usual division of India's industrial areas into major regions, minor regions and industrial districts, in which Kota is one of the 15 industrial districts (with Kanpur, Agra, Gwalior and others). Faridabad and Meerut lie in the larger Gurgaon-Delhi-Meerut industrial region.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The Non-Cooperation Movement was called off after which of the following incidents?
options: Outbreak of the First World War
questions.explanation: Gandhi called off the movement in February 1922 after a crowd set fire to the police station at Chauri Chaura, in Gorakhpur district, killing several policemen.

questions.text: Which composite number can divide the sum of the first 12 natural numbers?
questions.explanation: 1 + 2 + … + 12 = 12 × 13/2 = 78 = 2 × 3 × 13. Of the options only 6 divides it: 78 = 6 × 13.

questions.text: Let ABC be a triangle. If the mid-points of AB, BC and AC are D, E and F, respectively, then ∆DEF is NOT congruent to _____.
questions.explanation: Joining the mid-points divides ΔABC into four congruent triangles: ΔDEF, ΔADF, ΔBDE and ΔECF. Each has sides half as long as ΔABC's, so ΔABC is not congruent to ΔDEF.

questions.text: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3. The difference in the largest and smallest angle is (in degrees):
questions.explanation: 180° in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3 gives angles of 30°, 60° and 90°, so the difference is 90° − 30° = 60°.

questions.text: The income of a person is ₹16,500, and his expenditure is ₹12,000. Next year, his income increases by 24% but his expenditure decreases by 10%. The percentage increase (rounded off to the nearest integer) in his savings is:
If two straight lines are coinciding with each other, then the number of points of intersection is/are:
options: finite number of point of intersection
questions.explanation: Coinciding lines share every point, so they have infinitely many points of intersection.

questions.text: One year ago, the age of B was twice that of A. After 9 years, if the ratio of the ages of B and A would be 4 ∶ 3, then the sum of their present ages is _____ years.
questions.explanation: B − 1 = 2(A − 1) gives B = 2A − 1, and 3(B + 9) = 4(A + 9) gives 3B = 4A + 9. So 6A − 3 = 4A + 9, A = 6 and B = 11: 17 years.

questions.text: Pipe A can fill a cistern in 4 hours and Pipe B can fill the same cistern in 5 hours. Pipe C can empty a full cistern in 3 hours. If all three pipes are opened together, then the time (in minutes) taken to fill the tank is: (round to the nearest minute)
questions.explanation: Together the pipes fill 1/4 + 1/5 − 1/3 = 7/60 of the cistern an hour, so it takes 60/7 hours = 3,600/7 ≈ 514 minutes.

questions.text: A policeman is chasing a thief at a speed of 82 km/h. The thief is 1300 m away and is running at a speed of 64 km/h. In how much time will the policeman catch the thief if both are riding on bikes?
questions.explanation: The policeman gains 82 − 64 = 18 km/h = 5 m/s on the thief, so he closes 1,300 m in 1,300/5 = 260 seconds.

questions.text: Ramu lent ₹3,000 to Raju and a certain sum to Ravi at the same time and at the same rate of simple interest of 8% per annum. After 5 years, he received a sum of ₹1,600 from Raju and Ravi together as interest. Find the sum lent to Ravi.
The ratio of two numbers is 2 : 5 and their difference is 210. The smaller number is ____________.
questions.explanation: The numbers are 2x and 5x, so 3x = 210, x = 70 and the smaller number is 140.

questions.text: A line cuts two concentric circles. The length of chords formed by this line on the circles is 6 cm and 18 cm. Find the difference in the squares of the radii of two circles.
questions.explanation: Both chords lie on one line, at the same distance d from the centre, and the perpendicular from the centre bisects each. So r₁² = d² + 9² and r₂² = d² + 3², and r₁² − r₂² = 81 − 9 = 72.

questions.text: The ratio of the length, the breadth, and the height of a solid cuboid is given as 3 : 2 : 1, and the breadth of this cuboid is given as 12 cm. Find the volume (in cm³) of the cuboid.
questions.explanation: The breadth, 12 cm, is 2 parts, so one part is 6 cm: 18 × 12 × 6 = 1,296 cm³.

questions.text: A class of 30 students appeared in a test. The average score of 12 students is 62, and that of the rest is 78. What is the average score of the class?
If the market price of a bag is 25% above the cost price, and a discount of 18% is declared on it, then find the gain percentage.
questions.explanation: With a cost price of 100, the marked price is 125 and the selling price 125 × 0.82 = 102.5: a gain of 2.5%.

questions.text: If 436P5 is divisible by 3, then the largest value of P is:
questions.explanation: The digit sum 4 + 3 + 6 + P + 5 = 18 + P must be a multiple of 3, so P is 0, 3, 6 or 9. The largest digit is 9.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank. After months of dedication and effort, I finally completed the marathon. I can really _______________ for this accomplishment.
options: up a creek without a paddle
questions.explanation: To 'pat oneself on the back' is to congratulate oneself on an achievement.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Grotesque
questions.explanation: 'Grotesque' means repulsively ugly or distorted: 'ugly'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. We, as human beings, have a tendency of believing in the “things that can be seen and touched”.
questions.explanation: 'Tangible' means able to be touched, real and concrete; 'impalpable' is its opposite.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelled sentence.
questions.explanation: The correct spellings are 'restaurant' and 'delicious'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Loving
questions.explanation: 'Loving' means showing warmth and care: 'affectionate'. 'Offish' (aloof) is nearly its opposite.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. Essence or main point of any passage, lecture or book
questions.explanation: The 'gist' is the essence or main point of a text or speech.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Arushya purchased “the most good” of all the suits kept in the shop.
questions.explanation: 'Good' compares irregularly (good, better, best), so its superlative is 'the best', not 'the most good'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. The chef prepares the meal with great care.
options: The meal has been prepared with great care by the chef.
The meal will be prepared with great care by the chef.
The meal is prepared with great care by the chef.
The meal was prepared with great care by the chef.
questions.explanation: The simple present 'prepares' becomes 'is prepared' in the passive, with the chef as the agent.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the following sentence in active voice. The novels of Dickens are being read by Mayank.
options: Mayank had been reading the novels of Dickens.
Mayank is reading the novels of Dickens.
Mayank was reading the novels of Dickens.
Mayank has been reading the novels of Dickens.
questions.explanation: 'Are being read' is the present continuous passive, so the active is 'is reading': 'Mayank is reading the novels of Dickens.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in brackets to fill in the blanks. The soldiers spent long period ________ (convalescing).
questions.explanation: To 'convalesce' is to recover one's health after an illness or injury.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Even if you’ve never heard his name, you’ve probably met someone with his words “tattooed in their skin” or heard them sung at a music concert.
questions.explanation: Words are tattooed 'on' the skin, not 'in' it.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The lions became violently / when the visitors / started throwing / stones at them.
questions.explanation: 'Become' is a linking verb and takes an adjective: 'The lions became violent', not 'violently'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Necessary
questions.explanation: 'Necessary' means needed or required: 'essential'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Intelligible
questions.explanation: 'Intelligible' means able to be understood; its opposite is 'incoherent', unclear and hard to follow.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'unforeseen'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Fear of snakes
questions.explanation: Ophidiophobia is the fear of snakes (Greek 'ophis', snake). Claustrophobia is the fear of closed spaces and xenophobia the fear of foreigners.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Evoke
questions.explanation: To 'evoke' a feeling or response is to bring it about: 'induce'.

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. A. at the same time giving happiness to the poor B. by providing them with food, clothes, money or grain C. festivals in India are celebrated to share happiness D. by being in the presence of the members of the family and
questions.explanation: 'Festivals in India are celebrated to share happiness (C) by being in the presence of the members of the family and (D) at the same time giving happiness to the poor (A) by providing them with food, clothes, money or grain (B).'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence. The leader of the Legislative Assembly won the hearts of the members through his “maiden speech” during the session in state council.
questions.explanation: A 'maiden speech' is a member's first speech in a legislature.

questions.text: The given sentence is divided into four segments. Select the option that has the segment with a grammatical error. Jerry driving / home late / when the incident / took place.
questions.explanation: The past continuous needs its auxiliary: 'Jerry was driving home late when the incident took place.'

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option, in the questions that follow, to fill in each blank. Listening starts with hearing but goes (1)___________. Hearing, in other words, is necessary, but is not a sufficient (2)___________ for listening. Listening involves hearing with attention. Listening is a process that (3)___________ concentration. While listening, one should also be observant. In other words, listening has to do with the ears, (4)____________ with the eyes and the mind. Listening is to be understood as the total process that involves hearing with attention, being observant and making interpretations. Good communication is essentially a/an (5)___________ process.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Listening starts with hearing but 'goes beyond' it: it involves more than hearing.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option, in the questions that follow, to fill in each blank. Listening starts with hearing but goes (1)___________. Hearing, in other words, is necessary, but is not a sufficient (2)___________ for listening. Listening involves hearing with attention. Listening is a process that (3)___________ concentration. While listening, one should also be observant. In other words, listening has to do with the ears, (4)____________ with the eyes and the mind. Listening is to be understood as the total process that involves hearing with attention, being observant and making interpretations. Good communication is essentially a/an (5)___________ process.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Hearing is 'necessary, but not a sufficient condition' for listening.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option, in the questions that follow, to fill in each blank. Listening starts with hearing but goes (1)___________. Hearing, in other words, is necessary, but is not a sufficient (2)___________ for listening. Listening involves hearing with attention. Listening is a process that (3)___________ concentration. While listening, one should also be observant. In other words, listening has to do with the ears, (4)____________ with the eyes and the mind. Listening is to be understood as the total process that involves hearing with attention, being observant and making interpretations. Good communication is essentially a/an (5)___________ process.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Listening is a process that 'calls for', that is requires, concentration.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option, in the questions that follow, to fill in each blank. Listening starts with hearing but goes (1)___________. Hearing, in other words, is necessary, but is not a sufficient (2)___________ for listening. Listening involves hearing with attention. Listening is a process that (3)___________ concentration. While listening, one should also be observant. In other words, listening has to do with the ears, (4)____________ with the eyes and the mind. Listening is to be understood as the total process that involves hearing with attention, being observant and making interpretations. Good communication is essentially a/an (5)___________ process.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: Listening has to do with the ears 'as well as' with the eyes and the mind: all three together.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option, in the questions that follow, to fill in each blank. Listening starts with hearing but goes (1)___________. Hearing, in other words, is necessary, but is not a sufficient (2)___________ for listening. Listening involves hearing with attention. Listening is a process that (3)___________ concentration. While listening, one should also be observant. In other words, listening has to do with the ears, (4)____________ with the eyes and the mind. Listening is to be understood as the total process that involves hearing with attention, being observant and making interpretations. Good communication is essentially a/an (5)___________ process.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Communication needs both a speaker and an attentive listener, so it is an 'interactive' process.

questions.text: Based on the position in the English alphabetical order, three of the following letter-clusters are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the odd letter-cluster. Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter cluster.
questions.explanation: In every cluster the second letter is 3 after the first. In TWGD, JMQN and MPNK the fourth letter is also 3 before the third (G → D, Q → N, N → K); in PSKI it is only 2 before (K → I), so PSKI is the odd one.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? JHOQ, NFSO, ? , VBAK, ZZEI
questions.explanation: First letters move forward 4 (J, N, R, V, Z), second letters back 2 (H, F, D, B, Z), third letters forward 4 (O, S, W, A, E) and fourth letters back 2 (Q, O, M, K, I): RDWM.

questions.text: Select the number that will come in the place of the question mark(?), if ‘+’ and ‘ – ‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged 63 × 7 ÷ 13 – 64 + 42 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 63 ÷ 7 × 13 + 64 − 42 = 117 + 64 − 42 = 139.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'RADIO' is written as 'SZEHP' and 'FREQUENCY' is written as 'GQFPVDOBZ'. How will 'TELEVISION' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Letters move +1 and −1 in turn: R → S, A → Z, D → E, I → H, O → P. So TELEVISION → U D M D W H T H P M: UDMDWHTHPM.

questions.text: Three of the following numbers are alike in a certain way and one is different. Pick the odd one out. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The third number is 9 times the difference of the first two: (18 − 11) × 9 = 63, (12 − 8) × 9 = 36 and (15 − 3) × 9 = 108. But (21 − 14) × 9 = 63, not 72.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that, when placed from left to right in the blanks below, will complete the letter series. S _ Y A _ F I K M _ S U W
questions.explanation: The letters move +3, +3, +2, +2 in turn: S V Y A C F I K M P S U W. The blanks are V, C and P.

questions.text: Find the correct combination of letters that when sequentially filled in the blanks of the given series will make the series logically complete. ABF_HI_NOP_U_WABCDH_
questions.explanation: Filled in, the series reads AB FGHI MNOP TUVW ABCD HI: runs of consecutive letters with three skipped between them (CDE, JKL, QRS, XYZ, EFG). The blanks are G, M, T, V and I.

questions.text: Select the triad in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the given triads. (25, 22, 47), (31, 24, 55) (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: The third number is the sum of the first two: 25 + 22 = 47 and 31 + 24 = 55. Likewise 18 + 21 = 39.

questions.text: The position of how many letters will remain unchanged if all the letters in the word MOBILE are arranged in English alphabetical order?
questions.explanation: MOBILE rearranged is BEILMO. Position by position (M/B, O/E, B/I, I/L, L/M, E/O), no letter stays in its place.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 25 + 3 ÷ 9 −14 × 2 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 25 − 3 × 9 + 14 ÷ 2 = 25 − 27 + 7 = 5.

questions.text: Select the word-pair that best represents a similar relationship to the one expressed in the pair of words given below. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must NOT be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) France : Gallic Rooster
questions.explanation: The Gallic rooster is a national symbol of France, as the emu is of Australia. India's national bird is the peacock, New Zealand's is the kiwi, and Germany's emblem is an eagle.

questions.text: 12 is related to 235 by certain logic. Following the same logic, 14 is related to 287. To which of the following is 18 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The number is the square plus 91: 12² + 91 = 235 and 14² + 91 = 287. So 18² + 91 = 324 + 91 = 415.

questions.text: Select the option that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. BH14, CJ17, DL20, EN23, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move forward 1 (B, C, D, E, F), second letters forward 2 (H, J, L, N, P) and the numbers go up by 3 (14, 17, 20, 23, 26): FP26.

questions.text: All the alphabets in the word ‘DICTIONARY’ are arranged in the alphabetical order. How many alphabets are there in the English alphabetical series between the alphabet which is fourth from the left end and the one which is second from the right end in the newly formed letter-cluster?
questions.explanation: DICTIONARY in alphabetical order is A C D I I N O R T Y. The fourth from the left is I and the second from the right is T; between them come J to S: ten letters.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘BOTH’ is written as ‘DQVJ’ and ‘DARE’ is written as ‘FCTG’ How will ‘WILL’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places forward: BOTH → DQVJ and DARE → FCTG. So WILL → YKNN.

questions.text: If ‘A & Z’ means ‘A is the brother of Z’, ‘A # Z’ means ‘A is the sister of Z’, ‘A ^ Z’ means ‘A is the brother of Z’s father’, ‘A @ Z’ means ‘A is the wife of Z’, ‘A % Z’ means ‘A is the mother of Z’, ‘A α Z’ means ‘A is the father of Z’, then how is J related to Z in the following expression? J % K # L @ M α N & Z
questions.explanation: J is K's mother, K is L's sister, L is M's wife, M is N's father and N is Z's brother. So M is Z's father and L is Z's mother; J, the mother of L's sister, is L's mother: Z's mother's mother.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 389, 420, 457, 498, 541, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are consecutive primes: 31, 37, 41, 43, so the next is 47: 541 + 47 = 588.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of numbers. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 40 : 123 63 : 192
questions.explanation: The second number is three times the first plus 3: 40 × 3 + 3 = 123 and 63 × 3 + 3 = 192. Likewise 39 × 3 + 3 = 120.

questions.text: Which of the following is related to neem?
questions.explanation: Neem has pinnately compound leaves: the leaflets sit along a common axis, the rachis. In palmately compound leaves, such as silk cotton's, the leaflets spread from one point.

questions.text: For which film did Asha Bhosle win the International Indian Film Academy (IIFA) Award in the Best Playback Singer Female category in 2002?
questions.explanation: Asha Bhosle won the 2002 IIFA Award for Best Female Playback Singer for 'Radha Kaise Na Jale' from Lagaan.

questions.text: What is the duration of monsoon in India?
questions.explanation: NCERT puts the duration of the monsoon at 100-120 days, from early June to mid-September.

questions.text: The northern plain of the Indian subcontinent has been formed by the interplay of the three major river systems along with their tributaries. Choose the odd one out of the options given.
questions.explanation: The northern plain was formed by the Indus, the Ganga and the Brahmaputra with their tributaries. The Godavari is a river of the peninsula.

questions.text: Which of the following is mentioned in Article 1 of the Indian constitution?
options: India that is Bharat as parliamentary democracy
India that is Bharat as federation of states
India that is Bharat shall be a Union of states
India that is Bharat as presidential form of democracy
questions.explanation: Article 1(1) reads: 'India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States.'

questions.text: Who holds the record for the longest long jump in India as of 2023?
questions.explanation: Jeswin Aldrin set the national record of 8.42 m at Ballari, Karnataka, in March 2023, beating Murali Sreeshankar's 8.36 m.

questions.text: Name the phenomenon where an opaque object on the path of light becomes very small and where light has a tendency to bend around it and not walk in a straight line.
questions.explanation: When an opaque object in the path of light is very small, light bends around it instead of travelling in a straight line: diffraction.

questions.text: Articles 52 to 78 in Part V of the Indian Constitution deal with __________.
questions.explanation: Articles 52 to 78, Chapter I of Part V, deal with the Union Executive: the President, the Vice-President, the Council of Ministers and the Attorney-General.

questions.text: What is the position of India in the world’s telecommunication market, as of March 2024?
questions.explanation: India is the world's second-largest telecommunications market, after China, with over a billion subscribers.

questions.text: The National Youth Policy was launched in:
questions.explanation: The National Youth Policy 2014 was launched in February 2014; it defines youth as people aged 15 to 29.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following was the President of the Belgaum Session of the Indian National Congress held in 1924?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi presided over the Belgaum session of 1924, the only Congress session he presided over.

questions.text: Ali Akbar Khan is known for playing the ________.
questions.explanation: Ustad Ali Akbar Khan, son of Allauddin Khan, was a master of the sarod.

questions.text: Consider the following statements related to the Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) handbook. 1.It will be launched by the Ministry of Science and Technology. 2.ODR is the resolution for cases outside courts using digital technology and techniques of Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR), such as negotiation, mediation and arbitration. 3.The development of ICT and increased use of internet has played a major role for ODR. Which of the given statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The ODR handbook was launched by NITI Aayog in April 2021, not by the Ministry of Science and Technology, so statement 1 is wrong. Statements 2 and 3 are correct.

questions.text: The Flexible Inflation Targeting Framework (FITF) was introduced in India post the amendment of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Act, 1934 in __________.
questions.explanation: The RBI Act was amended in 2016 to give flexible inflation targeting a statutory basis: the government sets the target (4% CPI inflation, within 2 to 6%) and the Monetary Policy Committee pursues it.

questions.text: The government of which of the following states allocated ₹11,728 crore for the Aasara pension scheme in its annual budget for the fiscal year 2022-23?
questions.explanation: Telangana's 2022-23 budget set aside ₹11,728 crore for its Aasara pensions, paid to the elderly, widows, people with disabilities and others.

questions.text: ‘Atla Taddi’ is the widely celebrated festival of which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Atla Taddi is kept by the women of Andhra Pradesh on the third day after the full moon of Aswayuja; it is often compared to Karva Chauth.

questions.text: Which national park in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands is home to species like Megapode, crab-eating Macaque, Nicobar Pigeon, and Giant Robber Crab?
questions.explanation: Campbell Bay National Park, on Great Nicobar, is home to the megapode, crab-eating macaque, Nicobar pigeon and giant robber crab. Raimona is in Assam, Mouling in Arunachal Pradesh and Papikonda in Andhra Pradesh.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The Permanent Settlement came into operation in which of the following years?
questions.explanation: Lord Cornwallis introduced the Permanent Settlement of Bengal in 1793, fixing the zamindars' land revenue in perpetuity.

questions.text: Which part of the Constitution deals with the Panchayats?
questions.explanation: Part IX, added by the 73rd Amendment (1992), deals with the Panchayats.

questions.text: Which of the following battles was fought between Babur and Rana Sanga in 1527?
questions.explanation: Babur defeated Rana Sanga of Mewar at Khanwa in March 1527.

questions.text: Which among the following was NOT a part of the three sections of the Rigvedic tribe?
questions.explanation: The Rigvedic tribe was divided into warriors, priests and ordinary people; a fourth division, the shudras, appeared only towards the end of the Rigvedic period.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is/are correct? i. The first green revolution led to over-exploitation of natural resources. ii. The second Green Revolution was more focused on Southern India. iii. The second green revolution ensured in achieving sustainable livelihood security.
questions.explanation: The first Green Revolution's intensive farming over-exploited groundwater and soil, and the second aims at sustainable livelihood security. Statement ii is wrong: the second Green Revolution is aimed at eastern India, which the first largely missed.

questions.text: In which of the following states of India is Hojagiri dance predominantly performed?
questions.explanation: Hojagiri is a dance of the Reang (Bru) community of Tripura, performed by women balancing on pitchers with lamps on their heads.

questions.text: A chemical reaction in which the rate of reaction is directly proportional to the first power of the concentration of the reacting substance is called:
questions.explanation: In a first-order reaction the rate is proportional to the concentration of one reactant raised to the power one: rate = k[A].

questions.text: Where was the 1st World Cup of Kabaddi organised in 2004?
questions.explanation: The first Kabaddi World Cup was held in Mumbai in November 2004; India beat Iran in the final.

questions.text: 10 years ago, the age of Sunita was thrice the age of her daughter Tanya. 10 years hence, the age of Sunita will be twice the age of Tanya. What is the ratio of their present ages?
questions.explanation: Sunita − 10 = 3(Tanya − 10) and Sunita + 10 = 2(Tanya + 10), so 3T − 20 = 2T + 10. Tanya is 30 and Sunita 70: 7 : 3.

questions.text: A thief is noticed by a policeman from a distance of 92 m. The thief starts running and the policeman chases him. The thief and the policeman run at the speed of 90 km/h and 104.4 km/h, respectively. In how much time will the policeman catch the thief?
questions.explanation: The policeman gains 104.4 − 90 = 14.4 km/h = 4 m/s on the thief, so he closes 92 m in 92/4 = 23 seconds.

questions.text: R targets to score 85% marks in exams. He scores 450 marks and misses the target by 35%. How much increment in percentage should be there in his scored marks to meet the target?
questions.explanation: SSC's key reads the 35% as percentage points of the total: missing 85% by 35 points, he scored 50%, so 450 marks are half of 900. The target is 85% of 900 = 765, so he needs 315 more, which is 315/450 = 70% of his score.

questions.text: In the following sets, which set represents the sides of a right-angled triangle?
questions.explanation: 5² + 12² = 25 + 144 = 169 = 13², so these sides satisfy Pythagoras' theorem. The others fail: 25 + 100 ≠ 144, 9 + 16 ≠ 36 and 64 + 225 ≠ 256.

questions.text: The difference between the simple interests on the principal of ₹500 at an interest rate of 5% per annum for 3 years and 4% per annum for 4 years is:

Aman has certain number of notes of denomination ₹20 and ₹10 which amount to ₹390. If the numbers of notes of each kind are interchanged, then the new amount is ₹90 less than before. Find the number of notes of ₹20 denomination.
questions.explanation: With x notes of ₹20 and y of ₹10: 20x + 10y = 390 and 10x + 20y = 300. Adding gives x + y = 23 and subtracting x − y = 9, so x = 16.

questions.text: A tank can be filled by pipe A in 4 hours and pipe B in 6 hours. At 8:00 a.m., pipe A was opened. At what time will the tank be filled if pipe B is opened at 9:00 a.m.?
questions.explanation: By 9:00 a.m. pipe A has filled 1/4. Together the pipes fill 1/4 + 1/6 = 5/12 an hour, so the remaining 3/4 takes (3/4) ÷ (5/12) = 9/5 hours = 1 hour 48 minutes: 10:48 a.m.

questions.text: A triangle ABC is made on a circle, where AB is diameter of the circle. If BC is equal to the radius of the circle and ∠ABC = x ∠BAC, then x is :
questions.explanation: The angle in a semicircle is 90°, so ∠ACB = 90°. With BC = r and AB = 2r, sin ∠BAC = 1/2, so ∠BAC = 30° and ∠ABC = 60° = 2 × ∠BAC.

questions.text: Amit and Bilal buy goods for ₹1,500 and ₹2,000, respectively. Amit marks his goods up by y%, while Bilal marks his goods up by 2y% and offers a discount of y%. If both make the same profit, then find the value of y.
questions.explanation: Amit's profit is 1,500 × y/100 = 15y. Bilal sells at 2,000(1 + 2y/100)(1 − y/100) = 2,000 + 20y − 0.4y², a profit of 20y − 0.4y². Setting 15y = 20y − 0.4y² gives 0.4y = 5, so y = 12.5.

questions.text: 30 is the mean proportional of 18 and A. Find the value of A.
questions.explanation: The mean proportional of 18 and A satisfies 30² = 18 × A, so A = 900/18 = 50.

questions.text: A trader offers the following discount schemes on the purchase of a refrigerator. ( I ) a discount of 10% followed by a discount of 8% ( ii ) successive discounts of 12% and 10% ( iii ) two successive discounts of 12% ( iv ) a discount of 20% In which scheme is the selling price the lowest?
questions.explanation: The fraction of the price paid: (i) 0.9 × 0.92 = 0.828, (ii) 0.88 × 0.9 = 0.792, (iii) 0.88 × 0.88 = 0.7744, (iv) 0.8. Scheme (iii) leaves the lowest price.

questions.text: For what least value of n, 2²ⁿ + 2n is completely divided by 6, where n is an integer?
questions.explanation: For n = 0 the value is 2⁰ + 0 = 1, which 6 does not divide. For n = 1 it is 2² + 2 = 6, so the least value is 1.

questions.text: There is a 32 l mixture of milk and water. The ratio of milk and water in this mixture is 5 : 3. How many litres of water should be added to this mixture so that the resultant mixture has 50% water in it?
questions.explanation: The mixture has 20 l of milk and 12 l of water. For 50% water the water must equal the milk, 20 l, so 8 l must be added.

questions.text: Let x = r cos (t), y = r sin (t) cos (u), z = r sin (t)sin (u). Then the value of x² + y² + z² is ___.
questions.explanation: y² + z² = r² sin²(t)(cos²(u) + sin²(u)) = r² sin²(t), so x² + y² + z² = r² cos²(t) + r² sin²(t) = r².

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. (O) attitude is (P) or tendency in individuals (Q) a broad-based behaviour (R) which implies (S) a hypothetical postulate
questions.explanation: 'Attitude is (O) a hypothetical postulate (S) which implies (R) a broad-based behaviour (Q) or tendency in individuals (P).'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Off and on
questions.explanation: 'Off and on' means from time to time, intermittently: 'now and then'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The food intolerance industry has grown dramatically in the previous decade, “chiefly because of a boost” in Coeliac and Crohn’s disease cases, as well as increasing awareness among health-conscious clients.
options: pretty much entirely because of a boil-down
questions.explanation: A 'boost' is a welcome lift, which does not suit disease cases; 'owing primarily to a rise' keeps the sense of 'chiefly because of' with the right word for an increase.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. I have booked an apartment in the new residential colony.
options: An apartment had been booked by me in the new residential colony.
An apartment have been booked by me in the new residential colony.
An apartment has been booked by me in the new residential colony.
An apartment is been booked by me in the new residential colony.
questions.explanation: The present perfect 'have booked' becomes 'has been booked', agreeing with the singular 'an apartment'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Speaking disrespectfully about sacred or religious things.
questions.explanation: Blasphemy is speaking disrespectfully about God or sacred things. An atheist does not believe in God; a theist does.

questions.text: Identify the error in the following sentence. Ourselves should not boast of one’s knowledge.
questions.explanation: A reflexive pronoun cannot be the subject, and 'one's' later in the sentence calls for 'One': 'One should not boast of one's knowledge.'

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct logical sequence. A. These are responsible for producing the major fuel used across the globe. B. The country has 100 major oil and gas fields. C. The economy of Saudi Arabia is based on petroleum. D. The chief oil field is Ghawar Field having an estimated 70 billion reserve resource.
questions.explanation: C introduces Saudi Arabia's oil economy, B its 100 oil and gas fields, A what 'these' fields produce, and D names the chief field, Ghawar: CBAD.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate homonyms from the given alternatives to fill in the blanks. The rowing instructor commanded them to ________ in a ________. A.row (verb) B.roe C.row (sequence)
questions.explanation: They were told to 'row' (move a boat with oars) in a 'row' (a line): A, then C. 'Roe' is fish eggs.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined word segment in the given sentence. Sanat has just arrived in Mysore on transfer; he requests his friend Raghu to help him find “an appropriate location”.
questions.explanation: Someone who has just moved to a city on transfer needs somewhere to live: 'a rented accommodation'. 'An appropriate location' does not say what he is looking for.

questions.text: The given sentence is divided into four segments. Select the option that has the segment with a grammatical error. Two of the world’s / best forwards / has played alongside / David Beckham.
questions.explanation: The subject 'Two of the world's best forwards' is plural, so 'have played', not 'has played'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Brittle
questions.explanation: 'Brittle' means hard but easily broken: 'fragile'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Cherish
questions.explanation: To 'cherish' is to care for lovingly: to 'nurture'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Adequate
questions.explanation: 'Adequate' means enough for the purpose: 'sufficient'.

questions.text: Select the option that contains all the MISSPELT words in the following sentences. 1. The new restraunt offers a wide variety of delicious dishes. 2. I can't beleive he made such a silly mistake in his presentation. 3. The teacher asked the students to complete the assigment by Friday. 4. She felt utterly embarassed by her colleague’s comments.
questions.explanation: The correct spellings are 'restaurant', 'believe', 'assignment' and 'embarrassed'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. At a low ebb
options: In a depressed or weak state
questions.explanation: 'At a low ebb' means in a weak or depressed state, like the tide at its lowest.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. The teenager delivered the speech.
options: The speech has been delivered by the teenager.
The speech was delivered by the teenager.
The speech was being delivered by the teenager.
The speech is delivered by the teenager.
questions.explanation: The simple past 'delivered' becomes 'was delivered': 'The speech was delivered by the teenager.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. This book “giving us much information” about our freedom fighters who lost their lives while serving our motherland.
questions.explanation: The sentence needs a finite verb agreeing with the singular 'This book': 'gives'. 'Information' is uncountable, so 'much', not 'many'.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word to fill in the blank. My mother said that every relationship must have some amount of ___________.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'flexibility'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Material
questions.explanation: 'Material' means physical, made of matter; its opposite is 'abstract'. 'Concrete' is close to a synonym.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Culture is (1)_______, understanding, and protecting, like the cultivation of a garden, not the destruction or eradication of its roots. Understanding the roots and seeds, taking much care and providing instructed nourishment (2)_______ important for good gardening. Culture also is similar; understanding its acquaintance (3)______ literature and art and careful protection are required. Culture is the way of life of a particular society in which a group of people live together in one place. The society’s culture is visible in its literature, arts, social system, language and religion. It is a combination of traditions, customs, institutions, food habits, manners, morals, thoughts, tastes, views and beliefs. Usually, families (4)______ culture to the younger generations. As family system is becoming weak, schools, colleges and universities should take up this responsibility as education should promote potential values of its culture. The role of universities (5)_______ only to issue course completed certificates.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'Creating, understanding, and protecting': the gerund matches the other two in the list.
