Choose the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
questions.explanation: Singing is an 'intricate' art, 'a highly refined one' that needs strict training.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that, when sequentially placed from left to right in the blanks below, will complete the letter series. _ Y R W I Y _ X I _ R _ I Y R Z
questions.explanation: With I, R, Y, Y in the blanks the series is IYRW IYRX IYRY IYRZ: IYR, followed by W, X, Y and Z in turn.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘cat dog monkey’ is coded as ‘55 66 88’; ‘camel cat donkey’ is coded as ‘66 99 33’ and ‘dog goat tiger’ is coded as ‘88 11 22’. How is ‘monkey’ coded in that language?
questions.explanation: 'cat' is in the first two phrases and '66' in the first two codes, so cat = 66; 'dog' is in the first and third, as is '88', so dog = 88. That leaves monkey = 55.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 45, 52, 63, 76, 93, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are consecutive prime numbers: 7, 11, 13, 17. The next is 19: 93 + 19 = 112.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. MSD: NHW :: OAE : LZV :: NIP:?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite in the alphabet (their places add up to 27): M ↔ N, S ↔ H, D ↔ W and O ↔ L, A ↔ Z, E ↔ V. So NIP → MRK.

questions.text: The position(s) of how many letters will remain unchanged if all the letters in the word ‘LAUNDER’ are arranged in English alphabetical order?
questions.explanation: LAUNDER in alphabetical order is A D E L N R U. Compared place by place with L A U N D E R, no letter stays where it was.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 152 ÷ 6 + 1617 × 7 – 77 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 152 × 6 − 1617 ÷ 7 + 77 = 912 − 231 + 77 = 758.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'WJSL' is coded as '25-12-21-14' and 'DUOH' is coded as '6-23-17-10'. What is the code for 'PFKR' in the given language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is coded as its place in the alphabet plus 2: W (23) → 25, J (10) → 12, S (19) → 21, L (12) → 14. So P, F, K, R (16, 6, 11, 18) → 18-8-13-20.

questions.text: 13 is related to 21 following certain logic. Following the same logic, 35 is related to 43. To which of the following numbers is 66 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is the first plus 8: 13 + 8 = 21 and 35 + 8 = 43. Likewise 66 + 8 = 74.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter cluster in the same way as the second letter cluster is related to the first letter cluster and the fourth letter cluster is related to the third letter cluster. EXPENSE : EPXEESN :: FASHION : HSAFNOI :: FORTUNE : ?
questions.explanation: The first four letters are reversed, then the last three: EXPE|NSE → EPXE|ESN and FASH|ION → HSAF|NOI. So FORT|UNE → TROF|ENU: TROFENU.

questions.text: The question contains pairs of words that are related to each other in a certain way. Three of the following four word pairs are alike as these have the same relationship and thus form a group. Which word pair is the one that DOES NOT belong to that group? (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word.)
questions.explanation: Polo is played four a side, and boxing and chess one against one. A football team has 11 players, not 10, so that pair does not belong.

questions.text: Three of the following number-pairs are alike in some manner and hence form a group. Which number-pair does not belong to that group? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In 12 – 156, 21 – 462 and 17 – 306 the second number is the first times the next number (12 × 13, 21 × 22, 17 × 18). 14 – 196 is 14 × 14, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Which two numbers (not digits) should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 6 × 3 + 8 ÷ 2 + 21 + 5 × 4 – 14 ÷ 7 = 53

Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the given sets. (6, 31) (10, 91) (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: The second number is the square of the first, minus the first, plus 1: 6² − 6 + 1 = 31 and 10² − 10 + 1 = 91. Likewise 8² − 8 + 1 = 57.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will logically complete the series. ME_ICM_DIC_GDI_MHD_C
questions.explanation: With D, F, M, C, I in the blanks the series is MEDIC MFDIC MGDIC MHDIC: M, then E, F, G and H in turn, then DIC.

questions.text: 21 is related to 220 by certain logic. Following the same logic, 72 is related to 781. To which of the following is 27 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is 11 times one less than the first: 20 × 11 = 220 and 71 × 11 = 781. Likewise 26 × 11 = 286.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'A & B' means ‘ A is the brother of B’, 'A x B' means ‘A is the father of B’, 'A ? B' means ‘A is the mother of B’ and 'A ! B' means ‘A is the wife of B’. Which of the following means that W is the mother's mother of P?
options: W & R ! Y x O ? P
W ? R x Y ! O & P
W ? R ! Y & O x P
W ! R x Y ? O & P
questions.explanation: W is R's wife and R is Y's father, so W is Y's mother. Y is O's mother and O is P's brother, so Y is P's mother: W is P's mother's mother.

questions.text: Digestion of food is an important function of the animal body. In animals like lions, cows, humans, etc., the process involves use of various organs starting from the mouth and ending with the anus. The longest part of this canal is known as the ________.
questions.explanation: The small intestine is the longest part of the alimentary canal; much of digestion and absorption takes place there.

questions.text: Who among the following is known as ‘Captain Cool’ in Indian Cricket?
questions.explanation: Mahendra Singh Dhoni is called 'Captain Cool' for his calm captaincy.

questions.text: Papanasam Ramayya Sivan was an Indian composer of which music style?
questions.explanation: Papanasam Sivan was a composer of Carnatic music, mostly in Tamil, and is sometimes called the 'Tamil Thyagaraja'.

questions.text: Which of the following is a difference between self-help groups (SHGs) and microfinance institutions (MFIs) in India?
options: SHGs provide only credit, while MFIs provide a range of financial services.
SHGs rely on government subsidies for funding, while MFIs rely on commercial sources of funding.
SHGs are typically small, community-based organisations, while MFIs are larger and more formal institutions.
SHGs are non-profit organisations, while MFIs are for-profit organisations.
questions.explanation: Self-help groups are small, informal groups, usually of 10 to 20 people from one community, who pool their savings and lend to one another; microfinance institutions are larger, formally registered lenders.

questions.text: Which famous experiment was done by Michael Faraday in 1831?
questions.explanation: In 1831 Michael Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction: a changing magnetic field produces a current in a nearby conductor.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The book ‘Poverty and Un-British Rule in India’ was written by _______.
questions.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji's 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' (1901) set out his drain theory: that British rule was draining India's wealth.

questions.text: Where was the first meeting of the Employment Working Group of G20 conducted?
questions.explanation: The first G20 Employment Working Group meeting of India's presidency was held in Jodhpur, Rajasthan, on 2 to 4 February 2023.

questions.text: In which of the following states is the Chu-Faat dance performed?
questions.explanation: Chu-Faat is a Lepcha dance of Sikkim, performed in honour of Mount Khangchendzonga and its neighbouring peaks, with the dancers carrying butter lamps.

questions.text: What is the salinity of the Dead Sea (per litre of water)?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 340 grams, the figure usually quoted for the Dead Sea (a salinity of about 34%, nearly ten times the ocean's). NCERT's geography textbook gives a lower figure, 238 parts per thousand, close to the 240 grams option, so the answer depends on the source.

questions.text: Which of the following is the first Indian woman Grandmaster in Chess?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives S Vijayalakshmi, India's first Woman Grandmaster (WGM, the women's title). The open Grandmaster title was first won by an Indian woman in 2002, by Koneru Humpy, who is not among the options; Harika Dronavalli and R Vaishali won it later.

questions.text: Who reconciled Dalton's atomic hypothesis with Gay-Lussac's results on the combination of volumes in 1811?
questions.explanation: In 1811 Amedeo Avogadro proposed that equal volumes of gases at the same temperature and pressure hold equal numbers of molecules, reconciling Dalton's atoms with Gay-Lussac's law of combining volumes.

questions.text: As per the Census of India 2011, the increase in literacy rates for males and females, respectively, as compared to 2001 Census was:
questions.explanation: Census 2011 put literacy at 82.14% for males and 65.46% for females, against 75.26% and 53.67% in 2001: rises of 6.88 and 11.79 percentage points.

questions.text: Which of the following is a festival primarily celebrated in the state of Odisha?
questions.explanation: Raja Parba, a three-day festival in mid-June celebrating womanhood and the earth, belongs to Odisha. Chhath is mainly Bihar's; Me-Dam-Me-Phi (Ahom) and Baishagu (Bodo) are Assam's.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which Act was passed by the British Parliament in the year 1773 AD to regulate the activities of the East India Company?
questions.explanation: The Regulating Act of 1773 was the British Parliament's first step to control the East India Company; it created the post of Governor-General of Bengal. Pitt's India Act followed in 1784.

questions.text: The famous santoor player Pandit Shivkumar Sharma received the ________________________ in the year 1986.
questions.explanation: Pandit Shivkumar Sharma received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1986; the Padma Shri (1991) and the Padma Vibhushan (2001) followed.

questions.text: The Aryans lived in the land known as ‘Sapta Sindhu’ (Land of the Seven Rivers). Which of the following was NOT a part of it?
questions.explanation: Sapta Sindhu, the Rig Vedic land of seven rivers, lay in the north-west: the Indus and its Punjab tributaries such as the Jhelum and the Ravi, with the Saraswati. The Shipra flows in Madhya Pradesh, past Ujjain.

questions.text: Who was the chief coordinator for the G20 summit hosted by India?
questions.explanation: Former Foreign Secretary Harsh Vardhan Shringla was India's Chief G20 Coordinator for its 2023 presidency.

questions.text: Who among the following founded the Pala dynasty in 8th Century CE?
questions.explanation: Gopala, elected king in Bengal around 750 CE, founded the Pala dynasty; Dharmapala and Devapala were his successors.

questions.text: The ICAR – Sugarcane Breeding Institute is located at:
questions.explanation: The ICAR-Sugarcane Breeding Institute is at Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu.

questions.text: Who assumed charge as the new Vice Chief of the Indian Navy on 31 July 2021?
questions.explanation: Vice Admiral SN Ghormade took over as Vice Chief of the Naval Staff on 31 July 2021, succeeding Vice Admiral G Ashok Kumar.

questions.text: The number of ministers, including the Chief Minister, in a state shall NOT be less than _______.
questions.explanation: Under Article 164(1A), added by the 91st Amendment (2003), a state's council of ministers, Chief Minister included, may not exceed 15% of the Assembly's strength and may not be fewer than 12.

questions.text: ____________ Directive principles of State Policy were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976.
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment added four Directive Principles: healthy development of children (Article 39(f)), equal justice and free legal aid (39A), workers' participation in management (43A) and protection of the environment (48A).

questions.text: Who published the logistic equation model of population growth in 1838?
questions.explanation: Pierre François Verhulst published the logistic equation in 1838: a population grows ever more slowly as it nears its environment's carrying capacity.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a major climate control of a place?
questions.explanation: The major controls of a place's climate are latitude, altitude, pressure and winds, distance from the sea, ocean currents and relief. The earth's interior is not one of them.

questions.text: In a team of seven members, the average age of six of the members is 42 years while the age of the seventh member of the team is 36 years more than the average age of all the seven members taken together. Find the age (in years) of the seventh member of the team.
questions.explanation: Let the average of all seven be A. Then 7A = 6 × 42 + (A + 36), so 6A = 288 and A = 48. The seventh member is 48 + 36 = 84.

questions.text: If in a circle a chord of length 14 cm is at a distance of 24 cm from its centre, then the length of the radius of the circle is:
questions.explanation: The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord, so r = √(7² + 24²) = √625 = 25 cm.

questions.text: A boat covers a distance of 55 km downstream in 5 hours while it takes 11 hours to cover the same distance upstream. What is the speed of the boat?
questions.explanation: Downstream speed = 55/5 = 11 km/h and upstream speed = 55/11 = 5 km/h. The boat's speed is their average: (11 + 5)/2 = 8 km/h.

questions.text: A class of 30 students appeared in a test. The average score of 12 students is 62, and that of the rest is 60. What is the average score of the class?

The ratio of the ages of A and B, 3 years ago, was 5 : 7. The ratio of their ages, 13 years from now, will be 9 : 11. If the present age of C is 11 years less than that of B, then the present age of C, in years, is:
In ΔPQR, if 4∠P = 5∠Q = 20∠R, then the value of ∠Q is:
If an employee's income is ₹72,000, the amount he spends is 40% higher than his savings. Therefore, his savings (in ₹) is:
questions.explanation: Spending is 1.4 times the savings, so the income is 2.4 times the savings: 72,000/2.4 = ₹30,000.

questions.text: The number 4,29,714 is divisible by:
questions.explanation: The digit sum, 4 + 2 + 9 + 7 + 1 + 4 = 27, is divisible by 3, and the number is even, so it is divisible by 3 and by 6. It does not end in 0 or 5, and its last two digits, 14, are not divisible by 4.

questions.text: The single discount equivalent to a series discount of 60%, 70% and 80%.
questions.explanation: After the three discounts 0.4 × 0.3 × 0.2 = 0.024 of the price is left: a single discount of 97.6%.

questions.text: A customer pays ₹975 in instalments. The payment is done each month ₹5 less than the previous month. If the first instalment is ₹100, how much time will be taken to pay the entire amount?
questions.explanation: The instalments form an AP 100, 95, 90, ...: n/2 × [200 − 5(n − 1)] = 975 gives n² − 41n + 390 = 0, so n = 15 or 26. At 26 months the last instalments would be negative, so the debt is paid in 15 months.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The “cynical” investors believed in every word the analysts said.
questions.explanation: Investors who believed every word the analysts said were 'credulous', too ready to believe. 'Cynical' and 'distrustful' mean the opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. Her remarks were “relevant” to the discussion.
questions.explanation: 'Relevant' means connected with the matter and fitting; of the options, its opposite is 'inappropriate'. 'Suitable' is close to a synonym.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Lethargic
questions.explanation: 'Lethargic' means sluggish and lacking energy; its opposite is 'active'. 'Languid' is a synonym.

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the parts in the correct sequence to form a meaningful sentence. (P) unlock their potential (Q) empowers individuals to (O) and shape their future (R) the power of education
questions.explanation: 'The power of education (R) empowers individuals to (Q) unlock their potential (P) and shape their future (O).'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Athens was suffering under the rule of “a powerful small group” that had no concern for the people's welfare.
questions.explanation: Rule by a small powerful group is an 'oligarchy'; a monarchy is rule by a king or queen, and a democracy rule by the people.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence. Ranjith failed in all his exams “as he had been addicted of” social media.
options: as he had been addicted to
as he had been addicted at
as he had been addicted on
as he had been addicted in
questions.explanation: One is 'addicted to' something: 'as he had been addicted to social media'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can rectify the incorrectly spelt word in the following sentence. I doubt that these lifts can acommodate 100 people.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'accommodate', with a double 'c' and a double 'm'.

questions.text: Select the sentence that is expressed in passive voice.
options: Children are participating in sand-art competition.
questions.explanation: 'Was delivered' is 'was' + past participle, with the thing acted on as the subject: the passive. The other three sentences are active.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The evening time when the sun has just set and it is almost dark.
questions.explanation: Dusk is the darkening part of the evening just after sunset; dawn and daybreak come at the start of the day.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Dodge
questions.explanation: To 'dodge' something is to evade or 'avoid' it.

questions.text: Select the option with the correct use of future tense.
options: By next December, I will be completed six years in this home.
By next December, I will have been completed six years in this home.
By next December, I will have complete six years in this home.
By next December, I will have completed six years in this home.
questions.explanation: An action that will be finished by a time in the future takes the future perfect, 'will have' + past participle: 'will have completed'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the following sentence. The teammates made several “jibes” at the opponent team members during the interview.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'contradict', the opposite of the verb 'jibe', to agree or be consistent ('his story does not jibe with the facts'). Here, though, 'jibes' is a noun meaning mocking remarks, whose opposite would be praise; 'mockery' is a synonym.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. This year’s budget is unlikely to pass as law since the president’s proposed budgets typically face a “jaundiced eye” but this one has gotten even more scepticism.
questions.explanation: To view something with 'a jaundiced eye' is to regard it with bitterness and suspicion, as the 'scepticism' later in the sentence confirms; of the options, 'resentment' is closest. 'Jaundiced' can also suggest envy, but the sentence is about distrust, not jealousy.

questions.text: Select the correct spelling to fill in the blank. I often fail to ______ remember someone’s name.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'accurately'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. Mr. Suman / asked me / to pack / my luggages.
questions.explanation: 'Luggage' is uncountable and has no plural: 'my luggage'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. Her behaviour was so “ostentatious” that it attracted the attention of everyone in the room.
questions.explanation: 'Ostentatious' means showy, meant to attract notice; its opposite is 'restrained'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the following sentence in passive voice. The baker baked the cake.
options: The cake had been baked by the baker.
The cake has been baked by the baker.
The baker has been baking the cake.
The cake was baked by the baker
questions.explanation: The simple past 'baked' becomes 'was baked': 'The cake was baked by the baker.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A place to park aeroplanes
questions.explanation: A 'hangar' is a building where aircraft are kept; a 'hanger' is for hanging clothes.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Dissipate
questions.explanation: To 'dissipate' money or energy is to spend it, usually wastefully; the word also means to scatter.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence. Sejal visits the nearby temple “off and on”.
questions.explanation: 'Off and on' means now and then, at intervals: 'periodically'. 'Constantly' and 'continuously' mean without a break, and 'regularly' at fixed intervals.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Human Development Index (HDI) is a summary (1) _________ of average accomplishment in important areas of human development, (2) _________ living a long and healthy life, being informed and having a good quality of living. The HDI is the geometric mean of the normalised (3) _________ for each dimension. The health component is (4) _________ by life expectancy at birth, while the education dimension is measured by the average number of years of schooling for individuals aged 25 and above, as well as the (5) _________ number of years of schooling for school-age children.

Select the most appropriate answer for blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The HDI is 'a summary assessment', a single measure, of average achievement.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Human Development Index (HDI) is a summary (1) _________ of average accomplishment in important areas of human development, (2) _________ living a long and healthy life, being informed and having a good quality of living. The HDI is the geometric mean of the normalised (3) _________ for each dimension. The health component is (4) _________ by life expectancy at birth, while the education dimension is measured by the average number of years of schooling for individuals aged 25 and above, as well as the (5) _________ number of years of schooling for school-age children.

Select the most appropriate answer for blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The three areas follow as a list: 'including living a long and healthy life, being informed and having a good quality of living'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Human Development Index (HDI) is a summary (1) _________ of average accomplishment in important areas of human development, (2) _________ living a long and healthy life, being informed and having a good quality of living. The HDI is the geometric mean of the normalised (3) _________ for each dimension. The health component is (4) _________ by life expectancy at birth, while the education dimension is measured by the average number of years of schooling for individuals aged 25 and above, as well as the (5) _________ number of years of schooling for school-age children.

Select the most appropriate answer for blank number 3.
questions.explanation: The HDI is the geometric mean of the normalised 'indices' (plural of 'index') for the three dimensions.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Human Development Index (HDI) is a summary (1) _________ of average accomplishment in important areas of human development, (2) _________ living a long and healthy life, being informed and having a good quality of living. The HDI is the geometric mean of the normalised (3) _________ for each dimension. The health component is (4) _________ by life expectancy at birth, while the education dimension is measured by the average number of years of schooling for individuals aged 25 and above, as well as the (5) _________ number of years of schooling for school-age children.

Select the most appropriate answer for blank number 4.
questions.explanation: The health component is 'measured' by life expectancy at birth, just as the education dimension 'is measured by' years of schooling.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Human Development Index (HDI) is a summary (1) _________ of average accomplishment in important areas of human development, (2) _________ living a long and healthy life, being informed and having a good quality of living. The HDI is the geometric mean of the normalised (3) _________ for each dimension. The health component is (4) _________ by life expectancy at birth, while the education dimension is measured by the average number of years of schooling for individuals aged 25 and above, as well as the (5) _________ number of years of schooling for school-age children.

Select the most appropriate answer for blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Besides the average schooling of adults, the index uses the 'predicted' (expected) years of schooling for school-age children.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? AWSO, KGCY, UQMI, EAWS, ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 10 places forward, wrapping round after Z: A, K, U, E, O; W, G, Q, A, K; S, C, M, W, G; O, Y, I, S, C. The next term is OKGC.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’; ‘A − B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’; ‘A × B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’ and ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the father of B’. Based on the above, how is A related to D if ‘A × B ÷ C × D’?
questions.explanation: A is the wife of B, B is the father of C and C is the wife of D. So A is C's mother, and C is D's wife: A is D's wife's mother.

questions.text: Which number will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 20 + 10 × 2 − 4 ÷ 5 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 20 − 10 ÷ 2 + 4 × 5 = 20 − 5 + 20 = 35.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘TOUGH’ is coded as ‘89251’ and ‘GHOST’ is coded as ‘93258’. What is the code for ‘S’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: T, O, G and H are in both words, as are 8, 9, 2 and 5 in both codes. The letter left in GHOST is S and the digit left in its code is 3, so S = 3.

questions.text: ‘Wander’ is related to ‘Ramble’ in the same way as ‘Stray’ is related to ‘________’. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word.)
questions.explanation: 'Wander' and 'ramble' are synonyms: to move about aimlessly. Of the options only 'random' means the same as 'stray' (a stray remark is a random one).

questions.text: Each of the letters in the word ‘KEYBOARD’ are arranged in the English alphabetical order. How many letters are in the English alphabetical order between the letter which is the third from the right end and the second from the right end in the group of letters thus formed?
questions.explanation: KEYBOARD in alphabetical order is A B D E K O R Y. The third from the right is O and the second from the right is R; between them come P and Q: two letters.

questions.text: ‘RUCK’ is related to ‘TWAI’ in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, ‘DPHM’ is related to ‘FRFK’. To which of the following is ‘KNOM’ related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: The first two letters move 2 places forward and the last two move 2 places back: RUCK → TWAI and DPHM → FRFK. So KNOM → MPMK.

questions.text: Two sets of numbers are given below. In each set of numbers, certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number result(s) in the second number. Similarly, certain mathematical operation(s) on the second number result(s) in the third number and so on. Which of the given options follows the same set of operations as in the given sets? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 11 – 14 – 8 – 17; 12 – 15 – 9 – 18
questions.explanation: Each set adds 3, subtracts 6, then adds 9: 11, 14, 8, 17 and 12, 15, 9, 18. Likewise 6, 9, 3, 12.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that when placed from left to right in the blanks below will complete the given letter series. B _ E N B _ C E N B B C _ N B B C E _ B _ C
questions.explanation: With C, B, E, N, B in the blanks the block BCENB repeats: BCENB BCENB BCENB BCENB BC.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 14 : 30 :: 9 : 20 :: 4 : ? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is twice the first plus 2: 14 × 2 + 2 = 30 and 9 × 2 + 2 = 20. Likewise 4 × 2 + 2 = 10.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'SHE' is written as 'EIT' and 'SAD' is written as 'DBT'. How will 'SUN’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The word is written backwards and its last two letters then move one place forward: SHE → E H S → EIT and SAD → D A S → DBT. So SUN → N U S → NVT.

questions.text: Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-clusters are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which is the letter-cluster that DOES NOT belong to that group? (Note: The odd man out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter-cluster.)
questions.explanation: In FLI, MSP and AGD the letters move +6, then −3. CHE moves +5, then −3, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some eagles are sparrows. All sparrows are parrots. No parrot is a penguin. Conclusions: (I) Some parrots are eagles. (II) No penguin is a sparrow.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
questions.explanation: Some eagles are sparrows and all sparrows are parrots, so some parrots are eagles (I). All sparrows are parrots and no parrot is a penguin, so no penguin is a sparrow (II). Both follow.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 3, 17, 83, 329, ?, 1961

17 is related to 21 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 22 is related to 36. To which of the following is 29 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is three times the first minus 10: (17 − 10) × 3 = 21 and (22 − 10) × 3 = 36. So (29 − 10) × 3 = 57.

questions.text: BIRTHDAY - IBTRDHYA BLAZER - LBZARE REMOVE - ? Using the same logic as applied for the first two pairs of terms, select the term that can replace the question mark (?) in the third pair.
questions.explanation: Each pair of letters is swapped: BI RT HD AY → IB TR DH YA and BL AZ ER → LB ZA RE. So RE MO VE → ER OM EV: EROMEV.

questions.text: The same operation(s) are followed in all the given number pairs except one. Find that odd number pair. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In 49 : 8, 19 : 3 and 55 : 9 the second number is the first minus 1, divided by 6: 48 ÷ 6 = 8, 18 ÷ 6 = 3 and 54 ÷ 6 = 9. For 24 : 4, 23 ÷ 6 is not 4, so it is the odd pair.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 1205 × 5 + 35 – 197 ÷ 18 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 1205 ÷ 5 − 35 + 197 × 18 = 241 − 35 + 3546 = 3752.

questions.text: In which of the following years was the Right of Persons with Disabilities Act passed?
questions.explanation: The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act was passed in December 2016, replacing the Persons with Disabilities Act of 1995.

questions.text: Who among the following was one of the recipients of the inaugural ‘Prof CR Rao Centenary Gold Medal’ award in 2021?
questions.explanation: Jagdish Bhagwati and C Rangarajan were the first recipients of the medal, instituted by The Indian Econometric Society's trust to mark C R Rao's centenary.

questions.text: Which of the following Articles states that the Prime Minister should be appointed by the President?
questions.explanation: Under Article 75(1) the Prime Minister is appointed by the President, and the other ministers by the President on the Prime Minister's advice.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Due to which of the following events did Rabindranath Tagore return the title of ‘Knighthood’ to the British Government while expressing his anguish?
questions.explanation: Tagore gave up his knighthood in May 1919 in protest at the Jallianwala Bagh massacre in Amritsar that April.

questions.text: In which sport did India win its first individual Olympic medal?
questions.explanation: K D Jadhav's bronze in wrestling at the 1952 Helsinki Olympics was independent India's first individual Olympic medal.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of Phylum Arthropoda?
questions.explanation: Butterflies are insects, and insects are arthropods. Pila (the apple snail) is a mollusc; Nereis and Hirudinaria (the leech) are annelids.

questions.text: Tarun Bhattacharya, who was awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 2018, is known for playing which musical instrument?
questions.explanation: Pandit Tarun Bhattacharya is a santoor player.

questions.text: Which of the following is a component of the SHG-bank linkage program in India?
options: Microfinance institutions providing loans directly to SHGs
State government providing subsidies to SHGs for credit
Non-governmental organisations providing capacity building training to SHGs
Banks providing loans to individual members of SHGs
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives bank loans to SHG members. Under NABARD's SHG-bank linkage programme, begun in 1992, banks lend to the groups, which pass the credit on to their individual members; NGOs that form and train the groups also take part, so the question is loosely worded.

questions.text: As per the Timurid tradition, Humayun had to share power with his brothers. Humayun had the control of Delhi, Agra and Central India, while his brother Kamran controlled which of the following regions?
questions.explanation: Kamran held Kabul and Kandahar, in present-day Afghanistan, and also took the Punjab.

questions.text: Navratri festival is dedicated to which of the following Goddesses?
questions.explanation: Navratri's nine nights are dedicated to Goddess Durga in her nine forms.

questions.text: Which two organic chemists are known for observing the peroxide effect in adding reagents to unsaturated compounds in 1933?
options: Justus von Liebig and Friedrich Wöhler
Morris S Kharasch and Frank R Mayo
B Steven Bachrach and Roald Hoffmann
C John Cadogan and Luis M Campos
questions.explanation: In 1933 Morris Kharasch and Frank Mayo showed that peroxides reverse the way HBr adds to an alkene (anti-Markovnikov addition): the peroxide effect.

questions.text: The oath of office to the Vice-President is administered by the ________.
questions.explanation: Under Article 69 the Vice-President takes the oath before the President, or a person the President appoints for the purpose.

questions.text: What was the name of the wind measuring instrument invented for the first time in 1450?
questions.explanation: The Italian architect Leon Battista Alberti described the first mechanical anemometer, a swinging-plate design, around 1450.

questions.text: As per a report of the Ministry of Labour and Employment, what was the rate of unemployment in Maharashtra for the year 2021-22?
questions.explanation: The Periodic Labour Force Survey 2021-22 put Maharashtra's unemployment rate (usual status, persons aged 15 and above) at 3.5%, below the all-India 4.1%.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a unit of energy?
questions.explanation: The newton is the unit of force. Joules, kilowatt hours and calories all measure energy.

questions.text: The Wardha is a tributary of which of the following rivers?
questions.explanation: The Wardha joins the Wainganga to form the Pranhita, which flows into the Godavari.

questions.text: Pandit Omkar Nath Thakur was a student of ____________.
questions.explanation: Omkarnath Thakur trained under Vishnu Digambar Paluskar at the Gandharva Mahavidyalaya.

questions.text: Vijender Singh has represented India in Olympics for how many times?
questions.explanation: Vijender Singh boxed at the 2004, 2008 and 2012 Olympics, winning bronze at Beijing in 2008.

questions.text: Who among the following classical dancers is NOT related to Odissi?
questions.explanation: Geetanjali Lal is a Kathak dancer. Mayadhar Raut, Kiran Segal and Kumkum Mohanty are Odissi dancers.

questions.text: What were the main obstacles during the industrial development of India at the time of independence?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives capital. In NCERT's account, Indian industrialists at independence did not have the capital for the large investments industry needed; it adds that the market was not big enough either, so that option is also arguable.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Khudai Khidmatgar, a voluntary organisation, was established by which of the following leaders of India?
questions.explanation: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, the 'Frontier Gandhi', founded the Khudai Khidmatgar (Servants of God) in 1929.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Duty?
options: To prohibit trade in rare and endangered species
To safeguard public property and to abjure violence
To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India
To value and preserve rich heritage of the country’s composite culture
questions.explanation: Article 51A lists safeguarding public property, upholding India's sovereignty and preserving its composite culture as duties; prohibiting trade in rare and endangered species is not one of them.

questions.text: What is the other name of tetanus caused by toxin producing bacteria called clostridium tetani?
questions.explanation: Tetanus is called lockjaw because the toxin's muscle spasms clamp the jaw shut.

questions.text: During which of the following rules did Buddhism get split into two schools - Hinayana and Mahayana in the fourth Buddhist council?
questions.explanation: The fourth Buddhist council, held in Kashmir under the Kushana king Kanishka, saw Buddhism split into the Hinayana and Mahayana schools.

questions.text: As of Financial year 2019, which of the following state has the highest road density in India?
questions.explanation: Kerala has the highest road density of these states: the most road length per square kilometre of area.

questions.text: A vendor started selling vegetables at ₹10 per kg, but couldn’t find buyers at this rate. So he reduced the price to ₹7.2 per kg, but uses a faulty weight of 900 g instead of 1 kg. Find the percentage change in the actual price.
questions.explanation: He now charges ₹7.2 for 900 g, which is 7.2 ÷ 0.9 = ₹8 per kg. From ₹10 to ₹8 is a fall of 20%.

questions.text: 15 kg of ₹10 per kg wheat is mixed with 5 kg of another type of wheat to get a mixture costing ₹30 per kg. Find the price (per kg) of the costlier wheat.
questions.explanation: The mixture costs 20 × 30 = ₹600, of which the cheaper wheat is 15 × 10 = ₹150. So 5 kg of the costlier wheat cost ₹450: ₹90 per kg.

questions.text: AB is a chord of length 32 cm of a circle of radius 20 cm, the tangents at A and B intersect at a point T. Find length TA (rounded off to two digits after decimal).
questions.explanation: The centre O is √(20² − 16²) = 12 cm from the chord's midpoint M. Triangles OMA and OAT are similar (right-angled at M and A, with the angle at O common), so TA = OA × AM/OM = 20 × 16/12 = 26.67 cm.

questions.text: P, Q and R are the three angles of a triangle. If P − Q = 20° and Q − R = 26°, then ∠P is equal to:

Each of Ravi and Kavita had some marbles. Kavita had 12 more marbles than Ravi had. If each of them had one more marble, then three times the number of marbles Kavita would then have had would have been equal to four times the number of marbles Ravi would then have had. How many marbles did Kavita actually have?
questions.explanation: If Ravi had r, Kavita had r + 12, and 3(r + 13) = 4(r + 1). So 3r + 39 = 4r + 4, r = 35 and Kavita had 47.

questions.text: WXYZ is a quadrilateral in which XQ and ZP are perpendicular to WY such that XQ = ZP. Diagonals ZX and WY intersect each other at point O. If OX = 12 cm, then find the value of ZX (in cm).
questions.explanation: Triangles XQO and ZPO have right angles at Q and P, equal vertically opposite angles at O and XQ = ZP, so they are congruent (AAS) and OZ = OX = 12 cm. ZX = 24 cm.

questions.text: The cost of a diamond varies directly as the square of its weight. Once, this diamond broke into four pieces with weights in the ratio of 4 : 3 : 2 : 1 .When the pieces were sold, the merchant got ₹63,000 less than that of one piece. Find the original price of the diamond.
questions.explanation: Price = k × weight². Taking the weight as 10 units, the whole diamond is worth 100k and the pieces 16k + 9k + 4k + k = 30k. The loss of 70k is ₹63,000, so k = ₹900 and the diamond was worth ₹90,000.

questions.text: The cost of tomatoes per kg is increased by 300%. A housewife reduces her consumption of tomatoes by 70%. By what percentage does her expenditure on tomatoes increase or decrease?
questions.explanation: A 300% rise multiplies the price by 4 and a 70% cut the consumption by 0.3, so spending is multiplied by 4 × 0.3 = 1.2: an increase of 20%.

questions.text: Aman invested a sum of money in scheme A at the rate of 8% p.a. for a period of 5 years on simple interest. He invested four times of the sum of scheme A in scheme B at the rate of 5% p.a. for 7 years on simple interest. He received a total interest amount of ₹1,620. How much (in ₹) did he invest in scheme B?

Two trains of lengths 150 m and 250 m run on parallel lines. When they run in the same direction, they take 20 seconds to cross each other and, when they run in the opposite direction, they take 5 seconds to cross each other. What is the speed of the two trains?
questions.explanation: Together the trains are 400 m long. Same direction: the difference of their speeds is 400/20 = 20 m/s; opposite: the sum is 400/5 = 80 m/s. So the speeds are 50 m/s and 30 m/s, that is 180 km/h and 108 km/h.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. However, their population is declining nowadays due to noise pollution. B. It is one of the most common birds along with the other two species, the European starling, and the rock pigeon. C. Their constant presence outside our homes makes it easy to overlook them. D. House sparrows can be found in most places with and without houses (or other structures).
questions.explanation: D introduces house sparrows, B says they are among the commonest birds, C that their constant presence makes us overlook them, and A, with 'However', turns to their decline: DBCA.

questions.text: Out of the four sentences given, three have spelling errors. Identify the sentence that has no spelling error.
options: She tried to manoeuvre her trolley around people.
The computer's software detected an anamoly caused by a virus.
What advice did he give to young entreprenuers?
A clergyman read the litturgy from the prayer-book.
questions.explanation: 'Manoeuvre' is spelt correctly; the others should read 'anomaly', 'entrepreneurs' and 'liturgy'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Start from scratch
options: To start or create something from the very beginning
To develop something out of waste material
questions.explanation: To 'start from scratch' is to begin at the very beginning, with nothing done beforehand.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. The police told the agitators to back in, else they would lathi-charge.
questions.explanation: To retreat is to 'back off' (or 'move back'): 'told the agitators to back off'. 'Back in' means to go in backwards.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate order of the segments in the options that will fill in the blanks and make a coherent paragraph. Though Sheela loves watching horror movies, ________________/________________/________________/________________ she rented another romantic today.
options: she planned to try something different yesterday / so she rented the latest romantic / and to her surprise she enjoyed it very much / so much so that
so much so that / and to her surprise she enjoyed it very much / she planned to try something different yesterday / so she rented the latest romantic
so she rented the latest romantic / and to her surprise she enjoyed it very much / so much so that / she planned to try something different yesterday
and to her surprise she enjoyed it very much /so much so that /so she rented the latest romantic /she planned to try something different yesterday
questions.explanation: 'Though Sheela loves watching horror movies, she planned to try something different yesterday, so she rented the latest romantic, and to her surprise she enjoyed it very much, so much so that she rented another romantic today.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Transnational linkages, for example, sever the nation-state’s “integrity and corrupt” state-society relations.
questions.explanation: 'Cohesion and erode' keeps the sense: the linkages break the nation-state's unity and wear away its relations with society. The other pairs do not fit the sentence.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. The cashier had finished the assigned task on time.
options: The assigned task was finished by the cashier on time.
The assigned task has been finished by the cashier on time.
The assigned task had been finished by the cashier on time.
The assigned task is finished by the cashier on time.
questions.explanation: The past perfect 'had finished' becomes 'had been finished' in the passive.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Garnish
questions.explanation: To 'garnish' food is to 'decorate' it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Determined
questions.explanation: 'Determined' and 'resolute' both mean firmly set on a purpose.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. His house “is smaller than you” .
questions.explanation: His house is compared with your house, so the possessive pronoun is needed: 'smaller than yours'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word to fill in the blank. Capricious Share market prices have remained __________ for weeks.
questions.explanation: 'Capricious' means given to sudden changes; its opposite is 'stable': prices have remained stable for weeks.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. Data is being collected by the researcher.
options: The researcher has been collecting data.
The researcher will be collecting data.
questions.explanation: 'Is being collected' is the present continuous passive, so the active is 'is collecting'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. Evenings get “dark” very early in this cold weather.
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'dark' is 'bright'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A person who performs magic to entertain people
questions.explanation: A magician performs magic tricks to entertain an audience.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence. Fundamentels of every subject need to be learnt on priority basis.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'Fundamentals'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that has the same meaning as the italicised segment. His illness became “a blessing in disguise” when he married his nurse.
options: an apparent misfortune that eventually has good results
when someone finds it difficult to choose between two alternatives
deal with a problem if and when it becomes necessary
questions.explanation: A 'blessing in disguise' is an apparent misfortune that turns out well.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Desolate
questions.explanation: 'Desolate' means bleak and joyless; its opposite is 'festive'.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. We took dinner in a Chinese restaurant and were amazed to see the interior of a restaurant.
questions.explanation: The restaurant has already been mentioned, so it takes the definite article: 'the interior of the restaurant'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given phrase. A person who is kept captive for fulfilment of demands of money or conditions
questions.explanation: A hostage is held captive until demands, such as a ransom, are met.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Fallacy
questions.explanation: A 'fallacy' is a mistaken belief or argument: an 'error'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. When Ojeya Cruz Banks moved to Ohio from New Zealand (1) ________ years ago, she was overwhelmed by the logistics of uprooting her life. But Cruz Banks, a Denison University professor and a single mom, who is also my neighbour and friend, was (2) ________ to find a house next to a public elementary school. She assumed that she would be able to walk to pick up her daughter, a needed convenience given that she didn’t yet have a car. Unfortunately, when she went to register her daughter for kindergarten, she was met with an (3) ________ surprise: The only (4) ________ option was a half-day program that would bus students to a day-care centre on the outskirts of the town for the afternoon. The district did offer a limited number of full-day slots, but those had all been claimed in a lottery earlier that spring and came with a tuition cost. “I was like, ‘Cost me? What? Public school costs money here?’” she told me. Many parents across the United States, like Cruz Banks, may assume that free, full-day kindergarten is a (5) ________ part of the country’s public education system. I was one of them, until my youngest had to enter our district’s lottery several months ago. When he was assigned to the half-day program, I swung between alarm and frustration.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.explanation: She moved 'several years ago'; 'immense', 'enormous' and 'particular' do not describe a number of years.
