questions.text: In a certain code, 'it is raining' is coded as 'dy po ko', 'is raining now' is coded as 'po jo ko' and 'is now it' is coded as 'po jo dy'. (All the codes are two-letter codes only.) What is the code for 'raining'?
questions.explanation: 'is' is in all three sentences and 'po' in all three codes, so is = po. 'raining' is in the first two only, whose codes share po and ko, so raining = ko.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 625, 382, 301, 274, 265, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 243, 81, 27 and 9, each a third of the one before, so the next is 3: 265 − 3 = 262.

questions.text: In this question, three statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusion(s) logically follows/follow from the statements. Statements: All teachers are dancers. All dancers are engineers. Some engineers are beautiful. Conclusions: I. All teachers are beautiful. II. Some dancers are beautiful.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: All teachers are dancers and all dancers are engineers, but only some engineers are beautiful, and they need not include any dancer or teacher. Neither conclusion follows.

questions.text: 13 is related to 119 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 9 is related to 31. To which of the following is 8 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Square the number and subtract 50: 13² − 50 = 119 and 9² − 50 = 31. Likewise 8² − 50 = 14.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially place from left to right in the blanks below to balance the given equation. 8 _ 27 _ 9 _ 6 _ 5 = 0
Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? ABNI, DAQH, ?, JYWF
questions.explanation: First letters move +3 (A, D, G, J), second letters −1 (B, A, Z, Y), third letters +3 (N, Q, T, W) and fourth letters −1 (I, H, G, F): GZTG.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘+’ and ‘×’ are interchanged and ‘–’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 16 − 2 × 42 + 13 ÷ 12 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 16 ÷ 2 + 42 × 13 − 12 = 8 + 546 − 12 = 542.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'MAIN' is written as 'OHBL' and 'MAIL' is written as 'MHBL'. How will 'MANY’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The word is reversed and its letters moved +1, −1, +1, −1: MAIN → NIAM → OHBL and MAIL → LIAM → MHBL. So MANY → YNAM → ZMBL.

questions.text: Four letter-clusters have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the one that is different. Note :The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter cluster
questions.explanation: In LKM, HGI and TSU the letters move −1, then +2. XYW moves +1, then −2, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Select the word-pair that best represents a similar relationship to the one expressed in the pair of words given below. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must NOT be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) New Zealand : Wellington
questions.explanation: Wellington is the capital of New Zealand, as Addis Ababa is of Ethiopia. The capitals of South Korea, China and Egypt are Seoul, Beijing and Cairo; Tunis is Tunisia's.

questions.text: The second number in the given number-pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) is/are followed in all the number-pairs, except one. Find that odd number-pair. (NOTE: The relation should be found without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits)
questions.explanation: 1521 : 1600, 1764 : 1849 and 1156 : 1225 are squares of consecutive numbers (39² : 40², 42² : 43², 34² : 35²). 784 : 961 is 28² : 31², so it is the odd one.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘toys are gadgets’ is coded as ‘dj sq ty’ and ‘gadgets are machines’ is coded as ‘mp ty dj’. What is code for ‘gadgets’ in that language?
questions.explanation: 'are' and 'gadgets' are the words in both sentences and 'dj' and 'ty' the codes in both, so 'gadgets' is either 'ty' or 'dj'.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of numbers. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 13 : 55 23 : 105
questions.explanation: The second number is five times the first minus 10: 13 × 5 − 10 = 55 and 23 × 5 − 10 = 105. Likewise 31 × 5 − 10 = 145.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that when sequentially placed from left to right in the blanks below will complete the letter series. _ B _ _ _ A L _ _ L _ _
questions.explanation: With L, A, L, B, B, A, B, A in the blanks the block LBA repeats: LBA LBA LBA LBA.

questions.text: ‘NQRP’ is related to ‘RUVT’ in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, ‘DGLF’ is related to ‘HKPJ’. To which of the following is ‘KCUM’ related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 4 places forward: NQRP → RUVT and DGLF → HKPJ. So KCUM → OGYQ.

questions.text: 97 is related to 49 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 115 is related to 58. To which of the following is 133 related to, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

Each vowel in the word ‘ISOLATED’ is changed to the following letter in the English alphabetical order and each consonant is changed to the preceding letter in the English alphabetical order. How many letters are there in the English alphabetical order between the letter which is the third from the left end and the second from the left end in the group of letters thus formed?
questions.explanation: ISOLATED becomes J R P K B S F C. The third letter from the left is P and the second from the left is R; between them comes one letter, Q.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'A ! B' means ‘A is the father of B’, 'A & B' means ‘A is the brother of B’, 'A * B' means ‘A is the wife of B’ and 'A # B' means ‘A is the daughter of B’. Which of the following means that S is the husband's brother's wife of M?
questions.explanation: In S * F & J ! I # M, S is F's wife, F is J's brother, J is I's father and I is M's daughter, so M is J's wife. S is the wife of M's husband's brother. In the other options S is someone's brother.

questions.text: Which Indian musician and sitar player is the founder of the National Orchestra of India ?
questions.explanation: Ravi Shankar founded the National Orchestra (Vadya Vrinda) at All India Radio, where he was music director from 1949 to 1956.

questions.text: What is the disinvestment target of the Finance Ministry for the year 2023-24?
questions.explanation: The Union Budget 2023-24 set a disinvestment target of ₹51,000 crore.

questions.text: Where was the first official summit of the Non-Aligned movement held?
questions.explanation: The first summit of the Non-Aligned Movement was held at Belgrade, Yugoslavia, in September 1961.

questions.text: Gandharva Mahavidyalaya, which was founded by Pandit Vinaya Chandra Maudgalya, is located at ________.
questions.explanation: Pandit Vinaya Chandra Maudgalya's Gandharva Mahavidyalaya, a school of Hindustani music and dance, is in New Delhi.

questions.text: For a chemical reaction with rise in temperature by 10°, the rate constant becomes nearly ____________________.
questions.explanation: As NCERT puts it, the rate constant of a reaction nearly doubles for a 10° rise in temperature.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of joint sector industry?
questions.explanation: NCERT's example of a joint sector industry, owned by the state together with private parties, is Oil India Limited. SAIL and BHEL are public sector; TISCO is private sector.

questions.text: Which is the joint digital skills initiative for employability through digital skills by National Career Service and Microsoft India?
questions.explanation: DigiSaksham is the digital skills programme for young job-seekers run by the Ministry of Labour and Employment's National Career Service with Microsoft India.

questions.text: Which of the following commissions/committees identified the existence of legal provisions for implementation of some of the Fundamental Duties?
questions.explanation: The Verma Committee on Fundamental Duties of the Citizens (1999) identified the existing laws that enforce some of the Fundamental Duties.

questions.text: Pandwani singer Usha Barle was conferred with which of the following awards by the Government of India in 2023?
questions.explanation: Usha Barle, a Pandwani singer from Chhattisgarh, received the Padma Shri in 2023.

questions.text: Articles 245 to 255 in Part XI of the Indian Constitution deal with the ____________.
options: financial relations between the Centre and the states
legislative relations between the Centre and the states
questions.explanation: Articles 245 to 255, Chapter I of Part XI, deal with legislative relations between the Union and the states; administrative relations follow in Articles 256 to 263.

questions.text: In peninsular India, which of the following kingdoms was the local power that ruled over northern Maharashtra and Vidarbha?
questions.explanation: The Vakatakas, a Deccan power of the Gupta age, ruled northern Maharashtra and Vidarbha (Berar).

questions.text: In chess, which of the following may only move forward to the unoccupied square immediately in front of it?
questions.explanation: A pawn moves straight ahead into the empty square in front of it (two squares on its first move) and captures diagonally; the queen, bishop and rook move any number of squares.

questions.text: In which group of states does the Luni River flow?
questions.explanation: The Luni rises in the Aravalli range near Ajmer, flows south-west through Rajasthan and ends in the Rann of Kutch in Gujarat.

questions.text: ______ is the provision of small credit to those who would have no other access to financial services.
questions.explanation: Microfinance is the provision of small loans and other financial services to people who cannot use ordinary banks; a microloan is one such loan, not the service.

questions.text: Agricultural shot is a term used in which of the following sports?
questions.explanation: In cricket an 'agricultural shot' is a crude, cross-batted slog across the line of the ball.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of prokaryotic cells?
questions.explanation: Bacteria are prokaryotes, with no membrane-bound nucleus. Plasmodium and Leishmania (protozoa) and yeast (a fungus) are eukaryotes.

questions.text: The variation between a high air temperature and a low temperature that occurs during the same day is called _______ temperature.
questions.explanation: The diurnal range of temperature is the difference between a day's highest and lowest temperatures.

questions.text: As per Mendeleev’s prediction, atomic mass of eka-aluminium was:
questions.explanation: Mendeleev predicted an atomic mass of 68 for eka-aluminium; gallium, discovered later, has 69.7.

questions.text: Which of the following documents provides a framework, rules and regulations for setting up public and private industries in India?
options: Annual report of the trade union
questions.explanation: A government's industrial policy (as in 1948, 1956 and 1991) sets the framework and rules for public and private industry; the Union Budget is the yearly statement of receipts and spending.

questions.text: Which of the following is the best definition of ecological efficiency?
options: The ratio between the mass and the energy flow at different trophic levels in a food chain
The ratio between energy flows at different points in a food chain
The amount of energy stored at different trophic levels in a food chain
The amount of energy utilised at different trophic levels in a food chain
questions.explanation: Ecological efficiency compares the energy flowing at one point in a food chain with that at another, such as between successive trophic levels (typically about 10%).

questions.text: Which state Chief Minister launched the 'Kaushalya Matritva Yojana' in 2022, which provides financial assistance of ₹5,000 to women giving birth to a second girl child for safe motherhood?
questions.explanation: Chhattisgarh's Chief Minister Bhupesh Baghel launched the Kaushalya Matritva Yojana in March 2022.

questions.text: In which of the following states is Me-dam-me-phi festival primarily celebrated?
questions.explanation: Me-Dam-Me-Phi, the Ahom festival of ancestor worship, is celebrated in Assam on 31 January.

questions.text: Mulayam Singh Yadav, who passed away in October 2022, served as the Chief Minister of which state?
questions.explanation: Mulayam Singh Yadav, founder of the Samajwadi Party, was Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh three times.

questions.text: In 10th century India, Queen Didda became the ruler of which of the following regions of north India?
questions.explanation: Didda ruled Kashmir in the late 10th century, first as regent for her son and grandsons and then as queen in her own right.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which of the following years was VD Savarkar sent to Andaman Jail by the British?
questions.explanation: Savarkar, sentenced to two terms of transportation for life, was taken to the Cellular Jail at Port Blair in 1911.

questions.text: ΔABC and ΔDEF are two triangles such that ΔABC ≅ ΔFDE. If AB=17 cm, ∠B=52° and ∠A=95°, then which of the following options is true?
questions.explanation: ΔABC ≅ ΔFDE matches A with F, B with D and C with E. So DF = AB = 17 cm and ∠E = ∠C = 180° − 95° − 52° = 33°.

questions.text: Three years ago, the age of a person was six times the age of his younger brother. Eight years later, the age of the person will be three years less than twice the age of his younger brother. Find the present ages of the person and his younger brother.
questions.explanation: With present ages x and y: x − 3 = 6(y − 3) and x + 8 = 2(y + 8) − 3, so x = 6y − 15 = 2y + 5. Then y = 5 and x = 15.

questions.text: An article marked for ₹275 is sold at 5% discount. The seller still gains 4.5%. What did he pay for it?
questions.explanation: Selling price = 95% of ₹275 = ₹261.25. This is 104.5% of the cost, so the cost = 261.25/1.045 = ₹250.

questions.text: At a school building, there is an overhead tank. To fill this tank 50 buckets of water are required. Assume that the capacity of the bucket is reduced to two-fifth of the present. How many buckets of water are required to fill the same tank?
questions.explanation: Each new bucket holds 2/5 of an old one, so the tank needs 50 ÷ 2/5 = 125 buckets.

questions.text: The base radius of a circular cylinder is 10.5 cm. If the area of its curved surface is 792 cm², then what is the volume of the cylinder?
The radius of the circle is 10 cm and the perpendicular distance from the chord to the centre is 6 cm. The length of the chord is:
questions.explanation: Half the chord = √(10² − 6²) = √64 = 8 cm, so the chord is 16 cm.

questions.text: The average score of a batsman in twenty matches is 15 and in twenty-five other matches is 24. Find the average score in all the forty-five matches.

A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 200 metres. When the policeman starts the chase, the thief also starts running. If the speed of the thief is 9 km/h and that of the policeman 10 km/h, how far will the thief have to run before he is overtaken?
questions.explanation: The policeman gains 10 − 9 = 1 km/h, so he closes the 200 m (0.2 km) gap in 0.2 hours. In that time the thief runs 9 × 0.2 = 1.8 km.

questions.text: From the given numbers A, B, C and D, which number is NOT divisible by 11? A = 712712 B = 177210 C = 64614 D = 756148
questions.explanation: A number is divisible by 11 when the sums of its alternate digits differ by a multiple of 11. For 756148: (7 + 6 + 4) − (5 + 1 + 8) = 3, so it is not; for 712712, 177210 and 64614 the differences are 0, 0 and 11.

questions.text: The price of an item is increased twice successively. The final price is ₹2,295 and initial price was ₹1,000. The percentage increment the second time was twice the percentage increment the first time. By what percentage was the price increased the second time?
questions.explanation: If the first rise is x%, the second is 2x%: 1,000(1 + x/100)(1 + 2x/100) = 2,295. x = 35 fits (1.35 × 1.70 = 2.295), so the second rise was 70%.

questions.text: The sum of the ages of 6 children born at the interval of two years each is 90 years. What is the age (in years) of the eldest child?
questions.explanation: The ages x, x + 2, …, x + 10 add up to 6x + 30 = 90, so x = 10 and the eldest is 20.

questions.text: PQ and RS are common tangents to two circles intersecting at A and B. A and B, when produced on both the sides, meet the tangents PQ and RS at X and Y, respectively. If AB = 3 cm and XY = 5 cm, then PQ is ________.
questions.explanation: XP² = XA × XB = XQ², so X is the midpoint of PQ; by symmetry XA = YB = (5 − 3)/2 = 1 cm. XP² = 1 × 4 = 4, so XP = 2 cm and PQ = 4 cm.

questions.text: A sum of ₹1,456, when invested for ten years, amounts to ₹2,366 on maturity. Find the rate of simple interest per annum that was to be paid on the sum invested.

Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. (A) a lot (B) my daily routine (C) i have missed (D) since my retirement (E) at the workplace
questions.explanation: 'I have missed (C) my daily routine (B) at the workplace (E) a lot (A) since my retirement (D).'

questions.text: Select the correctly spelled sentence.
questions.explanation: The correct spellings are 'athlete’s', 'achievements' and 'impressive'.

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. A. all the plants and animals of today B. it is written that Brahma is the God of creation C. and it is He who has made D. in the book of Hindu mythology
questions.explanation: 'In the book of Hindu mythology (D) it is written that Brahma is the God of creation (B) and it is He who has made (C) all the plants and animals of today (A).'

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a spelling error. Big Data has inandated / the education industry. / It has transformed it / by leaps and bounds.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'inundated'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the following sentence in active voice. The concert tickets were bought by my friend
options: My friend has bought the concert tickets.
My friend buys the concert tickets.
My friend is buying the concert tickets.
My friend bought the concert tickets.
questions.explanation: The simple past passive 'were bought by my friend' becomes the simple past active 'My friend bought'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. In industries, it is very common to observe that people show “undue favour to one’s own relative during the hiring process”.
questions.explanation: Nepotism is favouring one's own relatives, especially in giving jobs.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. She was foolish enough to think that she “be completely safe” now.
questions.explanation: Of the options only 'is' agrees with 'she' and is a complete verb: 'that she is completely safe now'. 'She have been', 'she has being' and 'she were' are ungrammatical here.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. It takes time to “adapt” to a new environment.
questions.explanation: To 'adapt' to something is to 'adjust' to it.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into three segments. One of them may contain an error. Select the option that has the segment with the error. If you don’t find any error, select ‘No error’ as your answer. Mr. Ali’s shop / is further to / the hospital.
questions.explanation: 'Further to' means 'following on from', as in 'further to our talk'; for position the sentence needs 'next to' (or, for distance, 'farther from') the hospital.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom/phrase. I had heard of “henpecked husbands” and now, I felt that I saw one.
questions.explanation: A 'henpecked' husband is one dominated and nagged by his wife: an oppressed husband. The other options describe the one who dominates.

questions.text: Identity the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the following sentence. I love the “stunning” view of the mountain.
questions.explanation: 'Stunning' means strikingly beautiful or impressive; its opposite is 'mundane', dull and ordinary.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The statistical study of human populations.
questions.explanation: Demography is the statistical study of human populations; palaeography is the study of ancient writing.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. One who tends to look at the dark side of things
questions.explanation: A pessimist expects the worst; an optimist expects the best.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Hinder
questions.explanation: To 'hinder' is to obstruct; its opposite is to 'facilitate', to make easier. 'Block' is a synonym.

questions.text: Identify from the given options the word which is similar in meaning to the following word. Morbid
questions.explanation: 'Morbid' means preoccupied with gloomy, unpleasant things such as death: 'gloomy'. 'Blithe' is close to its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Inevitable
questions.explanation: 'Inevitable' means certain to happen; its opposite is 'avoidable'. 'Inexorable' is a synonym.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Roshan, it’s time for you to give your speech to the whole school, “wishing you luck to do well.”
questions.explanation: 'Break a leg' is said to wish a performer good luck.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. Inayat did not greet her.
options: She was not greeted by Inayat.
She was not going to be greeted by Inayat.
She was not at all greeted by Inayat.
She was not being greeted by Inayat.
questions.explanation: The simple past negative 'did not greet' becomes 'was not greeted', and the object 'her' becomes the subject 'She'.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. It rain a lot in this part of the country.
questions.explanation: A singular subject takes a singular verb in the simple present: 'It rains a lot'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. She is a very “creative” artist and one can see that in her paintings.
questions.explanation: 'Creative' means showing original ideas: 'innovative'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Recently, the (1)________ of heart-attacks in young Indians (2)________ increased tremendously. Doctors are surprised to note that young men and women with seemingly healthy lifestyle are suffering deadly heart attacks. (3)________ diet and exercise play a (4)________ role in a person’s overall wellbeing, mental health is also a valuable factor. The (5)________ urban lifestyle is causing anxiety and depression in young Indians which may be a major factor behind the increased numbers.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Heart attacks can be counted, so 'the number of'; 'amount' is for things that cannot be counted.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Recently, the (1)________ of heart-attacks in young Indians (2)________ increased tremendously. Doctors are surprised to note that young men and women with seemingly healthy lifestyle are suffering deadly heart attacks. (3)________ diet and exercise play a (4)________ role in a person’s overall wellbeing, mental health is also a valuable factor. The (5)________ urban lifestyle is causing anxiety and depression in young Indians which may be a major factor behind the increased numbers.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: 'The number of' takes a singular verb: 'the number of heart-attacks … has increased'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Recently, the (1)________ of heart-attacks in young Indians (2)________ increased tremendously. Doctors are surprised to note that young men and women with seemingly healthy lifestyle are suffering deadly heart attacks. (3)________ diet and exercise play a (4)________ role in a person’s overall wellbeing, mental health is also a valuable factor. The (5)________ urban lifestyle is causing anxiety and depression in young Indians which may be a major factor behind the increased numbers.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'Although' introduces the concession: 'Although diet and exercise play a … role, mental health is also a valuable factor.' 'In spite of' would need a noun, and 'However' cannot join the two clauses.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Recently, the (1)________ of heart-attacks in young Indians (2)________ increased tremendously. Doctors are surprised to note that young men and women with seemingly healthy lifestyle are suffering deadly heart attacks. (3)________ diet and exercise play a (4)________ role in a person’s overall wellbeing, mental health is also a valuable factor. The (5)________ urban lifestyle is causing anxiety and depression in young Indians which may be a major factor behind the increased numbers.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: A 'monumental' role is a very great or important one; 'a increased' is ungrammatical, and 'epic' and 'historic' do not describe a role in wellbeing.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Recently, the (1)________ of heart-attacks in young Indians (2)________ increased tremendously. Doctors are surprised to note that young men and women with seemingly healthy lifestyle are suffering deadly heart attacks. (3)________ diet and exercise play a (4)________ role in a person’s overall wellbeing, mental health is also a valuable factor. The (5)________ urban lifestyle is causing anxiety and depression in young Indians which may be a major factor behind the increased numbers.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: The 'fast-paced' urban lifestyle, hectic enough to cause anxiety; 'rapidly' is an adverb and cannot describe a noun.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘CYCLE’ is coded as ‘242241522’ and ‘FINAL’ is coded as ‘2118132615’. How will ‘MUSIC’ be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is coded by its place counted from Z (Z = 1, A = 26): C = 24, Y = 2, C = 24, L = 15, E = 22. So M = 14, U = 6, S = 8, I = 18, C = 24: 14681824.

questions.text: Four letter-clusters have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the letter-cluster that is different. Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter cluster...
questions.explanation: TVX, HJL and NPR move +2, then +2. MOP moves +2, then +1, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Select the triad in which the numbers are related to each other in the same way as the numbers in the following triads. 4-5-41 2-3-13 (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The third number is the sum of the squares of the first two: 4² + 5² = 41 and 2² + 3² = 13. Likewise 5² + 6² = 25 + 36 = 61.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘PANTHER’ is written as ‘0146283’ and ‘ANOTHER’ is written as ‘2864109’. How will ‘O’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: A, N, T, H, E and R are in both words, as are 0, 1, 2, 4, 6 and 8 in both codes. The letter left in ANOTHER is O and the digit left in its code is 9, so O = 9.

questions.text: ‘MPQO’ is related to ‘KNSQ’ in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, ‘DGHF’ is related to ‘BEJH’. To which of the following is ‘EINW’ related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: The first two letters move 2 back and the last two 2 forward: M → K, P → N, Q → S, O → Q. So E → C, I → G, N → P, W → Y: CGPY.

questions.text: Select the number from the given options to complete the series. 58, 70, 83, 97, ___
questions.explanation: The differences are 12, 13, 14, growing by 1, so the next is 15: 97 + 15 = 112.

questions.text: In a certain code language, X + Y means ‘X is the sister of Y’, X − Y means ‘X is the wife of Y’, X × Y means ‘X is the mother of Y’, X ÷ Y means ‘X is the father of Y’. Based on the above, how is H related to L if ‘H × I − J ÷ K + L’?
questions.explanation: H is the mother of I, I is the wife of J, J is the father of K and K is the sister of L. So I is L's mother and H is I's mother: H is L's mother's mother.

questions.text: Select the word-pair that best represents a similar relationship to the one expressed in the pair of words given below. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word.) Larva : Insect
questions.explanation: A larva is the young of an insect, as a fawn is the young of a deer. (A vixen is a female fox.)

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 69 + 2485 × 5 – 912 ÷ 2 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 69 − 2485 ÷ 5 + 912 × 2 = 69 − 497 + 1824 = 1396.

questions.text: Select the triad in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the given triads. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g., 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (11, 1, 10) (13, 7, 90)
questions.explanation: The third number is the product of the first two minus 1: 11 × 1 − 1 = 10 and 13 × 7 − 1 = 90. Likewise 4 × 5 − 1 = 19.

questions.text: Three of the following four options are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which is the one that does NOT belong to that group? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In the others the third number is twice the first plus three times the second: 2 × 88 + 3 × 23 = 245, 2 × 56 + 3 × 31 = 205 and 2 × 18 + 3 × 12 = 72. For 22 – 13 it would be 44 + 39 = 83, not 85.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of numbers. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 11 : 62 13 : 64
questions.explanation: The second number is the first plus 51: 11 + 51 = 62 and 13 + 51 = 64. Likewise 16 + 51 = 67.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 49 × 7 – 6 ÷ 8 +13 =
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 49 ÷ 7 + 6 × 8 − 13 = 7 + 48 − 13 = 42.

questions.text: In this question, three statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusion(s) logically follows/follow from the statements. Statements: Some shirts are pants. All pants are jackets. All jackets are trousers. Conclusions: I. Some trousers are shirts. II. All jackets are shirts.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
questions.explanation: Some shirts are pants, and all pants are jackets and so trousers, so some shirts are trousers: some trousers are shirts (I). Nothing says every jacket is a shirt, so II does not follow.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? HDLB, LBPZ, PZTX, ? , XVBT
questions.explanation: The first and third letters move 4 forward (H, L, P, T, X and L, P, T, X, B) and the second and fourth 2 back (D, B, Z, X, V and B, Z, X, V, T): TXXV.

questions.text: The position of how many letters will remain unchanged if each of the letters in the word ‘DRAFTING’ is arranged in the English alphabetical order?
questions.explanation: DRAFTING in alphabetical order is A D F G I N R T. Set against D R A F T I N G, no letter is in the same place.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that when sequentially placed from left to right in the blanks below will complete the letter series. I _ _ I _ I _ _ I _ J _
options: J I J I J I I
J I I I J J I
I J I I J J I
I I J J J I J
questions.explanation: With J, I, J, I, J, I, I in the blanks the block IJI repeats: IJI IJI IJI IJI.

questions.text: Which of the following is the largest inhabited riverine island in the world?
questions.explanation: Majuli, in the Brahmaputra in Assam, is the world's largest inhabited river island.

questions.text: In the Right-Hand Thumb Rule, the thumb is directed towards the direction of:
questions.explanation: Holding a straight current-carrying conductor in the right hand with the thumb along the current, the curled fingers give the direction of the magnetic field lines.

questions.text: Which is the most important protein component in milk, both quantitatively and nutritionally, that accounts for about 80% of the total protein in bovine milk?
questions.explanation: Casein makes up about 80% of the protein in cow's milk; most of the rest is whey protein.

questions.text: Which web portal was launched by the Department of Telecommunications for sharing information on mobile towers and EMF emission compliance?
questions.explanation: The Department of Telecommunications' Tarang Sanchar portal shows the mobile towers in any locality and whether they comply with the EMF emission norms.

questions.text: In 1539, the Battle of Chausa was fought between Humayun and ______.
questions.explanation: Sher Shah Suri defeated Humayun at Chausa in 1539, and again at Kannauj in 1540, driving him out of India.

questions.text: Sardhana Christian Fair is held in which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Sardhana, near Meerut in Uttar Pradesh, is home to the Basilica of Our Lady of Graces built by Begum Samru, the centre of its annual Christian fair.

questions.text: Ali Akbar Khan was associated with which of the following gharanas?
questions.explanation: The sarod maestro Ali Akbar Khan was the son and disciple of Allauddin Khan, who shaped the Maihar gharana.

questions.text: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that ‘The State shall endeavour to promote cottage industries on an individual or co-operative basis in rural areas’?
questions.explanation: Article 43, a Directive Principle, asks the State to secure a living wage for workers and to promote cottage industries in rural areas.

questions.text: Which of the following is the most controversial Article in the Indian Constitution, which provides for President’s rule in any state?
questions.explanation: Article 356 lets the President take over a state's government when its constitutional machinery fails; its frequent use has made it controversial. Article 352 covers a national emergency and Article 360 a financial one.

questions.text: A dense mass of water drops on smoke or dust particles in the lower atmosphere layers is referred to as:
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives smog: fog mixed with smoke, its water droplets condensed on smoke and dust particles in the lower atmosphere. The description fits fog in general, which is not an option; 'dense' and 'smoke' point to smog rather than mist, which is lighter. Frost is ice deposited on surfaces, and a blizzard is a snowstorm.

questions.text: Bhakti Pradeep Kulkarni is associated with ________.
questions.explanation: Bhakti Kulkarni of Goa is a chess Woman Grandmaster.

questions.text: Who among the following was the youngest recipient of the Sangeetha Kalanidhi awarded by the Music Academy in 1947?
questions.explanation: Semmangudi Srinivasa Iyer received the Music Academy's Sangeetha Kalanidhi in 1947, at 39 its youngest recipient. Bhimsen Joshi and Mallikarjun Mansur were Hindustani vocalists.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which year was the battle of Buxar fought?
questions.explanation: At Buxar in 1764 the East India Company defeated the combined forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula and the Mughal emperor Shah Alam II.

questions.text: Which of the following State governments has launched a scheme ‘Ankur’ in May 2021 to promote planting of trees in public, wherein people will be awarded for planting and taking care of the saplings?
questions.explanation: Madhya Pradesh launched 'Ankur' in May 2021: people who plant a sapling and look after it can win the Pranvayu Award.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following Acts passed under Warren Hastings was also called ‘half-loaf system’?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Pitt's India Act of 1784, passed while Warren Hastings was Governor-General. It set up dual control: the Company's Court of Directors kept its commercial affairs, while a Board of Control appointed by the Crown supervised the government of its territories.

questions.text: In Newlands’ Octaves, the properties of lithium and ________ were found to be the same.
questions.explanation: In Newlands' Octaves every eighth element resembles the first, as sodium, the eighth from lithium, does.

questions.text: India hosted the Asian Games in which of the following years?
questions.explanation: New Delhi hosted the first Asian Games in 1951 and the ninth in 1982.

questions.text: Which of the following movements created regional disparities between large and small farmers in India?
questions.explanation: The Green Revolution's gains went mostly to large farmers, who could afford irrigation, high-yielding seeds and fertilisers, and to a few regions, widening the gaps.

questions.text: What was the main objective of the Second Green Revolution in India?
options: Ensuring food security in the western states
Focusing on holistic development in agriculture
Increasing the use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides
questions.explanation: The Second Green Revolution looks beyond the first one's push for wheat and rice yields in a few north-western states, to holistic and sustainable development of agriculture as a whole.

questions.text: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution CANNOT be suspended even during an emergency declared on the grounds of war or external aggression?
questions.explanation: Since the 44th Amendment (1978), Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended during a national emergency.

questions.text: Elelakkaradi dance of Kerala is performed by which of the following tribes?
questions.explanation: Elelakkaradi is a group dance of the Irular (Irula) tribe of Kerala, in which men, women and children take part.

questions.text: Two inlet pipes, P1 and P2, can fill a cistern in 20 hours and 30 hours, respectively. They were opened at the same time, but pipe P1 had to be closed 5 hours before the cistern was full. How many hours in total did it take for the two pipes to fill the cistern?
questions.explanation: If it took T hours, P1 ran for T − 5 of them: (T − 5)/20 + T/30 = 1, so 3T − 15 + 2T = 60 and T = 15.

questions.text: The ratio of boys to girls initial in a college is 5 : 6. If 40 boys leave the college and 50 girls join the college, the ratio will become 8 : 11. Find the number of girls (initial) in the college.
questions.explanation: With 5x boys and 6x girls: (5x − 40)/(6x + 50) = 8/11, so 55x − 440 = 48x + 400, x = 120 and there were 6 × 120 = 720 girls.

questions.text: From a point A, a tangent line is drawn to the circle of radius 7 units. From the same point, a secant is drawn to the circle which cuts the circle at B and C and the point B is near A than C. What is the length of BC in units if the length of the tangent to the circle from point A is 21 units and the length of AB is 14 units?
questions.explanation: Tangent² = AB × AC, so 21² = 14 × AC and AC = 31.5. BC = AC − AB = 31.5 − 14 = 17.5. (The radius is not needed.)

questions.text: Pranav borrows a sum of ₹598397 at the rate of 20% per annum simple interest. At the end of the first year, he repays ₹24284 towards return of principal amount borrowed. If Pranav clears all pending dues at the end of the second year, including interest payment that accrued during the first year, how much does he pay (in ₹) at the end of the second year?
questions.explanation: First-year interest: 20% of ₹598397 = ₹119679.40. After he repays ₹24284, ₹574113 is owed, with second-year interest of ₹114822.60. He pays 574113 + 119679.40 + 114822.60 = ₹808615.

questions.text: A class of 30 students appeared in a test. The average score of 12 students is 62, and that of the rest is 68. What is the average score of the class?
If the area of a sector of a circle is 462 cm² and the central angle is 120°, then its radius is ____.
Which of the following numbers is NOT divisible by 8?
questions.explanation: 7497 is odd, so it cannot be divisible by 8. The others are: 5544 = 8 × 693, 7344 = 8 × 918 and 4608 = 8 × 576.

questions.text: A cooker is marked at ₹12,500. The dealer allows successive discounts of 6%, 6% and 4% on it. What is the net selling price of the cooker?

A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 195 metres. When the policeman starts the chase, the thief also starts running. If the speed of the thief is 22 km/h and that of the policeman is 27 km/h, then how far would the thief have run (in m) before he is overtaken?
questions.explanation: The policeman gains 27 − 22 = 5 km/h, so he closes 195 m in 0.195/5 = 0.039 hours. In that time the thief runs 22 × 0.039 = 0.858 km = 858 m.

questions.text: In a kite ABCD, longer diagonal BD is drawn. If ∠ABD = 54° and ∠ADB = 50°, then what is the measure (in degrees) of the ∠DCB?
questions.explanation: ∠ABD ≠ ∠ADB, so AB ≠ AD: the equal sides must be AB = CB and AD = CD, making BD the axis of symmetry. Triangles ABD and CBD are then congruent, so ∠DCB = ∠DAB = 180° − 54° − 50° = 76°.

questions.text: Three candidates X, Y and Z participated in an election. X got 30% more votes than Y, whereas Z got 25% more votes than Y. X also overtook Z by 5000 votes. If 71% of the voters voted and no invalid votes were cast, then what was the total number of voters in the voting list?
questions.explanation: With y votes for Y, X got 1.3y and Z 1.25y, so 0.05y = 5,000 and y = 1,00,000. Votes cast = 3.55y = 3,55,000, which is 71% of the list: 3,55,000/0.71 = 5,00,000.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Appreciate
questions.explanation: To 'appreciate' is to rise in value or to value highly; to 'depreciate' is to fall in value or to belittle.

questions.text: Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the following sentence and select its correct spelling from the given options. The occurence of this phenomenon is quite rare.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'occurrence', with double c and double r.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. The school will hire new teachers.
options: New teachers will join the school.
New teachers are hired by the school.
New teachers will be hired by the school.
The school will be hiring new teachers.
questions.explanation: 'Will hire' becomes 'will be hired', with the object 'new teachers' as the subject.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Magnificent
questions.explanation: 'Magnificent' means impressively beautiful or grand: 'splendid'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The US ________ building was built in the year 1800.
questions.explanation: The building where the US Congress meets is the 'Capitol'; a 'capital' is the city that is the seat of government.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. In some countries, you are not able to drink until you are 21.
questions.explanation: The sentence is about permission, not ability: 'you are not allowed to drink until you are 21'.

questions.text: Select the term which means the same as the given group of words. A continuing unpleasant situation, created when one problem causes another problem that then makes the first problem worse
questions.explanation: In a 'vicious cycle' (or circle) each problem makes the other worse.

questions.text: Select the option that corrects the error in the given sentence. She sings good.
questions.explanation: A verb is modified by an adverb: 'She sings well', not 'good'.

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the parts in the correct sequence to form a meaningful sentence. (P) society benefits from diversity (Q) enriching cultures and (O) by fostering understanding and empathy (R) perspectives from around the world
questions.explanation: 'Society benefits from diversity (P) by fostering understanding and empathy (O), enriching cultures and (Q) perspectives from around the world (R).'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Lack of interest, enthusiasm or concern
questions.explanation: Apathy is a lack of interest or concern; antipathy is dislike.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The study of ancient things such as art, graves, ruins etc.
questions.explanation: Archaeology studies the human past through remains such as buildings, graves and artefacts.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. No sooner did Mr. Piyahri Mishra finish his chemistry lecture “that the students began to leave”.
options: than the students began to leave.
then the students began to leave.
so the students began to leave.
and the students began to leave.
questions.explanation: 'No sooner' is followed by 'than': 'No sooner did he finish his lecture than the students began to leave.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. An utter state of confusion
questions.explanation: Chaos is complete disorder and confusion.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'beginning'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Miraculous
questions.explanation: 'Miraculous' means so remarkable as to seem a miracle: 'incredible'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. After reflecting on the matter regarding his boss’s selfish attitude, Raju decided to “force himself to perform an unpleasant action in a difficult situation in order to resolve the matter.”
questions.explanation: To 'bite the bullet' is to force oneself to do something unpleasant that cannot be avoided.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Absolve
questions.explanation: To 'absolve' is to declare someone free of blame; its opposite is to 'accuse'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. Meenakshi could have sent a reply.
options: A reply could have been send by Meenakshi.
A reply could have be sent by Meenakshi.
A reply could have been sent by Meenakshi.
A reply could have sent by Meenakshi.
questions.explanation: 'Could have sent' becomes 'could have been sent', with the past participle 'sent'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Beseech
questions.explanation: To 'beseech' is to beg earnestly: 'implore'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A person who has supreme power or authority
questions.explanation: A sovereign holds supreme power or authority.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Augmented reality and virtual reality are two types of reality technologies that either augment or replace a real-world environment with a (1)________ one. In augmented reality, a virtual environment coexists (2)________ the actual world, to be instructive and offer more data about the real world that a user can access without having to search. When a handset is pointed at a piece of malfunctioning (3)________, for example, industrial AR apps might provide rapid troubleshooting information. Virtual reality is a (4)________ environmental simulation that completely replaces the user's surroundings with a totally virtual world. For example, VR may provide a user with a box containing a cartoon (5)________ of Mike Tyson in a virtual boxing ring.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: AR and VR either add to a real-world environment or replace it with a 'simulated' one.
