He was (5)_________ for a while.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Having lost his cat, the boy was 'inconsolable', too upset to be comforted.

questions.text: Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it. First row: 24, 12, 27 Second row: 29, 13, 64 Third row: 32, 24, ? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the number into its constituent digits. For example, 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In each row the third number is the cube of a quarter of the difference of the first two: (24 − 12)/4 = 3 and 3³ = 27; (29 − 13)/4 = 4 and 4³ = 64. So (32 − 24)/4 = 2 and 2³ = 8.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'LETTUCE' is written as 'ECUTTEL' and ‘PEPPERS’ is written as ‘SREPPEP’. How will 'PARSNIP' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each word is written backwards: LETTUCE → ECUTTEL and PEPPERS → SREPPEP. So PARSNIP → PINSRAP.

questions.text: Seven friends S, T, U, V, W, X and Y, each has a different age. W is older than X but younger than V. Only three people are older than V. T is older than U but younger than S. Y is the youngest among all. How many persons are younger than U?
questions.explanation: Only three people are older than V, so V is fourth oldest; W and X come below V, and Y is youngest, so W, X and Y take the last three places. S, T and U (S > T > U) take the top three, so U is third oldest and four people (V, W, X, Y) are younger.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. EVIDENT : NTIDEEV :: DYNAMIC : ICNAMDY :: FICTION : ?
questions.explanation: The last two letters move to the front, the middle three stay and the first two go to the end: EV IDE NT → NT IDE EV and DY NAM IC → IC NAM DY. So FI CTI ON → ON CTI FI: ONCTIFI.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 1024, 1032, 1059, 1123, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are cubes: +8 (2³), +27 (3³), +64 (4³), so next +125 (5³): 1123 + 125 = 1248.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 25 * 5 * 10 * 2 * 8 * 17
Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? OLJB, ?, IVDL, FAAQ, CFXV
questions.explanation: First letters move back 3 (O, L, I, F, C), second letters forward 5 (L, Q, V, A, F), third letters back 3 (J, G, D, A, X) and fourth letters forward 5 (B, G, L, Q, V): LQGG.

questions.text: The second number in the given number pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number pairs except one. Find that odd number pair.
questions.explanation: The second number is the square root of the first minus 2: √169 − 2 = 11, √36 − 2 = 4 and √9 − 2 = 1. √25 − 2 = 3, not 5, so 25 : 5 is the odd pair.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 16, 32, 29, ?, 111, 666

Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 6 : 24 :: 9 : 54 :: 12 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is two-thirds of the square of the first: 6² × 2/3 = 24 and 9² × 2/3 = 54. Likewise 12² × 2/3 = 96.

questions.text: If P denotes ‘×’, Q denotes ‘÷’, R denotes ‘+’ and S denotes ‘−’, then what will come in place of ‘?’ in the following equation? (128 Q 8) R (5 P 7) S 23 R (18 P 2) = ?
Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 48 * 12 * 625 * 25 * 21
questions.explanation: 48 ÷ 12 = 625 ÷ 25 − 21, as both sides equal 4.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 5, 9, 21, 43, 91, 185, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is double the one before plus −1, 3, 1, 5, 3 and 7 in turn (the added number goes up 4 and down 2 alternately): 5 × 2 − 1 = 9, 9 × 2 + 3 = 21, 21 × 2 + 1 = 43, 43 × 2 + 5 = 91, 91 × 2 + 3 = 185, so 185 × 2 + 7 = 377.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? TSXA, XBLT, ?, FTNF, JCBY
questions.explanation: First letters move forward 4 (T, X, B, F, J), second letters forward 9 (S, B, K, T, C), third letters back 12 (X, L, Z, N, B) and fourth letters forward 19 (A, T, M, F, Y): BKZM.

questions.text: The second number in the given number-pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number-pairs EXCEPT one. Find that odd number-pair.
questions.explanation: The second number is half of one more than the square of the first: (3² + 1)/2 = 5, (7² + 1)/2 = 25 and (5² + 1)/2 = 13. (1² + 1)/2 = 1, not 2, so 1 : 2 is the odd pair.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘BRIGHT’ is written as ‘IYTRGS’ and ‘LOCATE’ is written as ‘LOZXVG’. How will ‘COSTLY’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter becomes its opposite in the alphabet (A ↔ Z, B ↔ Y and so on) and each pair of letters is then swapped: LOCATE → OLXZGV → LOZXVG. So COSTLY → XLHGOB → LXGHBO.

questions.text: The average of five numbers, given in a particular order, is 32. The average of the first three numbers is 28, while that of the last three numbers is 34. What is the average of the first two numbers?
questions.explanation: The five numbers add to 160, the first three to 84 and the last three to 102. 84 + 102 − 160 = 26 is the middle number, counted twice, so the first two add to 84 − 26 = 58: average 29.

questions.text: Find the principal amount if the interest compounded annually at the rate of 10% for two years is ₹4,200.
questions.explanation: Compound interest for 2 years at 10% is P(1.1² − 1) = 0.21P = ₹4,200, so P = ₹20,000.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers is NOT divisible by 75?
questions.explanation: 75 = 3 × 25, so a multiple of 75 must end in 00, 25, 50 or 75 and have a digit sum divisible by 3. 163750 ends in 50, but its digit sum is 22, so it is not divisible by 3 or by 75.

questions.text: The area of two similar triangles XYZ and ABC are 361 cm² and 225 cm², respectively. If the longest side of the larger ∆ XYZ be 38 cm, then what is the length (in cm) of the longest side of the smaller ∆ ABC?
questions.explanation: The areas of similar triangles are in the ratio of the squares of their sides, so the sides are in the ratio √361 : √225 = 19 : 15. The longest side of ΔABC is 38 × 15/19 = 30 cm.

questions.text: "The difference between the CI and the SI on a sum of money lent for 2 years at 20% interest per annum is ₹ 80. The sum is:"
The price of a book is first increased by 8% and later decreased by 8%. What is the percentage change in the price of the book?
questions.explanation: 1.08 × 0.92 = 0.9936 of the original price: a decrease of 0.64% (8² ÷ 100).

questions.text: A book with a marked price of ₹600 is available at a discount of 18%. What is the discount given?
The price of a pen is first increased by 15% and later on the price was decreased by 20% due to reduction in sales. Find the net percentage change in the final price of a pen.
questions.explanation: 1.15 × 0.80 = 0.92 of the original price: a net change of −8%.

questions.text: Simplify the following expression. (0.14×0.14)-(2×0.14×5.14)+(5.14×5.14)
questions.explanation: The expression is a² − 2ab + b² = (b − a)² with a = 0.14 and b = 5.14: (5.14 − 0.14)² = 5² = 25.

questions.text: An athlete crosses a distance of 3600 m in 12 minutes. What is his speed (in km/h)?
questions.explanation: 3600 m = 3.6 km and 12 minutes = 1/5 hour, so the speed is 3.6 × 5 = 18 km/h.

questions.text: Which of the following ratios is the smallest? 3 : 4, 1 : 2 , 2 : 5, 1 : 3
questions.explanation: As fractions: 3/4 = 0.75, 1/2 = 0.5, 2/5 = 0.4 and 1/3 ≈ 0.33, so 1 : 3 is the smallest.

questions.text: A shopkeeper sells rice at cost price but uses a faulty weighing machine and thus gains a profit of 25%. Find how many grams rice he is giving in 1 kg ?
questions.explanation: Giving x g for the price of 1,000 g yields a 25% profit when 1000/x = 1.25, so x = 800 g.

questions.text: The average salary per head of all the workers in a workshop is ₹8,850. If the average salary per head of 9 technicians is ₹10,000, and the average salary per head of the rest is ₹7,780, find the total number of workers in the workshop.(Consider integral part only)
questions.explanation: With n workers: 8,850n = 9 × 10,000 + (n − 9) × 7,780, so 1,070n = 19,980 and n = 18.67; the integral part is 18.

questions.text: In the early 1900s, which German climatologist divided the world's climate into different categories based on temperature, amount of rainfall and the time of year when rainfall occurs?
questions.explanation: Wladimir Köppen's classification, set out around 1900 and revised later, groups climates by temperature, the amount of rainfall and the season in which it falls.

questions.text: Ustad Allah Rakha was famous for playing the ___________.
questions.explanation: Ustad Allah Rakha, father of Zakir Hussain, was a celebrated tabla player who often accompanied Ravi Shankar.

questions.text: Who among the following, after winning the Russian Grand Prix 2021, became the first F1 driver to win 100 races?
questions.explanation: Lewis Hamilton's win at the 2021 Russian Grand Prix in Sochi was his 100th in Formula One, the first time any driver had reached 100.

questions.text: Pt Bhimsen Joshi is associated with which of the following?
questions.explanation: Pandit Bhimsen Joshi was a Hindustani classical vocalist of the Kirana gharana.

questions.text: Which is the toxin-causing bacterium that spoils cream, cheese and milk and makes them taste bitter, sour or bitter?
questions.explanation: Bacillus cereus produces toxins and spoils dairy products, curdling milk and giving it a bitter taste. Streptococcus thermophilus, Bifidobacterium and Lactobacillus plantarum are beneficial bacteria used in yoghurt, cheese and probiotics.

questions.text: Which north bank tributary of the Ganges River comprises of two streams, namely Kaligandak and Trishulganga?
questions.explanation: The Gandak, formed by the Kaligandak and the Trishulganga, rises in Nepal and joins the Ganga at Sonpur, near Patna.

questions.text: Guru MK Saroja has been conferred with the Padma Shri for the relentless pursuit of which of the following dances?
questions.explanation: Guru M. K. Saroja, a Bharatanatyam dancer and teacher from Chennai, received the Padma Shri in 2011.

questions.text: ‘The Autobiography of an Unknown Indian’ is the autobiography of _____.
questions.explanation: 'The Autobiography of an Unknown Indian' (1951) is Nirad C. Chaudhuri's account of his early life.

questions.text: V Satyanarayana Sarma, an exponent of the Kuchipudi dance form was conferred which of the following awards by the Government of India?
questions.explanation: Vedantam Satyanarayana Sarma, a Kuchipudi dancer famous for female roles such as Satyabhama, received the Padma Shri in 1970.

questions.text: What is a biotechnological process accomplished by yeast, some type of bacteria, or some other microorganism to convert sugar into ethyl alcohol and carbon dioxide?
questions.explanation: In alcoholic fermentation, yeast and some bacteria break down sugars such as glucose into ethyl alcohol and carbon dioxide without oxygen.

questions.text: The ‘Kalidas Samman’ is awarded by the government of which of the following Indian states?
questions.explanation: The Kalidas Samman is presented by the Government of Madhya Pradesh.

questions.text: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek was known for which discovery in late 17th century?
options: Discovery of the properties of a stem cell
Discovery of the role of ATP as the source of energy for cells
Discovery of nucleus in the cell
questions.explanation: Using microscopes he made himself, Antonie van Leeuwenhoek was the first to observe bacteria and protozoa, which he called 'animalcules'.

questions.text: Who among the following Indian music composers and singers, who is popular by nickname ‘the Mozart of Madras’, was placed in The Time’s list of the world’s most influential people in 2009?
questions.explanation: A. R. Rahman, called 'the Mozart of Madras', was named in Time's 2009 list of the world's 100 most influential people.

questions.text: The ‘Room on the roof’ a novel about an orphaned English boy living with his guardian is written by whom among the following authors?
questions.explanation: 'The Room on the Roof', Ruskin Bond's first novel, follows Rusty, an orphaned boy who leaves his strict guardian's home in Dehra.

questions.text: Which of the following Indian cities will host the International Olympic Committee session in 2023?
questions.explanation: Mumbai hosted the 141st IOC Session in October 2023, the first in India since New Delhi's in 1983.

questions.text: The historical fiction novel ‘The King Within’ is authored by:
questions.explanation: 'The King Within' is a historical novel by Nandini Sengupta.

questions.text: Who among the following was appointed as the head coach of the Indian cricket team in November 2021?
questions.explanation: Rahul Dravid was appointed head coach of the Indian men's cricket team in November 2021, succeeding Ravi Shastri after the T20 World Cup.

questions.text: Identify the word that means vertical columns of Periodic Table.
questions.explanation: The vertical columns of the periodic table are groups; the horizontal rows are periods.

questions.text: Vedantam Satyanarayana Sarma was an exponent of which Indian classical dance form?
questions.explanation: Vedantam Satyanarayana Sarma was a Kuchipudi dancer, famous for female roles such as Satyabhama.

questions.text: Where is the JRD Tata Sports Complex located?
questions.explanation: The JRD Tata Sports Complex is in Jamshedpur, Jharkhand.

questions.text: A judge of the High Court retires at the age of _____.
questions.explanation: Under Article 217 a High Court judge holds office until the age of 62; Supreme Court judges retire at 65.

questions.text: The Regional Rural Banks Act was passed in __________.
questions.explanation: Regional Rural Banks were first set up in 1975 under an ordinance, which the Regional Rural Banks Act replaced in 1976.

questions.text: Dr. Purushottam Dadheech, who was awarded the prestigious Padma Shri award in 2020, is associated with which of the following dance forms?
questions.explanation: Purushottam Dadheech, a Kathak guru from Madhya Pradesh, received the Padma Shri in 2020.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. The “train was already left” before we reached the platform.
questions.explanation: An action completed before another past action takes the past perfect: 'The train had already left before we reached the platform.'

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph A. The two children were so like, that without much difficulty it could not be discerned of their proper parents, which was Titus from Gisippus, or Gisippus from Titus. B. There was in the city of Rome a noble senator, named Fulvius, who sent his son, called Titus, being a child, to the city of Athens, in Greece (which was the fountain of all manner of doctrine), there to learn good letters : and caused him to be hosted with a worshipful mart of that city, called Chremes. C. This Chremes happened to have also a son named Gisippus, who not only was equal to the said young Titus in years, but also in stature, proportion of body, favour, and colour of visage, countenance and speech D. These two young gentlemen, as they seemed to be one in form and personage, so shortly after acquaintance, the same nature wrought in their hearts such a mutual affection, and their wills and appetites daily more and more so confederated themselves, that it seemed none other, when their names were declared, but that they had only changed their places, issuing (as I might say) out of the one body, and entering into the other.
questions.explanation: B introduces Fulvius sending his son Titus to Athens to live with Chremes, C introduces Chremes' son Gisippus and his likeness to Titus, A says the two could hardly be told apart, and D describes their friendship: BCAD.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Absurd
questions.explanation: 'Absurd' means wildly unreasonable or foolish; its opposite is 'sensible'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Quintessential
questions.explanation: 'Quintessential' means representing the most perfect or typical example of something: 'typical'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. Their behaviour vexes us.
options: We had been vexed by their behaviour.
We are vexed by their behaviour.
We have been vexed by their behaviour.
We are being vexed by their behaviour
questions.explanation: The present simple 'vexes' becomes 'are vexed', with the object 'us' as the subject: 'We are vexed by their behaviour.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To bite the bullet
options: To reject doing something difficult or unpleasant
To be brave in a difficult situation
questions.explanation: To 'bite the bullet' is to face something difficult or unpleasant with courage.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'succession'.

questions.text: Complete the sentence with an appropriate ANTONYM of the word mentioned in the bracket. Many Bollywood movies show _________(cheerful) stories nowadays.
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'cheerful' is 'gloomy'; 'chirpy', 'radiant' and 'jaunty' are all close to 'cheerful'.

questions.text: Spot the error in the given sentence and select the correct sentence from the options given. When the villagers put up a firm resistance to the fearsome bandit with all their might, he ultimately fleed the spot
options: When the villagers put up a firm resistance to the fearsome bandit with all their might, he ultimately flew the spot.
When the villagers putted up a firm resistance to the fearsome bandit with all their might, he ultimately fleed the spot.
When the villagers put up a firm resistance to the fearsome bandit with all their might, he ultimately flown the spot.
When the villagers put up a firm resistance to the fearsome bandit with all their might, he ultimately fled the spot.
questions.explanation: The past tense of 'flee' is 'fled': 'he ultimately fled the spot'. 'Put' does not change in the past tense, and 'flew' and 'flown' belong to 'fly'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The art of beautiful handwriting
questions.explanation: Calligraphy is the art of beautiful handwriting; epigraphy is the study of inscriptions.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. I can see lots of colours “on” the picture.
questions.explanation: What is shown in a picture is 'in' it: 'I can see lots of colours in the picture.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The work inscribed on the tomb in the memory of the person
questions.explanation: An epitaph is the words inscribed on a tomb in memory of the person buried there; an epigraph is an inscription, or a quotation at the start of a book.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. The meal is being prepared by the chef.
options: The chef is preparing the meal.
The chef will prepare the meal.
The chef did prepare the meal.
The chef was preparing the meal.
questions.explanation: The present continuous passive 'is being prepared by' becomes the active 'is preparing', with the agent as the subject: 'The chef is preparing the meal.'

questions.text: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The app gets Larry’s parents involved in the learning and improvement process, sending them advice about Larry’s behaviours and progress, and recommending motivational _______ they might undertake that are _______ to Larry’s situation and the program’s _________ about his attitudes and behaviours.
questions.explanation: The app recommends motivational 'interventions' (actions meant to bring about change) that are 'targeted' to Larry's situation and to the program's 'inferences' (conclusions) about his attitudes and behaviours.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underline segment in the given sentence. I cannot “sit up with” this sort of insult in office.
questions.explanation: To 'put up with' something is to tolerate it: 'I cannot put up with this sort of insult in office.'

questions.text: Select the correct homonym from the given options to fill in the blank. The athlete’s________ was badly injured due to a fall on the track.
questions.explanation: An athlete can injure a 'toe', part of the foot; 'tow' (to pull) sounds the same but means something else.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. She swallowed ______ her breakfast in a hurry.
questions.explanation: Food is swallowed 'down', here gulped in a hurry; 'swallow up' means to engulf or use up completely, as in 'costs swallowed up the profit'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. One of the most devastating periods in European history came (1)_______ the fourteenth century, with the epidemic of bubonic plague, also known as the ‘Great Plague’ and later dubbed the ‘Black Death’. At the time of its first pandemic, the bubonic plague was a terrifying disease, killing indiscriminately and (2)________ cities and towns devastated in its wake. It appeared to spread just by touching clothes and people who (3)_____ healthy one day might be dead the next. Faced with such a mysterious and horrifying illness, many believed that this was a divine (4)_________ for their sins. Researchers in Hong Kong at the end of the nineteenth century discovered that the disease is caused by the bacteria ‘Yersinia Pestis’. Modern (5)_______ practices and medicine have greatly subdued the impact of the bubonic plague, but have never completely eliminated it.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: A period of time takes 'during': the devastating period 'came during the fourteenth century'.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. ANOXIC : ONACIX :: EQUITY : UQEYTI :: REFUND : ?
questions.explanation: Each half of the word is reversed: ANO XIC → ONA CIX and EQU ITY → UQE YTI. So REF UND → FER DNU: FERDNU.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 3 : 19::2 : 7::5 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is the cube of the first minus the cube of one less: 3³ − 2³ = 19 and 2³ − 1³ = 7. Likewise 5³ − 4³ = 125 − 64 = 61.

questions.text: Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it. First row:7, 9, 39; Second row:4, 8, 28; Third row:6, 7, ? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the number into its constituent digits. For example, 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In each row the third number is three times the first plus twice the second: 3 × 7 + 2 × 9 = 39 and 3 × 4 + 2 × 8 = 28. So 3 × 6 + 2 × 7 = 32.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 14, 28, 31, ?, 129, 774
Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 249, 255, 238, ?, 227, 277
questions.explanation: The differences are +6, −17, +28, −39, +50: they alternate in sign and grow by 11. So 238 + 28 = 266, and 266 − 39 = 227.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) in the following series? UYBD, ZDGI, ? , JNQS
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 5 places forward: UYBD → ZDGI → EILN → JNQS.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? IZDK, OHVO, UPNS, AXFW, ?
questions.explanation: The first letters are the vowels in turn (I, O, U, A, E); the second move 8 places forward (Z, H, P, X, F), the third 8 back (D, V, N, F, X) and the fourth 4 forward (K, O, S, W, A). So EFXA.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘PEN’ is written as ‘OCK’, and ‘ZEN’ is written as ‘YCK’. How will ‘TON’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move back 1, 2 and 3 places: P → O, E → C, N → K. So T → S, O → M, N → K: SMK.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that, when sequentially placed from left to right in the blanks below, will complete the letter series. C _ _ r E _ t C U r _ _ n t C _ r _ E n t
options: E r n r E U r
U r U r E U r
U r n r U U r
U r n r E U r
questions.explanation: With U, r, n, r, E, U, r in the blanks, 'CUrrEnt' repeats three times: CUrrEnt CUrrEnt CUrrEnt.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in an English dictionary. 1.Sarcastic 2.Satisfaction 3.Salutation 4.Sanctions 5.Sacrifice
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Sacrifice (5), Salutation (3), Sanctions (4), Sarcastic (1), Satisfaction (2). 'Sac', 'Sal', 'San', 'Sar' and 'Sat' come in that order.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 45*17*3*41*81*9*56
Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 65*50*5*2*4*63
In a certain code language, ‘KITCHEN’ is written as NJUDIFK’ and ‘RESPECT’ is written as ‘TFTQFDR’. How will ‘WELCOME’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The first and last letters swap places and the letters between them move one place forward: K ITCHE N → N JUDIF K and R ESPEC T → T FTQFD R. So W ELCOM E → E FMDPN W: EFMDPNW.

questions.text: The second number in the given number pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number pairs except one. Find that odd number pair.
questions.explanation: The second number is the cube of half the first plus 1: 14 → 8³ = 512, 22 → 12³ = 1728 and 38 → 20³ = 8000. For 46 that gives 24³ = 13824, not 12167 (23³), so 46 : 12167 is the odd pair.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 93*65*3*56*14*146

The second number in the given number-pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number-pairs EXCEPT one. Find that odd number-pair.
questions.explanation: The second number is the square root of the first minus 3: √25 − 3 = 2, √225 − 3 = 12 and √169 − 3 = 10. √64 − 3 = 5, not 6, so 64 : 6 is the odd pair.

questions.text: If 28 February 2020 was Friday, then what was the day of the week on 30 December 2015?
questions.explanation: From 30 December 2019 to 28 February 2020 is 60 days, or 4 odd days, so 30 December 2019 was a Monday. Each year back moves the day back 1, or 2 across 29 February 2016: Sunday in 2018, Saturday in 2017, Friday in 2016 and Wednesday on 30 December 2015.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 134,186,238,290,342,?
questions.explanation: Each term is 52 more than the one before: 342 + 52 = 394.

questions.text: Seven friends S, T, U, V, W, X and Y, each has a different height. W is taller than X but shorter than V. Only three people are taller than V. T is taller than U but shorter than S. Y is the shortest among all. How many persons are taller than U?
questions.explanation: Three are taller than V, so V is fourth. W and X are shorter than V (W taller than X) and Y is the shortest, so W, X and Y are fifth to seventh. The top three are then S, T and U in that order (S > T > U), so two people are taller than U.

questions.text: In an examination, Gopal secured 15% more marks than Asha, and Asha secured 10% more marks than Sachin. How much per cent more marks did Gopal secure than Sachin?
questions.explanation: Gopal's marks are 1.15 × 1.10 = 1.265 times Sachin's: 26.5% more.

questions.text: Pranjal takes twice as much time as Vikram or thrice as much time as Ashwin to finish a piece of work. Working together, they can finish the work in 6 days. Vikram can do the work alone in:
questions.explanation: If Pranjal takes 6x days, Vikram takes 3x and Ashwin 2x. Together they do 1/(6x) + 1/(3x) + 1/(2x) = 6/(6x) = 1/x of the work a day, so x = 6 and Vikram takes 3 × 6 = 18 days.

questions.text: If 60% of a number is equal to three-fourth of another number, what is the ratio of the first number to the second number?
It is given that the average of 19 numbers is 8.5. If one number with value 63 was entered incorrectly as 25, then the corrected average is:
questions.explanation: The sum was 19 × 8.5 = 161.5; putting 63 in place of 25 adds 38, giving 199.5. 199.5 ÷ 19 = 10.5.

questions.text: The volume of a sphere is 38808 cm³. What is its surface area (in cm²)? (Take π = 22/7)
Which of the following numbers is divisible by 360?
questions.explanation: 360 = 8 × 9 × 5. 171720 ends in 0, its last three digits (720) are divisible by 8 and its digit sum (18) by 9. The digit sums of the others (20, 15, 17) are not multiples of 9.

questions.text: Under a sale offer, Suresh was offered 20% discount on the part of the marked price that was paid in cash, but was charged 0.5% on the part of the marked price paid through a credit card. If Suresh paid 40% of the marked price in cash and the rest through a credit card, what percentage of the marked price was his total final payment?
questions.explanation: Cash: 40% × 0.8 = 32% of the marked price. Card: 60% × 1.005 = 60.3%. Total 92.3%.

questions.text: A woman can row 36 km downstream in 4 hours and 49 km upstream in 7 hours. What is the speed of the current?
questions.explanation: Downstream speed = 36/4 = 9 km/h and upstream = 49/7 = 7 km/h. The current is (9 − 7)/2 = 1 km/h.

questions.text: The marked price of a cell phone is ₹23,000. The shopkeeper offers successive discounts of 14% and 16%. How much, approximately, does a customer have to pay?

The expenses of a family on rice, vegetables and cooking oil are in the ratio 9 : 11 : 5. If the prices of these items increases by 10%, 20% and 30%, respectively, then the total expenses of the family on these items will increase by:
A library has an average of 330 visitors on Sundays and 240 on the other days. Find the average of the number of visitors per day in a month of 30 days, beginning with a Saturday.
questions.explanation: A 30-day month starting on a Saturday has Sundays on days 2, 9, 16, 23 and 30: five. Average = (5 × 330 + 25 × 240)/30 = 7,650/30 = 255.

questions.text: Three smaller cubes with sides of 3, 4, and 5 cm are melted together to form a large cube. What is the ratio of the smaller cubes' total surface area to the larger cube's total surface area?
questions.explanation: The small cubes' surface areas total 6(9 + 16 + 25) = 300 cm². Their volumes total 27 + 64 + 125 = 216 cm³, so the large cube has side 6 cm and surface area 216 cm². 300 : 216 = 25 : 18.

questions.text: Rajesh purchased a machine for ₹5,000 and paid ₹250 for its transportation. If he sells the machine for ₹5,075, what is his percentage profit or loss? (Correct to two decimal places)
The effective annual rate of interest, corresponding to a nominal rate of 6% per annum, compounded half-yearly, is:
questions.explanation: 6% a year compounded half-yearly is 3% a half-year: 1.03² = 1.0609, an effective annual rate of 0.0609 (6.09%).

questions.text: An arc on a circle that is 18 cm long, subtends a 28.8° angle at the centre. What is the circumference of the circle?
questions.explanation: 28.8° is 28.8/360 = 0.08 of the circle, so the circumference is 18/0.08 = 225 cm.

questions.text: Find the volume of the cylinder circumscribing a sphere with a diameter of 14 cm. (Use π=22/7)
questions.explanation: The cylinder has the sphere's radius, 7 cm, and its diameter as height, 14 cm: V = (22/7) × 7² × 14 = 2156 cm³.

questions.text: A sum of money was invested at 10% interest per year, compounded half-yearly for 18 months. If the amount payable on maturity was ₹83,349, what was the sum invested?
questions.explanation: Half-yearly for 18 months is 3 periods at 5%: P × 1.05³ = P × 1.157625 = ₹83,349, so P = ₹72,000.

questions.text: Alarmel Velli is recognised as a classical dancer of ________ dance form.
questions.explanation: Alarmel Valli is one of India's leading Bharatanatyam dancers, of the Pandanallur style.

questions.text: Identify the alga that is NOT a marine algae.
questions.explanation: Chlorella is a single-celled green alga of fresh water. Sargassum, Porphyra and Laminaria are seaweeds.

questions.text: In the given main characteristics of farming of India, which is the characteristic of primitive subsistence farming?
questions.explanation: Primitive subsistence farming is done on small plots with simple tools, often as slash-and-burn (shifting) cultivation. Chemical fertilisers, pesticides and high-yielding seeds belong to intensive and commercial farming.

questions.text: Who among the following personalities, also associated with poetry and Music has been conferred with the Noble Prize?
questions.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore, poet and composer of Rabindrasangeet, won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913.

questions.text: ‘The Palace of Illusions’ is an award-winning novel that retells the Hindu mythological epic Mahabharata from the perspective of Draupadi, it’s lead female character. Who among the following is the author of this novel?
questions.explanation: Chitra Banerjee Divakaruni wrote 'The Palace of Illusions', the Mahabharata told by Draupadi.

questions.text: Who among the following won the ‘Dronacharya Award’ (Regular Category) 2021 in Athletics discipline?
questions.explanation: Radhakrishnan Nair P, deputy chief coach of India's athletics team, received the Dronacharya Award (Regular Category) in 2021.

questions.text: Which singer, music director was awarded with the Padma Vibhushan posthumously in 2021?
questions.explanation: S. P. Balasubrahmanyam, who died in September 2020, was awarded the Padma Vibhushan posthumously in 2021.

questions.text: Identify the shallowest part of the ocean.
questions.explanation: The continental shelf, the gently sloping edge of a continent under the sea, is the shallowest part of the ocean floor; the slope, the deep-sea plains and the trenches lie progressively deeper.

questions.text: What was India's ranking in Paralympic 2020 medal tally?
questions.explanation: India won 19 medals at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics (5 gold, 8 silver, 6 bronze) and finished 24th in the medal table.

questions.text: Which of the following dance forms is performed by Sonal Mansingh?
questions.explanation: Sonal Mansingh is known for both Bharatanatyam and Odissi.

questions.text: Name the classical dancer who is associated with the Kuchipudi classical dance.
questions.explanation: Vempati Chinna Satyam was one of the great gurus of Kuchipudi.

questions.text: Who among the following is an outstanding player to have mastered the surbahar instrument?
questions.explanation: Ustad Imrat Khan was a master of the surbahar, the bass sitar. Ali Akbar Khan played the sarod and Abdul Karim Khan was a vocalist.

questions.text: Part III of the Constitution of India deals with:
questions.explanation: Part III (Articles 12 to 35) deals with the Fundamental Rights; Part II covers citizenship, Part IV the Directive Principles and Part IVA the Fundamental Duties.

questions.text: Which of the following pairs of authors and autobiographies is CORRECTLY matched?
options: Aribam Syam Sharma – Jakhan Choto Chilam
questions.explanation: 'My Times' is the autobiography of J. B. Kripalani. The Baburnama is Babur's memoir, not Jahangir's, and 'Jakhan Choto Chilam' is Satyajit Ray's memoir of his childhood.

questions.text: In November 2021 at Zonal Council Meet, Chief Minister N Rangaswamy made the statement regarding which union territory that upgrading the status of the Union Territory is critical to its survival?
questions.explanation: N. Rangasamy is Chief Minister of Puducherry, the only one of these Union Territories with an elected government; at the Southern Zonal Council meeting in Tirupati he pressed for its statehood.

questions.text: Which of the following leucoplasts store oil and fat?
questions.explanation: Elaioplasts store oils and fats; amyloplasts store starch and aleuroplasts proteins.

questions.text: __________ and _________ are called as narrow and broad money, respectively, in the context of money supply in an economy.
questions.explanation: In the RBI's measures of money supply, M1 (currency with the public plus demand deposits) is narrow money and M3 (M1 plus time deposits with banks) is broad money.

questions.text: Who was appointed as the Chairman of ISRO in January 2022?
questions.explanation: S. Somanath succeeded K. Sivan as Chairman of ISRO in January 2022.

questions.text: Which of the following is the Galilean moon that was observed in 1610 by the Italian astronomer Galileo Galilei using a homemade telescope?
questions.explanation: Ganymede is one of the four moons of Jupiter (with Io, Europa and Callisto) that Galileo discovered in 1610. Phobos orbits Mars, Titan orbits Saturn and Namaka the dwarf planet Haumea.

questions.text: Famous playback singer Kishore Kumar was born in 1929 in _________.
questions.explanation: Kishore Kumar was born on 4 August 1929 in Khandwa, now in Madhya Pradesh.

questions.text: The Amazon River, considered the longest river in the world, with a length of 6,400 km, is located in the northern part of _________.
questions.explanation: The Amazon flows across northern South America, mainly through Peru and Brazil, to the Atlantic. (Most sources rank the Nile as the longest river and the Amazon second; the Amazon carries by far the most water.)

questions.text: Australia won the 2020 ICC Women's T20 World Cup Cricket by defeating _________.
questions.explanation: Australia beat India by 85 runs in the final at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on 8 March 2020.

questions.text: ‘Finding My Way’ is a famous autobiography written by which of the following Gond artists of India with the help of Mukul S Anand?
questions.explanation: 'Finding My Way' is the illustrated autobiography of the Pardhan Gond artist Venkat Raman Singh Shyam, nephew of Jangarh Singh Shyam.

questions.text: Maguni Charan Das was awarded Padma Shri for his contribution to which of the following forms of dances?
questions.explanation: Guru Maguni Charan Das of Raghurajpur, Odisha, received the Padma Shri for Gotipua, the dance performed by young boys dressed as girls.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underline segment in the given sentence. His disease is no doubt very serious but he will “pull over”.
questions.explanation: To 'pull through' is to recover from a serious illness; to 'pull over' is to bring a vehicle to the side of the road.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in the brackets to fill in the blank. Collection of money through illegal means without any hard work increased the ___________ (greed) of the corrupt officials.
questions.explanation: 'Cupidity' is greed, especially for money or possessions.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'instantaneous'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The mother loving looked / at her baby / as the nurse / brought her in.
questions.explanation: The verb 'looked' needs the adverb 'lovingly', not the adjective 'loving': 'The mother looked lovingly at her baby.'

questions.text: In the following passage, a word has been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Growing up in Bengaluru, I have watched the city grow and _______ at its seams, welcoming, as its own, all the _______ population in search of jobs and pleasant _________.
questions.explanation: A growing city 'flexes' (stretches) at its seams as it takes in a 'migrant' population, people who come for jobs and Bengaluru's pleasant 'weather'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Laconic
questions.explanation: 'Laconic' means using very few words: 'concise'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. In this “situation of no organisation and control due to the lack of an effective government,” the rate of crime has increased exponentially.
questions.explanation: Anarchy is a state of disorder in which there is no effective government or control.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Annoy
questions.explanation: To 'annoy' is to irritate; its opposite is to 'comfort'. 'Miff', 'get' and 'ruffle' all mean to annoy.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. When we reached the hill station, it was raining “the heaviest”.
questions.explanation: The verb 'raining' is modified by an adverb, and nothing is being compared, so 'raining heavily'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Strong taste or liking for something
questions.explanation: A penchant is a strong liking or inclination for something.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Start from scratch
options: Start it from the previous situation
Start something fast to finish it before a particular time
questions.explanation: To 'start from scratch' is to begin again from the very beginning, building on nothing done before.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Vain
questions.explanation: 'Vain' means having too high an opinion of oneself; its opposite is 'modest'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. Where can I find the way to the library?
options: Where can they be found in the library?
They cannot be found in the way to library?
Where can the way to the library be found?
Who can found with the way to library?
questions.explanation: The object 'the way to the library' becomes the subject and 'can find' becomes 'can be found'; the agent 'by me' is dropped.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. They “didn’t ate” anything yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'Did' is followed by the base form of the verb: 'They didn't eat anything yesterday.'

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. Premchand wrote this novel.
options: This novel was written by Premchand.
Premchand novel has been written by him.
questions.explanation: The simple past active 'wrote' becomes 'was written': 'This novel was written by Premchand.'

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A.Holi is the festival of colours which is celebrated not only in India but all across the world. B.Then on the next day, people of all ages gather together to play with colours called 'gulal’ and coloured water called 'Dulahandi’. C.People celebrate 'Holika Dahan’ on the first day by gathering around and burning piles of wood and cow dung and singing bhajans related to Holi. D.It is also a festival of unity as it brings people together to celebrate a festival regardless of caste, ethnicity, or religion.
questions.explanation: A introduces Holi, D adds that it is also a festival of unity, C describes the first day (Holika Dahan) and B, opening 'Then on the next day', the second: ADCB.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Resplendent
questions.explanation: 'Resplendent' means splendid and dazzling in appearance: 'magnificent'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Our host started to read and the (1)_________ stopped. There was a sweet (2)_________ as each person read, not one that felt forced or imposed in any way. People did not seem to (3)_________ or cough, but perhaps that is just how I remember it now. I know I was increasingly self-conscious as the readings came closer to me and that when it was my turn I think I (4)_________ through most of it, probably without making any sense of the (5)_________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: When the host started to read, the 'chatter' (idle talk) of the audience stopped.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Our host started to read and the (1)_________ stopped. There was a sweet (2)_________ as each person read, not one that felt forced or imposed in any way. People did not seem to (3)_________ or cough, but perhaps that is just how I remember it now. I know I was increasingly self-conscious as the readings came closer to me and that when it was my turn I think I (4)_________ through most of it, probably without making any sense of the (5)_________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Once the chatter stopped there was a 'silence', sweet because nobody forced it.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Our host started to read and the (1)_________ stopped. There was a sweet (2)_________ as each person read, not one that felt forced or imposed in any way. People did not seem to (3)_________ or cough, but perhaps that is just how I remember it now. I know I was increasingly self-conscious as the readings came closer to me and that when it was my turn I think I (4)_________ through most of it, probably without making any sense of the (5)_________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: The listeners did not 'fidget' (move restlessly) or cough while each person read.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Our host started to read and the (1)_________ stopped. There was a sweet (2)_________ as each person read, not one that felt forced or imposed in any way. People did not seem to (3)_________ or cough, but perhaps that is just how I remember it now. I know I was increasingly self-conscious as the readings came closer to me and that when it was my turn I think I (4)_________ through most of it, probably without making any sense of the (5)_________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: Nervous and self-conscious, the writer 'mumbled' through the reading, as 'without making any sense of' it suggests.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Our host started to read and the (1)_________ stopped. There was a sweet (2)_________ as each person read, not one that felt forced or imposed in any way. People did not seem to (3)_________ or cough, but perhaps that is just how I remember it now. I know I was increasingly self-conscious as the readings came closer to me and that when it was my turn I think I (4)_________ through most of it, probably without making any sense of the (5)_________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Each person took a turn to read aloud, and of the options only 'poetry' is something read; music, dance and pottery are not.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 27,31,42,72,139,?
questions.explanation: The differences are 4, 11, 30, 67, that is 1³ + 3, 2³ + 3, 3³ + 3, 4³ + 3. The next is 5³ + 3 = 128: 139 + 128 = 267.

questions.text: Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some hexagons are rectangles. Some rectangles are decagons. All decagons are rhombuses. Conclusions: I. Some rhombuses are rectangles. II. Some rhombuses are hexagons. III. Some decagons are hexagons.
options: Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions I and III follow
questions.explanation: Some rectangles are decagons and all decagons are rhombuses, so some rectangles are rhombuses: some rhombuses are rectangles (I). Nothing links the hexagons to the decagons or the rhombuses, so II and III do not follow.

questions.text: Pointing to a lady in a photograph, Harsh said, “My wife’s son is the father of her mother’s daughter”. How is the lady related to Harsh?
questions.explanation: Her mother's daughter is the lady herself, and Harsh's wife's son is Harsh's son. So the lady's father is Harsh's son: she is his son's daughter.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? GJWC, JPFO, ?, PBXM, SHGY
questions.explanation: The first letters move +3 (G, J, M, P, S), the second +6 (J, P, V, B, H), the third +9 (W, F, O, X, G) and the fourth +12 (C, O, A, M, Y), wrapping round after Z: MVOA.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'RATE' is written as 'UDWH' and ‘RICH’ is written as ‘ULFK’. How will 'SAVE' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places forward: RATE → UDWH and RICH → ULFK. So SAVE → VDYH.

questions.text: Select the correct option that indicates the arrangement of the following words in a logical and meaningful order. 1- Eat 2- Fruit 3- Seed 4- Pluck 5- Plant
questions.explanation: A seed is sown, it grows into a plant, the plant bears fruit, the fruit is plucked and then eaten: Seed, Plant, Fruit, Pluck, Eat.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must NOT be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Goldsmith : Jewellery :: Cobbler : ?
questions.explanation: A goldsmith makes jewellery; a cobbler makes and mends shoes.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 71*56*14*15*5

Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it. First row - 19, 81, 30 Second row - 42, 57, 107 Third row - 23, 45, ? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: In each row the third number is 3 times the first minus a third of the second: 3 × 19 − 81 ÷ 3 = 57 − 27 = 30 and 3 × 42 − 57 ÷ 3 = 126 − 19 = 107. So 3 × 23 − 45 ÷ 3 = 69 − 15 = 54.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. LEAN : NEAL :: MEAN : NEAM :: HEAR : ?
questions.explanation: The first and last letters swap: LEAN → NEAL and MEAN → NEAM. So HEAR → REAH.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 15 * 2 * 18 * 6 * 3 * 30
If M denotes ‘−’, N denotes ‘÷’, O denotes ‘×’ and P denotes ‘+’, then what will come in place of ‘?’ in the following equation? (81 N 27) O 4 M 21 P 72 P 3 M 3 O 9 = ?
Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 19*4*44*59*61
Select the option that represents the letters that, when placed from left to right in the given blanks, will complete the letter series. _ T Z S S T _ Y S S T T _ S S _ T W _ S
questions.explanation: With T, T, X, T, S in the blanks the series is TTZSS TTYSS TTXSS TTWSS: TT and SS round a middle letter that moves back one each time.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 5 :33 :: 11 : 141 :: 7 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is the square of one more than the first, minus 3: 6² − 3 = 33 and 12² − 3 = 141. Likewise 8² − 3 = 61.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (17, 13, 68) (55, 46, 495) (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed)
questions.explanation: The third number is the first times the difference of the first two: (17 − 13) × 17 = 68 and (55 − 46) × 55 = 495. Likewise (45 − 39) × 45 = 270.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 6 : 218::3 : 56::5 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is 6 times the square of the first, plus 2: 6 × 36 + 2 = 218 and 6 × 9 + 2 = 56. Likewise 6 × 25 + 2 = 152.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fourth term in the same way as the first term is related to the second term and the fifth term is related to the sixth term 7 : 512 :: ? : 2744 :: 15 : 4096
questions.explanation: Each number is paired with the cube of one more than itself: 512 = 8³ (7 + 1) and 4096 = 16³ (15 + 1). 2744 = 14³, so the missing number is 13.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘FATHER’ is written as ‘REHTAF’, and ‘COUPLE’ is written as ‘ELPUOC’. How will ‘REMAIN’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each word is written in reverse: FATHER → REHTAF and COUPLE → ELPUOC. So REMAIN → NIAMER.

questions.text: In an election that was contested by 2 candidates, one candidate got 20% of the total votes and yet lost by 600 votes. What is the total number of votes cast in the election, assuming all votes are valid?
questions.explanation: The loser got 20% and the winner 80%, a margin of 60% of the votes. 60% = 600, so 1,000 votes were cast.

questions.text: Find the average of the numbers 61, 51, 41, 31, 21 and 11.
20 workers can paint 24 walls in 36 days. In how many days can 30 workers paint 20 walls?
questions.explanation: 24 walls take 20 × 36 = 720 worker-days, so one wall takes 30. 20 walls take 600 worker-days: 600/30 = 20 days for 30 workers.

questions.text: An article is sold for ₹840 after two successive discounts of 20% and 30% on its marked price. What is the discount (in ₹)?
questions.explanation: After 20% and then 30% off, 0.8 × 0.7 = 0.56 of the marked price is left: marked price = 840/0.56 = ₹1,500, so the discount is 1,500 − 840 = ₹660.

questions.text: The marked price of a mobile phone is 12% more than its cost price. If a discount of 8% is given on the marked price, then the gain per cent is:
questions.explanation: On a cost price of 100 the marked price is 112 and the selling price 112 × 0.92 = 103.04: a gain of 3.04%.

questions.text: On a certain sum, the difference between the compound interest, compounded annually, and the simple interest at 10% per annum for 3 years is ₹93. The sum is:
If the tax on a commodity is diminished by 20% and its consumption increased by 15%, the revenue decreases by:
questions.explanation: Revenue = tax × consumption: 0.8 × 1.15 = 0.92, a fall of 8%.

questions.text: A train running at the speed of 63 km/h crosses a pole in 24 seconds. What is the length of the train?
questions.explanation: 63 km/h = 63 × 5/18 = 17.5 m/s. Passing a pole, the train covers its own length: 17.5 × 24 = 420 m.

questions.text: The maximum number of 4m × 50 cm × 20 cm slabs that may be stored in a 16m long, 12m wide, and 4m deep trench is:
questions.explanation: The slabs fit exactly: 16/4 = 4 along the length, 12/0.5 = 24 across and 4/0.2 = 20 deep, so 4 × 24 × 20 = 1,920 slabs (768 m³ ÷ 0.4 m³).

questions.text: A girl travels 30 km at a speed of 15 km/h. She travels another 20 km at a speed of 10 km/h. What is her average speed for the entire journey?
Find the 3rd proportional to 9 and 21.
questions.explanation: The third proportional x satisfies 9 : 21 = 21 : x, so x = 21²/9 = 441/9 = 49.

questions.text: How many positive two-digit numbers can be divided by 6?
questions.explanation: The two-digit multiples of 6 run from 12 (6 × 2) to 96 (6 × 16): 16 − 2 + 1 = 15.

questions.text: The average score of a cricket team (of ten players and one captain) is 32. The scores of ten players are: 22, 11, 5, 34, 21, 32, 0, 28, 9 and 53. What is the score of the captain?
questions.explanation: The 11 scores total 11 × 32 = 352. The ten players' scores add up to 215, so the captain scored 352 − 215 = 137.

questions.text: Vishnu sold two items X and Y for ₹600 each, thereby gaining 20% on item X and losing 20% on item Y. Find his overall loss or gain percentage.
questions.explanation: Cost prices: 600/1.2 = ₹500 and 600/0.8 = ₹750, ₹1,250 in all, against sales of ₹1,200. Loss = 50/1,250 = 4%.

questions.text: Which of the following novels is written by Anita Desai?
questions.explanation: 'Clear Light of Day' (1980) is Anita Desai's novel. 'The White Tiger' is by Aravind Adiga and 'The Blue Umbrella' by Ruskin Bond.

questions.text: Identify the correct formula to find the potential difference between two points.
questions.explanation: The potential difference between two points is the work done in moving a unit charge between them: V = W/Q.

questions.text: A mentorship programme to train young authors named 'Young, Upcoming and Versatile Authors' (YUVA) scheme was launched in June 2021. Under the mentorship scheme, a consolidated scholarship of _____________ per month was proposed to be paid for a period of six months per author.
questions.explanation: Under the Ministry of Education's PM-YUVA mentorship scheme, each selected author was to receive ₹50,000 a month for six months.

questions.text: What type of climate do the two island regions of India, Lakshadweep and Andaman and Nicobar Islands experience?
questions.explanation: Lying in the tropics and surrounded by the sea, both island groups are warm and humid all year round, with little seasonal change in temperature.

questions.text: Who is the author of the historical book ‘Delhi: A Novel’?
questions.explanation: Khushwant Singh's 'Delhi: A Novel' (1990) tells the city's history through the centuries. Ahmed Ali wrote 'Twilight in Delhi'.

questions.text: Who among the following is India’s only publicly well-known woman shehnai player?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Bageshwari Qamar. Gauhar Jaan and Rasoolan Bai were singers and Binodini Dasi a stage actress, not shehnai players.

questions.text: Manish Narwal is related to which of the following sports?
questions.explanation: Manish Narwal is a para pistol shooter; he won gold in the mixed 50 m pistol SH1 event at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics.

questions.text: What type of farming is Kumari which is practiced in Western Ghats?
questions.explanation: Kumari is the Western Ghats name for slash-and-burn (shifting) cultivation, a form of primitive subsistence farming; in the north-east it is called jhumming.

questions.text: Which of the following books was awarded the Booker Prize in 2021?
options: No One Is Talking About This
questions.explanation: Damon Galgut's 'The Promise' won the 2021 Booker Prize; the other three were on that year's shortlist.

questions.text: Who among the following won the US Open 2021 men’s tennis singles final?
questions.explanation: Daniil Medvedev beat Novak Djokovic in the 2021 US Open final for his first Grand Slam title.

questions.text: Which Emmy Award-nominated Indian choreographer has won the 10th Annual 'World Choreography Award 2020'?
questions.explanation: Suresh Mukund, founder of the Mumbai dance crew Kings United, won the World Choreography Award 2020 for his work on the television show World of Dance.

questions.text: When the commodity value of money is less than the monetary value of money, it is called _____________.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives credit money: in the usual textbook classification, money whose value as money is greater than its value as a commodity (paper notes, token coins) is credit money, while full-bodied money's two values are equal. Fiat money also has little commodity value, but it is defined by being issued on the government's order, not by this comparison.

questions.text: In February 2022, the Sports Authority of India (SAI) established a para centre under its National Centre of Excellence Scheme at which of the following SAI regional centres?
questions.explanation: SAI set up the para centre at its Gandhinagar regional centre, for para athletics, swimming, powerlifting and table tennis.

questions.text: The book ‘Man Kautuhal’ was compiled by which of the following kings of Medieval India?
questions.explanation: 'Man Kautuhal', a treatise on music, was compiled under Raja Man Singh Tomar of Gwalior (1486-1516), a great patron of dhrupad.

questions.text: Why are species of moss used as fuel?
options: Provide peat that have long been used as fuel
questions.explanation: Sphagnum moss builds up in bogs as peat, which is dried and burnt as fuel.

questions.text: Which of the following microscopic cells are of an amoeboid shape with a distinctive central membrane?
questions.explanation: White blood cells can change shape and move like an amoeba; red blood cells are biconcave discs, guard cells are bean-shaped and nerve cells are long and branched.

questions.text: Oleo gum resin (Asafoetida) can be obtained from:
options: dried latex from the stem of ferula
dried latex from the roots of mango tree
dried latex from the banana leaves
dried latex from the tap root of ferula
questions.explanation: Asafoetida (hing) is the dried latex that oozes from cuts in the thick tap root of Ferula plants.

questions.text: Pandit Shivkumar Sharma is a classical ______ player.
questions.explanation: Pandit Shivkumar Sharma made the santoor, a hammered string instrument from Kashmir, an instrument of the classical concert stage.

questions.text: Who has the right to appoint an inter-state council to promote centre-state and inter-state cooperation?
options: Both the President and Governor together
Both the Prime Minister and Chief Minister together
questions.explanation: Under Article 263 the President may establish an Inter-State Council to advise on disputes and subjects of common interest between the states and the Centre.

questions.text: Which algae produces agar?
questions.explanation: Agar is extracted from red algae such as Gracilaria and Gelidium. Chlorella is a green alga and Sargassum a brown one.

questions.text: Which of the following dance types belong to the northern India?
questions.explanation: Kathak comes from northern India; Kuchipudi is from Andhra Pradesh, Odissi from Odisha and Mohiniyattam from Kerala.

questions.text: Who was the first musician to be awarded the prestigious Bharat Ratna, India’s highest civilian honour?
questions.explanation: The Carnatic singer M S Subbulakshmi received the Bharat Ratna in 1998, the first musician to do so; Ravi Shankar followed in 1999.

questions.text: Shovana Narayan, a Padma Shri awardee, is a dancer of which of the following classical dance forms of India?
questions.explanation: Shovana Narayan is a leading exponent of Kathak.

questions.text: Spot the error in the given sentence and select the correct sentence from the options given. When it was time to chose between staying or leaving the country, she choose to stay back.
options: When it was time to choose between staying or leaving the country, she chose to stay back.
When it was time to chose between staying or leaving the country, she chose to stay back.
When it was time to choice between staying or leaving the country, she choose to stay back.
When it was time to have chose between staying or leaving the country, she chose to stay back.
questions.explanation: After 'to' the verb takes its base form, 'to choose', and the main clause needs the past tense, 'she chose'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The Young Global Leaders Community is an________for a dynamic community of exceptional people with the vision, courage, and influence to drive positive change in the world.
questions.explanation: An 'accelerator' speeds things up, which fits a community meant to drive positive change; an 'impediment' would hold it back.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'avarice'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. Looking for her father, Minu finally reached the “area where animals are slaughtered for the market.”
questions.explanation: An abattoir is a slaughterhouse. An apiary is where bees are kept, an arsenal stores weapons and an archive keeps records.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Constructive thinking should be developed through _________ reading.
questions.explanation: Wide, 'extensive' reading develops constructive thinking, which 'narrow' or 'brief' reading would limit; 'avid' (eager) says how keen the reader is, not how widely they read.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Up in arms
questions.explanation: To be 'up in arms' is to protest angrily, in revolt: 'in rebellion'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech. Gogol offered me to go to the market in his car.
options: “Let me take you to the market,” Gogol offered.
“Can I take to the market,” Gogol asked me.
“Let’s go to the market in my car,” Gogol told me.
“Can you come with me to the market,” Gogol asked me.
questions.explanation: In direct speech the offer becomes Gogol's own suggestion, with 'his car' turned into 'my car': 'Let's go to the market in my car.' The other options drop the car or turn the offer into a question.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. A lot has been learnt from my experiences.
options: I will learn a lot from my experiences.
I would learn a lot from my experiences.
I have learnt a lot from my experiences.
I will have learnt a lot from my experiences.
questions.explanation: 'Has been learnt' is the present perfect passive; in the active the doer, 'I' (from 'my experiences'), becomes the subject: 'I have learnt a lot from my experiences.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. to renovate or improve
questions.explanation: To 'revamp' something is to renovate or improve it; to 'revalue' it is to set a new value on it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Cut straight to the chase
options: Allow to introduce an unimportant part
Avoid unnecessary introduction and go to the more important part
Avoid the most important part of text
Disallow important introduction and go to the least important part
questions.explanation: To 'cut to the chase' is to skip the preliminaries and come straight to the point.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. “Its” time we left to the airport.
questions.explanation: The sentence needs 'it's' (it is): 'It's time we left'. 'Its' is the possessive.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. To work as a journeyman he needed to have had the seven years of apprenticeship under his belt. B. Under advice from his well-wishers at the University, Watt proceeded to London to learn his trade. C. Watt made acquaintances with folks at the University of Glasgow. D. In London, he found out that as an apprentice he had to spend seven years learning the trade.
questions.explanation: C introduces Watt at the University of Glasgow, B sends him to London on the advice of his well-wishers there, D says what he learnt in London and A follows from it: CBDA.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'involve'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Terse
questions.explanation: 'Terse' means brief and to the point; its opposite is 'verbose', using more words than needed. 'Succinct' and 'concise' are synonyms.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Me and my friends / often go / to the cinema / together.
questions.explanation: The subject pronoun is 'I', and courtesy puts it last: 'My friends and I often go to the cinema together.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Excruciating
questions.explanation: 'Excruciating' means intensely painful: 'piercing'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Cloud computing is a type of Internet-based computing that provides (1)_________ computer processing resources and data to computers and other devices on demand. Cloud computing and storage solutions provide users and enterprises (2)_______ various capabilities to store and process their data in third-party data centres. Local computers no longer have to do all the heavy lifting when it comes to running applications. The goal of cloud computing is to apply traditional supercomputing or high-performance computing power, normally used by military and research (3)______, to perform tens of trillions of computations per second, in consumer-oriented application such as financial (4)__________, to deliver personalised information and to provide data storage. In 2013, it was reported that cloud computing had become a highly demanded service or (5)_________ due to the advantages of high computing power, cheap cost of services, high performance, scalability, accessibility as well as availability.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Cloud computing provides 'shared' processing resources, drawn on by many users on demand.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Cloud computing is a type of Internet-based computing that provides (1)_________ computer processing resources and data to computers and other devices on demand. Cloud computing and storage solutions provide users and enterprises (2)_______ various capabilities to store and process their data in third-party data centres. Local computers no longer have to do all the heavy lifting when it comes to running applications.
