questions.text: The second number in the given number-pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) is/are followed in all the number-pairs, except one. Find that odd number-pair.
questions.explanation: In each pair but one the second number is the square of a quarter of the first: (12/4)² = 9, (8/4)² = 4 and (20/4)² = 25. For 4 it would be (4/4)² = 1, not 15.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘MEAL’ is written as ‘BMNF’ and ‘FOOD’ is written as ‘PEGP’. How will ‘FARE’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one place forward and the two halves swap: MEAL → NFBM → BMNF and FOOD → GPPE → PEGP. So FARE → GBSF → SFGB.

questions.text: The second number in the given number pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number pairs except one. Find that odd number pair.
questions.explanation: The second number is the square of half of one more than the first: 29 → 15² = 225, 17 → 9² = 81 and 31 → 16² = 256. For 45 it would be 23² = 529, not 576.

questions.text: Three Statements are given followed by Three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All reds are roses. No violet is a red. Some tulips are violets. Conclusions: I. Some roses are violets. II. No tulip is a red. III. No rose is a tulip.
options: Both conclusions I and III follow.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: No violet is red, but the roses that are not red may or may not be violets (I); the tulips that are not violets may be red (II); and nothing links roses with tulips (III). None follows.

questions.text: If 12th February 2011 was a Saturday, then what was the day of the week on 13th February 2015?
questions.explanation: From 12 February 2011 to 12 February 2015 is 4 years with one 29 February (2012), so the day moves 4 + 1 = 5 places: Saturday → Thursday. 13 February 2015 was a Friday.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 25*7*56*8*88*14
If ‘A’ denotes ‘+’, ‘B’ denotes ‘×‘, ‘C’ denotes ‘–’ and ‘D’ denotes ‘÷’, then what will come in place of ‘?’ in the following equation? 11 B (25 D 5) A 7 B 3 C 24 A 1 B (16 D 4) = ?

Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it. First row- 15, 62, 120; Second row- 18, 74, ?; Third row- 21, 86, 168 (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed)
questions.explanation: In each row the second number is 4 times the first plus 2 and the third is 8 times the first: 62 = 4 × 15 + 2 and 120 = 8 × 15; 86 = 4 × 21 + 2 and 168 = 8 × 21. So 8 × 18 = 144.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 121 : 9 :: 212 : 10 :: 508 : ?
questions.explanation: Each first number is 4 less than a cube and the second is the cube root plus 4: 121 = 5³ − 4 → 9 and 212 = 6³ − 4 → 10. 508 = 8³ − 4, so 8 + 4 = 12.

questions.text: If 01 February 2011 was Tuesday, then what was the day of the week on 01 January 2012?
questions.explanation: From 1 February 2011 to 1 January 2012 is 28 + 306 = 334 days (2011 was not a leap year): 47 weeks and 5 days. Tuesday + 5 = Sunday.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 150,154,1232,1244,19904,?
questions.explanation: Add 4, multiply by 8, add 12, multiply by 16, then add 20: 19904 + 20 = 19924.

questions.text: If A denotes ‘+’, B denotes ‘×’, C denotes ‘−’ and D denotes ‘÷’, then what will come in place of ‘?’ in the following equation? (84 D 6) B 7 A (22 B 4) C 16 A (15 B 8) = ?
Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? HIRC, ACYI, TWFO, MQMU, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move back 7 (H, A, T, M, F), second letters back 6 (I, C, W, Q, K), third letters forward 7 (R, Y, F, M, T) and fourth letters forward 6 (C, I, O, U, A): FKTA.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that, when sequentially placed from left to right in the blanks below, will complete the letter series. _ M _ _ G _ D _ _ M _ C G _ D C
options: G D C M C G D G
M D C M C G D M
G D C M C G D M
G D C D C G D M
questions.explanation: With G, D, C, M, C, G, D, M in the blanks the block GMDC repeats: GMDC GMDC GMDC GMDC.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'GIRL' is written as '*$#!' and ‘BOY’ is written as ‘@∑£’. How will 'LILY' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: From GIRL = *$#!, I = $ and L = !; from BOY = @∑£, Y = £. So LILY = !$!£.

questions.text: Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it. First row:32, 40, 18; Second row:38, 46, 21; Third row:33, 43, ? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the number into its constituent digits. For example, 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In each row the third number is a quarter of the sum of the first two: (32 + 40)/4 = 18 and (38 + 46)/4 = 21. So (33 + 43)/4 = 19.
'Of', division and multiplication first: (7 + 8 − 3 × 2) + [52 − 20 + 28] = 9 + 60 = 69.

questions.text: A work is done by P & Q, Q & R, and R & P in 12, 15, and 20 days, respectively. How many days will P alone take to complete the work?
questions.explanation: In a day P + Q do 1/12, Q + R 1/15 and R + P 1/20 of the work; adding, 2(P + Q + R) = 12/60, so P + Q + R = 1/10. P alone = 1/10 − 1/15 = 1/30: 30 days.

questions.text: A man can swim in still water at a speed of 6 km/h, but he takes thrice as long to swim upstream as downstream. The speed of the man, when swimming downstream is:
questions.explanation: Taking three times as long upstream, his upstream speed is a third of his downstream speed: 6 + s = 3(6 − s), so the stream flows at 3 km/h and he swims downstream at 9 km/h.

questions.text: If 30 men can harvest a meadow in 7 days, in how many days can 21 men harvest the same meadow?
questions.explanation: The meadow takes 30 × 7 = 210 man-days; 210 ÷ 21 = 10 days.

questions.text: A shopkeeper gives 15% and 35% discounts on a bottle. If the selling price of the bottle is ₹1,547, then the marked price of the bottle is:
questions.explanation: After the two discounts 0.85 × 0.65 = 0.5525 of the marked price is left: 1,547 ÷ 0.5525 = ₹2,800.

questions.text: A batsman in his 11th inning scores 88 runs, thereby increasing his average score by 4. What is his average after the 11th innings?
questions.explanation: If the new average is x, 10(x − 4) + 88 = 11x, so x = 88 − 40 = 48.

questions.text: In an election between two candidates, one got 40% of the total valid votes, and 30% of the votes were invalid. If the total number of votes was 7500, the number of valid votes that the other candidate got was:
questions.explanation: Valid votes = 70% of 7,500 = 5,250. The other candidate got the remaining 60% of them: 3,150.

questions.text: The diagonal of a rectangle is 17 cm long and its perimeter is 46 cm. The area of the rectangle is:
questions.explanation: Length + breadth = 23 cm and length² + breadth² = 17² = 289. 2 × area = 23² − 289 = 529 − 289 = 240, so the area is 120 cm².

questions.text: If a +b =8 and a − b =6, then find the value of ‘ab’.
What is the average of the following data? 1.2, 1.7, 3, 4.8, 10.5, 17.3 and 24.5
questions.explanation: The seven values add up to 63, so the average is 63 ÷ 7 = 9.

questions.text: The selling price of a watch after successive discounts of 20% and 20% is ₹640. What is the marked price of the watch?
questions.explanation: Two 20% discounts leave 0.8 × 0.8 = 0.64 of the marked price: 640 ÷ 0.64 = ₹1,000.

questions.text: What will be the present value of ₹ 484 due in 2 years at 10% per annum compound interest?

A train takes 3 hours to travel from place A to B at the speed of 60 km/h. The same train takes 2 hours to travel from B to C at 50% increased speed. What is the average speed of the train from place A to C?
questions.explanation: A to B is 60 × 3 = 180 km; B to C, at 90 km/h for 2 hours, another 180 km. Average speed = 360 ÷ 5 = 72 km/h.

questions.text: In an election four candidates were there in the fray, out of which three were nominated from the three national parties and they got votes in a ratio of 2:3:4.The total votes polled were 1,89,000 and the fourth candidate got 18,000 votes. The votes obtained by the three candidates of the national parties are respectively: (assuming all votes valid)
questions.explanation: The three national candidates shared 1,89,000 − 18,000 = 1,71,000 votes in 9 parts of 19,000: 38,000, 57,000 and 76,000.

questions.text: Which of the following is a large group of rock-forming silicate minerals that constitutes more than 50% of the Earth's crust and is widely used in the glass and ceramic industries?
questions.explanation: Feldspars, silicates of aluminium with potassium, sodium or calcium, make up about half of the Earth's crust and are used in making ceramics and glass.

questions.text: Pandit Shambhu Maharaj, a classical __________ dancer, was awarded with Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1967.
questions.explanation: Pandit Shambhu Maharaj was a Kathak dancer of the Lucknow gharana.

questions.text: Which two gases are having the highest percentage of the earth’s atmosphere?
questions.explanation: By volume dry air is about 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen.

questions.text: Which of the following teams won the Indian Premier League (IPL) 2021?
questions.explanation: Chennai Super Kings won IPL 2021, beating Kolkata Knight Riders in the final.

questions.text: Who among the following is a sitar player?
questions.explanation: Shahid Parvez is a sitar player of the Etawah (Imdadkhani) gharana. Shivkumar Sharma played the santoor, Sultan Khan the sarangi and Sheik Chinna Moulana the nadaswaram.

questions.text: ‘A Champion’s Mind: Lessons from a Life in Tennis’ is the autobiography of which of the following tennis players?
questions.explanation: 'A Champion's Mind' is the autobiography of the American tennis player Pete Sampras.

questions.text: Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with the impeachment of the President?
questions.explanation: Article 61 sets out the procedure for impeaching the President for violation of the Constitution.

questions.text: In which of the following sports is 'dunk shot' used?
questions.explanation: A dunk, or slam dunk, is a basketball shot in which the player forces the ball down through the hoop.

questions.text: Kishori Amonkar, Indian classical vocalist of Jaipur gharana. received Padma Vibhushan, India’s second highest civilian award, in which of the following years?
questions.explanation: Kishori Amonkar received the Padma Vibhushan in 2002.

questions.text: The number of silver medals won by India in Tokyo Olympics 2020 is __________.
questions.explanation: India's two silver medals at Tokyo 2020 were won by Mirabai Chanu in weightlifting and Ravi Kumar Dahiya in wrestling.

questions.text: ‘The Man Who Made The Elephant Dance’ is an autobiography of the famous entrepreneur _________.
questions.explanation: 'The Man Who Made the Elephant Dance' is the audio autobiography of Dr Verghese Kurien, the father of India's White Revolution.

questions.text: Which membrane-bound organelles, first discovered in 1857, are often referred to as the ‘energy factories’ of the cell because they are responsible for making adenosine triphosphate (ATP), the cell's main energy-carrying molecule?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria make most of the cell's ATP through aerobic respiration, which is why they are called the powerhouses of the cell.

questions.text: Padma Bhushan awardee Padma Subrahmanyam is a _________ dancer.
questions.explanation: Padma Subrahmanyam is a Bharatanatyam dancer and scholar.

questions.text: In the Satbir Singh vs _________ case, in 2021, the Supreme Court laid down guidelines for dowry death trials.
questions.explanation: In Satbir Singh v. State of Haryana (2021) the Supreme Court laid down guidelines for trials of dowry deaths under Section 304B of the IPC.

questions.text: 'GOAL' is an autobiography of which famous Indian player?
questions.explanation: 'Goal!' is the autobiography of the hockey player Major Dhyan Chand.

questions.text: Which enzyme is present in saliva?
questions.explanation: Saliva contains salivary amylase (ptyalin), which begins the digestion of starch. Pepsin and rennin act in the stomach, trypsin in the small intestine.

questions.text: Indian music maestro Bhimsen Joshi was related to the________ Gharana.
questions.explanation: Pandit Bhimsen Joshi was a vocalist of the Kirana gharana.

questions.text: Choose the correct sequence for central dogma.
options: Protein translation, DNA Replication, m-RNA transcription
DNA Replication, m-RNA transcription, Protein translation
m-RNA transcription, Protein translation, DNA Replication
m-RNA transcription, DNA Replication, Protein translation
questions.explanation: DNA is copied by replication, its information is transcribed into mRNA, and the mRNA is translated into protein.

questions.text: The First Five Year Plan was released in the year __________.
questions.explanation: The First Five Year Plan covered 1951 to 1956 and was launched in 1951.

questions.text: Who among the following won the FIH Women’s Hockey Player of the Year at the International Hockey Federation's (FIH) Hockey Stars Awards 2020-21?
questions.explanation: India's Gurjit Kaur was named the FIH Women's Player of the Year for 2020-21. Sjoerd Marijne, among the options, was India's women's coach, not a player.

questions.text: Who among the following got the Sangeet Natak Akademi 2017 for her contribution to Odissi dance?
options: L N Oinam Ongbi Dhoni Devi
questions.explanation: Sujata Mohapatra, a disciple of Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra, received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Odissi for 2017.

questions.text: Padma Shri awardee Guru Keezhpadam Kumaran Nair was a dancer of which of the following classical dances of India?
questions.explanation: Guru Keezhpadam Kumaran Nair was a Kathakali dancer and teacher from Kerala.

questions.text: Which of the following is the birthplace of Tansen?
questions.explanation: Tansen was born at Behat, near Gwalior, and his tomb is in Gwalior.

questions.text: Spot the error in the given sentence and select the correct sentence from the options given. He wished he has more resources to support the poor.
options: He wished his having more resources to support the poor.
He wished he have more resources to support the poor.
He wishing he has more resources to support the poor.
He wished he had more resources to support the poor.
questions.explanation: A wish about a situation that is not real takes the past tense: 'He wished he had more resources'.

questions.text: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In the Second World War, the British __________ thousands of so-called interceptors – mostly women – whose job it was to tune in every day and night to the radio _______ of the various divisions of the German military.
questions.explanation: The British 'assembled' (gathered) thousands of interceptors to listen to the German military's radio 'broadcasts'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Elbow grease
questions.explanation: 'Elbow grease' is hard physical effort, such as vigorous scrubbing or polishing.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. The rules forbid passengers to cross the railway bridge.
options: Forbidden are the passengers to cross the railway bridge.
Forbidden by the rules, the passengers cannot cross railway bridge.
Passengers are forbidden by the rules to cross the railway bridge.
Railway bridge is forbidden for the passengers to cross.
questions.explanation: The object 'passengers' becomes the subject, 'forbid' becomes 'are forbidden' and 'the rules' the agent: 'Passengers are forbidden by the rules to cross the railway bridge.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word ‘Exaggerate’ from the given sentence. Rajni did understate Sheila’s embroider work as, according to her, it was worthless to decorate a piece of cloth with abstract ideas and then elaborate it to the audience on the stage.
questions.explanation: To 'exaggerate' is to overstate; to 'understate' is to make something seem smaller or less important than it is.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The organisation “had set up for” a Free Mandela Committee and launched a lively campaign with the slogan ‘Free Mandela’.
questions.explanation: 'Set up' (establish) takes a direct object: 'had set up a Free Mandela Committee'; 'for' does not belong.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Something that will cure all illnesses
questions.explanation: A panacea is a remedy for all diseases or difficulties.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. He ordered the police to pursue the robber and his gang.
options: Order the police to pursue the robber gang.
Pursue the robber and gang were the orders by police.
The robber and gang were pursued.
The police were ordered to pursue the robber and his gang.
questions.explanation: The object 'the police' becomes the subject and 'ordered' becomes 'were ordered'; the agent ('by him') can be dropped: 'The police were ordered to pursue the robber and his gang.'

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. Wearing noise cancellation headphones is an example of such equipment. B. Preventive measures involve the availability of proper equipment. C. Noise exposure is the primary reason for hearing loss among the workers. D. It affects the working class in a big way both mentally and physically.
questions.explanation: C names noise as the main cause of workers' hearing loss, D describes its effects, B introduces preventive equipment and A gives an example of it: CDBA.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Donkey's years
questions.explanation: 'Donkey's years' means a very long time.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Abrogate
questions.explanation: To 'abrogate' a law or an agreement is to repeal or abolish it.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. The national anthem was being sung very enthusiastically by young students in the annual event.
options: The young students in the annual event were singing the national anthem very enthusiastically.
The national anthem was sung very enthusiastically for young students in the annual event.
The young students in the annual event had been singing the national anthem very enthusiastically.
The national anthem sang the young students very enthusiastically.
questions.explanation: 'Was being sung' is the past continuous passive; in the active it becomes 'were singing', with 'the young students' as the subject.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Delay
questions.explanation: 'Delay' is slowness or putting something off; its opposite is 'haste'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Discipline must be __________ at any cost
questions.explanation: Discipline must be 'maintained', that is kept up, at any cost.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'millennium', with a double 'l' and a double 'n'.

questions.text:

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fourth term in the same way as the first term is related to the second term and the fifth term is related to the sixth term 9 : 45 :: ? : 50 :: 32 : 68
questions.explanation: Each pair differs by 36: 45 − 9 = 36 and 68 − 32 = 36. So ? = 50 − 36 = 14.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 50 * 5 * 10 * 1 * 5 * 5
questions.explanation: 50 ÷ 5 = 10 × 1 + 5 − 5: both sides equal 10.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the sixth term is related to the fifth term. 35 : 135 :: 17 : ? :: 24 : 91
questions.explanation: The second number is four times the first minus 5: 35 × 4 − 5 = 135 and 24 × 4 − 5 = 91. Likewise 17 × 4 − 5 = 63.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the sixth term is related to the fifth term. 13 : 69 :: 17 : ? :: 23 : 129
questions.explanation: The second number is six times the first minus 9: 13 × 6 − 9 = 69 and 23 × 6 − 9 = 129. Likewise 17 × 6 − 9 = 93.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ' PLATINUM ' is codedas ‘171322110152214’ and ‘COPPER’ is coded as ’4161717619’. How will 'GOLD' be codedin that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is coded as its place in the alphabet plus 1: P (16) → 17, L (12) → 13, A (1) → 2 and so on. GOLD → 8, 16, 13, 5: 816135.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘SAVIOUR’ is written as ‘UYXGQST’ and ‘HEATERS’ is written as ‘JCCRGPU’. How will ‘HEIGHTS’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +2 and −2 alternately: S → U, A → Y, V → X, I → G and so on. HEIGHTS → J C K E J R U: JCKEJRU.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in an English dictionary. 1.Charger 2.Chapel 3.Chapter 4.Charcoal 5.Character
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Chapel (2), Chapter (3), Character (5), Charcoal (4), Charger (1). 'Chape' comes before 'Chapt', and 'Chara', 'Charc' and 'Charg' in that order.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 18 : 216 : : 20 : 280 : :12 : ?
questions.explanation: Each number is multiplied by itself minus 6: 18 × 12 = 216 and 20 × 14 = 280. Likewise 12 × 6 = 72.

questions.text: Seven friends A, B, C, D, E, F and G, each has a different age. C is older than D. B is the oldest among all. E is older than G but younger than F. G is older than C. Only two people are younger than C. D is not the youngest. How many persons are younger than E?
questions.explanation: B is the oldest. Only two are younger than C, so C is fifth; D, younger than C but not the youngest, is sixth, and A is the youngest. F, E and G fill second to fourth: B, F, E, G, C, D, A. G, C, D and A are younger than E: 4.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and fourth term is related to third term. GRAPES : SAREPG :: VERBAL : LREABV :: NUMBER : ?
questions.explanation: The first and last letters swap, as do the second and third and the fourth and fifth: GRAPES → SAREPG and VERBAL → LREABV. So NUMBER → RMUEBN.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 27 * 3 * 10 * 10 * 10
questions.explanation: 27 + 3 − 10 = 10 + 10: both sides equal 20.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 46*75*41*16*5
questions.explanation: 46 + 75 − 41 = 16 × 5: both sides equal 80.

questions.text: If 2st January 2008 was a Wednesday, then what was the day of the week on 1st January 2012?
questions.explanation: The paper's '2st January' is 2 January (which was indeed a Wednesday in 2008), so 1 January 2008 was a Tuesday. The leap year 2008 adds 2 days and 2009, 2010 and 2011 one each: Tuesday + 5 days = Sunday.

questions.text: The second number in the given number pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number pairs except one. Find that odd number pair
questions.explanation: In 16 : 224, 21 : 399 and 35 : 1155 the second number is the first times two less than itself (16 × 14, 21 × 19, 35 × 33). 238 is 17 × 14, not 17 × 15 = 255, so 17 : 238 is the odd pair.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? UBEJ, VEJQ, ?, XKTE, YNYL
questions.explanation: The first letters move +1 (U, V, W, X, Y), the second +3 (B, E, H, K, N), the third +5 (E, J, O, T, Y) and the fourth +7 (J, Q, X, E, L): WHOX.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? ZOFB, ?, VKJF, TILH, RGNJ
questions.explanation: The first two letters move back 2 (Z, X, V, T, R and O, M, K, I, G) and the last two forward 2 (F, H, J, L, N and B, D, F, H, J): XMHD.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 348, 353, 339, ?, 330, 371
questions.explanation: The differences are +5, −14, +23, −32, +41: they grow by 9 and alternate in sign. 339 + 23 = 362.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 17,22,11,16,8,13,?

Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some woods are metals. All metals are stones. Some plastics are metals. Conclusions: I. Some stones are plastics. II. Some woods are stones. III. All stones are metals.
options: Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions I and III follow
questions.explanation: The plastics that are metals are stones, so some stones are plastics (I); likewise the woods that are metals are stones (II). All metals being stones does not make all stones metals, so III does not follow.

questions.text: Which scheme among the following is most beneficial to the customer? i) Successive discounts of 25% and 25% ii) Flat discount of 40% iii) Buy one, get one free iv) Successive discounts of 30% and 20%
questions.explanation: Successive 25% and 25% leave 0.75 × 0.75 = 0.5625 of the price, a 43.75% discount; 30% and 20% leave 0.7 × 0.8 = 0.56, a 44% discount; the flat discount is 40%. Buy one, get one free is a 50% discount, the largest.

questions.text: A 640 metre long train travelling at 80 km/h overtook a 540 metre long train travelling at 72 km/h in the same direction. How long did it take the faster train to cross the other train completely?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 80 − 72 = 8 km/h = 20/9 m/s. The faster train must gain 640 + 540 = 1,180 m: 1,180 × 9/20 = 531 seconds = 8 minutes 51 seconds.

questions.text: In an assembly election of two candidates, the winner got 56% of the total valid votes. 5% of the total votes were declared invalid. If the total number of voters is 3,20,000 then what is the number of valid votes polled for the winning candidate?
Which of the following numbers is divisible by 55?
questions.explanation: 55 = 5 × 11, and all four numbers end in 5. For 11, the alternate digit sums of 185625 are 1 + 5 + 2 = 8 and 8 + 6 + 5 = 19, which differ by 11; for the others they differ by 4, 9 and 2. (185625 = 55 × 3,375.)

questions.text: Evaluate 99 × 99 − 1.
A bus covers a certain distance travelling at a speed of 40 km/h and returns to the starting point at a speed of 60 km/h. The average speed (in km/h) for the entire journey is:
questions.explanation: Over equal distances the average speed is 2xy/(x + y) = 2 × 40 × 60/100 = 48 km/h.

questions.text: The population of village has been continuously increasing at the rate of 10% per year. If its present population is 54,450, what was it two years ago?
questions.explanation: Two years of 10% growth multiply the population by 1.1² = 1.21: 54,450 ÷ 1.21 = 45,000.

questions.text: If p = 38, then the value of p(p² + 3p + 3) is _________.
A person borrowed a sum of ₹8,000 at an interest rate of 10% p.a., compounded semi-annually. What is the compound interest for a period of 1 year?
questions.explanation: Compounded half-yearly, 1 year is 2 periods at 5%: 8,000 × 1.05² = ₹8,820, so the interest is ₹820.

questions.text: Sudhir claimed to sell his items at only 8% above the cost of production, but used a weight that had 750 grams written on it, though it actually weighed 720 grams. What was the actual profit percentage earned by Sudhir?
questions.explanation: He charges for 750 grams at 8% above cost but gives only 720 grams: profit = (750 × 1.08)/720 − 1 = 810/720 − 1 = 12.5%.

questions.text: Copper and bronze are in the ratio 3 : 4 in 350 gm of an alloy. The quantity (in gm) of copper to be added to it to make the ratio 4 : 3 is:
questions.explanation: The alloy has 150 gm of copper and 200 gm of bronze. For 4 : 3 the copper must be 200 × 4/3 = 266.67 gm, so 116.67 gm must be added.

questions.text: Find the volume of a cuboid whose dimensions are 15 m, 22 m and 5 m.

In an examination it is required to get a minimum of 340 marks in aggregate to pass. A student gets 244 marks and is declared failed by 12% of the total marks. What are the maximum aggregate marks a student can get?
questions.explanation: The student falls short by 340 − 244 = 96 marks, which is 12% of the total: 96 ÷ 0.12 = 800.

questions.text: The area of a right-angled triangle is 42 cm². If the length of one of its two sides containing the right angle is 10 cm, find the length of the other side that contain the right angle.
questions.explanation: Area = ½ × base × height: ½ × 10 × h = 42, so h = 8.4 cm.

questions.text: A merchant gives an additional discount of 10% on the product after an initial discount of 20% on the listed price. He managed to make a 10% profit by selling the product for ₹54,000. What was the listed price of the product?
questions.explanation: Discounts of 20% and then 10% leave 0.8 × 0.9 = 0.72 of the listed price, and that is the selling price: ₹54,000 ÷ 0.72 = ₹75,000. (The profit is not needed.)

questions.text: The difference between mean proportion of 9 & 16 and 4 & 9 is:
questions.explanation: The mean proportional of a and b is √(ab): √(9 × 16) = 12 and √(4 × 9) = 6. The difference is 6.

questions.text: Which mountain range covers a distance of about 1500 miles (2400 km) and passes through India, Pakistan, Afghanistan, China, Bhutan, and Nepal?
questions.explanation: The Himalayas run about 2,400 km from the Indus in the west to the Brahmaputra in the east. The Purvanchal, Aravalli and Pir Panjal are much shorter ranges.

questions.text: Article 32 of the Constitution of India deals with the:
options: Right to Freedom of Speech and Expression
questions.explanation: Article 32 gives the right to move the Supreme Court to enforce the Fundamental Rights: the Right to Constitutional Remedies.

questions.text: Which biological stain is used in histology and cytology to colour all cell nuclei red?
questions.explanation: Safranin is a red stain used for cell nuclei and as the counterstain in Gram staining. Methyl orange, phenolphthalein and cresol red are acid-base indicators.

questions.text: What is the area of coverage in a hectare of forest and tree cover in India as per Forest Survey 2021?
questions.explanation: By the India State of Forest Report 2021, forest and tree cover together came to 80.9 million hectares, 24.62% of the country's geographical area.

questions.text: Name the first Indian woman to be conferred with Grammy Award.
questions.explanation: Tanvi Shah won a Grammy in 2010 as a co-writer of 'Jai Ho' from 'Slumdog Millionaire', the first Indian woman to win one.

questions.text: Which of the following is the autobiography of the international athlete Maria Sharapova?
questions.explanation: Maria Sharapova's memoir is 'Unstoppable: My Life So Far'. 'Open' is Andre Agassi's, 'Unbreakable' Mary Kom's and 'But Seriously' John McEnroe's.

questions.text: In an economy, fisheries are a part of __________.
questions.explanation: Fisheries, like agriculture, forestry and mining, draw directly on natural resources: the primary sector.

questions.text: Padma Shri awardee Shobha Naidu was a _______ dancer.
questions.explanation: Shobha Naidu, a disciple of Vempati Chinna Satyam, was a leading Kuchipudi dancer.

questions.text: Which of the following countries won two ICC T20 World Cup Cricket titles?
questions.explanation: West Indies won the men's T20 World Cup in 2012 and 2016. When the paper was set (June 2022) Australia (2021) and India (2007) had one title each and New Zealand none; India have since won in 2024 and 2026.

questions.text: Veteran Dance guru, Jatin Goswami was awarded with the Kalidas Samman for his significant contribution to which of the following dance forms?
questions.explanation: Jatin Goswami, a guru of Sattriya, the classical dance of Assam's Vaishnava monasteries, received Madhya Pradesh's Kalidas Samman for 2017.

questions.text: The Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order Amendment Bill, 2021 was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 13 February 2021, which amended the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, ___________.
questions.explanation: The Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950 lists the Scheduled Castes state by state; the 2021 Bill grouped seven Tamil Nadu castes in it as 'Devendrakula Velalar'.

questions.text: Who among the following was honoured with the Padma Shri in 2011 for his/her excellence in Chhau, a semi-classical dance form of Eastern India?
questions.explanation: Makar Dhwaja Darogha, a Seraikella Chhau guru from Jharkhand, received the Padma Shri in 2011.

questions.text: As in August 2021, which State Government agreed to continue to sponsor the men’s and women’s national hockey teams for another 10 years after the current sponsorship ends in 2023?
questions.explanation: In August 2021, after the Tokyo Olympics, Odisha said it would go on sponsoring both national hockey teams for another 10 years, to 2033.

questions.text: Which of the following is the title of the autobiography of Sania Mirza?
questions.explanation: 'Ace Against Odds' is Sania Mirza's autobiography. 'Sunny Days' is Sunil Gavaskar's and 'Unbreakable' Mary Kom's.

questions.text: ‘A Shot at History: My Obsessive Journey to Olympic Gold’ is the autography of the famous sportsperson ______________.
questions.explanation: Abhinav Bindra, India's first individual Olympic gold medallist (10 m air rifle, Beijing 2008), wrote 'A Shot at History' with Rohit Brijnath.

questions.text: In which year did Dmitri Mendeleev and Lothar Meyer individually come up with their own periodic law and proposed that on arranging elements in the increasing order of their atomic weights, similarities appear in physical and chemical properties at regular intervals?
questions.explanation: Mendeleev published his periodic table in 1869, and 1869 is the year textbooks (NCERT among them) give for both him and Lothar Meyer, who reached a very similar arrangement independently. Meyer's own paper appeared in print in 1870, after Mendeleev's.

questions.text: Who among the following is the best Rudra Veena player in Hindustani Classical Music?
questions.explanation: Ustad Asad Ali Khan, of the dhrupad tradition, was the foremost rudra veena player of his time. Rashid Khan was a vocalist and Sultan Khan a sarangi player.

questions.text: Which gymnastic event takes place on a large floor mat?
questions.explanation: The floor exercise is performed on a 12 m square sprung floor mat; the other events use apparatus: bars, a vaulting table and a beam.

questions.text: Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica, popularly known as Principia, published in 1687, is the great work of which scientist?
questions.explanation: Isaac Newton's Principia (1687) set out his three laws of motion and the law of universal gravitation.

questions.text: identify the formula that represents Ohm's law.
questions.explanation: Ohm's law: V = IR, voltage equals current times resistance. In units, volts = amperes × ohms, so V = A × Ω.

questions.text: Who among the following Indian musician founded Harmony and Universality through Music (HUM) to perform in different parts of the world and draw people’s attention to specially-abled children?
questions.explanation: Tabla player Sandeep Das, a member of Yo-Yo Ma's Silk Road Ensemble, founded HUM (Harmony and Universality through Music), which supports the arts education of specially-abled children.

questions.text: Sitara Devi, Padma Shri and Kalidas Samman awardee was awarded for reviving which of the following dance forms in India?
questions.explanation: Sitara Devi was one of the great Kathak dancers of the twentieth century.

questions.text: Which of the following plants is on the verge of extinction due to insensitivity to our environment?
questions.explanation: Madhuca insignis, a Western Ghats tree once thought extinct, is critically endangered. The damask rose, sunflower and common daisy are widely grown.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. In 1920’s, new technology “has allowed” filmmakers to attach to each film a soundtrack of speech.
questions.explanation: The action belongs to a finished past time (the 1920s), so the simple past 'allowed' replaces the present perfect 'has allowed'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'spacious'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Get away
questions.explanation: To 'get away' is to leave or escape from a place.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. The disabled should not be oppressed.
options: Let not the disabled be oppressed.
The disabled have not been oppressed.
We should not be oppressing the disabled.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the imperative 'Do not oppress the disabled.': grammar books give 'X should not be oppressed' (or 'Let not X be oppressed') as the passive of a negative command. 'We should not be oppressing' is active too but changes the verb to the continuous, and the other two options are still passive.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Attract
questions.explanation: To 'attract' is to draw towards; its opposite is to 'repel', to drive away.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Between Scylla and Charybdis
questions.explanation: Scylla and Charybdis were two sea monsters of Greek myth on either side of a narrow strait; to be between them is to face two dangers, where escaping one means meeting the other.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. We love to swing from the branches _______ the pond.
questions.explanation: The branches hang above the pond: 'over' the pond.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. “Is he remembering” our help?
questions.explanation: 'Remember' is a stative verb, not normally used in the continuous: 'Does he remember our help?'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Be at a loose end
questions.explanation: To 'be at a loose end' is to have nothing to do.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Lasting for a very short period of time
questions.explanation: 'Ephemeral' means lasting a very short time; 'permanent' and 'ceaseless' mean the opposite.

questions.text: Select the sentence which has no spelling error.
options: He incorporates daily vocablary in his gestures.
She has her own vockbulary words from English and Hindi.
Vocabulary raises the standard of English language.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'vocabulary'; the other sentences have 'vocablary', 'vocabluary' and 'vockbulary'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. After he had / ate that lobster,/ he began to / feel sick.
questions.explanation: The past perfect takes the past participle: 'After he had eaten that lobster', not 'had ate'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in the brackets to fill in the blank. It will be _______________ (illogical) to accept the demands of the protesters this time.
questions.explanation: 'Absurd' means wildly unreasonable or illogical.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. I was not hired by her.
options: She has not been hired me.
questions.explanation: The agent 'her' becomes the subject 'She', and the simple past passive 'was not hired' becomes 'did not hire': 'She did not hire me.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word in the given sentence. His strategy is to “protract” negotiations until the enemy are exhausted while assembling the forces necessary to crush them.
questions.explanation: To 'protract' something is to make it last longer: to 'prolong' it.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. It provides a high-quality learning opportunity, improves student outcomes and skills, and expands educational choice options B. Therefore, location, time, and quality are no longer considered factors in seeking degree courses or higher education because of online education. C. Online education is an amenable instructional delivery process that includes any learning that takes place via the internet. D. Its potential advantages involve increased educational access.
questions.explanation: C defines online education, D introduces its advantages, A sets them out and B draws the conclusion with 'Therefore': CDAB.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Readers have been (1) _________ conditioned that they feel embarrassed to admit that they find it hard (2) _________ stomach the work of a literary giant for fear it would betray their plebian taste. The (3) __________ is that a few read, and fewer enjoy, the novels of those who sit on the literary pedestal. We have (4) _________ ourselves to be persuaded that a book with a story can't be quite in the same class as a book that leaves us to (5) __________ what is unsaid.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'So … that' links a degree to its result: readers have been 'so' conditioned that they feel embarrassed.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Readers have been (1) _________ conditioned that they feel embarrassed to admit that they find it hard (2) _________ stomach the work of a literary giant for fear it would betray their plebian taste. The (3) __________ is that a few read, and fewer enjoy, the novels of those who sit on the literary pedestal. We have (4) _________ ourselves to be persuaded that a book with a story can't be quite in the same class as a book that leaves us to (5) __________ what is unsaid.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: 'Find it hard' is followed by the to-infinitive: hard 'to' stomach the work.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Readers have been (1) _________ conditioned that they feel embarrassed to admit that they find it hard (2) _________ stomach the work of a literary giant for fear it would betray their plebian taste. The (3) __________ is that a few read, and fewer enjoy, the novels of those who sit on the literary pedestal. We have (4) _________ ourselves to be persuaded that a book with a story can't be quite in the same class as a book that leaves us to (5) __________ what is unsaid.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'The fact is that' introduces the truth the writer sets against the readers' embarrassment.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Readers have been (1) _________ conditioned that they feel embarrassed to admit that they find it hard (2) _________ stomach the work of a literary giant for fear it would betray their plebian taste. The (3) __________ is that a few read, and fewer enjoy, the novels of those who sit on the literary pedestal. We have (4) _________ ourselves to be persuaded that a book with a story can't be quite in the same class as a book that leaves us to (5) __________ what is unsaid.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: We have 'allowed' ourselves to be persuaded: let ourselves be persuaded.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Readers have been (1) _________ conditioned that they feel embarrassed to admit that they find it hard (2) _________ stomach the work of a literary giant for fear it would betray their plebian taste. The (3) __________ is that a few read, and fewer enjoy, the novels of those who sit on the literary pedestal. We have (4) _________ ourselves to be persuaded that a book with a story can't be quite in the same class as a book that leaves us to (5) __________ what is unsaid.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: A book that leaves us to 'interpret' what is unsaid makes the reader work out its meaning.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the sixth term is related to the fifth term. 27 : 75 :: 45 : ? :: 39 : 111
questions.explanation: The second number of each pair is 3 times the first minus 6: 27 × 3 − 6 = 75 and 39 × 3 − 6 = 111. Likewise 45 × 3 − 6 = 129.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'ELBOW' is written as 'DLYOV' and ‘ANKLE' is written as 'VOPMZ'. How will 'WRIST' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The word is reversed and each letter replaced by its opposite in the alphabet (A↔Z, B↔Y, …): ELBOW → WOBLE → DLYOV and ANKLE → ELKNA → VOPMZ. So WRIST → TSIRW → GHRID.

questions.text: If 15 July 2002 is a Monday, then what will be the day of the week on 16 October 2005?
questions.explanation: 15 July 2002 to 15 July 2005 is 3 years with one leap day (29 February 2004): 4 odd days, so 15 July 2005 was a Friday. The 93 days (16 + 31 + 30 + 16) on to 16 October are 13 weeks and 2 days: Sunday.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series. B E _ K P C _ H K P _ E H K P_ E H K P
questions.explanation: With H, E, D, E in the blanks the series reads BEHKP CEHKP DEHKP EEHKP: the first letter moves on one each time and EHKP repeats.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 64 : 18 :: 196 : 24 :: 529 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is the square root of the first plus 10: √64 + 10 = 18 and √196 + 10 = 24. Likewise √529 + 10 = 23 + 10 = 33.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. UNCLEAR : CNULRAE :: PRIVACY : IRPVYCA :: NUCLEAR : ?
questions.explanation: The first three letters are reversed, the fourth stays and the last three are reversed: UNC L EAR → CNU L RAE and PRI V ACY → IRP V YCA. So NUC L EAR → CUNLRAE.

questions.text: A is the brother of C. B is the only sister of D who is the maternal uncle of C. If E is the father of C, then how is A related to B?
questions.explanation: D is C's maternal uncle, so C's mother is D's sister; B is D's only sister, so B is C's mother. A is C's brother, so A is B's son.

questions.text: Three Statements are given followed by Three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All cakes are sweets. No sweet is a biscuit. Some chocolates are biscuits. Conclusions: I. Some biscuits are cakes. II. Some chocolates are sweets. III. No cake is a chocolate.
options: Both conclusions I and III follow.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: All cakes are sweets and no sweet is a biscuit, so no cake is a biscuit: I is false. The chocolates that are biscuits cannot be sweets, and nothing ties the other chocolates to sweets or cakes, so II and III are only possibilities. None follows.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (45, 9, 12) (21, 3, 14) (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed)
questions.explanation: The third number is the first divided by the second, plus 7: 45 ÷ 9 + 7 = 12 and 21 ÷ 3 + 7 = 14. Likewise 80 ÷ 10 + 7 = 15.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'RESET' is written as '36538540' and 'START' is written as '384013640'. How will 'STOP' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each consonant is written as twice its place in the alphabet and each vowel as its place: RESET → 36 5 38 5 40 and START → 38 40 1 36 40. So STOP → 38 40 15 32.

questions.text: The second number in the given number-pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) is/are followed in all the number-pairs, except one. Find that odd number-pair.
questions.explanation: The second number is the square of one more than the first: 3 → 4² = 16, 6 → 7² = 49 and 12 → 13² = 169. But 9 → 10² = 100, not 64.

questions.text: If ‘A’ denotes ‘+’, ‘B’ denotes ‘×’, ‘C’ denotes ‘–’ and ‘D’ denotes ‘÷’, then what will come in place of ‘?’ in the following equation? (84 D 14) A 17 C 13 B (75 D 15) A 9 B 7 = ?
In a certain code language, “IS” is coded as “169”, and “AM” is coded as “11”. How will “IN” be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: The code is the product of the letters' places in the alphabet minus 2: IS → 9 × 19 − 2 = 169 and AM → 1 × 13 − 2 = 11. So IN → 9 × 14 − 2 = 124.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fourth term in the same way as the first term is related to the second term and the fifth term is related to the sixth term 8 : 508 :: ? : 2193 :: 2 : 4
questions.explanation: The second number is the cube of the first minus 4: 8³ − 4 = 508 and 2³ − 4 = 4. 2193 + 4 = 2197 = 13³.

questions.text: The second number in the given number pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number pairs, except one. Find that odd number pair.
questions.explanation: In 12 : 2, 36 : 3 and 80 : 4 the first number is the cube plus the square of the second (8 + 4, 27 + 9, 64 + 16). In 25 : 5 it is not: 5³ + 5² = 150.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 10, 21, 35, 56, 90, 145, 231, 360, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 11, 14, 21, 34, 55, 86, 129, and theirs are 3, 7, 13, 21, 31, 43, which grow by 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. The next grows by 14: 43 + 14 = 57, 129 + 57 = 186 and 360 + 186 = 546.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and fourth term related to third term. 16:576 :: 8:80 :: 22:?
questions.explanation: Half the first number, squared, times one more than that half: 16 → 8² × 9 = 576 and 8 → 4² × 5 = 80. Likewise 22 → 11² × 12 = 1452.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? SYGZ, NIRT, ?, DCNH, YMYB
questions.explanation: First letters move −5 (S, N, I, D, Y), second letters +10 (Y, I, S, C, M), third letters +11 (G, R, C, N, Y) and fourth letters −6 (Z, T, N, H, B), wrapping round the alphabet. The missing cluster is ISCN.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 762, 755, 741, 720, 692, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are −7, −14, −21, −28, so the next is −35: 692 − 35 = 657.

questions.text: If the 9-digit number 5p42978n6 is divisible by 72, what is the value of (2p – 1), where n is the second largest of all the possible values of n? Given that p and n are natural numbers.
questions.explanation: For 8, the last three digits 8n6 must be divisible by 8: 816, 856 and 896 are, so n is 1, 5 or 9 and the second largest is 5. For 9, the digit sum 5 + p + 4 + 2 + 9 + 7 + 8 + 5 + 6 = 46 + p must be 54, so p = 8 and 2p − 1 = 15.

questions.text: Champa buys type 1 sugar at ₹45 per kg. He mixes it with type 2 sugar having a price of ₹48 per kg. The final mixture becomes worth ₹46 per kg. What is the ratio of the quantities of type 1 sugar to type 2 sugar in the final mixture?
questions.explanation: By alligation, type 1 : type 2 = (48 − 46) : (46 − 45) = 2 : 1.

questions.text: A retailer offers the following discount schemes for an article to his customers. A. Two equal successive discounts of 15% . B. Two successive discounts of 12% and 18%. C. Buy 7 articles and get 3 free. Which scheme is favourable to a customer? (assuming buys articles in a multiple of 10)
options: Both A and C are the same
questions.explanation: A leaves 0.85 × 0.85 = 0.7225 of the price (27.75% off), B leaves 0.88 × 0.82 = 0.7216 (27.84% off), and C charges for 7 articles in every 10 (30% off). C is the best.

questions.text: The average of 16 numbers is 23. The average of the first 7 numbers is 21 and that of the last 8 numbers is 24. Find the 8th number.
If a solid piece of iron in the form of a cuboid, of dimensions 49 cm × 33 cm × 24 cm, is moulded to form a solid sphere, then the radius of the sphere is ______. [Use π = 22/7]
The ratio of the distances Ravina and Suhel had to travel from their respective houses to their workplaces was 4 : 7. If Suhel had to travel 63 km, how much did Ravina have to travel?
questions.explanation: Ravina travelled 63 × 4/7 = 36 km.

questions.text: 64% of the students of a class are girls and 81.25% of the girls have chosen soccer as their favourite sport. If 143 girls have chosen soccer as their favourite sport, what is the total number of students in the class?
questions.explanation: The girls who chose soccer are 0.64 × 0.8125 = 0.52 of the class: 143/0.52 = 275 students.

questions.text: A woman sold her earphone for ₹2,000 and got a percentage profit equal to the numerical value of cost price. The cost price of the earphone is:
questions.explanation: With cost price x, the profit is x% of x = x²/100, so x + x²/100 = 2,000, x² + 100x − 2,00,000 = 0 and x = 400 (a 400% profit of ₹1,600).

questions.text: A sum of money amounts to ₹4,624 in 2 years and to ₹4,913 in 3 years at a certain rate of interest, when interest is compounded per annum. The sum is _______.

The marked price of a laptop is ₹50,000.A shopkeeper gives the following four schemes of discount to his customers. Which one is more beneficial to the customers? i)Discount of ₹10,000 ii)Discount of flat 25% iii)Discount of 10% of 10% iv)Discount of 15% of 10%

Four runners started running simultaneously from a point on a circular track. They took 400 seconds, 600 seconds, 720 seconds and 900 seconds to complete one round. After how much time did they meet at the starting point for the first time since the race started?
questions.explanation: They next meet at the start after LCM(400, 600, 720, 900) = 2⁴ × 3² × 5² = 3,600 seconds.

questions.text: In an election between two candidates, 15% of the voters did not cast their votes and 10% of the votes polled were found invalid. The successful candidate got 55% of the valid votes and won by a majority of 6120 votes. The number of voters enrolled on the voters list was:
questions.explanation: Valid votes are 0.85 × 0.9 = 0.765 of the electorate. The winning margin, 55% − 45% = 10% of them, is 0.0765 of the electorate = 6,120, so 80,000 voters were enrolled.

questions.text: If x-2y=3 and 2xy = 5, then find the value of (x+2y)².
A group of 36 students has an average present age of 14 years. When the age of the teacher is included, the average age rises by one. Calculate the teacher's age (in years).
If ABC is a triangle in which DE ǁ BC and AD ∶ DB = 9 ∶ 8, then DE : BC is _________.
questions.explanation: DE ∥ BC makes ΔADE similar to ΔABC, so DE : BC = AD : AB = 9 : (9 + 8) = 9 : 17.

questions.text: Manoj and his wife Swathi fill a tank with water fetched from a well. Manoj fetches 5 litres of water in 4 minutes whereas Swathi fetches 4 litres of water in 5 minutes. Find the time taken by them together to fetch 205 litres of water.
questions.explanation: Manoj fetches 5/4 = 1.25 litres a minute and Swathi 4/5 = 0.8; together 2.05 litres a minute, so 205 litres take 100 minutes.

questions.text: Who among the following has been conferred the prestigious title of ‘Maestro’ by London’s Royal Philharmonic Orchestra, with whom he had been the only Asian to have composed a full symphony as on 6th March 2022?
questions.explanation: Ilaiyaraaja is called 'Maestro', the title conferred on him by London's Royal Philharmonic Orchestra, which performed the full symphony he composed in 1993.

questions.text: In India, CRR is fixed by _______________.
questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India fixes the cash reserve ratio, the share of their deposits that banks must keep with it.

questions.text: Which of the following is the first city in history to host the Paralympic Games for a second time?
questions.explanation: Tokyo hosted the Summer Paralympics in 1964 and again in 2021 (the Tokyo 2020 Games), the first city to host the Summer Games twice; Beijing's second Paralympics, the 2022 Winter Games, came later.

questions.text: Which Indian cartoonist’s autobiography is titled ‘The Tunnel of Time’?
questions.explanation: 'The Tunnel of Time' is the autobiography of R. K. Laxman, the cartoonist who created 'The Common Man'.

questions.text: In January 2022, in which city an initiative - Deaddiction, Reformation and Entrepreneurial Assistance for Making a Safe Society (Dreams) was launched to rehabilitate drug addicts?
questions.explanation: DREAMS is an initiative of the Bhubaneswar-Cuttack Commissionerate Police in Odisha to rehabilitate drug users through de-addiction, skill training and livelihood support.

questions.text: Name the only Indian athlete who received the Padma Bhushan Award for the year 2022.
questions.explanation: Paralympic javelin thrower Devendra Jhajharia was the only sportsperson among the Padma Bhushan awardees of 2022; Vandana Katariya, Faisal Ali Dar and Sankaranarayana Menon Chundayil received the Padma Shri.

questions.text: Who among the following was the author of the famous work “Sangita Ratnakara”?
questions.explanation: Sharngadeva wrote the 'Sangita Ratnakara' in the 13th century at the Yadava court of Devagiri.

questions.text: Padma Bhushan, Kanak Rele was conferred with the award for her significant contribution to which of the following dance forms?
questions.explanation: Kanak Rele, who received the Padma Bhushan in 2013, was a leading exponent and scholar of Mohiniyattam.

questions.text: Which disease refers to the inflammation of the liver caused by a variety of infectious viruses and non-infectious agents leading to a variety of health problems?
questions.explanation: Hepatitis is inflammation of the liver; it can be caused by the hepatitis viruses and also by alcohol, toxins and some drugs.

questions.text: Out of the given four alternatives, select the one that is NOT a constitutional body?
questions.explanation: The National Human Rights Commission is a statutory body, set up under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. The Finance Commission (Article 280), the Election Commission (Article 324) and the UPSC (Article 315) are constitutional bodies.

questions.text: Kelucharan Mohapatra, awarded with Padma Vibhushan in 2000, was a dancer of which of the following dances?
questions.explanation: Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra was the foremost figure in the revival of Odissi.

questions.text: Who was recognised as ‘Asthana Nartaki’ (resident dancer) of the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanam?
questions.explanation: The Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi dancer Yamini Krishnamurthy was the 'Asthana Nartaki' of the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams.

questions.text: Among the following, whose autobiography is ‘Daughter of Destiny: An Autobiography’?
questions.explanation: 'Daughter of Destiny' is the autobiography of Benazir Bhutto, Prime Minister of Pakistan; it was first published in Britain as 'Daughter of the East'.

questions.text: Which music director duo of India made their debut in the ‘Forbes India Celebrity 100 List 2015’?
questions.explanation: The Marathi composer brothers Ajay and Atul Gogavale entered the Forbes India Celebrity 100 list for the first time in 2015, at 82nd.

questions.text: Which kind of sport is bungee jumping?
questions.explanation: Bungee jumping, a leap from a height on an elastic cord, is an adventure sport.

questions.text: Which of the following characters are correct about Phylum Echinodermata?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'coelom present, bilateral symmetry'. Echinoderms are coelomates and their larvae are bilaterally symmetrical, though the adults are radially symmetrical. Roundworms are pseudocoelomate, and a gastrovascular cavity marks cnidarians and flatworms, which have no coelom.

questions.text: What components are often called the building blocks of the body that play a vital role in helping to repair and strengthen muscle tissues after exercise?
questions.explanation: Proteins, made of amino acids, are called the body's building blocks; they build and repair muscle tissue.

questions.text: The given equation describes the _________ relation. s = u t +1/2 a t²
questions.explanation: NCERT calls s = ut + ½at² the equation for the position-time relation; v = u + at is the velocity-time relation and 2as = v² − u² the position-velocity relation.

questions.text: Which crop grows best in areas with hot, humid climate and requires temperature between 21°C to 37°C with well distributed rainfall or irrigation facilities of about 100 cm?
questions.explanation: Rice, a kharif crop, needs high temperature, high humidity and about 100 cm of rain or more, or irrigation where rain is less.

questions.text: How do humans acclimatise at high altitudes where atmospheric pressure is low for normal breathing?
options: By decreasing red blood cell production, decreasing the binding affinity of haemoglobin and by increasing breathing rate
By increasing red blood cell production, decreasing the binding affinity of haemoglobin and by increasing breathing rate
By increasing white blood cell production, decreasing the binding affinity of haemoglobin and by increasing breathing rate
questions.explanation: At high altitude the body makes more red blood cells, lowers haemoglobin's binding affinity for oxygen (so it gives up oxygen to the tissues more readily) and breathes faster.

questions.text: Who among the following won the National Film Award for Best Choreography at the 67th National Film Awards?
questions.explanation: Raju Sundaram won the award at the 67th National Film Awards (for 2019) for the song 'Paala Pitta' in the Telugu film 'Maharshi'.

questions.text: Who is the author of ‘The Interpreter of Maladies’?
questions.explanation: Jhumpa Lahiri's short-story collection 'Interpreter of Maladies' won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction in 2000.

questions.text: In which month of 2021 was the Gram Ujala Yojana, aimed at providing high-quality electricity at an affordable cost to villages across the country, launched in Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh?
questions.explanation: Gram Ujala, run by Convergence Energy Services Ltd, gives villagers LED bulbs at ₹10 each in exchange for working incandescent bulbs; it was launched in Varanasi on 24 March 2021, days after its start in Arrah, Bihar.

questions.text: Padma Bhushan awardee Ustad Sabri Khan was a ______ player.
questions.explanation: Ustad Sabri Khan was a renowned sarangi player; he received the Padma Bhushan in 2006.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. Please bring me a glass of water.
options: Let a glass of water being brought to me, please.
Let a glass of water be brought to me, please.
Let a glass of water come to me.
Let a glass of water be given to me.
questions.explanation: A request becomes 'Let ... be' + past participle: 'Let a glass of water be brought to me, please.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Startle
questions.explanation: To 'startle' someone is to give them a sudden fright or shock: to 'surprise' them.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underline segment in the given sentence. The delegates “talked of” the matter for an hour but without any result.
questions.explanation: To 'talk over' a matter is to discuss it thoroughly; 'talk of' only mentions it.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. Sahukaars provide loan “in 2% interest rate for a month”, which is higher than the bank charges.
questions.explanation: Interest is charged 'at' a rate, and the period is given by 'per': 'at 2% interest rate per month'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an INCORRECTLY spelt word Subsequent to the delegation’s visit to the villages, / a new working commitee and a task force / have been formed to carry out / all the developmental works as promised to the people.
options: Subsequent to the delegation’s visit to the villages
have been formed to carry out
a new working commitee and a task force
all the developmental works as promised to the people
questions.explanation: 'Commitee' is misspelt: the word is 'committee', with double 'm', double 't' and double 'e'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. As was customary, the young prince was brought to the podium in a diamond studded carriage for the coronation ceremony.
options: As was customary, the young prince brings himself to the podium in a diamond studded carriage for the coronation ceremony
As was customary, the young prince is bought to the podium in a diamond studded carriage for the coronation ceremony.
As was customary, the young prince brought in a diamond studded carriage to the podium for the coronation ceremony.
As was customary, the palace staff brought the young prince to the podium in a diamond studded carriage for the coronation ceremony.
questions.explanation: The active voice needs a doer as subject, kept in the simple past: 'the palace staff brought the young prince to the podium'. The other options change the meaning or the tense.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. We should all “stays” united.
questions.explanation: After a modal such as 'should' the verb takes its base form: 'We should all stay united.'

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. Reena got “embarrassed and started crying.”
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'humiliated and started weeping', the only option that keeps the sense: 'weeping' is crying and 'humiliated' a stronger 'embarrassed'. The sentence as printed is already correct, and there is no 'no improvement' option.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'sabotage'.

questions.text: Which word in the given sentence is the ANTONYM of – nibble? They sprinted across the floor and leaped up to the elevated platforms, poking their soft muzzles into the stanchions to gobble the grain.
questions.explanation: To 'nibble' is to eat in small bites; to 'gobble' is to eat greedily in large mouthfuls.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. One who loves the company of others
questions.explanation: 'Gregarious' describes one who is fond of company. A misanthrope dislikes people, and a philanthropist works for the welfare of others.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Under the weather
questions.explanation: To be 'under the weather' is to feel ill or unwell.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. The sharp increase in our consumption of fossil fuels has led to their depletion at an alarming rate. B. Unchecked burning of fossil fuel is like an unchecked dripping tap which will eventually run dry. C. The toxic pollutants released from burning these fuels are also a cause for concern. D. This has led to the tapping of various non-conventional sources of energy that are cleaner alternatives to fossil fuels.
questions.explanation: A states the problem (fossil fuels running out), C adds a second concern ('also'), B sums it up as a tap that will run dry, and D gives the result ('This has led to'): ACBD.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Pure
questions.explanation: 'Pure' in its moral sense means clean and decent; its opposite is 'indecent'. 'Flawless' is close to a synonym.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error You and I / am going / to make / a great team.
questions.explanation: 'You and I' is a plural subject, so the verb is 'are': 'You and I are going to make a great team.'

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. I was “forbidden to take” any drink.
questions.explanation: 'Prohibit' takes 'from' with an -ing form, and 'receiving' keeps the meaning of 'take'; rebuffing, rejecting and snubbing all mean refusing.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. By leaps and bounds
options: Superb catch in a cricket match
questions.explanation: To grow 'by leaps and bounds' is to grow very quickly.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Relate comic things (1)__________ pompous fashion. Irregularity, in other words the unexpected, the surprising, the astonishing, are essential to and characteristic (2)__________ beauty. Two fundamental literary qualities: supernaturalism and irony. The blend (3)__________ the grotesque and the tragic are attractive to the mind, as is discord to blasé ears. Imagine a canvas for a lyrical, magical farce, for a pantomime, and translate it (4) __________ a serious novel. Drown the whole thing in an abnormal, (5) ___________ atmosphere, in the atmosphere of great days – the region of pure poetry.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Manner takes 'in': relate comic things 'in pompous fashion'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Relate comic things (1)__________ pompous fashion. Irregularity, in other words the unexpected, the surprising, the astonishing, are essential to and characteristic (2)__________ beauty. Two fundamental literary qualities: supernaturalism and irony. The blend (3)__________ the grotesque and the tragic are attractive to the mind, as is discord to blasé ears. Imagine a canvas for a lyrical, magical farce, for a pantomime, and translate it (4) __________ a serious novel. Drown the whole thing in an abnormal, (5) ___________ atmosphere, in the atmosphere of great days – the region of pure poetry.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: 'Characteristic' takes 'of': essential to and 'characteristic of beauty'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Relate comic things (1)__________ pompous fashion. Irregularity, in other words the unexpected, the surprising, the astonishing, are essential to and characteristic (2)__________ beauty. Two fundamental literary qualities: supernaturalism and irony. The blend (3)__________ the grotesque and the tragic are attractive to the mind, as is discord to blasé ears. Imagine a canvas for a lyrical, magical farce, for a pantomime, and translate it (4) __________ a serious novel. Drown the whole thing in an abnormal, (5) ___________ atmosphere, in the atmosphere of great days – the region of pure poetry.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: A mixture is 'the blend of' its parts: the blend of the grotesque and the tragic.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Relate comic things (1)__________ pompous fashion. Irregularity, in other words the unexpected, the surprising, the astonishing, are essential to and characteristic (2)__________ beauty. Two fundamental literary qualities: supernaturalism and irony. The blend (3)__________ the grotesque and the tragic are attractive to the mind, as is discord to blasé ears. Imagine a canvas for a lyrical, magical farce, for a pantomime, and translate it (4) __________ a serious novel. Drown the whole thing in an abnormal, (5) ___________ atmosphere, in the atmosphere of great days – the region of pure poetry.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: Turning a work from one form to another is translating it 'into' that form: 'translate it into a serious novel'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Relate comic things (1)__________ pompous fashion. Irregularity, in other words the unexpected, the surprising, the astonishing, are essential to and characteristic (2)__________ beauty. Two fundamental literary qualities: supernaturalism and irony. The blend (3)__________ the grotesque and the tragic are attractive to the mind, as is discord to blasé ears. Imagine a canvas for a lyrical, magical farce, for a pantomime, and translate it (4) __________ a serious novel. Drown the whole thing in an abnormal, (5) ___________ atmosphere, in the atmosphere of great days – the region of pure poetry.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: An abnormal, 'dreamy' atmosphere suits the magical farce and 'the region of pure poetry' the passage describes.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the sixth term is related to the fifth term. 13 : 78 :: 23 : ? :: 19 : 228
questions.explanation: Each number is multiplied by itself minus 7: 13 × 6 = 78 and 19 × 12 = 228. Likewise 23 × 16 = 368.

questions.text: If 25 March 1995 is a Saturday, then what will be the day of the week on 12 December 1997?
questions.explanation: From 25 March 1995 to 25 March 1997 is 366 + 365 = 731 days (1996 was a leap year), 3 odd days: a Tuesday. From 25 March to 12 December 1997 is 262 days, 3 more odd days: Friday.

questions.text: Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it. First row:54, 72, 90 Second row: 79, 97, 115 Third row:83, 101, ? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the number into its constituent digits. For example, 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
In a certain code language, ‘PAIR’ is written as ‘ZKIR’ and ‘SAIL’ is written as ‘ZHOR’. How will ‘BULK’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite in the alphabet (A ↔ Z, B ↔ Y, ...) and the letters are then swapped in pairs: PAIR → KZRI → ZKIR and SAIL → HZRO → ZHOR. So BULK → YFOP → FYPO.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that, when sequentially placed from left to right in the blanks below, will complete the letter series. K a _ _ N _ a K _ R a _ K a _a R _ N K a
options: R a K a N K a
K a K a N K a
R a K a N R a
R a R a N K a
questions.explanation: With R, a, K, a, N, K, a in the blanks the block KaRaNKa repeats: KaRaNKa KaRaNKa KaRaNKa.

questions.text: If ‘A’ denotes ‘+’, ‘B’ denotes ‘×’, ‘C’ denotes ‘–’ and ‘D’ denotes ‘÷’, then what will come in place of ‘?’ in the following equation? 21 A 34 C 6 B (72 D 9) A 13 B 1 + (56 D 4) = ?
Select the option that represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in an English dictionary. 1.Proper 2.Pronoun 3.Proof 4.Prophecy 5.Propel
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Pronoun (2), Proof (3), Propel (5), Proper (1), Prophecy (4). 'Pron' comes before 'Proo' and 'Prop'; 'Propel' before 'Proper' (l before r), and 'Prope' before 'Proph'.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set.
