(50, 10, 15) (60, 10, 16) (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed)
questions.explanation: The first number divided by the second, plus the second, gives the third: 50 ÷ 10 + 10 = 15 and 60 ÷ 10 + 10 = 16. Likewise 60 ÷ 15 + 15 = 19.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 57, 62, 45, ?, 33, 86
questions.explanation: Two series alternate: 57, 45, 33 fall by 12, and 62, ?, 86 rise by 12, so ? = 74.

questions.text: Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some strawberries are bananas. All bananas are avocados. Some avocados are grapes. Conclusion: I. Some avocados are bananas. II. Some grapes are bananas. III. Some avocados are strawberries.
options: Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions I and III follow
questions.explanation: All bananas are avocados, so some avocados are bananas (I); the strawberries that are bananas are avocados, so some avocados are strawberries (III). The grapes need not overlap the bananas, so II does not follow.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'BROWSER' is written as 'DTQYUGT' and ‘MONITOR’ is written as ‘OQPKVQT’. How will 'PRINTER' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places forward: BROWSER → DTQYUGT and MONITOR → OQPKVQT. So PRINTER → RTKPVGT.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. BURGER : UBTIRE :: EDITOR : DEKVRO :: PLASMA : ?
questions.explanation: In pairs of letters, the first pair is swapped, each letter of the middle pair moves 2 places forward and the last pair is swapped: BU RG ER → UB TI RE and ED IT OR → DE KV RO. So PL AS MA → LP CU AM.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 13 : 120 : : 17 : 152 : : 21 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is the first plus 2, times 8: 15 × 8 = 120 and 19 × 8 = 152. Likewise 23 × 8 = 184.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and fourth term related to third term. 12:1764 :: 8:528 :: 16:?
questions.explanation: The second number is the cube of the first plus the square of its half: 12³ + 6² = 1728 + 36 = 1764 and 8³ + 4² = 512 + 16 = 528. Likewise 16³ + 8² = 4096 + 64 = 4160.

questions.text: Each of the seven friends, Misha, Minshu, Mohi, Priya, Veer, Pari and Krishi, has a different height. Krishi is taller than only three people. Pari is taller than only Veer. Misha is taller than Minshu but not Mohi. Priya is taller than Mohi. Who among the following is taller than Krishi?
questions.explanation: Veer is the shortest and Pari next. Krishi, taller than exactly three, is fourth from the bottom, and Minshu < Misha < Mohi < Priya fill the other places, so Minshu is third and Misha, Mohi and Priya are taller than Krishi. Of the options, only Mohi is.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 23, 22, 26, 17, 33, 8, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are −1, +4, −9, +16, −25: squares with alternating signs. The next is +36: 8 + 36 = 44.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 16, 96, 101, ?, 407, 814
Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 91*13*26*51*18
questions.explanation: 91 ÷ 13 + 26 = 51 − 18, as both sides equal 33.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that, when placed from left to right in the blanks, will complete the letter series. _ V E F I B V _ F I C V E F _ D _ E F _
questions.explanation: With A, E, I, V, I in the blanks the series is AVEFI BVEFI CVEFI DVEFI: the first letter runs A, B, C, D and VEFI repeats.

questions.text: In an election between two candidates, a candidate who gets 72% of votes is elected by a majority of 572 votes. Find the total number of the votes polled. (assuming all votes are valid)
questions.explanation: The winner's majority is 72% − 28% = 44% of the votes polled, so the total is 572 ÷ 0.44 = 1300.

questions.text: If we want ₹8,640 three years from now and the compounded interest rate is 20% p.a how much should we invest today? (assuming interest is compounded yearly)

A man offers a 21% discount on an item. He offers a further discount of 40% on the reduced price for the first 100 customers. If the selling price of the item is ₹4,740, and the customer is one of the frist 100 then the marked price (in ₹) of the item is
questions.explanation: Marked price × 0.79 × 0.6 = 0.474 × marked price = ₹4,740, so the marked price is ₹10,000.

questions.text: A dealer purchased a food processor for ₹10,000. He offered a discount of 20% on its listed price and still gained a profit of 40%. Find the listed price of the food processor.
questions.explanation: A 40% profit on ₹10,000 means a selling price of ₹14,000. That is 80% of the listed price, so the listed price is 14,000 ÷ 0.8 = ₹17,500.

questions.text: In a 1500-m race, if A beats B by 100 m and B beats C by 150 m, then by what distance (in m) does A beat C?
questions.explanation: While A runs 1500 m, B runs 1400 m; while B runs 1500 m, C runs 1350 m, so while B runs 1400 m, C runs 1400 × 1350/1500 = 1260 m. A beats C by 1500 − 1260 = 240 m.

questions.text: Find the third proportional to 27 and 18.
questions.explanation: The third proportional to a and b is b²/a = 18²/27 = 324/27 = 12.

questions.text: Raman has a certain average after 9 innings. In the 10th inning he scores 100 runs, thereby increasing his average by 8 runs. His new average is ________.
questions.explanation: With the old average a, 9a + 100 = 10(a + 8), so a = 20 and the new average is 28.

questions.text: Find the volume of a solid hemisphere whose radius is 6.3 cm.(Use π=22/7)
Which of the following numbers is NOT divisible by 36?
questions.explanation: A number divisible by 36 must be divisible by both 4 and 9. The digits of 136216 add up to 19, not a multiple of 9; the other three have digit sums of 18 or 36, and their last two digits (44, 84, 16) are multiples of 4.

questions.text: PQ and RS are two parallel chords of a circle of length 10 cm and 24 cm, respectively, and lie on the same side of the centre O. If the distance between the chords is 7 cm, what is the radius (in cm) of the circle?
questions.explanation: With radius r, the chords lie √(r² − 5²) and √(r² − 12²) from the centre, and these differ by 7. For r = 13 they are 12 and 5, which are 7 apart.

questions.text: A seller combines 26 kg of rice priced at ₹20 per kg with 30 kg of rice priced at ₹36 per kg and sells the mixture for ₹30 per kg. What is the percentage of profit he makes?
With an average speed of 60 km/h, a train reaches its destination on time. If it goes with an average speed of 45 km/h, it is late by 20 minutes. The distance covered by the train is _____.
questions.explanation: The 20 minutes is the difference of the two journey times: d/45 − d/60 = d/180 = 1/3 hour, so d = 60 km.

questions.text: The surface area of a solid metallic sphere is 616 cm². It is melted and recast into a solid cone of height 28 cm. Find the diameter of the base of the cone so formed. (Take π=22/7)
questions.explanation: 4πr² = 616 gives r² = 49, so r = 7 cm. Equal volumes: (1/3)πR² × 28 = (4/3)π × 7³, so R² = 4 × 343/28 = 49, R = 7 cm and the diameter is 14 cm.

questions.text: What is the radius of a sphere having volume of 4851cm³? (Use π=22/7)
A dealer had 120 kg of wheat. A part of it was sold by him at 10% gain and the rest at 25% gain. overall, he had a gain of 15%. How much of the wheat was sold at 10% gain?
questions.explanation: By alligation, the parts sold at 10% and 25% gain are in the ratio (25 − 15) : (15 − 10) = 2 : 1, so 2/3 × 120 = 80 kg was sold at 10% gain.

questions.text: In one-sixth of the time that B takes to complete a piece of work, A can complete half of the same work. If working together they take 16 days to complete the work, how much time shall B take to complete it alone?
questions.explanation: If B takes b days for the whole work, A does half of it in b/6 days, so all of it in b/3 days. Together: 3/b + 1/b = 4/b = 1/16, so b = 64 days.

questions.text: In February 2022, the Karnataka High Court declared certain provisions of the Karnataka Police (Amendment) Act, 2021 as unconstitutional, which prohibited and criminalised the activities related to ________.
questions.explanation: In February 2022 the Karnataka High Court struck down the provisions of the 2021 amendment that banned and criminalised online games played for stakes, games of skill included.

questions.text: How many countries share the natural heritage of the Caspian Sea?
questions.explanation: Five countries border the Caspian Sea: Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran and Azerbaijan.

questions.text: Who among the following described the Indian Constitution as ‘quasi federal’?
questions.explanation: K C Wheare called the Indian Constitution 'quasi-federal': in his view a unitary state with subsidiary federal features, rather than a federal state with subsidiary unitary features.

questions.text: Who among the following became the youngest player to defeat world number one chess champion, Magnus Carlsen, of Norway in an online chess tournament in February 2021?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives R Praggnanandhaa, who at 16 beat Magnus Carlsen in the online Airthings Masters rapid tournament. That game was played in February 2022, not February 2021 as the question says.

questions.text: To combat inflation, what is the usual monetary policy stance adopted?
questions.explanation: A 'hawkish' stance, with higher interest rates and tighter money, is used to curb inflation; a 'dovish' one favours growth with easier money.

questions.text: Which of the following novel is written by Bhisham Sahni?
questions.explanation: Bhisham Sahni's 'Tamas' is a novel about the riots of Partition. 'Nirmala' is Premchand's, and 'Gunahon Ka Devta' Dharamvir Bharati's.

questions.text: What is the role of ribosomes of a polysome?
questions.explanation: Several ribosomes reading one mRNA form a polysome, and each of them translates the mRNA into protein.

questions.text: Who synthesised acetic acid for the first time?
questions.explanation: Kolbe synthesised acetic acid from inorganic starting materials in 1845, after Wöhler's synthesis of urea; Berthelot made methane in 1856.

questions.text: The Novel ‘Train to Pakistan’ dealing with the tragedy of India’s Partition is written by whom among the following authors?
questions.explanation: 'Train to Pakistan' (1956), set in a border village during Partition, is by Khushwant Singh.

questions.text: Identify the factor that does NOT affect the salinity of the ocean.
options: The type of marine organisms found in the water bodies
The rate of evaporation and precipitation
The amount of fresh water flowing into the ocean
questions.explanation: Ocean salinity depends on evaporation and precipitation, the inflow of fresh water from rivers, wind and ocean currents; the kinds of marine organisms present do not affect it.

questions.text: Who among the following is NOT a recipient of Bharat Ratna Award?
questions.explanation: Kumar Gandharva was not given the Bharat Ratna. Ravi Shankar (1999), Bismillah Khan (2001) and Bhimsen Joshi (2009) received it.

questions.text: The systematic name of which compound is nitrogen trihydride that is widely used in many industrial processes, and as a fertiliser and refrigerant?
questions.explanation: Ammonia, NH₃, is nitrogen trihydride, used to make fertilisers and as a refrigerant.

questions.text: The “Sattriya” classical dance is associated with which state?
questions.explanation: Sattriya, created by Srimanta Sankardeva in the Vaishnava monasteries (sattras), is the classical dance of Assam.

questions.text: Allah Jilai Bai, a singer from Rajasthan is famous for which of the following?
questions.explanation: Allah Jilai Bai of Bikaner was a celebrated singer of Rajasthani folk songs in the Maand style, best known for 'Kesariya Balam'.

questions.text: What is the maximum number of players of a single team on the floor at one time in a basketball game?
questions.explanation: A basketball team has five players on the court at a time.

questions.text: Which of the following teams was defeated by the Indian Hockey team to win the bronze medal in Asian Champions Trophy 2021 on December 22, 2021?
questions.explanation: India beat Pakistan 4-3 in the bronze-medal match of the 2021 Asian Champions Trophy in Dhaka.

questions.text: Rama Vaidyanathan was awarded with the honour of the Devadasi National Award in 2013 for her contribution in which of the following Indian dance forms?
questions.explanation: Rama Vaidyanathan is a leading Bharatanatyam dancer.

questions.text: Famous singer Teejan Bai is related to which of the following folk musics?
questions.explanation: Teejan Bai of Chhattisgarh is the best-known performer of Pandvani, which sings the story of the Mahabharata.

questions.text: Which of the following is used as a pesticide or fumigant for cereals and as an igniting agent in flares?
questions.explanation: Aluminium phosphide is the common fumigant for stored grain: with moisture it gives off phosphine, a poisonous gas.

questions.text: As per coding convention of India Census, how many digit code is used for showing state code?
questions.explanation: In the Census of India's location codes each state has a 2-digit code; districts have 3 digits.

questions.text: In which sport is the term LONA used?
questions.explanation: In kabaddi a 'lona' is scored when a side puts out all the players of the other team, earning bonus points.

questions.text: Who among the following has been awarded the Padma Shri in 2020 for her contribution in Indian Classical dance?
questions.explanation: Indira P P Bora, a Sattriya and Bharatanatyam dancer from Assam, received the Padma Shri in 2020.

questions.text: Kamalini Asthana and Nalini Asthana, the celebrated dancer duo have been conferred the Padma Shri for their significant contribution to which of the following dance forms in 2022?
questions.explanation: Kamalini and Nalini Asthana, a Kathak duo, received the Padma Shri in 2022.

questions.text: Autobiography of an Unknown Indian is the collective memoir of ____________.
questions.explanation: 'The Autobiography of an Unknown Indian' (1951) is Nirad C Chaudhuri's memoir.

questions.text: Who among the following won the Best Male Singer National Award at the 67th National Film Awards?
questions.explanation: B Praak won the award for 'Teri Mitti' from the film 'Kesari' at the 67th National Film Awards.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Have a long face
questions.explanation: To 'have a long face' is to look unhappy or disappointed.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'curiosity'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. One who believes in the existence of a god or gods
questions.explanation: A theist believes in God or gods; an atheist does not.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Marvellous
questions.explanation: 'Marvellous' means wonderful; its opposite is 'terrible'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. It is better to contact “someone who draws maps” to get help in your research project.
questions.explanation: A cartographer draws maps; a lexicographer compiles dictionaries.

questions.text: Identify the option that arranges the given parts in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. a) Further, loud music is also a cause of noise pollution b) Noise pollution is the result of aircraft and heavy traffic. c) which has been seen to affect people’s hearing and d) give them severe headaches and high blood pressure
questions.explanation: 'Noise pollution is the result of aircraft and heavy traffic (b). Further, loud music is also a cause of noise pollution (a) which has been seen to affect people's hearing and (c) give them severe headaches and high blood pressure (d).'

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. Danny is the “better” basketball player in the team.
questions.explanation: Comparing one player with the rest of a team needs the superlative: 'the best basketball player in the team'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Two __________ control the judge’s decision: justice and impartiality.
questions.explanation: Justice and impartiality are the two 'principles' that guide the judge's decision.

questions.text: The following sentence contains a grammatical error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error. As a rule, single sentences should not be write or printed as paragraphs.
options: As a rule, single sentences should not be wrote or printed as paragraphs.
As a rule, single sentences should not write or print as paragraphs.
As a rule, single sentences shall not have written or printed as paragraphs.
As a rule, single sentences should not be written or printed as paragraphs.
questions.explanation: The passive takes 'be' with the past participle: 'should not be written or printed'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Pleasing
questions.explanation: 'Pleasing' and 'gratifying' both mean giving pleasure or satisfaction.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Ardent
questions.explanation: 'Ardent' means passionate and eager; its opposite is 'apathetic', showing no interest.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underline segment in the given sentence. Some politicians “turn up their face” at the hard life of downtrodden people.
questions.explanation: To 'turn up one's nose at' something is to treat it with disdain.

questions.text: Spot the error in the given sentence and select the correct sentence from the options given. All the panel members has been invited for the monthly meeting.
options: All the panel members was invited for the monthly meeting.
All the panel members been invited for the monthly meeting.
All the panel members have been invited for the monthly meeting.
All the panel members would have being invited for the monthly meeting.
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'members' takes a plural verb: 'have been invited'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Someone who is shy and spends time alone rather than being with others
questions.explanation: An introvert is shy and prefers to be alone; an extrovert is the opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. The best of both worlds
options: The best practices in both, ancient times and present times
The best people on Earth and in heaven
An advantageous situation from two different things at a time
Being good in dreams and in reality
questions.explanation: 'The best of both worlds' is a situation in which one enjoys the advantages of two different things at once.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. He does not trust anybody.
options: Anybody is not to be trusted by him.
Anybody is trusted not by him.
questions.explanation: The object 'anybody' becomes the subject, with the negative carried into it: 'Nobody is trusted by him.'

questions.text: Select the sentence which has no spelling error.
options: A magnifisent Humayun tomb was built by Hamida Bano in Delhi.
There are many magnificent churches in Goa.
The sight of waterfall was magnifecent in the brochure.
The bride looked bright, simple and magneficent.
questions.explanation: 'Magnificent' is spelt correctly only in the sentence about the churches in Goa.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Stymie
questions.explanation: To 'stymie' is to obstruct or 'hinder'.

questions.text: Parts of the given sentence have been given as options. One of them contains a grammatical error. Select the option that has the error. Though you may not be able to conquer, I exhort you to fought bravely to the last.
options: to fought bravely to the last
questions.explanation: 'To' before a verb takes the base form: 'I exhort you to fight bravely'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Many of the major supermarket chains have come under fire with accusations of (1)__________ unethical acts over the past decade. They've wasted tonnes of food, they've underpaid their suppliers and they've contributed to excessive plastic waste in their packaging, which has had its impact on our environment. But supermarkets and grocers are (2)__________ to sit up and take notice. In response to (3)__________ consumer backlash against the huge amounts of plastic waste generated by plastic packaging, some of the largest UK supermarkets have (4)__________ up a pact promising to transform packaging and cut plastic wastage. In a pledge to reuse, recycle or compost all plastic wastage by 2025, supermarkets are now beginning to take (5)__________ responsibility for the part they play in contributing to the damage to our environment, with one major supermarket announcing their plan to eliminate all plastic packaging in their own-brand products by 2023.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'Accusations of various unethical acts': the sentences that follow list several kinds of wrongdoing.

questions.text: The second number in the given number pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number pairs except one. Find that odd number pair.
questions.explanation: In 25 : 8, 169 : 16 and 64 : 11 the second number is the square root of the first plus 3 (5 + 3, 13 + 3, 8 + 3). For 225 it would be 15 + 3 = 18, not 12.

questions.text: Consider the given statement and the following conclusions and decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement. Statement: Private school teachers are hard-working. Conclusion: (I) Some hard-working teachers are private school teachers. (II) Government employees are not hard-working.
questions.explanation: If private school teachers are hard-working, some hard-working teachers must be private school teachers (I). The statement says nothing about government employees, so II does not follow.

questions.text: Seven friends S, T, U, V, W, X and Y, each has scored different marks in an examination. W scored more than X but less than V. Only three people scored more than V. T scored more than U but less than S. Y scored the least among all. How many persons scored between T and X?
questions.explanation: Y is last and V fourth. W and X are below V, so the three above V are S, T and U, with S > T > U. The order is S, T, U, V, W, X, Y, and three people, U, V and W, come between T and X.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘PLURAL’ is written as ‘MQSVMB’ and ‘SINGLE’ is written as ‘JTHOFM’. How will ‘DOUBLE’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters are taken in pairs, each pair reversed and every letter moved one place forward: PL UR AL → LP RU LA → MQ SV MB. So DO UB LE → OD BU EL → PE CV FM: PECVFM.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 17:48 :: 23:66 :: 15:?
questions.explanation: The second number is three times the first minus 3: 17 × 3 − 3 = 48 and 23 × 3 − 3 = 66. Likewise 15 × 3 − 3 = 42.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 2 * 5 * 5 * 10 * 5
questions.explanation: 2 × 5 − 5 = 10 − 5: both sides equal 5.

questions.text: In a certain code language, “REPORT” is written as “SDQNSS”, and “THANKS” is written as “UGBMLR”. How will “WINTER” be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +1 and −1 alternately: R → S, E → D, P → Q, O → N, R → S, T → S. So WINTER → XHOSFQ.

questions.text: Pointing to a man in photograph, Rohan said, “His daughter’s brother is my mother’s son’s brother.” How is the man related to Rohan?
questions.explanation: Rohan's mother's son's brother is Rohan's brother (or Rohan himself), and the man's daughter's brother is the man's son. So the man's son is Rohan or his brother, and the man is Rohan's father.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 21*5*61*84*4*8*15

Select the option that is related to the fourth number in the same way as the first number is related to the second number and the fifth number is related to the sixth number. 8 : 72 :: ? : 152 :: 17 : 297
questions.explanation: Each first number squared plus 8 gives its partner: 8² + 8 = 72 and 17² + 8 = 297. So ?² + 8 = 152, ?² = 144 and ? = 12.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. SYMBOL : YSNYLO :: TALENT : ATOVTN :: MOBILE : ?
questions.explanation: Taken in pairs, the first and last pairs are written in reverse, and the middle pair is replaced by its opposite letters (A ↔ Z, B ↔ Y, ...): SY MB OL → YS NY LO. So MO BI LE → OM YR EL: OMYREL.

questions.text: Which two numbers, from amongst the given options, should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? (36 ÷ 4) ×12 + (7×6) – 18 + (3×9) = 63

Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it. First row- 12, 51, 159 Second row- 9, 39, 123 Third row- 8, 35,? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed)
questions.explanation: In each row the second number is 4 × the first + 3 and the third is 3 × the second + 6: 12 → 51 → 159 and 9 → 39 → 123. So 8 → 35 → 3 × 35 + 6 = 111.

questions.text: If 19 April 1962 is a Thursday, then what will be the day of the week on 15 June 1965?
questions.explanation: From 19 April 1962 to 19 April 1965 is 365 + 366 + 365 = 1,096 days (1964 is a leap year), 4 odd days, so 19 April 1965 was a Monday. The 57 days on to 15 June (11 + 31 + 15) add 1 odd day: Tuesday.

questions.text: If ‘A’ denotes ‘+’, ‘B’ denotes ‘×’, ‘C’ denotes ‘–’ and ‘D’ denotes ‘÷’, then what will come in place of ‘?’ in the following equation? (91 D 13) B 8 C 50 A 16 B 2 A (99 D 11) = ?

Select the option that is related to the fourth number in the same way as the first number is related to the second number and the fifth number is related to the sixth number. 19 : 361 :: ? : 576 :: 6 : 36
questions.explanation: Each first number is the square root of its partner: 19² = 361 and 6² = 36. So ?² = 576 and ? = 24.

questions.text: Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it. First row: 17, 8, 153 Second row: 19, 6, 133 Third row: 13, 7, ? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the number into its constituent digits. For example, 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In each row the third number is the first × (the second + 1): 17 × 9 = 153 and 19 × 7 = 133. So 13 × 8 = 104.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series. A B _ K P C D H _ P E F H K _ G _ H K P
questions.explanation: The series is groups of five letters, two consecutive letters followed by H K P: ABHKP, CDHKP, EFHKP, GHHKP. The blanks are H, K, P, H.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that, when sequentially placed from left to right in the blanks below, will complete the letter series. r d _ n _ d r _ _ b n n d _ r d b _ n d r
options: r n r d r n
b n r d r r
n n r d r n
b n r d r n
questions.explanation: With b, n, r, d, r, n in the blanks the block 'rdbnndr' repeats: rdbnndr rdbnndr rdbnndr.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 3?
questions.explanation: A number is divisible by 3 when its digit sum is: 7 + 8 + 6 + 5 + 0 + 0 + 1 = 27. The other digit sums are 32, 28 and 35.

questions.text: An authorised rice dealer purchases rice at ₹32 per kg and sells it at ₹40 per kg. But while selling, he is giving only 900 grams instead of 1 kg. Find the actual profit percentage of the dealer (Correct to one decimal place)
When the price of an article was reduced by 25%, its sale was increased by 75%. Calculate the net effect on revenue.
questions.explanation: Revenue = price × sales: 0.75 × 1.75 = 1.3125, a 31.25% increase.

questions.text: A person runs at an average speed of 20 km/h for 30 minutes and cycles at a speed of 32 km/h for 1 hour 15 minutes. Calculate the average speed (in km/h, rounded off to 1 decimal place).
questions.explanation: Distance = 20 × ½ + 32 × 1¼ = 10 + 40 = 50 km in 1¾ hours: 50 ÷ 1.75 = 28.6 km/h.

questions.text: The average of 25 numbers is 18. The average of the first 12 of these numbers is 14 and that of the last 12 of these numbers is 17. The 13th number is:
questions.explanation: Total = 25 × 18 = 450; the first 12 sum to 168 and the last 12 to 204. The 13th = 450 − 168 − 204 = 78.

questions.text: In a school, students using school bus, bike and bicycle for transport are in the proportion 6 : 3 : 1. If the total strength of the school is 1200, find the number of students who use bicycle for transport. (Each student uses only one of the given 3 modes of transport)
questions.explanation: Bicycle users are 1 part of 6 + 3 + 1 = 10: 1200 ÷ 10 = 120.

questions.text: Which of the following options does NOT give the lengths of three sides of any triangle?
questions.explanation: Any two sides of a triangle must add up to more than the third. 18 + 23 = 41 only equals the third side, so 18, 23, 41 cannot form a triangle.

questions.text: In a class there are 26 boys and 24 girls. The Math teacher administered a test and found that the average score of the whole class is 85.If the average score of the boys was 82, find the average score of the girls.
A shopkeeper buys a note book for ₹85. He wants a profit of 20% after giving a discount of 15%. At what price should he mark the note book?
questions.explanation: Selling price = 85 × 1.2 = ₹102, which is 85% of the marked price: 102/0.85 = ₹120.

questions.text: Taking π = 3.14, find the volume of a cylinder having its radius of base as 5 cm and its height as 24 cm.
What is the value of the expression 100(sin 15° cos 15°)?
questions.explanation: sin 15° cos 15° = ½ sin 30° = ¼, so the value is 100 × ¼ = 25.

questions.text: The perimeter of an isosceles triangle is 80 cm. If the side that is not equal in length to any of the other two sides is 20 cm, find the length of each of the equal sides.
questions.explanation: The two equal sides total 80 − 20 = 60 cm, so each is 30 cm.

questions.text: A number is first increased by 25% and then decreased by 10%. If the resulting number is 72, what is the original number?
A sum of money becomes ₹2,000 in 3 years and ₹2,400 in 4 years, at the certain rate of yearly compound interest in case of annual compounding. Find the yearly rate of compound interest.
questions.explanation: In the fourth year ₹2,000 earns ₹400 of interest: 400/2,000 × 100 = 20%.

questions.text: A boat’s speed in still water is 22 km/h, while the river is flowing with a speed of 8 km/h and the time taken to cover a certain distance upstream is 4 hours more than the time taken to cover the same distance downstream. Find the distance.
questions.explanation: Downstream speed is 22 + 8 = 30 km/h and upstream 22 − 8 = 14 km/h. d/14 − d/30 = 4 gives 16d/420 = 4, so d = 105 km.

questions.text: Ram and Shawan working together can complete a job in 5 hours, where as Ram alone can complete the same job in 6 hours. In how many hours can Shawan alone complete the job?
questions.explanation: Shawan's rate = 1/5 − 1/6 = 1/30 of the job an hour: 30 hours.

questions.text: A shopkeeper offers the following four schemes. Which scheme has the maximum discount percentage? a)Two successive discounts of 22% and 25% b)Buy 3, get 2 free c)Buy 5, get 4 free d)Buy 4, get 3 free
questions.explanation: Discounts: (a) 1 − 0.78 × 0.75 = 41.5%; (b) 2 free in 5 = 40%; (c) 4 free in 9 = 44.4%; (d) 3 free in 7 = 42.9%. Buy 5, get 4 free gives the most.

questions.text: Ustad Bade Ghulam Ali Khan, often touted as Tansen of the 20th century is famous for which of the following music genres?
questions.explanation: Bade Ghulam Ali Khan, of the Patiala gharana, was a Hindustani classical vocalist.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following is the autobiography of Maulana Abul Kalam Azad?
questions.explanation: 'India Wins Freedom' is Maulana Abul Kalam Azad's autobiographical account of the freedom struggle and Partition.

questions.text: Tanya Hemant is related to which of the following sports?
questions.explanation: Tanya Hemanth is an Indian badminton player.

questions.text: In October 2021, an order was issued by the Social Justice and Empowerment Department of Rajasthan to give the benefits of a pension scheme to all persons within __________________ categories of disabilities under the 'Rajasthan Social Security Special Persons Pension Scheme' in the state.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 21: the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 lists 21 specified disabilities, and the order extended the pension to all of them.

questions.text: What happens to the salinity at the surface of the ocean?
options: Decreases by the loss of water to ice or evaporation
Increases by the loss of water to ice or evaporation
questions.explanation: Evaporation, and freezing into ice, remove water but leave the salt behind, so surface salinity rises; precipitation and river water lower it.

questions.text: What is the common name of CHCl₃?
questions.explanation: CHCl₃, trichloromethane, is commonly called chloroform.

questions.text: In the context of micro-finance, SHG refers to _______________.
questions.explanation: In micro-finance an SHG is a Self Help Group: a small group, often of women, that pools its savings and borrows from banks together.

questions.text: In April 2021, the state government of Assam launched the Tractor Distribution Scheme under the Chief Minister Samagra Gramya Unnayan Yojna (CMSGUY) for farmers, with the objectives of reviving the agriculture sector and helping in doubling the farmer’s income by ___________________.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 2022, in line with the Centre's goal of doubling farmers' incomes by 2022.

questions.text: Renowned dancer and actor Minati Mishra was conferred with the Padma Shri for her significant contribution to which of the following Classical Dance forms?
questions.explanation: Minati Mishra was an Odissi dancer who also acted in Odia films.

questions.text: In Budget 2022-23,Government of India decided to continue the Scheme of ‘Khelo India – National Programme for Development of Sports’ over the 15th Finance Commission Cycle (2021-22 to 2025-26) at an outlay of________.
questions.explanation: The Khelo India scheme was continued for the 15th Finance Commission cycle, 2021-22 to 2025-26, with an outlay of ₹3,165.50 crore.

questions.text: Padma Bhushan awardee, Buddhadev Das Gupta was an Indian classical _________ player.
questions.explanation: Buddhadev Das Gupta was a celebrated sarod player.

questions.text: T Balasaraswati, a dance legend from India was awarded the Padma Vibhushan for her contribution to Indian art and culture, in which of the following dance forms?
questions.explanation: T. Balasaraswati was one of the great Bharatanatyam dancers of the twentieth century.

questions.text: Who among the following is NOT a Veena player?
questions.explanation: Pandit Jasraj was a Hindustani classical vocalist of the Mewati gharana. Jayanthi Kumaresh, S. Balachander and Veenai Dhanammal are all veena players.

questions.text: The reflection on a bathroom mirror, the lake, and the glare on a pair of glasses are caused by which type of reflection?
questions.explanation: Specular reflection is the mirror-like reflection from a smooth surface, where parallel rays stay parallel; a rough surface gives diffuse reflection.

questions.text: Of which of the following forms are Kelucharan Mahapatra, Sonal Mansingh and Geeta Mahalik famous dancers?
questions.explanation: Kelucharan Mohapatra, Sonal Mansingh and Geeta Mahalik are all Odissi dancers.

questions.text: Who among the following Kuchipudi dancers received the Padma Shri Award in 2022?
questions.explanation: The Kuchipudi dancer Padmaja Reddy received the Padma Shri in 2022.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of active transport?
questions.explanation: The sodium-potassium pump uses energy from ATP to move sodium ions out of the cell and potassium ions in, against their concentration gradients.

questions.text: Identify the disease that is caused due to inadequate secretion of the hormone insulin from the pancreas?
questions.explanation: Diabetes mellitus results when the pancreas secretes too little insulin (or the body does not respond to it), so blood sugar stays high.

questions.text: ‘Raavan - Enemy of Aryavarta’ is written by which of the following writers?
questions.explanation: 'Raavan: Enemy of Aryavarta' (2019) is the third book of Amish Tripathi's Ram Chandra series.

questions.text: Who showed that heating silver cyanide (an inorganic compound) with ammonium chloride (another inorganic compound) produced urea without the aid of any living organism or part of a living organism, in 1828?
questions.explanation: In 1828 Friedrich Wöhler made urea, an organic compound, from inorganic substances (the silver salt he used was silver cyanate), undermining the idea that organic compounds need a living 'vital force'.

questions.text: Which state in India as per the 2021 Census has the lowest population Density per km²?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Arunachal Pradesh, the state with the lowest population density at the 2011 Census, 17 persons per km². No census was taken in 2021 (it was postponed), so the question rests on the 2011 figures.

questions.text: ‘Jakhan Choto Chilam’ is the autobiography of __________.
questions.explanation: 'Jakhan Choto Chilam' ('When I Was Small') is Satyajit Ray's memoir of his childhood.

questions.text: Which Schedule of the Indian Constitution divides the power between the Centre and the state in terms of the union, state and concurrent list?
questions.explanation: The Seventh Schedule divides the subjects of legislation into the Union, State and Concurrent Lists (Article 246).

questions.text: The World Badminton Championship event 2026 will be organised by__________.
questions.explanation: India, with New Delhi as the host city, was chosen to stage the 2026 BWF World Championships.

questions.text: ____________ is a reputed classical dancer of Kathak dance form.
questions.explanation: Shovana Narayan is a leading Kathak dancer. Kanak Rele is known for Mohiniyattam and Madhavi Mudgal for Odissi.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. White elephant
questions.explanation: A 'white elephant' is a possession that costs a great deal to keep but is of little use.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. One thing that can be divided
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'divisible', able to be divided, the usual one-word substitute for 'that which can be divided' (as 'edible' is for 'that which can be eaten'). A 'dividend' is the number being divided in a particular sum, the quotient the result and the remainder what is left over.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Banter
questions.explanation: 'Banter' is playful, teasing talk: 'repartee', a quick and witty exchange.

questions.text: Parts of the given sentence have been underlined and given as options. One of them contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error. It is possible “to prevent oneself” “with respiratory diseases” “by maintaining” “a disciplined lifestyle.”
questions.explanation: 'Prevent' takes 'from', not 'with': 'to prevent oneself from respiratory diseases'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To put someone's back up
questions.explanation: To 'put someone's back up' is to annoy or irritate them.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Freadom' is misspelt: the correct spelling is 'freedom'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate spelling that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. He had to prepare for his “competation”
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'competition'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. The door was opened by the children for their father.
options: The children was opened the door for their father.
The children are opens the door for their father.
The children opened the door for their father.
The children opens the door for their father.
questions.explanation: The simple past passive 'was opened by the children' becomes the simple past active 'The children opened the door', with 'for their father' kept.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Though he is stout, he runs ____________.
questions.explanation: 'Fast' is itself the adverb ('fastly' is not a word), and with nothing compared the plain form fits, not 'faster' or 'fastest'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Austere
questions.explanation: 'Austere' means severe and strict in manner: 'stern'.

questions.text: Parts of the given sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. The Minister announced that the bridge would constructed within a week.
questions.explanation: The passive needs 'be': 'the bridge would be constructed within a week'.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. Two astronomers – Johannes Kepler from Germany and Galileo from Italy – supported the Copernican theory after nearly a century passed by. B. Copernicus’ view was that the sun was stationary and the earth and the planets moved in orbits around the sun. C. Nicholas Copernicus, a Polish priest, proposed a model in 1514. D. There are many popular theories about the solar system. Ancient People believed that the sun moved around the earth and the earth was static.
questions.explanation: D introduces the theories and the old belief, C brings in Copernicus's model of 1514, B gives his view, and A tells how Kepler and Galileo supported it a century later: DCBA.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. They “had eaten” an apple every day for breakfast.
questions.explanation: A daily habit takes the simple present: 'They eat an apple every day for breakfast.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Famous
questions.explanation: 'Famous' means widely known; its opposite is 'obscure', little known.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Other countries of comparable size and exposure to Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) have adopted a decentralised organizational structure, liberal policies, and a __________ dispute resolution mechanism, deployed state-of-the-art infrastructure and used the private- public partnership to market Domain Name Registration Services (DNS), resulting in phenomenal growth of their country code domain name.
questions.explanation: The sentence lists strengths that brought growth (decentralisation, liberal policies), so the mechanism is a 'comprehensive' one; 'short', 'narrow' and 'restricted' would be weaknesses.

questions.text: Select the sentence which has no spelling error.
options: Aries is the first sign of the zodiac.
Many cities are named after zodaic signs.
Water bearer is the symbol for zodiak Aquarius.
The zodyac signs are split in twelve months.
questions.explanation: Only the first sentence spells 'zodiac' correctly; the others have 'zodaic', 'zodiak' and 'zodyac'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Unselfish interest in the welfare of others
questions.explanation: Altruism is unselfish concern for the welfare of others; misanthropy is dislike of people, egoism self-interest and celibacy abstaining from marriage.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. I am going to ask all employees about the incident that took place in the canteen yesterday.
options: All the employees are gone to be asked about the incident that took place in the canteen yesterday.
All the employees are going to be asked about the incident that took place in the canteen yesterday.
All the employees are asked by me about the incident that took place in the canteen yesterday.
All the employees will go to be questioned by me about the incident that took place in the canteen yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'Am going to ask' becomes 'are going to be asked', with 'all employees' as the subject; the agent 'by me' can be dropped.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Salander sat for a while (1) _________ the telephone after Armansky hung up. She went to her work corner in the living room (2) ______ looked at the notes she had pinned up on the wall and the papers she had (3)_________ on the desk. What she had managed to collect was mostly press cuttings and articles (4)_________ from the Internet. She took the papers and dropped (5) ______ in a desk drawer.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: She sat for a while 'holding' the telephone: the participle says how she sat.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Salander sat for a while (1) _________ the telephone after Armansky hung up. She went to her work corner in the living room (2) ______ looked at the notes she had pinned up on the wall and the papers she had (3)_________ on the desk. What she had managed to collect was mostly press cuttings and articles (4)_________ from the Internet. She took the papers and dropped (5) ______ in a desk drawer.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Two actions in sequence: she went to her work corner 'and' looked at the notes.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Salander sat for a while (1) _________ the telephone after Armansky hung up. She went to her work corner in the living room (2) ______ looked at the notes she had pinned up on the wall and the papers she had (3)_________ on the desk. What she had managed to collect was mostly press cuttings and articles (4)_________ from the Internet. She took the papers and dropped (5) ______ in a desk drawer.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Papers kept in a pile on a desk are 'stacked'; 'tacked' means pinned in place, 'slacked' means loosened, and 'mounded', heaped into a mound, is not the usual word for papers.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Salander sat for a while (1) _________ the telephone after Armansky hung up. She went to her work corner in the living room (2) ______ looked at the notes she had pinned up on the wall and the papers she had (3)_________ on the desk. What she had managed to collect was mostly press cuttings and articles (4)_________ from the Internet. She took the papers and dropped (5) ______ in a desk drawer.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: Articles taken from the Internet are 'downloaded'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Salander sat for a while (1) _________ the telephone after Armansky hung up. She went to her work corner in the living room (2) ______ looked at the notes she had pinned up on the wall and the papers she had (3)_________ on the desk. What she had managed to collect was mostly press cuttings and articles (4)_________ from the Internet. She took the papers and dropped (5) ______ in a desk drawer.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: The pronoun stands for 'the papers', a plural object: 'dropped them'.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'CONCEPT' is written as ‘3o14c5p20’ and ‘PROBLEM’ is written as ‘16r15b12e13’. How will 'SOLVE' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Letters in odd places are written as their positions in the alphabet and those in even places as small letters: C = 3, o, N = 14, c, E = 5, p, T = 20. So SOLVE → 19, o, 12, v, 5: 19o12v5.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in an English dictionary. 1.Necessary 2.Networks 3.Negotiate 4.Needlework 5.Neigh
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Necessary (1), Needlework (4), Negotiate (3), Neigh (5), Networks (2). 'Nec' comes before 'Nee', 'Neg', 'Nei' and 'Net'.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 7, 7, 9, 27, 31, 155,?
questions.explanation: The steps alternate: ×1, +2, ×3, +4, ×5, so the next is +6: 155 + 6 = 161.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 9 : 135 :: 6 : 54 : :7 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is the first times (twice the first minus 3): 9 × 15 = 135 and 6 × 9 = 54. Likewise 7 × 11 = 77.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that, when sequentially placed from left to right in the blanks below, will complete the letter series. H _H_ _ S r _ a H _ _ S r H _ _ S a S r
options: a S a H S a a H
a S a S S a a H
S S a H S a a H
a S a a a a a H
questions.explanation: With a, S, a, H, S, a, a, H in the blanks the block HaHSaSr repeats: HaHSaSr HaHSaSr HaHSaSr.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. PEARL : LRAEP :: ULTRA : ARTLU :: VIRAL : ?
questions.explanation: Each word is written in reverse: PEARL → LRAEP and ULTRA → ARTLU. So VIRAL → LARIV.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and fourth term related to third term. 12:208 :: 9:108 ::15:?
questions.explanation: The second number is the square of the first plus the cube of one third of it: 12² + 4³ = 144 + 64 = 208 and 9² + 3³ = 81 + 27 = 108. Likewise 15² + 5³ = 225 + 125 = 350.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 207 : 30 : :108 : 19 : : 63 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is the first divided by 9, plus 7: 207 ÷ 9 + 7 = 30 and 108 ÷ 9 + 7 = 19. Likewise 63 ÷ 9 + 7 = 14.

questions.text: The second number in the given number pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number pairs, except one. Find that odd number pair.
questions.explanation: Each pair is a square and the cube of the same root: 25 and 125 (5), 49 and 343 (7), 36 and 216 (6). 81 = 9², but 9³ = 729, not 730.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'CURD' is written as '342184' and 'BREAD' is written as '2181024'. How will 'BUTTER' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Consonants are written as their positions in the alphabet and vowels as twice theirs: C = 3, U = 42, R = 18, D = 4; B = 2, R = 18, E = 10, A = 2, D = 4. So BUTTER → 2, 42, 20, 20, 10, 18: 24220201018.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fourth term in the same way as the first term is related to the second term and the fifth term is related to the sixth term 16 : 36 :: ? : 50 :: 9 : 22
questions.explanation: The second term is twice the first plus 4: 16 × 2 + 4 = 36 and 9 × 2 + 4 = 22. So ? × 2 + 4 = 50 gives 23.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the sixth number is related to the fifth number. 21 : 54 :: 24 : ? :: 29 : 78
questions.explanation: The second number is three times the first minus 9: 21 × 3 − 9 = 54 and 29 × 3 − 9 = 78. Likewise 24 × 3 − 9 = 63.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in an English dictionary. 1. Facsimile 2. Frightful 3. Favourable 4. Fructification 5. Fanatical
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Facsimile (1), Fanatical (5), Favourable (3), Frightful (2), Fructification (4). 'Fac', 'Fan' and 'Fav' come in that order, and 'Fri' before 'Fru'.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 50 * 24 * 2 * 5 * 3

Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (37, 28, 333) (41, 39, 82) (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed)
questions.explanation: The third number is the first times the difference of the first two: 37 × (37 − 28) = 37 × 9 = 333 and 41 × (41 − 39) = 82. Likewise 18 × (18 − 13) = 18 × 5 = 90.

questions.text: The second number in the given number pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number pairs, EXCEPT one. Find that odd number pair.
questions.explanation: In the other pairs the second number is three times the first: 50 × 3 = 150, 40 × 3 = 120 and 20 × 3 = 60. 30 × 3 = 90, not 80.

questions.text: In a certain code language, “QUOTE” is written as “RWRXJ”, and “UNION” is written as “VPLSS”. How will “YOUNG” be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +1, +2, +3, +4, +5: QUOTE → RWRXJ and UNION → VPLSS. So YOUNG → ZQXRL.

questions.text: Which letter cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? UQMI, VOPE, WMSA, ?, YIYS
questions.explanation: First letters move +1 (U, V, W, X, Y), second letters −2 (Q, O, M, K, I), third letters +3 (M, P, S, V, Y) and fourth letters −4 (I, E, A, W, S): XKVW.

questions.text: In a circular race of 2500 m, a man and a woman start from a point towards opposite directions with speeds of 37 km/h and 35 km/h, respectively. After how much time from the start of the race will they meet for the first time?
questions.explanation: Running in opposite directions they close the gap at 37 + 35 = 72 km/h = 20 m/s, so they first meet after 2500/20 = 125 seconds: 2 min 5 sec.

questions.text: What will be the area of a triangle whose sides are 13 cm, 5 cm and 12 cm?
questions.explanation: 5² + 12² = 13², so the triangle is right-angled with legs 5 cm and 12 cm: area = ½ × 5 × 12 = 30 cm².

questions.text: Find the fourth proportional to 7, 13 and 21.
3 sinA − 4 sin³A = ?
questions.explanation: The triple-angle formula: sin 3A = 3 sin A − 4 sin³A.

questions.text: Find the ratio in which a grocer should mix two varieties of pulses costing ₹75 and ₹90 per kg, respectively, so as to get a mixture costing ₹80 per kg.

The expenses of a family on wheat, vegetables and oil are in the ratio 12 : 8 : 5. The prices of these items increased by 50%, 25% and 40%, respectively. The total expenses of the family on these items increased by:
questions.explanation: Taking the expenses as 12, 8 and 5 (total 25), after the rises they are 18, 10 and 7, a total of 35. The rise is 10/25 = 40%.

questions.text: A shopkeeper gives a 35% discount on the marked price of a bottle. If the selling price of the bottle is ₹ 1,755, then the marked price of the bottle will be:
questions.explanation: After a 35% discount 65% of the marked price is paid: 1,755/0.65 = ₹2,700.

questions.text: The average age of a group is increased by 6 years when a person whose age is 24 years was replaced by a person whose age is 66. Find the number of persons in the group.
questions.explanation: The total rises by 66 − 24 = 42 years, which is 6 years for each person: 42/6 = 7 persons.

questions.text: A sells an article to B at 10% profit. B sells it to C at 25% profit. If C pays ₹6,875 for it, then the price at which A bought it is:
What will be the present value of ₹90,774 due 2 years hence, when the interest is compounded at 23% per annum?
The value of a residential flat constructed at a cost of ₹10,00,000 is depreciating at a rate of 10% per annum. What will be its value 3 years after the construction

Sonam is a cab driver, who plies within a city. The number of kilometres that she drives on a Tuesday was 12.5% less than the number of kilometres that she drives on the day before.On the other hand, the number of kilometres that she drives on Wednesday was 20% more than the number of kilometres that she drives on Tuesday. If Sonam drives a total of 336 km on Wednesday, how many kilometres did she drive on Monday?
questions.explanation: Tuesday = 0.875 × Monday and Wednesday = 1.2 × Tuesday = 1.05 × Monday. Monday = 336/1.05 = 320 km.

questions.text: The largest six-digit number exactly divisible by 81 is:
questions.explanation: 999999 = 81 × 12345 + 54, so the largest six-digit multiple of 81 is 999999 − 54 = 999945.

questions.text: A is 3 times as fast as B and is, therefore, able to complete a work in 32 days lesser than B. A and B, working together, can complete the work in _________.
questions.explanation: If A takes t days, B takes 3t, and 3t − t = 32 gives t = 16: A 16 days, B 48. Together they do 1/16 + 1/48 = 4/48 = 1/12 of the work a day: 12 days.

questions.text: Simplify the expression ((82×82) − (18×18))⁰·⁵
Who among the following wrote two books on the history and dance structure of Mohiniyattam?
questions.explanation: Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma, who did much to revive and systematise Mohiniyattam, wrote two books on it in Malayalam, among them 'Mohiniyattam: Charitravum Attaprakaravum' (its history and dance structure).

questions.text: In which year will India host the ICC Champions Trophy?
questions.explanation: Under the ICC's hosting plan for 2024-2031, announced in November 2021, India hosts the 2029 Champions Trophy; Pakistan was given the 2025 edition.

questions.text: Malka Jaan of Agra Gharana was the court musician at the durbar of which of the following Nawabs of Calcutta?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Wajid Ali Shah, the last Nawab of Awadh, who after he was deposed in 1856 lived in exile at Matiaburj in Calcutta and kept a court of musicians there; Malka Jaan of Agra is said to have joined it. The other three were earlier Nawabs of Awadh, at Faizabad or Lucknow.

questions.text: Who among the following Indian singers has written ‘Raag Sarita’?
questions.explanation: Pandit C. R. (Chintaman Raghunath) Vyas, the Hindustani vocalist, published 'Raag Sarita', a collection of his own bandishes with their notation.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The first train inaugurated in 1853 was between which two stations?
questions.explanation: India's first passenger train ran from Bombay (Bori Bunder) to Thane on 16 April 1853.

questions.text: Ustad Bade Ghulam Ali Khan was renowned a____________.
questions.explanation: Ustad Bade Ghulam Ali Khan of the Patiala gharana was one of the great Hindustani classical vocalists, famed for his khayal and thumri.

questions.text: The title of the autobiography of actor Dilip Kumar is _________.
options: The Substance And The Shadow: An Autobiography
questions.explanation: Dilip Kumar's autobiography, 'The Substance and the Shadow', was published in 2014. 'Romancing with Life' is Dev Anand's.

questions.text: Who won the Saraswati Samman for the year 2020?
questions.explanation: Sharankumar Limbale received the Saraswati Samman for 2020 for his Marathi novel 'Sanatan'.

questions.text: Indian men's hockey team won its first Olympic gold medal in which year?
questions.explanation: India won its first Olympic hockey gold at Amsterdam in 1928.

questions.text: What is the domestic income if national income is ₹10,000 crore and net factor income from abroad is ₹2,000 crore?
questions.explanation: Domestic income = national income − net factor income from abroad = ₹10,000 crore − ₹2,000 crore = ₹8,000 crore.

questions.text: The bodies of the animals of phylum Platyhelminthes show _________ grade organisation.
questions.explanation: Flatworms show the tissue-organ grade: their tissues are built into organs. Protozoans show the protoplasmic grade, sponges the cellular grade and cnidarians the cell-tissue grade.

questions.text: Who was famous for inventing the power battery, one of the first devices to provide a reliable source of electricity, in 1800?
questions.explanation: Alessandro Volta built the voltaic pile in 1800, the first battery to give a steady electric current.

questions.text: Whose autobiography is titled ‘Ace against Odds’?
questions.explanation: 'Ace Against Odds', published in 2016, is the autobiography of tennis player Sania Mirza.

questions.text: Which group was given the name ‘paraffin’ earlier?
questions.explanation: Alkanes were once called paraffins, from the Latin 'parum affinis', little affinity, because they react so little.

questions.text: Who among the following was the third Vice-President of India?
questions.explanation: The Vice-Presidents in order: S. Radhakrishnan, Zakir Husain, V. V. Giri (1967-69), G. S. Pathak and B. D. Jatti.

questions.text: Uma Sharma was conferred the Padma Bhushan award for enriching which of the following forms of Classical Dances in India?
questions.explanation: Uma Sharma, the Kathak dancer, received the Padma Bhushan in 2001.

questions.text: Mrinalini Sarabhai was awarded the ___________ in 1992.
questions.explanation: Mrinalini Sarabhai, the classical dancer and founder of the Darpana Academy, received the Padma Bhushan in 1992, after the Padma Shri in 1965.

questions.text: Vilayat Khan is associated with which musical instrument?
questions.explanation: Ustad Vilayat Khan was one of the great sitar players of the twentieth century.

questions.text: Who among the following invented and perfected India’s classical dance form Sattras?
questions.explanation: Sattriya was created by the Vaishnava saint Srimanta Sankardev in Assam in the 15th-16th century and kept alive in the sattras, the Vaishnava monasteries.

questions.text: Which sea is the north-western part of the Indian Ocean that covers a total area of approximately 14,91,000 square miles and forms a part of the major sea route between Europe and India?
questions.explanation: The Arabian Sea, the north-western part of the Indian Ocean, covers about 38,62,000 km² (14,91,000 square miles) and is part of the main sea route between Europe and India.

questions.text: Who among the following Indians was selected as a member of International Law Commission for a 5 year term starting January 1, 2023 in the month of November 2021?
questions.explanation: In November 2021 Bimal Patel was elected to the UN's International Law Commission for the five-year term beginning on 1 January 2023.

questions.text: Find the odd one out with respect to animals’ response to abiotic factors.
questions.explanation: Animals respond to abiotic conditions by regulating, conforming, migrating or suspending activity (hibernation, aestivation, diapause). Reproducing is not one of these responses.

questions.text: Which is the major microtubule-organising centre (MTOC) in eukaryotic cells involved in various cellular processes, including sensory reception, locomotion, and embryogenesis?
questions.explanation: The centrosome, with its pair of centrioles, is the main microtubule-organising centre of animal cells; centrioles also give rise to the basal bodies of cilia and flagella.

questions.text: The ‘Nijaat’ (riddance) anti-drug campaign launched by a district police of which state has been acknowledged and appreciated by many Bollywood actors in 2021?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Chhattisgarh, whose police ran 'Nijaat', a campaign against drugs and illicit liquor started by Superintendent of Police Santosh Singh in Koriya and Rajnandgaon districts.

questions.text: Who is the only Indian female sportsperson to win two consecutive Olympic medals?
questions.explanation: P. V. Sindhu won badminton silver at Rio 2016 and bronze at Tokyo 2020, the first Indian woman to win medals at two Olympics in a row.

questions.text: Parts of the given sentence have been given as options. One of them contains a grammatical error. Select the option that has the error. When you have worked out this sum, you may went out to play.
questions.explanation: The modal 'may' takes the base form of the verb: 'you may go out to play'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Going to the weekly market / in every Tuesday / is a ritual that has been followed / by generations in my family.
options: is a ritual that has been followed
questions.explanation: Days take 'on', not 'in', and 'every Tuesday' can stand without a preposition: 'Going to the weekly market every Tuesday is a ritual ...'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Despair
questions.explanation: 'Despair' is the complete loss of hope; its opposite is 'hope'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'attendance'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Wax
questions.explanation: To 'wax' is to grow, as the moon does before it is full; its opposite is to 'wane', to shrink.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underline segment in the given sentence. It was apparent that the girl was “heading into” a serious disaster.
questions.explanation: To be 'heading for' something, usually trouble, is to be on course for it: 'heading for a serious disaster' is the set phrase.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. He requested the bank to give him more time as at present he was “unable to pay his debts.”
questions.explanation: A person unable to pay his debts is 'bankrupt'. 'Destitute' means without the basic necessities of life, 'meticulous' very careful and 'reckless' heedless of danger.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Dark horse
questions.explanation: A 'dark horse' is a little-known competitor who unexpectedly wins or does well.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. The people will make him the leader.
options: He had been made the leader by people.
He will be made the leader by the people.
He was made leader by the people.
questions.explanation: The future active 'will make' becomes 'will be made', with 'him' as the subject 'he' and the agent kept: 'He will be made the leader by the people.'

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. I know him.
options: Let him be known to me.
questions.explanation: In the passive 'know' takes 'to', not 'by'. The object 'him' becomes the subject 'he', and 'I' becomes 'me': 'He is known to me.'

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. Mahatma Gandhi in undoubtedly one of the “much” popular authors of our times.
questions.explanation: 'One of the' is followed by a superlative: 'one of the most popular authors'. (The 'in' before 'undoubtedly' is the paper's misprint for 'is'.)

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. Sheela “is trying” for a job since last year.
questions.explanation: An action that began in the past ('since last year') and is still going on takes the present perfect continuous; with the singular subject 'Sheela', 'has been trying'.

questions.text: In the following passage, a word has been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Gifting is generally taken to be the easiest act to ________, if only you have the heart to part with something in your ________.
questions.explanation: An act is 'performed', and what one parts with is something in one's 'possession'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. He is a ______ in shining armour.
questions.explanation: A 'knight in shining armour' is a chivalrous rescuer; 'night' and 'nite' only sound the same, and to 'knit' is to make fabric from yarn.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. However, after studying the myths scientifically, only a simpleton would find them irrational or worthless. B. Moreover, it is wrong to analyse myths on the yardstick of their factual accuracy as they were designed to serve a greater, deeper purpose. C. Myths have always been regarded as a complex and intriguing aspect in human life D. In modern scientific world, they are essentially seen as something unscientific and meaningless.
questions.explanation: C introduces myths, D says the modern scientific world sees them as meaningless, A ('However') counters that view and B ('Moreover') adds a further point: CDAB.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Be like chalk and cheese
questions.explanation: Two people or things 'like chalk and cheese' are completely different from each other.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word ‘Lead’ from the given sentence. All the class monitors were asked to follow the guide who was there to manage and control their visit to Yamuna Biodiversity Park.
questions.explanation: To 'lead' is to go ahead and guide others; its opposite in the sentence is 'follow'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. I “had get back from” Hyderabad last month.
questions.explanation: A completed action at a stated past time ('last month') takes the simple past: 'I got back from Hyderabad last month.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Salubrious
questions.explanation: 'Salubrious' means health-giving or wholesome: 'beneficial'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. While I was sitting there (1)_________ over my failure to keep from having to spend (2) glistering _________ summer months on the freaking Cote of Azur, Grandmere started (3)_________ me from the phone. She kept (4)_________ her fingers on the phone to catch my attention. I just sat there blinking at her until finally she put her hand over the receiver and (5)_________ (so that nobody listens), “Amelia! In my bedroom, there is something for you”.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: She was 'sulking', silently resentful, over her failure; smirking, grinning and clapping would all show pleasure.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. While I was sitting there (1)_________ over my failure to keep from having to spend (2) glistering _________ summer months on the freaking Cote of Azur, Grandmere started (3)_________ me from the phone. She kept (4)_________ her fingers on the phone to catch my attention. I just sat there blinking at her until finally she put her hand over the receiver and (5)_________ (so that nobody listens), “Amelia! In my bedroom, there is something for you”.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The possessive 'my' goes before the noun phrase: 'to spend my glistering summer months' (the sheet prints the blank after 'glistering'). 'Mine' stands alone, and 'me' is an object pronoun.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. While I was sitting there (1)_________ over my failure to keep from having to spend (2) glistering _________ summer months on the freaking Cote of Azur, Grandmere started (3)_________ me from the phone. She kept (4)_________ her fingers on the phone to catch my attention. I just sat there blinking at her until finally she put her hand over the receiver and (5)_________ (so that nobody listens), “Amelia! In my bedroom, there is something for you”.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Grandmere started 'beckoning' the narrator from the phone, signalling to her to come over.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. While I was sitting there (1)_________ over my failure to keep from having to spend (2) glistering _________ summer months on the freaking Cote of Azur, Grandmere started (3)_________ me from the phone. She kept (4)_________ her fingers on the phone to catch my attention. I just sat there blinking at her until finally she put her hand over the receiver and (5)_________ (so that nobody listens), “Amelia! In my bedroom, there is something for you”.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: She kept 'tapping' her fingers on the phone to catch the narrator's attention.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. While I was sitting there (1)_________ over my failure to keep from having to spend (2) glistering _________ summer months on the freaking Cote of Azur, Grandmere started (3)_________ me from the phone. She kept (4)_________ her fingers on the phone to catch my attention. I just sat there blinking at her until finally she put her hand over the receiver and (5)_________ (so that nobody listens), “Amelia! In my bedroom, there is something for you”.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: To 'hiss' is to speak in a sharp, low whisper, as she does with her hand over the receiver.

questions.text: Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it. First row- 5, 39, 8; Second row- 7, 36, 5; Third row- 11, ?, 9 (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed)
questions.explanation: In each row the middle number is three times the sum of the other two: (5 + 8) × 3 = 39 and (7 + 5) × 3 = 36. So (11 + 9) × 3 = 60.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 6:96 :: 8:144 :: 5:?
questions.explanation: The second number is the first times (the first + 10): 6 × 16 = 96 and 8 × 18 = 144. Likewise 5 × 15 = 75.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in an English dictionary. 1.Catalyst 2.Carrot 3. Calcium 4. Calculate 5.Calendar
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Calcium (3), Calculate (4), Calendar (5), Carrot (2), Catalyst (1). 'Calci' comes before 'Calcu', 'Calc' before 'Cale', and 'Cal', 'Car' and 'Cat' in that order.

questions.text: Three Statements are given followed by Three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All moons are suns. No moon is a star. Some stars are planets. Conclusions: I. Some suns are planets. II. No sun is a star. III. No planet is a moon.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Both conclusions I and III follow.
