questions.text: If 26 January 2019 was Saturday, then what was the day of the week on 30 January 2022?
questions.explanation: From 26 January 2019 to 26 January 2022 is 3 years with one leap day (29 February 2020): 4 odd days, so 26 January 2022 was a Wednesday. Four days later, 30 January, was a Sunday.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. ACCURATE : RATEACCU :: ANALYSIS : YSISANAL :: CAPACITY : ?
questions.explanation: The last four letters move to the front: ACCU RATE → RATEACCU and ANAL YSIS → YSISANAL. So CAPA CITY → CITYCAPA.

questions.text: In a certain code language, “ABROAD” is written as “BDUNYA”, and “BECAME” is written as “CGFZKB”. How will “CANCER” be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +1, +2, +3, −1, −2, −3: ABROAD → BDUNYA and BECAME → CGFZKB. So CANCER → DCQBCO.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 13, 26, 23, ?, 87, 522
Select the option that represents the letters that, when sequentially placed from left to right in the blanks below, will complete the letter series. t _ r a s _ t _ s _ a _ _ _ t _ r _ s r t
options: s r t r a r t s a
s r a r s r t s a
s r t r s r t s t
s r t r s r t s a
questions.explanation: With s, r, t, r, s, r, t, s, a in the blanks the block tsrasrt repeats: tsrasrt tsrasrt tsrasrt.

questions.text: If P denotes ‘×’, Q denotes ‘÷’, R denotes ‘+’ and S denotes ‘−’, then what will come in place of ‘?’ in the following equation? 130 S 61 R (23 P 4) S 83 R (62 Q 2) = ?

Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it. First row: 187, 164, 141 Second row: 215, 192, 169 Third row: 178, 155, ? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the number into its constituent digits. For example, 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In each row every number is 23 less than the one before: 187, 164, 141 and 215, 192, 169. So 155 − 23 = 132.

questions.text: The second number in the given number pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number pairs, except one. Find that odd number pair.
questions.explanation: The second number is the square of two less than the first's square root: 36 → (6 − 2)² = 16, 49 → 5² = 25 and 81 → 7² = 49. But 100 → 8² = 64, not 81.

questions.text: Which two numbers, from amongst the given options, should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? (40×6) ÷8 + 14 – (7×16) + (13×12) =26
Which number will replace the question mark (?) in the following series? 6, 12, 20, 30, ?, 56
In a certain code language, 'CHECK' is written as '6165622' and 'SURGE' is written as '382136145'. How will 'PRIEST' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each consonant is written as twice its place in the alphabet and each vowel as its place: CHECK → 6 16 5 6 22 and SURGE → 38 21 36 14 5. So PRIEST → 32 36 9 5 38 40.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 19, 37, 74, 147, 294, ?
By selling a fridge for ₹18,200, Anu loses 15%. Find the cost price of the fridge. (Consider integral part only)
questions.explanation: ₹18,200 is 85% of the cost price: 18,200/0.85 = ₹21,411.76, whose integral part is ₹21,411.

questions.text: The marked price of a mobile phone is ₹18,000. It is sold with two successive discounts of 25% and 4%. An additional discount of 5% is offered for cash payment. The selling price of the mobile on cash payment is:
In still water, the speed of a motorboat is 15 km/h. The boat travels 30 km downstream and returns in 4 hours and 30 minutes. The stream's speed (in km/h) is:
A cot was marked for ₹15,000 but sold for ₹13,500. What was the discount percentage offered on it?
questions.explanation: The discount is ₹1,500 on a marked price of ₹15,000: 1,500/15,000 = 10%.

questions.text: Two years ago, the population of a village was 1,000. The population increased by 10% is the first year and decreased by 10% in the second year. Find the present population.

As part of Diwali offer, a jeweller allows a discount of 15%. Even after giving the discount, he makes a profit of 6.25%. Rani bought a gold chain which was marked at ₹5,000 from this jeweller. Find the cost price of the chain for the jeweller.
The average weight of 18 boys in a class is 45 kg and that of the remaining 8 boys is 48.75 kg. Find the average weight (in kg) of all the boys in the class.(Correct to two decimal places)
If 5 persons can prepare 5 tables in 5 days, then how long will it take 25 persons to prepare 25 tables?
questions.explanation: Each person makes one table in 5 days, so 25 persons make 25 tables in the same 5 days.

questions.text: The average weight of a family of 4 members is 45 kg. The grandfather and the grandmother come to visit the family. Now the average weight of the 6 members of the family is 48 kg. Find the average weight of the grandparents (in kg).
questions.explanation: The grandparents weigh 6 × 48 − 4 × 45 = 288 − 180 = 108 kg together: an average of 54 kg.

questions.text: A chord of 10 cm passes through the centre of a circle. What is the diameter of the circle?
questions.explanation: A chord through the centre is a diameter, so the diameter is 10 cm.

questions.text: The diameter of a solid hemisphere is 10 cm. Find its total surface area (use π=3.14).
questions.explanation: A solid hemisphere's total surface area is 3πr² = 3 × 3.14 × 5² = 235.5 cm².

questions.text: A cone-shaped temple top has slant height of 10 m and radius of base is 11 m. Find the total cost for painting its curved surface area at the rate of ₹7/m². [Use π=22/7]
questions.explanation: Curved surface area = πrl = (22/7) × 11 × 10 = 2,420/7 m²; at ₹7/m² the cost is ₹2,420.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Surendranath Banerjee’s autobiography is called ____________.
questions.explanation: Surendranath Banerjee's autobiography, published in 1925, is 'A Nation in Making'. 'Hind Swaraj' is Gandhi's book and 'Young India' the weekly he edited; 'Hints for Self Culture' is Lala Har Dayal's.

questions.text: Who termed Article 32 as the ‘heart and soul of the Constitution of India’?
questions.explanation: B. R. Ambedkar called Article 32, the right to constitutional remedies, the very heart and soul of the Constitution.

questions.text: Which phylum of the Kingdom Animalia includes animals such as Hydra, Adamsia, Physalia and Corals?
questions.explanation: Hydra, Adamsia (a sea anemone), Physalia (the Portuguese man-of-war) and corals are coelenterates (cnidarians): radially symmetrical animals with stinging cells.

questions.text: Payment of loan by the government is an example of _____________.
questions.explanation: Repaying a loan reduces the government's liabilities, so it is capital expenditure; the interest paid on a loan is revenue expenditure.

questions.text: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
options: Miyan Tansen – One of the nine jewels
questions.explanation: Ustad Bismillah Khan was the master of the shehnai, not the sitar. Chaurasia plays the bamboo flute, Tansen was one of Akbar's nine jewels and Ali Akbar Khan played the sarod.

questions.text: At the December 2021 BWF World Tour Finals in Bali, Indonesia, shuttler ______________ clinched the silver medal.
questions.explanation: P. V. Sindhu lost the final of the 2021 BWF World Tour Finals to South Korea's An Se-young and took the silver medal.

questions.text: Pandit Sunder Prasad who was awarded with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1959 was a ______ dancer.
questions.explanation: Pandit Sunder Prasad was a Kathak dancer and guru of the Jaipur gharana.

questions.text: Which of the following states present Kalidas Samman annually?
questions.explanation: The Kalidas Samman is presented by the Government of Madhya Pradesh.

questions.text: Totaram Sharma is an exponent of ____________.
questions.explanation: Pandit Totaram Sharma is known as a master of the pakhawaj, the barrel-shaped drum that accompanies dhrupad.

questions.text: The 10th Women's Hockey Asia Cup was held at __________.
questions.explanation: The 10th Women's Hockey Asia Cup was held in Muscat, Oman, in January 2022.

questions.text: In April 2021, Nethra Kumanan became the first Indian woman ever to qualify for the Olympics in ________________.
questions.explanation: Nethra Kumanan qualified in the Laser Radial class at the Mussanah Open in Oman in April 2021, the first Indian woman sailor to reach the Olympics.

questions.text: Who among the following won the first National Film Award for Best Choreography in 1992?
questions.explanation: Laxmibai Kolhapurkar won the first National Film Award for Best Choreography, at the 40th National Film Awards (for 1992), for the Marathi film 'Ek Hota Vidushak'.

questions.text: BS Yediyurappa resigned as the Chief Minister of Karnataka for the _________________ time in July 2021.
questions.explanation: B. S. Yediyurappa became Chief Minister four times (2007, 2008, 2018 and 2019), and his resignation on 26 July 2021 ended the fourth term.

questions.text: From which of the following years was the National Kalidas Samman started in India?
questions.explanation: The Government of Madhya Pradesh instituted the Kalidas Samman in 1980.

questions.text: The famous novel ‘Ananda Math’ was originally written in _________ language.
questions.explanation: Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay wrote 'Anandamath' (1882) in Bengali; 'Vande Mataram' appears in it.

questions.text: Who among the following was the first Indian musician conferred with the Ramon Magsaysay Award and also the first Indian to have performed in United Nations General Assembly in 1966?
questions.explanation: M. S. Subbulakshmi sang at the UN General Assembly in 1966 and in 1974 became the first Indian musician to receive the Ramon Magsaysay Award.

questions.text: Which enzyme is responsible for the oxidation reaction that occurs in some foods, mostly fruits and vegetables, that turns the food brown?
questions.explanation: Polyphenol oxidase oxidises phenolic compounds in cut fruit and vegetables, turning them brown. Bromelain and papain break down proteins.

questions.text: Which is the fourth largest water body in the world recognised by the US Board on Geographic Names as a body of water extending off the coast of Antarctica?
questions.explanation: The US Board on Geographic Names recognised the Southern Ocean, around Antarctica, in 1999; it is the fourth largest of the five oceans.

questions.text: Who among the following is the author of the book ‘The Inheritance of Loss’?
questions.explanation: Kiran Desai's 'The Inheritance of Loss' won the Booker Prize in 2006.

questions.text: Which water body is adjacent to the Atlantic Ocean, located in the southeast of the Gulf of Mexico?
questions.explanation: The Caribbean Sea, an arm of the Atlantic bounded by Central America and the West Indies, lies south-east of the Gulf of Mexico.

questions.text: Who among the following was given the title of Mallika-e-Ghazal?
questions.explanation: Begum Akhtar, the great ghazal singer, is remembered as 'Mallika-e-Ghazal', the queen of ghazals.

questions.text: Which of the following minerals’ primary constituent is iron oxide containing equal amounts of iron (II) and iron (III) that is mainly used for steel manufacturing?
questions.explanation: Magnetite, Fe₃O₄ (FeO·Fe₂O₃), is an iron oxide holding iron(II) and iron(III) in the ratio 1:2, and a rich ore of iron for steelmaking. Mica, limestone and bauxite are not iron ores.

questions.text: Identify the component found only in a eukaryotic cell.
questions.explanation: Only eukaryotic cells have a nucleus bounded by a nuclear membrane. Ribosomes, a plasma membrane and cytoplasm are found in prokaryotic cells too.

questions.text: Which of the following pairs are NOT correctly matched? I.13th ICC One Day Cricket World Cup - India II.12th ICC Women’s one day Cricket World Cup - New Zealand III.8th T20 Women’s Cricket World Cup - South Africa IV.8th T20 Men's Cricket World Cup – India
questions.explanation: The 8th ICC Men's T20 World Cup (2022) was held in Australia, not India. India hosted the 13th Men's ODI World Cup (2023), New Zealand the 12th Women's ODI World Cup (2022) and South Africa the 8th Women's T20 World Cup (2023).

questions.text: When is the approximate arrival of the Arabian Sea branch of monsoon in Mumbai?
questions.explanation: By NCERT's account the Arabian Sea branch of the monsoon reaches Mumbai about ten days after Kerala, around 10 June.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Break a leg
questions.explanation: 'Break a leg' is said to wish someone, especially a performer, good luck.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Miss the boat
questions.explanation: To 'miss the boat' is to lose an opportunity by acting too slowly.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word Comely
questions.explanation: 'Comely' means attractive; its opposite is 'grotesque', ugly or distorted. 'Gorgeous' is close to a synonym.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Arraign
questions.explanation: To 'arraign' someone is to call them before a court to answer a charge: to 'prosecute' them. To 'persecute' is to harass or oppress.

questions.text: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Many times ________ starts with the creative _________ and the enduring passion of a single individual.
questions.explanation: 'Innovation' is what starts with a creative 'spark'; lethargy, dullness and stagnation contradict the creative passion the sentence describes.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. Alfred’s doctor treated Rohan for his fever.
options: Rohan will be treated by Alfred’s doctor for his fever.
Rohan has been treated by Alfred’s doctor for his fever.
Rohan was treats by Alfred’s doctor for his fever.
Rohan was treated by Alfred’s doctor for his fever.
questions.explanation: The simple past 'treated' becomes 'was treated', with the object as subject: 'Rohan was treated by Alfred's doctor for his fever.'

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. In 1895, a man named Birsa was seen roaming the forests and villages of Chottanagpur in Jharkhand. B. Soon thousands began following Birsa, believing that he was God and had come to solve all their problems. C. Birsa himself declared that God had appointed him to save his people from trouble, free them from the slavery of ‘dikus’. D. People said he had miraculous powers – he could cure all diseases and multiply grain.
questions.explanation: A introduces Birsa in 1895, D says what people believed of him, C what he himself declared, and B the result, thousands following him: ADCB.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. The flyer for the international symposium is being sent by students to institutes all over the country.
options: Students are being sent the flyer for the international symposium to institutes all over the country.
The flyer for the international symposium is sent by students to institutes all over the country.
Students are sending the flyer for the international symposium to institutes all over the country.
The flyer is sending the students to institutes all over the country for the international symposium.
questions.explanation: The present continuous passive 'is being sent by students' becomes the present continuous active, with the students as subject: 'Students are sending the flyer …'

questions.text: The following sentence contains a grammatical error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error. In its August 1992 issue, the highly respected British Journal of Addiction describe three unusual cases of carrot dependence.
options: In its August 1992 issue, the highly respected British Journal of Addiction was describing three unusual cases of carrot dependence.
In its August 1992 issue, the highly respected British Journal of Addiction describing three unusual cases of carrot dependence.
In its August 1992 issue, the highly respected British Journal of Addiction described three unusual cases of carrot dependence.
In its August 1992 issue, the highly respected British Journal of Addiction has been described three British Journal of Addiction has been described three
questions.explanation: The August 1992 issue is in the past, so the verb takes the simple past 'described'; 'describe' does not even agree with the singular 'Journal'. (The paper itself prints the 'has been described' option garbled.)

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. On cloud nine
questions.explanation: To be 'on cloud nine' is to be extremely happy.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Reinforce
questions.explanation: To 'reinforce' is to strengthen; its opposite is 'weaken'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'queer'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. To dispute angrily
questions.explanation: To 'wrangle' is to argue angrily and at length. To 'wrench' is to twist, to 'wreck' to destroy and to 'wrack' to torment.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the following sentence. there are some technologies available today that make a notebook “dispensable”.
questions.explanation: 'Dispensable' means not necessary; its opposite is 'essential'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. She was __________ right nor wrong.
questions.explanation: 'Neither' pairs with 'nor': 'She was neither right nor wrong.'

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. The children “opens the door” silently, yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'Yesterday' calls for the simple past: 'The children opened the door silently, yesterday.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Admire
questions.explanation: To 'admire' someone is to regard them with approval: to 'appreciate' them. To 'admonish' is to scold.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. Nisha participates in almost every activity and in all functions held in the school as she “has many skills.”
questions.explanation: A 'versatile' person has many different skills or abilities.

questions.text: Which word in the given sentence is the ANTONYM of – exonerate? It was difficult to convict him of the falsity of his beliefs.
questions.explanation: To 'exonerate' is to declare someone free of blame; to 'convict' is to declare them guilty.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Hall of Dharma was in a circular building, built of stone and mortar, with a (1)________ dome. The delicate (2)________of the dome was believed to represent the feminine while the typical temple spire represented the masculine. The hall was also (3)________ All rishis sat as (4)________ without a moderating ‘head’, debating issues openly and without fear, freedom of (5)________at its zenith.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: A large dome is a 'massive' one; 'passive', 'intrusive' and 'conclusive' cannot describe a dome.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Hall of Dharma was in a circular building, built of stone and mortar, with a (1)________ dome. The delicate (2)________of the dome was believed to represent the feminine while the typical temple spire represented the masculine. The hall was also (3)________ All rishis sat as (4)________ without a moderating ‘head’, debating issues openly and without fear, freedom of (5)________at its zenith.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The dome's delicate 'elegance', its graceful beauty, is what could stand for the feminine.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Hall of Dharma was in a circular building, built of stone and mortar, with a (1)________ dome. The delicate (2)________of the dome was believed to represent the feminine while the typical temple spire represented the masculine. The hall was also (3)________ All rishis sat as (4)________ without a moderating ‘head’, debating issues openly and without fear, freedom of (5)________at its zenith.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: The hall was 'circular', like the building; in a round hall no seat is at the head, which leads into the next sentence.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Hall of Dharma was in a circular building, built of stone and mortar, with a (1)________ dome. The delicate (2)________of the dome was believed to represent the feminine while the typical temple spire represented the masculine. The hall was also (3)________ All rishis sat as (4)________ without a moderating ‘head’, debating issues openly and without fear, freedom of (5)________at its zenith.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: The rishis sat as 'equals', with no moderating 'head' above them.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Hall of Dharma was in a circular building, built of stone and mortar, with a (1)________ dome. The delicate (2)________of the dome was believed to represent the feminine while the typical temple spire represented the masculine. The hall was also (3)________ All rishis sat as (4)________ without a moderating ‘head’, debating issues openly and without fear, freedom of (5)________at its zenith.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'Freedom of expression' is the set phrase for speaking openly and without fear.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? TVEQ, PBWA, ?, HNGU, DTYE
questions.explanation: First letters move back 4 (T, P, L, H, D), second letters forward 6 (V, B, H, N, T), third letters back 8 (E, W, O, G, Y) and fourth letters forward 10 (Q, A, K, U, E), wrapping round the alphabet. The missing cluster is LHOK.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. Tis : Sit :: Tip : Pit :: Ten : ?
questions.explanation: Each word is written backwards: Tis → Sit and Tip → Pit. So Ten → Net.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fourth term in the same way as the first term is related to the second term and the fifth term is related to the sixth term 9 : 126 :: ? : 238 :: 21 : 294
questions.explanation: The second number is 14 times the first: 9 × 14 = 126 and 21 × 14 = 294. So 238 ÷ 14 = 17.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in an English dictionary. 1.Absorption 2.Absolutely 3.Abduct 4.Abbreviation 5.Accurate
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Abbreviation (4), Abduct (3), Absolutely (2), Absorption (1), Accurate (5). 'Abb' comes before 'Abd', and 'Absol' before 'Absor'.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 229,233,239,241,251,?
questions.explanation: The terms are consecutive prime numbers: 229, 233, 239, 241, 251. The next prime is 257 (253 = 11 × 23 and 255 = 3 × 5 × 17).

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. SIMPLE : ISNKEL :: PUBLIC : UPYOCI :: MINUTE : ?
questions.explanation: The first two letters swap, the middle two are each replaced by the letter in the same place from the other end of the alphabet (M → N, P → K; B → Y, L → O), and the last two swap: SIMPLE → IS NK EL. So MINUTE → IM MF ET: IMMFET.

questions.text: Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it. First row- 6, 8, 34 Second row- 3, 2, 10 Third row- 11, 18, ? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed).
questions.explanation: In each row the first number plus 3.5 times the second gives the third: 6 + 8 × 3.5 = 34 and 3 + 2 × 3.5 = 10. So 11 + 18 × 3.5 = 11 + 63 = 74.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in an English dictionary. 1.Draft 2.Drake 3.Drain 4.Drape 5.Dragon
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Draft (1), Dragon (5), Drain (3), Drake (2), Drape (4), going by the fourth letters f, g, i, k, p.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 14*5*55*74*12*4*3
In a certain code language, “CASTLE” is written as “BYPUNH”, and “DEMAND” is written as “CCJBPG”. How will “EITHER” be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move −1, −2, −3, +1, +2, +3: CASTLE → BYPUNH and DEMAND → CCJBPG. So EITHER → D G Q I G U: DGQIGU.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given number series? 5, 6, ?, 45, 184, 925
questions.explanation: Each term is the one before times 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 plus the same number: 5 × 1 + 1 = 6, 6 × 2 + 2 = 14, 14 × 3 + 3 = 45, 45 × 4 + 4 = 184 and 184 × 5 + 5 = 925.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (360, 12, 60)
questions.explanation: The first number is half the product of the other two: 12 × 60 ÷ 2 = 360. Likewise 19 × 36 ÷ 2 = 342; none of the other sets fits.

questions.text: Two statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some apartments are bungalows. Some bungalows are flats. Conclusions: I. Some apartments are flats. II. Some flats are bungalows.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: 'Some bungalows are flats' can be reversed: some flats are bungalows (II). The apartments that are bungalows need not be among the bungalows that are flats, so I does not follow.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 6, 36, 41, ?, 167, 334
Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 16*4*8*10*2*52
Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 13, 17, 24, 36, 55, 85, 128, 188, ?
questions.explanation: The differences 4, 7, 12, 19, 30, 43, 60 grow by the prime numbers 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17. The next difference is 60 + 19 = 79: 188 + 79 = 267.

questions.text: Which letter cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? KGCJ, JEZF, ? , HATX, GYQT
questions.explanation: First letters move back 1 (K, J, I, H, G), second letters back 2 (G, E, C, A, Y), third letters back 3 (C, Z, W, T, Q) and fourth letters back 4 (J, F, B, X, T), wrapping round the alphabet. The missing cluster is ICWB.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'DIVIDE' is coded as ‘7 17 43 17 7 9’ and ‘SUBTRACT’ is coded as ’37 41 3 39 35 1 5 39’. How will 'ADDITION' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is coded as twice its place in the alphabet minus 1: D (4) → 7, I (9) → 17, V (22) → 43. So ADDITION → 1 7 7 17 39 17 29 27.

questions.text: The second number in the given number-pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number-pairs EXCEPT one. Find that odd number-pair.
questions.explanation: In 64 : 6, 169 : 11 and 196 : 12 the second number is the square root of the first minus 2 (8 − 2, 13 − 2, 14 − 2). √36 − 2 = 4, not 5, so 36 : 5 is the odd pair.

questions.text: ∆ABC is similar to ∆PQR. The area of ∆ABC is 64 cm², and the area of ∆PQR is 121 cm².If QR=15.4 cm, what is the length of BC?
questions.explanation: The areas of similar triangles are in the ratio of the squares of their sides, so BC : QR = √64 : √121 = 8 : 11. BC = 15.4 × 8/11 = 11.2 cm.

questions.text: The ratio of time taken by Anamika and Bani to complete a work is 1 : 3, respectively. Therefore, Anamika is able to finish a job in 40 days less than Bani. If they work together, they can complete the work in ______ days.
questions.explanation: Anamika takes 1 part and Bani 3, and the 2-part difference is 40 days, so Anamika takes 20 days and Bani 60. Together they do 1/20 + 1/60 = 4/60 = 1/15 of the work a day: 15 days.

questions.text: If a sum on compound interest (compounded yearly) becomes three times in 4 years, then with the same interest rate, the sum will become 81 times in:
questions.explanation: The sum triples every 4 years, and 81 = 3⁴, so it takes 4 × 4 = 16 years.

questions.text: There is a 20% discount on a dozen pairs of shoes marked at ₹7,200. How many pair of shoes can be bought with ₹1,440?
questions.explanation: One pair is marked at 7,200 ÷ 12 = ₹600 and costs 0.8 × 600 = ₹480 after the discount. 1,440 ÷ 480 = 3 pairs.

questions.text: In a right circular cylinder, the ratio of the curved surface to the total surface area is 3:7. Find the ratio of the height of the cylinder to the radius of its base.
questions.explanation: Curved surface : total surface = 2πrh : 2πr(h + r) = h : (h + r) = 3 : 7. So 7h = 3h + 3r, 4h = 3r and h : r = 3 : 4.

questions.text: The salaries of P and Q together amount to ₹1,20,000. P spends 95% of his salary and Q 85% of his. If their savings are the same, then what is P’s salary?
questions.explanation: Equal savings: 5% of P's salary = 15% of Q's, so P earns three times as much as Q. P + Q = 4Q = ₹1,20,000, so Q = ₹30,000 and P = ₹90,000.

questions.text: The monthly income of Manisha was ₹1,20,000 and her monthly expenditure was ₹55,000. Next year, her income increased by 22% and her expenditure increase by 10%. Find the percentage increase in her savings (correct to 2 decimal places).
When a certain number is multiplied by 11, the product is a six-digit number containing only 6s. Find the number that is multiplied by 11.
questions.explanation: The six-digit number of 6s is 666666, and 666666 ÷ 11 = 60606.

questions.text: Under a sale offer, Tanvir was offered a 32% discount on the part of the marked price that was paid in cash, but had to add 1.2% on the part of the marked price paid through a credit card. If Tanvir paid 75% of the marked price in cash and the rest through a credit card, what percentage of the marked price was his total final payment?
The average weight of 8 persons increased by 2.5 kg when a new person comes in place of one of them weighting 45 kg. What is the weight of the new person?
questions.explanation: The total weight rises by 8 × 2.5 = 20 kg, so the new person weighs 45 + 20 = 65 kg.

questions.text: The mean proportional between 6 and another number is 30. What is that number?
questions.explanation: The mean proportional of 6 and x is √(6x) = 30, so 6x = 900 and x = 150.

questions.text: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 480 m. When the policeman starts the chase, the thief also starts running. If the speed of the thief is 19 km/h and that of the policeman is 23 km/h, then how far would the thief have to run before he is overtaken?
questions.explanation: The policeman gains 23 − 19 = 4 km/h, so he closes the 0.48 km gap in 0.48/4 = 0.12 hours. In that time the thief runs 19 × 0.12 = 2.28 km = 2280 m.

questions.text: In what proportion must wheat at ₹20.40 per kg be mixed with wheat at ₹25.50 per kg, so that the mixture is worth ₹23.80 per kg?
The Wadali Brothers are famous for which of the following?
questions.explanation: The Wadali Brothers, Puranchand and Pyarelal Wadali of Amritsar, are known for Punjabi Sufi music.

questions.text: The important singers of ___________Gharana are Faiyyaz Khan, Latafat Hussein Khan and Dinkar Kakini.
questions.explanation: Faiyaz Khan, Latafat Hussain Khan and Dinkar Kaikini were vocalists of the Agra gharana.

questions.text: Who among the following has written the autobiography ‘In the afternoon of time: An autobiography’?
questions.explanation: 'In the Afternoon of Time' (1998) is Harivansh Rai Bachchan's autobiography in English, translated from his Hindi memoirs by Rupert Snell.

questions.text: ‘Faster than Lightning: My Autobiography’ is the story of which of the following international sprinters?
questions.explanation: 'Faster than Lightning: My Autobiography' (2013) is Usain Bolt's story.

questions.text: The proportion of a small increase in income which will lead to increased consumption expenditure is known as ________.
questions.explanation: The marginal propensity to consume is the share of a small increase in income that is spent on consumption; the rest is the marginal propensity to save.

questions.text: Who among the following is NOT a Padma Shri awardee 2022?
questions.explanation: Avani Lekhara, Sumit Antil and Neeraj Chopra received the Padma Shri in 2022; Mithali Raj received hers in 2015.

questions.text: The ‘Karbi Anglong Agreement’ signed in September 2021 is related to the ethnic community of the state of ________.
questions.explanation: The Karbi Anglong Agreement, signed on 4 September 2021 by the Centre, the Assam government and Karbi groups, concerns the Karbi community of Assam.

questions.text: What is the number of players in a cricket team on the ground?
questions.explanation: A cricket team has 11 players on the field.

questions.text: Who among the following is the author of the book ‘Sultry Days’?
questions.explanation: 'Sultry Days' (1994) is a novel by Shobhaa De.

questions.text: Which state does Brahmaputra river enters when it takes U turn at Namcha Barwa?
questions.explanation: The Brahmaputra (the Tsangpo in Tibet) takes a U-turn round Namcha Barwa and enters India in Arunachal Pradesh, where it is called the Siang or Dihang.

questions.text: Who shared the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2005 with Barry J Marshall for the discovery of the Helicobacter pylori bacterium and its role in gastritis and peptic ulcer disease?
questions.explanation: Barry J. Marshall and J. Robin Warren shared the 2005 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering Helicobacter pylori and its role in gastritis and peptic ulcers.

questions.text: Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma was an Indian Classical Dancer of _________ dance form.
questions.explanation: Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma, called the mother of Mohiniyattam, did much to revive Kerala's classical dance.

questions.text: Which Indian dancer was awarded the French Palme D'or by the French Government in 1977?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Mallika Sarabhai, the Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi dancer, whose profiles record a 1977 award in Paris: the Golden Star for best dance soloist, at the Théâtre des Champs-Élysées.

questions.text: Who received the Noble Prize in 1906,for recognition of the great merits of his theoretical and experimental investigations on the conduction of electricity by gases?
questions.explanation: J. J. Thomson, who discovered the electron, received the 1906 Nobel Prize in Physics for this work on the conduction of electricity by gases.

questions.text: Who among the following has written ‘Sangeet Kala Prakash’?
questions.explanation: 'Sangeet Kala Prakash' (1938), in two volumes, is by the vocalist Ramkrishnabuwa Vaze; it collects compositions in rare ragas.

questions.text: How many seats were reserved for the Scheduled Tribes in Lok Sabha for the 2019 general election?
questions.explanation: 47 Lok Sabha seats are reserved for the Scheduled Tribes, and 84 for the Scheduled Castes.

questions.text: What is the number of players playing in a team in a hockey match?
questions.explanation: A hockey team has 11 players on the field.

questions.text: The name of which element is derived from an Anglo-Saxon word and its symbol comes from the Latin word ‘Aurum’?
questions.explanation: The name 'gold' comes from Anglo-Saxon (Old English) and its symbol, Au, from the Latin 'aurum'.

questions.text: Sartaj Khan, Sarwar Khan, Swaroop Khan and Mame Khan are famous for which of the following?
questions.explanation: All four are known as Rajasthani folk singers; Mame Khan and Swaroop Khan come from the Manganiyar community of western Rajasthan.

questions.text: Famous Folk dancer Gulabo Sapera was conferred Padma Shri award for her contribution to which of the following dance forms?
questions.explanation: Gulabo Sapera, who received the Padma Shri in 2016, is the best-known performer of Kalbeliya, the dance of Rajasthan's Kalbeliya (snake-charmer) community.

questions.text: Which type of biome is located in Eastern North America, Western Europe, and Northeast Asia?
questions.explanation: Temperate deciduous forests, whose trees shed their leaves in autumn, cover eastern North America, western Europe and north-east Asia.

questions.text: Which of the following mountains was formed when molten rock from the depths of the earth rose from the crust and piled up on its own?
questions.explanation: Kilimanjaro is a volcanic mountain, built up from lava and ash; the Rockies, the Urals and the Alps are fold mountains.

questions.text: The Guru of Kuchipudi dance form ‘Guru Vempati Chinna Satyam’ who was instrumental in getting classical status to Kuchipudi was conferred by which of the following awards in 1998?
questions.explanation: Vempati Chinna Satyam, the Kuchipudi guru, received the Padma Bhushan in 1998.

questions.text: Who among the following won Arjuna Award 2021 in Para Table Tennis discipline?
questions.explanation: Bhavina Patel, silver medallist in para table tennis at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics, received the Arjuna Award in 2021.

questions.text: Which metal sulphate, composed of potassium, aluminium, and sulphate ions in the ratio 1 : 1 : 2, plays a role as a flame retardant, a mordant and an astringent?
questions.explanation: Potash alum, KAl(SO₄)₂·12H₂O, has potassium, aluminium and sulphate in the ratio 1 : 1 : 2; it is used as a mordant in dyeing, an astringent and a flame retardant.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. The car was being washed by me.
options: I had been washing the car.
questions.explanation: 'Was being washed' is the past continuous passive, so the active is 'was washing', with 'me' becoming the subject 'I': 'I was washing the car.'

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Whenever he is / on a holiday, / he travels by foot / to the temple nearby.
questions.explanation: One travels 'on foot', not 'by foot'; 'by' goes with vehicles, as in 'by bus' or 'by train'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Lion’s share
questions.explanation: The 'lion's share' is the largest part of something.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. If you had consulted me, I would have ________ you.
questions.explanation: In a past unreal condition ('If you had consulted me') the main clause takes 'would have' with the past participle: 'would have advised'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. All the electric poles in the suburbs were destroyed by the cyclone last year.
options: The cyclone destroyed all the electric poles in the suburbs last year.
The cyclone was being destroyed with all the electric poles in the suburbs last year.
The cyclone was destroyed by the all the electric poles in the suburbs last year.
The cyclone destroyed all the suburbs by the electric poles last year.
questions.explanation: The agent, the cyclone, becomes the subject and 'were destroyed' becomes the simple past 'destroyed': 'The cyclone destroyed all the electric poles in the suburbs last year.'

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. The deeper you immerse it, the greater will be the difference in the water level. B. This difference in the levels in the U-tube is a measure of the pressure applied by your palm. C. If you immerse the funnel into a bucket of water, you will again see the difference in the water level in the U-tube. D. When you gently apply pressure on the rubber film with your palm, you will find that a difference in the water level is created in the manometer.
questions.explanation: D describes pressing the rubber film and the difference it makes in the manometer, B says that difference measures the pressure, C moves on to immersing the funnel in water, and A adds that the deeper it goes the greater the difference: DBCA.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate spelling that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. We love to play with our “neighboar’s” children
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'neighbour', in the possessive before 'children': 'our neighbour's children'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Decipher
questions.explanation: To 'decipher' something is to work out the meaning of what is hard to read or understand: to 'interpret' it.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. The utensils have been cleaned.
questions.explanation: 'Have been cleaned' is the present perfect passive, so the active is 'has cleaned'; with no agent given, 'someone' becomes the subject: 'Someone has cleaned the utensils.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. A note of ______ during the leaders' meeting at the UN.
questions.explanation: 'A note of discord' is the usual phrase for a sign of disagreement coming to the surface.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Get the axe
questions.explanation: To 'get the axe' is to be dismissed from one's job.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Wipe the floor with someone
questions.explanation: To 'wipe the floor with someone' is to defeat them completely and easily.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Reject as invalid, especially by legal procedure
questions.explanation: To 'quash' a decision or conviction is to reject it as invalid, usually by a court. 'Reiterate' means repeat, and 'putrid' and 'putrefy' have to do with decay.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option fill in the blank. The death of her father had made her sullen and __________ .
questions.explanation: Her father's death made her gloomy: 'sullen and melancholic'. 'Jovial', 'joyful' and 'smug' do not fit a bereavement or sit with 'sullen'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'supersede'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Vulgar
questions.explanation: 'Vulgar' means coarse or lacking in taste; its opposite is 'refined'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Merry, convivial, hearty and good humoured
questions.explanation: 'Jovial' means merry, friendly and good-humoured. 'Joyous' means simply full of joy, a 'jowl' is the lower cheek and a 'jubilee' an anniversary.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Overture
questions.explanation: An 'overture' is an introduction to something larger, like the opening music of an opera: a 'preamble'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Most of the valley had been (1)_________ over the ages by the river waters, (2)_________ rainfall, and fierce winds. All except for one giant monolith, a (3)_________ tower-like mountain of a single rock. It stood at a proud (4)_________ of eight hundred and fifty metres from the valley floor, towering well above the (5)_________ shoulders.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: River waters, rain and wind wear rock away over the ages: the valley had been 'eroded'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Most of the valley had been (1)_________ over the ages by the river waters, (2)_________ rainfall, and fierce winds. All except for one giant monolith, a (3)_________ tower-like mountain of a single rock. It stood at a proud (4)_________ of eight hundred and fifty metres from the valley floor, towering well above the (5)_________ shoulders.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Rainfall strong enough to wear the valley away is 'heavy' rainfall; 'scanty' or 'less' rain would not do it.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Most of the valley had been (1)_________ over the ages by the river waters, (2)_________ rainfall, and fierce winds. All except for one giant monolith, a (3)_________ tower-like mountain of a single rock. It stood at a proud (4)_________ of eight hundred and fifty metres from the valley floor, towering well above the (5)_________ shoulders.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: The monolith is 'giant' and stands 850 metres high, so it is 'humongous' (huge), not small or tiny.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Most of the valley had been (1)_________ over the ages by the river waters, (2)_________ rainfall, and fierce winds. All except for one giant monolith, a (3)_________ tower-like mountain of a single rock. It stood at a proud (4)_________ of eight hundred and fifty metres from the valley floor, towering well above the (5)_________ shoulders.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: Eight hundred and fifty metres from the valley floor is a 'height'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Most of the valley had been (1)_________ over the ages by the river waters, (2)_________ rainfall, and fierce winds. All except for one giant monolith, a (3)_________ tower-like mountain of a single rock. It stood at a proud (4)_________ of eight hundred and fifty metres from the valley floor, towering well above the (5)_________ shoulders.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: The possessive is needed before 'shoulders': the mountain towered above 'the valley's shoulders', its upper slopes.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that, when placed from left to right in the blanks below, will complete the letter series. B E _ K D F _ H K D J E H _ D _ E H K D
questions.explanation: With H, E, K, N in the blanks the series reads BEHKD FEHKD JEHKD NEHKD: the first letter moves 4 places on each time (B, F, J, N) and EHKD repeats.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 3, 3,12,108,?
questions.explanation: Each term is the one before multiplied by 1², 2², 3², 4² in turn: 3 × 1 = 3, 3 × 4 = 12, 12 × 9 = 108 and 108 × 16 = 1728.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 13 * 5 * 60 * 6 * 11 * 64
Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 25*5*8*4*15*20
Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 19, 114, 119, ?, 479, 958

Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All cranes are bears. Some tigers are cranes. All jackals are tigers. Conclusion: I. Some bears are tigers. II. All jackals are bears. III. Some jackals are bears.
options: Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: The tigers that are cranes are bears, so some bears are tigers (I). All jackals are tigers, but they need not be the tigers that are cranes, so neither II nor III follows.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the sixth number is related to the fifth number. 3 : 18 :: 9 : ? :: 5 : 100
questions.explanation: The second number is the cube of the first minus its square: 3³ − 3² = 27 − 9 = 18 and 5³ − 5² = 125 − 25 = 100. Likewise 9³ − 9² = 729 − 81 = 648.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘CHOICE’ is written as ‘OHCECI’ and ‘DEMAND’ is written as ‘MEDDNA’. How will ‘EXPECT’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each half of the word is reversed: CHO ICE → OHC ECI and DEM AND → MED DNA. So EXP ECT → PXE TCE: PXETCE.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (90, 15, 21) (16, 2, 10) (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed)
questions.explanation: The third number is the first divided by the second, plus the second: 90 ÷ 15 + 15 = 21 and 16 ÷ 2 + 2 = 10. Likewise 46 ÷ 23 + 23 = 25.

questions.text: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series to make it logically complete? ACF, DFI, GIL, JLO, ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places forward from one cluster to the next: J → M, L → O and O → R, giving MOR.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must NOT be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Castle : Building :: Sedan : ?
questions.explanation: A castle is a kind of building, as a sedan is a kind of car.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'SIGNAL' is coded as 'H18T13Z15', and 'TARGET' is coded as 'G26I20V7'. How will 'VOLUME' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite in the alphabet (A ↔ Z, B ↔ Y and so on), and the 2nd, 4th and 6th are written as that opposite letter's position: SIGNAL → H, R (18), T, M (13), Z, O (15). So VOLUME → E, L (12), O, F (6), N, V (22): E12O6N22.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'COMMON' is written as ‘EQOOQP’ and ‘PREP’ is written as ’RTGR’.How will 'MAGNET' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Every letter moves 2 places forward: COMMON → EQOOQP and PREP → RTGR. So MAGNET → OCIPGV.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 2 * 7 * 3 * 21 * 2 * 23
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (56, 12, 672)
questions.explanation: The third number is the product of the first two: 56 × 12 = 672. Likewise 14 × 21 = 294; the other sets would need 221, 270 and 256.

questions.text: If I denotes ‘÷’, J denotes ‘×’, K denotes ‘−’ and L denotes ‘+’, then what will come in place of ‘?’ in the following equation? 118 L (16 I 4) K (72 J 2) L 28 L (39 J 3) = ?

The second number in the given number pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number pairs, EXCEPT one. Find that odd number pair.
questions.explanation: In 441 : 49, 729 : 81 and 369 : 41 the second number is the first divided by 9. 343 ÷ 9 is not 47 (nor a whole number), so 343 : 47 is the odd pair.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in an English dictionary. 1.Projectile 2.Projector 3.Prolong 4.Prolific 5.Prohibit
questions.explanation: Prohibit comes first ('proh' before 'proj'), then Projectile before Projector ('projecti' before 'projecto'), then Prolific before Prolong ('proli' before 'prolo'): 5, 1, 2, 4, 3.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in an English dictionary. 1.Campaigns 2. Catalytic 3. Candidature 4. Camphor 5. Cataracts
questions.explanation: Campaigns before Camphor ('campa' before 'camph'), then Candidature ('can'), then Catalytic before Cataracts ('catal' before 'catar'): 1, 4, 3, 2, 5.

questions.text: If AB = QR, BC = PR and CA = PQ, then
questions.explanation: AB and BC meet at B, and the sides equal to them, QR and PR, meet at R, so B corresponds to R; then A corresponds to Q and C to P. By SSS, ∆CBA ≅ ∆PRQ.

questions.text: In a decade, a town's population grew from 1,75,000 to 2,62,500. What is the average annual percentage increase in population?
questions.explanation: The population rose by 87,500, which is 50% of 1,75,000. Spread over the 10 years of the decade, that is 5% a year on average.

questions.text: A train covers the distance between two stations X and Y in 6 hours. If the speed of the train is reduced by 13 km/h, then it travels the same distance in 9 hours. Find the distance between the two stations
questions.explanation: With speed v: 6v = 9(v − 13), so 3v = 117 and v = 39 km/h. Distance = 6 × 39 = 234 km.

questions.text: In a bag, black tablet covers and white tablet covers are in the ratio 5:9. If there are 450 white tablet covers, how many black tablet covers are there in the bag?
questions.explanation: 9 parts are 450 covers, so 1 part is 50 and the 5 black parts are 250.

questions.text: The average weight of A, B and C is 65 kg. If the average weight of A and B is 62 kg and that of B and C is 66 kg, then the weight (in kg) of B is:
Anil offers his customer a discount of 15% on a T-shirt and he still makes a profit of 25%. What is the actual cost of the T-shirt marked ₹500?
questions.explanation: After 15% off, the T-shirt sells for 0.85 × 500 = ₹425. That is 125% of the cost, so the cost is 425/1.25 = ₹340.

questions.text: A family consists of two grandparents, two parents and four grandchildren. The average age of the grandparents is 67 years, that of the parents is 35 years and that of the grandchildren is 9 years. What is the average age of the family?
questions.explanation: Total age = 2 × 67 + 2 × 35 + 4 × 9 = 134 + 70 + 36 = 240 years for 8 people: 240 ÷ 8 = 30 years.

questions.text: Find the total surface area of a cuboid whose length is 20 cm, width is 15 cm, and height is 8 cm.
questions.explanation: Total surface area = 2(lb + bh + lh) = 2(300 + 120 + 160) = 2 × 580 = 1160 cm².

questions.text: The diagonal of a cube is 24 cm. Find its total surface area.
questions.explanation: The diagonal of a cube is a√3, so a√3 = 24 and a² = 576/3 = 192. Total surface area = 6a² = 1152 cm².

questions.text: The sum of two numbers is 17 and their product is 34.Find the sum of their squares.

A container is normally filled in 5 hours. However, it takes 6 hours when there is a leak at the bottom. If the container is full, in what time would the leak empty it, if no water is allowed into the container during that period?
questions.explanation: The leak empties 1/5 − 1/6 = 1/30 of the container an hour, so on its own it takes 30 hours.

questions.text: When two numbers are separately divided by 44, the remainders are 11 and 38, respectively. If the sum of the two numbers is divided by 44, then the remainder will be:
questions.explanation: The sum leaves the same remainder as 11 + 38 = 49, and 49 = 44 + 5.

questions.text: Find the compound interest on ₹40,000 after 2 years 6 months at 20% per annum, if the interest is compounded half-yearly.
questions.explanation: Compounded half-yearly, the rate is 10% for 5 half-years: 40,000 × 1.1⁵ = 40,000 × 1.61051 = ₹64,420.40. Compound interest = 64,420.40 − 40,000 = ₹24,420.40.

questions.text: A shoe manufacturing company offers 3 types of discount schemes to its customers: (i) 20% and 12% (ii) 25% and 5% (iii) 30% and 3% at different stages of sales. Find the best scheme for the customer.
questions.explanation: The price left after each pair of discounts: (i) 0.8 × 0.88 = 0.704, (ii) 0.75 × 0.95 = 0.7125, (iii) 0.7 × 0.97 = 0.679. Scheme (iii) leaves the lowest price, a single discount of 32.1%.

questions.text: Rahul bought 20 dozen toys at a cost of ₹375 each dozen. He sold each of them for ₹33. The profit percentage is:
questions.explanation: Each toy costs 375 ÷ 12 = ₹31.25 and sells for ₹33, a profit of ₹1.75: 1.75/31.25 × 100 = 5.6%.

questions.text: The value of a machine depreciates every year by 10%. If its present value is ₹35,000, then the value of the machine after 2 years will be:
questions.explanation: Two years of 10% depreciation: 35,000 × 0.9 × 0.9 = ₹28,350.

questions.text: A beaker contains a mixture of two liquids X and Y in the ratio 5 : 3. When 6 litres of the mixture is drawn off and then replaced with Y, the ratio of X and Y becomes 5 : 7. How many litres of liquid X was contained in the beaker initially?
questions.explanation: With T litres in all, drawing off 6 litres and adding Y leaves (5/8)(T − 6) litres of X in T litres. This must be 5/12 of T: (T − 6)/8 = T/12, so T = 18 and X was 5/8 × 18 = 11.25 litres.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Duty?
options: To uphold and protect the unity and integrity of India
questions.explanation: Casting a vote is not among the Fundamental Duties listed in Article 51A. Protecting the natural environment, abiding by the Constitution and upholding the unity and integrity of India all are.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is correct about mitochondria?
options: Mitochondria is present only in bacteria.
Mitochondria is present in all living cells.
Mitochondria is not bound by any membrane.
Mitochondria without outer membrane is called mitoplast.
questions.explanation: A mitoplast is a mitochondrion stripped of its outer membrane. Mitochondria have a double membrane, are absent from bacteria and are not found in every living cell (mature red blood cells lack them).

questions.text: Who among the following Indian Playback Singers holds the Guinness world record for singing the highest number of songs in one day?
questions.explanation: Kumar Sanu entered the Guinness World Records in 1993 for recording 28 songs in a single day.

questions.text: Who recognised the elements carbon, hydrogen and oxygen and opposed the phlogiston theory by discovering the role of oxygen in combustion and respiration?
questions.explanation: Antoine Lavoisier named oxygen and hydrogen, showed the part oxygen plays in combustion and respiration, and so overturned the phlogiston theory.

questions.text: Which type of radiation designates a part of the electromagnetic spectrum with frequencies approximately from 300 GHz to 3 kHz, or equivalent, wavelengths approximately from 1 mm to 100km?
questions.explanation: Radio waves span frequencies from about 3 kHz to 300 GHz, wavelengths from 100 km down to 1 mm. Microwaves are only the top of that band, and infrared and ultraviolet lie at higher frequencies still.

questions.text: The current in the bulb will stop flowing:
options: when the switch is turned on
questions.explanation: Current flows only round a closed circuit; when the circuit is broken, for example by switching off, it stops.

questions.text: NDP at FC = GDP at FC minus ____________
questions.explanation: Net domestic product is gross domestic product minus depreciation (the consumption of fixed capital).

questions.text: Which of the following brought out the publication ‘Elderly in India 2021’?
options: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
questions.explanation: 'Elderly in India 2021' was published by the National Statistical Office of the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.

questions.text: Who among the following is the author of the book ‘Boys Don’t Cry’?
questions.explanation: 'Boys Don't Cry', a novel about a woman accused of her ex-husband's murder, is by the author and journalist Meghna Pant.

questions.text: The Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2021 was introduced in Lok Sabha on 15 March 2021, which amended the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, _________.
questions.explanation: The Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act of 1957 is the main law governing mining in India; the 2021 Bill amended it.

questions.text: Padma Shri Guru Mayadhar Raut’s pioneering spirit revived which of the following dances in 1950s and redefined the grammar and Abhinaya vocabulary of the dance form?
questions.explanation: Guru Mayadhar Raut was one of the gurus who revived and codified Odissi in the 1950s.

questions.text: Why do people living in the Konkan coast NOT encounter extremes of temperature and seasonal rhythm?
options: Location on leeward side of Sahyadri
questions.explanation: The sea moderates the climate of coastal places such as the Konkan, so they have no extremes of heat or cold.

questions.text: Which place in the southern slopes of the Khasi Hills receives an average of 12,000 mm of rainfall per year?
questions.explanation: Mawsynram, on the southern slopes of the Khasi Hills in Meghalaya, receives the highest average rainfall in the world.

questions.text: Where is Indian Institute of Skiing and Mountaineering situated?
questions.explanation: The Indian Institute of Skiing and Mountaineering is at Gulmarg in Jammu and Kashmir.

questions.text: In Budget 2022, the Khelo India Scheme, a flagship Central Sector Scheme of the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports has been included in which of the following?
questions.explanation: Khelo India was made one of the priority programmes of the Prime Minister's Awards for Excellence in Public Administration, presented on Civil Services Day 2022; the sports minister cited this with its larger allocation in Budget 2022.

questions.text: Name the classical dancer who was awarded the ‘Sangeet Natak Akademi Award’ in 1966 for his contribution to Odissi.
questions.explanation: Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra, the leading Odissi guru, received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1966.

questions.text: Which of the following is the Sahitya Akademi Award winning novel of the Indian writer Amitav Ghosh?
questions.explanation: Amitav Ghosh won the Sahitya Akademi Award for 'The Shadow Lines' in 1989.

questions.text: In 2019, which disease,according to WHO,was ranked as the seventh leading cause of death globally?
questions.explanation: In WHO's 2019 global estimates, Alzheimer's disease and other dementias were the seventh leading cause of death; stroke was second, lung cancer sixth and diabetes ninth.

questions.text: Who among the following Hindustani classical vocalists was awarded the Padma Bhushan by the Government of India and the title of ‘Rajya Gayika’ by the Government of Maharashtra in 1969?
questions.explanation: Kesarbai Kerkar of the Jaipur-Atrauli gharana received the Padma Bhushan in 1969, and the Government of Maharashtra named her 'Rajya Gayika' the same year.

questions.text: Who among the following internationally acclaimed Kuchipudi dancers has been honoured with the prestigious Bharata Shastra Nritya Praveena National Award 2021?
questions.explanation: Aparna Satheesan, a US-based Kuchipudi and Bharatanatyam dancer, received the Bharata Shastra Nritya Praveena National Award for Kuchipudi in 2021, at a festival of the All India Dancer's Association.

questions.text: The central theme of Tokyo Paralympic 2020 was ________.
questions.explanation: 'United by Emotion' was the motto of the Tokyo 2020 Games, Olympic and Paralympic alike. 'Inspire a Generation' was London 2012's and 'One World, One Dream' Beijing 2008's.

questions.text: Which of the following books is an autobiography of the professional boxer Mike Tyson?
options: Straight From the Heart: An Autobiography
questions.explanation: 'Undisputed Truth' (2013) is Mike Tyson's autobiography.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Clamour
questions.explanation: 'Clamour' is a loud, confused noise; its opposite is 'quiet'. 'Babble' is close to a synonym.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The thief / entered the house, / in the middle of the night, / quiet.
options: in the middle of the night
questions.explanation: The word describes how the thief entered, so it must be the adverb 'quietly', not the adjective 'quiet'.

questions.text: Parts of the given sentence have been given as options. One of them contains a grammatical error. Select the option that has the error. He is such an untruthful man, that no one will believing him.
questions.explanation: The modal 'will' takes the base form of the verb: 'no one will believe him'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. The sweet and bitter memories of her past “make her weak and sad.”
options: ought to make her pallid and unhappy
had to make her pale and unhappy
must make her pastel and unhappy
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'made her feeble and unhappy': 'feeble and unhappy' keeps the sense of 'weak and sad', while 'ought to', 'had to' and 'must' add an obligation the sentence does not mean, and 'pallid' and 'pastel' describe colour. The original 'make' was itself acceptable; the key's change is to the simple past.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Have a soft spot for someone
options: To argue something with no effect
To show the true nature of someone
questions.explanation: To 'have a soft spot for' someone is to be fond of them.

questions.text: In the following passage, a word has been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. In a ________ move, the robbers chose their next place of attack over 255 km away from the locations they had earlier ________ in Dewas.
questions.explanation: A 'shrewd' (cleverly calculated) move, away from the places the robbers had earlier 'targeted'. 'Righteous' and 'noble' do not fit robbers, and 'vanished' cannot take an object.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Reconnoitre
questions.explanation: To 'reconnoitre' is to survey or inspect an area, usually to gather information.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Rescind
questions.explanation: To 'rescind' an order or law is to cancel it officially: to 'revoke' it.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. The thieves were caught by the police.
options: The police was caught the thieves.
The police were caught the thieves.
The police had caught the thieves.
questions.explanation: The simple past passive 'were caught by the police' becomes the simple past active, with the police as subject: 'The police caught the thieves.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Pull the plug
questions.explanation: To 'pull the plug' on something is to bring it to an end, typically by stopping its support.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'suspicious'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. One expects better behaviour from a senior student.
options: Better behaviour was expected from senior student.
As a senior student you need to behave.
Better behaviour is expected from a senior student.
Senior student behaviour is expected better.
questions.explanation: 'Expects' becomes 'is expected', with the object as subject, and the general agent 'one' is dropped: 'Better behaviour is expected from a senior student.'

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. One morning the Giant was lying awake in bed when he heard some lovely music. B. Then the Hail stopped dancing over his head, and the North Wind ceased roaring, and a delicious perfume came to him through the open casement. “I believe the Spring has come at last,” said the Giant; and he jumped out of bed and looked out. C. It was really only a little linnet singing outside his window, but it was so long since he had heard a bird sing in his garden that it seemed to him to be the most beautiful music in the world. D. It sounded so sweet to his ears that he thought it must be the King’s musicians passing by.
questions.explanation: A opens with the Giant hearing music, D says what he took it to be, C says what it really was, and B follows with the Spring arriving: ADCB.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. At loggerheads
questions.explanation: People 'at loggerheads' are in strong disagreement with each other.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A journey undertaken by a group of people with a particular purpose, especially that of exploration or research.
questions.explanation: An expedition is a journey by a group for a particular purpose, such as exploration or research. A sojourn is a temporary stay, and a pilgrimage a journey to a holy place.

questions.text: Select the correct homonym from the given options to fill in the blank. She couldn’t eat the________ pizza by herself
questions.explanation: 'Whole' means entire: she could not eat the entire pizza. 'Hole' sounds the same but means an opening.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. “I am watching” a movie, when my mother came into the room.
questions.explanation: An action in progress in the past, interrupted by another ('came'), takes the past continuous: 'I was watching a movie when my mother came into the room.'

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The notice / that the office / posted over the wall / is very appropriate.
questions.explanation: A notice is put up 'on' a wall, not 'over' it: 'posted on the wall'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The contract (1) __________ the author and the reader is a game. And the game is one of the greatest inventions (2) __________ Western civilisation: the game of telling stories, inventing characters and creating the (3) ___________ paradise of the individual, from whence no one can be expelled (4) ____________, in a novel, no one owns the truth and everyone has the right to be (5) _____________ and understood.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: A contract is 'between' two parties: here the author and the reader.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The contract (1) __________ the author and the reader is a game. And the game is one of the greatest inventions (2) __________ Western civilisation: the game of telling stories, inventing characters and creating the (3) ___________ paradise of the individual, from whence no one can be expelled (4) ____________, in a novel, no one owns the truth and everyone has the right to be (5) _____________ and understood.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: One of the greatest inventions 'of' Western civilisation.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The contract (1) __________ the author and the reader is a game. And the game is one of the greatest inventions (2) __________ Western civilisation: the game of telling stories, inventing characters and creating the (3) ___________ paradise of the individual, from whence no one can be expelled (4) ____________, in a novel, no one owns the truth and everyone has the right to be (5) _____________ and understood.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Telling stories and inventing characters creates an 'imaginary' paradise.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The contract (1) __________ the author and the reader is a game. And the game is one of the greatest inventions (2) __________ Western civilisation: the game of telling stories, inventing characters and creating the (3) ___________ paradise of the individual, from whence no one can be expelled (4) ____________, in a novel, no one owns the truth and everyone has the right to be (5) _____________ and understood.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: The clause gives the reason no one can be expelled: 'because', in a novel, no one owns the truth.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The contract (1) __________ the author and the reader is a game. And the game is one of the greatest inventions (2) __________ Western civilisation: the game of telling stories, inventing characters and creating the (3) ___________ paradise of the individual, from whence no one can be expelled (4) ____________, in a novel, no one owns the truth and everyone has the right to be (5) _____________ and understood.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Everyone has the right to be 'heard' and understood.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘PULSE’ is written as ‘QTMRF’ and ‘HEART’ is written as ‘IDBQU’. How will ‘LIVER’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +1, −1, +1, −1, +1 in turn: PULSE → QTMRF and HEART → IDBQU. So LIVER → M H W D S: MHWDS.

questions.text: If 13 September 2003 is a Saturday, then what will be the day of the week on 14 February 2005?
questions.explanation: From 13 September 2003 there are 17 + 31 + 30 + 31 = 109 days to the end of 2003, 366 in the leap year 2004 and 31 + 14 = 45 to 14 February 2005: 520 days. 520 = 74 × 7 + 2, so the day moves on 2 from Saturday: Monday.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'GRAPES' is written as 'EPYNCQ' and ‘ROSE’ is written as ‘PMQC’. How will 'SAGE' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places back (A wraps round to Y): GRAPES → EPYNCQ and ROSE → PMQC. So SAGE → QYEC.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the sixth number is related to the fifth number. 9 : 17 :: 22 : ? :: 30 : 59
questions.explanation: The second number is twice the first minus 1: 9 × 2 − 1 = 17 and 30 × 2 − 1 = 59. Likewise 22 × 2 − 1 = 43.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 67, 79, 64, ?, 61, 85
questions.explanation: Two series alternate: 67, 64, 61 (down 3) and 79, ?, 85 (up 3). The missing term is 79 + 3 = 82.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 2, 26, ?, 170, 290, 442
questions.explanation: The differences 24, 56, 88, 120, 152 grow by 32 each time: 2 + 24 = 26, 26 + 56 = 82, and 82 + 88 = 170.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 12,37,114,347,1048,?

Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. ABILITY : ITYLABI :: INSTEAD : EADTINS :: ENGLISH : ?
questions.explanation: The last three letters come first, then the middle letter, then the first three: ABI L ITY → ITY L ABI and INS T EAD → EAD T INS. So ENG L ISH → ISH L ENG: ISHLENG.

questions.text: If I denotes ‘÷’, J denotes ‘×’, K denotes ‘−’ and L denotes ‘+’, then what will come in place of ‘?’ in the following equation? 15 L (3 J 9) K (12 J 2) L (189 I 9) L 29 = ?
Select the option that represents the letters that, when placed from left to right in the blanks, will complete the letter series. D _ R X E C M R _ E _ M R X _ A M _ X E
questions.explanation: With M, X, B, E, R in the blanks the series reads DMRXE CMRXE BMRXE AMRXE: the first letter moves back one each time and MRXE repeats.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 2168,1979,1790,1601,1412,?
