questions.explanation: Each term is 189 less than the one before: 1412 − 189 = 1223.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word and the fourth word is related to the third word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must NOT be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Bear : Cub :: Owl : Owlet :: Deer : ?
questions.explanation: A cub is a young bear and an owlet a young owl; a young deer is a fawn.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 4 : 31::7 : 223::6 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is the cube of one less than the first, plus the first: 3³ + 4 = 31 and 6³ + 7 = 223. Likewise 5³ + 6 = 131.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 16*4*8*10*2*16
Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? RJGZ, NQWM, ?, FECM, BLSZ
questions.explanation: First letters move back 4 (R, N, J, F, B), second letters forward 7 (J, Q, X, E, L), third letters back 10 (G, W, M, C, S), wrapping round the alphabet, and the fourth letters alternate Z, M: JXMZ.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given number series? 209, 318, 427, 536, ?, 754
questions.explanation: Each term is 109 more than the one before: 536 + 109 = 645, and 645 + 109 = 754.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 48*6*17*3*12*5*1
questions.explanation: 48 ÷ 6 + 17 × 3 = 12 × 5 − 1: the left side is 8 + 51 = 59 and the right side 60 − 1 = 59.

questions.text: Select the correct option that indicates the arrangement of the following words in a logical and meaningful order. 1.Solar System 2.Earth 3.India 4.Asia 5.Milky way
questions.explanation: From the largest to the smallest: the Milky Way contains the Solar System, which contains the Earth, on which lies Asia, which contains India: 5, 1, 2, 4, 3.

questions.text: Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some rains are cyclones. Some cyclones are draughts. No draught is a thunder. Conclusions: I. Some cyclones are rains. II. No thunder is a cyclone. III. No draught is a rain.
options: Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: 'Some rains are cyclones' can be reversed: some cyclones are rains (I). The statements only show that the cyclones that are draughts are not thunders, so II is not certain, and nothing links draughts to rains, so III is not certain either.

questions.text: A can do a piece of work in 15 days, but with the help of B, he can do it in 9 days. In what time can B do it alone?
questions.explanation: B does 1/9 − 1/15 = 2/45 of the work a day, so B alone takes 45/2 = 22.5 days.

questions.text: On buying 24 bangles Isha gets 6 bangles free of cost. What percent does Isha get as a discount?
questions.explanation: She takes 30 bangles for the price of 24, so the discount is 6/30 = 20%.

questions.text: A shopkeeper mixes two qualities of rice, which cost him ₹40 per kg and ₹47.50 per kg respectively, in such a way that he has 15 kg of the blended rice costing him a total of ₹645. What is the weight (in kg) of the rice that cost him ₹47.50 per kg?

A is the average marks of a group of 10 students in a class and A+8 is the average of a group of 15 students which includes the group of 10 students as given. The total marks obtained by the group of 10 students is X and the total marks obtained by the group of 15 students is Y. If X : Y = 3 : 5, then the value of A+X+Y is _________.
Two trains leave Agra for Calcutta at 9:00 a.m. and 9:30 a.m., respectively, and travel at 240 km/h and 300 km/h, respectively. How many kilometres from Agra will the two trains meet?
questions.explanation: By 9:30 a.m. the first train is 120 km ahead, and the second gains 60 km/h on it, so it catches up in 2 hours, at 11:30 a.m. The first train has then run for 2.5 hours: 240 × 2.5 = 600 km.

questions.text: The identity 4(z + 7)(2z – 1) = Az² + Bz + C holds for all real values of z. Find the value of A² – B – C .
Find the total surface area of a container in cylindrical shape whose diameter is 14 cm and height is 25 cm. [Use π = 22/7]
questions.explanation: Total surface area = 2πr(r + h) = 2 × 22/7 × 7 × (7 + 25) = 44 × 32 = 1,408 cm².

questions.text: A shopkeeper wanted to sell ₹3,000 worth of products. He gave two options — giving three successive discounts of 10% each, or giving a single discount of 30%. If a buyer chooses the former option how much extra/less does he pay as compared to the second option?
questions.explanation: Three 10% discounts leave 0.9³ = 0.729 of the price, ₹2,187; a single 30% discount leaves ₹2,100. The buyer pays ₹87 extra.

questions.text: At an election there were two candidates. A candidate got 38% of votes and lost by 7200 votes. The total number of valid votes is ________.
questions.explanation: The winner got 62%, so the margin is 62% − 38% = 24% of the valid votes = 7,200. Valid votes = 7,200 ÷ 0.24 = 30,000.

questions.text: If x=9, then the value of x⁵-10x⁴+10x³-10x²+10x-1 is:
questions.explanation: With x = 9, 10 = x + 1, so the expression is x⁵ − (x + 1)x⁴ + (x + 1)x³ − (x + 1)x² + (x + 1)x − 1. The terms cancel in pairs, leaving x − 1 = 8.

questions.text: The third proportional of 42 and 63 is:
questions.explanation: The third proportional of a and b is b²/a = 63²/42 = 3,969/42 = 94.5.

questions.text: A man travelled by car from city A to city B at a speed of 24 km/h and returned from city B to city A at 16 km/h. Find his average speed over the whole journey.
questions.explanation: Over equal distances the average speed is 2uv/(u + v) = 2 × 24 × 16/40 = 19.2 km/h.

questions.text: A solid toy is in the shape which is a combination of a cylinder, cone and a hemispherical bowl. The cylinder contributes to 50% of the total volume of the toy, the cone contributes to 20% of the volume. Find the ratio of the contribution (in terms of volume) of the cone, cylinder and hemisphere.
questions.explanation: The hemisphere makes up the remaining 100 − 50 − 20 = 30% of the volume. Cone : cylinder : hemisphere = 20 : 50 : 30 = 2 : 5 : 3.

questions.text: Find the area of the sector of a circle of radius 7 cm with a central angle of 90°.
questions.explanation: A 90° sector is a quarter of the circle: (1/4) × 22/7 × 7² = 154/4 = 38.5 cm².

questions.text: If a company gives a discount of 20% on the marked price of an article and gains 20% on that particular article, then at what percentage above the cost price did the company mark its goods?
questions.explanation: Take the cost as 100: the selling price is 120, which is 80% of the marked price, so the marked price is 150, 50% above cost.

questions.text: The total surface area of a cuboid of length 90 cm, breadth 50 cm and height 4 m is:
The average of the natural numbers divisible by 5 from the integers −10 to 35 is:
questions.explanation: The natural numbers in the range divisible by 5 are 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30 and 35 (0, −5 and −10 are not natural numbers). Their average is (5 + 35)/2 = 20.

questions.text: __________ is a world-renowned exponent of the Bansuri or bamboo flute.
questions.explanation: Hariprasad Chaurasia is India's best-known bansuri (bamboo flute) player; Anjanibai Malpekar and Ajoy Chakrabarty are vocalists.

questions.text: As of March 2021, with a throw of 88.07 m, javelin star Neeraj Chopra set a national record in the third Indian Grand Prix in ____________________.
questions.explanation: Neeraj Chopra threw 88.07 m at the third Indian Grand Prix at Patiala in March 2021, bettering his own national record of 88.06 m set at the 2018 Asian Games.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following freedom fighters wrote ‘The Story of My Experiments with Truth’?
questions.explanation: 'The Story of My Experiments with Truth' is Mahatma Gandhi's autobiography, written first in Gujarati.

questions.text: Rajeev Taranath, a disciple of Ali Akbar Khan, is a __________ player.
questions.explanation: Rajeev Taranath is a sarod player, a disciple of the sarod master Ali Akbar Khan.

questions.text: Kum Kum Mohanty received the Padma Shri award for her contribution to which of the following dance forms?
questions.explanation: Kumkum Mohanty is a leading Odissi dancer from Odisha.

questions.text: Which of the following angles of the flow of factor payments forms the basis to estimate the national income?
questions.explanation: Factor payments (rent, wages, interest and profit) are the incomes earned by the factors of production, so adding up their flow is the income, or income distribution, method of estimating national income.

questions.text: ‘Straight from the Heart: An Autobiography’ is the autobiography of which of the following Indian cricketers?
questions.explanation: 'Straight from the Heart' is the autobiography of Kapil Dev, who led India to the 1983 World Cup.

questions.text: Which of the following cities will be the host of Summer Olympics 2028?
questions.explanation: Los Angeles will host the 2028 Summer Olympics, its third after 1932 and 1984.

questions.text: In the case of Vikas KishanRao Gawali vs _________, in January 2021, the Supreme Court observed that OBC reservation cannot exceed 50%.
questions.explanation: The case was about OBC reservation in Maharashtra's local bodies; the Supreme Court held that reservation for SCs, STs and OBCs there together cannot exceed 50%.

questions.text: Famous classical dancer Tanjore Balasaraswati was awarded the _________ in 1977.
questions.explanation: T. Balasaraswati, the great Bharatanatyam dancer, received the Padma Vibhushan in 1977; she had received the Padma Bhushan in 1957.

questions.text: How many seats of Rajya Sabha are present in the state of Maharashtra?
questions.explanation: Maharashtra has 19 Rajya Sabha seats, the second most after Uttar Pradesh's 31.

questions.text: Solanum lycopersicum L. is the scientific name of which of the following highly consumed vegetables?
questions.explanation: Solanum lycopersicum is the tomato, of the same genus as the potato (Solanum tuberosum).

questions.text: 'Third man' is related to which of the following sports?
questions.explanation: Third man is a fielding position in cricket, behind the slips on the off side.

questions.text: How is the voltmeter connected across the points between which the potential difference is to be measured?
questions.explanation: A voltmeter is connected in parallel across the two points, so that it has the same potential difference as they do; an ammeter is connected in series.

questions.text: As of June 2021, India men's football team captain ____________ became the second-highest goal-scorer among the active international footballers.
questions.explanation: Sunil Chhetri's two goals against Bangladesh in June 2021 took him to 74, past Lionel Messi and second only to Cristiano Ronaldo among active players.

questions.text: Who among the following Indian Carnatic musicians received the Padma Vibhushan award in 1991 and established the Academy of Performing Arts and Research in Switzerland?
questions.explanation: M. Balamuralikrishna, the Carnatic vocalist, received the Padma Vibhushan in 1991. Kishan Maharaj, Ghulam Mustafa Khan and Chhannulal Mishra are Hindustani musicians.

questions.text: Which outside layer of the Earth is less dense, thick, and andesitic to granite composition?
questions.explanation: The continental crust is thicker and less dense than the oceanic crust, and broadly granitic in composition; the oceanic crust is basaltic.

questions.text: Identify the solution extracted from a plant belonging to division Thallophyta.
questions.explanation: Litmus is extracted from lichens, which NCERT places in the division Thallophyta.

questions.text: Titanium dioxide, which is used as a white pigment in products such as toothpaste, is derived from which mineral?
questions.explanation: Titanium dioxide is obtained mainly from the titanium minerals ilmenite (FeTiO₃) and rutile.

questions.text: Soorya Classical Dance Festival is held in , __________ for 10 days every year.
questions.explanation: The Soorya Classical Dance Festival is held every year in Thiruvananthapuram, the capital of Kerala.

questions.text: Kanaka Raju was awarded Padma Shri in 2021 for contribution to which of the following dance forms?
questions.explanation: Kanaka Raju of Telangana received the Padma Shri in 2021 for Gussadi, the dance of the Raj Gond community.

questions.text: The electromagnetic spectrum describes the full range of light that is generally divided into ________ regions of wavelength and in the order of increasing energy and frequency.
questions.explanation: The seven regions, in order of increasing energy and frequency, are radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays.

questions.text: Which artist’s musical album is titled ‘Land of Gold’?
questions.explanation: 'Land of Gold' (2016) is an album by the sitar player Anoushka Shankar.

questions.text: Who among the following is the author of the famous classic ‘Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland’?
questions.explanation: 'Alice's Adventures in Wonderland' (1865) was written by Lewis Carroll, the pen name of Charles Dodgson.

questions.text: Sandalwood is found in which type of forests in India?
questions.explanation: NCERT lists sandalwood among the trees of the tropical deciduous forests, with teak, sal, shisham and khair.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. The South Indian dish was “approved by the guests” as it was tasty.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'accepted by the visitors', the only option that keeps the sense of 'approved by the guests': a dish is not 'gratified', and 'doomed' and 'condemned' contradict 'tasty'. The original wording is itself acceptable, but no 'no improvement' option is offered.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. She's been off work with __________ stomach.
questions.explanation: 'An upset stomach' is the usual phrase for a stomach disorder.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Rohan is _______ self-sufficient man who needs no assistance.
questions.explanation: 'Self-sufficient' begins with a consonant sound, and the man is not one already identified: 'a self-sufficient man'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'accommodation', with a double 'c' and a double 'm'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Suffice
questions.explanation: To 'suffice' is to be enough, to satisfy a need; its opposite among the options is 'dissatisfy'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Opulence
questions.explanation: 'Opulence' is great wealth or luxury: 'prosperity'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Back out
questions.explanation: To 'back out' of something is to withdraw from a promise or arrangement.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Suchitra will have / to wait another month / before she received / any reply to her letter.
questions.explanation: The main clause is in the future ('will have to wait'), so the time clause takes the simple present: 'before she receives'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. My mom told me “to have cleaning up” the kitchen before I go outside.
questions.explanation: 'Tell someone to' is followed by the base form of the verb, and 'clean up' (make tidy) keeps the original meaning: 'told me to clean up the kitchen'. To 'clean out' is to empty something, such as a cupboard.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. You are “so efficient as he”
questions.explanation: An affirmative comparison takes 'as … as'; 'so … as' is used mainly after a negative. 'As efficient as him' is the only option with 'as … as' (formal English also has 'as efficient as he').

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Comparing apples with oranges
options: Comparison between two kinds of fruits
questions.explanation: 'Comparing apples with oranges' is comparing two things too different to be fairly compared.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Their new house costed them _______ hundred and fifty-six thousand pounds.
questions.explanation: 'A hundred' means one hundred: 'a hundred and fifty-six thousand pounds'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word in the given sentence. The new software provides a perfect solution to the complex issues “pertaining” to pick up and delivery.
questions.explanation: 'Pertaining to' means relating or referring to.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. Shrija “enquired about his daughter’s reputation.”
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'asked about his daughter's character': 'enquired about' means 'asked about', and character is close to reputation. One does not 'assess about', 'condemn about' or 'poke about' something in this sense; the original wording is itself acceptable.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A.In its most humble function, it is a necessary guide without which progress from place to place would be a ceaseless experiment; it is a sustenance without which organised society would be impossible, thus the Road moves and controls all history. B.The Road is one of the great fundamental institutions of mankind. C.It is the Road which controls the development of strategies and fixes the sites of battles. It is the Road that gives framework to all economic development. It is the Road which is the channel of all trade, and, what is more important, of all ideas. D.Not only is the Road one of the great human institutions because it is fundamental to social existence, but also because its varied effects appear in every department of the State. It is the Road which determines the sites of many cities and the growth and nourishment of all.
questions.explanation: B introduces the Road as a fundamental institution, D explains why it is one, C lists what it controls, and A ends with the conclusion 'thus the Road moves and controls all history': BDCA.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A sudden unsteady movement ; a stagger
questions.explanation: To 'lurch' is to make a sudden unsteady movement, to stagger. A lupin is a plant, a lugger a small sailing boat and a lumen a unit of light.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. His poems are “recondite” in subject matter
questions.explanation: 'Recondite' means obscure, known only to a few; its opposite is 'simple'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'absent'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In everyday language, the phrase ‘sleepwalking’ can be used (1)____________ informally and symbolically to describe a lack of energy or attention. However, for (2)_________ infants and adults, sleepwalking is a genuine disorder with serious (3)___________. Sleepwalking, also known as somnambulism, is a sleep-related behaviour condition that causes people to walk or execute other (4)___________ acts while they are still partly sleeping. It is more (5)____________ in children than in adults, and it is more likely to develop if a person has a family history of the illness, is sleep deprived or has many nightly awakenings.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'Both informally and symbolically': 'both' pairs with 'and' to join the two adverbs.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In everyday language, the phrase ‘sleepwalking’ can be used (1)____________ informally and symbolically to describe a lack of energy or attention. However, for (2)_________ infants and adults, sleepwalking is a genuine disorder with serious (3)___________. Sleepwalking, also known as somnambulism, is a sleep-related behaviour condition that causes people to walk or execute other (4)___________ acts while they are still partly sleeping. It is more (5)____________ in children than in adults, and it is more likely to develop if a person has a family history of the illness, is sleep deprived or has many nightly awakenings.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: A genuine disorder has serious 'repercussions', that is consequences; 'impetus', 'impulsions' and 'causes' do not fit.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In everyday language, the phrase ‘sleepwalking’ can be used (1)____________ informally and symbolically to describe a lack of energy or attention. However, for (2)_________ infants and adults, sleepwalking is a genuine disorder with serious (3)___________. Sleepwalking, also known as somnambulism, is a sleep-related behaviour condition that causes people to walk or execute other (4)___________ acts while they are still partly sleeping. It is more (5)____________ in children than in adults, and it is more likely to develop if a person has a family history of the illness, is sleep deprived or has many nightly awakenings.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: Sleepwalkers walk or carry out other 'complicated' acts while still partly asleep.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In everyday language, the phrase ‘sleepwalking’ can be used (1)____________ informally and symbolically to describe a lack of energy or attention. However, for (2)_________ infants and adults, sleepwalking is a genuine disorder with serious (3)___________. Sleepwalking, also known as somnambulism, is a sleep-related behaviour condition that causes people to walk or execute other (4)___________ acts while they are still partly sleeping. It is more (5)____________ in children than in adults, and it is more likely to develop if a person has a family history of the illness, is sleep deprived or has many nightly awakenings.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: It is more 'prevalent', that is more common, in children than in adults.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'CHILD' is written as ‘6169248' and 'GUEST' is written as '142153840'. How will 'BOOK' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Consonants are written as twice their alphabet positions and vowels as their positions: C, H, I, L, D → 6, 16, 9, 24, 8 and G, U, E, S, T → 14, 21, 5, 38, 40. So B, O, O, K → 4, 15, 15, 22: 4151522.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 4 : 80 :: 7 : 392 :: 5 : ?
questions.explanation: Each second number is the square of the first times one more than it: 4² × 5 = 80 and 7² × 8 = 392. So 5² × 6 = 150.

questions.text: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series to make it logically complete? YXZ, VUW, SRT, POQ, ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places back: Y, V, S, P, M; X, U, R, O, L; Z, W, T, Q, N. The next cluster is MLN.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 4, 8, 5, ?, 15, 90

Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. GREATLY : ERGAYLT :: MIXTURE : XIMTERU :: TROUBLE : ?
questions.explanation: The first three letters are reversed, the middle letter stays and the last three are reversed: GRE A TLY → ERG A YLT and MIX T URE → XIM T ERU. So TRO U BLE → ORT U ELB: ORTUELB.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? NHMS, HNOU, ?, HNSY, NHUA
questions.explanation: The first two letters alternate NH, HN, NH, HN, NH; the third letters move 2 places forward (M, O, Q, S, U) and so do the fourth (S, U, W, Y, A). The missing cluster is NHQW.

questions.text: Three Statements are given followed by Three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All towels are cloths. No cloth is a blanket. Some blankets are cushions. Conclusions: I. Some towels are cushions. II. No cushion is a cloth. III. No towel is a blanket.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Both conclusions I and III follow.
questions.explanation: All towels are cloths and no cloth is a blanket, so no towel is a blanket (III). Nothing links towels or cloths to cushions with certainty, so I and II do not follow.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 43*11*4*71*16
Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 57*35*7*14*2*80

The second number in the given number-pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number-pairs EXCEPT one. Find that odd number-pair.
questions.explanation: In 4 : 5, 9 : 6 and 36 : 9 the second number is the square root of the first plus 3 (2 + 3, 3 + 3, 6 + 3). For 16 it would be 4 + 3 = 7, not 8, so 16 : 8 is the odd pair.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in an English dictionary. 1.Resolve 2.Rodent 3.Resonant 4.Return 5.Respond 6.Rigidity
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Resolve (1), Resonant (3), Respond (5), Return (4), Rigidity (6), Rodent (2). 'Resol' comes before 'Reson', and both before 'Resp'.

questions.text: The second number in the given number pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number pairs except one. Find that odd number pair.
questions.explanation: In 53 : 2916, 23 : 576 and 19 : 400 the second number is the square of one more than the first (54², 24², 20²). 42² = 1764, not 1765, so 41 : 1765 is the odd pair.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 13, 25, 38, 62, 88, 124, 163, 211, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 12, 13, 24, 26, 36, 39, 48: multiples of 12 and of 13 in turn. The next difference is 4 × 13 = 52: 211 + 52 = 263.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fourth term in the same way as the first term is related to the second term and the fifth term is related to the sixth term 7 : 58 :: ? : 370 :: 12 : 153
questions.explanation: Each second number is the square of the first plus 9: 7² + 9 = 58 and 12² + 9 = 153. 370 − 9 = 361 = 19², so the missing number is 19.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and fourth term related to third term. 13 : 130 :: 15 : 180 :: 27 : ?
questions.explanation: Each number is multiplied by 3 less than itself: 13 × 10 = 130 and 15 × 12 = 180. So 27 × 24 = 648.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fourth term in the same way as the first term is related to the second term and the fifth term is related to the sixth term 64 : 320 :: ? : 70 :: 22 : 110
questions.explanation: The second number is five times the first: 64 × 5 = 320 and 22 × 5 = 110. So 70 ÷ 5 = 14.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'RAIN' is written as 'MHZQ' and ‘COAT’ is written as ‘SZNB’. How will 'ROLE' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The word is written in reverse and each letter moves one place back: RAIN → NIAR → MHZQ and COAT → TAOC → SZNB. So ROLE → ELOR → DKNQ.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'SITAR' is written as 'RHSZQ' and ‘BANJO’ is written as ‘AZMIN’. How will 'TABLA' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one place back: SITAR → RHSZQ and BANJO → AZMIN. So TABLA → SZAKZ.

questions.text: The average runs scored by Sunil in 17 innings is 37. What is his score in the 17th inning, thereby, increasing his average score by 9 runs?
questions.explanation: After 17 innings the total is 17 × 37 = 629. Before the 17th inning the average was 37 − 9 = 28, a total of 16 × 28 = 448. The 17th inning scored 629 − 448 = 181.

questions.text: In a company, there are only two types of employees: workers and officers. The average monthly salary of an officer is ₹78,000 more than the combined average monthly salary of an employee, while the combined average monthly salary of an employee is ₹42,000 more than the average monthly salary of a worker. What percentage of all the employees are officers?
questions.explanation: Let officers be a fraction f of the staff and the overall average A. Officers average A + 78,000 and workers A − 42,000, so 78,000f = 42,000(1 − f): 1,20,000f = 42,000 and f = 0.35, that is 35%.

questions.text: What is the volume of a right circular cylinder whose curved surface area is 12 π cm² and the circumference of its base is 4 π cm?
questions.explanation: 2πr = 4π gives r = 2 cm, and 2πrh = 12π gives h = 3 cm. V = πr²h = π × 4 × 3 = 12π cm³.

questions.text: The curved surface area of a right circular cone of radius 28 cm is 4664 cm². What is the slant height of the cone?(Use π=22/7)
questions.explanation: Curved surface area = πrl: (22/7) × 28 × l = 88l = 4664, so l = 53 cm.

questions.text: The number 36 is increased by a certain percentage and becomes 63. Calculate that percentage.
questions.explanation: The increase is 63 − 36 = 27, and 27/36 × 100 = 75%.

questions.text: Find the third proportion to 16 and 24.
If a + b = 25, then (a – 15)³ + (b – 10)³ is:
If p³ + 3p² + 3p = 26, then the value of p² + 2p is:
questions.explanation: Adding 1 to both sides: p³ + 3p² + 3p + 1 = (p + 1)³ = 27, so p = 2. Then p² + 2p = 4 + 4 = 8.

questions.text: In a triangle ABC, CA is produced to P, ∠ BAP=126°. If ∠B : ∠C = 5 : 2, the degree measures of ∠B and ∠C are respectively:
questions.explanation: The exterior angle ∠BAP equals the sum of the interior opposite angles: ∠B + ∠C = 126°. In the ratio 5 : 2, ∠B = 90° and ∠C = 36°.

questions.text: When the price of a watch was reduced by 20%, the number of watches sold is increased by 40%. What was the effect on the sales in percentage?
questions.explanation: Sales value = price × number sold: 0.8 × 1.4 = 1.12, a 12% increase.

questions.text: Simplify the following : 6 × {6 of (6 + 6)} ÷ {(6 ÷ 6) × (600% of 6)}
A book is sold for ₹1,554 by allowing a discount of 26% on its marked price. Find the marked price of the book.
questions.explanation: After a 26% discount the selling price is 74% of the marked price: 1,554/0.74 = ₹2,100.

questions.text: Malay walks around a circular field at the rate of 7 rounds per hour,while Neha runs around it at the rate of 11 rounds per hour. They start in the same direction from the same point at 02:45 p.m. They shall first cross each other at:
questions.explanation: Going the same way, Neha gains 11 − 7 = 4 rounds an hour on Malay, so she first passes him after 1/4 hour, 15 minutes: at 03:00 p.m.

questions.text: A can do a piece of work alone in 96 days and B can do it alone in 104 days. In how many days can the duo, working together, complete the work?
The Earth makes a complete rotation about its axis in 24 hours. Through what angle will it turn in 3 hours 30 minutes?
questions.explanation: The Earth turns 360° in 24 hours, 15° an hour. In 3.5 hours it turns 3.5 × 15° = 52.5°.

questions.text: What is the compound interest on ₹20,000 for 9 months at the rate of 4% per annum, when interest is compounded quarterly?
questions.explanation: Compounded quarterly at 1% for 3 quarters: 20,000 × (1.01³ − 1) = 20,000 × 0.030301 = ₹606.02.

questions.text: The marked price of a shirt is ₹2,150. Let two successive discounts offered by the store be 10% and ‘x%’. If the selling price of the shirt is ₹1,505, then calculate the value of ‘x’. [Give your answer correct to two decimal places.]
questions.explanation: After 10% off, 2,150 × 0.9 = ₹1,935. The second discount takes it to ₹1,505: x = 430/1,935 × 100 = 22.22%.

questions.text: Romesh opened a fixed deposits account in his bank for 3 years by depositing ₹80,000.The bank has promised to pay him compound interest annually at the rate of 7% per annum. What is the maturity value of his FDR? (Nearest to a ₹)
If the number 5X8146Y is divisible by 88, then what is the value of X?
questions.explanation: 88 = 8 × 11. For 8, the last three digits 46Y must be divisible by 8, so Y = 4 (464). For 11, (5 + 8 + 4 + 4) − (X + 1 + 6) = 14 − X must be a multiple of 11, so X = 3.

questions.text: A man bought a piece of land for ₹48,000. He sold two-fifth of it at a loss of 10%. At what gain percentage (rounded off to 1 decimal place) should he sell the remaining land to earn an overall profit of 42%?
questions.explanation: Two-fifths cost ₹19,200 and sold for ₹17,280. For a 42% profit the whole must fetch ₹68,160, so the remaining three-fifths (cost ₹28,800) must sell for ₹50,880: a gain of 22,080/28,800 = 76.7%.

questions.text: Ustad Bade Ghulam Ali Khan is also known as ______.
questions.explanation: Ustad Bade Ghulam Ali Khan, the Patiala gharana vocalist, is often called the 'Tansen of the 20th century'. He was a singer, not a sitarist, and received the Padma Bhushan, not the Bharat Ratna; Alla Rakha was a tabla player.

questions.text: In which track and field event is the hop used?
questions.explanation: The triple jump is a hop, a step and a jump in sequence.

questions.text: In December 2021, who among the following inaugurated the ‘Bharat Darshan Park’ in Delhi, which has replicas of major monuments from across the country created by a group of artists?
questions.explanation: Union Home Minister Amit Shah opened the Bharat Darshan Park, built by the South Delhi Municipal Corporation with replicas made largely from scrap, in late December 2021.

questions.text: Which of the following books is an autobiography of the Indian novelist Khushwant Singh?
questions.explanation: Khushwant Singh's autobiography is 'Truth, Love & A Little Malice' (2002).

questions.text: A batsman can be given out in_________ ways.
questions.explanation: Traditionally a batsman can be out in ten ways: bowled, caught, leg before wicket, stumped, run out, hit wicket, handled the ball, hit the ball twice, obstructing the field and timed out. (Since 2017 the Laws count handling the ball as obstructing the field, leaving nine, which is not an option.)

questions.text: The Sangeet Natak Akademi is a body working under which of the following ministries of the Government of India?
questions.explanation: The Sangeet Natak Akademi, the national academy of music, dance and drama, is an autonomous body under the Ministry of Culture.

questions.text: In cell biology, what is a large double-membraned organelle that is sometimes referred to as the ‘central unit’ of the cell because it contains the chromosomes that bear genetic material?
questions.explanation: The nucleus, enclosed by a double membrane (the nuclear envelope), holds the chromosomes and controls the cell's activities.

questions.text: Lemon juice contains ________ which when mixed with baking soda reacts to form carbon dioxide and sodium citrate causing the liquid to fizz and bubble.
questions.explanation: Lemon juice contains citric acid, which reacts with baking soda (sodium hydrogencarbonate) to give carbon dioxide, sodium citrate and water.

questions.text: Rukmini Devi Arundale, awarded with Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1957, was a _________ dancer.
questions.explanation: Rukmini Devi Arundale, who founded Kalakshetra in Madras in 1936, was a Bharatanatyam dancer who led the revival of the form.

questions.text: ‘The Private life of an Indian Prince’ is a novel written by whom among the following authors?
questions.explanation: 'The Private Life of an Indian Prince' (1953) is a novel by Mulk Raj Anand.

questions.text: The valleys lying between the lesser Himalayas and Shivaliks are called:
questions.explanation: NCERT calls the longitudinal valleys between the Lesser Himalaya and the Shiwaliks 'duns': Dehra Dun, Kotli Dun and Patli Dun among them.

questions.text: When was the Lalit Kala Akademi established?
questions.explanation: The Lalit Kala Akademi, the national academy of the visual arts, was set up in 1954.

questions.text: The micro finance movement in India was formally launched on a pilot basis by the _______________in __________.
options: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD); 1992
National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD); 1994
Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI); 1994
Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI); 1992
questions.explanation: NABARD launched the Self-Help Group-Bank Linkage Programme as a pilot in 1992, aiming to link 500 self-help groups with banks.

questions.text: When do electrons move for the flow of charges in a conducting metallic wire?
options: When there is no difference of electric pressure
Only if there is a difference of electric pressure
questions.explanation: Electrons flow along a conductor only when there is a potential difference, the 'difference of electric pressure', across it, such as a cell provides.

questions.text: A Minister who for any period of ______ is not a member of either House of Parliament shall at the expiration of that period cease to be a Minister.
questions.explanation: Under Article 75(5) a Minister who is not a member of either House for six consecutive months ceases to be a Minister at the end of that period.

questions.text: A balanced diet takes care of all the following aspects, EXCEPT one. Identify the aspect.
options: Meets the RDA for all nutrients
Includes a variety of food items
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'Promotes a healthy mind': the other three describe what a balanced diet is, a variety of foods supplying every nutrient in the right proportions to meet the recommended dietary allowance (RDA). Good nutrition does also help the mind, so the key rests on that definition.

questions.text: Which of the following novels was written by the Indian author Anuradha Roy?
options: The Illicit Happiness of Other People
questions.explanation: Anuradha Roy wrote 'Sleeping on Jupiter' (2015), which won the DSC Prize for South Asian Literature. 'Midnight's Children' is Salman Rushdie's and 'The Illicit Happiness of Other People' Manu Joseph's.

questions.text: Which state of India launched the ‘Ashirbad’ scheme for education, health and maintenance of Covid orphans in June 2021?
questions.explanation: Odisha launched 'Ashirbad' on 20 June 2021 for children who had lost one or both parents, or the family's earning member, to Covid-19.

questions.text: As per statistics published by National Crime Records Bureau for 2020, which state tops in total number of crime incidences against senior citizens (60 years and above)?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Maharashtra as the state with the most cases of crime against senior citizens in NCRB's 'Crime in India 2020'.

questions.text: Ustad Bismillah Khan is best known for playing which of the following instruments?
questions.explanation: Ustad Bismillah Khan, Bharat Ratna (2001), was the great master of the shehnai.

questions.text: Sangeet Natak Akademi Award was constituted in which of the following years?
questions.explanation: The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (Akademi Puraskar) was instituted in 1952, the year the Akademi was set up.

questions.text: Pandit Ananda Gopal Bandopadhyay was a _________ player of the Banaras gharana.
questions.explanation: Pandit Ananda Gopal Bandopadhyay was a tabla player trained in the style of the Banaras gharana.

questions.text: How is food stored in brown algae?
options: In the form of complex carbohydrates that may be in the form of laminarin or mannitol
In the form of complex lipids
In the form of oil droplets
questions.explanation: In brown algae (Phaeophyceae) food is stored as complex carbohydrates, laminarin or mannitol.

questions.text: Who among the following is credited with building Delhi’s Lāl Quilā (Red Fort)?
questions.explanation: Shah Jahan built the Red Fort between 1639 and 1648 as the palace of his new capital, Shahjahanabad.

questions.text: Select the correct homonym from the given options to fill in the blank. The police returned to the________of the crime.
questions.explanation: The police returned to the 'scene', the place of the crime; 'seen' sounds the same but means something else.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in the brackets to fill in the blank. The western side of the country has some ____________ (vacant) islands to explore.
questions.explanation: 'Vacant' islands are empty of people: 'uninhabited'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'facilitation'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. I goes / to the school / every day / irrespective of the weather.
questions.explanation: 'I' takes 'go', not 'goes': 'I go to the school every day'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. Several literary pieces of the Old English period are written by authors “whose names are not known”.
questions.explanation: A work whose author's name is not known is 'anonymous'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In this scene, a close-up shot was taken by the cameraman “for display the emotions.”
options: in order to display the emotions
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'in order to display the emotions': purpose takes 'in order to' or 'to' with the verb, not 'for display'. 'To show emotions' is also grammatical, but it changes the sentence's own words and drops 'the'.

questions.text: Spot the error in the given sentence and select the correct sentence from the options given. Fatima and Sana has both taken the vaccine.
options: Fatima and Sana was both taken the vaccine.
Fatima and Sana have both taken the vaccine.
Fatima and Sana were both taken the vaccine
Fatima and Sana are both taken the vaccine.
questions.explanation: Two subjects joined by 'and' take a plural verb: 'Fatima and Sana have both taken the vaccine'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. I am not sure / if the red car / in the parking slot / is your.
questions.explanation: The possessive pronoun standing alone is 'yours': 'is yours'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underline segment in the given sentence. I “called of” an explanation for his rude behaviour.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'called out': to 'call someone out' is to challenge them openly over their conduct, the closest of the options to demanding an explanation. The natural phrase is 'called for', which is not among the options; 'called in', 'called into' and plain 'called' make no sense with 'an explanation'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Donkey’s years
questions.explanation: 'Donkey's years' means a very long time.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Disseminate
questions.explanation: To 'disseminate' information is to spread it widely: to 'circulate' it.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. My boss keeps telling me / all the time / that money / doesn’t grows on trees.
questions.explanation: After 'does not' the verb takes its base form: 'money doesn't grow on trees'.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A.These great leaders never escaped from their responsibilities and challenges because they knew greatness would come through great responsibilities. B.Leadership is one of the crucial elements in the field of management because most of the time success or failure depends on the managerial skills of a leader. C.There are not many leaders in the present world because, unlike ancient times, people are not ready to accept responsibilities. D.Ancient India produced millions of people with leadership because it is an inner part of Indian culture to create leaders in every sphere of life. Chandragupta Mourya, Gandhi, Buddha, Bose etc. were leaders on this soil.
questions.explanation: B introduces leadership in management, C says there are few leaders today, D contrasts this with ancient India's many leaders, and A ('These great leaders') refers back to those named in D: BCDA.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Go to the wall
questions.explanation: To 'go to the wall' is to fail, especially of a business that is ruined.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Ecstasy
questions.explanation: 'Ecstasy' is overwhelming happiness: 'bliss'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. I would like to thank you “for your coming out” tonight.
questions.explanation: After 'thank you', 'for coming out' is enough; 'your' only repeats 'you'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. People “was empty out of” the malls and roads.
questions.explanation: 'People' is plural and the action was in progress: 'People were emptying out of the malls and roads'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. personification gives (1) ________ qualities to non-living things or ideas. Imagery is a language used by poets, novelists and other writers to create images in the mind of the (2) _______. Rhyme scheme is the (3) ___________ that is created at the end of the lines of poetry. Irony is defined as when (4) _________ meaning is completely (5) __________ from the literal meaning.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Personification gives 'human' qualities to non-living things or ideas.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. personification gives (1) ________ qualities to non-living things or ideas. Imagery is a language used by poets, novelists and other writers to create images in the mind of the (2) _______. Rhyme scheme is the (3) ___________ that is created at the end of the lines of poetry. Irony is defined as when (4) _________ meaning is completely (5) __________ from the literal meaning.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The writers' imagery creates pictures in the mind of the 'readers'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. personification gives (1) ________ qualities to non-living things or ideas. Imagery is a language used by poets, novelists and other writers to create images in the mind of the (2) _______. Rhyme scheme is the (3) ___________ that is created at the end of the lines of poetry. Irony is defined as when (4) _________ meaning is completely (5) __________ from the literal meaning.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: A rhyme scheme is the 'pattern' of rhymes at the ends of the lines of a poem.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. personification gives (1) ________ qualities to non-living things or ideas. Imagery is a language used by poets, novelists and other writers to create images in the mind of the (2) _______. Rhyme scheme is the (3) ___________ that is created at the end of the lines of poetry. Irony is defined as when (4) _________ meaning is completely (5) __________ from the literal meaning.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: In irony the 'actual', intended meaning is not the literal one.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. personification gives (1) ________ qualities to non-living things or ideas. Imagery is a language used by poets, novelists and other writers to create images in the mind of the (2) _______. Rhyme scheme is the (3) ___________ that is created at the end of the lines of poetry. Irony is defined as when (4) _________ meaning is completely (5) __________ from the literal meaning.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Irony is when the actual meaning is completely 'different' from the literal one; 'similar' and 'parallel' would take 'to' and give the opposite sense.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? CFJK, JMQR, QTXY, ?, EHLM
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 7 places forward from one cluster to the next, wrapping round after Z: C → J → Q → X → E, F → M → T → A → H, J → Q → X → E → L and K → R → Y → F → M. So ? = XAEF.

questions.text: The second number in the given number pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number pairs, except one. Find that odd number pair.
questions.explanation: In the other pairs the second number is the cube of the first minus the first: 5³ − 5 = 120, 4³ − 4 = 60 and 6³ − 6 = 210. For 7 this gives 343 − 7 = 336, not 337.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. ABSENT : ANESBT :: NOTIFY : NFITOY :: LAUNCH : ?
questions.explanation: The first and last letters stay and the four between them are reversed: A(BSEN)T → ANESBT and N(OTIF)Y → NFITOY. So L(AUNC)H → LCNUAH.

questions.text: The second number in the given number pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number pairs except one. Find that odd number pair.
questions.explanation: In the other pairs the second number is the first times two less than itself: 53 × 51 = 2703, 24 × 22 = 528 and 68 × 66 = 4488. 47 × 45 = 2115, not 2116.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'BASKET' is coded as ‘211911520’ and ‘BOX’ is coded as ’21524’. How will 'COVER' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is written as its place in the alphabet: B 2, A 1, S 19, K 11, E 5, T 20. COVER → 3, 15, 22, 5, 18 = 31522518.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'TRAIN' is written as 'WUDLQ' and ‘ROAD’ is written as ‘URDG’. How will 'TAXI' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places forward: T → W, R → U, A → D, I → L, N → Q. So TAXI → WDAL (X wraps round to A).

questions.text: The second number in the given number pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number pairs EXCEPT one. Find that odd number pair.
questions.explanation: The second number is 3.5 times the first: 48 × 3.5 = 168, 52 × 3.5 = 182 and 26 × 3.5 = 91. 34 × 3.5 = 119, not 118.

questions.text: If 01 March 2012 was Thursday, then what was the day of the week on 01 February 2016?
questions.explanation: From 1 March 2012 to 1 March 2015 are three years of 365 days (3 odd days), and from 1 March 2015 to 1 February 2016 are 337 days (1 odd day). Four days on from Thursday is Monday.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 57*35*7*14*2*43
Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and fourth term related to third term. 786:7 :: 645:5 :: 282 :?
questions.explanation: The second number is the sum of the first number's digits divided by 3: (7 + 8 + 6)/3 = 7 and (6 + 4 + 5)/3 = 5. Likewise (2 + 8 + 2)/3 = 4.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 9 : 109 :: 7 : 71 :: 13 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is n × (n + 3) + 1: 9 × 12 + 1 = 109 and 7 × 10 + 1 = 71. Likewise 13 × 16 + 1 = 209.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'MATHS' is written as '13320819' and 'HINDI' is written as '82714427'. How will 'PHYSICS' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Consonants are written as their place in the alphabet and vowels as three times it: MATHS → 13, 3, 20, 8, 19 and HINDI → 8, 27, 14, 4, 27. PHYSICS → 16, 8, 25, 19, 27, 3, 19 = 168251927319.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 45, 55, 72, 97, 131, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 10, 17, 25, 34, growing by 7, 8 and 9; the next grows by 10 to 44: 131 + 44 = 175.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fourth term in the same way as the first term is related to the second term and the fifth term is related to the sixth term 8 : 512 :: ? : 1728 :: 18 : 5832
questions.explanation: Each second number is the cube of the first: 8³ = 512 and 18³ = 5832. So 12³ = 1728.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that, when sequentially placed from left to right in the blanks below, will complete the letter series. m n _ m n _ o m _ m_ nn o m _ m m _ n o
options: m n n m n n
o n n m n n
m n o m n n
m n n m o o
questions.explanation: With m, n, n, m, n, n in the blanks the block mnmmnno repeats: mnmmnno mnmmnno mnmmnno.

questions.text: Which two numbers, from amongst the given options, should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 15 – 4 + (8×6)÷16 + 9×3 – 7 = 31
If 20 February 2013 was Wednesday, then what was the day of the week on 28 February 2016?
questions.explanation: From 20 February 2013 to 20 February 2016 are three years of 365 days (29 February 2016 comes later), so 20 February 2016 is 3 days on: Saturday. 28 February is 8 days after that: Sunday.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 2, 22, 32, 42, 57, 87, 162, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 20, 10, 10, 15, 30, 75, each the one before times 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2 and 2.5. The next is 75 × 3 = 225: 162 + 225 = 387.

questions.text: The marked price of a mobile phone is ₹36,000.A shopkeeper gives a discount of 11% on the marked price. Further, if a customer purchases it through credit card the discount increases by 15%.Pooja purchases it through the credit card. How much does she pay?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives ₹30,600, which reads the card offer as raising the discount to 15% in all: 36,000 × 0.85 = ₹30,600. Read literally, as 15 points more (26%), a further 15% off, or 15% more than 11% (12.65%), the price would be ₹26,640, ₹27,234 or ₹31,446, none of them an option.

questions.text: Suraj travels 124 km at a speed of 31 km/h by bus, 96 km at a speed of 16 km/h using a car, and another 105 km at 7 km/h by car. Find his average speed for the entire distance travelled.
questions.explanation: The three legs take 124/31 = 4, 96/16 = 6 and 105/7 = 15 hours: 325 km in 25 hours, an average of 13 km/h.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 33?
questions.explanation: 33 = 3 × 11. 185592 has digit sum 30, a multiple of 3, and its alternate digits sum to 1 + 5 + 9 = 15 and 8 + 5 + 2 = 15, so it is divisible by 11: 185592 = 33 × 5624. The other numbers' digit sums (28, 22, 17) are not multiples of 3.

questions.text: A mobile is marked at a price 25% above its cost price. At what discount percentage should it be sold to make a 10% profit?
questions.explanation: With cost 100 the marked price is 125 and the selling price 110: a discount of 15 on 125, or 12%.

questions.text: The average weight of 52 girls is 47 kg. What will be the sum of their weights?
questions.explanation: Sum = average × number = 47 × 52 = 2444 kg.

questions.text: As air is pumped into a spherical balloon, its radius increases from 7 cm to 14 cm. Find the ratio of volume of the balloon's in both circumstances.
questions.explanation: Volume goes with the cube of the radius: (7/14)³ = 1/8, so 1 : 8.

questions.text: The average age of a man and his son is 56 years. The ratio of their ages is 11 : 5. What is the son's age?
questions.explanation: Their ages total 2 × 56 = 112 years, in 11 + 5 = 16 parts of 7 years: the son is 5 × 7 = 35.

questions.text: A loan is to be repaid in two equal yearly instalments. If the rate of interest is 10% per annum, compounded annually, and each instalment is ₹6,897, then find the total interest charged.
questions.explanation: The loan is the present value of the instalments: 6,897/1.1 + 6,897/1.21 = 6,270 + 5,700 = ₹11,970. In all ₹13,794 is repaid, so the interest is ₹1,824.

questions.text: Calculate the area of the quadrilateral formed with the vertices (-3,2),(5,4),(7,-6) and (-5,-4).
questions.explanation: By the shoelace formula, area = ½|(−12 − 10) + (−30 − 28) + (−28 − 30) + (−10 − 12)| = ½ × 160 = 80 square units.

questions.text: A shopkeeper normally makes a profit of 20% in a certain transaction; he weighs 900 g instead of 1 kg, due to an issue with the weighing machine. If he charges 10% less than what he normally charges, what is his actual profit or loss percentage?
questions.explanation: Take 1 kg to cost ₹100, normally sold at ₹120. He now charges 10% less, ₹108, for 900 g that cost him ₹90: a profit of 18/90 = 20%.

questions.text: Admissions into a commerce course of a university increase by 5% every year. If the number of admissions presently is 2400 into that course, after three years, the number of admissions is Nearest to an integer :
The fourth proportional to 5, 8 and 30 is:
A man and a boy together can do a certain amount of digging in 24 days. Their speeds in digging are in the ratio of 4 :3. How many days will the boy take to complete the work if engaged alone?
questions.explanation: The man and the boy do 4 and 3 units a day, 7 together, so the work is 7 × 24 = 168 units. The boy alone takes 168/3 = 56 days.

questions.text: If the circumradius of an equilateral triangle is 18 cm, then the measure of its in-radius is:
questions.explanation: In an equilateral triangle the centroid divides each median 2 : 1, so the circumradius is twice the in-radius: 18/2 = 9 cm.

questions.text: In a class of 45 students, there are 20 girls who scored an average of 42 marks in a test of 50 marks. If the class average is 36, what are the average marks of the boys?
questions.explanation: The class total is 45 × 36 = 1,620 and the girls' is 20 × 42 = 840, so the 25 boys scored 780: an average of 31.20.

questions.text: A number is increased by 10% and then the increased number is decreased by 20%. The net increase or decrease is:
questions.explanation: 1.1 × 0.8 = 0.88 of the number: a net decrease of 12%.

questions.text: Who among the following cricketers won the orange cap in IPL 2021?
questions.explanation: Ruturaj Gaikwad of Chennai Super Kings won the Orange Cap for the most runs (635) in IPL 2021.

questions.text: Which type of carbohydrate CANNOT be broken down by the GI tract, does not provide energy, but helps the body get rid of wastes and keeps the intestinal tract healthy?
questions.explanation: Dietary fibre is a carbohydrate the gut cannot digest: it gives no energy, but adds bulk that helps clear wastes and keeps the intestines healthy.

questions.text: Who among the following players wrote his autobiography entitled ‘The Race of My Life’?
questions.explanation: 'The Race of My Life' (2013) is the autobiography of the sprinter Milkha Singh, written with his daughter Sonia Sanwalka.

questions.text: Who among the following came up with his own style of dance called ‘Hi-dance’, which he later rechristened it and called it 'Creative dance'?
questions.explanation: Uday Shankar, a pioneer of modern Indian dance, blended Indian classical and folk dance with European theatre in a style called 'Hi-dance', which he later named 'Creative dance'.

questions.text: Who among the following Bharatanatyam exponents received the ‘Chevalier of Arts and Letters award’ from the Government of France in 2004?
questions.explanation: The Bharatanatyam dancer Alarmel Valli was made a Chevalier of Arts and Letters by the French government in 2004.

questions.text: Who was the recipient of Nobel prize for literature in 2021?
questions.explanation: The Tanzanian-born novelist Abdulrazak Gurnah won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2021. Bob Dylan (2016), Peter Handke (2019) and Louise Glück (2020) won it earlier.

questions.text: S Balachander a famous musician from India is known for playing which of the following instruments?
questions.explanation: S. Balachander was a celebrated veena player of Carnatic music.

questions.text: The Kalaimamani awards are given in which of the following states of India?
questions.explanation: The Kalaimamani awards are Tamil Nadu's honours for artists, given by the Tamil Nadu Eyal Isai Nataka Mandram.

questions.text: Which Indian sportsperson has been nominated for the prestigious Laureus World Breakthrough of the Year Award 2022?
questions.explanation: Neeraj Chopra, the Tokyo 2020 javelin champion, was nominated for the Laureus World Breakthrough of the Year Award 2022.

questions.text: What is the mode of adaptation done by aquatic plants and animals where the osmotic concentration of the body fluids changes with that of the ambient air and water osmotic concentration?
questions.explanation: Conformers cannot hold their internal state constant: in aquatic conformers the osmotic concentration of the body fluids changes with that of the surrounding water. Regulators keep it constant.

questions.text: Who among the following is an Indian Singer of Hindustani Classical Music?
questions.explanation: Shubha Mudgal is a Hindustani classical vocalist. L. Subramaniam and Dwaram Venkataswamy Naidu are Carnatic violinists, and Kishan Maharaj was a tabla player.

questions.text: Which river basin covers an area of 65,145 km², of which about 80% lies in Maharashtra?
questions.explanation: The Tapi rises in Madhya Pradesh's Betul district and flows west to the Arabian Sea; its basin of 65,145 km² lies mostly in Maharashtra.

questions.text: The first regional rural bank set up in India was __________.
questions.explanation: Prathama Grameen Bank, set up at Moradabad (Uttar Pradesh) on 2 October 1975, was India's first regional rural bank.

questions.text: What is the maximum number of players that can be on the field during a football match in a team?
questions.explanation: A football team has 11 players on the field, the goalkeeper included.

questions.text: Which violinist was conferred Pt. Bhimsen Joshi Lifetime Achievement Award for 2021?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives N. Rajam, the Hindustani classical violinist, honoured with the Maharashtra government's Pandit Bhimsen Joshi Lifetime Achievement Award. (Some records list hers as the award for 2020, reported in February 2021.)

questions.text: The first playback song in Hindi Movies was recorded by music directors RC Boral and Pankaj Mullick in which year?
questions.explanation: Playback singing came to Hindi films in 1935 with 'Dhoop Chhaon', whose music was by R.C. Boral and Pankaj Mullick.

questions.text: ______________ government launched Dayanand Social Security Scheme 2022 for senior citizens, single women, disabled persons and HIV/AIDS patients.
questions.explanation: The Dayanand Social Security Scheme is Goa's pension scheme for senior citizens, single women, the disabled and people with HIV/AIDS, named after the state's first Chief Minister, Dayanand Bandodkar.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a federal feature of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The All India Services, common to the Union and the states, are a unitary feature. Dual government, the division of powers and a written constitution are federal features.

questions.text: In 1869, who named a new term ‘Oecologie’that defined the study of the relationship of organisms with their environment?
questions.explanation: The German zoologist Ernst Haeckel coined 'Oekologie', ecology, for the study of organisms' relations with their surroundings. Arthur Tansley later coined 'ecosystem'.

questions.text: In which year was the Board of Control for Cricket in India established
questions.explanation: The Board of Control for Cricket in India was set up in December 1928.

questions.text: Shobana Chandrakumar, a recipient of Padma Shri, is a dancer of which of the following Indian classical dance forms?
questions.explanation: Shobana Chandrakumar, the actor and Padma Shri awardee, is a Bharatanatyam dancer.

questions.text: One of the important minerals for the generation of nuclear energy is:
questions.explanation: Uranium (with thorium) is the fuel of nuclear power; mica and manganese are not fuels, and coal is burnt in thermal power stations.

questions.text: What type of trees are found in the northern central Himalayan range (1801 to 3001 m) and the southern Nilgiri high mountain ranges?
questions.explanation: Oak, juniper and maple are trees of the temperate mountain forests. Kusum, arjun and mulberry, rosewood, mahogany and bamboo, and teak, sal and peepal are trees of the tropical forests of lower land.

questions.text: Which group of animals has a body wall composed of both circular and longitudinal muscle fibres surrounded by a moist, cellular cuticle that is secreted by an epidermal epithelium?
questions.explanation: Annelids, such as earthworms, have a body wall of circular and longitudinal muscle layers under a moist cuticle secreted by the epidermis. Arthropods instead have a hard, jointed exoskeleton of chitin.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Pseudo
questions.explanation: 'Pseudo' means false or pretended; its opposite is 'genuine'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The birds flew / fastly above / as we stood / on our terrace.
questions.explanation: 'Fast' is itself the adverb; 'fastly' is not standard English: 'The birds flew fast above'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech. She said, “I can play the guitar pretty well.”
options: She said that she can play the guitar pretty well.
She said that she would play the guitar pretty well
She said that she could play the guitar pretty well.
She said that she plays the guitar pretty well.
questions.explanation: After 'said', 'can' moves back to 'could' and 'I' becomes 'she': 'She said that she could play the guitar pretty well.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. Samantha keeps herself occupied by “helping other people willingly without expecting any payment for her services.”
questions.explanation: A volunteer offers to help or work without being paid; a mercenary works only for money.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The state of being full or complete
questions.explanation: 'Plenitude' is fullness or completeness: abundance. A plebiscite is a direct vote, and pliability is flexibility.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Knock down
questions.explanation: To 'knock down' a building is to demolish it.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'hostile'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. Tell her to finish the work.
options: To finish the work be told to her.
The work is to be finished by her.
Let her be told to finish the work.
questions.explanation: An imperative with an object becomes passive with 'let': 'Tell her' becomes 'Let her be told', and 'to finish the work' stays.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. They will meet Freddy outside the airport.
options: Freddy would have been met outside the airport.
They would be met by Freddy outside the airport.
Freddy will meet them outside the airport.
Freddy will be met by them outside the airport.
questions.explanation: The future active 'will meet' becomes 'will be met', and the subject 'they' becomes the agent 'by them': 'Freddy will be met by them outside the airport.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Eat like a horse
questions.explanation: To 'eat like a horse' is to eat a lot of food.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A remedy to counteract the effects of poison
questions.explanation: An antidote counteracts a poison. Antibodies are made by the body against infection, and antiseptics and antibiotics act against germs.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'courteous'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Beat around the bush
options: To discuss minute details of something
To avoid talking about what is important
To search for a lost thing in vain
To hope for something that is unattainable
questions.explanation: To 'beat around the bush' is to avoid coming to the point.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Scared
questions.explanation: 'Scared' means 'afraid'. 'Sacred' looks similar but means holy.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Assiduous
questions.explanation: 'Assiduous' means diligent and hard-working; its opposite is 'idle'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. Life is hard, unpredictable, but “though manageable.”
questions.explanation: 'But' and 'though' both mark a contrast and cannot be used together: 'but still controllable'. 'Although' and 'despite' make the same mistake.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. When the fish at last had been safely landed, I asked the brothers if they ate fish. B. The condition that I put was that they had to help me land another fish for my men. C. On receiving their eager answer that they most certainly did, I told them I would give them the fish we had just landed. D. To this they readily agreed and the wait started again.
questions.explanation: A (the brothers are asked if they eat fish), C (their eager yes and the offer of the fish), B (the condition attached to it) and D (they agree and the wait begins): ACBD.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Ebb
questions.explanation: 'Ebb' is the going out of the tide; its opposite is 'flow', the tide coming in.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word in the given sentence. Police fear that terrorists may try to “assassinate” the president during his appearance at the summit.
questions.explanation: To 'assassinate' is to murder an important person, often for political reasons.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A question like "How big is Faerie?” does not admit (1)_________ a simple answer. Faerie, after all, is not one land, one principality or (2)_________ Maps of Faerie are unreliable, and may not be (3)_________ upon. Faerie is bigger than England, as it is bigger than the world. In the middle of a wood so thick it was very nearly a forest was a small hut, (4)_________ of thatch and grey clay. A yellow bird in a cage sat on its perch outside the house. It did not sing, and sat (5)_________ silent.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'Admit of' means allow or leave room for: the question 'does not admit of a simple answer'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A question like "How big is Faerie?” does not admit (1)_________ a simple answer. Faerie, after all, is not one land, one principality or (2)_________ Maps of Faerie are unreliable, and may not be (3)_________ upon. Faerie is bigger than England, as it is bigger than the world. In the middle of a wood so thick it was very nearly a forest was a small hut, (4)_________ of thatch and grey clay. A yellow bird in a cage sat on its perch outside the house. It did not sing, and sat (5)_________ silent.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Faerie is 'not one land, one principality or dominion': like 'land' and 'principality', a dominion is a territory under one ruler.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A question like "How big is Faerie?” does not admit (1)_________ a simple answer. Faerie, after all, is not one land, one principality or (2)_________ Maps of Faerie are unreliable, and may not be (3)_________ upon. Faerie is bigger than England, as it is bigger than the world. In the middle of a wood so thick it was very nearly a forest was a small hut, (4)_________ of thatch and grey clay. A yellow bird in a cage sat on its perch outside the house. It did not sing, and sat (5)_________ silent.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'Depended upon' means relied on: unreliable maps 'may not be depended upon'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A question like "How big is Faerie?” does not admit (1)_________ a simple answer. Faerie, after all, is not one land, one principality or (2)_________ Maps of Faerie are unreliable, and may not be (3)_________ upon. Faerie is bigger than England, as it is bigger than the world.
