options: W L a a L W L a
W L a a a W L a
W L a a a W L W
L L a a a W L a
questions.explanation: With W, L, a, a, a, W, L, a in the blanks the block WaLaWaL repeats three times: WaLaWaL WaLaWaL WaLaWaL.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and fourth term related to third term. 14:21::6:9::12:?
questions.explanation: The second number is 1.5 times the first: 14 × 1.5 = 21 and 6 × 1.5 = 9. Likewise 12 × 1.5 = 18.

questions.text: If 20 July 2021 was Tuesday, then what was the day of the week on 28 November 2021?
questions.explanation: From 20 July to 28 November 2021 is 11 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 28 = 131 days, 18 weeks and 5 days. Five days after Tuesday is Sunday.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘RACE’ is written as ‘AREC’, and ‘PEAK’ is written as ‘EPKA’. How will ‘CORE’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each pair of letters is swapped: RA CE → AR EC and PE AK → EP KA. So CO RE → OC ER: OCER.

questions.text: If ‘A’ denotes ‘+’, ‘B’ denotes ‘×’, ‘C’ denotes ‘–’ and ‘D’ denotes ‘÷’, then what will come in place of ‘?’ in the following equation? 71 A 3 B 2 C 6 B (65 D 13) C 7 B4 = ?
questions.explanation: After replacing the letters: 71 + 3 × 2 − 6 × (65 ÷ 13) − 7 × 4 = 71 + 6 − 30 − 28 = 19.

questions.text: The difference between a number and the square root of the number is 2. The number is:
questions.explanation: With √x = t: t² − t = 2, so (t − 2)(t + 1) = 0 and t = 2. The number is 4, and 4 − √4 = 2.

questions.text: If the average marks of three batches of 30, 50 and 70 students is 55, 70 and 70 respectively, then the average marks of all the students is:
Which of the following options is divisible by 11?
questions.explanation: A number is divisible by 11 when the alternating sum of its digits is: for 28171, 2 − 8 + 1 − 7 + 1 = −11, and 28171 = 11 × 2561. The others give 2, 7 and −8.

questions.text: Compute the compound interest on ₹ 8,400 for one and half years at 12% rate of interest per annum, compounded half yearly.
questions.explanation: Compounded half-yearly, 1½ years at 12% is 3 periods at 6%: 8,400 × 1.06³ = ₹10,004.53, so the interest is ₹1,604.53, which the option gives as ₹1,604.50.

questions.text: If x : y = 1 : 2, find the value of (2x + 4y) : (x + 4y).
The speed of a train is 108 km/h. The distance covered by the train in 11 seconds will be:
questions.explanation: 108 km/h = 108 × 5/18 = 30 m/s, so in 11 seconds the train covers 30 × 11 = 330 m.

questions.text: Find the area of the triangle whose sides are 5 cm, 12 cm and 13 cm.
questions.explanation: 5² + 12² = 13², so the triangle is right-angled with legs 5 cm and 12 cm: area = ½ × 5 × 12 = 30 cm².

questions.text: Rohan scored 70 and 75 marks in the first two tests. How many marks should he score in the third test to get an average of 70 marks?
questions.explanation: An average of 70 over three tests needs 3 × 70 = 210 marks: 210 − (70 + 75) = 65.

questions.text: Harsh purchased a scooter for ₹48,000. He sold it at a loss of 15%. With that money he purchased another scooter and sold it at a profit of 22.5%. What is his overall loss/profit percentage?
questions.explanation: He sold the first scooter for 48,000 × 0.85 = ₹40,800 and the second for 40,800 × 1.225 = ₹49,980. His ₹48,000 became ₹49,980: a profit of ₹1,980, or 4.125%.

questions.text: The marked price of a toy was ₹4,875. Successive discounts of 28% and 30% were offered on it during a clearance sale. What was the selling price of the toy?
Find the sum of money which when increased by 15% becomes ₹19,320.
After successive discounts of 25% and 10% a shirt was sold for ₹480. What was the original price of the shirt (Nearest to a ₹)?
questions.explanation: After both discounts 0.75 × 0.9 = 0.675 of the price is left: 480 ÷ 0.675 = ₹711.11, about ₹711.

questions.text: In a class, the ratio of the number of boys to that of the girls is 11∶9. 30% of the boys and 20% of the girls passed an exam. Find the percentage of students who passed the exam.
questions.explanation: Take 110 boys and 90 girls: 30% of 110 = 33 and 20% of 90 = 18 passed, 51 of 200 students, or 25.5%.

questions.text: If the ratio of the volumes of two cones is 11:16 and the ratio of the radii of their bases is 3:4, then the ratio of their heights will be:
Guru Padmaja Reddy was awarded the Padma Shri in 2022 for her contributions to which of the following dance forms?
questions.explanation: Gaddam Padmaja Reddy, a Kuchipudi exponent and teacher, received the Padma Shri for art in 2022.

questions.text: _________’s ‘The Year of the Runaways’ follows the lives of three migrant workers who flee India to look for work in England.
questions.explanation: 'The Year of the Runaways' (2015), shortlisted for the Booker Prize, is by the British novelist Sunjeev Sahota.

questions.text: Who among the following was popularly known as ‘Gurudev’ for his expertise in binding together elements of Indian classical music and folk pieces to suit the western tunes entailed with precision along with his expertise in other art domains?
questions.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore, called 'Gurudev', composed the songs known as Rabindra Sangeet, which blend Indian classical, folk and western influences; he was also a poet, writer and painter.

questions.text: As of December 2021, how many sports infrastructure projects of various categories have been sanctioned in the North Eastern Region under the ‘Khelo India’ scheme?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 62 sports infrastructure projects sanctioned in the North Eastern Region under the Khelo India scheme as of December 2021.

questions.text: Which state has the highest length (in km) of national highways as per the data of 2017?
questions.explanation: In 2017 Maharashtra had the greatest length of national highways of any state, well ahead of Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Karnataka.

questions.text: Identify the INCORRECT pair with respect to the substances and their specific heat capacity (J kg⁻¹K⁻¹) at room temperature and atmospheric pressure.
questions.explanation: Water's specific heat capacity is about 4186 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, not 1200. The other values match the standard table: aluminium 900.0, carbon 506.5, tungsten 134.4.

questions.text: ___________ demand for money arises mainly due to the uncertainty of future receipts and expenses.
questions.explanation: In Keynes's theory the precautionary demand for money is money held against unforeseen expenses and emergencies; transactions demand is for routine payments, and speculative demand for gains from changes in interest rates.

questions.text: ‘In The Afternoon of Time: An Autobiography’ was written by which of the following Indian poets of the 20th century?
questions.explanation: 'In the Afternoon of Time' is the English version of the autobiography of the Hindi poet Harivansh Rai Bachchan.

questions.text: The Asian Games 2022 will be organised in which of the following countries?
questions.explanation: The 2022 Asian Games were awarded to Hangzhou, China; postponed because of Covid-19, they were held in 2023.

questions.text: What was the theme for the International Day for Older persons 2021?
questions.explanation: The UN's theme for the International Day of Older Persons (1 October) in 2021 was 'Digital Equity for All Ages'.

questions.text: The Eld's deer subspecies, which is classified as endangered in the IUCN Red List, is found only in the:
options: Keibul Lamjao National Park in Manipur
Pench National Park in Madhya Pradesh
questions.explanation: The Sangai, Manipur's brow-antlered Eld's deer, lives only in Keibul Lamjao National Park, on the floating phumdis of Loktak Lake.

questions.text: Which of the following is a group of primitive vertebrates having a large jawless sucking mouth, no limbs or paired fins and a completely cartilaginous skeleton with a persistent notochord?
questions.explanation: Cyclostomes (lampreys and hagfish) are jawless vertebrates with a circular sucking mouth, no paired fins and a cartilaginous skeleton.

questions.text: The South Indian film dance choreographer, K Shivashankar, won which of the following prestigious awards in 2010 for the best choreography in the Telugu film Magadheera?
questions.explanation: K. Shivashankar won the National Film Award for Best Choreography for 'Magadheera' (the 57th awards, for 2009, announced in 2010).

questions.text: Mohanan Chandrasekaran, an awardee of Madras Music Academy's Sangeetha Kalanidhi, is a __________ player of Carnatic classical music.
questions.explanation: M. Chandrasekaran is a Carnatic violinist; the Music Academy conferred the Sangita Kalanidhi on him in 2005.

questions.text: Who among the following dancers is the first transwoman to receive a Padma Shri Award for her contribution to Indian Classical dance?
questions.explanation: Narthaki Nataraj, a Bharatanatyam dancer, received the Padma Shri in 2019, the first transgender woman to receive it.

questions.text: How many members of the Legislative Council are there in the state of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The Karnataka Legislative Council has 75 members.

questions.text: The particles of which metal on heating to the boiling point of 357°C go from liquid state to gas state?
questions.explanation: Mercury, a metal that is liquid at room temperature, boils at about 357°C. Copper and gallium boil at well over 2,000°C, and bronze is an alloy.

questions.text: Sonal Mansingh is a prominent Indian classical dancer who specialises in __________.
questions.explanation: Sonal Mansingh is best known as an exponent of Bharatanatyam and Odissi.

questions.text: Who is the author of the famous Marathi novel ‘Mrityunjay’?
questions.explanation: 'Mrityunjay', the Marathi novel that tells the story of Karna, is by Shivaji Sawant.

questions.text: Ustad Zakir Hussain, Ustad Allah Rakha, Ustad Sabir Khan, Pt. Kishan Maharaj are known for which of the following instruments?
questions.explanation: Zakir Hussain, his father Allah Rakha, Sabir Khan and Kishan Maharaj are all tabla players.

questions.text: Who is NOT an awardee of the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award 2021?
questions.explanation: The twelve Khel Ratna awardees of 2021 included hockey captain Manpreet Singh and the para-athletes Sumit Antil and Krishna Nagar; Mandeep Singh was not among them.

questions.text: Ustad Amir Khan belonged to which of the following Gharanas?
questions.explanation: Ustad Amir Khan founded the Indore gharana of Hindustani vocal music.

questions.text: Lake Baikal, the world's largest freshwater lake (by volume) and the world's deepest lake with a depth of 1620 m (5315 ft), is located in which country?
questions.explanation: Lake Baikal is in southern Siberia, Russia.

questions.text: What do you call the water holding compounds produced in large quantities by marine brown and red algae?
questions.explanation: Marine brown and red algae produce hydrocolloids, water-holding substances such as algin (from brown algae) and carrageen (from red algae).

questions.text: Which of the following countries will host the FIFA World Cup in 2026?
questions.explanation: The United States, Canada and Mexico were chosen in 2018 to co-host the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. In order to win the competition, one has to be “creative”.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'more creative': to win, one has to be more creative than the other entrants. The superlative would need 'the' ('the most creative'), and 'creativest' and 'creativer' are not used, as long adjectives take 'more' and 'most'. The sentence as printed is also correct, but no option keeps it.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Eternal; lasting forever or indefinitely
questions.explanation: 'Perpetual' means lasting for ever, or continuing without end.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'charisma'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underline segment in the given sentence. The Ukranian soldiers “passed in” for several weeks.
questions.explanation: To 'hold out' is to go on resisting an attack, as soldiers do for weeks; 'passed in' makes no sense here.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. We should ______ his outfit as he has put on weight.
questions.explanation: To 'alter' clothes is to change them to fit; an 'altar' is the table in a place of worship.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Sanguinity
questions.explanation: 'Sanguinity' is cheerful confidence about the future: 'optimism'.

questions.text: Select the correct homonym from the given options to fill in the blank. The French perfume has a wonderful________
questions.explanation: A perfume has a 'scent'; 'sent' and 'cent' only sound the same.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. The new bride is going to be admired by everyone in the family.
options: Everybody in the family is going to admire the new bride.
Everybody in the family was admiring the new bride.
Everybody in the family has been going to admire the new bride.
Everybody in the family was going to admire the new bride.
questions.explanation: 'Is going to be admired by everyone' becomes 'Everybody is going to admire': the same future form, with the agent as subject.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. Mohan frequently “wastes his money on luxurious objects” such as cars and digital devices.
questions.explanation: Someone who spends money wastefully on luxuries is 'extravagant'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Safe pair of hands
options: A person who can be trusted to do something efficiently
questions.explanation: A 'safe pair of hands' is a person who can be relied on to do a job well.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. An outlook that is influenced by people from all over the world
questions.explanation: A 'cosmopolitan' outlook draws on people and cultures from all over the world.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. Admittance was refused to him by the airport security.
options: The airport security is refusing him admittance.
The airport security has refused him admittance.
The airport security had refused him admittance.
The airport security refused him admittance.
questions.explanation: The simple past passive 'was refused' becomes the simple past active 'refused', with the airport security as subject.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. I told Pooja “that she could have use my car to get around” while she is in my hometown.
options: that she could have use my car to get around with
that she can use my car to get around
that she could have use my car to get away
that she can use my car to get away with
questions.explanation: 'Could have' needs a past participle, so 'could have use' is wrong; 'can use' fits 'while she is in my hometown'. To 'get around' is to travel about; to 'get away' is to escape.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. The government presented awards to eminent people.
options: Eminent people were presented awards by the government.
Eminent people are presented awards by the government.
Eminent people are being presented awards by the government.
Eminent people were being presented awards by the government.
questions.explanation: The simple past 'presented' becomes the simple past passive 'were presented', with 'eminent people' as subject.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. Due to his hard work, he established a “succesful” career.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'successful'.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. Dumbledore tells McGonagall that someone named Voldemort has killed a Mr. and Mrs. Potter and tried unsuccessfully to kill their baby son, Harry. B. Dumbledore leaves Harry with an explanatory note in a basket in front of the Dursley home. C. Mr. Dursley, a well-off Englishman, notices strange happenings on his way to work one day. D. That night, Albus Dumbledore, the head of a wizardry academy called Hogwarts, meets Professor McGonagall, who also teaches at Hogwarts, and a giant named Hagrid outside the Dursley home.
questions.explanation: C opens with Mr. Dursley's strange day, D tells of the meeting outside his home that night, A gives Dumbledore's news to McGonagall and B ends with Harry left at the door: CDAB.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. We “expended” most of our savings on this tour.
questions.explanation: To 'expend' savings is to use them up: 'exhausted'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Let down
questions.explanation: To 'let someone down' is to fail them, to disappoint them.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Trust is (1) _________ confidence, faith and hope in someone or something. There are many ways to show trust. If you want to be trusted, just be (2)_________. Trust takes years to build, seconds to (3) ________ and forever to repair. Trust is like a mirror you can fix if (4) _______ but still see the cracks in that reflection. Whether it is a friendship or a relationship, all (5)________ are based on trust.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Trust is 'showing' confidence, faith and hope in someone, as the next sentence's 'ways to show trust' confirms.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Trust is (1) _________ confidence, faith and hope in someone or something. There are many ways to show trust. If you want to be trusted, just be (2)_________. Trust takes years to build, seconds to (3) ________ and forever to repair. Trust is like a mirror you can fix if (4) _______ but still see the cracks in that reflection. Whether it is a friendship or a relationship, all (5)________ are based on trust.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: To be trusted, 'just be honest'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Trust is (1) _________ confidence, faith and hope in someone or something. There are many ways to show trust. If you want to be trusted, just be (2)_________. Trust takes years to build, seconds to (3) ________ and forever to repair. Trust is like a mirror you can fix if (4) _______ but still see the cracks in that reflection. Whether it is a friendship or a relationship, all (5)________ are based on trust.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Trust takes years to build and seconds to 'break', set against 'forever to repair'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Trust is (1) _________ confidence, faith and hope in someone or something. There are many ways to show trust. If you want to be trusted, just be (2)_________. Trust takes years to build, seconds to (3) ________ and forever to repair. Trust is like a mirror you can fix if (4) _______ but still see the cracks in that reflection. Whether it is a friendship or a relationship, all (5)________ are based on trust.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: A mirror can be fixed if 'broken', but the cracks still show in the reflection.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Trust is (1) _________ confidence, faith and hope in someone or something. There are many ways to show trust. If you want to be trusted, just be (2)_________. Trust takes years to build, seconds to (3) ________ and forever to repair. Trust is like a mirror you can fix if (4) _______ but still see the cracks in that reflection. Whether it is a friendship or a relationship, all (5)________ are based on trust.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Friendships and relationships are 'bonds', and all of them rest on trust.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. SOCCER : OSFFRE :: ROLLER : OROORE :: TOPPER : ?
questions.explanation: The first two letters swap, the middle pair moves 3 places forward and the last two swap: SO CC ER → OS FF RE and RO LL ER → OR OO RE. So TO PP ER → OT SS RE: OTSSRE.

questions.text: If P denotes ‘×’, Q denotes ‘÷’, R denotes ‘+’ and S denotes ‘−’, then what will come in place of ‘?’ in the following equation? (40 Q 4 ) P 5 R (3 P 6) S (7 P 8) R 21 = ?
Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the sixth term is related to the fifth term. 5 : 14 :: 12 : ? :: 17 : 86
questions.explanation: The second number is 6 times the first minus 16: 6 × 5 − 16 = 14 and 6 × 17 − 16 = 86. Likewise 6 × 12 − 16 = 56.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'HELP' is written as '1652432' and 'SAVE' is written as '381445'. How will 'MAIL' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Consonants are written as twice their place in the alphabet and vowels as their place: H(16) E(5) L(24) P(32) and S(38) A(1) V(44) E(5). So M(26) A(1) I(9) L(24): 261924.

questions.text: The second number in the given number pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number pairs except one. Find that odd number pair.
questions.explanation: In 15 : 32.5, 19 : 38.5 and 17 : 35.5 the second number is 1.5 times the first plus 10 (22.5 + 10, 28.5 + 10, 25.5 + 10). 13 × 1.5 + 10 = 29.5, not 28.5, so 13 : 28.5 is the odd one.

questions.text: R is the brother of N. R is the only son of K. S is the only daughter-in-law of K. How is N related to S?
questions.explanation: R is K's only son, so his sibling N is K's daughter; S, K's only daughter-in-law, is R's wife. N is therefore S's husband's sister.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (56, 8, 15) (32, 16, 18) (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed)
questions.explanation: First ÷ second + second = third: 56 ÷ 8 + 8 = 15 and 32 ÷ 16 + 16 = 18. Likewise 66 ÷ 6 + 6 = 17.

questions.text: Three Statements are given followed by Three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All ants are beetles. No beetle is a frog. Some frogs are bugs. Conclusions: I. Some bugs are ants. II. No bug is a beetle. III. No frog is an ant.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Both conclusions I and III follow.
questions.explanation: All ants are beetles and no beetle is a frog, so no ant is a frog (III). The bugs that are frogs are not beetles, but other bugs may or may not be beetles or ants, so neither I nor II follows.

questions.text: The second number in the given number-pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number-pairs EXCEPT one. Find that odd number-pair.
questions.explanation: The second number is 2 less than the square root of the first: √25 − 2 = 3, √64 − 2 = 6 and √81 − 2 = 7. √100 − 2 = 8, not 9, so 100 : 9 is the odd one.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'WAVE' is coded as ‘426522’ and ‘SOUND’ is coded as ’81261323’. How will 'LIGHT' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is written as its place counted from Z (Z = 1, A = 26): W(4) A(26) V(5) E(22) and S(8) O(12) U(6) N(13) D(23). So L(15) I(18) G(20) H(19) T(7): 151820197.

questions.text: The birth date of Viaan is 9 March 2002. Find the day of the week of that day.
questions.explanation: Counting odd days: 2000 years give 0 and 2001 gives 1; then January gives 3, February (28 days) 0 and 9 days of March 2. 1 + 3 + 0 + 2 = 6 odd days, which is Saturday.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? TBNF, CJUL, LRBR, UZIX, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move +9 (T, C, L, U, so D), second letters +8 (B, J, R, Z, so H), third letters +7 (N, U, B, I, so P) and fourth letters +6 (F, L, R, X, so D), wrapping round the alphabet: DHPD.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 39*4*61*18*4*49*7*30
questions.explanation: 39 × 4 − 61 = 18 × 4 − 49 ÷ 7 + 30: the left side is 156 − 61 = 95 and the right side 72 − 7 + 30 = 95.

questions.text: Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it. First row: 17, 26, 60; Second row:8, 15, 31; Third row: 11, 19, ? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the number into its constituent digits. For example, 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In each row, 2 × first + middle = third: 2 × 17 + 26 = 60 and 2 × 8 + 15 = 31. So 2 × 11 + 19 = 41.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 50 * 2 * 3 * 30 * 10 * 40 * 20
questions.explanation: 50 × 2 = 3 × 30 × 10 − 40 × 20: the left side is 100 and the right side 900 − 800 = 100.

questions.text: The second number in the given number pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number pairs, EXCEPT one. Find that odd number pair.
questions.explanation: In 16 : 4, 48 : 12 and 20 : 5 the second number is a quarter of the first. In 24 : 8 it is a third, so that pair is the odd one.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 23, 28, 280, 295, 5900, ?
questions.explanation: The steps alternate: +5, ×10, +15, ×20, so next +25: 5900 + 25 = 5925.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'DUCK' is written as 'FSEI' and ‘FISH’ is written as ‘HGUF’. How will 'FROG' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +2, −2, +2, −2: DUCK → FSEI and FISH → HGUF. So FROG → HPQE.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that, when sequentially placed from left to right in the blanks below, will complete the letter series. _ M o N _ _ _ o M _ _ o _ _o M _ N o J o
options: o o J o o N J o M
o o J o o N J o o
o M J o o N J o o
M o J o o N J o o
questions.explanation: With o, o, J, o, o, N, J, o, o in the blanks the block oMoNoJo repeats: oMoNoJo oMoNoJo oMoNoJo.

questions.text: The third proportional to 81 and 27 is:
questions.explanation: The third proportional to a and b is b²/a: 27²/81 = 729/81 = 9.

questions.text: The marked price of a study table is ₹3,200. It will be offered for ₹2,448 after two successive discounts. If the first discount is 10%, the second discount is:
questions.explanation: After 10% off, ₹3,200 becomes ₹2,880. ₹2,448/₹2,880 = 0.85, so the second discount is 15%.

questions.text: In an election between two candidates, 10% of the voters did not cast their vote and 5% of the votes polled were found invalid. The successful candidate got 55% of the valid votes and won by a majority of 1710 votes. How many voters were enrolled?
questions.explanation: With N voters enrolled, 0.9N voted and 0.95 × 0.9N = 0.855N votes were valid. The winner's margin is 55% − 45% = 10% of these: 0.0855N = 1,710, so N = 20,000.

questions.text: 15 identical solid spherical balls of radius 5 cm are melted to form a single sphere. In this process, 35% of the mass is wasted. What is the radius (in cm) of the single sphere that is now formed? [Use π = 22/7, and give your answer correct to two decimal places.]
questions.explanation: 65% of the volume of 15 balls remains: (4/3)πR³ = 0.65 × 15 × (4/3)π × 5³, so R³ = 1,218.75 and R ≈ 10.68 cm.

questions.text: The side of a square is 5 cm. If the side is doubled, by how many times will the area of the square increase?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 4 times, taking 'increase by how many times' to mean how many times as large the area becomes: from 5² = 25 cm² to 10² = 100 cm². Read strictly, the increase is 75 cm², 3 times the original area, which is also an option.

questions.text: A bus goes to Mumbai from Delhi at the speed of 60 km/h for 60% of the journey, and covers the remaining part of its journey at the speed of 70 km/h. What is the average speed of the bus (in km/h) during the entire journey under consideration?
questions.explanation: Take 100 km: 60 km at 60 km/h takes 1 hour and 40 km at 70 km/h takes 4/7 hour. Average speed = 100 ÷ 11/7 = 700/11 ≈ 63.6 km/h, which rounds to 64.

questions.text: A manufacturer sells an item to a wholesale dealer at a profit of 11%. The wholesaler sells the same to a retailer at a profit of 15%. The retailer in turn sells it to a customer for ₹17,045, thereby earning a profit of 19%. The cost price of the manufacturer is (consider integral part only):
In an examination, the average marks of 60 girls is 15 and the average marks of 40 boys is 30. The average marks of the group in which the boys and girls are taken together is:
A grocer has a sale of ₹8,435, ₹8,927, ₹8,855, ₹9,230 and ₹8,562 in 5 consecutive weeks. How much sale must he have in the 6th week so that he gets an average sale of ₹8,500?
questions.explanation: Six weeks at ₹8,500 need ₹51,000. The five weeks total ₹44,009, so the sixth must bring ₹51,000 − ₹44,009 = ₹6,991.

questions.text: Ram is travelling at a speed of 72 km per hour while Shyam is travelling at a speed of 90 km per hour. What is the difference in their speeds (in metres per second)?
A tractor is sold after allowing three successive discounts of 10%, 5% and 2%. If the marked price of the tractor is Rs 4,88,000, find its net selling price.
If a = 2022, b = 2021 and c = 2020, then value of a² + b² + c² – ab – bc – ca is:
questions.explanation: a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca = ½[(a − b)² + (b − c)² + (c − a)²] = ½(1 + 1 + 4) = 3.

questions.text: Calculate the difference between the compound interest and the simple interest on a sum of ₹5,000 at the rate of 8% for 3 years. (to nearest ₹)
Two parallel chords are drawn in a circle of diameter 10 m. The length of one chord is 8 m and the distance between the two chords is 6 m. Find the length of the other chord.
questions.explanation: The radius is 5 m, so the 8 m chord is √(5² − 4²) = 3 m from the centre. The other chord, 6 m away, cannot be on the same side (9 m > 5 m), so it is 3 m from the centre on the other side and also 2 × 4 = 8 m long.

questions.text: Evaluate the following expression: 3 tan²45° + 2 cos 60° − 2 sin 30°
If the price of rice is raised by 20%, then by what percentage should a person reduce his consumption of rice so that his expenditure remains the same? (correct to one decimal place)
questions.explanation: To keep spending the same, consumption must fall by 20/120 = 1/6 ≈ 16.7%.

questions.text: Which Indian woman hockey player was made the brand ambassador of the Centre's 'Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao' scheme for Haridwar district in August 2021?
questions.explanation: In August 2021 hockey player Vandana Katariya was named the brand ambassador of 'Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao' for her home district, Haridwar.

questions.text: What is the distance of the Marathon race?
questions.explanation: The marathon is run over 42.195 km.

questions.text: Which Indian musician won a Grammy twice for Danny Boyle’s film Slumdog Millionaire in 2010?
questions.explanation: A. R. Rahman won two Grammys in 2010 for 'Slumdog Millionaire': for the soundtrack album and for the song 'Jai Ho'.

questions.text: Who among the following is associated with the Tabla?
questions.explanation: Zakir Hussain is known for the tabla; Hariprasad Chaurasia for the flute, Sultan Khan for the sarangi and Amjad Ali Khan for the sarod.

questions.text: Which element replaced eka aluminium according to the Mendeleev’s periodic table?
questions.explanation: Mendeleev left a gap below aluminium for 'eka-aluminium'; gallium, discovered in 1875, filled it with the properties he had predicted.

questions.text: In which year was the POSHAN Abhiyaan launched to emphasise the nutritional status of adolescent girls, pregnant women, lactating mothers, and children in the age group of 0-6 years?
questions.explanation: POSHAN Abhiyaan, the National Nutrition Mission, was launched in March 2018 at Jhunjhunu, Rajasthan.

questions.text: Who among the following versatile musicians of India won the Best Music Director National Award for the Hindi movie ‘Rudaali’ and was also known as the ‘Bard of Brahmaputra’?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Bhupen Hazarika, the 'Bard of the Brahmaputra', who composed the music of 'Rudaali' (1993). His award for that score was the best-music prize of the 1993 Asia-Pacific Film Festival; his National Award for Best Music Direction was for 'Chameli Memsaab' (1975).

questions.text: Ashish Sankrityayan is an exponent of _________ music.
questions.explanation: Ashish Sankrityayan is a dhrupad singer trained by the Dagars, who took charge of the Dhrupad Kendra in Bhopal in 2011.

questions.text: Who among the following writers has written the famous Hindi novel ‘Godan’?
questions.explanation: 'Godan' (1936), the story of the poor farmer Hori, was Munshi Premchand's last completed novel.

questions.text: Who among the following personalities is a Padma Vibhushan, legendary Indian Classical Dancer behind reviving the classical dance form of Odissi in the 20th century?
questions.explanation: Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra, a Padma Vibhushan, led the twentieth-century revival of Odissi.

questions.text: Identify the chemical name for Ge.
questions.explanation: Ge is the symbol of germanium; gallium is Ga, gold Au and gadolinium Gd.

questions.text: What percentage of the rural population uses safe and functional toilets as per the 2019-20 National Sample Survey report?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 85% as the share of the rural population using safe and functional toilets in the 2019-20 survey; analyses of the National Annual Rural Sanitation Survey quote the same 85% for rural use of functional toilets.

questions.text: The nineteenth century saw the golden age of Kathak under the patronage of Wajid Ali Shah, the last Nawab of __________.
questions.explanation: Wajid Ali Shah, the last Nawab of Oudh (Awadh), was a great patron of Kathak at his court in Lucknow.

questions.text: The rate at which RBI lends to commercial banks for the short term is called ________.
questions.explanation: The repo rate is the rate at which the RBI lends to banks for the short term against government securities; at the reverse repo rate it borrows from them.

questions.text: Who among the following won Arjuna Award 2021 in Para Archery discipline?
questions.explanation: Para-archer Harvinder Singh, bronze medallist at the Tokyo Paralympics, received the Arjuna Award in 2021.

questions.text: How many types of writs can be issued by the Supreme Court of India for the protection of Fundamental Rights?
questions.explanation: Under Article 32 the Supreme Court can issue five writs: habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari and quo warranto.

questions.text: Vannadil Pudiyaveettil Dhananjayan and Shanta Dhananjayan, popularly known as the Dhananjayans were awarded with Rashtriya Kalidas Samman for the year __________.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 2019-20: in November 2021 Madhya Pradesh announced its Rashtriya Kalidas Samman for the years 2019 and 2020, and the classical dance award went to Sunaina Hazarilal and to the Dhananjayans, the Bharatanatyam couple from Chennai.

questions.text: Which Manipuri Classical Dancer opened the ‘Govindji Nartanalaya’ dance school for women in Imphal?
questions.explanation: Guru Bipin Singh opened the Govindji Nartanalaya in Imphal so that women from ordinary families could learn the Manipuri dance of the royal palace.

questions.text: Which of the following was the venue of the first ICC Test Championship final between India and New Zealand?
questions.explanation: The first World Test Championship final, India v New Zealand in June 2021, was played at Southampton in England.

questions.text: In January 2021, which state/Union Territory issued its ‘School Bag Policy 2020’, according to which the weight of the school bag should be at a maximum of 3.5 kgs to 5 kgs?
questions.explanation: In January 2021 Delhi's Directorate of Education told its schools to follow the School Bag Policy 2020, which keeps a bag within 10% of the pupil's body weight in classes 1 to 10 and sets limits class by class.

questions.text: Which of the following groupsconsists of elements that are non-reactive, monoatomic elements with extremely low boiling points?
questions.explanation: Group 18 holds the noble gases: unreactive, monatomic elements with very low boiling points.

questions.text: Which of the following books is an autobiography of the Indian constitutional jurist Fali S Nariman?
questions.explanation: 'Before Memory Fades' is the autobiography of the jurist Fali S. Nariman.

questions.text: Which of the following is a mountain pass in the Pir Panjal range at a maximum altitude of 2832 metresthat connects the Kashmir Valley in the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir with the Outer Himalayas and the plains in the south?
questions.explanation: The Banihal Pass (2,832 m) crosses the Pir Panjal range between the Kashmir Valley and Jammu; the Jawahar Tunnel runs beneath it.

questions.text: ‘I, Me, Mine’ is the autobiography of which international musician?
questions.explanation: 'I, Me, Mine' (1980) is the autobiography of George Harrison of the Beatles, named after one of his Beatles songs.

questions.text: Identify the cell that is amoeboid in shape.
questions.explanation: White blood cells are amoeboid: they change shape and move by pseudopodia, which lets them engulf germs.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. Ravi got the job easily because he “speaks many languages.”
questions.explanation: A polyglot is a person who speaks several languages.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Loathe
questions.explanation: To 'loathe' is to hate intensely: to 'abhor'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A snake in the grass
questions.explanation: 'A snake in the grass' is a treacherous person who pretends to be a friend: a deceitful person.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'guilty'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underline segment in the given sentence. During the war, the comedian proved to be a “man of music”.
questions.explanation: 'A man of straw' is a weak person of no real substance, the only established idiom among the options: when war came, the comedian proved feeble.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence. All his bones could be counted because his body was totally “shrivelled and wrinkled with age.”
questions.explanation: 'Wizened' means shrivelled and wrinkled with age.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Asha was ___________ made a fool by her friend.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'deliberately', on purpose: the friend set out to make a fool of Asha. 'Unknowingly' (Asha did not realise it) also makes sense, but the key reads the adverb as describing the friend's act.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. You never hear of a happy billionaire.
options: A happy billionaire is never heard of.
A happy billionaire never heard of.
A happy billionaire is never heard by you.
No one hears a happy billionaire.
questions.explanation: 'Hear of' becomes 'is heard of', keeping its preposition, and the general agent 'you' is dropped: 'A happy billionaire is never heard of.'

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. The most recent studies on the human body are likely to alter the face of health sciences.
options: The most recent studies on the human body are likely to be altered by the face of health sciences.
The face of health sciences will be altering the most recent studies on the human body.
The face of health sciences is likely to be altered by the most recent studies on the human body.
The most face of health sciences is likely to alter the recent studies on the human body.
questions.explanation: The object 'the face of health sciences' becomes the subject, and 'are likely to alter' becomes 'is likely to be altered by'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The river / flowed besides / the hillock / in our village.
questions.explanation: 'Beside' means next to; 'besides' means in addition to. The river flowed 'beside' the hillock.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Tit for tat
questions.explanation: 'Tit for tat' is paying back an injury in kind: a counter attack.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the following sentence. Eventually the patient “succumbed” to her illness.
questions.explanation: To 'succumb' to an illness is to give way to it; its opposite is to 'overcome' it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Show me “the better” dress in the shop.
questions.explanation: 'In the shop' compares the dress with every dress there, more than two, so the superlative is needed: 'the best dress in the shop'.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. Their brother, John, is more blatantly hostile to Jane, reminding her that she is a poor dependent of his mother. B. Orphaned as an infant, Jane Eyre lives at Gateshead with her aunt, Sarah Reed, as the novel opens. C. Her female cousins, Georgiana, and Eliza, tolerate, but don't love her. D. Jane is ten years old, an outsider in the Reed family.
questions.explanation: B introduces Jane at Gateshead, D says she is an outsider in the Reed family, C turns to her female cousins and A to their brother, who is 'more' openly hostile: BDCA.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'beautician'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. At the end of our first two weeks on the island, “we were informed” that our lawyers, Bram Fischer and Joel Joffe, were going to be visiting the following day.
questions.explanation: The account is in the past ('At the end of our first two weeks'), so the past passive 'we were informed' is correct as it stands.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Perilous
questions.explanation: 'Perilous' means full of danger: 'dangerous'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Serendipity
questions.explanation: 'Serendipity' is a happy event that comes by chance; a 'godsend' is something good that arrives unexpectedly.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Psychologists discovered that there are two routes (1) ___________ achievement: conformity and originality. Conformity means following the crowd (2) __________ conventional paths and (3) ___________ the status quo. Originality is taking the road (4) __________ travelled, championing a set of novel ideas that go against the grain but (5) __________ making things better.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'Two routes to achievement': 'to' names where the routes lead.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Psychologists discovered that there are two routes (1) ___________ achievement: conformity and originality. Conformity means following the crowd (2) __________ conventional paths and (3) ___________ the status quo. Originality is taking the road (4) __________ travelled, championing a set of novel ideas that go against the grain but (5) __________ making things better.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Following the crowd 'down' conventional paths, that is, along them.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Psychologists discovered that there are two routes (1) ___________ achievement: conformity and originality. Conformity means following the crowd (2) __________ conventional paths and (3) ___________ the status quo. Originality is taking the road (4) __________ travelled, championing a set of novel ideas that go against the grain but (5) __________ making things better.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Conformity means 'maintaining', keeping up, the status quo.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Psychologists discovered that there are two routes (1) ___________ achievement: conformity and originality. Conformity means following the crowd (2) __________ conventional paths and (3) ___________ the status quo. Originality is taking the road (4) __________ travelled, championing a set of novel ideas that go against the grain but (5) __________ making things better.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'The road less travelled' is the fixed phrase for an unconventional choice, the opposite of following the crowd.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Psychologists discovered that there are two routes (1) ___________ achievement: conformity and originality. Conformity means following the crowd (2) __________ conventional paths and (3) ___________ the status quo. Originality is taking the road (4) __________ travelled, championing a set of novel ideas that go against the grain but (5) __________ making things better.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Novel ideas go against the grain but 'ultimately', in the end, make things better.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word and the fourth word is related to the third word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must NOT be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Nut and Bolt : Wrenches :: Screw : Screwdriver :: Nail : ?
questions.explanation: A wrench tightens a nut and bolt and a screwdriver drives a screw; a nail is driven with a hammer.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 10, 20 , 23, ?, 97, 582
questions.explanation: The terms are multiplied and added in turn: 10 × 2 = 20, 20 + 3 = 23, 23 × 4 = 92, 92 + 5 = 97, 97 × 6 = 582.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'GREAT' is codedas '2015187', 'WORK' is codedas '11181523' and 'GOING' is codedas '7149157'. How will ‘WELL' be codedin that language?
questions.explanation: Each word is written backwards as its letters' places in the alphabet: GREAT → T(20) A(1) E(5) R(18) G(7) = 2015187. So WELL → L(12) L(12) E(5) W(23) = 1212523.

questions.text: The second number in the given number pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number pairs, EXCEPT one. Find that odd number pair.
questions.explanation: In 25 : 100, 24 : 96 and 18 : 72 the second number is four times the first. In 22 : 66 it is three times, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 11, 13, 29, 91, 369, ?

Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must NOT be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Car : Bonnet :: Boat : ?
questions.explanation: The bonnet is at the front of a car; the bow is the front of a boat.

questions.text: In a certain code language, “CLIENT” is written as “LCEITN”, and “CLOSED” is written as “LCSODE”. How will “FAMILY” be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each pair of letters is swapped: CL IE NT → LC EI TN and CL OS ED → LC SO DE. So FA MI LY → AF IM YL: AFIMYL.

questions.text: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series to make it logically complete? WDV, TGS, QJP, NMM, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move back 3 (W, T, Q, N, K), second letters forward 3 (D, G, J, M, P) and third letters back 3 (V, S, P, M, J): KPJ.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the sixth term is related to the fifth term. 14 : 21 :: 34 : ? :: 47 : 87
questions.explanation: The second term is twice the first minus 7: 14 × 2 − 7 = 21 and 47 × 2 − 7 = 87. Likewise 34 × 2 − 7 = 61.

questions.text: Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it. First row: 86, 72, 158 Second row: 98, 111, 209 Third row: 76, 65, ? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the number into its constituent digits. For example, 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The third number in each row is the sum of the first two: 86 + 72 = 158 and 98 + 111 = 209. So 76 + 65 = 141.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 62*17*6*81*23*2*37
Select the option that represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in an English dictionary. 1.Sanitization 2.Sanctuary 3.Salvation 4.Salmon 5.Salesman
questions.explanation: Salesman, Salmon and Salvation (s-a-l, then e, m, v) come before Sanctuary and Sanitization (s-a-n, then c, i): 5, 4, 3, 2, 1.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in an English dictionary. 1.Curator 2.Culminate 3.Curriculum 4.Culinary 5.Cucumber
questions.explanation: Cucumber (c-u-c) comes first, then Culinary and Culminate (c-u-l, then i before m), then Curator and Curriculum (c-u-r, then a before r): 5, 4, 2, 1, 3.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 25*5*10*2*4*10

Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it. First row- 2, 57, 7 Second row- 6, 225, 3 Third row- 5, ?, 2 (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed)
questions.explanation: The middle number is the cube of the first plus the square of the third: 2³ + 7² = 8 + 49 = 57 and 6³ + 3² = 216 + 9 = 225. So 5³ + 2² = 125 + 4 = 129.

questions.text: Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All pencils are erasers. All sharpeners are erasers. All compasses are sharpeners. Conclusions: I. All compasses are erasers. II. Some compasses are pencils. III. Some erasers are compass.
options: Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: All compasses are sharpeners and all sharpeners are erasers, so all compasses are erasers (I), and so some erasers are compasses (III). Pencils and compasses are both erasers, but nothing links them, so II does not follow.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series. A B Z _ P A B _ K P A B X K _ A B _ K P
questions.explanation: With K, Y, P, W in the blanks the series reads ABZKP ABYKP ABXKP ABWKP: the third letter steps back Z, Y, X, W.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 1724, 1716,1689,1625,1500,?
questions.explanation: The cubes 2³, 3³, 4³ and 5³ are subtracted in turn: −8, −27, −64, −125. Next 6³: 1500 − 216 = 1284.

questions.text: The Group Leader of a group of 6 students reported that their average weight is 46 kg. When the members of the group were asked about their individual weights, 5 of them answered: 50 kg, 52 kg, 40 kg, 44 kg, 48 kg. The 6th member said, “I can’t recall my weight”. What is his weight?
questions.explanation: The six weigh 6 × 46 = 276 kg in all and the five 50 + 52 + 40 + 44 + 48 = 234 kg, so the sixth weighs 42 kg.

questions.text: What will be the smallest natural number to be filled in the blank for the number ’23_45678’ to be divisible by 22?
questions.explanation: 22 = 2 × 11, and the number ends in 8, so it is even; it must also pass the test for 11. Digits in odd places from the right minus those in even places: (8 + 6 + 4 + 3) − (7 + 5 + x + 2) = 7 − x, which is 0 when x = 7.

questions.text: If the cost price of 70 articles is equal to the selling price of 40 articles, what will be the profit percentage?
questions.explanation: Take the cost of one article as ₹1: 40 articles cost ₹40 and sell for ₹70. Profit = 30/40 = 75%.

questions.text: Kamal purchases 80 articles for ₹11,180 and sells them at a loss equal to the selling price of 6 articles. What will be the selling price of 1 article?
questions.explanation: The loss is the SP of 6 articles, so the cost of 80 articles equals the SP of 86: SP of one = 11,180/86 = ₹130.

questions.text: 700 grams of cane sugar solution has 60% of sugar in it. How much sugar should be added to make it 75% in the solution?
questions.explanation: The 700 g hold 420 g of sugar and 280 g of water. At 75% sugar the water is 25%, so the solution must weigh 1,120 g: 1,120 − 700 = 420 g of sugar to add.

questions.text: If the sum of two numbers is 25 and their product is 144, then what is the position difference between the two numbers?
questions.explanation: (a − b)² = (a + b)² − 4ab = 625 − 576 = 49, so the difference is 7 (the numbers are 16 and 9).

questions.text: A can do a piece of work in 24 days and B can do it in 80 days. B works alone for 2 days and A works alone on the 3rd day. This process continues till the work is completed. In how many days will the work be completed?
questions.explanation: Each 3-day round does 2/80 + 1/24 = 1/40 + 1/24 = 1/15 of the work. 15 rounds finish it exactly: 45 days.

questions.text: The difference between the simple interest and compound interest on ₹1,000 for 1 year at 20% per annum, compounded half-yearly, is:
questions.explanation: SI = ₹200. Compounded half-yearly, at 10% a half-year: 1,000 × 1.1² − 1,000 = ₹210. Difference ₹10.

questions.text: Rakesh runs 4/3 times as fast as Mukesh. In a race, if Rakesh gives a lead of 60 m to Mukesh, find the distance from the starting point where both of them will meet.
questions.explanation: In the same time Rakesh runs 4/3 of Mukesh's distance. If they meet d m from the start, Mukesh has run d − 60: d = (4/3)(d − 60), so d = 240 m.

questions.text: A bike is purchased for ₹50,000. Its rate depreciates at 10% annually. In how many years will its value be ₹36,450?
If 2945 ÷ 19 – 11 × 5 = 29 + a, find the value of a.
If 15 kg of sugar cost ₹600, what is the cost of 25 kg of sugar?
questions.explanation: Sugar costs 600/15 = ₹40 a kg, so 25 kg cost ₹1,000.

questions.text: Nikhil suffers a loss of ₹140 when he sells a perfume at 20% discount. Find the marked price of the perfume if the cost price is ₹380.
questions.explanation: SP = 380 − 140 = ₹240, which is 80% of the marked price: 240/0.8 = ₹300.

questions.text: A family spends ₹240 per month to buy sugar. A rise of 25% in the price of sugar compels the family to reduce the monthly consumption of sugar by 1.5 kg as it decides to spend the same amount of money on purchase of the commodity. What is the increased price per kg of sugar?
questions.explanation: After a 25% rise the same money buys 1/1.25 = 4/5 as much, 1/5 less. That 1/5 is 1.5 kg, so the family used to buy 7.5 kg at 240/7.5 = ₹32 a kg. New price = 32 × 1.25 = ₹40.

questions.text: Who wrote the autobiography entitled ‘I am No Messiah’?
questions.explanation: The actor Sonu Sood's 'I Am No Messiah' (2020) recounts his work helping migrant workers get home during the Covid-19 lockdown.

questions.text: Who wrote the famous novel ‘The Inheritance of Loss’?
questions.explanation: Kiran Desai's 'The Inheritance of Loss' won the Man Booker Prize in 2006.

questions.text: India’s men’s hockey team beat Pakistan to win a bronze medal in December 2021 at the:
questions.explanation: India beat Pakistan 4-3 in the bronze-medal match of the Asian Champions Trophy in Dhaka in December 2021.

questions.text: ______________is the money which is accepted as a medium of exchange because of the trust between the payer and the payee.
questions.explanation: Fiduciary money, such as a cheque, is accepted because of trust between payer and payee; fiat money (currency notes and coins) is money by order of the government.

questions.text: In which sport are arrows used?
questions.explanation: In archery arrows are shot from a bow at a target.

questions.text: Rajeev Janardan is an Indian classical __________ player of the Imdadkhani gharana.
questions.explanation: Rajeev Janardan is a sitar (and surbahar) player of the Imdadkhani gharana, a pupil of Bimalendu Mukherjee and Arvind Parikh.

questions.text: Tulsidas Borkar, who was awarded with the Padma Shri in 2016, was a _________ player.
questions.explanation: Tulsidas Borkar of Goa was a noted harmonium player; he received the Padma Shri in 2016.

questions.text: Dr. Tamilisai Soundararajan was given the additional charge of ________ and was sworn in as the Lt. Governor of this Union Territory in February 2021, apart from being the Governor of Telangana.
questions.explanation: When Kiran Bedi was removed in February 2021, Tamilisai Soundararajan, Governor of Telangana, was given additional charge as Lieutenant Governor of Puducherry.

questions.text: Aqua regia is an acidic, corrosive and oxidative mixture consisting of ________ volume/volumes of concentrated hydrochloric acid and one volume of concentrated nitric acid, often used to dissolve gold and platinum.
questions.explanation: Aqua regia is three parts concentrated hydrochloric acid to one part concentrated nitric acid, by volume.

questions.text: Maithili Thakur and Lydian Nadhaswaram were bestowed with Sur Jyotsna National Music Awards _____________.
questions.explanation: Lokmat's Sur Jyotsna National Music Awards 2021 went to the singer Maithili Thakur and the pianist Lydian Nadhaswaram.

questions.text: Which compound has the chemical formula CHCl₃ whose melting point is 209 K?
questions.explanation: CHCl₃ is chloroform (trichloromethane), which melts at about −64 °C, or 209 K.

questions.text: Who was the runner-up of Yonex Swiss open 2021 women single badminton tournament?
questions.explanation: Carolina Marin beat PV Sindhu in the women's singles final of the Swiss Open in March 2021.

questions.text: Who among the following Sadir dancer received the Padma Shri 2022?
questions.explanation: R Muthukannammal of Viralimalai, Tamil Nadu, one of the last Sadir dancers of the temple tradition, received the Padma Shri in 2022.

questions.text: The famous Jhaveri sisters are associated with the _________classical dance form.
questions.explanation: The Jhaveri sisters of Mumbai are known for performing, teaching and spreading Manipuri dance.

questions.text: The Northern Plains of India are made of alluvial soil. They are formed by the interplay of which three rivers?
questions.explanation: The Northern Plains were built up from the alluvium of the Indus, the Ganga and the Brahmaputra and their tributaries.

questions.text: Which inorganic compound is used to manufacture soap, rayon, paper, explosives, dyes, and petroleum products?
questions.explanation: Sodium hydroxide (caustic soda), made by the chlor-alkali process, is used to make soap, rayon, paper, explosives and dyes and in refining petroleum.

questions.text: Pandit Bhimsen Guracharya Joshi was an Indian classical vocalist born in ___________.
questions.explanation: Pandit Bhimsen Joshi, the Kirana gharana vocalist, was born in 1922 at Ron, in what is now the Gadag district of Karnataka.

questions.text: Which State Government will provide financial support to Indian wrestling till 2032 Olympics?
questions.explanation: In 2021 the Uttar Pradesh government undertook to back Indian wrestling until the 2032 Olympics.

questions.text: Which red-orange pigment found in plants and fruits, especially carrots and colourful vegetables, acts as a powerful antioxidant that can benefit our brain, skin, lungs, and eye health?
questions.explanation: Beta-carotene, the red-orange pigment of carrots, is an antioxidant that the body turns into vitamin A.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: ‘Waiting for a Visa’ is an autobiographical work of which of the following leaders of India?
questions.explanation: 'Waiting for a Visa' is B. R. Ambedkar's short autobiographical account of the untouchability he faced.

questions.text: Haleem Khan is associated with which of the following classical dances?
questions.explanation: Haleem Khan is a Kuchipudi dancer from Andhra Pradesh, known for performing female roles.

questions.text: What test is used where the elements present in the compound are converted from covalent form into the ionic form by fusing the compound with sodium metal?
questions.explanation: In Lassaigne's test the organic compound is fused with sodium, turning its nitrogen, sulphur and halogens into ionic sodium salts that can then be detected.

questions.text: Members of Public Accounts Committee are elected for a period of:
questions.explanation: The Public Accounts Committee is elected by Parliament every year, so its members serve for one year.

questions.text: Guru Makar Dhwaja Darogha, was conferred the Padma Shri award for his contribution to which form of dance in India?
questions.explanation: Guru Makar Dhwaja Darogha of Seraikela, Jharkhand, received the Padma Shri in 2011 for Chhau dance.

questions.text: Which English ecologist was the first to describe the distinctive shape of the food web, which he called the pyramid of numbers?
questions.explanation: Charles Elton described the pyramid of numbers in 'Animal Ecology' (1927); it is also called the Eltonian pyramid.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underline segment in the given sentence. My sincerity and patience “drove me” through all odds and problems of life
questions.explanation: To 'carry someone through' a hard time is to help them get through it: 'My sincerity and patience carried me through all odds'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence. He is “an excessively enthusiastic and strict follower” of Judaism.
questions.explanation: A zealot is a fanatical, uncompromising follower of a religion or cause. A Zionist supports a Jewish homeland, and a janissary was a Turkish soldier.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined part in the given sentence. Her writing is very “ilegible” and so she loses marks in her exam.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'illegible' (not readable), with a double 'l'; 'illegal' means against the law.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. My uncle “is doing” business in Hyderabad for the last 10 years.
questions.explanation: An action that began in the past and is still going on, 'for the last 10 years', takes the present perfect continuous: 'has been doing'.

questions.text: Complete the sentence with an appropriate synonym of the word mentioned in the bracket. The party was so amazing that everyone _________ (hated) leaving it.
questions.explanation: To 'loathe' something is to hate it intensely.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in the brackets to fill in the blank. Doing adventure sports is banned for athletes as it can be ___________ (perilous).
questions.explanation: 'Perilous' means full of danger: 'treacherous'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. The library building was renovated in 2020.
options: They were renovating the building in 2020.
They had renovated the library building in 2020.
They renovated the library building in 2020.
They did renovating the building in 2020.
questions.explanation: The simple past passive 'was renovated' becomes the simple past active 'renovated', with 'They' for the unnamed doer.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. Has the assignment been uploaded by you?
options: Have you been uploaded the assignment?
questions.explanation: The present perfect passive question 'Has ... been uploaded by you?' becomes the present perfect active 'Have you uploaded ...?'

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. Coffee is sipped by me.
questions.explanation: The simple present passive 'is sipped by me' becomes the simple present active 'I sip'.

questions.text: In the following passage, a word has been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Manpower exporters and overseas recruiters commonly __________ in illegal business practices for short-term _______ gain.
questions.explanation: To 'indulge in' is to take part in something, often something wrong; the short-term gain they seek is 'monetary', that is financial.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Grease someone’s palm
questions.explanation: To 'grease someone's palm' is to bribe them.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'embarrassment', with a double 'r' and a double 's'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. She is “educated” than her sister.
questions.explanation: 'Than' needs a comparative: 'She is more educated than her sister.'

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. I went to college from the eleventh grade and never went to the twelfth grade, and skipped another grade earlier, so I was a pretty young fellow at Morehouse. B. At the age of fifteen, I entered Morehouse College and my father and my maternal grandfather had also attended, so Morehouse has had three generations of Kings. C. The professors were not caught up in the clutches of state funds and could teach what they wanted with academic freedom and encouraged us in a positive quest for a solution to racial ills. D. I shall never forget the hardships that I had upon entering college, for though I had been one of the top students in high school, I was still reading at only an eighth-grade level.
questions.explanation: B introduces Morehouse, D recalls the hardships of entering it, A explains why he was so young (he had skipped two grades), and C turns to the professors: BDAC, the order of King's own account.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. I keep telling myself “how I am lucky to have” such wonderful sisters.
options: how lucky I am to have
how lucky I am to having
how I am lucky for having
questions.explanation: In an exclamation introduced by 'how', the adjective comes straight after it and the subject before the verb: 'how lucky I am to have'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Yoga is a personal journey for everyone as now most people are turning to it, not for fitness (1) ________, but for the union of both, body and soul. Yoga is an ancient practice that (2) _________ in India. It involves movement, meditation and breathing (3) _________ to promote mental and physical well-being. There are many styles of yoga. A person should (4) __________ a style based on their goals and fitness level. If yoga and pranayam are complemented with other forms of spiritual practice to purify the mental body and other bodies, then a person can achieve rapid spiritual progress in his lifetime. Thus a person can make progress to achieve the purpose of life which is to (5) __________ with God.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'Not for fitness alone, but for the union of both': not only for fitness.

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Yoga is a personal journey for everyone as now most people are turning to it, not for fitness (1) ________, but for the union of both, body and soul.
