questions.explanation: The eight marks add up to 8 × 75 = 600 and the middle six to 6 × 80 = 480, so the highest and lowest add up to 120. In the ratio 3 : 1 they are 90 and 30, and 90/600 = 15%.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 7, 10, 18, 29, ?, 78
questions.explanation: The differences are 3, 8, 11, 19, 30, each the sum of the two before it. So 29 + 19 = 48, and 48 + 30 = 78.

questions.text: In a certain code language, BIRTH is coded as 25129719 and DEVIL is coded as 23851215. How will GLORY be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each consonant is coded by the position of its opposite letter (B → Y = 25, R → I = 9, D → W = 23) and each vowel by its own position plus 3 (I → 12, E → 8). GLORY: G → 20, L → 15, O → 18, R → 9, Y → 2: 20151892.

questions.text: Four words have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the word that is different
questions.explanation: Violet, yellow and orange are colours of the rainbow (VIBGYOR); black is not.

questions.text: ‘Risk’ is related to ‘Hazard’ in the same way as ‘Absurd’ is related to ‘______’.
questions.explanation: 'Hazard' means the same as 'risk', and 'ridiculous' the same as 'absurd'.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series. c _ t e m c p _ e m _ p t _ _
questions.explanation: With p, t, c, e, m in the blanks the block 'cptem' repeats: cptem cptem cptem.

questions.text: Four numbers have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the number that is different.
questions.explanation: 146 = 12² + 2, 198 = 14² + 2 and 326 = 18² + 2. 378 − 2 = 376 is not a perfect square, so 378 is the odd one.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some dogs are carnivores. All carnivores are animals. Some animals are tigers. Conclusions: I. Some tigers are dogs. II. Some carnivores are tigers. III. All dogs are animals.
options: Only conclusions I and III follow.
questions.explanation: Nothing links tigers to dogs or to carnivores, so I and II need not follow. Only the dogs that are carnivores must be animals, so III need not follow either.

questions.text: Four letter-clusters have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the letter-cluster that is different.
questions.explanation: In PTZW, MQWT and FJPM the letters move +4, +6, −3. In TXDB they move +4, +6 (X → D, counting round) and then −2, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the following equation correct? 6 +12 × 8 ÷ 16 – 12 = 8
In a certain code language, RATIONALE is written as NOIELATAR. How will STATEMENT be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The word is split into three blocks of three, each block is reversed, and the blocks are put in the order second, third, first: RAT ION ALE → NOI ELA TAR. So STA TEM ENT → MET TNE ATS: METTNEATS.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number. 8 : 36 : : 12 : ?
questions.explanation: 36 is the sum of 1 to 8, 8 × 9 ÷ 2. Likewise 12 × 13 ÷ 2 = 78.

questions.text: ______ contains and manages all the programs and applications that a computer or other device is able to run.
questions.explanation: The operating system, such as Windows, Android or Linux, manages the device's resources and all the programs and applications that run on it.

questions.text: As on 9 December 2020, how many states of India have implemented 'one nation one ration card system'?
questions.explanation: On 9 December 2020 the Finance Ministry said nine states had completed the One Nation One Ration Card reform, which earned them extra borrowing of ₹23,523 crore.

questions.text: In which of the following countries is the headquarters of International Table Tennis Federation situated?
questions.explanation: The International Table Tennis Federation has its headquarters in Lausanne, Switzerland.

questions.text: A ______ is a hydraulic structure of impervious material built across a river to create a reservoir on its upstream side for impounding water for various purposes.
questions.explanation: A dam is a barrier of impervious material built across a river; the water it holds back on its upstream side forms a reservoir.

questions.text: What was the contribution of the manufacturing sector in India’s GDP in Q2 of 2020-21?
questions.explanation: In the NSO's estimates for July-September 2020, released in November 2020, manufacturing GVA grew 0.6% while GDP shrank 7.5%.

questions.text: What is the keyboard shortcut to add a new row above a given row in Microsoft Excel?
questions.explanation: Alt + I + R opens Excel's Insert menu (I) and inserts a row (R) above the selected cell. Shift + Spacebar only selects the row.

questions.text: The minimum paid up equity capital to set up a small finance bank should be of _______, as proposed by RBI as of May 2020.
questions.explanation: Under RBI's guidelines of December 2019 for 'on tap' licensing, a new small finance bank needs a minimum paid-up voting equity capital of ₹200 crore.

questions.text: Who among the following was elected as the President of the All India Chess Federation in January 2021?
questions.explanation: Sanjay Kapoor was elected President of the All India Chess Federation in its election of January 2021, with Bharat Singh Chauhan as Secretary.

questions.text: Which of the following institutes bagged the UNESCO Asia-Pacific Award for cultural heritage conservation in December, 2020?
questions.explanation: The restoration of Amar Singh College, Srinagar, received an Award of Merit in the 2020 UNESCO Asia-Pacific Awards for Cultural Heritage Conservation, announced in December 2020.

questions.text: Who among the following was conferred the title of 'Global Visionary of Sustainable Business and Peace' in 2020 by the Federation of Israel Chambers of Commerce for epitomising 'unity, peace and sustainability'?
questions.explanation: Ratan Tata received the 'Global Visionary of Sustainable Business and Peace' award in December 2020 from the Federation of Indo-Israel Chambers of Commerce.

questions.text: Sur Sarovar, also known as Keetham Lake, is a man-made reservoir. In which of the following years was it added in the list of Ramsar Sites?
questions.explanation: Sur Sarovar, near Agra in Uttar Pradesh, was added to the list of Ramsar sites in 2020; its listing was announced in November 2020.

questions.text: CSIR as an autonomous body is the largest research and development organisation in India. What does CSIR stands for?
options: Council of Scientific and Industrial Research
Council of Space and Industrial Research
Centre of Space and Industrial Research
Chamber of States and Industrial Research
questions.explanation: CSIR is the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research, set up in 1942.

questions.text: Which doctor of Indian origin was honoured with 'Great Immigrants-2020' in the US?
questions.explanation: The Carnegie Corporation of New York named the oncologist and author Siddhartha Mukherjee among its 'Great Immigrants' of 2020, for his work explaining COVID-19 to the public.

questions.text: Which of the following banks was declared as the ’Safest Bank in Asia’ for the 12th consecutive year by New York-based trade publication ‘Global Finance’ in 2020?
questions.explanation: Global Finance named Singapore's DBS the Safest Bank in Asia for the 12th consecutive year in 2020.

questions.text: To which group of organic molecules does 'Monosaccharides' belong?
questions.explanation: Monosaccharides, such as glucose and fructose, are the simplest carbohydrates, the units from which disaccharides and polysaccharides are built.

questions.text: Who among the following won the 2002 International Shooting Sport Federation (ISSF) Champion of Champions combined-air-rifle event to become the first Indian to win that competition?
questions.explanation: Anjali Bhagwat won the ISSF Champion of Champions combined air rifle event in 2002, the first Indian to win it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Traditional
questions.explanation: 'Traditional' means following long-established custom; its opposite is 'modern'. 'Customary' and 'conventional' are synonyms.

questions.text: Select the option which means the same as the group of words given. A hunting weapon which comes back, used by Australian Aborigines
questions.explanation: A boomerang is the curved throwing weapon of the Australian Aborigines that comes back to the thrower.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. It would be / more better if / she sang / with an orchestra.
questions.explanation: 'Better' is already comparative, so 'more better' is a double comparative: 'It would be better if she sang with an orchestra.'

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech. "Our teacher returned from Mumbai last month", she said.
options: She said that her teacher had returned from Mumbai the earlier month.
Her teacher returned from Mumbai last month, she said.
She said that their teacher had returned from Mumbai the previous month.
She said that her teacher had returned from Mumbai the previous month.
questions.explanation: 'Our' (first person plural) becomes 'their', the past 'returned' becomes 'had returned' and 'last month' becomes 'the previous month'.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. In the evening we water the plants.
options: The plants will be watered in the evening.
The plants are watered in the evening.
The plants have been watered in the evening.
The plants were watered in the evening.
questions.explanation: The simple present 'water' becomes 'are watered', and the agent 'by us' is dropped.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Causing a strong dislike
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'repulsive', which dictionaries define in just these words: causing a feeling of strong dislike or disgust. 'Hateful' is close, but it centres on hatred (arousing it, or full of it); 'redundant' means not needed and 'revealing' showing something.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. Mr. Sharma is “kind as” his father.
questions.explanation: A comparison of equals takes 'as … as': 'Mr. Sharma is as kind as his father.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Not one’s cup of tea
questions.explanation: Something that is 'not one's cup of tea' is not what one likes or is interested in.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, pick the one that gives their correct order. A. The man who had caught me was a dreadful sight. B. Suddenly I was picked up, whirled through the air, and made to sit on a tombstone. C. He was about forty years old, hard-faced and fierce. D. I was only a child, and small for my age.
questions.explanation: D introduces the narrator, B tells what happened to him, A turns to the man who had caught him and C describes the man: DBAC.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. The whole area has been designed like a garden from Alice in Wonderland. B. It’s about having fun and learning, too; all the activities help to explain the modern world of technology to the young visitors. C. But ‘The World of Children’ isn’t just about playing games and having joy rides. D. There are several different attractions in this vast area and there is a lot to see and do.
questions.explanation: D introduces the area and its attractions, A describes its design, C ('But') says it is not just about games and rides, and B says what else it offers: DACB.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'rockery'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. REPULSIVE
questions.explanation: 'Repulsive' means causing disgust: 'disgusting'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'. He won’t come to the party unless you “will invite” him personally.
questions.explanation: After 'unless', the simple present refers to the future: 'unless you invite him personally'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiomatic expression given. To cross one’s mind
options: To put a thought away from one’s mind
To move from one idea to another
questions.explanation: When something 'crosses one's mind', one thinks of it, usually briefly.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. The marking of answer papers is ______ out by the course teacher.
questions.explanation: To 'carry out' a task is to perform it: 'The marking of answer papers is carried out by the course teacher.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. BUOYANT
questions.explanation: 'Buoyant' means able to float, or light and cheerful; 'weighted', held down by weight, is the opposite. 'Enthusiastic', 'lively' and 'bouncy' are synonyms.

questions.text: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. Cyclone Amphan roared into West Bengal on Wednesday leave behind a trail of devastation across a large area of the State.
questions.explanation: The second action needs the participle: 'roared into West Bengal on Wednesday, leaving behind a trail of devastation'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Ban
questions.explanation: To 'ban' something is to 'prohibit' it.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Every Monday, on his way back from work, Bepin Chaudhury would drop in at KaliCharan’s in New Market (1)______ books. Crime stories, ghost stories, and thrillers. (2)______ had to buy at least five at a time to last him (3)______ the week. He lived alone, was not a good mixer, had few (4)______ , and didn't like spending time in idle chat. Today, at KaliCharan's, Bepin Babu had a (5)______ that somebody was observing him from close quarters.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 1.
questions.explanation: Purpose is shown by the infinitive: he would drop in at the shop 'to buy' books.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Every Monday, on his way back from work, Bepin Chaudhury would drop in at KaliCharan’s in New Market (1)______ books. Crime stories, ghost stories, and thrillers. (2)______ had to buy at least five at a time to last him (3)______ the week. He lived alone, was not a good mixer, had few (4)______ , and didn't like spending time in idle chat. Today, at KaliCharan's, Bepin Babu had a (5)______ that somebody was observing him from close quarters.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 2.
questions.explanation: Bepin Chaudhury is a man, so the subject pronoun is 'He'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Every Monday, on his way back from work, Bepin Chaudhury would drop in at KaliCharan’s in New Market (1)______ books. Crime stories, ghost stories, and thrillers. (2)______ had to buy at least five at a time to last him (3)______ the week. He lived alone, was not a good mixer, had few (4)______ , and didn't like spending time in idle chat. Today, at KaliCharan's, Bepin Babu had a (5)______ that somebody was observing him from close quarters.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 3.
questions.explanation: The five books had to last him 'through' the week, from beginning to end.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Every Monday, on his way back from work, Bepin Chaudhury would drop in at KaliCharan’s in New Market (1)______ books. Crime stories, ghost stories, and thrillers. (2)______ had to buy at least five at a time to last him (3)______ the week. He lived alone, was not a good mixer, had few (4)______ , and didn't like spending time in idle chat. Today, at KaliCharan's, Bepin Babu had a (5)______ that somebody was observing him from close quarters.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 4.
questions.explanation: He was not a good mixer and had few 'friends'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Every Monday, on his way back from work, Bepin Chaudhury would drop in at KaliCharan’s in New Market (1)______ books. Crime stories, ghost stories, and thrillers. (2)______ had to buy at least five at a time to last him (3)______ the week. He lived alone, was not a good mixer, had few (4)______ , and didn't like spending time in idle chat. Today, at KaliCharan's, Bepin Babu had a (5)______ that somebody was observing him from close quarters.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 5.
questions.explanation: To 'have a feeling that' is to sense something without being sure of it: somebody seemed to be watching him.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (2, 3, 62)
questions.explanation: The third number is twice the sum of the square of the first and the cube of the second: 2 × (2² + 3³) = 2 × 31 = 62. Likewise 2 × (7² + 4³) = 2 × 113 = 226.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers in the set share the same relationship as that shared by the numbers of the given set. (14, 18, 42)
questions.explanation: The third number is the product of the first two divided by 6: 14 × 18 ÷ 6 = 42. Likewise 16 × 21 ÷ 6 = 56.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs to balance the following equation. 40 * 15 * 3 * 72 * 9 = 77
questions.explanation: Every option ends with the '=' already printed before 77: 40 + 15 × 3 − 72 ÷ 9 = 40 + 45 − 8 = 77.

questions.text: Three of the following four words are alike in a certain way and one is different. Select the odd one.
questions.explanation: The heart, lungs and liver are internal organs; the nose is on the outside of the body.

questions.text: Select the correct option that indicates the arrangement of the given words in the order in which they appear in an English dictionary. 1. Industry 2. Indent 3. Indoor 4. Indolent 5. Index
questions.explanation: Indent, Index (n before x), Indolent, Indoor (l before o), Industry (u after o): 2, 5, 4, 3, 1.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series. c k _ g k c _ t _ k _ k t g _ c k _ g k
options: t, k, g, c, k, t
t, k, g, c, c, t
t, g, k, c, k, t
t, k, c, g, k, t
questions.explanation: With t, k, g, c, k, t in the blanks the block cktgk repeats: cktgk cktgk cktgk cktgk.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fourth number in the same way as the first number is related to the second number and the fifth number is related to the sixth number. 127 : 11 :: ? : 16 :: 367 : 19
questions.explanation: Each larger number is the square of its pair plus 6: 11² + 6 = 127 and 19² + 6 = 367. Likewise 16² + 6 = 262.

questions.text: Select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 25, 26, 53, 160, 641, ?
Four letter-clusters have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the letter-cluster that is different.
questions.explanation: In HNTZ, AGMS and VBHN each letter is 6 places after the one before it (B follows V by wrapping round after Z). IPVA moves +7, +6, +5, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. AZW : GFC : : LSM : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 6 places forward, wrapping round after Z: A → G, Z → F, W → C. So L → R, S → Y and M → S: RYS.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'FROZEN' is coded as '504' and 'TONSILS' is coded as '756'. How will 'MARINE' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: The code is the sum of the letters' places in the alphabet times the number of letters: FROZEN = 84 × 6 = 504 and TONSILS = 108 × 7 = 756. MARINE = (13 + 1 + 18 + 9 + 14 + 5) × 6 = 60 × 6 = 360.

questions.text: In a code language, TOUCH is written as UTOHC. How will PLANT be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters are written in reverse alphabetical order: TOUCH → U T O H C, so PLANT → T P N L A.

questions.text: Two statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: No field is a house. All fields are parks. Conclusions: I. No house is a field. II. Some parks are fields. III. Some houses are fields.
options: Only conclusions II and III follow
Only conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: 'No field is a house' converts to 'No house is a field' (I), and 'All fields are parks' gives 'Some parks are fields' (II). III contradicts the first statement.

questions.text: Four number-pairs have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the number-pair that is different.
questions.explanation: In the other pairs the second number is the first times two more than itself: 7 × 9 = 63, 5 × 7 = 35 and 13 × 15 = 195. 19 × 21 = 399, not 324, so 19 : 324 is the odd one.

questions.text: In a class of 68 students, 34 students participated only in Debate and 8 students participated in both Quiz and Debate. If every student of the class has participated in at least one of these two competitions, how many students participated in Quiz?
questions.explanation: Everyone not in Debate only took part in Quiz: 68 − 34 = 34 (26 in Quiz only and 8 in both).

questions.text: If 'A & B' means 'A is the father of B' and 'A @ B' means 'A is the sister of B', then which of the following expressions means 'H is the father of M'?
questions.explanation: H & K: H is K's father. K @ P @ M: K is P's sister and P is M's sister, so K, P and M are siblings and H is M's father.

questions.text: Select the option in which the words share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of words. Astronomy : Stars
questions.explanation: Astronomy is the study of stars, as numismatics is the study of coins.

questions.text: ‘East’ is related to ‘Direction’ in the same way as ‘Summer’ is related to ‘______’.
questions.explanation: East is a direction, as summer is a season.

questions.text: National Rifle Association of India was founded in:
questions.explanation: The National Rifle Association of India, the governing body for shooting sports, was founded in 1951.

questions.text: Which of the following factors is NOT responsible for soil formation?
questions.explanation: Soil forms from its parent material under the influence of relief (topography), climate, living organisms and time. Cattle grazing is not one of these factors; overgrazing is a cause of soil erosion.

questions.text: Who among the following was NOT included in the ICC Hall of Fame in August 2020?
questions.explanation: Jacques Kallis, Zaheer Abbas and Lisa Sthalekar were inducted into the ICC Hall of Fame in August 2020; Graeme Smith was not among them.

questions.text: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India is related to the oath or affirmation by the President?
questions.explanation: Article 60 lays down the President's oath or affirmation. Article 54 is on the President's election, Article 57 on eligibility for re-election and Article 66 on the Vice-President's election.

questions.text: Rickets and night-blindness are caused by the deficiency of ______ and ______, respectively.
questions.explanation: A lack of vitamin D causes rickets (soft, weak bones in children); a lack of vitamin A causes night-blindness.

questions.text: Who among the following foreign travellers is NOT correctly matched with their respective country they hail from?
questions.explanation: Peter Mundy was an English traveller who visited India in Shah Jahan's reign. Marco Polo was from Venice (Italy), Ibn Battuta from Tangier (Morocco) and Al-Biruni from Khwarazm, now in Uzbekistan.

questions.text: With which of the following states is the ‘Mand’ or ‘Maand' style of singing associated?
questions.explanation: Maand is a folk singing style of Rajasthan, made famous by singers such as Allah Jilai Bai.

questions.text: With which country did India hold its 14th Defence Policy Dialogue via video conferencing in August 2020?
questions.explanation: The 14th India-Singapore Defence Policy Dialogue was held by video conference on 28 August 2020.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is NOT correct about alluvial soil?
options: Deltas of Mahanadi, the Godavari and the Krishna are made from alluvial soil.
Old alluvial is called ‘bangar’ and new alluvial is called ‘khadar’.
In the Himalayan region we find alluvial soil.
Northern plains are made of alluvial soil.
questions.explanation: Alluvial soil covers the northern plains and the river deltas of the east coast; the Himalayan region has mountain soils. 'Bangar' (old alluvium) and 'khadar' (new alluvium) are its two kinds.

questions.text: As of January 2021, GMR Group was associated with which of the following franchises in the Indian Premier League (IPL) cricket tournament?
questions.explanation: The GMR Group co-owns Delhi Capitals (formerly Delhi Daredevils), with the JSW Group since 2018.

questions.text: According to the fundamental rights provided by the Constitution of India, the state is bound to provide free and compulsory education to all children from the age of:
questions.explanation: Article 21A, added by the 86th Amendment in 2002, makes free and compulsory education a fundamental right of children aged 6 to 14.

questions.text: Swollen bluish veins resulting from the valves that do not close properly are called ______.
questions.explanation: Varicose veins are swollen, twisted veins, usually in the legs, where faulty valves let blood pool.

questions.text: Dogri language is mainly spoken in which of the following states/union territories?
questions.explanation: Dogri is spoken mainly in the Jammu region of Jammu and Kashmir; it was added to the Eighth Schedule by the 92nd Amendment Act, 2003.

questions.text: Which of the following states was popularly known as the ‘Land of Gods’? It got a separate identity as a state on 9 November 2000.
questions.explanation: Uttarakhand, called Devbhoomi (Land of Gods) for its many shrines, was carved out of Uttar Pradesh on 9 November 2000.

questions.text: 'Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Urban)-PMAY (U)’s mission is to achieve the goal of Housing for All in urban areas by:
questions.explanation: PMAY (Urban), launched in 2015, set out to provide housing for all in urban areas by 2022, the 75th year of independence.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an example of an optical disk?
questions.explanation: PROM (programmable read-only memory) is a memory chip. Blu-ray discs, CD-ROMs and DVDs are optical discs, read by a laser.

questions.text: A device or program that enables a computer to transmit data over telephone or cable lines is called:
questions.explanation: A modem (modulator-demodulator) converts a computer's digital data into signals that can travel over telephone or cable lines, and back.

questions.text: Where was the Patrika Gate inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in September 2020?
questions.explanation: In September 2020 the Prime Minister inaugurated, by video conference, the Patrika Gate at Jawahar Circle in Jaipur.

questions.text: Who among the following was honoured with the long-overdue record title for ‘fastest human computation’ by Guinness World Records on 30 July 2020?
questions.explanation: Shakuntala Devi, the 'human computer', multiplied two 13-digit numbers in 28 seconds in 1980; Guinness World Records presented the certificate for it to her daughter in 2020.

questions.text: The mutual funds industry in India is regulated by which of the following organisations?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives SEBI and RBI: SEBI registers and regulates mutual funds, and the RBI comes in as the regulator of the banks that sponsor some of them. None of the other bodies regulates the industry.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following was responsible for the partition of Bengal in 1905?
questions.explanation: Lord Curzon, Viceroy from 1899 to 1905, partitioned Bengal in 1905; the partition was annulled in 1911.

questions.text: Where is the Sariska Tiger Reserve located?
questions.explanation: Sariska Tiger Reserve is in the Aravalli hills of Alwar district, Rajasthan.

questions.text: In September 2020, who was appointed as Executive Director of Asian Development Bank, Manila?
questions.explanation: In September 2020 the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet approved Sameer Kumar Khare, an Additional Secretary in the Department of Economic Affairs, as Executive Director at the ADB; Rajesh Khullar went to the World Bank.

questions.text: Which of the following gases is released in the process of photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis uses carbon dioxide and water and releases oxygen.

questions.text: The total liability of the monetary authority of the country, Reserve Bank of India, is called:
questions.explanation: NCERT's macroeconomics calls the total liability of the RBI the monetary base, or high powered money: currency held by the public, banks' vault cash, and the deposits of banks and the government with the RBI.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, select the one that gives their correct order. A. He told his friends that his difficulties were a sign of God’s confidence in him. B. A businessman remained cheerful even though he suffered one catastrophe after another. C. Therefore, when he was serving in the armed forces too, his senior officer had chosen him for dangerous missions because he knew he could be trusted. D. First, his son had a serious accident and then he had huge losses in his business, but he was not perturbed.
questions.explanation: B introduces the cheerful businessman, D lists his misfortunes ('First, ...'), A gives his view of them, and C, with 'Therefore', links that view to the trust his senior officer once showed in him: BDAC.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'acceptance'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Travail
questions.explanation: 'Travail' is painful, exhausting effort or suffering: 'agony'. It does not mean a journey.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. Doctors and nurses who are treating COVID-19 patients are finding it difficult ______ long working hours.
questions.explanation: To 'cope with' something is to deal with it successfully, and 'difficult' takes a to-infinitive: 'finding it difficult to cope with long working hours'.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. Sarita said to me, “I’m glad I did not leave my village.”
options: Sarita told me she was glad she was not leaving her village.
Sarita told me she is glad she had not left her village.
Sarita told me I am glad she had not left her village.
Sarita told me she was glad she had not left her village.
questions.explanation: After 'said', the present 'I'm' becomes 'she was', the past 'did not leave' becomes the past perfect 'had not left', and 'my village' becomes 'her village'.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. In other words, chess and basketball are contests. B. As games, chess and basketball are obviously different from leapfrog and playing house. C. One can win a game of basketball, but it makes no sense to ask who has won a game of leapfrog. D. The first two games are competitive, the second two are not.
questions.explanation: B contrasts the two pairs of games, D says how they differ (the first two are competitive), C illustrates it, and A sums up with 'In other words': BDCA.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. CORDIAL
questions.explanation: 'Cordial' means warm and 'friendly'; 'hostile' is its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. Everything in the village was grown organically as the majority of the population indulged in farming for _____.
questions.explanation: Farming 'for sustenance' is growing food to live on, not for sale.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Off and on
questions.explanation: 'Off and on' means from time to time, not regularly.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Hang on every word
questions.explanation: To 'hang on every word' is to listen very carefully to someone, usually with admiration.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. ABUNDANCE
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'abundance', a great quantity, is 'scarcity'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. There is constant friction / between the executive members / of the Association.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives this part, on the rule that 'between' is used of two and 'among' of more than two: 'friction among the executive members'. ('Between' is also widely used of relations within a larger group, so 'No error' is arguable.)

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Exclusive
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'exclusive', keeping others out, is 'inclusive'.

questions.text: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. Each players must play according to his full potential and not think only about winning.
questions.explanation: 'Each' takes a singular noun: 'Each player must play according to his full potential'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. If you “tries” to dictate your terms, I don’t think we can work together.
questions.explanation: 'You' takes the plain form of the verb, not the -s form: 'If you try to dictate your terms'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. Arvind delivered the packet at the address given by Asha.
options: The packet had been delivered at the address given by Arvind.
The packet was being delivered by Arvind at the address given by Asha.
The packet was delivered by Arvind at the address given by Asha.
Asha delivered the packet at the address given by Arvind.
questions.explanation: The past simple 'delivered' becomes 'was delivered', with 'the packet' as the subject and Arvind as the agent: 'The packet was delivered by Arvind at the address given by Asha.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Certain to happen
questions.explanation: 'Inevitable' means certain to happen, unavoidable.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. “Most of us” hesitate to accept our mistakes.
questions.explanation: 'Most of us' (the greater part of us) is correct as it stands. 'Much' is used with uncountable nouns, and 'more' and 'lots many' do not fit.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. people existing or living at the same time
questions.explanation: 'Contemporaries' are people living or working at the same time.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The short story in literature is usually concerned with a single effect conveyed in only one or (1) _____ few significant episodes or scenes. (2) The _____ encourages economy of setting, (3)_____ narrative, and the omission of a (4) _____ plot; character is disclosed in action and a (5) _____ encounter but is seldom fully developed. Despite its relatively limited scope, though, a short story is often judged by its ability to provide a ‘complete’ or satisfying treatment of its characters and subject.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no.1.
questions.explanation: 'Only one or a few significant episodes': 'a few' means some, while 'few' alone would mean hardly any.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The short story in literature is usually concerned with a single effect conveyed in only one or (1) _____ few significant episodes or scenes. (2) The _____ encourages economy of setting, (3)_____ narrative, and the omission of a (4) _____ plot; character is disclosed in action and a (5) _____ encounter but is seldom fully developed. Despite its relatively limited scope, though, a short story is often judged by its ability to provide a ‘complete’ or satisfying treatment of its characters and subject.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no.3.
questions.explanation: Along with economy of setting, the short story favours a 'concise', brief narrative; 'curt' describes a rude, abrupt manner of speaking.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The short story in literature is usually concerned with a single effect conveyed in only one or (1) _____ few significant episodes or scenes. (2) The _____ encourages economy of setting, (3)_____ narrative, and the omission of a (4) _____ plot; character is disclosed in action and a (5) _____ encounter but is seldom fully developed. Despite its relatively limited scope, though, a short story is often judged by its ability to provide a ‘complete’ or satisfying treatment of its characters and subject.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no.4.
questions.explanation: The short story leaves out a 'complex', intricate plot.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The short story in literature is usually concerned with a single effect conveyed in only one or (1) _____ few significant episodes or scenes. (2) The _____ encourages economy of setting, (3)_____ narrative, and the omission of a (4) _____ plot; character is disclosed in action and a (5) _____ encounter but is seldom fully developed. Despite its relatively limited scope, though, a short story is often judged by its ability to provide a ‘complete’ or satisfying treatment of its characters and subject.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no.5.
questions.explanation: Character is shown in action and in a 'dramatic' encounter, one full of conflict or tension.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term. PAINTER : AEINPRT : : GLAMOUR : ?
questions.explanation: The letters of the word are put in alphabetical order: PAINTER → A E I N P R T. So GLAMOUR → A G L M O R U.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. Outright : Complete : : Rampant : ?
questions.explanation: 'Outright' means complete; 'rampant' means unchecked, spreading without restraint.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number. 9 : 99 : : 15 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is the first times the number 2 more than it: 9 × 11 = 99. Likewise 15 × 17 = 255.

questions.text: A kid's mother's father-in-law's daughter is Rashmi, whose daughter is Pihoo. How is Pihoo related to the kid?
questions.explanation: The kid's mother's father-in-law is the kid's paternal grandfather, so his daughter Rashmi is the kid's aunt. Her daughter Pihoo is the kid's cousin.

questions.text: Select the word-pair in which the two words are related in the same way as are the two words in the given word-pair. Resistance : Ohm
questions.explanation: The ohm is the unit of resistance, as the radian is a unit of angle. 'Ampere : Current' puts the unit first, and the watt and the joule are not units of pressure or volume.

questions.text: Which two digits and signs need to be interchanged so as to balance the given equation? 26 ÷ 6 − 54 + 24 × 8 = 174
questions.explanation: Interchanging 8 and 6, and × and ÷: 28 × 8 − 54 + 24 ÷ 6 = 224 − 54 + 4 = 174.

questions.text: Four words have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the word that is different.
questions.explanation: Growl, grunt and bleat are sounds animals make; to waddle is a way of walking.

questions.text: In an entrance test, Tiwari scored 25% marks and failed by 64 marks. If he had scored 40% marks, then he would have secured 32 marks more than the pass marks. Find the pass marks.
questions.explanation: The 15% between 25% and 40% is worth 64 + 32 = 96 marks, so the maximum is 640. Pass marks = 25% of 640 + 64 = 160 + 64 = 224.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 89, 79, 71, ?, 53, 43

Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All racks are books. All racks are pens. Conclusions: I. All pens are books. II. Some books are pens.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: The racks are both books and pens, so some books are pens (II). Nothing says that all pens are books, so I does not follow.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in an English dictionary? 1. Pamphlet 2. Paleface 3. Painless 4. Partiality 5. Pabulums
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Pabulums (5), Painless (3), Paleface (2), Pamphlet (1), Partiality (4). After 'Pa' the next letters are b, i, l, m and r.

questions.text: Three of the following number-pairs are alike in a certain way and one is different. Select the odd one.
questions.explanation: In the others the first number is the square of one more than the second, plus the second: 271 = 16² + 15, 181 = 13² + 12 and 305 = 17² + 16. For 18 this gives 19² + 18 = 379, not 398.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (697, 13, 866)
questions.explanation: The third number is the first plus the square of the second: 697 + 13² = 697 + 169 = 866. Likewise 541 + 14² = 541 + 196 = 737.

questions.text: In a certain code language, PROMISE is written as WXTQLUF. How will MELTING be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move forward 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2 and 1 places: P → W, R → X, O → T, M → Q, I → L, S → U, E → F. So MELTING → TKQXLPH.

questions.text: If CALENDAR is coded as 91452313 and FACEMASK is coded as 210142316, then how will SECURITY be coded as?
questions.explanation: The word is coded from the last letter back: a consonant by the sum of the digits of its place in the alphabet (R = 18 → 9, S = 19 → 10), a vowel by its place among the vowels (A = 1, E = 2, I = 3, U = 5). SECURITY reversed is YTIRUCES: 7, 2, 3, 9, 5, 3, 2, 10 = 723953210.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series. K _ T Z _ Y _ M _ Z O _ K _ T _ O Y
options: M O T T Y N Z
M N K T Y K Z
M O T Y K M Z
M O K T Y M Z
questions.explanation: With M, O, K, T, Y, M, Z in the blanks the block KMTZOY repeats: KMTZOY KMTZOY KMTZOY.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. 25 : 75 : 150
questions.explanation: Each number is the one before it multiplied by the difference of its digits: 25 × (5 − 2) = 75 and 75 × (7 − 5) = 150. Likewise 13 × (3 − 1) = 26 and 26 × (6 − 2) = 104. The others fail: 29 × 7 = 203, not 36; 253 is not a multiple of 126; and 324 = 108 × 3, but no two digits of 108 differ by 3.

questions.text: Three of the following four letter-clusters are alike in a certain way and one is different. Select the odd one.
questions.explanation: Counting backwards and wrapping round from A to Z, the letters move −5, −7, −15, −13 in IDWHU (I → D → W → H → U), UPITG and CXQBO. In EZSFV the last two steps are −13 and −10, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: With which of the following literary magazines was poet and writer Amrita Pritam associated?
questions.explanation: Amrita Pritam edited 'Nagmani', a Punjabi monthly literary magazine, for many years with the artist Imroz.

questions.text: Who among the following was the founder of the Kirana Gharana of classical music?
questions.explanation: Ustad Abdul Karim Khan founded the Kirana gharana of Hindustani classical music, named after Kairana in Uttar Pradesh.

questions.text: Where in a computer would you use a 'joystick' for computer games and assistive technology?
questions.explanation: A joystick is an input device that moves the cursor or a pointer on the screen, used in games and as an assistive device.

questions.text: Which one of the following became the first Indian club to qualify for AFC Champions league in 2020?
questions.explanation: FC Goa won a place in the AFC Champions League group stage by topping the 2019-20 Indian Super League table, the first Indian club to do so.

questions.text: Which player from Pakistan is credited with 10 British Open titles and six World Championship crowns in professional squash?
questions.explanation: Jahangir Khan won the British Open ten years running (1982-1991) and the World Open six times.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which modern-day Indian state was created on 1 April 1937 as the United Provinces by the Britishers?
questions.explanation: The United Provinces of Agra and Oudh were renamed the United Provinces on 1 April 1937, when provincial autonomy under the Government of India Act 1935 took effect; the state became Uttar Pradesh in 1950.

questions.text: In the state of ______, the general direction of the Himalayas is from southwest to northeast.
questions.explanation: In Arunachal Pradesh the Himalayas run from southwest to northeast; in Darjeeling and Sikkim they run east-west, and in Nagaland, Manipur and Mizoram north-south.

questions.text: What is India’s rank according to the ‘Human Development report 2020’ released by the United Nations Development Programme?
questions.explanation: The UNDP's Human Development Report 2020 ranked India 131st of 189 countries.

questions.text: In which of the following years did the Government of India set up the Monetary Policy Committee?
questions.explanation: The Monetary Policy Committee, which sets the RBI's policy repo rate, was constituted in 2016 under the amended RBI Act.

questions.text: What is the total charge of an electric dipole?
questions.explanation: An electric dipole is a pair of equal and opposite charges, +q and −q, so its total charge is zero.

questions.text: Which state in India has the highest number of Districts?
questions.explanation: Uttar Pradesh has 75 districts, more than any other state.

questions.text: Which river has the tributaries by the name of Mayurakshi, Damodar, Kangsabati and Rupnarayan?
questions.explanation: The Mayurakshi, Damodar, Rupnarayan and Kangsabati (through the Haldi) flow east from the Chota Nagpur plateau into the Bhagirathi-Hooghly in West Bengal.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who was the Nawab of Bhopal that ruled from 1868 to 1901?
questions.explanation: Shah Jahan Begum ruled Bhopal from 1844 to 1860 and again from 1868 until her death in 1901; her daughter Sultan Kaikhusrau Jahan succeeded her.

questions.text: Who is the author of the book 'Poskem'?
questions.explanation: 'Poskem: Goans in the Shadows' (2017) is by the Goan fashion designer Wendell Rodricks.

questions.text: Which bank got the 'Best Bank in Innovation' award at Business Today -Money Today Financial Awards 2020?
questions.explanation: ICICI Bank took the innovation award; SBI and HDFC Bank jointly won Bank of the Year.

questions.text: Which of the following does the Special Marriage Act 1954 NOT support?
questions.explanation: The Act lets two people marry by civil registration whatever their caste or religion. Strict endogamy, marrying only within one's own caste or community, is what it moves away from.

questions.text: Which one of the following is NOT a viral disease?
questions.explanation: Leprosy is caused by a bacterium, Mycobacterium leprae; rabies, smallpox and measles are viral diseases.

questions.text: Which of the following schools in Shillong is the first Khelo India Sports school in North-East India?
questions.explanation: Assam Rifles Public School at Laitkor, Shillong, was launched as a Khelo India Sports School in January 2021, the first in the North-East.

questions.text: What does LED stand for?
questions.explanation: An LED is a light-emitting diode, a semiconductor device that gives out light when current passes through it.

questions.text: Where in India can we find the Jarawa and the Onge tribes?
questions.explanation: The Jarawa and the Onge are tribes of the Andaman Islands; the Onge live on Little Andaman.

questions.text: Which Indian chess player won the Cairns Cup chess tournament 2020?
questions.explanation: Koneru Humpy won the Cairns Cup in St. Louis in February 2020.

questions.text: Which of the following islands is/are located in the Bay of Bengal?
questions.explanation: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands lie in the Bay of Bengal; Minicoy (Lakshadweep) and Diu are in the Arabian Sea.

questions.text: According to 'World Language Database Ethnologue-2019', brought out in February 2020, which Indian language is the third most spoken language of the world in 2019?
questions.explanation: Ethnologue's 2019 figures put Hindi third, with about 615 million speakers, after English and Mandarin Chinese.

questions.text: Which of the following is a part of the central processing unit of a computer?
questions.explanation: Registers are small, fast memory locations inside the CPU; the mouse, scanner and joystick are input devices.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'unpretentious'.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. This cooled off into darkness after a few million years. B. The first time was when the universe began its existence as a glowing fireball. C. In the modern scientific story, light was created not once but twice. D. The second time was when the cold material condensed into dense nuggets and ignited to become the first stars.
questions.explanation: C says light was created twice, B gives the first time, A ('This cooled off') follows the glowing fireball and D gives the second time: CBAD.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech. The new employee asked the manager, "When do I have to report for work?"
options: The new employee told the manager that when he had to report for work.
The new employee asked the manager when he had to report for work.
The manager told the new employee when to report for work.
The new manager asked the employee when he would report for work.
questions.explanation: A reported question keeps 'asked', drops the question form and moves the tense back: 'asked the manager when he had to report for work'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Appalling
questions.explanation: 'Appalling' means causing shock or dismay: 'shocking'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'. We have finished our work for the day, so “let we go home” early today.
questions.explanation: 'Let' takes an object pronoun: 'let us go', not 'let we go'. (The sheet's underline also takes in 'home', which the options leave out.)

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. When you speak, there are gestures and body language that ______ your words.
questions.explanation: Gestures and body language go along with, or 'accompany', the spoken words.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in the active or passive voice. Fifteen children were rescued from an unregistered home by the police.
options: The police rescued fifteen children from an unregistered home.
Fifteen children rescued the police from an unregistered home.
The police were rescued fifteen children from an unregistered home.
The police have rescued fifteen children from an unregistered home.
questions.explanation: The agent, 'the police', becomes the subject and 'were rescued' becomes the simple past active 'rescued': 'The police rescued fifteen children from an unregistered home.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To fish in troubled waters
options: To take advantage of a difficult situation
To try to find a big catch in the deep sea
To try to do something that is very difficult
To catch fish in stormy weather in the sea
questions.explanation: To 'fish in troubled waters' is to take advantage of a confused or difficult situation for one's own gain.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. This means that decisions should not be taken under any kind of pressure to benefit individuals or only a small section of society. B. First, there should be transparency in making decisions; secrecy breeds corruption. C. There are certain values that civil servants need to imbibe in themselves for better administration. D. Then, all decisions must be taken only in public interest, to benefit the community at large.
questions.explanation: C introduces the values civil servants need, B gives the first (transparency), D the next (the public interest) and A explains what D means: CBDA.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Gloomy
questions.explanation: 'Gloomy' means dark or sad; its opposite is 'bright'. 'Dull' and 'dismal' are close in meaning to 'gloomy'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Trail
questions.explanation: A 'trail' is a track: a 'path'. 'Rehearsal' would suit 'trial', a test run, which is a different word.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Although we had / very good batsmen, / we couldn’t be able to / score high.
questions.explanation: 'Could' already expresses ability, so 'couldn't be able to' says it twice: 'we couldn't score high' or 'we were not able to score high'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A quick, sudden movement
questions.explanation: A 'flick' is a quick, sudden movement, as of the wrist. A fleck or a speck is a small spot.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Only five minutes / are allowed / for each speaker / during the function.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'are allowed', on the rule that a plural amount of time taken as one quantity takes a singular verb: 'Only five minutes is allowed for each speaker'. The other three parts are correct.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Curt
questions.explanation: 'Curt' means rudely brief; its opposite is 'polite'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'. You “must return back” the book you borrowed last month.
questions.explanation: 'Return' already means give back, so 'return back' is redundant: 'You must return the book'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A busy, main road for public use
questions.explanation: A 'thoroughfare' is a main road open to public traffic.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. Schools will restart physical classes partially and states have ______ their own conditions and procedures to ensure the safety of students.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'devised': to devise is to work out or plan, and the conditions and procedures are the states' own. 'Adopted' could also be argued, though one usually adopts something that already exists; 'insisted' would need 'on', and 'accepted' does not fit rules a state draws up itself.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiomatic expression given. At a stone’s throw
questions.explanation: 'At a stone's throw' means at a very short distance.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. What are the future possibilities for space travel in the long term? (1) ______ will humans go after they have explored our solar system? It is said that ‘Star Trek’ could hold the (2) ______ to these questions. It is predicted that travel to other galaxies will only be (3) ______ in huge ‘starships’. These will wander through space for hundreds or even thousands of years. Each of them will carry a large human (4) ______. Some of those people will take over a suitable new planet and settle down there. This search for new planets to settle in will continue until life on planet Earth could be just a (5) ______ memory.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The question asks about a destination: 'Where will humans go after they have explored our solar system?'

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. What are the future possibilities for space travel in the long term? (1) ______ will humans go after they have explored our solar system? It is said that ‘Star Trek’ could hold the (2) ______ to these questions. It is predicted that travel to other galaxies will only be (3) ______ in huge ‘starships’. These will wander through space for hundreds or even thousands of years. Each of them will carry a large human (4) ______. Some of those people will take over a suitable new planet and settle down there. This search for new planets to settle in will continue until life on planet Earth could be just a (5) ______ memory.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: To 'hold the answer to' these questions is to contain their answer.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. What are the future possibilities for space travel in the long term? (1) ______ will humans go after they have explored our solar system? It is said that ‘Star Trek’ could hold the (2) ______ to these questions. It is predicted that travel to other galaxies will only be (3) ______ in huge ‘starships’. These will wander through space for hundreds or even thousands of years. Each of them will carry a large human (4) ______. Some of those people will take over a suitable new planet and settle down there. This search for new planets to settle in will continue until life on planet Earth could be just a (5) ______ memory.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Travel to other galaxies will only be 'possible' in huge starships.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. What are the future possibilities for space travel in the long term? (1) ______ will humans go after they have explored our solar system? It is said that ‘Star Trek’ could hold the (2) ______ to these questions. It is predicted that travel to other galaxies will only be (3) ______ in huge ‘starships’. These will wander through space for hundreds or even thousands of years. Each of them will carry a large human (4) ______. Some of those people will take over a suitable new planet and settle down there. This search for new planets to settle in will continue until life on planet Earth could be just a (5) ______ memory.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: Each starship will carry a large human 'population', some of whom will settle on a new planet.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. What are the future possibilities for space travel in the long term? (1) ______ will humans go after they have explored our solar system? It is said that ‘Star Trek’ could hold the (2) ______ to these questions. It is predicted that travel to other galaxies will only be (3) ______ in huge ‘starships’. These will wander through space for hundreds or even thousands of years. Each of them will carry a large human (4) ______. Some of those people will take over a suitable new planet and settle down there. This search for new planets to settle in will continue until life on planet Earth could be just a (5) ______ memory.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Life on Earth would become just a 'distant' memory, one far back in the past.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'UMBRELLA' is written as 'VNCSDKKZ' and 'FASTENED' is written as 'GBTUDMDC'. How will 'MONUMENT' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The first four letters move one place forward and the last four one place back: UMBR → VNCS and ELLA → DKKZ. So MONU → NPOV and MENT → LDMS: NPOVLDMS.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (25, 17, 170)
questions.explanation: The third number is the second times twice the square root of the first: 17 × (2 × 5) = 170. Likewise 12 × (2 × 6) = 144.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 59, 59, 61, 183, 187, ?
Four words have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the word that is different.
questions.explanation: The mandolin is a stringed instrument; the flute, saxophone and clarinet are wind instruments.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term. SHOVEL : MFWPIT : : NOVICE : ?
questions.explanation: SHOVEL written backwards is LEVOHS, and each letter then moves one place forward: MFWPIT. NOVICE backwards is ECIVON, which becomes FDJWPO.

questions.text: What was the day of the week on 31 January 2009?
questions.explanation: 1 January 2001 was a Monday. 2001 to 2008 add 8 + 2 (the leap years 2004 and 2008) = 10 odd days, that is 3, so 1 January 2009 was a Thursday. 30 days later (2 odd days) is a Saturday.

questions.text: Four number-pairs have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the number-pair that is different.
questions.explanation: In 30 : 225, 20 : 100 and 14 : 49 the second number is the square of half the first: 15², 10² and 7². Half of 24 is 12, and 12² = 144, not 130.

questions.text: Select the correct option that indicates the arrangement of the given words in the order in which they appear in an English dictionary. 1. Ruthless 2. Ruler 3. Routine 4. Rusticate 5. Rugby
questions.explanation: Routine (Ro-) comes first; the rest begin 'Ru' and go by their third letter: Rugby (g), Ruler (l), Rusticate (s), Ruthless (t). So 3, 5, 2, 4, 1.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 45 – 49 + 26 × 70 ÷ 35 = 42
questions.explanation: After interchanging + and −: 45 + 49 − 26 × 70 ÷ 35 = 45 + 49 − 52 = 42.

questions.text: Four letter-clusters have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the letter-cluster that is different.
questions.explanation: In EBCD, NKLM and IFGH the second letter is 3 places before the first, and the rest follow it in order. WXYZ runs straight through, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (16, 60, 240)
questions.explanation: The third number is the first times a quarter of the second: 16 × (60 ÷ 4) = 240. Likewise 18 × (56 ÷ 4) = 252.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series. p _ t b c p r _ b c _ r t b _ p _ t _ c
options: r, c, p, b, t, r
r, p, c, t, b, r
r, t, p, c, r, b
r, p, t, r, b, c
questions.explanation: With r, t, p, c, r, b in the blanks the block prtbc repeats: prtbc prtbc prtbc prtbc.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fourth number in the same way as the first number is related to the second number and the fifth number is related to the sixth number. 24 : 144 : : ? : 174 : : 35 : 210
questions.explanation: The second number is six times the first: 24 × 6 = 144 and 35 × 6 = 210. So ? × 6 = 174 and ? = 29.

questions.text: If Aniket is the brother of the son of Priyanka's son, then how is Aniket related to Priyanka?
questions.explanation: The son of Priyanka's son is her grandson, and Aniket, his brother, is her grandson too.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some balls are spoons. All stones are balls. No ball is a pebble. Conclusions: I. Some balls are stones. II. No spoon is a stone. III. No stone is a pebble.
options: Both conclusions I and III follow.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
Both conclusions II and III follow.
questions.explanation: All stones are balls, so some balls are stones (I); and as no ball is a pebble, no stone is a pebble (III). Nothing links spoons to stones, so II does not follow.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'TOPPER' is coded as '66' and 'MARK' is coded as '61'. How will 'INDUCE' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter counts as 26 minus its place in the alphabet, and the code is the sum: TOPPER = 6 + 11 + 10 + 10 + 21 + 8 = 66 and MARK = 13 + 25 + 8 + 15 = 61. INDUCE = 17 + 12 + 22 + 5 + 23 + 21 = 100.

questions.text: Select the option in which the words share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of words. Libya : Tripoli
questions.explanation: Tripoli is the capital of Libya, so the pair is country : capital, as in Zambia : Lusaka. Kampala : Uganda and Harare : Zimbabwe put the capital first, and Jakarta is the capital of Indonesia.

questions.text: Which of the following mountain passes is situated in the state of Uttarakhand?
questions.explanation: Mangsha Dhura, in Pithoragarh district, links Uttarakhand with Tibet. Nathu La is in Sikkim, Baralacha La in Himachal Pradesh and Bomdi La in Arunachal Pradesh.

questions.text: Who was appointed as UNICEF's celebrity advocate for a children's rights campaign in September 2020?
questions.explanation: Ayushmann Khurrana became UNICEF's celebrity advocate for its campaign on children's rights in September 2020.

questions.text: ‘PVC’ is a high strength thermoplastic material widely used in applications, such as pipes, medical devices, wire and cable insulation. What is the full form of PVC?
questions.explanation: PVC is polyvinyl chloride, a polymer of vinyl chloride.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: After over 21 years stay in South Africa, Gandhiji returned to India in ______.
questions.explanation: Gandhiji returned from South Africa in January 1915, landing at Bombay on 9 January, the day now marked as Pravasi Bharatiya Divas.

questions.text: What was India’s rank in the World Press Freedom Index 2020?
questions.explanation: India ranked 142nd of 180 countries in Reporters Without Borders' World Press Freedom Index 2020.

questions.text: The nephron is the microscopic structural and functional unit of the:
questions.explanation: The nephron, of which each kidney has about a million, filters the blood and forms urine.

questions.text: National Highway No. 7 connects:
questions.explanation: NH 7 runs from Fazilka in Punjab, near the Pakistan border, to Mana in Uttarakhand, near the Tibet border. Varanasi–Kanyakumari was NH 7 only under the numbering replaced in 2010; that road now carries other numbers, mostly NH 44.

questions.text: To which country does the French Open 2020 women's singles winner, Iga Swiatek belong?
questions.explanation: Iga Swiatek of Poland won the 2020 French Open women's singles, Poland's first Grand Slam singles title.

questions.text: Which of the following diseases damages the eye’s optic nerve and results in vision loss and blindness and occurs when the normal fluid pressure inside the eyes slowly rises?
questions.explanation: Glaucoma damages the optic nerve, usually as the pressure inside the eye builds up, and can lead to blindness. Vitiligo and psoriasis are skin disorders and gonorrhoea is a sexually transmitted infection.

questions.text: India's first lithium refinery, which will process lithium ore to produce battery-grade material, will be set up in:
questions.explanation: Manikaran Power, with Australia's Neometals, planned India's first lithium refinery in Gujarat, to turn imported ore into battery-grade lithium hydroxide.

questions.text: The ‘Hornbill Festival’ is a celebration held every year from 1 to 10 December in ______.
questions.explanation: Nagaland holds the Hornbill Festival every year from 1 to 10 December at Kisama, near Kohima.

questions.text: In which of the following states is Neora Valley National Park situated?
questions.explanation: Neora Valley National Park lies in Kalimpong district, in northern West Bengal.

questions.text: Which of the following organisations was awarded with the Nobel Peace Prize 2020?
questions.explanation: The World Food Programme won the 2020 Nobel Peace Prize for its efforts to combat hunger.

questions.text: Who is the Chief Justice of Bangladesh as of May 2020?
questions.explanation: Syed Mahmud Hossain was Chief Justice of Bangladesh from February 2018 to December 2021. Abdul Hamid was the President and Sheikh Hasina the Prime Minister.

questions.text: Which of the following writs is a challenge to the legality of a prisoner's detention?
questions.explanation: Habeas corpus ('you may have the body') orders a detained person to be brought before the court, which then tests whether the detention is lawful.

questions.text: Which of the following Hindu festivals is celebrated in the last month of the Hindu calendar?
questions.explanation: Holi falls on the full moon of Phalguna, the last month of the Hindu lunar calendar, which begins with Chaitra.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The Battle of Bedara was fought between the British Army and the Dutch Army in:
questions.explanation: The Battle of Bedara (Chinsurah), in November 1759, ended the Dutch challenge to the British in Bengal.

questions.text: Who among the following won the ‘Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Award’ in August 2020 in the ‘Water Adventure’ category?
questions.explanation: Para-swimmer Satyendra (Satendra) Singh Lohiya of Madhya Pradesh received the Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Award for 2019, announced in August 2020, for water adventure.

questions.text: Which of the following is an open source operating system?
questions.explanation: Android is built on the Linux kernel and released as open source through the Android Open Source Project; Windows and iOS are proprietary.

questions.text: Which of the following is the correct definition of bank rate?
options: It is the rate of interest payable by commercial banks to RBI.
It is the rate of interest payable by a scheduled bank at which RBI lends overnight.
It is the rate of interest payable by a consumer to commercial banks.
It is the rate of interest payable by RBI to commercial banks.
questions.explanation: Bank rate is the rate at which RBI lends to commercial banks, by rediscounting their bills of exchange, so it is the interest the banks pay RBI. Overnight lending to banks is at the repo and MSF rates.

questions.text: Which of the following is an input device used to verify the legitimacy or originality of paper documents, especially cheques?
questions.explanation: Magnetic ink character recognition (MICR) reads the magnetic-ink characters printed along the foot of a cheque, letting banks verify and process cheques.

questions.text: Chulia waterfall is situated on Chambal River in ______.
questions.explanation: Chulia Falls is on the Chambal near Rawatbhata, in Chittorgarh district, Rajasthan.

questions.text: In which of the following states was the Monpa handmade paper making unit inaugurated in December 2020?
questions.explanation: In December 2020 the KVIC opened a Monpa handmade paper unit in Tawang, Arunachal Pradesh, reviving a craft about 1,000 years old used for Buddhist scriptures.

questions.text: Who among the following was the first female hockey player to have won the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award?
questions.explanation: Rani Rampal received the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna in 2020, the first woman hockey player to win it.

questions.text: In the Union Budget 2020-21, the Government of India proposed to spend ₹30,42,230 crore in 2020-21, which is ______ higher than the revised estimate of 2019-20.
questions.explanation: The Budget of February 2020 put the revised estimate of spending for 2019-20 at about ₹26.99 lakh crore, and 30.42 ÷ 26.99 ≈ 1.127: a rise of 12.7%.

questions.text: Select the incorrectly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'irreparable'.

questions.text: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. My tailor is made some very stylish dresses for me as well as for my daughter.
questions.explanation: The present perfect active needs 'has', not 'is': 'My tailor has made some very stylish dresses for me'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A dime a dozen
options: common and so of little value
in great demand as not easily available
questions.explanation: Something that is 'a dime a dozen' is so common that it has little value.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. someone who runs away from justice
questions.explanation: A fugitive is someone who has run away, especially from the law. A stowaway hides on a ship or plane to travel free.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. The government has opened many new centres of excellence to train teachers in conducting online classes ______.
questions.explanation: Teachers are trained to conduct online classes well, that is 'effectively'.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, select the one that gives their correct order. A. It is only after sunset that he satisfies his hunger and quenches his thirst. B. In this way, by practicing self-restraint for one month in a year, he is able to lead a life of self-discipline in all matters for the rest of the year. C. During the month of Ramzan, the believer abstains from food and drink in the daytime of his own free will. D. Fasting is an exercise in self-discipline and is good for everyone.
questions.explanation: D says that fasting is an exercise in self-discipline, C describes the Ramzan fast, A says when the fast is broken and B ('In this way') draws the conclusion: DCAB.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. PRECIOUS
questions.explanation: 'Precious' means of great value; its opposite is 'worthless'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. HAZARDOUS
questions.explanation: 'Hazardous' means risky: 'dangerous'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A red letter day
options: a day of fun and enjoyment
questions.explanation: A 'red letter day' is a special, memorable day.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. It “was the biggest” jump in earnings for me and I was delighted.
questions.explanation: The superlative 'the biggest' is right, and the past 'was' matches 'I was delighted', so no change is needed.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. These days, wherever district courts are functioning, “hearings is limit” to urgent matters.
