questions.explanation: The plural 'hearings' takes 'are', the passive needs the past participle 'limited', and 'These days' calls for the present tense.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, select the one that gives their correct order. A. According to sources, one of the degrees will have to be in the regular mode and the other either in open and distance learning or online mode. B. In a move to improve students’ career prospects, the University Grants Commission has approved the proposal to allow them to pursue two degree programmes at the same time. C. A committee formed under the UGC vice chairperson worked on the proposal based on feedback from the public. D. Once the guidelines are notified, a student studying in a university will be able to pursue another degree programme simultaneously.
questions.explanation: B gives the UGC's decision, C tells how the proposal was prepared, D says what students can do once the guidelines are notified and A adds the condition on the two modes: BCDA.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'alert'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. POLLUTE
questions.explanation: To 'pollute' is to make dirty or impure: to 'contaminate'.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. The counsellor gave very good advice to the students.
options: Very good advice to the students has been given by the counsellor.
Very good advice to the students had been given by the counsellor.
Very good advice is given to the students by the counsellor.
Very good advice was given to the students by the counsellor.
questions.explanation: The simple past 'gave' becomes 'was given' in the passive, with 'advice' as the subject.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. Mother said to me, “Enjoy your vacation with your friends.”
options: Mother told me to enjoy my vacation with my friends.
Mother asked me to enjoyed my vacation with my friends.
Mother told me that you should enjoy your vacation with your friends.
Mother told me that I will enjoy my vacation with my friends.
questions.explanation: An order is reported with 'told' and the infinitive, and 'your' becomes 'my': 'Mother told me to enjoy my vacation with my friends.'

questions.text: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. The manager said that Rahul does not wants to go to Mumbai for the new project.
questions.explanation: After 'does not' the verb takes its base form: 'does not want'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. The jail ______ have started yoga and meditation classes for the inmates.
questions.explanation: Those in charge of a jail, who would start classes for its inmates, are its 'authorities'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Infallible
questions.explanation: 'Infallible' means incapable of error; its opposite is 'faulty'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. A place where a dead person's body is burnt.
questions.explanation: A crematorium is where the dead are burnt; a graveyard is where they are buried.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. As the full impact of cyclone Amphan’s fury emerged on Thursday morning and the count of uprooted trees (1) ______ the 5000 mark, environmentalists, horticulturists, and nature lovers mourned the huge (2) ______ . But they also felt that Kolkata could emerge stronger from the (3) ______ if it used the opportunity to move from arbitrary plantation drives to ones that (4) ______ more scientific and rational. The loss of trees is bound to have a great impact on the climate in (5) ______ parts of West Bengal as oxygen levels will go down.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 1.
questions.explanation: The past tense, like 'emerged' in the same sentence: the count of uprooted trees 'crossed' the 5000 mark.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. As the full impact of cyclone Amphan’s fury emerged on Thursday morning and the count of uprooted trees (1) ______ the 5000 mark, environmentalists, horticulturists, and nature lovers mourned the huge (2) ______ . But they also felt that Kolkata could emerge stronger from the (3) ______ if it used the opportunity to move from arbitrary plantation drives to ones that (4) ______ more scientific and rational. The loss of trees is bound to have a great impact on the climate in (5) ______ parts of West Bengal as oxygen levels will go down.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 2.
questions.explanation: Nature lovers mourned the huge 'loss' of trees; 'death' and 'passing' are used of people.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. As the full impact of cyclone Amphan’s fury emerged on Thursday morning and the count of uprooted trees (1) ______ the 5000 mark, environmentalists, horticulturists, and nature lovers mourned the huge (2) ______ . But they also felt that Kolkata could emerge stronger from the (3) ______ if it used the opportunity to move from arbitrary plantation drives to ones that (4) ______ more scientific and rational. The loss of trees is bound to have a great impact on the climate in (5) ______ parts of West Bengal as oxygen levels will go down.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 3.
questions.explanation: Kolkata could emerge stronger from the 'destruction' the cyclone caused.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. As the full impact of cyclone Amphan’s fury emerged on Thursday morning and the count of uprooted trees (1) ______ the 5000 mark, environmentalists, horticulturists, and nature lovers mourned the huge (2) ______ . But they also felt that Kolkata could emerge stronger from the (3) ______ if it used the opportunity to move from arbitrary plantation drives to ones that (4) ______ more scientific and rational. The loss of trees is bound to have a great impact on the climate in (5) ______ parts of West Bengal as oxygen levels will go down.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 4.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. As the full impact of cyclone Amphan’s fury emerged on Thursday morning and the count of uprooted trees (1) ______ the 5000 mark, environmentalists, horticulturists, and nature lovers mourned the huge (2) ______ . The loss of trees is bound to have a great impact on the climate in (5) ______ parts of West Bengal as oxygen levels will go down.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 5.
questions.explanation: 'Several' goes with a plural countable noun: 'several parts of West Bengal'. 'Much' and 'abundant' do not fit.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given letter series will complete the series. M T _ R M _ Q R _ V Q _ M W _ R M _ Q R
options: R U M R Q Y
Q U M Q R X
Q U M R Q X
Q U S R Q R
questions.explanation: With Q, U, M, R, Q, X in the blanks the series reads MTQR MUQR MVQR MWQR MXQR: M, Q and R stay and the second letter runs T, U, V, W, X.

questions.text: Three of the following four letter-clusters are alike in a certain way and one is different. Select the odd one.
questions.explanation: In DZHW, GCKT and HDLS the letters move −4, then +8 (D → Z → H, G → C → K, H → D → L). In PLSK the second step is +7 (L → S), so it is the odd one.

questions.text: In a code language, ORANGE is written as LKZGTX and MIRACLE is written as NBITXEV. How will LOCKDOWN be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Letters in odd places are replaced by their opposites (A ↔ Z, B ↔ Y …) and letters in even places move 7 back: ORANGE → L K Z G T X. So LOCKDOWN → O H X D W H D G.

questions.text: Select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 4, 11, 31, 65, 193, ?
Pointing towards Kapil, Aditya said, "His father is the husband of my father's father's daughter". How is Aditya’s father related to Kapil's mother?
questions.explanation: Aditya's father's father's daughter is his father's sister, and her husband is Kapil's father. So Kapil's mother is the sister of Aditya's father, who is therefore her brother.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs to balance the given equation. 1496*8*13*40*5=0
Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in English dictionary? 1. Rumoured 2. Rudiment 3. Rumanian 4. Royalties 5. Rigorous
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Rigorous (5), Royalties (4), Rudiment (2), Rumanian (3), Rumoured (1). 'Rud' comes before 'Rum', and 'Ruma' before 'Rumo'.

questions.text: Two numbers, A and B, are such that the sum of 3% of A and 6% of B is four-fifth of the sum of 4% of A and 6% of B. Find the ratio of A + B and A – B?
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (13, 37, 77)
questions.explanation: The second number is three times the first minus 2, and the third is twice the second plus 3: 13 × 3 − 2 = 37 and 37 × 2 + 3 = 77. Likewise 14 × 3 − 2 = 40 and 40 × 2 + 3 = 83.

questions.text: Three of the following four words are alike in a certain way and one is different. Select the odd one.
questions.explanation: Contention, turmoil and conflict all mean strife or disorder; tranquility means calm, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (4, 140, 6)
questions.explanation: The middle number is half the sum of the cubes of the outer two: (4³ + 6³)/2 = (64 + 216)/2 = 140. Likewise (5³ + 7³)/2 = (125 + 343)/2 = 234.

questions.text: Select the word-pair that best represents a similar relationship to the one expressed in the given word-pair. Spanner : Grip
questions.explanation: A spanner is used to grip, as an auger is used to bore holes. In 'Carve : Chisel' the order is reversed, and an axe chops rather than digs.

questions.text: Three of the following four number-pairs are alike in a certain way and one is different. Select the one that is different.
questions.explanation: In 4 : 48, 7 : 294 and 6 : 180 the second number is the square of the first times one less than the first: 4² × 3, 7² × 6, 6² × 5. But 5² × 4 = 100, not 105, so 5 : 105 is the odd one.

questions.text: ‘Awl’ is related to ‘Cobbler’ and ‘Chisel’ is related to ‘Sculptor’ in the same way as ‘Anvil’ is related to '______'.
questions.explanation: Each is a tool and the worker who uses it: a cobbler uses an awl, a sculptor a chisel and a blacksmith an anvil.

questions.text: If STROKE is coded as 2317131089 and GLUTEN is coded as 1423871621, then how will CHARGE be coded as?
questions.explanation: The letters are written in reverse order, each as 28 minus its place in the alphabet: STROKE → E K O R T S → 23 17 13 10 8 9. So CHARGE → E G R A H C → 23 21 10 27 20 25.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. PRINT : TWRIP : : CLOSE : ?
questions.explanation: The first and last letters swap, the second moves 5 forward, the middle letter is replaced by its opposite (I ↔ R) and the fourth moves 5 back: PRINT → T W R I P. So CLOSE → E Q L N C.

questions.text: In the following question, the second number is related to the first number in some way, choose the alternative which is similarly related to the third number 13 : 196 : : 15 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is the square of one more than the first: (13 + 1)² = 196. Likewise (15 + 1)² = 256.

questions.text: Which of the following is a replica of the famous Taj Mahal built in 1679?
questions.explanation: Bibi Ka Maqbara in Aurangabad, the tomb of Aurangzeb's wife Dilras Banu Begum, is modelled on the Taj Mahal and is known as the 'Taj of the Deccan'.

questions.text: In which year was Jharkhand made a separate state of India?
questions.explanation: Jharkhand was carved out of Bihar on 15 November 2000.

questions.text: As on 2019, which is the largest multinational bank company in the world as measured by total assets?
options: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China
questions.explanation: The Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC) was the world's largest bank by total assets in 2019.

questions.text: Which Indian state is surrounded by Bangladesh on its north, west and south?
questions.explanation: Tripura is bordered by Bangladesh on the north, west and south; only on the east does it meet Assam and Mizoram.

questions.text: Which Indian journalist was awarded the Windham-Campbell Prize 2019 for the book 'Farthest Field: An Indian Story of the Second World War'?
questions.explanation: Raghu Karnad won a 2019 Windham-Campbell Prize in non-fiction for 'Farthest Field'.

questions.text: What was the theme for 11 February 2020, celebration of the United Nations International Day of Women and Girls in Science?
options: Investment in Women and Girls in Science for Inclusive Green Growth
Welcome the women and girl achievers in science
Inclusive growth of women and girls in science
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'Investment in Women and Girls in Science for Inclusive Green Growth', the theme many sources reported for 2020. Strictly, that was the 2019 theme: the 2020 UN assembly's was 'Investment in Equality in Science, Technology and Innovation in the Digitalization Era for Inclusive Green Growth', to which the key's option is the nearest.

questions.text: 'Bauhche' is a traditional bridegroom’s sword worn during a tribal wedding ceremony in:
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Arunachal Pradesh, where the bridegroom's 'Bauhche' sword is one of the accessories worn at a tribal wedding.

questions.text: ______ was the first athlete to win an Olympic medal for Sri lanka.
questions.explanation: Duncan White won silver in the 400 m hurdles at the 1948 London Olympics, the first Olympic medal for Ceylon (now Sri Lanka).

questions.text: In which year did Nepal adopt its first democratic constitution?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 2015, which fits either reading of the year. Nepal's first democratic constitution, granted by King Mahendra in 1959, is the Constitution of 2015 in Nepal's own Bikram Sambat calendar; and on 20 September 2015 Nepal adopted its present constitution, the first drawn up by an elected Constituent Assembly. None of the other years listed brought a constitution.

questions.text: Mario de Miranda was a ______ from the state of Goa.
questions.explanation: Mario de Miranda, from Goa, was one of India's best-known cartoonists and illustrators.

questions.text: Which Indian sportsperson won a gold medal at the Para-badminton World Championship 2019?
questions.explanation: Manasi Joshi won the women's singles SL3 gold at the 2019 BWF Para-Badminton World Championships in Basel.

questions.text: Which one of the following is a rare disease caused by the deficiency of Vitamin D that causes the bones to become soft and to bend?
questions.explanation: Rickets, caused by a lack of vitamin D (which the body needs to absorb calcium), softens children's bones so that they bend. Pernicious anaemia comes from a lack of vitamin B12.

questions.text: What is the other name for 'transistor computer'?
questions.explanation: Second-generation computers used transistors in place of the vacuum tubes of the first generation; integrated circuits came with the third.

questions.text: 'Maimata' is a popular dance of the Kaloi community from the state of ______.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Tripura: 'Maimata' is the Mamita dance, which Tripura's Tripuri people perform at their harvest festival.

questions.text: Annu Rani is the first Indian woman to cross a distance of 60 m in ______ throw.
questions.explanation: Annu Rani, India's national record holder in the women's javelin, was the first Indian woman to throw it beyond 60 m.

questions.text: The rivers Damodar, Brahmani and Kharkai originate from the state of ______ in India.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Jharkhand. The Damodar rises on the Chota Nagpur plateau in Jharkhand, and the South Koel and the Sankh, which meet near Rourkela to form the Brahmani, also rise there. The Kharkai rises in the Simlipal hills of Odisha's Mayurbhanj district, but flows through Jharkhand to join the Subarnarekha at Jamshedpur.

questions.text: ______ glands release tears from our eyes.
questions.explanation: The lacrimal glands, above the outer corner of each eye, produce tears.

questions.text: In which year was the Bombay Stock Exchange established?
questions.explanation: The Bombay Stock Exchange, Asia's oldest, was founded in 1875 as the Native Share and Stock Brokers' Association.

questions.text: In January 2020, ______ has secured a top position among the 115 aspirational districts that received grading on a system devised by the NITI Aayog.
questions.explanation: Sukma, a Maoist-affected district of Bastar in southern Chhattisgarh, came top of NITI Aayog's delta ranking of the 115 aspirational districts released at the end of 2019.

questions.text: Who created FORTRAN — the first high-level computer programming language?
questions.explanation: John Backus led the IBM team that created FORTRAN in the 1950s. Dan Bricklin co-created VisiCalc, Marc Andreessen the Mosaic browser, and Larry Ellison co-founded Oracle.

questions.text: In which year did the state of Himachal Pradesh come into existence?
questions.explanation: Himachal Pradesh, a Union Territory from 1956, became a full state on 25 January 1971.

questions.text: 'Sandalwood' is the state tree of ______.
questions.explanation: Sandalwood, for which Mysuru is famous, is Karnataka's state tree.

questions.text: Which Indian sportsperson won the 'World Games Athlete of the Year' award in January 2020?
questions.explanation: Rani Rampal, captain of India's women's hockey team, was voted World Games Athlete of the Year for 2019, announced in January 2020: the first hockey player to win it.

questions.text: Which of the following is the largest dental tissue?
questions.explanation: Dentin forms the bulk of a tooth, beneath the enamel of the crown and the cementum of the root. Enamel is the hardest tissue but only a thin outer layer.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A large cage, building or enclosure to keep birds
questions.explanation: An aviary is a large enclosure for keeping birds; an apiary is where bees are kept, and an aquarium holds fish.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. Expunge
questions.explanation: To 'expunge' is to erase or remove something completely; its opposite is 'insert'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Uphold
questions.explanation: To 'uphold' is to support or maintain; its opposite is 'oppose'.

questions.text: Given below are four sentences in jumbled order. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. His school was closed as it was the height of summer. B. It was on one such day that Ranji discovered a pool in the forest. C. As he had no friends yet, he wandered alone in the hills and forests. D. Ranji had been less than a month in Rajpur.
questions.explanation: D introduces Ranji in Rajpur, A says his school was closed, C has him wandering alone in the hills and B ('one such day') follows: DACB.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. The Prime Minister chair a high-level meeting / with senior officials / to review the Covid situation.
options: The Prime Minister chair a high-level meeting
questions.explanation: The singular subject 'The Prime Minister' needs a singular verb: 'chairs' (or 'chaired') a high-level meeting.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. In the past month, the price of oil has ______ several times.
questions.explanation: A price that rises and falls again and again 'fluctuates'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given words. Leather straps put around a horse’s head to control it
questions.explanation: A bridle is the set of straps on a horse's head used to control it; 'bridal' (of a bride) only sounds the same, and a saddle and stirrups are for the rider.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. Mother said, “All the guests will arrive tonight.”
options: Mother said that all the guests would arrive that night.
Mother said that all the guests will arrive tonight.
Mother told that all the guests would arrive tonight.
Mother said that all the guests will arrive that night.
questions.explanation: After 'said', 'will' moves back to 'would' and 'tonight' becomes 'that night'.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. The word Jama means ‘a robe or shawl’ and War means ‘Yard (the measuring unit)’. B. Jamawar (also spelled as Jamavar) is a fabric that has its roots in Kashmir. C. People in the earlier times used to buy a yard of the shawl to protect themselves from the chilly winter. D. The Jamawar is an adulterated form of Pashmina silk since it contains a blend of cotton and wool.
questions.explanation: B introduces Jamawar, A explains its name ('War' means a yard), C follows with people buying a yard of the shawl and D ends with what the fabric is made of: BACD.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Rank and file
options: The manager of a personnel department
questions.explanation: The 'rank and file' are the ordinary members of an organisation, as opposed to its leaders.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. My brother has decided to settle in London “for good”.
questions.explanation: To do something 'for good' is to do it permanently: forever.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. “Unless someone makes a complaint,” they will not clear the garbage from the street.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if ... not', which is the sense here: the garbage will not be cleared if no one complains. The sentence is correct as it stands.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'wrinkle'.

questions.text: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. We are yet living in the same house.
questions.explanation: In a positive statement an action that is continuing takes 'still', not 'yet': 'We are still living in the same house.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. FORSAKE
questions.explanation: To 'forsake' is to abandon: 'desert'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Profuse
questions.explanation: 'Profuse' means plentiful: 'abundant'. 'Meagre' and 'limited' are its opposites.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. The clouds hid the sun.
options: The sun was hidden by the clouds.
The sun is hidden by the clouds.
The clouds are hid by the sun.
The sun was hide by the clouds.
questions.explanation: The simple past active 'hid' becomes the simple past passive 'was hidden', with 'the sun' as subject.

questions.text: Select the misspelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'miserable'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. How long have you “being seating” on this bench?
questions.explanation: The present perfect continuous is 'have been' + -ing, and resting on a seat is 'sitting': 'How long have you been sitting on this bench?' (To 'seat' someone is to give them a seat.)

questions.text: Fill in the blank with most appropriate word. The air ______ has gone up significantly.
questions.explanation: The price paid for a journey is the 'fare': the air fare.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Kashmiri carpets have been appreciated since a long time for their intricate work. Their uniqueness (1) ______ in their manufacturing. These carpets are (2) ______ handmade and are knotted, not tufted. You can (3) ______ different carpets from a variety of silk or woolen ones. These are (4) ______ in colourful themes. The main art of carpet manufacturing is (5) ______ with the knotting. These knots determine the durability and value of the carpet.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.explanation: 'Their uniqueness lies in their manufacturing': the singular subject and a general fact take the simple present 'lies'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Kashmiri carpets have been appreciated since a long time for their intricate work. Their uniqueness (1) ______ in their manufacturing. These carpets are (2) ______ handmade and are knotted, not tufted. You can (3) ______ different carpets from a variety of silk or woolen ones. These are (4) ______ in colourful themes. The main art of carpet manufacturing is (5) ______ with the knotting. These knots determine the durability and value of the carpet.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
questions.explanation: 'Purely' means entirely, with nothing else: the carpets are made wholly by hand.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Kashmiri carpets have been appreciated since a long time for their intricate work. Their uniqueness (1) ______ in their manufacturing. These carpets are (2) ______ handmade and are knotted, not tufted. You can (3) ______ different carpets from a variety of silk or woolen ones. These are (4) ______ in colourful themes. The main art of carpet manufacturing is (5) ______ with the knotting. These knots determine the durability and value of the carpet.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
questions.explanation: You can 'choose' different carpets from a variety of silk or woollen ones.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Kashmiri carpets have been appreciated since a long time for their intricate work. Their uniqueness (1) ______ in their manufacturing. These carpets are (2) ______ handmade and are knotted, not tufted. You can (3) ______ different carpets from a variety of silk or woolen ones. These are (4) ______ in colourful themes. The main art of carpet manufacturing is (5) ______ with the knotting. These knots determine the durability and value of the carpet.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
questions.explanation: The carpets are 'designed' in colourful themes: made to a planned pattern.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Kashmiri carpets have been appreciated since a long time for their intricate work. Their uniqueness (1) ______ in their manufacturing. These carpets are (2) ______ handmade and are knotted, not tufted. You can (3) ______ different carpets from a variety of silk or woolen ones. These are (4) ______ in colourful themes. The main art of carpet manufacturing is (5) ______ with the knotting. These knots determine the durability and value of the carpet.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
questions.explanation: The main art of carpet making 'is associated with', that is connected with, the knotting, as the next sentence explains.

questions.text: Four options have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the option that is different.
questions.explanation: Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu & Kashmir are union territories with legislative assemblies of their own. Chandigarh has none, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Four number-pairs have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the one that is different.
questions.explanation: In 17 : 291, 15 : 227 and 11 : 123 the second number is the square of the first plus 2 (17² + 2 = 291). 13 : 169 is 13² with nothing added, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers share the same relationship as that shared by the numbers in the given set. (7, 4, 33)
questions.explanation: The third number is the difference of the squares of the first two: 7² − 4² = 49 − 16 = 33. Likewise 9² − 5² = 81 − 25 = 56.

questions.text: Which two digits need to be interchanged so as to balance the given equation? 75 ÷ 18 + 51 × 8 − 82 = 87
If Raman is the brother of the son of Kshitij’s son, how is Raman related to Kshitij?
questions.explanation: The son of Kshitij's son is Kshitij's grandson, and his brother Raman is a grandson too.

questions.text: Select the word-pair in which the two words are related in the same way as are the two words in the following word-pair. Growth : Expansion
questions.explanation: Growth and expansion mean much the same, as do urge and request (both ask for something). First and last, and temporary and permanent, are opposites.

questions.text: Three of the following four letter-clusters are alike in a certain way and one is different. Select the odd one.
questions.explanation: In LNQU, QSVZ and ACFJ the letters move +2, +3, +4. KMQT moves +2, +4, +3, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Select the correct option that indicates the arrangement of the following words in a logical and meaningful order. 1. Universe 2. Chennai 3. World 4. Asia 5. Tamil Nadu
questions.explanation: From the largest to the smallest: Universe (1), World (3), Asia (4), Tamil Nadu (5), Chennai (2).

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given letter series will complete the series. a _ bcd _ _ aabc _ dea _ _ cd _ e
questions.explanation: With a, d, e, d, a, b, d in the blanks the block aabcdde repeats: aabcdde aabcdde aabcdde.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ENDORSE is written as VMWLIHV. How will INSTRUCT be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite in the alphabet (A ↔ Z, B ↔ Y and so on): E → V, N → M, D → W, O → L, R → I, S → H. So INSTRUCT → R M H G I F X G: RMHGIFXG.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 8, 24, 48, 80, ?, 168

Vishal has a total of ₹4,100 in the denominations of 5, 10, 20 and 50 rupee notes. He has an equal number of 5 and 10 rupee notes. The number of 20 rupee notes is double the number of 5 rupee notes. The number of 50 rupee notes is thrice the number of 10 rupee notes. How many 5 rupee notes are there with Vishal?
questions.explanation: With x notes each of ₹5 and ₹10, 2x of ₹20 and 3x of ₹50: 5x + 10x + 40x + 150x = 205x = 4,100, so x = 20.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All computers are calculators. All calculators are boxes. Conclusions: I. All computers are boxes. II. Some boxes are computers.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
questions.explanation: All computers are calculators and all calculators are boxes, so all computers are boxes (I); and so some boxes are computers (II). Both follow.

questions.text: In a code language, if FORTUNE is written as 716192122156, then how will OCTOBER be written in the same language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is written as its place in the alphabet plus 1: F (6) → 7, O (15) → 16, R (18) → 19 and so on. OCTOBER → 16, 4, 21, 16, 3, 6, 19: 16421163619.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. 29 : 36 : 39
questions.explanation: Each number is the one before it plus the difference of its digits: 29 + (9 − 2) = 36 and 36 + (6 − 3) = 39. Likewise 48 + (8 − 4) = 52 and 52 + (5 − 2) = 55. 54 : 58 : 61 has the same gaps but fails the rule: 54 + (5 − 4) = 55.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term. DEBONAIR : EDRIOBAN : : HALLMARK : ?
questions.explanation: The letters are taken in pairs, each pair reversed and the pairs put in the order 1, 4, 2, 3: DE BO NA IR → ED RI OB AN. So HA LL MA RK → AH KR LL AM: AHKRLLAM.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number. 6 : 27 : : 9 : ?

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which part of India did the Nizams of Asafjahi dynasty rule?
questions.explanation: The Asaf Jahi Nizams ruled Hyderabad State in the Deccan from 1724, when Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah I made himself independent of the Mughals, until 1948.

questions.text: Who among the following is the youngest mayor in India as of January 2021?
questions.explanation: Arya Rajendran became Mayor of Thiruvananthapuram in December 2020 at the age of 21, the youngest mayor in India.

questions.text: Which of the following places in India has 0% forest area as per the Indian State of Forest Report 2019?
questions.explanation: The India State of Forest Report 2019 shows no recorded forest area in Lakshadweep (no land there is notified or recorded as forest), although its tree-covered land, mostly coconut plantations, still counts as forest cover, about 90% of its area.

questions.text: Who among the following was a Portuguese writer who wrote about the trade and society in south India?
questions.explanation: Duarte Barbosa, a Portuguese official in India early in the sixteenth century, wrote a detailed account of trade and society in south India. Manucci was Venetian, and Bernier and Tavernier were French.

questions.text: ‘Maand’ is primarily a traditional folk singing style from ______.
questions.explanation: Maand is a Rajasthani folk singing style, once sung in the royal courts; 'Kesariya Balam' is its best-known song.

questions.text: Which of the following types of computer is used in climate research and weather forecasting?
questions.explanation: Weather forecasting and climate modelling need enormous numbers of calculations, so they are run on supercomputers.

questions.text: Who among the following introduced the concept of electric field for the first time?
questions.explanation: Michael Faraday introduced the idea of a field, picturing electric and magnetic forces as lines of force filling the space around charges and magnets.

questions.text: Which of the following keys will you press in Windows 10 to turn the volume up?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives F8. Windows itself assigns no function key to the volume; the media keys are set by the keyboard's maker. On HP and Samsung laptops, for example, F6, F7 and F8 are mute, volume down and volume up, while Dell and Lenovo use F1, F2 and F3.

questions.text: Who among the following Indian cricketers holds the record of most number of catches taken by a non-wicketkeeper while standing in the slip cordon, as of January 2021?
questions.explanation: Rahul Dravid, a specialist slip fielder, took 210 catches in Test cricket, the world record for a non-wicketkeeper when the question was set.

questions.text: Which of the following is the state flower of Manipur?
questions.explanation: The Shirui lily, which grows wild only on the Shirui hills of Ukhrul district, is Manipur's state flower.

questions.text: Which of the following months was celebrated as 'Nutrition Month' in India in the year 2020?
questions.explanation: Since 2018 September has been observed as Rashtriya Poshan Maah (National Nutrition Month) under the POSHAN Abhiyaan.

questions.text: Who among the following was awarded the International Children's Peace Prize 2020?
questions.explanation: Sadat Rahman of Bangladesh won the International Children's Peace Prize 2020 for his work against cyberbullying, including the 'Cyber Teens' app.

questions.text: ‘Nikshay Poshan Yojana’ is a scheme introduced by the Government of India to provide nutritional support to ______ patients.
questions.explanation: Under the Nikshay Poshan Yojana, launched in 2018, tuberculosis patients were paid ₹500 a month by direct benefit transfer for nutritional support during treatment; the amount was raised to ₹1,000 in October 2024.

questions.text: Chemicals called ______ link to form proteins.
questions.explanation: Proteins are chains of amino acids joined by peptide bonds.

questions.text: In which of the following cities was the 89th Annual General Meeting of the Board of Control for Cricket in India held?
questions.explanation: The BCCI's 89th Annual General Meeting was held in Ahmedabad on 24 December 2020; it approved a ten-team IPL from 2022.

questions.text: Which of the following has a tetragonal crystal system?
questions.explanation: SSC's key follows NCERT's table of the seven crystal systems, which lists calcium sulphate among its tetragonal examples, potassium nitrate as orthorhombic and zinc oxide and cadmium sulphide as hexagonal. (Mineralogists class anhydrite, natural calcium sulphate, as orthorhombic.)

questions.text: Which of the following states emerged as a separate state in 1963?
questions.explanation: Nagaland became a state on 1 December 1963. Tripura became a state in 1972, and Mizoram and Arunachal Pradesh in 1987.

questions.text: When was the Editors Guild of India founded?
questions.explanation: The Editors Guild of India was founded in 1978 to protect press freedom and raise the standards of editorial leadership.

questions.text: Which present day Indian state came into existence as the Mysore state in 1953?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Karnataka, the only one of these states ever called Mysore. Mysore State gained most of Bellary district from Madras on 1 October 1953 under the Andhra State Act, took its present shape on 1 November 1956 and was renamed Karnataka in 1973.

questions.text: Where was the world's largest solar tree installed in India in 2020?
questions.explanation: The world's largest solar tree was installed in 2020 by CSIR-CMERI (the Central Mechanical Engineering Research Institute) at Durgapur, West Bengal.

questions.text: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India mentions 'Continuance of the rights of citizenship'?
questions.explanation: Article 10 provides that every person who is or is deemed to be a citizen under the preceding provisions continues to be one, subject to any law made by Parliament. Article 9 deals with acquiring a foreign citizenship, Article 11 lets Parliament regulate citizenship by law and Article 12 defines 'the State'.

questions.text: Who among the following athletes was the first ever youth ambassador of United Nations International Children's Emergency Fund (UNICEF) India?
questions.explanation: In November 2018 UNICEF India named the sprinter Hima Das its first youth ambassador.

questions.text: Where was the first factory of the Indian Iron and Steel Company (IISCO) set up?
questions.explanation: IISCO, formed in 1918, set up its first factory at Hirapur and later another at Kulti, both near Asansol in West Bengal.

questions.text: Which of the following states has the longest roadway network as on March 2021?
questions.explanation: Maharashtra has the longest road network of any Indian state, national highways included.

questions.text: 'Rahide' is a long scarf worn by the women of ______ to protect their head from cool breeze as well as to show their traditional social affinity.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Himachal Pradesh, where women wear the rahide, a long scarf over the head.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'disappear'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. REPULSION
questions.explanation: 'Repulsion' is a force or feeling that drives things apart; its opposite is 'attraction'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'. This is the student “which won” the first prize in the recitation.
questions.explanation: 'Who' is the relative pronoun for a person who is the subject of the clause: 'This is the student who won the first prize in the recitation.'

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. A professional who works with patients who have heart problems
questions.explanation: A cardiologist treats heart problems; a urologist treats the urinary tract and a paediatrician treats children.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The study of ancient civilisations and cultures by examining their sites
questions.explanation: Archaeology studies ancient cultures through their sites and remains; entomology is the study of insects, etymology of word origins and arachnology of spiders and other arachnids.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. DILEMMA
questions.explanation: A 'dilemma' is a difficult situation that calls for a hard choice: a 'predicament'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Select the segment that contains a grammatical error from the given options. I am going / to home / soon after the / programme gets over.
questions.explanation: 'Home' after a verb of motion takes no preposition: 'I am going home'.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. Shashi was enjoying the game.
options: The game is being enjoyed by Shashi.
The game was enjoying by Shashi.
The game has been enjoyed by Shashi.
The game was being enjoyed by Shashi.
questions.explanation: The past continuous 'was enjoying' becomes 'was being enjoyed' in the passive: 'The game was being enjoyed by Shashi.'

questions.text: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. Due to the lockdown most schools teaches students through online classes.
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'most schools' takes the plural verb: 'most schools teach students'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech. My mother said to me, "Aravind, the baby has been crying all day."
options: My mother said Aravind that the baby has been crying all the day.
My mother told me that the baby had been crying all day.
My mother told to Aravind why the baby has been crying all day.
Aravind told my mother that the baby had been crying all day.
questions.explanation: 'Said to me' becomes 'told me', the form of address 'Aravind' is dropped, and the present perfect continuous 'has been crying' moves back to 'had been crying'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Lucid
questions.explanation: 'Lucid' means clear and easy to understand; its opposite is 'confusing'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Burn the midnight oil
options: work many nights at a stretch
questions.explanation: To 'burn the midnight oil' is to work or study late into the night.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. The government is making air bags ______ for front seat passengers in all cars.
questions.explanation: Making air bags 'compulsory' means every car must have them.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, select the one that gives their correct order. A. I sat patiently through them knowing they were not for me. B. The headmaster read the list of qualities this year’s best student award had - most giving, contributed most to society, and so on. C. At my high school graduation, the awards were being presented for achievement, contribution to the school, the community, scholarship, and more. D. But when I heard my name called, I began to cry as I could not believe that I was actually chosen for the award.
questions.explanation: C sets the scene at the graduation awards, A says the writer sat through them, B has the headmaster reading out the qualities for the best student award, and D tells of the writer's name being called: CABD.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To come round
options: To spend a lot of time with someone
questions.explanation: To 'come round' is to regain consciousness.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. The test procedure starts at 10 a.m. in all the test centres. B. When you enter the test hall, you should have your Test Admit Card with you. C. You are, therefore, required to reach the test centre by 9.30 a.m. D. Remember that, if you report after 10 a.m., you will not be admitted.
questions.explanation: A gives the start time, C draws the conclusion ('therefore') that candidates must arrive by 9.30, D warns about reporting late, and B adds what to bring into the hall: ACDB.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Emerge
questions.explanation: To 'emerge' is to come out into view: to 'appear'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. The migrant said that he “did not planning” to come back to the city for quite some time.
questions.explanation: 'Did' is followed by the base form of the verb: 'he did not plan to come back'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. The mother monkey picked up her baby and climbed up the tree to ______.
questions.explanation: The mother monkey climbed the tree to reach 'safety' with her baby.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. An open-minded person can very easily accept as well as respect the (1)______ person's viewpoint or ideas. Such a person willingly and cordially (2)______ to others' views, accepts their different ideas, and even goes ahead to implement them (3)______. With an open mindset, positive and vibrant energy (4)______ that not only helps such people (5)_______ also keeps other people around them happy.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 1.
questions.explanation: 'The other person's viewpoint': the person other than oneself.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. An open-minded person can very easily accept as well as respect the (1)______ person's viewpoint or ideas. Such a person willingly and cordially (2)______ to others' views, accepts their different ideas, and even goes ahead to implement them (3)______. With an open mindset, positive and vibrant energy (4)______ that not only helps such people (5)_______ also keeps other people around them happy.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 2.
questions.explanation: The subject 'such a person' is singular and the passage is in the present tense, like 'accepts': 'listens to others' views'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. An open-minded person can very easily accept as well as respect the (1)______ person's viewpoint or ideas. Such a person willingly and cordially (2)______ to others' views, accepts their different ideas, and even goes ahead to implement them (3)______. With an open mindset, positive and vibrant energy (4)______ that not only helps such people (5)_______ also keeps other people around them happy.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 3.
questions.explanation: Such a person goes ahead and implements the ideas 'successfully'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. An open-minded person can very easily accept as well as respect the (1)______ person's viewpoint or ideas. Such a person willingly and cordially (2)______ to others' views, accepts their different ideas, and even goes ahead to implement them (3)______. With an open mindset, positive and vibrant energy (4)______ that not only helps such people (5)_______ also keeps other people around them happy.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 4.
questions.explanation: The passage is in the simple present: positive and vibrant energy 'is created'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. An open-minded person can very easily accept as well as respect the (1)______ person's viewpoint or ideas. Such a person willingly and cordially (2)______ to others' views, accepts their different ideas, and even goes ahead to implement them (3)______. With an open mindset, positive and vibrant energy (4)______ that not only helps such people (5)_______ also keeps other people around them happy.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 5.
questions.explanation: 'Not only' pairs with 'but also': 'not only helps such people but also keeps other people around them happy'.

questions.text: In a family, Divya and Monika are sisters. Monika is the mother of Anamika. Kishore is the son of Anamika. Lillu is the son of Divya. How is Anamika related to Lillu?
questions.explanation: Anamika is the daughter of Monika and Lillu the son of Divya. As Monika and Divya are sisters, Anamika and Lillu are cousins.

questions.text: Four letter-clusters have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the letter-cluster that is different.
questions.explanation: In TWZCF, DGJMP and HKNQT each letter is 3 places after the one before it (Z wraps round to C). BEGLN moves +3, +2, +5, +2, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 1, 2, 10, 37, ? , 226
questions.explanation: The differences are the cubes 1³, 2³, 3³, 4³, 5³: 37 + 64 = 101 and 101 + 125 = 226.

questions.text: Select the correct option that indicates the arrangement of the given words in the order in which they appear in an English dictionary. 1. Fragile 2. Freedom 3. Fresher 4. Fraudster 5. Frame
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Fragile (1), Frame (5), Fraudster (4), Freedom (2), Fresher (3). 'Frag' comes before 'Fram' and 'Frau', and 'Free' before 'Fres'.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. BIOLOGY : COUMUHZ : : CHEMISTRY : ?
questions.explanation: Each consonant moves one place forward and each vowel becomes the next vowel: B → C, I → O, O → U, L → M, G → H, Y → Z. So C → D, H → I, E → I, M → N, I → O, S → T, T → U, R → S, Y → Z: DIINOTUSZ.

questions.text: Which of the following equations will be correct when the signs + and ×, and the numbers 3 and 6 are interchanged?
questions.explanation: After interchanging: 12 + 6 × 3 = 12 + 18 = 30. The others give 11 + 3 × 6 = 29, 7 × 6 + 3 = 45 and 9 + 6 × 3 = 27.

questions.text: Three of the following four number triads are alike in a certain way and one is different. Select the one that is different.
questions.explanation: In the other three triads the digit sums of the numbers are 3, 6 and 9 in some order, so every number is a multiple of 3. In (202, 404, 909) they are 4, 8 and 18: 202 and 404 are not multiples of 3.

questions.text: Two statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some managers are bosses. Some doctors are managers. Conclusions: I. Some managers are executives. II. Some doctors are bosses.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows .
Both conclusions I and II follow .
questions.explanation: Executives are not mentioned in the statements, so I does not follow. Two 'some' statements give no definite conclusion, so II does not follow either.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given letter series will complete the series. T _ R _ _ S _ D T _ R D _ S _ D
options: S T S R R T R
S D T D S T T
D S T R T T R
S D T R S T R
questions.explanation: With S, D, T, R, S, T, R in the blanks the block TSRD repeats: TSRD TSRD TSRD TSRD.

questions.text: Three of the following four words are alike in a certain way and one is different. Select the odd one.
questions.explanation: Engineers, designers and architects plan and create things (machines, products, buildings); a doctor treats the sick.

questions.text: In a certain code language, DORM is coded as 4303626 and FIRST is coded as 69363840. How will CANCER be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Letters A to I keep their place number in the alphabet, and letters from J on are written as twice it: DORM → 4, 30, 36, 26 and FIRST → 6, 9, 36, 38, 40. So CANCER → 3, 1, 28, 3, 5, 36: 31283536.

questions.text: Select the option in which the words share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of words. Warrior : Battlefield
questions.explanation: A warrior fights on a battlefield as an actor performs on a stage: a person and the place where he works. Umpire : Cricket pairs a person with a game, and Soldier : Army a person with the force he belongs to.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (5, 14, 350)
questions.explanation: The first number squared times the second gives the third: 5² × 14 = 350. Likewise 7² × 9 = 441; the others give 1,024, 180 and 432.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fourth number in the same way as the first number is related to the second number and the fifth number is related to the sixth number. 68 : 4 : : ? : 7 : : 220 : 6
questions.explanation: The first number is the cube of the second plus 4: 4³ + 4 = 68 and 6³ + 4 = 220. Likewise 7³ + 4 = 347.

questions.text: The sum of the salaries of three persons, A, B and C, is ₹66,500. B's salary is half the salary of C. B's salary is 125% of A's salary. What is the salary of C?
If in a code language, GOD is coded as 15 and DEVIL is coded as 43, then how will you code HUMEN?
questions.explanation: Each consonant counts as its position in the alphabet and each vowel as its position in the sequence A, E, I, O, U (1 to 5): GOD = 7 + 4 + 4 = 15 and DEVIL = 4 + 2 + 22 + 3 + 12 = 43. HUMEN = 8 + 5 + 13 + 2 + 14 = 42.

questions.text: ‘Eye’ is related to ‘Glasses’ in the same way as ‘______’ is related to ‘Dialyser’.
questions.explanation: Glasses correct the sight of a failing eye; a dialyser does the work of failing kidneys, filtering the blood.

questions.text: Four number-pairs have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the number-pair that is different.
questions.explanation: 17 : 204, 7 : 84 and 11 : 132 are each a number and 12 times it (17 × 12, 7 × 12, 11 × 12). 9 : 99 is 9 × 11, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Who among the following was NOT one of the recipients of the US military decoration 'the Legion of Merit' in December 2020?
questions.explanation: In December 2020 the US conferred the Legion of Merit on Narendra Modi, Shinzo Abe and Scott Morrison. Boris Johnson was not among the recipients.

questions.text: Which of the following national waterways has been INCORRECTLY matched with its associated river?
questions.explanation: The Sutlej is not National Waterway 6: under the National Waterways Act, 2016, NW 6 is the Aai river in Assam (the Barak is NW 16). NW 1 is the Ganga, NW 2 the Brahmaputra and NW 4 includes the Krishna (with the Godavari).

questions.text: Who founded the famous Vikramashila University in the ninth century?
questions.explanation: Vikramashila, in present-day Bihar, was founded by the Pala king Dharmapala.

questions.text: Which country was the host of the 15th G20 Leaders’ Summit 2020?
questions.explanation: Saudi Arabia hosted the 15th G20 Leaders' Summit, held virtually from Riyadh in November 2020.

questions.text: The legal provisions governing the management of foreign exchange reserves are laid down in the Reserve Bank of India Act, ______.
questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 sets out how the RBI may hold and invest the country's foreign exchange reserves.

questions.text: Who among the following won the ‘Golden Boot’ at FIFA World Cup 2018?
questions.explanation: England's Harry Kane won the Golden Boot at the 2018 World Cup with six goals.

questions.text: The nucleus of a cell is surrounded by a jelly-like substance called:
questions.explanation: The cytoplasm is the jelly-like substance between the cell membrane and the nucleus.

questions.text: Which of the following Union Ministries of India launched a pilot ‘Pey Jal Survekshan’ on 16 February 2021?
options: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs launched the pilot Pey Jal Survekshan under the Jal Jeevan Mission (Urban), to survey drinking water supply in cities.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who was the Governor-General of Bengal when the Permanent Settlement was introduced there in 1793?
questions.explanation: Lord Cornwallis introduced the Permanent Settlement of land revenue in Bengal in 1793.

questions.text: Which of the following is the largest bituminous coalfield in India?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Jharia, in the Damodar valley in Jharkhand's Dhanbad district, which holds India's largest reserves of bituminous coking coal, the coal used for making steel.

questions.text: In which of the following states is the Ajanta caves situated?
questions.explanation: The Ajanta caves, Buddhist rock-cut caves famous for their murals, are in Maharashtra.

questions.text: The total number of fundamental duties provided by the Constitution of India is:
questions.explanation: Article 51A lists 11 Fundamental Duties: ten added by the 42nd Amendment (1976) and the eleventh by the 86th Amendment (2002).

questions.text: On a computer keyboard, the Shift and Alt keys are examples of:
questions.explanation: Modifier keys such as Shift, Alt and Ctrl change the action of another key pressed with them.

questions.text: With which of the following sports is the FedEx Cup associated?
questions.explanation: The FedEx Cup is the season-long points championship of golf's PGA Tour.

questions.text: Where was ‘Dev Deepawali Mahotsav’ celebrated in the presence of the PM Narendra Modi in November 2020?
questions.explanation: Dev Deepawali is celebrated on the ghats of the Ganga at Varanasi on Kartik Purnima; the Prime Minister attended it on 30 November 2020.

questions.text: What is the meaning of the term 'collateral' in the context of the banking system?
options: Collateral is an asset of the government that is used for the protection of consumers.
Collateral is an asset that a borrower owns and uses this as a guarantee to a lender until the loan is repaid.
Collateral is an asset that a borrower took as a loan.
Collateral is an asset that the government provides to farmers.
questions.explanation: Collateral is an asset the borrower pledges to the lender as security; the lender may take it if the loan is not repaid.

questions.text: Which of the following is the slowest type of internet connection?
questions.explanation: Dial-up connects over a telephone line at no more than 56 kbit/s, far slower than DSL, cable or satellite.

questions.text: World Thyroid Day is observed on ______.
questions.explanation: World Thyroid Day is observed on 25 May.

questions.text: A mango tree is an example of a/an:
questions.explanation: A mango tree makes its own food by photosynthesis, so it is an autotroph.

questions.text: In October 2019, who became the youngest cricketer in the world to score a double century in List A cricket?
questions.explanation: Yashasvi Jaiswal scored 203 for Mumbai against Jharkhand in the Vijay Hazare Trophy in October 2019, at 17 the youngest batsman to score a List A double century.

questions.text: Which of the following nations is the smallest neighbour of India in terms of area?
questions.explanation: The Maldives, about 300 km², is the smallest of India's neighbours by area; Nepal, Bangladesh and Afghanistan are far larger.

questions.text: Who among the following singers was called ‘Mallika-e-Ghazal’ or the queen of Ghazal?
questions.explanation: Begum Akhtar, the singer of ghazal, dadra and thumri, was called 'Mallika-e-Ghazal'.

questions.text: Who is the author of the novel ‘Burnt Sugar’?
questions.explanation: 'Burnt Sugar' is the debut novel of Avni Doshi; it was shortlisted for the 2020 Booker Prize.

questions.text: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India makes provision for protection in respect of conviction for offences?
questions.explanation: Article 20 protects a person against retrospective criminal laws, being punished twice for the same offence, and being compelled to be a witness against himself.

questions.text: Which of the following hills is situated in Andhra Pradesh?
questions.explanation: The Nagari Hills are in Chittoor district, Andhra Pradesh. The Kaimur Hills lie across Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, Pachmarhi is in Madhya Pradesh and Girnar in Gujarat.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Break the ice
options: Make a beginning or start something
Make things available for a party
questions.explanation: To 'break the ice' is to make a start, easing the awkwardness at the beginning of a meeting or conversation.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. “Regard of whether” the students were ready or not the teacher announced the dates of the test.
questions.explanation: 'Regardless of whether' (without considering whether) is the set phrase; 'regard of whether' is not idiomatic.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Silt
questions.explanation: 'Silt' is the fine sand and clay that flowing water carries and leaves behind: a 'residue'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'succeed'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The arrangement of events or dates in the order of their occurrence.
questions.explanation: Chronology is the arrangement of events in the order in which they happened. 'Chronic' means long-lasting.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Vacillate
questions.explanation: To 'vacillate' is to keep changing one's mind: to 'waver'.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. The country gained admission to the United Nations in 1955. B. In 2008, however, after a decade long period of violence and turbulent negotiation with a strong Maoist insurgency, the monarchy was dissolved, and Nepal was declared a democratic republic. C. In 1991 the kingdom established a multiparty parliamentary system. D. Nepal, long under the rule of hereditary prime ministers favouring a policy of isolation, remained closed to the outside world until a palace revolt in 1950 restored the crown’s authority in 1951.
questions.explanation: D introduces Nepal and its history up to 1951; A (1955), C (1991) and B (2008, 'however') follow in order of date: DACB.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Vidya put on her mask, / sanitise her hands / and walked into the shop.
questions.explanation: The three actions are in sequence and must share the past tense: 'put on her mask, sanitised her hands and walked into the shop'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Rigid
questions.explanation: 'Rigid' means stiff and unbending; its opposite is 'flexible'. 'Firm' and 'adamant' are near synonyms.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. Ravi drove the car towards the highway for a trial run.
options: The car was driving towards the highway for a trial run by Ravi.
The car had driven towards the highway for a trial run by Ravi.
The car had been driven for a trial run by Ravi towards the highway.
The car was driven towards the highway for a trial run by Ravi.
questions.explanation: The simple past 'drove' becomes 'was driven', with the rest of the sentence kept in order and the agent 'by Ravi' at the end.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. First, a new article comes into our offices. B. Every article in the Encyclopedia goes through a rigorous editorial process to make sure it's clear, accurate, objective and fair. C. The article is first reviewed by a fact checker, who uses a variety of sources to make sure the article is accurate and the facts are correct. D. The author may be an editor at the Encyclopedia who knows that subject or a prominent scholar with specialised expertise in that field.
questions.explanation: B introduces the editorial process, A begins it ('First, a new article comes'), D describes the article's author and C the review by a fact checker: BADC.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. As the Principal was busy, she ______ a senior teacher to attend the conference on her behalf.
questions.explanation: To 'depute' someone is to appoint them to act on one's behalf.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. If a person tests positive for Covid-19, “he have to isolate himself” immediately so that he does not infect others.
questions.explanation: The singular subject 'he' takes 'has': 'he has to isolate himself'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech. The customer asked the bank manager if they were working on the following Saturday.
options: The customer asked the bank manager, “Are they working on the previous Saturday?”
The customer said to the bank manager, “Are you working next Saturday?”
The customer asks the bank manager, “If you were working on the following Saturday?”
The customer said to the bank manager, “Were they working on the previous Saturday?”
questions.explanation: In direct speech 'asked' becomes 'said to', 'they were working' returns to 'Are you working', and 'the following Saturday' becomes 'next Saturday'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Your advices were timely / and guided me / to take the right decisions.
questions.explanation: 'Advice' is uncountable and takes a singular verb: 'Your advice was timely'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Inept
questions.explanation: 'Inept' means lacking skill; its opposite is 'competent'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A lean patch
options: Cloth that is beginning to tear
A part of hair that is thin
questions.explanation: A 'lean patch' is a period of poor performance or little success.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A place of ideal perfection especially in laws, government, and social conditions
questions.explanation: A utopia is an imagined place or state where everything, its laws, government and society included, is perfect.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. Carbohydrates are so called because they _____ carbon, oxygen and hydrogen.
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates 'contain' carbon, hydrogen and oxygen; 'consist' would need 'of'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Seychelles, one of the world’s smallest countries, is (1)______ of two main island groups: the Mahé group of (2)______ than 40 central, mountainous granitic islands and a (3)______ group of more than 70 outer, flat, coralline islands. The islands of the Mahé group are rocky and (4)______ have a narrow coastal strip and a central range of hills. The (5)______ feature of those islands, with their lush tropical vegetation, is that of high hanging gardens overlooking silver-white beaches and clear lagoons.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.explanation: 'Is composed of' means is made up of: Seychelles is made up of two main island groups.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Seychelles, one of the world’s smallest countries, is (1)______ of two main island groups: the Mahé group of (2)______ than 40 central, mountainous granitic islands and a (3)______ group of more than 70 outer, flat, coralline islands. The islands of the Mahé group are rocky and (4)______ have a narrow coastal strip and a central range of hills. The (5)______ feature of those islands, with their lush tropical vegetation, is that of high hanging gardens overlooking silver-white beaches and clear lagoons.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
questions.explanation: 'More than 40' gives the number of islands, as 'more than 70' does later in the sentence.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Seychelles, one of the world’s smallest countries, is (1)______ of two main island groups: the Mahé group of (2)______ than 40 central, mountainous granitic islands and a (3)______ group of more than 70 outer, flat, coralline islands. The islands of the Mahé group are rocky and (4)______ have a narrow coastal strip and a central range of hills. The (5)______ feature of those islands, with their lush tropical vegetation, is that of high hanging gardens overlooking silver-white beaches and clear lagoons.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
questions.explanation: The passage names two groups: the Mahé group and 'a second group' of outer, coralline islands.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Seychelles, one of the world’s smallest countries, is (1)______ of two main island groups: the Mahé group of (2)______ than 40 central, mountainous granitic islands and a (3)______ group of more than 70 outer, flat, coralline islands. The islands of the Mahé group are rocky and (4)______ have a narrow coastal strip and a central range of hills. The (5)______ feature of those islands, with their lush tropical vegetation, is that of high hanging gardens overlooking silver-white beaches and clear lagoons.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
questions.explanation: 'Typically' means as is characteristic: the rocky islands usually have a narrow coastal strip. 'Routinely', 'regularly' and 'habitually' describe repeated actions, not features.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Seychelles, one of the world’s smallest countries, is (1)______ of two main island groups: the Mahé group of (2)______ than 40 central, mountainous granitic islands and a (3)______ group of more than 70 outer, flat, coralline islands. The islands of the Mahé group are rocky and (4)______ have a narrow coastal strip and a central range of hills. The (5)______ feature of those islands, with their lush tropical vegetation, is that of high hanging gardens overlooking silver-white beaches and clear lagoons.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
questions.explanation: 'Predominant' means main or most noticeable: the islands' chief feature is their high hanging gardens.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 8, 11, 17, 26, 38, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 3, 6, 9, 12, so the next is 15: 38 + 15 = 53.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of numbers. 56 : 67
questions.explanation: The second number is the first plus the sum of its digits: 56 + 5 + 6 = 67. Likewise 85 + 8 + 5 = 98.

questions.text: Train A, which runs at a speed of 90 km/h, starts from Station Y at 8 a.m. Train B, which runs at a speed of 120 km/h, starts from Station Y on the same route at 8.10 a.m.. If Train B catches up with Train A at 8.40 a.m. at Station Z, then what is the distance between Stations Y and Z?
questions.explanation: From 8.10 to 8.40 a.m. Train B runs for half an hour at 120 km/h: 60 km. (Train A, in 40 minutes at 90 km/h, has also covered 60 km.)

questions.text: Sunaina introduced Ritik as the son of the brother of her mother. How is Ritik related to Sunaina?
questions.explanation: The son of her mother's brother is the son of Sunaina's maternal uncle: her cousin.

questions.text: In a certain code language, TOGETHER is coded as 119 and MASTER is coded as 87. How will REVERSE be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter takes the place of its opposite in the alphabet (A = 26, B = 25, ..., Z = 1) and 1 is added to the total: MASTER = 14 + 26 + 8 + 7 + 22 + 9 + 1 = 87. REVERSE = 9 + 22 + 5 + 22 + 9 + 8 + 22 + 1 = 98.

questions.text: Four letter-clusters have been given in the options, out of which three letter-clusters are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the letter-cluster that is different.
questions.explanation: In UROL, QNKH and JGDA each letter is 3 places before the one before it. GDBY moves −3, −2, −3 (B back to Y wrapping round), so it is the odd one.

questions.text: In a certain code language, TRAILER is written as QPXGICO. How will ALMIRAH be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move back 3 and 2 places in turn: T → Q, R → P, A → X, I → G, L → I, E → C, R → O. So A → X, L → J, M → J, I → G, R → O, A → Y, H → E: XJJGOYE.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. 32 : 63 : 123
questions.explanation: Each number is twice the one before it minus the difference between that number's digits: 32 × 2 − (3 − 2) = 63 and 63 × 2 − (6 − 3) = 123. Likewise 26 × 2 − (6 − 2) = 48 and 48 × 2 − (8 − 4) = 92.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. Hollow : Worthless : : Solid : ?
questions.explanation: Said of a promise or an argument, 'hollow' means worthless and 'solid' means sound: each pair are words of similar meaning.

questions.text: Four words have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the word that is different.
questions.explanation: Confident, intelligent and honest are adjectives naming good qualities; 'coward' is a noun, and names a weakness.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All bats are sticks. All sticks are woods. Conclusions: I. Some woods are not bats. II. All bats are woods.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
questions.explanation: All bats are sticks and all sticks are woods, so all bats are woods (II). I need not follow: every wood might be a bat.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. Sacred : Profane : : Barren : ?
questions.explanation: 'Profane' is the opposite of 'sacred', as 'fertile' is the opposite of 'barren'.

questions.text: Select the correct option that indicates the arrangement of the given words in a logical and meaningful order. 1. Beam 2. Canopy 3. Foundation 4. Roof 5. Column
questions.explanation: A building rises from its foundation (3) through columns (5) and beams (1) to the roof (4), with a canopy (2), a projecting cover, added last.

questions.text: Which two digits and two signs need to be interchanged so as to balance the given equation? 98 ÷ 4 − 126 + 96 × 5 = 266
Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term. COMPETE : OCETPME : : EXTREME : ?
