questions.text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given words. a period of two weeks
questions.explanation: A fortnight is a period of two weeks.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined segment in the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement' I must have dropped “one” of my gloves in the car.
questions.explanation: 'One of' is followed by a plural noun, and 'one of my gloves' says that a single glove was dropped, so no change is needed.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. It is ______ to see so many of our fellow Indians help the migrants in their struggle to go home.
questions.explanation: 'Heartening' means encouraging or cheering: the sight of people helping lifts the spirits. 'Savouring' and 'relishing' mean enjoying something, which does not fit 'It is ___ to see'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. In the ‘Kingdom of Fools’, both the king and the ministers were complete fools. They didn’t want to do things (1)______ other kingdoms, so they decided to (2)______ night into day and day into night. They (3)______ that everyone should be awake at night, (4)_______ their lands and run their (5)______ only after dark and should go to bed as soon as the sun came up.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank no. 1.
questions.explanation: They did not want to do things 'like' other kingdoms, that is, in the same way as them.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. In the ‘Kingdom of Fools’, both the king and the ministers were complete fools. They didn’t want to do things (1)______ other kingdoms, so they decided to (2)______ night into day and day into night. They (3)______ that everyone should be awake at night, (4)_______ their lands and run their (5)______ only after dark and should go to bed as soon as the sun came up.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank no. 2.
questions.explanation: They decided to 'change' night into day: the phrase is 'change into'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. In the ‘Kingdom of Fools’, both the king and the ministers were complete fools. They didn’t want to do things (1)______ other kingdoms, so they decided to (2)______ night into day and day into night. They (3)______ that everyone should be awake at night, (4)_______ their lands and run their (5)______ only after dark and should go to bed as soon as the sun came up.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank no. 3.
questions.explanation: The king and his ministers 'ordered' that everyone should be awake at night.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. In the ‘Kingdom of Fools’, both the king and the ministers were complete fools. They didn’t want to do things (1)______ other kingdoms, so they decided to (2)______ night into day and day into night. They (3)______ that everyone should be awake at night, (4)_______ their lands and run their (5)______ only after dark and should go to bed as soon as the sun came up.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank no. 4.
questions.explanation: To 'till' the land is to plough and prepare it for crops.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. In the ‘Kingdom of Fools’, both the king and the ministers were complete fools. They didn’t want to do things (1)______ other kingdoms, so they decided to (2)______ night into day and day into night. They (3)______ that everyone should be awake at night, (4)_______ their lands and run their (5)______ only after dark and should go to bed as soon as the sun came up.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank no. 5.
questions.explanation: People were to 'run their business', their trade and work, only after dark.

questions.text: Four letter-clusters have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the letter-cluster that is different.
questions.explanation: In BDMS, HKPT and KMPV each letter comes later in the alphabet than the one before it. MIGF runs backwards, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: ₹481 is distributed among A, B and C in such a way that B gets two-thirds of what A gets and C gets three-fourths of what B gets. How much does B get?

Two statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All statements are answers. Some statements are questions. Conclusions: I. No question is a statement. II. Some answers are statements. III. Some questions are statements.
options: Only conclusions I and III follow
Either conclusion I or III follows
Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions II and III follow
questions.explanation: All statements are answers, so some answers are statements (II). Some statements are questions, so some questions are statements (III), which rules out I.

questions.text: If 'A + B' means 'A is the mother of B', 'A × B' means 'A is the sister of B', and 'A * B' means 'A is the daughter of B', then how is R related to P in the following expression? 'R + V × Q × M * P'
questions.explanation: R is the mother of V; V, Q and M are sisters; and M is the daughter of P. So R and P are M's parents: R is P's wife.

questions.text: Select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 35, 35, 33, 99, 95, 475, ?
questions.explanation: Multiply by 1, subtract 2, multiply by 3, subtract 4, multiply by 5, subtract 6: 35, 35, 33, 99, 95, 475, so next comes 475 − 6 = 469.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. {2, 2, 9}
questions.explanation: In {2, 2, 9} the second number is half the square of the first (2² ÷ 2 = 2) and the third is the square of one more than the first (3² = 9). Likewise 4² ÷ 2 = 8 and 5² = 25.

questions.text: In a certain code language, BANKER is coded as 57 and SPAN is coded as 54. How will PRANK be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each code is the sum of the letters' places in the alphabet plus the number of letters: BANKER = 2 + 1 + 14 + 11 + 5 + 18 + 6 = 57 and SPAN = 19 + 16 + 1 + 14 + 4 = 54. So PRANK = 16 + 18 + 1 + 14 + 11 + 5 = 65.

questions.text: Four numbers have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the number that is different.
questions.explanation: 2197 = 13³, 4913 = 17³ and 1331 = 11³; 2379 is not a perfect cube, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers in the set share the same relationship as the numbers in the given set. (14, 22, 77)
questions.explanation: The third number is the product of the first two divided by 4: 14 × 22 ÷ 4 = 77. Likewise 18 × 32 ÷ 4 = 144.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of numbers. 28 : 70
questions.explanation: The second number is 2.5 times the first: 28 × 2.5 = 70. Likewise 18 × 2.5 = 45.

questions.text: ‘Bracelet’ is related to ‘Ornaments’ in the same way as ‘Clove’ is related to ‘______’.
questions.explanation: A bracelet is a kind of ornament, as a clove is a kind of spice.

questions.text: Select the correct option that indicates the arrangement of the given words in a logical and meaningful order. 1. Class 2. Admission 3. Certificate 4. Application 5. Assessment
questions.explanation: Application (4), Admission (2), Class (1), Assessment (5), Certificate (3).

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 39 ÷ 3 × 13 + 26 – 13 = 2
Three of the following four words are alike in a certain way and one is different. Select the odd one.
questions.explanation: Contentment is a pleasant feeling; jealousy, sadness and disgust are unpleasant ones.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. NEED : OGHH : : FAST : ?
questions.explanation: N, E, E, D move +1, +2, +3, +4 to give OGHH. Likewise F, A, S, T give G, C, V, X: GCVX.

questions.text: In a code language, SAUCE is written as ASVEC. How will MEANT be written as in that language?
questions.explanation: The first two letters swap, the middle one moves one place forward and the last two swap: SA U CE → AS V EC. So ME A NT → EM B TN: EMBTN.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that, when placed from left to right in the blanks below, will complete the letter sequence correctly. K _ P _ L C _ R _ C P _ N _ P R
options: E R P R R C
C P P M R R
M R P M R R
C R P M R C
questions.explanation: With C, R, P, M, R, C in the blanks the series reads KCPR LCPR MCPR NCPR: the first letter moves one place forward each time and CPR repeats.

questions.text: Select the option in which the words share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of words. Necklace : Gold
questions.explanation: A necklace is made from gold, as paper is made from wood pulp.

questions.text: Whose autobiography is titled 'The Substance and the Shadow'?
questions.explanation: 'The Substance and the Shadow' (2014) is the autobiography of the actor Dilip Kumar.

questions.text: Which of the following file formats does MS Paint use to open and save files in Windows?
questions.explanation: MS Paint opens and saves image files such as JPEG, PNG, BMP and GIF; .DOC, .XLS and .PPT are Word, Excel and PowerPoint formats.

questions.text: Which of the following nations ranked first in the World Press Freedom index 2020?
questions.explanation: Norway topped Reporters Without Borders' World Press Freedom Index 2020, for the fourth year running.

questions.text: The musical instrument 'Kartal' from the state of Rajasthan comes under the category of ______.
questions.explanation: The kartal is a pair of wooden clappers struck together; an instrument whose own body vibrates to make the sound is an idiophone.

questions.text: Who among the following is India’s highest wicket taker in test cricket as of December 2020?
questions.explanation: Anil Kumble took 619 Test wickets, the most by an Indian bowler.

questions.text: What is India’s rank on the World Economic Forum’s Global Competitiveness Index of 141 countries for the year 2019?
questions.explanation: India fell ten places, from 58th to 68th of 141 economies, in the World Economic Forum's Global Competitiveness Index 2019.

questions.text: The deficiency of which of the following vitamins causes night blindness?
questions.explanation: Vitamin A is needed to make rhodopsin, the light-sensitive pigment of the retina, so its deficiency causes night blindness.

questions.text: Which of the following is a computer application software?
questions.explanation: A word processor is application software for writing documents. RAM is hardware, and Visual Basic and Java are programming languages.

questions.text: How many states does the ‘STARS’ project launched by the Government of India and World Bank in 2020 seek to cover?
questions.explanation: STARS (Strengthening Teaching-Learning and Results for States), backed by the World Bank, covers six states: Himachal Pradesh, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Kerala and Odisha.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In the Battle of Swally (1612) the British fought against the ______.
questions.explanation: At Swally (Suvali), near Surat, the English East India Company's ships under Thomas Best defeated the Portuguese in 1612.

questions.text: Where is Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple) situated?
questions.explanation: The Harmandir Sahib, the holiest gurdwara of Sikhism, is in Amritsar, Punjab.

questions.text: Which Indian state was the highest contributor to Food Corporation of India (FCI)’s total paddy procurement across the country till May 2020?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Telangana, which supplied the largest share of the paddy procured in the 2019-20 rabi (yasangi) season, the procurement under way in April and May 2020. Over the whole 2019-20 marketing season, kharif included, Punjab procured more.

questions.text: Heat, in ______, is a type of energy transfer from a warmer substance to a colder one.
questions.explanation: In thermodynamics, heat is energy that passes from a hotter body to a colder one because of the difference in their temperatures.

questions.text: LAC (Line of Actual Control) is an effective border between India and ______.
questions.explanation: The Line of Actual Control separates Indian-held and Chinese-held territory; the line with Pakistan in Jammu and Kashmir is the Line of Control.

questions.text: In which of the following categories does Indian boxer Lovlina Borgohain play?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 69 kg: when the exam was held, in August 2021, Lovlina Borgohain boxed as a welterweight (69 kg), in which she had just won bronze at the Tokyo Olympics. She later moved up to 75 kg, the class in which she won the 2023 world title.

questions.text: Dr. Tsering Landol, who was one of the recipients of the Padma Bhushan 2020 award, hails from:
questions.explanation: Dr Tsering Landol, Ladakh's first woman gynaecologist, received the Padma Bhushan in 2020 for her work in women's healthcare.

questions.text: The National Education Policy (NEP), 2020 commits to raising the total expenditure by states and centre on education to ______ of GDP.
questions.explanation: NEP 2020 aims to raise public spending on education by the Centre and the states together to 6% of GDP.

questions.text: Which sport has been approved to be played at the 2024 Summer Olympics in Paris for the first time?
questions.explanation: In December 2020 the IOC added breaking (breakdancing) to the Paris 2024 programme, its first appearance at the Olympic Games.

questions.text: What was the total number of gold medals won by India at Commonwealth Games 2018?
questions.explanation: India won 66 medals at the 2018 Commonwealth Games on the Gold Coast: 26 gold, 20 silver and 20 bronze.

questions.text: As of January 2021, more than 93% of India’s chromite resources were located in:
questions.explanation: Odisha holds well over 90% of India's chromite resources, most of them in the Sukinda valley.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following presided over the special session of Congress in September 1923 and at the age of 35 became the youngest man to be elected as the President of the Congress?
questions.explanation: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad presided over the special session at Delhi in September 1923; at 35 he was the youngest President of the Congress.

questions.text: ______ holds office from the date of his/her election till immediately before the first meeting of the Lok Sabha after the dissolution of the one to which he/she was elected.
questions.explanation: Under Article 94 the Speaker does not vacate office when the Lok Sabha is dissolved, but holds it until just before the new House first meets.

questions.text: One-third of the members of the Vidhan Parishad retire every ______ year/s.
questions.explanation: A Legislative Council is not dissolved; as nearly as possible one-third of its members retire on the expiry of every second year (Article 172(2)).

questions.text: Which among the following is used as the fining agent in wine?
questions.explanation: Gelatin is added to wine as a fining agent: it binds tannins and haze-forming particles so that they settle out.

questions.text: 'Per Drop More Crop' is the goal for which Government of India scheme?
questions.explanation: 'Per Drop More Crop', which promotes micro-irrigation such as drip and sprinklers, is a component of the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Hard nut to crack
options: a person who likes to joke around
questions.explanation: A 'hard nut to crack' is a problem that is difficult to solve, or a person who is difficult to deal with.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution ’. The miscreants were shifted to another building that same evening and “was keeping” in custody by the police.
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'miscreants' needs a plural verb, and they were acted upon, so the passive: 'were kept in custody'.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. “Madam, please watch this program on our folk songs,” says Sitab.
options: Sitab says Madam is watching the program on our folk songs.
Sitab requests Madam to watch that program on their folk songs.
Sitab asks Madam have you watched the program on their folk songs.
Sitab said to Madam to watch the program on our folk songs.
questions.explanation: A request is reported with 'requests' and a to-infinitive, and 'our' becomes 'their': 'Sitab requests Madam to watch that program on their folk songs.' With the present-tense 'says', 'this' could strictly have stayed, but no other option reports the request: they turn it into a statement or a question, or use 'said to Madam to watch' with 'our' unchanged.

questions.text: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. When I was at school I found my class teacher to be the best mentor as she always have time to listen and guide.
options: as she always have time to listen and guide
questions.explanation: 'She' cannot take 'have', and the sentence is in the past: 'as she always had time to listen and guide'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. BONHOMIE
questions.explanation: 'Bonhomie' is cheerful friendliness: 'companionship'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. BEWILDER
questions.explanation: To 'bewilder' is to confuse; its opposite is to 'enlighten', to make clear. 'Confuse' is a synonym.

questions.text: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. The teacher and her student was engaged in a discussion on the current political crisis.
questions.explanation: Two subjects joined by 'and' take a plural verb: 'The teacher and her student were engaged'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined segment in the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement' The advertising industry wants us to believe “that buy more” stuff will make us happier.
questions.explanation: The subject of 'will make' must be a noun phrase, so the gerund: 'that buying more stuff will make us happier'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. Something which cannot be taken by force
questions.explanation: 'Impregnable' means unable to be captured or broken into by force. 'Irresistible' means too strong to be resisted.

questions.text: Select the option which means the same as the group of words given. Not active or growing
questions.explanation: 'Dormant' means inactive or not growing for a time, like a seed or a volcano. 'Inanimate' means not alive at all.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom: know inside out
options: To know a little about something
To know everything by rote memory
To always know a lot about every topic
questions.explanation: To 'know something inside out' is to know it thoroughly, in every detail.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. Radha plays the sitar very well.
options: The sitar is being played by Radha very well.
Radha has been playing the sitar very well.
Radha is playing the sitar very well.
The sitar is played very well by Radha.
questions.explanation: The simple present 'plays' becomes 'is played', with the object 'the sitar' as the subject: 'The sitar is played very well by Radha.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. Savita was crying ______ as she felt that her world had fallen apart due to the accident.
questions.explanation: To 'cry bitterly' is to cry with deep grief, which fits a world that had fallen apart.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. FASCINATION
questions.explanation: 'Fascination' is the power to attract and hold interest: 'appeal'.

questions.text: Examine the four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, pick the one that gives their correct order. A. Yet few people know the long history of making soap. B. As a prevention, they recommend the frequent washing of hands for 20 seconds. C. Scientists have declared that COVID-19 is here to stay. D. This advice is practical and easy to follow as soap is a common and inexpensive consumer product.
questions.explanation: C says COVID-19 is here to stay, B gives the scientists' advice, D says the advice is easy to follow because soap is common, and A turns ('Yet') to soap's little-known history: CBDA.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The migrant crisis led several states to ______ existing labour laws in order to improve their condition.
questions.explanation: Laws already in force are changed, that is 'amended'; existing laws cannot be 'introduced' or 'initiated', and 'abandon' does not fit 'to improve their condition'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. EQUILIBRIUM
questions.explanation: 'Equilibrium' is a state of balance; its opposite is 'imbalance'. 'Stability' is a synonym.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'noncommittal' (also 'non-committal').

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, select the one that gives their correct order. A. How will we ever reach our goal if we don't follow our ideals and principles and follow the path we say we believe in? B. Many of us believe in God, do our daily prayers and vow to be good. C. But unfortunately, when it comes to putting our ideas into practice, we procrastinate. D. There may be variations in our chosen ideals of Him, but each of us believes in Him nevertheless.
questions.explanation: B says many of us believe in God, D adds that our ideals of Him vary, C turns ('But') to our failure to practise them and A asks how we will ever reach our goal: BDCA.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. An appetising and nutritious meal is always recommended because what we eat (1) ______ our senses. The effect of food on our mind, body and spirit had been the centre (2) ______ discussion even in ancient Greece, when Pythagoras argued in favour of a healthy, vegetarian (3) ______. Though at the time when the philosopher lived, in around 500 BC, the term ‘vegetarianism’ was (4) ______, his diet came to be known as ‘the Pythagorean diet'. He is known for his theory on geometry, but few are aware of his profound (5) ______ on food habits!

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 1.
questions.explanation: What we eat 'affects', that is has an effect on, our senses, as the next sentence's 'effect of food' confirms.

questions.explanation: Few know of his profound 'wisdom' on food habits, in contrast to his fame for geometry.

questions.text: In a code language, CIRCUS is written as DKUGZY. How will JOKER be written in the same language?
questions.explanation: The letters move forward 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 places: CIRCUS → DKUGZY. So J + 1 = K, O + 2 = Q, K + 3 = N, E + 4 = I, R + 5 = W: KQNIW.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. {46, 53, 64}
questions.explanation: The second number is the first plus 7 and the third is the first with its digits reversed: 46 + 7 = 53, and 64. Likewise 34 + 7 = 41, and 43.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. REST : SCTR : : BEST : ?
questions.explanation: The letters move +1, −2, +1, −2: R → S, E → C, S → T, T → R gives SCTR. So BEST → CCTR.

questions.text: Select the correct option that indicates the arrangement of the given words in a logical and meaningful order. 1. Income 2. Employment 3. Superannuation 4. Interview 5. Education 6. Promotion
questions.explanation: Education comes first, then the interview, employment, income, promotion and finally superannuation (retirement): 5, 4, 2, 1, 6, 3.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series. b a _ d a _ b b _ d _ a c b _ a d d _ c b
options: c a d d b a
d c d a b d
b c a c b a
d c a d b a
questions.explanation: With d, c, a, d, b, a in the blanks the block 'baddacb' repeats: baddacb baddacb baddacb.

questions.text: ‘Second’ is related to ‘Minute’ in the same way as ‘Day’ is related to ‘______’.
questions.explanation: Seconds make up a minute (60 of them), as days make up a week (7 of them).

questions.text: If ‘×’ means ‘–’, ‘÷’ means ‘+’, ‘+’ means ‘×’ and ‘–’ means ‘÷’, then what will be the value of the following expression? 16 ÷ 32 – 4 × 2 + 1 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 16 + 32 ÷ 4 − 2 × 1 = 16 + 8 − 2 = 22.

questions.text: In a certain code language, MAKER is coded as 90. How will BROTHER be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Consonants take their place in the alphabet and vowels their place counted from Z: MAKER = 13 + 26 + 11 + 22 + 18 = 90. So BROTHER = 2 + 18 + 12 + 20 + 8 + 22 + 18 = 100.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (2, 6, 9)
questions.explanation: The second number is three times the first and the third is 1.5 times the second: 2 × 3 = 6 and 6 × 1.5 = 9. Likewise 4 × 3 = 12 and 12 × 1.5 = 18.

questions.text: Sunita appeared for a test consisting of 260 questions and answered 40% of the first 130 questions correctly. What percentage of the rest 130 questions must she answer correctly so as to score 60% in the entire test?
questions.explanation: 60% of 260 is 156 correct answers. She has 40% of 130 = 52, so she needs 104 more out of 130: 104/130 = 80%.

questions.text: ‘U + W’ means ‘U is the father of W’; ‘U – W’ means ‘U is the wife of W’; ‘U × W’ means ‘U is the brother of W’; and ‘U ÷ W’ means ‘U is the daughter of W’. If ‘K ÷ L + M + N’, then how is K related to N?
questions.explanation: K is the daughter of L, L is the father of M and M is the father of N. So K is M's sister, and N, M's child, is her brother's child: K is N's aunt.

questions.text: Four numbers have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the number that is different.
questions.explanation: 73, 127 and 89 are prime numbers; 115 = 5 × 23 is not.

questions.text: Four letter-clusters have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the letter-cluster that is different.
questions.explanation: The letters' places in the alphabet add up to 50 in HKMR (8 + 11 + 13 + 18), FMNQ (6 + 13 + 14 + 17) and BJPV (2 + 10 + 16 + 22). DLRT adds up to 4 + 12 + 18 + 20 = 54.

questions.text: Three statements are given, followed by four conclusions numbered I, II, III and IV. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follows from the statements. Statements: All cats are birds. Some tigers are cats. All bees are tigers. Conclusions: I. All bees are birds. II. Some bees are birds. III. Some birds are tigers. IV. All tigers are birds.
questions.explanation: Some tigers are cats and all cats are birds, so some tigers are birds: some birds are tigers (III). All bees are tigers, but those tigers need not be the ones that are cats, so I and II do not follow, and nothing says all tigers are birds (IV).

questions.text: Three of the following four words are alike in a certain way and one is different. Select the odd one.
questions.explanation: The cat, the lion and the tiger belong to the cat family (felines); the dog does not.

questions.text: Select the option in which the words share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of words. Purification : Filter
questions.explanation: A filter is the tool used for purification, as a spade is the tool used for digging.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of numbers. 24 : 37
questions.explanation: 24 = 5² − 1 and 37 = 6² + 1: one less than a square, then one more than the next square. Likewise 63 = 8² − 1 and 82 = 9² + 1.

questions.text: Select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 63, 63, 56, 56, 49, 49, 42, ?
questions.explanation: Each number appears twice and then falls by 7: 63, 63, 56, 56, 49, 49, 42, 42.

questions.text: In which of the following states is the Loktak Lake located?
questions.explanation: Loktak Lake, the largest freshwater lake in North-East India, known for its floating phumdis, is in Manipur.

questions.text: Which of the following mountain ranges is home to the second-highest peak of the world, K2?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the East Karakoram Range. K2 is the highest peak of the Karakoram, in its Baltoro Muztagh (more often described as the central Karakoram), and this is the only option that names the Karakoram; none of the other three ranges reaches 8,000 m.

questions.text: What was the theme of the World Sustainable Development Summit 2021?
options: Towards 2030 Goals: Making the Decade Count
Attaining the 2030 Agenda: Delivering on our Promise
Redefining Our Common Future: Safe and Secure Environment For All
questions.explanation: The theme of TERI's World Sustainable Development Summit 2021 was 'Redefining Our Common Future: Safe and Secure Environment for All'.

questions.text: Hamideh Banu Maryam Makani was the wife of Mughal emperor ______.
questions.explanation: Hamida Banu Begum, given the title Maryam Makani, was Humayun's wife and the mother of Akbar.

questions.text: In which of the following states is the Sirki Waterfall located?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Arunachal Pradesh, where the Sirki Waterfall lies near Pasighat in East Siang district.

questions.text: Which of the following international awards did Indian drama series 'Delhi Crime' win in 2020?
options: Golden Globe Award for Best Television Series – Drama
British Academy Television Award for Best Drama Series
International Emmy Award for Best Drama Series
Cannes Corporate Media & TV Awards – Best Drama
questions.explanation: 'Delhi Crime' won the International Emmy Award for Best Drama Series in November 2020, the first Indian series to win it.

questions.text: Who among the following won the Golden Globe 2020 award for ‘Best Performance by an Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama’?
questions.explanation: Renée Zellweger won the 2020 Golden Globe for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama for 'Judy'.

questions.text: Since 2000, Euro norms are followed in India under the name ______ Stage Emission Standards for four wheeled vehicles.
questions.explanation: India's emission norms for motor vehicles, based on the European (Euro) norms, are called the Bharat Stage (BS) Emission Standards.

questions.text: The innermost part of a flower is called the:
questions.explanation: The pistil, the female part (stigma, style and ovary), sits at the centre of the flower inside the ring of stamens; petals and sepals form the outer whorls.

questions.text: Which of the following indigenous games is included in the Khelo India Youth Games 2021?
questions.explanation: In December 2020 the Sports Ministry added four indigenous games to the Khelo India Youth Games 2021: Gatka, Kalaripayattu, Thang-Ta and Mallakhamba.

questions.text: Who among the following was one of the winners of Nobel Prize in Physics 2020?
questions.explanation: Roger Penrose shared the 2020 Nobel Prize in Physics with Reinhard Genzel and Andrea Ghez, for work on black holes. Michel Mayor won in 2019, Arthur Ashkin in 2018 and Kip Thorne in 2017.

questions.text: In which of the following mountain ranges will you find the Guru Shikhar peak?
questions.explanation: Guru Shikhar, near Mount Abu in Rajasthan, is the highest peak of the Aravalli Range.

questions.text: Which keyboard shortcut in Microsoft Excel 2016 should you use to insert a new worksheet for Windows 10 operating system?
questions.explanation: In Excel, Shift + F11 inserts a new worksheet.

questions.text: Which of the following companies in India has tied up with Facebook to train offline retailers to go digital on social media platforms?
questions.explanation: In May 2020 Samsung India partnered Facebook to train its offline retailers to set up on Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp and reach customers online.

questions.text: According to Article 24 of the Constitution of India, a person below ______ years of age shall not be employed to work in any factory.
questions.explanation: Article 24 forbids employing a child below the age of fourteen in any factory, mine or other hazardous work.

questions.text: With which of the following musical instruments is the musician Zakir Hussain associated?
questions.explanation: Ustad Zakir Hussain, son of the tabla player Ustad Alla Rakha, was a tabla maestro.

questions.text: Who among the following film makers was conferred with the 'Padma Shri', the fourth highest civilian honour of the country, in 2020?
questions.explanation: Film and television producer Ekta Kapoor was among the Padma Shri awardees of 2020.

questions.text: With which of the following sports is Indian sportsperson Bhavani Devi associated?
questions.explanation: C. A. Bhavani Devi is a sabre fencer; at Tokyo 2020 she became the first Indian fencer to compete at the Olympics.

questions.text: Litmus paper changes to ______ colour when put in soap water.
questions.explanation: Soap solution is basic, and a base turns red litmus blue.

questions.text: Who among the following is the only Indian to have won an individual gold medal at the Olympics?
questions.explanation: Abhinav Bindra's 10 m air rifle gold at Beijing 2008 was India's only individual Olympic gold when this exam was held; Neeraj Chopra won the javelin gold at Tokyo on 7 August 2021, the day after this shift.

questions.text: What was India’s per capita net national income (estimated) during 2019-20?
questions.explanation: The first advance estimates (January 2020) put India's per capita net national income for 2019-20, at current prices, at ₹1,35,050.

questions.text: Who among the following was the President of the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) as of December 2020?
questions.explanation: Sourav Ganguly was President of the BCCI from October 2019 to October 2022.

questions.text: The normal term of every Lok Sabha is ______ years.
questions.explanation: Under Article 83(2) the Lok Sabha continues for five years from its first meeting, unless dissolved sooner.

questions.text: ‘Memoirs of Babur’ or ‘Baburnama’, also known as ‘Tuzk-e Babri’, was written by:
questions.explanation: The Baburnama is Babur's own memoir, written in Chagatai Turkic; Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khanan translated it into Persian under Akbar.

questions.text: ‘Ranapa’, a folk dance form of Odisha, consists of enacting chapters from the life of Lord ______.
questions.explanation: Ranapa, danced on stilts mainly in Odisha's Ganjam district, enacts episodes from the childhood of Krishna.

questions.text: Select the misspelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'boundary'. ('Instalment' is the British spelling.)

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. My brother lost / his job during the lockdown, / but he had got / a new job now.
questions.explanation: 'Now' calls for the present perfect: 'but he has got a new job now', not the past perfect 'had got'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'. A school teacher earns “fewer salary from” a college lecturer.
questions.explanation: 'Fewer' goes only with plural nouns ('fewer jobs'), and a comparison takes 'than', not 'from': 'A school teacher earns a lower salary than a college lecturer.'

questions.text: Given below are four sentences in jumbled order. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. Once, on an airplane, I leaned over to tie my shoelace. B. I found myself pinned helplessly in the crash position, unable to move. C. I always have catastrophes when I travel. D. Just at that moment, the person in the seat ahead threw his seat back into full recline.
questions.explanation: C states the theme (catastrophes when travelling), A begins the story, D gives the moment the seat came back and B the result: CADB.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A strong interest in something or someone
questions.explanation: A fixation is a very strong, even obsessive, interest in something or someone.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech. She told the car mechanic that her car was giving very low mileage.
options: The car mechanic said to her, “Your car is giving very low mileage.”
She said to the car mechanic, “Her car has been giving very low mileage.”
She said to the car mechanic, “My car is giving very low mileage.”
She asked the car mechanic, “Why is my car giving very low mileage?”
questions.explanation: In direct speech 'told' becomes 'said to', the past continuous 'was giving' returns to the present 'is giving', and 'her car' becomes 'my car'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. SAVAGE
questions.explanation: 'Savage' means wild and uncivilised; its opposite is 'cultured'. 'Violent', 'vicious' and 'brutal' are near synonyms.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. The workers’ union has threatened “for going to” an indefinite strike.
questions.explanation: 'Threaten' takes a to-infinitive, and a strike is something one goes 'on': 'threatened to go on an indefinite strike'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given words. To come to an end
questions.explanation: To 'expire' is to come to an end, as a licence or a period of time does.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. COMMENCE
questions.explanation: To 'commence' is to begin: to 'launch'. 'Resume' means to begin again after a pause.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Friendly
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'friendly' is 'hostile'. 'Amiable' is a synonym.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. Organic food seems to be “in vogue” these days.
questions.explanation: 'In vogue' means in fashion, popular at the time.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. Oprah Winfrey is one of the richest and most powerful American women, loved and admired by everyone. B. When she was only 19, she became the first black female assistant to Nashville’s evening news anchor. C. But Oprah had a very difficult and traumatic childhood. D. In 1986, Oprah became the television presenter of her own talk show called ‘The Oprah Winfrey Show’.
questions.explanation: A, which introduces Oprah, opens the paragraph, and ABDC is the only option that begins with it: B and D follow her career in order of date (at 19, then in 1986), and C, starting with 'But', sets her hard childhood against that success.

questions.text: Fill in the blank with most appropriate word. I am ______ of joining the armed forces.
questions.explanation: 'Desirous' takes 'of': 'desirous of joining'. 'Interested' takes 'in', 'keen' takes 'on' and 'eager' takes 'to' or 'for'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'beneficiary'.

questions.text: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. Every participant gave so outstanding performance that it became difficult to choose the winner.
questions.explanation: An adjective with a singular noun takes 'such a/an', not 'so': 'gave such an outstanding performance that it became difficult'.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. She has put fresh flowers in the flower vase.
options: Fresh flowers are put in the flower vase.
Fresh flowers are being put in the flower vase.
Fresh flowers has been put in the flower vase.
Fresh flowers have been put in the flower vase.
questions.explanation: The present perfect 'has put' becomes 'have been put', plural to agree with 'fresh flowers'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To play with fire
options: To act in a dangerous and risky way
To hold a revenge against someone
To fight fires like a fireman
To pour oil on a burning fire
questions.explanation: To 'play with fire' is to do something dangerous and risky.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Imitate
questions.explanation: To 'imitate' is to copy: to 'mimic'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. You don’t usually discuss money with friends, because it may ______ the relationship negatively.
questions.explanation: 'Affect' is the verb meaning to influence; 'effect' as a verb means to bring about. 'Improve' and 'strengthen' do not fit 'negatively'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. The little princess said, “I shut you in a golden cage because I wanted to have you all to (1) ______. I never knew it would make you so unhappy. I love you (2) ______ to grant you freedom and let you be happy in your (3) ______.” Then she opened the cage and let out the (4) ______ little bird. The bird said, “I will come back to sing you the (5) ______ songs I know,” and flew away into the blue.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank no. 1.
questions.explanation: The speaker is 'I', so the reflexive is 'myself': 'to have you all to myself'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. The little princess said, “I shut you in a golden cage because I wanted to have you all to (1) ______. I never knew it would make you so unhappy. I love you (2) ______ to grant you freedom and let you be happy in your (3) ______.” Then she opened the cage and let out the (4) ______ little bird. The bird said, “I will come back to sing you the (5) ______ songs I know,” and flew away into the blue.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank no. 2.
questions.explanation: 'Enough to' gives the degree that makes something possible: 'I love you enough to grant you freedom'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. The little princess said, “I shut you in a golden cage because I wanted to have you all to (1) ______. I never knew it would make you so unhappy. I love you (2) ______ to grant you freedom and let you be happy in your (3) ______.” Then she opened the cage and let out the (4) ______ little bird. The bird said, “I will come back to sing you the (5) ______ songs I know,” and flew away into the blue.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank no. 3.
questions.explanation: To be happy 'in your way', living as the bird itself chooses.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. The little princess said, “I shut you in a golden cage because I wanted to have you all to (1) ______. I never knew it would make you so unhappy. I love you (2) ______ to grant you freedom and let you be happy in your (3) ______.” Then she opened the cage and let out the (4) ______ little bird. The bird said, “I will come back to sing you the (5) ______ songs I know,” and flew away into the blue.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank no. 4.
questions.explanation: 'Terrified' (feeling fear) describes the caged bird; 'terrifying' would mean causing fear.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. The little princess said, “I shut you in a golden cage because I wanted to have you all to (1) ______. I never knew it would make you so unhappy. I love you (2) ______ to grant you freedom and let you be happy in your (3) ______.” Then she opened the cage and let out the (4) ______ little bird. The bird said, “I will come back to sing you the (5) ______ songs I know,” and flew away into the blue.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank no. 5.
questions.explanation: 'The ... songs I know' calls for a superlative: 'the loveliest songs'. 'Most lovelier' wrongly puts 'most' before the comparative 'lovelier'.

questions.text: Two statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All bottles are utensils. All kitchens are utensils. Conclusions: I. No bottle is a kitchen. II. Some bottles are kitchens. III. No utensil is a bottle.
options: Either conclusion I or II follows
Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions II and III follow
questions.explanation: Bottles and kitchens are both utensils, but nothing links them to each other, so neither I nor II is certain; they are a complementary pair (no bottle is a kitchen / some bottles are kitchens), so one of them must be true. III contradicts the first statement.

questions.text: Mahendra is the son of Naman, who is the brother of Reema’s mother. How is Mahendra related to Reema?
questions.explanation: Naman is the brother of Reema's mother, so he is her maternal uncle; his son Mahendra is Reema's cousin.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (15, 7, 252)
Three of the following four words are alike in a certain way and one is different. Select the odd one.
questions.explanation: Almond, cashew and walnuts are all dry fruits; 'dry fruits' is the class they belong to.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. FOR : MVY : : DEX : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 7 places forward: F → M, O → V, R → Y. So D → K, E → L and X → E (wrapping round after Z): KLE.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given letter series will complete the series. p _ q q r _ p p q _ r r _ p q _ _ r
options: p r q p q r
r p q r p q
q q p p r r
q p r q r q
questions.explanation: With p, r, q, p, q, r in the blanks the block ppqqrr repeats: ppqqrr ppqqrr ppqqrr.

questions.text: Select the option in which the words share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of words. Axe : Chop
questions.explanation: An axe is used to chop, as a chisel is used to carve: a tool and its work.

questions.text: Four letter-clusters have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the letter-cluster that is different.
questions.explanation: In XZCG, BDGK and MORV the letters move +2, +3, +4 (Z to C wrapping round). VYAE moves +3, +2, +4, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: In a code language, MAGIC is written as NZTRX. How will LAYER be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite in the alphabet (A ↔ Z, B ↔ Y, ...): M → N, A → Z, G → T, I → R, C → X. So L → O, A → Z, Y → B, E → V, R → I: OZBVI.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'FOSTER' is coded as '61219202218' and 'CARGO' is coded as '32618712'. How will 'MARRIAGE' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Consonants are written as their place in the alphabet, and vowels as the place of their opposite letter (A → Z = 26, E → V = 22, I → R = 18, O → L = 12): FOSTER = 6 12 19 20 22 18. MARRIAGE = 13 26 18 18 18 26 7 22.

questions.text: Four number-pairs have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the number-pair that is different.

Ankit is 30 years younger than his father. After 4 years Ankit's sister will be half the age of her father. The total of the present ages of Ankit and his sister is 67 years. What is the present age of Ankit's father?
questions.explanation: Let the father be F. Ankit is F − 30, and the sister, half the father's age in 4 years, is (F + 4)/2 − 4 = (F − 4)/2 now. (F − 30) + (F − 4)/2 = 67 gives 3F = 198, so F = 66.

questions.text: Select the correct option that indicates the arrangement of the given words in the order in which they appear in an English dictionary. 1. Mosaic 2. Mosquito 3. Mortgage 4. Moratorium 5. Morphed
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Moratorium (4), Morphed (5), Mortgage (3), Mosaic (1), Mosquito (2). 'Mora', 'Morp' and 'Mort' come in that order, then 'Mosa' before 'Mosq'.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fourth number in the same way as the first number is related to the second number and the fifth number is related to the sixth number. 26 : 182 : : ? : 203 : : 38 : 266
questions.explanation: The second number is 7 times the first: 26 × 7 = 182 and 38 × 7 = 266. So 203 ÷ 7 = 29.

questions.text: Which two signs and two numbers should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 12 × 5 + 7 ÷ 4 – 6 = 25
questions.explanation: Interchanging ÷ and − and 4 and 12: 4 × 5 + 7 − 12 ÷ 6 = 20 + 7 − 2 = 25.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers share the same relationship as that shared by the numbers in the given set. (6, 8, 192)
questions.explanation: The third number is 4 times the product of the first two: 6 × 8 × 4 = 192. Likewise 11 × 9 × 4 = 396.

questions.text: Select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 14, 29, 60, 123, ? , 505
‘Soldier’ is related to ‘Security’ in the same way as ‘Farmer’ is related to ‘________’.
questions.explanation: A soldier works for security, as a farmer works in agriculture: a worker and the field of his work.

questions.text: Who among the following represented India at the international level in shooting?
questions.explanation: Anjum Moudgil is an Indian rifle shooter, silver medallist in the 10 m air rifle at the 2018 World Championship. Aditi Chauhan and Ashalata Devi are footballers and Amit Panghal is a boxer.

questions.text: Ujjain is on the banks of river ______.
questions.explanation: Ujjain stands on the Kshipra (Shipra), a tributary of the Chambal, where the Simhastha Kumbh Mela is held.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a correct match of Dargah and its respective location?
options: Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki Dargah - Delhi
questions.explanation: The dargah of Shaikh Nizamuddin Auliya is in Delhi, not Agra. Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki's is at Mehrauli, Delhi, Haji Ali's in Mumbai and Muinuddin Chishti's at Ajmer.

questions.text: Which of the following was the first operating system written in 'C' language?
questions.explanation: UNIX, rewritten in C at Bell Labs in 1973, was the first operating system written in C.

questions.text: Which of the following is the correct full form of JPEG?
questions.explanation: JPEG stands for Joint Photographic Experts Group, the committee that created the image standard.

questions.text: Who among the following was the captain of women's hockey team of India as of December 2020?
questions.explanation: Rani Rampal was captain of India's women's hockey team in 2020, the year she received the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna.

questions.text: Who won the Chess.com's 2020 Junior Speed Online Chess Championship after beating Russia's Alexey Sarana?
questions.explanation: Nihal Sarin won Chess.com's 2020 Junior Speed Chess Championship, beating Alexey Sarana 18-7 in the final.

questions.text: Which Indian actor received the ‘Crystal Award’ at the World Economic Forum 2020?
questions.explanation: Deepika Padukone received the Crystal Award at the World Economic Forum in Davos in January 2020 for her work in raising awareness of mental health.

questions.text: Ministry of Finance introduced a new form called Form 26AS for:
questions.explanation: Form 26AS is a taxpayer's annual tax statement: it shows the tax deducted or collected at source and the taxes paid against the PAN.

questions.text: Which of the following national parks is situated in Kerala?
questions.explanation: Eravikulam National Park, in Idukki district, Kerala, is home to the Nilgiri tahr. Tadoba and Sanjay Gandhi National Parks are in Maharashtra and Kaziranga is in Assam.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about blood pressure is correct?
options: The normal systolic pressure is about 80 mm of Hg and diastolic pressure is 120 mm of Hg.
The normal systolic pressure is about 72 mm of Hg and diastolic pressure is 35 mm of Hg.
The normal systolic pressure is about 160 mm of Hg and diastolic pressure is 80 mm of Hg.
The normal systolic pressure is about 120 mm of Hg and diastolic pressure is 80 mm of Hg.
questions.explanation: A healthy adult's blood pressure is about 120/80 mm of Hg: 120 systolic, as the heart contracts, and 80 diastolic, as it relaxes.

questions.text: How many recognised essential vitamins are there as on March 2021?
questions.explanation: There are 13 essential vitamins: A, C, D, E, K and the eight B vitamins.

questions.text: For which of the following categories were Paul R Milgrom and Robert B Wilson awarded the Nobel Prize in 2020?
questions.explanation: Paul Milgrom and Robert Wilson won the 2020 prize in Economic Sciences for improvements to auction theory and new auction formats.

questions.text: Which of the following states had the highest per capita income for the year 2019-2020?
questions.explanation: Goa had the highest per capita income (net state domestic product per head) of India's states in 2019-20, with Sikkim second; Gujarat and Kerala were well behind.

questions.text: Which country apart from India was declared a winner at the 2020 Online FIDE Chess Olympiad?
questions.explanation: In the final of the 2020 Online Chess Olympiad two Indian players lost on time after their internet connections dropped; on India's appeal, FIDE declared India and Russia joint winners.

questions.text: Good Governance Day is observed annually on 25 December on the birth anniversary of ______.
questions.explanation: Good Governance Day, observed since 2014, marks the birth anniversary of former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee on 25 December.
IC 1101 is a giant galaxy at the centre of the Abell 2029 galaxy cluster, one of the largest galaxies known.

questions.text: Which of the following was the first High Court established in India?
questions.explanation: The Calcutta High Court, set up in 1862 under the Indian High Courts Act, 1861, is India's oldest; the Bombay and Madras High Courts followed later that year.

questions.text: Who among the following is NOT a part of the committee, which is constructed to provide suggestions to the Prime Minister regarding the appointment of a chief commissioner of Central Information Commission?
options: A Union Cabinet Minister appointed by Prime Minister
Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha
questions.explanation: Under Section 12(3) of the RTI Act the Chief Information Commissioner is appointed on the recommendation of a committee of the Prime Minister (chair), the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister. The Speaker is not on it.

questions.text: Which of the following rivers is a tributary of Krishna River?
questions.explanation: The Tungabhadra is a major tributary of the Krishna. The Bhavani, Hemavati and Amravati (Amaravathi) are tributaries of the Kaveri.

questions.text: To which of the following states does the dance drama ‘Khyal’ belong?
questions.explanation: Khyal is a traditional folk drama of Rajasthan, sung and danced, with regional styles such as the Kuchamani Khyal.

questions.text: In Indian history who were referred to as the 'atavika rajya'?
questions.explanation: The 'atavika rajyas' were the forest kingdoms of central India; Samudragupta's Allahabad Pillar inscription records that he brought their rulers under his control.

questions.text: Which of the following ministries launched the e-Sampada mobile app in December 2020?
options: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare
Ministry of Ayurveda, Yoga & Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha and Homoeopathy
questions.explanation: The Directorate of Estates of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs launched the e-Sampada web portal and mobile app on 25 December 2020, for services such as allotting government housing and booking holiday homes.

questions.text: Which of the following festivals is celebrated for fertility and better fortune in Jharkhand?
questions.explanation: Jawa is celebrated mainly by unmarried tribal girls of Jharkhand around the Karam festival: they tend baskets of germinating seeds and pray for fertility and a prosperous household.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. Today you may not ______ what you hear, but that is the truth and you have to accept it.
questions.explanation: The contrast with 'you have to accept it' calls for 'like': you may not like what you hear, but it is the truth.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The branch of physics concerned with the properties of sound
questions.explanation: Acoustics is the branch of physics that deals with sound; optics deals with light and mechanics with motion and forces.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. His voice was ______ by the sound of the helicopter.
questions.explanation: A sound is 'drowned' (out) when a louder one makes it impossible to hear.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'haughtily'.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. As a result, he had a debt of 500 million US dollars at the time of his death. B. Unfortunately, he began spending lavishly on anything he desired, not what he actually needed. C. Michael Jackson, called the ‘King of Pop Music’, stayed at the top of his career for many years. D. He was respected for his work culture; he would spend long nights at the studio to fix a note correctly in a song.
questions.explanation: C introduces Michael Jackson, D praises his work culture, B turns to his lavish spending and A gives the result, his debt: CDBA.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To have eggs on one’s face
options: To be embarrassed because of one’s action
To apply egg yolk on one’s face for making it look beautiful
To throw eggs on a speaker’s face
To buy eggs and break them
questions.explanation: To have egg on one's face is to be left looking foolish or embarrassed by one's own action.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. Sai Kumari gave Akhila a bouquet of lilies on her birthday.
options: Akhila was given a bouquet of lilies on her birthday by Sai Kumari.
Akhila was gave a bouquet of lilies on her birthday by Sai Kumari.
Akhila is given a bouquet of lilies on her birthday by Sai Kumari.
Akhila gave a bouquet of lilies on her birthday to Sai Kumari.
questions.explanation: The indirect object 'Akhila' becomes the subject, the simple past 'gave' becomes 'was given', and 'by Sai Kumari' is the agent.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. A probe has been ordered / by the incident / that occurred at the celebrations.
questions.explanation: A probe is ordered 'into' an incident: 'A probe has been ordered into the incident'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Disheveled
questions.explanation: 'Disheveled' means untidy in appearance; its opposite is 'ordered', neat. 'Untidy', 'cluttered' and 'unkempt' are close to synonyms.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Despicable
questions.explanation: 'Despicable' means deserving contempt: 'contemptible'. 'Commendable' and 'laudable' are its opposites.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'. India has identified “a nose-based vaccine” against Covid-19 that could be a ‘game-changer’.
questions.explanation: The adjective for the nose is 'nasal': 'a nasal vaccine' is one given through the nose.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A new project or business activity involving some risk
questions.explanation: A venture is a new undertaking, especially in business, that involves risk; an entrepreneur is the person who starts one.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. Lavanya was happy to see that the tree they had planted the previous year “has grow quite taller”.
questions.explanation: The main clause is in the past ('was happy'), so the earlier growth takes the past perfect 'had grown'; 'quite' goes with the positive degree 'tall', not 'taller'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The sports day events / will be conducted / from 3:30 p.m. and 5:30 p.m. / on Saturday.
questions.explanation: A span of time is 'from … to' or 'between … and': 'from 3:30 p.m. to 5:30 p.m.'

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech. The students asked the teacher where they could find the information for their project.
options: The students said to the teacher, “Where can you find the information for our project?”
The students asked the teacher, “Where can we find the information for our project?”
The teacher said to the students, “Where you can find the information for your project.”
The teacher said to the students, “I will tell you where you can find the information for your project.”
questions.explanation: The question goes back into quotation marks as a question: 'they could' becomes 'can we' and 'their' becomes 'our'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Forbid
questions.explanation: To 'forbid' is to refuse to allow: to 'prohibit'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Accustomed
questions.explanation: 'Accustomed' means usual or customary ('his accustomed seat'); its opposite is 'unusual'.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. Humans work because they have to; they play because they want to. B. The most useful definitions are those that clarify the relationship of sports to play, games and contests. C. “Play,” wrote the German theorist Carl Diem, “is purposeless activity, for its own sake, the opposite of work.” D. Sports are part of every culture, past and present, but each culture has its own definition of sports.
questions.explanation: D opens with sports and how each culture defines them, B narrows to the most useful definitions, which relate sports to play, C quotes a definition of play as the opposite of work, and A explains the difference: DBCA.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Thick as thieves
questions.explanation: People who are 'thick as thieves' are very close friends.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Meghalaya, a hilly state of India, is located in the northeastern part of the country. It is (1)______ by the Indian state of Assam in the north and northeast and (2) ______ Bangladesh in the south and southwest. The state capital is (3) ______ hill town of Shillong, located in east-central Meghalaya. Meghalaya is an upland area formed by a (4)______ block of the Deccan plateau. Its summits vary in (5) ______ from 4,000 to 6,000 feet (1,220 to 1,830 metres).

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no.1.
questions.explanation: A state is 'bounded by' the land along its borders: Meghalaya is bounded by Assam in the north and northeast.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Meghalaya, a hilly state of India, is located in the northeastern part of the country. It is (1)______ by the Indian state of Assam in the north and northeast and (2) ______ Bangladesh in the south and southwest. The state capital is (3) ______ hill town of Shillong, located in east-central Meghalaya. Meghalaya is an upland area formed by a (4)______ block of the Deccan plateau. Its summits vary in (5) ______ from 4,000 to 6,000 feet (1,220 to 1,830 metres).

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no.2.
questions.explanation: The sentence goes on with the same verb, 'bounded … by Bangladesh in the south and southwest', so 'by' again.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Meghalaya, a hilly state of India, is located in the northeastern part of the country. It is (1)______ by the Indian state of Assam in the north and northeast and (2) ______ Bangladesh in the south and southwest. The state capital is (3) ______ hill town of Shillong, located in east-central Meghalaya. Meghalaya is an upland area formed by a (4)______ block of the Deccan plateau. Its summits vary in (5) ______ from 4,000 to 6,000 feet (1,220 to 1,830 metres).

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no.3.
questions.explanation: A particular, named town takes the definite article: 'the hill town of Shillong'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Meghalaya, a hilly state of India, is located in the northeastern part of the country. It is (1)______ by the Indian state of Assam in the north and northeast and (2) ______ Bangladesh in the south and southwest. The state capital is (3) ______ hill town of Shillong, located in east-central Meghalaya. Meghalaya is an upland area formed by a (4)______ block of the Deccan plateau. Its summits vary in (5) ______ from 4,000 to 6,000 feet (1,220 to 1,830 metres).

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no.4.
questions.explanation: The Meghalaya plateau is a 'detached' block of the Deccan plateau, cut off from the main plateau.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Meghalaya, a hilly state of India, is located in the northeastern part of the country. It is (1)______ by the Indian state of Assam in the north and northeast and (2) ______ Bangladesh in the south and southwest. The state capital is (3) ______ hill town of Shillong, located in east-central Meghalaya. Meghalaya is an upland area formed by a (4)______ block of the Deccan plateau. Its summits vary in (5) ______ from 4,000 to 6,000 feet (1,220 to 1,830 metres).

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no.5.
questions.explanation: Height above sea level is 'elevation': the summits vary in elevation from 4,000 to 6,000 feet.

questions.text: Ruchi's husband's grandfather is Abhinav, whose grandson's father is Viyan. If Abhinav and his wife have only one son, how is Viyan related to Ruchi's husband?
questions.explanation: Ruchi's husband is Abhinav's grandson, whose father is Viyan; as Abhinav has only one son, Viyan is that son. So Viyan is Ruchi's husband's father.

questions.text: Select the correct option that indicates the arrangement of the given words in the order in which they appear in an English dictionary. 1.Inhaler 2.Inimitable 3.Inhabitant 4.Ingenuous 5.Inheritance
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Ingenuous (4), Inhabitant (3), Inhaler (1), Inheritance (5), Inimitable (2). 'Ing' comes before 'Inh' and 'Ini', and 'Inhab' before 'Inhal' before 'Inher'.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 71, 56, 44, 35, 29, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are −15, −12, −9, −6, shrinking by 3, so the next is −3: 29 − 3 = 26.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. 47 : 58 : 71
questions.explanation: Each number is the one before plus the sum of its digits: 47 + 11 = 58 and 58 + 13 = 71. Likewise 72 + 9 = 81 and 81 + 9 = 90.

questions.text: Four numbers have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the number that is different.
questions.explanation: 463, 137 and 229 are prime numbers; 308 is even (2 × 154), so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Four letter-clusters have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the letter-cluster that is different.
questions.explanation: In each cluster the second letter is 4 after the first and the fourth 6 before the third (wrapping round the alphabet). In GKPJ, KOLF and QUFZ the middle two letters are also opposites (K-P, O-L, U-F, positions adding to 27); in TXBV, X and B are not (24 + 2 = 26).

questions.text: In a certain code language, VICTORY is coded as 29472435 and HASTY is coded as 278119. How will SUBLIME be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: The word is reversed; each consonant becomes the position of its opposite letter (Y → B = 2, R → I = 9) and each vowel its place among the vowels (A 1, E 2, I 3, O 4, U 5): VICTORY → YROTCIV → 2 9 4 7 24 3 5. So SUBLIME → EMILBUS → 2 14 3 15 25 5 8.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some dogs are bulls. All bulls are donkeys. Conclusions: I. All dogs are donkeys. II. Some donkeys are dogs.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
questions.explanation: Some dogs are bulls and all bulls are donkeys, so those dogs are donkeys: some donkeys are dogs (II). Nothing says the other dogs are donkeys, so I does not follow.

questions.text: Select the option in which the words share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of words. Mosquito : Swarm
questions.explanation: A swarm is a group of mosquitoes, as a school is a group of sharks (or fish). A pride is of lions, a sleuth of bears and a murder of crows.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number. 18 : 163 : : 24 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is half the square of the first, plus 1: 18² ÷ 2 + 1 = 162 + 1 = 163. Likewise 24² ÷ 2 + 1 = 288 + 1 = 289.

questions.text: Which two digits and signs need to be interchanged so as to balance the given equation? 65 + 13 − 119 ÷ 32 × 8 = 175
questions.explanation: Swapping 9 and 8 and the signs + and ÷: 65 ÷ 13 − 118 + 32 × 9 = 5 − 118 + 288 = 175.

questions.text: The District Transport Authority has started special bus services for college going students. One bus starts from village P. The number of girls in the bus is one-fourth of the number of boys. In village Q, 20 boys leave the bus at their college stop and ten girls enter the bus. Now the number of boys and girls is equal. How many students enter the bus in the beginning?
questions.explanation: With b boys and b/4 girls: b − 20 = b/4 + 10, so 3b/4 = 30 and b = 40. There were 40 boys and 10 girls: 50 students.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term. OUTSTAY : AOSTTUY :: ROUGHLY : ?
questions.explanation: The letters are put in alphabetical order: OUTSTAY → AOSTTUY. So ROUGHLY → GHLORUY.

questions.text: Four options have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the option that is different.
questions.explanation: Singapore, Indonesia and Sri Lanka are island nations; Bangladesh is not.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. Flock : Sheep :: Crowd : ?
questions.explanation: A flock is a group of sheep, as a crowd is a group of humans.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given letter series will complete the series. k j i _ k _ _ i k j i _ k _ _ i
options: j k j k j k
i j i i j i
k i j k i j
i k j i k j
questions.explanation: With i, j, i, i, j, i in the blanks the block 'kjii' repeats: kjii kjii kjii kjii.

questions.text: In a certain code language, EXTREME is written as VCGIVNV. How will INITIAL be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite in the alphabet (A ↔ Z, B ↔ Y …): E → V, X → C, T → G, R → I, M → N. So INITIAL → RMRGRZO.

questions.text: Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it. 13 50 8; 12 39 5; 15 51 ?
questions.explanation: In each row the middle number is twice the first plus three times the third: 2 × 13 + 3 × 8 = 50 and 2 × 12 + 3 × 5 = 39. So 2 × 15 + 3 × ? = 51 and ? = 7.

questions.text: Who among the following was the first Indian Governor of the Reserve Bank of India?
questions.explanation: C. D. Deshmukh, appointed in 1943, was the first Indian Governor of the Reserve Bank of India.

questions.text: Which of the following hormone is secreted by brain that helps to regulate sleep-wake cycles?
questions.explanation: Melatonin, secreted by the pineal gland in the brain, regulates the sleep-wake cycle.

questions.text: Which of the following is one of the file formats used for web graphics?
questions.explanation: GIF (Graphics Interchange Format) is an image format widely used for web graphics; .exe is a program, .txt plain text and .docx a Word document.

questions.text: In which of the following years did the Prime Minister of India, Narendra Modi, launch Atal Pension Yojana?
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched the Atal Pension Yojana in Kolkata on 9 May 2015.

questions.text: Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize is associated with which of the following disciplines?
questions.explanation: The Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize, given by the CSIR, is one of India's leading awards for science and technology.

questions.text: In which year did the Central Government of India appoint the States Reorganisation Commission?
questions.explanation: The States Reorganisation Commission, under Fazl Ali, was appointed in December 1953; its report led to the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.

questions.text: In which of the following North Eastern states is the first ever specialised ‘Ginger’ Processing Plant being revived in December 2020?
questions.explanation: The North East's first specialised ginger processing plant, at Byrnihat in Meghalaya's Ri Bhoi district, idle for about 16 years, was being revived through NERAMAC in December 2020.

questions.text: Dandeli Wildlife Sanctuary is located in which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Dandeli Wildlife Sanctuary is in Uttara Kannada district, Karnataka.

questions.text: In which of the following districts was Telangana’s first rescue and rehabilitation centre for monkeys, launched in December 2020?
questions.explanation: Telangana's first monkey rescue and rehabilitation centre was opened at Chincholi in Nirmal district in December 2020.

questions.text: Which of the following is a salt-water lake?
questions.explanation: Pangong Tso in Ladakh is a saline (brackish) lake; Kolleru, Nainital and Loktak are freshwater lakes.

questions.text: FIFA World Cup 2022 venue, Ahmad Bin Ali Stadium, which was built by Indian construction giant Larsen & Turbo is located in which of the following countries?
questions.explanation: The Ahmad Bin Ali Stadium, a 2022 FIFA World Cup venue built by Larsen & Toubro, is at Al Rayyan in Qatar.

questions.text: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: An electric field has both magnitude and direction, so it is a vector. Charge, flux and current are scalars (current has a direction but does not add as a vector).

questions.text: According to the Constitution of India a Judge of the Supreme Court cannot be removed from office except by an order of the ______.
questions.explanation: Under Article 124(4) a Judge of the Supreme Court can be removed only by an order of the President, after each House of Parliament passes an address by a special majority.

questions.text: Who among the following persons was awarded the Padma Shri for social work in 2019?
