questions.explanation: Devarapalli Prakash Rao, a Cuttack tea seller who runs a school for slum children, received the Padma Shri for social work in 2019. The other three were honoured that year for literature and education, medicine and art.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who was appointed as the first Surveyor General of India in 1815?
questions.explanation: Colin Mackenzie was appointed the first Surveyor General of India in 1815.

questions.text: Kisan Fasal Rahat Yojana, which will replace (PMFBY) Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna, has been launched by which of the following states government in December 2020?
questions.explanation: In December 2020 Jharkhand announced its own crop relief scheme, which compensates farmers for crop loss without any premium, in place of the PMFBY.

questions.text: Who among the following persons was elected, unopposed, as the President of Hockey India in November 2020?
questions.explanation: Gyanendro Ningombam of Manipur was elected unopposed as President of Hockey India in November 2020, the first from the North East to hold the post.

questions.text: Where is Mount Diavolo, an important mountain peak in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, located?
questions.explanation: Mount Diavolo is in Middle Andaman; Saddle Peak, the islands' highest point, is in North Andaman.

questions.text: Raja Parba is a unique festival celebrating the onset of monsoon and the earth’s womanhood. It is celebrated in which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Raja Parba, a three-day festival in mid-June, is celebrated in Odisha.

questions.text: Ustad Iqbal Ahmed Khan, a recipient of the Sangeet Natak Academy Award, belongs to the ______ Gharana.
questions.explanation: The vocalist Ustad Iqbal Ahmed Khan was the khalifa (head) of the Dilli (Delhi) gharana.

questions.text: Which country ranked first in the ‘Human Development Report 2020’ released by the United Nations Development Programme?
questions.explanation: Norway topped the Human Development Index in UNDP's Human Development Report 2020; India was 131st.

questions.text: ______ is an advanced discipline that teaches students how to analyse and find patterns in large amounts of data.
questions.explanation: Data science combines statistics and computing to find patterns and insights in large amounts of data.

questions.text: Who among the following sportsmen is the brand ambassador of SBOTOP, which is a global online betting platform?
questions.explanation: The West Indian all-rounder Dwayne Bravo was announced as SBOTOP's brand ambassador in August 2020.

questions.text: Which of the following parts of the body/glands maintains the body temperature?
questions.explanation: The hypothalamus acts as the body's thermostat, keeping body temperature steady; it also governs hunger and thirst.

questions.text: ______’s foster mother Mahapajapati Gotami was the first woman to be ordained as a bhikkhuni.
questions.explanation: Mahapajapati Gotami, the Buddha's aunt and foster mother, was the first woman ordained as a Buddhist nun (bhikkhuni).

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. What are the “options available of me” for a change of career?
questions.explanation: Something is available 'to' someone: 'What are the options available to me for a change of career?'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Instrument that measures the altitude of the land surface
questions.explanation: An altimeter measures altitude; a barometer measures air pressure, a thermometer temperature and a chronometer time.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. “If the box breaking” the glass bottle will be shattered.
questions.explanation: A first conditional takes the present simple in the 'if' clause and 'will' in the main clause: 'If the box breaks, the glass bottle will be shattered.'

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. Due to this tilt as the Earth wobbles around the Sun, different points of the Earth receive more or less sunlight. B. Furthermore, we also wouldn’t have solstices or equinoxes. C. We know that seasons are caused by the Earth having a slight tilt on its axis. D. If the Sun just shone directly on the Equator all year long, we would be left without seasons.
questions.explanation: C says the seasons come from the Earth's tilt, A explains the effect of that tilt, D imagines the Sun shining on the Equator all year, and B adds a further consequence: CADB.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Naïve
questions.explanation: 'Naïve' means lacking experience or judgement; its opposite is 'sophisticated'. 'Simple', 'immature' and 'unsuspicious' are close to synonyms.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. The energy required / for perform various functions of the body / is obtained from food.
options: for perform various functions of the body
questions.explanation: After the preposition 'for' the verb takes the -ing form: 'for performing various functions of the body' (or 'to perform').

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'attractive'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. A micromanager frequently demands reports and updates leaving little room for subordinates to take ______ on their own.
questions.explanation: Subordinates 'take decisions' on their own; 'verdicts' and 'decrees' are pronounced by courts and rulers.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. Games involved gladiators fighting wild animals or each other. B. Inside, tiered seating encircled the arena, where animals were caged and stage sets prepared. C. Inaugurated in AD 80, the 50,000-seat Colosseum is also known as the Flavian Amphitheatre. D. Rome’s great gladiatorial arena is the most monumental of the city's ancient sights.
questions.explanation: D introduces Rome's great gladiatorial arena, C names and dates it, B describes its inside and A the games held there: DCBA.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Compel
questions.explanation: To 'compel' is to force someone to do something; its opposite is 'dissuade', to persuade someone not to. 'Induce', 'influence' and 'persuade' are close in meaning to 'compel'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. The first van was sent as a ______ to mislead the thugs.
questions.explanation: A 'decoy' is something used to mislead or lure: the first van was sent out to draw the thugs away.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Salient
questions.explanation: 'Salient' means most noticeable or important: 'noticeable'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Apathetic
questions.explanation: 'Apathetic' means showing no interest or concern: 'indifferent'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Butter fingers
questions.explanation: 'Butter fingers' describes a clumsy person who keeps dropping things.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. The monkeys swinged / on the branches and / jumped over the compound wall.
questions.explanation: The past tense of 'swing' is 'swung': 'The monkeys swung on the branches'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech. Neil Armstrong said, “It’s a small step for man but a giant leap for mankind.”
options: Neil Armstrong said that a small step for man can be giant leap for mankind.
Neil Armstrong had said that a small step for man is a giant leap for mankind.
Neil Armstrong said that it was a small step for man but a giant leap for mankind.
Neil Armstrong says that was a small step for man but a giant leap for mankind.
questions.explanation: The reporting verb 'said' is in the past, so 'it is' becomes 'it was', introduced by 'that'; the rest of the statement is unchanged.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. Have you submitted the papers at the post office?
options: Have the papers been submit by you at the post office?
Had the papers submitted by you to the post office?
Has the papers been submitted by you at the post office?
Have the papers been submitted by you at the post office?
questions.explanation: The present perfect question becomes 'Have the papers been submitted by you': 'have' agrees with the plural 'papers' and is followed by 'been' and the past participle.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A place or scene of activity, debate, or conflict
questions.explanation: An arena is a place or scene of activity, debate or conflict.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Large-hearted
questions.explanation: A large-hearted person is kind and generous.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In the generation of hydroelectric power, water is collected or (1) ______ at a higher elevation and led downward (2) ______ large pipes to a lower elevation; the difference in elevations is (3) ______ as the head. At the end of its passage down the pipes, the falling water (4) ______ turbines to rotate. The turbines in turn drive generators, (5) ______ convert the turbines’ mechanical energy into electricity.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no.1.
questions.explanation: Water is collected or 'stored' at a height; 'hoarded' and 'amassed' are used of goods or wealth gathered up.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In the generation of hydroelectric power, water is collected or (1) ______ at a higher elevation and led downward (2) ______ large pipes to a lower elevation; the difference in elevations is (3) ______ as the head. At the end of its passage down the pipes, the falling water (4) ______ turbines to rotate. The turbines in turn drive generators, (5) ______ convert the turbines’ mechanical energy into electricity.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no.2.
questions.explanation: The water is led downward 'through' large pipes.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In the generation of hydroelectric power, water is collected or (1) ______ at a higher elevation and led downward (2) ______ large pipes to a lower elevation; the difference in elevations is (3) ______ as the head. At the end of its passage down the pipes, the falling water (4) ______ turbines to rotate. The turbines in turn drive generators, (5) ______ convert the turbines’ mechanical energy into electricity.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no.3.
questions.explanation: The difference in elevations 'is known as' the head: the passive needs the past participle 'known'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In the generation of hydroelectric power, water is collected or (1) ______ at a higher elevation and led downward (2) ______ large pipes to a lower elevation; the difference in elevations is (3) ______ as the head. At the end of its passage down the pipes, the falling water (4) ______ turbines to rotate. The turbines in turn drive generators, (5) ______ convert the turbines’ mechanical energy into electricity.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no.4.
questions.explanation: The pattern 'cause something to do' fits: the falling water 'causes' the turbines to rotate.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In the generation of hydroelectric power, water is collected or (1) ______ at a higher elevation and led downward (2) ______ large pipes to a lower elevation; the difference in elevations is (3) ______ as the head. At the end of its passage down the pipes, the falling water (4) ______ turbines to rotate. The turbines in turn drive generators, (5) ______ convert the turbines’ mechanical energy into electricity.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no.5.
questions.explanation: 'Which' refers back to the generators, which are things; 'who' is for people and 'whose' shows possession.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term. QUORATE : AEOQRTU :: SANDBOX : ?
questions.explanation: The letters are rearranged in alphabetical order: QUORATE → AEOQRTU. SANDBOX in alphabetical order is ABDNOSX.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of numbers. 12 : 20
questions.explanation: 12 = 3 × 4 and 20 = 4 × 5: products of consecutive numbers, the second pair starting where the first ends. Likewise 30 = 5 × 6 and 42 = 6 × 7.

questions.text: Select the correct option that indicates the arrangement of the given words in the order in which they appear in an English dictionary. 1. Expanse 2. Expansive 3. Expandable 4. Expansion 5. Expanded
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Expandable (3), Expanded (5), Expanse (1), Expansion (4), Expansive (2). 'Expanda' comes before 'Expande', 'Expanse' before 'Expansi', and 'Expansio' before 'Expansiv'.

questions.text: Tushar is the only son of Jitendra, and Kirti is the daughter of Jitendra's father's brother. Suhani is the sister of Tushar. How is Suhani related to Kirti?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives niece. Suhani, Tushar's sister, is Jitendra's daughter, and Kirti, the daughter of Jitendra's father's brother, is Jitendra's cousin. So Suhani is the daughter of Kirti's cousin, a generation below Kirti, and the key follows the common usage that calls a cousin's daughter a niece (strictly, she is Kirti's first cousin once removed).

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (72, 56, 42)

Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some ducks are hens. Some hens are chickens. Conclusions: I. Some ducks are chickens. II. Some hens are ducks.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: 'Some ducks are hens' can be turned round: some hens are ducks (II). The hens that are chickens need not be the ones that are ducks, so I does not follow.

questions.text: Select the option in which the words share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of words. Virus : Ebola
questions.explanation: Ebola is a disease caused by a virus; plague is a disease caused by a bacterium (Yersinia pestis).

questions.text: A notebook costs ₹12 each. A pen costs ₹9 each. Tina spends ₹123 on a total of 11 pieces of these articles. How many notebooks did she purchase?
questions.explanation: If she bought n notebooks, 12n + 9(11 − n) = 123, so 3n + 99 = 123 and n = 8.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ENVELOPE is written as IQZHPRTH. How will INTIMATE be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +4 and +3 in turn: E → I, N → Q, V → Z, E → H and so on. INTIMATE: I → M, N → Q, T → X, I → L, M → Q, A → D, T → X, E → H: MQXLQDXH.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. 221 : 348 : 517
Which two digits and signs need to be interchanged so as to balance the given equation? 97 ÷ 24 − 16 × 5 + 37 = 53
questions.explanation: Interchanging 7 and 6, and + and −: 96 ÷ 24 + 17 × 5 − 36 = 4 + 85 − 36 = 53.

questions.text: Four letter-clusters have been given in the options, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the letter-cluster that is different.
questions.explanation: EHLQ, ILPU and ORVA move +3, +4, +5 (V + 5 wraps round to A). KOSW moves +4, +4, +4, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Four numbers have been given in the options, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the number that is different.
Four words have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the word that is different.
questions.explanation: Entomology (insects), mycology (fungi) and genomics (genomes) study living things; geology studies the Earth's rocks and structure.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 12, 22, 40, 74, 140, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is twice the one before minus an even number rising by 2: 12 × 2 − 2 = 22, 22 × 2 − 4 = 40, 40 × 2 − 6 = 74, 74 × 2 − 8 = 140, and 140 × 2 − 10 = 270.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. Hindi : Devanagari :: English : ?
questions.explanation: Hindi is written in the Devanagari script, and English in the Latin (Roman) script.

questions.text: In a certain code language, BOOTLACE is coded as 49960372 and CAPELIN is coded as 7382015. How will TAPIOCA be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter has its own digit: BOOTLACE gives T = 6, A = 3, O = 9 and C = 7, and CAPELIN gives P = 8 and I = 1. So TAPIOCA is 6381973.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series. O _ E _ O Z _ T _ Z _ T
questions.explanation: With Z, T, E, O, E in the blanks the block OZET repeats: OZET OZET OZET.

questions.text: Who among the following politicians was the Home Minister of India in Rajiv Gandhi's cabinet from 1986 to 1989?
questions.explanation: Buta Singh was Union Home Minister from 1986 to 1989, in Rajiv Gandhi's government.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which maharaja of Manipur signed the Instrument of Accession with the Government of India?
questions.explanation: Maharaja Bodhchandra Singh signed Manipur's Instrument of Accession in 1947, and the agreement merging the state into India in 1949.

questions.text: The world's only floating national park, Keibul Lamjao National Park, is located in ______.
questions.explanation: Keibul Lamjao National Park floats on the phumdis, mats of floating vegetation, of Loktak Lake in Manipur.

questions.text: Which of the following is a Kharif crop in North India and a Rabi crop in South India?
questions.explanation: NCERT notes that sesamum (til) is a kharif crop in the north and a rabi crop in south India. Wheat and barley are rabi crops, and finger millet (ragi) is mainly a kharif crop.

questions.text: Which of the following is a single user operating system?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives MS-DOS, the textbook single-user system: it has no user accounts or logins and serves one person at a time. Windows NT and Linux are multi-user systems, and Windows 7, built on Windows NT, keeps separate accounts and lets several users stay signed in at once, though some textbooks class desktop Windows as single-user.

questions.text: In January 2021, the Defence Research Development Organisation (DRDO) developed India's first indigenous machine pistol called ‘Asmi’ in collaboration with ______.
questions.explanation: Asmi, India's first indigenous 9 mm machine pistol, was developed by DRDO's Armament Research and Development Establishment, Pune, with the Infantry School, Mhow.

questions.text: How many terabytes make one petabyte?
questions.explanation: In binary units 1 petabyte = 1,024 terabytes, just as 1 terabyte = 1,024 gigabytes.

questions.text: Public Sector Banks account for about ______ of market share in Indian banking as per the Economic Survey 2019-20.
questions.explanation: The Economic Survey 2019-20 put the public sector banks' share of the Indian banking market at about 70%.

questions.text: Who among the following did the Sports Authority of India appoint as the middle-and-long distance coach of the Indian athletics team in January 2021?
questions.explanation: In January 2021 the Belarusian Nikolai Snesarev was appointed again as middle- and long-distance coach of the Indian athletics team, a post he had left in 2019.

questions.text: The inertia of an object is measured by its ______.
questions.explanation: Inertia, an object's resistance to a change in its state of rest or motion, depends on its mass: the greater the mass, the greater the inertia.

questions.text: Which of the following beaches was NOT awarded the international ‘Blue Flag’ certification by Foundation of Environment Education, Denmark as of October 2020?
questions.explanation: In October 2020 eight Indian beaches received the Blue Flag, among them Kappad (Kerala), Ghoghla (Diu) and Rushikonda (Andhra Pradesh); Talasari in Odisha was not one of them.

questions.text: Which web portal and mobile application did the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, Government of India, launch in December 2020?
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs launched the e-Sampada portal and app on 25 December 2020, Good Governance Day, for the allotment of government accommodation and other estate services.

questions.text: Who among the following was a World War II veteran, also associated with cricket?
questions.explanation: Alan Burgess, a first-class cricketer for Canterbury in New Zealand, served in the Second World War in Egypt and Italy; he died in January 2021, aged 100.

questions.text: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India deals with the organisation of agriculture and animal husbandry?
questions.explanation: Article 48, a Directive Principle, asks the State to organise agriculture and animal husbandry on modern and scientific lines.

questions.text: The Sufi shrine Charar-e-Sharief (or Sharif) is located near ______ city.
questions.explanation: Charar-e-Sharief, the shrine of the Sufi saint Sheikh Noor-ud-din Noorani (Nund Rishi), is in Budgam district, south-west of Srinagar.

questions.text: Which of the following watershed development projects is sponsored by the Central Government aims at enabling the rural population to conserve water?
questions.explanation: NCERT describes Haryali as a watershed development project sponsored by the Central Government to enable the rural population to conserve water for drinking, irrigation, fisheries and afforestation. Neeru-Meeru (Andhra Pradesh) and Arvary Pani Sansad (Alwar, Rajasthan) are state and local efforts.

questions.text: Which was the first empire in ancient India to use elephants in its war on a large scale?
questions.explanation: Magadha, with the forests of eastern India to supply them, was the first kingdom to use elephants on a large scale in its wars.

questions.text: ‘Purusha Sukta’ is a hymn from which Veda?
questions.explanation: The Purusha Sukta is hymn 90 of the tenth book (mandala) of the Rigveda.

questions.text: Which of the following was the country in focus at the 51st International Film Festival of India held in Goa in January 2021?
questions.explanation: Bangladesh was the Country in Focus at the 51st IFFI, held in Goa from 16 to 24 January 2021.

questions.text: Who discovered blood circulation?
questions.explanation: William Harvey described the circulation of the blood, pumped round the body by the heart, in 1628.

questions.text: Which of the following diseases is caused by Leishmania, a protozoan organism?
questions.explanation: Kala-azar (visceral leishmaniasis) is caused by Leishmania and spread by sandflies. Sleeping sickness is caused by Trypanosoma and malaria by Plasmodium.

questions.text: Which of the following is a main species of moist deciduous forests?
questions.explanation: NCERT lists sandalwood among the main species of tropical moist deciduous forests, with teak, sal and shisham. Amaltas and neem belong to the drier deciduous forests and khejri to the thorn forests.

questions.text: A Shadava Raga has only ______ notes in its scale.
questions.explanation: A shadava raga uses six notes; an audava raga uses five and a sampurna raga all seven.

questions.text: As per Union Budget 2021, 9% of the government revenue will be spent on ______.
questions.explanation: In the Budget 2021-22 statement of where the rupee goes, centrally sponsored schemes take 9 paise of every rupee; interest payments take 20 paise, defence 8 paise and pensions 5 paise.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'temporary'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiomatic expression given. To poke one’s nose into
options: To clean one’s nose with a twig
To bury oneself in another matter
To insert something in another’s nose
To take interest in others’ affairs
questions.explanation: To 'poke one's nose into' something is to meddle in matters that are not one's concern: to take an interest in others' affairs.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. Large glasses magnified his eyes “so that to gave” him the appearance of a wise owl.
questions.explanation: Purpose is expressed by 'so as to' with the base form of the verb: 'so as to give him the appearance of a wise owl'.

questions.text: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. Despite of being a close friend he did not help me in any way.
questions.explanation: 'Despite' takes no 'of': 'Despite being a close friend' (or 'In spite of being').

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Restrictive
questions.explanation: 'Restrictive' means limiting freedom; its opposite is 'liberal', allowing freedom. 'Closed' is nearer a synonym.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Relating to soldiers or war
questions.explanation: 'Martial' means relating to soldiers or war, as in 'martial law'; 'marital' means relating to marriage.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. NEGLECT
questions.explanation: To 'neglect' is to fail to look after something; its opposite is to 'care' for it. 'Fail' and 'omit' are close to synonyms.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active or passive voice. Wi-Fi hotspots will be installed by the government in remote areas by 2022.
options: Wi-Fi hotspots will install in remote areas by 2022 by the government.
Remote areas will install Wi-Fi hotspots by the government by 2022.
The government will install remote areas and hotspots by 2022.
The government will install Wi-Fi hotspots in remote areas by 2022.
questions.explanation: The future passive 'will be installed by the government' becomes the active 'The government will install', with 'Wi-Fi hotspots' as its object.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The police arrested / two young men, but / neither of them were / responsible for the robbery.
questions.explanation: 'Neither of them' is singular and takes a singular verb: 'neither of them was responsible'.

questions.text: Fill in the blank with most appropriate word. The old building was ______ by the authorities.
questions.explanation: To 'pull down' a building is to demolish it; to 'pull through' is to recover, to 'pull up' is to stop and to 'pull off' is to succeed in something difficult.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Herald
questions.explanation: To 'herald' something is to announce or signal its coming.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'. I want to buy this book. Please give me “any money”.
questions.explanation: Requests and offers take 'some'; 'any' belongs in questions and negatives: 'Please give me some money.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given words. one who pretends to be what he is not
questions.explanation: A hypocrite pretends to be what he is not, above all to have virtues he lacks.

questions.text: Select the misspelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'treacherous'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. Despite their ______, impersonal rules that apply to all are essential in large systems.
questions.explanation: 'Despite' signals a contrast: the rules are essential in spite of their 'limitations'. 'Support', 'advantages' and 'benefits' would not contrast with 'essential'.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. The watchman said, “I did not see anyone last night.”
options: The watchman said that he had not seen anyone the previous night.
The watchman said that he did not see anyone last night.
The watchman said that he did not saw anyone the previous night.
The watchman said that I had not seen anyone last night.
questions.explanation: After 'said', the simple past 'did not see' becomes the past perfect 'had not seen', 'I' becomes 'he' and 'last night' becomes 'the previous night'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. The friends quarrelled some time ago but now they are trying “to make up” with each other.
questions.explanation: To 'make up' with someone is to end a quarrel and become friends again.

questions.text: Given below are four sentences in jumbled order. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. The other was a ruffled, glum-faced man, heavily built and roughly dressed. B. One man had a handsome presence with a bold and frank look. C. But the most striking thing was that they were handcuffed together. D. The two men who boarded the train from Denver were an odd pair.
questions.explanation: D introduces the odd pair, B describes one man and A 'the other', and C ends with the most striking thing, the handcuffs: DBAC.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. Earlier, they had to look through hundreds of mugshots in large books and they could make a positive identification only in 5% of the cases. B. This saves a lot of time and effort and also leads to more positive identifications. C. Now computers make this easier for witnesses by projecting only pictures that match the descriptions closely. D. After a crime, witnesses often give the police a description and thus help to identify the criminal.
questions.explanation: D says witnesses describe the criminal, A says how identification worked earlier, C how computers help now and B what this saves: DACB.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. ADEPT
questions.explanation: 'Adept' means very skilled; 'clumsy' is its opposite.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. We must understand that people can process very little information presented orally. So, it is (1) ______, particularly for a teacher, to realise that the students have sometimes listened to three or four teachers (2) ______ you. So, the teacher must have props like notes, handouts and slides that will make the learning material (3) ______ alive for the students and stay that way with them. A visual aid, a little movement or colour will get the students’ attention. Another important thing to (4) ______ is that long, complicated sentences spoken fast are simply too difficult for students to understand. It is, therefore, (5) ______ to use short sentences that make sense to them instantly.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: It is 'important', particularly for a teacher, to realise this; 'unnecessary' and 'immaterial' say the opposite.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. We must understand that people can process very little information presented orally. So, it is (1) ______, particularly for a teacher, to realise that the students have sometimes listened to three or four teachers (2) ______ you. So, the teacher must have props like notes, handouts and slides that will make the learning material (3) ______ alive for the students and stay that way with them. Another important thing to (4) ______ is that long, complicated sentences spoken fast are simply too difficult for students to understand. It is, therefore, (5) ______ to use short sentences that make sense to them instantly.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The students have already listened to three or four teachers 'before' you.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. We must understand that people can process very little information presented orally. So, it is (1) ______, particularly for a teacher, to realise that the students have sometimes listened to three or four teachers (2) ______ you. It is, therefore, (5) ______ to use short sentences that make sense to them instantly.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Notes, handouts and slides make the material 'come alive': become vivid for the students.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. We must understand that people can process very little information presented orally. So, it is (1) ______, particularly for a teacher, to realise that the students have sometimes listened to three or four teachers (2) ______ you. Another important thing to (4) ______ is that long, complicated sentences spoken fast are simply too difficult for students to understand. It is, therefore, (5) ______ to use short sentences that make sense to them instantly.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'Another important thing to realise' echoes 'to realise' earlier in the passage: something the teacher must understand.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. We must understand that people can process very little information presented orally. So, it is (1) ______, particularly for a teacher, to realise that the students have sometimes listened to three or four teachers (2) ______ you. It is, therefore, (5) ______ to use short sentences that make sense to them instantly.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: The passage is giving advice, so short sentences are 'advisable'; 'mandatory' and 'compulsory' are too strong.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some drivers are artists. All fathers are artists. No father is a doctor. Conclusions: I. No doctor is an artist. II. No driver is a doctor. III. Some artists are fathers.
options: Both conclusions I and III follow
Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: All fathers are artists, so some artists are fathers (III). I and II need not follow: no father is a doctor, but artists who are not fathers, and drivers, may be doctors.

questions.text: In a code language, if LOCK is written as 1212311 and KEY is written as 112225, then how will DEAR be written in the same language?
questions.explanation: Consonants are written as their place in the alphabet and vowels as their place counted from Z: LOCK → 12, 12, 3, 11 and KEY → 11, 22, 25. So DEAR → 4, 22, 26, 18: 4222618.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 52, ?, 113, 162, 226, 307
Three of the following four letter-cluster pairs are alike in a certain way and one is different. Select the odd one.
questions.explanation: In TAP : VDT, DRY : FUC and RAT : TDX the letters move +2, +3, +4 (Y wraps round to C). In FRY : HTB they move +2, +2, +3, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. Kick : Football : : Backstroke : ?
questions.explanation: A kick is a move in football, as the backstroke is a stroke in swimming.

questions.text: In a group of 72 workers, each worker participates in one or more of three activities, i.e. Quiz, Mono-acting and Mimicry. 11 workers participate in Quiz only, 15 participate in Mono-acting only and 14 participate in Mimicry only. If 5 workers participate in all three activities, then how many workers participate in any two activities?
questions.explanation: Those in exactly two activities = 72 − (11 + 15 + 14) − 5 = 72 − 40 − 5 = 27.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (21, 13, 17)
questions.explanation: The third number is the average of the first two: (21 + 13) ÷ 2 = 17. Likewise (32 + 46) ÷ 2 = 39.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers in the set share the same relationship as the numbers in the given set. (25, 19, 36)
questions.explanation: The third number is the square of the difference of the first two: (25 − 19)² = 36. Likewise (22 − 17)² = 25.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'MODERATE' is written as 'OQEFTBVF' and 'LIFE' is written as 'NJGF'. How will 'CLEAR' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves forward by the number of digits in its place in the alphabet: A to I (1 to 9) move 1 place and J to Z (10 to 26) move 2, which fits every letter of MODERATE → OQEFTBVF and LIFE → NJGF. So C → D, L → N, E → F, A → B and R → T: DNFBT.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term. TANGLE : XERKPI : : FIGHTS : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 4 places forward: TANGLE → XERKPI. So FIGHTS → JMKLXW.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series. H _ Z _ H O Z C H O _ D _ O _ E H _ Z F
options: O B Z H Z O
O C Z H Z H
O B H O Z O
H B Z H H O
questions.explanation: With O, B, Z, H, Z, O in the blanks the series reads HOZB HOZC HOZD HOZE HOZF: HOZ followed by B, C, D, E and F.

questions.text: Select the word-pair in which the two words are related in the same way as are the two words in the following word-pair. Courage : Bravery
questions.explanation: Courage and bravery mean the same, as do systematic and orderly. The words in the other pairs are not synonyms.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fourth number in the same way as the first number is related to the second number and the fifth number is related to the sixth number. 11 : 242 : : ? : 162 : : 14 : 392
questions.explanation: The second number is twice the square of the first: 2 × 11² = 242 and 2 × 14² = 392. Likewise 2 × 9² = 162.

questions.text: Four words have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the word that is different.
questions.explanation: A gastroenterologist, an ophthalmologist and a cardiologist each treat an organ of the body (the digestive tract, the eye and the heart); a psychiatrist treats disorders of the mind.

questions.text: A family consists of six members. Surendar is the son of Revant. Pranavi is the wife of Revant. Yugal is the brother of Revant. Kundana is the daughter of Pranavi. Janardan is the brother of Pranavi. How many children does Pranavi have?
questions.explanation: All six members are named: Revant, his wife Pranavi, their son Surendar and daughter Kundana, Revant's brother Yugal and Pranavi's brother Janardan. With no one else in the family, Pranavi has two children.

questions.text: Four number-pairs have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the one that is different.
questions.explanation: Each pair is n : n³ + 5: 9³ + 5 = 734, 7³ + 5 = 348 and 5³ + 5 = 130. But 8³ + 5 = 517, not 516.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in an English dictionary. 1. Primary 2. Pristine 3. Predator 4. Precaution 5. Preserve
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Precaution (4), Predator (3), Preserve (5), Primary (1), Pristine (2). 'Prec' comes before 'Pred' and 'Pres', and 'Prim' before 'Pris'.

questions.text: How many Olympic Medals did India win in the sport of wrestling, as of January 2021?
questions.explanation: India's five Olympic wrestling medals by then were K. D. Jadhav's bronze (1952), Sushil Kumar's bronze (2008) and silver (2012), Yogeshwar Dutt's bronze (2012) and Sakshi Malik's bronze (2016).

questions.text: Which of the following is the world's third-highest mountain that connects the borders of India and Nepal?
questions.explanation: Kanchenjunga, the world's third-highest mountain, stands on the border between Sikkim and Nepal. K2, the second-highest, and Broad Peak are in the Karakoram, and Nanga Parbat is at the western end of the Himalayas.

questions.text: In which state was the foundation stone for a water supply project laid down by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in July 2020?
questions.explanation: On 23 July 2020 the Prime Minister laid the foundation stone of the Manipur Water Supply Project by video conference; it is to bring tap water to Greater Imphal, 25 towns and about 1,700 villages.

questions.text: What is the minimum age to be an eligible voter for Lok Sabha elections?
questions.explanation: Under Article 326 every citizen aged 18 or more may vote in Lok Sabha elections; the 61st Amendment (1988) lowered the voting age from 21.

questions.text: Which type of storage device is a hard disk?
questions.explanation: A hard disk is secondary storage: it keeps data when the power is off and is not accessed directly by the CPU, unlike primary memory (RAM).

questions.text: What is the use of the functional key F7 in Microsoft Word 2010?
options: It is used to open the Help window.
It is used to run spell check and grammar check.
It is used for renaming files and folders.
It is used as a search key.
questions.explanation: In Microsoft Word, F7 runs the spelling and grammar check; F1 opens Help.

questions.text: The cause of Siderosis is excessive deposition of ______ in the body tissue.
questions.explanation: Siderosis is the deposit of excess iron in body tissue, for example in the lungs of those who breathe in iron dust.

questions.text: How many storeys does Qutab Minar have in Delhi?
questions.explanation: The Qutab Minar has five storeys, each marked by a projecting balcony.

questions.text: Who among the following was conferred with the ‘Best Actor’ award at the Dadasaheb Phalke International Film Festival in February 2020?
questions.explanation: Hrithik Roshan was named Best Actor at the festival in February 2020 for 'Super 30'.

questions.text: By which amendment of the Constitution of India were the terms ‘socialist’ and ‘secular’ added in the preamble?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment (1976) added 'socialist', 'secular' and 'integrity' to the Preamble.

questions.text: Who won the 10 m air rifle event at the fifth edition of the International Online Shooting Championship in October 2020?
questions.explanation: Visnu Shivaraj Pandian, then 16, won the 10 m air rifle at the fifth International Online Shooting Championship in October 2020.

questions.text: Lohit river is a tributary of:
questions.explanation: The Lohit, which flows through Arunachal Pradesh into Assam, is a tributary of the Brahmaputra.

questions.text: Who among the following is the first Indian to be awarded with UN Military Gender Advocate Award in May 2020?
questions.explanation: Major Suman Gawani, who served with the UN Mission in South Sudan, received the UN Military Gender Advocate of the Year Award on 29 May 2020, the first Indian peacekeeper to win it.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about bromine is correct?
options: It is a gas at room temperature.
It is a solid at room temperature.
It is a liquid at room temperature.
questions.explanation: Bromine is a non-metal and the only one that is liquid at room temperature.

questions.text: In September 2020, who was appointed as the Chairman of National School of Drama?
questions.explanation: The actor Paresh Rawal was appointed Chairman of the National School of Drama on 10 September 2020, for four years.

questions.text: In the central budget 2020-21 the eligibility limit for NBFCs for debt recovery under the SARFAESI Act was proposed to be reduced to an asset size of:
questions.explanation: The Budget proposed cutting the limit from an asset size of ₹500 crore to ₹100 crore (and the loan size from ₹1 crore to ₹50 lakh).

questions.text: With which of the following sports is Murugappa Gold Cup associated?
questions.explanation: The Murugappa Gold Cup is an all-India hockey tournament held in Chennai.

questions.text: In which of the following states is Sambhar Salt Lake situated?
questions.explanation: Sambhar, India's largest inland salt lake, is in Rajasthan, near Jaipur.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: In 1774, the Asiatic Society was founded by Sir Williams Jones.
In 1775, the Siraj ud-Daulah was defeated in the Battle of Plassey.
In 1776, the first railway service began from Bombay to Thane.
In 1793, the Cornwallis code was enacted.
questions.explanation: The Cornwallis Code was enacted in 1793. The Asiatic Society was founded in 1784, the Battle of Plassey was fought in 1757 and the first train ran from Bombay to Thane in 1853.

questions.text: Where is Kandariya Mahadev Temple situated?
questions.explanation: The Kandariya Mahadev Temple, the largest of the Khajuraho group, is at Khajuraho in Madhya Pradesh.

questions.text: Which of the following Indian cities hosted the International Summit on Women in STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics) in January 2020?
questions.explanation: The Department of Biotechnology held the International Summit on Women in STEM in New Delhi on 23 and 24 January 2020.

questions.text: In which of the following states is the Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary located?
questions.explanation: Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary, also a tiger reserve, is in the Western Ghats of Karnataka.

questions.text: Cuscuta is an example of:
questions.explanation: Cuscuta (dodder) has no chlorophyll and draws its food from the host plant it twines round: it is a parasite.

questions.text: Who was the founder of the Mamluk dynasty in India?
questions.explanation: Qutb-ud-din Aibak founded the Mamluk (Slave) dynasty in 1206.

questions.text: In which year was the Marine Products Export Development Authority (MPEDA) established in India?
questions.explanation: MPEDA was set up in 1972 under the Marine Products Export Development Authority Act, 1972, to promote exports of marine products.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. If he doesn't reach the station in time, he “would sure miss” the train.
questions.explanation: A first conditional pairs the present simple in the 'if' clause with 'will' in the main clause, and the verb needs the adverb 'surely', not the adjective 'sure': 'he will surely miss the train'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. It is claimed that if you take a certain homeopathic medicine, it will ______ you against the coronavirus.
questions.explanation: To 'fortify' someone against something is to strengthen them to resist it, as the medicine is claimed to do. 'Immune' is an adjective, not a verb, and 'shelter' (to cover or protect) does not suit a medicine.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. WRY
questions.explanation: 'Wry' first meant twisted or bent to one side, as in a wry face: 'crooked'.

questions.text: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. My mother generally read the local newspaper to keep abreast of the local news.
questions.explanation: 'Generally' describes a habit, which takes the present simple: 'My mother generally reads the local newspaper'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. SUSTENANCE
questions.explanation: 'Sustenance' is the food and drink that keep one alive; its opposite is 'starvation'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'superfluous'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined segment in the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement' What a “palace” home!
questions.explanation: The adjective meaning 'like a palace' is 'palatial', as in 'a palatial home'. 'Palatable' means pleasant to taste.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. MALIGNANT
questions.explanation: 'Malignant' means evil in nature or effect, wishing harm to others: 'vicious'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Under wraps
questions.explanation: Something kept 'under wraps' is kept secret.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. DEVIOUS
questions.explanation: 'Devious' means dishonest and indirect; its opposite is 'straight', honest and direct.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. Anju said to Vijaya, "You can stay with us whenever you are in Delhi."
options: Anju told Vijaya that she could stay with them whenever she was in Delhi.
Anju told Vijaya that she could stay with them whenever you were in Delhi.
Anju told Vijaya that she can stay with us whenever she is in Delhi.
Anju told Vijaya that you can stay with us whenever you are in Delhi.
questions.explanation: After 'told', 'can' becomes 'could' and 'are' becomes 'was', and the pronouns change to the reporter's point of view: 'you' becomes 'she' and 'us' becomes 'them'.

questions.text: Select the option which means the same as the group of words given. A government run by the wealthy people
questions.explanation: Plutocracy is government by the wealthy; oligarchy is rule by a small group, aristocracy by a privileged class and monarchy by a king or queen.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. The Central Board of Secondary Education has launched a new helpline for students.
options: A new helpline for students is launched by the Central Board of Secondary Education.
A new helpline for students will be launched by the Central Board of Secondary Education.
A new helpline for students had been launched by the Central Board of Secondary Education.
A new helpline for students has been launched by the Central Board of Secondary Education.
questions.explanation: The present perfect 'has launched' becomes 'has been launched', with the object 'a new helpline for students' as the new subject.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, pick the one that gives their correct order. A. He lived in a small house near the main road of a village. B. As both, he and his wife, worked hard, they made a small fortune. C. But one thing caused them great sorrow: they had no children. D. After he got married, he started a tailor's shop.
questions.explanation: A introduces the man, D tells of his marriage and his shop, B how he and his wife prospered, and C, opening with 'But', their one sorrow: ADBC.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. Debjyoti’s short animation film ______ highlights the stark contrast between the rich and the poor in India.
questions.explanation: A film that brings out a stark contrast between rich and poor does so 'poignantly', in a way that moves the viewer.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. On tenterhooks
questions.explanation: To be 'on tenterhooks' is to be anxious or tense while waiting for something.

questions.text: Examine the four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, pick the one that gives their correct order. A. We gently put the fledgling back into the nest. B. One morning, we found one of the four fallen on the ground. C. The robin couple built a nest in our verandah and laid four eggs. D. Once they had hatched, they busily took turns feeding the four.
questions.explanation: C tells of the nest and the four eggs, D of the hatching and feeding, B of the chick found on the ground one morning and A of putting it back: CDBA.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. That which is incapable of being read or understood
questions.explanation: Illegible writing cannot be read; 'intelligible' means the opposite, able to be understood, and 'indelible' means impossible to remove.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. Deepu’s mother / has repeated asked him / to lower the volume / of his mobile.
questions.explanation: The verb 'asked' needs the adverb 'repeatedly', not the participle 'repeated': 'has repeatedly asked him'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. A year is hardly sufficient time for a Master to (1) ______ about a new school, leave alone absorb a distinct tradition like (2) ______. Most of the new appointees had not served in a residential school and (3) ______ time to learn. But the short tenure did not allow (4) ______. They could not develop understanding of the student and his (5) ______.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 1.
questions.explanation: 'To' takes the base form of the verb: 'time for a Master to learn about a new school'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. A year is hardly sufficient time for a Master to (1) ______ about a new school, leave alone absorb a distinct tradition like (2) ______. Most of the new appointees had not served in a residential school and (3) ______ time to learn. But the short tenure did not allow (4) ______. They could not develop understanding of the student and his (5) ______.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 2.
questions.explanation: 'A distinct tradition like ours': the possessive pronoun stands for 'our tradition'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. A year is hardly sufficient time for a Master to (1) ______ about a new school, leave alone absorb a distinct tradition like (2) ______. Most of the new appointees had not served in a residential school and (3) ______ time to learn. But the short tenure did not allow (4) ______. They could not develop understanding of the student and his (5) ______.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 3.
questions.explanation: The past tense matches 'had not served': the new appointees 'needed time to learn'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. A year is hardly sufficient time for a Master to (1) ______ about a new school, leave alone absorb a distinct tradition like (2) ______. Most of the new appointees had not served in a residential school and (3) ______ time to learn. But the short tenure did not allow (4) ______. They could not develop understanding of the student and his (5) ______.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 4.
questions.explanation: 'That' refers back to the time they needed: the short tenure did not allow it.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. A year is hardly sufficient time for a Master to (1) ______ about a new school, leave alone absorb a distinct tradition like (2) ______. Most of the new appointees had not served in a residential school and (3) ______ time to learn. But the short tenure did not allow (4) ______. They could not develop understanding of the student and his (5) ______.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 5.
questions.explanation: The possessive 'his' must be followed by a noun: 'the student and his environment'.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All computers are machines. No television is a computer. All televisions are instruments. Conclusions: I. Some instruments are machines. II. Some machines are computers. III. Some televisions are machines.
options: Only conclusions II and III follow.
questions.explanation: All computers are machines, so some machines are computers (II). No television is a computer, and nothing links televisions, or the instruments that include them, to machines, so neither I nor III follows.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given letter series will complete the series. a_ _bcde_ _abbcd_ _aabb_ _ee
questions.explanation: With a, b, e, a, e, e, c, d in the blanks the block aabbcdee repeats three times: aabbcdee aabbcdee aabbcdee.

questions.text: Select the option in which the words share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of words. Ammeter : Electric current
questions.explanation: An ammeter measures electric current, as a hygrometer measures humidity, in the same order. The density and pressure pairs are the other way round, and a polarimeter does not measure steps.

questions.text: ‘Straw’ is related to ‘Nest’ in the same way as ‘Cotton’ is related to ‘______’.
questions.explanation: A nest is made of straw, as thread is made of cotton.

questions.text: The sales boy of a washing machine store charges his customers 24% more than the cost price. If a customer paid ₹6,200 for a washing machine, then what was the cost price of the washing machine?
questions.explanation: The price paid is 124% of the cost price: 6,200 × 100/124 = ₹5,000.

questions.text: Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it. 28 16 27; 44 16 15; 84 ? 24
questions.explanation: In each row the middle number is a quarter of the first plus a third of the last: 28 ÷ 4 + 27 ÷ 3 = 7 + 9 = 16 and 44 ÷ 4 + 15 ÷ 3 = 11 + 5 = 16. So 84 ÷ 4 + 24 ÷ 3 = 21 + 8 = 29.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number. 12 : 150 : : 14 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is the square of the first plus half of it: 12² + 6 = 150. Likewise 14² + 7 = 196 + 7 = 203.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 3, 5, 15, 41, ?, 173
Four letter-clusters have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the letter-cluster that is different.
questions.explanation: In DHSZ, TXCJ and GKPW the second letter is 4 after the first, the third is the second's opposite in the alphabet (H/S, X/C, K/P: positions adding up to 27) and the fourth is 7 after the third. In NRJQ the opposite of R is I, not J.

questions.text: In a certain code language, FORWARD is written as CSZXQPE. How will NUMERAL be written in that language?
questions.explanation: FORWARD is written backwards, DRAWROF, and its letters are moved 1 back and 1 forward in turn: CSZXQPE. NUMERAL backwards is LAREMUN, which becomes KBQFLVM.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the following equation correct? 12 – 8 + 4 ÷ 2 × 8 = 4
questions.explanation: After interchanging × and +: 12 − 8 × 4 ÷ 2 + 8 = 12 − 16 + 8 = 4.

questions.text: In a certain code language, HAMPER is coded as 17212322036 and INSULT is coded as 16286421340. How will SAFETY be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Letters in odd places become 25 minus their position in the alphabet and letters in even places are doubled: HAMPER = 17, 2, 12, 32, 20, 36. SAFETY: S (19) → 6, A → 2, F (6) → 19, E → 10, T (20) → 5, Y → 50: 621910550.

questions.text: Four words have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the word that is different.
questions.explanation: Integrity, honesty and truthfulness all mean being honest; joviality is cheerfulness.

questions.text: Snigda said that she met her mother's only brother's son's mother's father-in-law. Whom did she meet?
questions.explanation: Snigda's mother's only brother is her maternal uncle; his son's mother is the uncle's wife, and her father-in-law is the uncle's father: Snigda's grandfather.

questions.text: Four numbers have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the number that is different.
questions.explanation: The digits of 6341, 5423 and 1652 add up to 14; those of 6138 add up to 18.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. {9, 12, 18}
questions.explanation: From 9 to 12 is +3 and from 12 to 18 is +6, twice as much. Likewise 13 to 19 is +6 and 19 to 31 is +12.

questions.text: Select the correct option that indicates the arrangement of the given words in the order in which they appear in an English dictionary. 1. Multifocal 2. Movement 3. Multinomial 4. Moviemaker 5. Mutual fund
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Movement (2), Moviemaker (4), Multifocal (1), Multinomial (3), Mutual fund (5). 'Move' comes before 'Movi', 'Multif' before 'Multin', and 'Mul' before 'Mut'.

questions.text: Who among the following is the first Indian pistol shooter to reach number one in world rankings by the International Shooting Sport Federation?
questions.explanation: Heena Sidhu became the first Indian pistol shooter to be ranked world number one by the ISSF, in the 10 m air pistol in 2014.

questions.text: Who among the following has become the first woman umpire to officiate in a men’s Test match in January 2021?
questions.explanation: Australia's Claire Polosak was the fourth umpire in the India-Australia Test at Sydney in January 2021, the first woman to officiate in a men's Test.

questions.text: Which part of soil has organic materials incorporated with the mineral matter, nutrients and water?
questions.explanation: Horizon A, the topmost zone, is where organic material is mixed with mineral matter, nutrients and water; B is a transition zone and C is the weathered parent material.

questions.text: In which of the following states is Sabarimala Sree Dharma Sastha Temple located?
questions.explanation: The Sabarimala Sree Dharma Sastha (Ayyappa) Temple is in Pathanamthitta district, Kerala.

questions.text: Identify the Indian state which was known as 'Pragjyotisha' during the epic period.
questions.explanation: Pragjyotisha, later called Kamarupa, is the epics' name for the kingdom in present-day Assam.

questions.text: What is the SI unit for measuring pressure?
questions.explanation: The pascal, one newton per square metre, is the SI unit of pressure; the candela, ampere and kelvin measure luminous intensity, electric current and temperature.

questions.text: Who among the following was appointed by AIFF (All India Football Federation) as its first Deputy General Secretary in January 2021?
questions.explanation: Abhishek Yadav, a former India striker, was appointed the AIFF's first Deputy General Secretary in January 2021.

questions.text: Kabartal Wetland was designated as a Ramsar site in 2020. In which of the following states is it located?
questions.explanation: Kabartal (Kanwar Jheel), in Begusarai district, became Bihar's first Ramsar site in 2020.

questions.text: ______ are gently sloping areas of the ocean basins.
questions.explanation: Deep sea (abyssal) plains are the gently sloping areas of the ocean basins, the flattest and smoothest regions of the world.

questions.text: Who among the following was appointed as the Chief Justice of the Andhra Pradesh High Court in January 2021?
questions.explanation: Justice Arup Kumar Goswami, until then Chief Justice of the Sikkim High Court, became Chief Justice of the Andhra Pradesh High Court in January 2021.

questions.text: Who among the following Indian nationals got the ‘Legion of Merit’ Award 2020 from the US?
questions.explanation: The US President awarded Prime Minister Narendra Modi the Legion of Merit, in its highest degree, Chief Commander, in December 2020.

questions.text: Who among the following became the first Lokpal of India?
questions.explanation: Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose, a former Supreme Court judge, was appointed India's first Lokpal in March 2019.

questions.text: In which of the following states did the Land Grabbing (Prohibition) Act, 2020 come into force in December 2020?
questions.explanation: Gujarat's Land Grabbing (Prohibition) Act, 2020, which carries up to 14 years in jail for land grabbing, began to be enforced in December 2020.

questions.text: What happens to Indian exports when Indian rupee is devalued?
questions.explanation: After devaluation a rupee buys less foreign currency, so Indian goods cost foreign buyers less: exports become cheaper.

questions.text: ______ is the process of turning on a computer and powering up the system.
questions.explanation: Booting is starting a computer and loading its operating system into memory.

questions.text: What do you call a key on a computer keyboard that is used to move the pointer (cursor) around on the screen?
questions.explanation: Navigation keys, such as the arrow keys, Home, End, Page Up and Page Down, move the cursor around the screen.

questions.text: Vitamin B12 is generally NOT present in ______.
questions.explanation: Vitamin B12 is found naturally in animal foods such as milk, fish, eggs and meat, but generally not in plant foods.

questions.text: Who among the following is considered as the ‘Father of Modern Atomic Theory’?
questions.explanation: John Dalton put forward the modern atomic theory in the early 19th century.

questions.text: ______ plains are formed due to the weathering of soluble rocks such as limestone and dolomite.
questions.explanation: Karst landforms, karst plains among them, form where water dissolves soluble rocks such as limestone and dolomite.

questions.text: Which of the following state governments unveiled a Braille version of the Constitution of India in January 2021?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Maharashtra, whose Social Justice Minister, Dhananjay Munde, unveiled in Mumbai a Braille version of the Constitution of India prepared by the Thane-based Astitva Foundation.

questions.text: In which of the following cities is the corporate centre of State Bank of India (SBI) situated?
questions.explanation: SBI's corporate centre, State Bank Bhavan, is at Nariman Point in Mumbai.

questions.text: In which of the following years was the Vijayanagar empire founded?
questions.explanation: Harihara I and Bukka Raya of the Sangama dynasty founded the Vijayanagara empire in 1336.

questions.text: In which of the following years did Telangana become the 29th state of India after the reorganisation of the state of Andhra Pradesh?
questions.explanation: Telangana was formed from Andhra Pradesh on 2 June 2014 under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014.

questions.text: 'Kati Bihu' in Assam is celebrated by lighting a lamp in front of a ______ tree / plant.
questions.explanation: At Kati Bihu, in October, earthen lamps are lit at the foot of the tulsi plant in the courtyard, and in the paddy fields.

questions.text: Who among the following was awarded the Rabindranath Tagore Literary Award 2020?
questions.explanation: Raj Kamal Jha won the Rabindranath Tagore Literary Prize 2020 for his novel 'The City and the Sea'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To go red in the face
options: To shout at someone for doing something wrong
To feel very happy and proud
questions.explanation: To 'go red in the face' is to blush with shame or awkwardness: to feel embarrassed.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. His jokes “fell flat” on the audience.
questions.explanation: To 'fall flat' is to fail to produce the intended effect: the jokes drew no laughs.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. She said to her friend, “Will you take my dog for a walk?”
options: She asked her friend that if she will take her dog for a walk.
She asked her friend will she take her dog for a walk.
She asked her friend if she would take her dog for a walk.
She asked to her friend if she would take my dog for a walk.
questions.explanation: A yes/no question is reported with 'asked ... if'; 'will' becomes 'would' and 'my' becomes 'her': 'She asked her friend if she would take her dog for a walk.'

questions.text: Fill in the blank with most appropriate word. This train is ______ for Bihar.
questions.explanation: A train 'bound for' a place is on its way there.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. We were quite impressed with the enthusiasm “that she work for”.
questions.explanation: One works 'with' enthusiasm, and the past tense matches 'were impressed': 'the enthusiasm that she worked with'.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. On the other, there is the principle of leadership. B. Democracy rests on a tension between two different principles. C. While the first gives priority to rules, the second gives importance to persons. D. On the one hand, there is the principle of equality before the law, or more generally, equality.
questions.explanation: B names the tension between two principles, D gives the first ('On the one hand ... equality'), A the second ('On the other ... leadership') and C contrasts them: BDAC.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given words. a person who formally requests something, especially a job
questions.explanation: An applicant is a person who formally applies for something, such as a job.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Continuing for a long time
questions.explanation: 'Prolonged' means continuing for a long time. 'Infinite' means without end, and 'profound' means deep.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. All our / furnitures were / spoiled in the recent / rains and floods.
questions.explanation: 'Furniture' is uncountable and has no plural: 'All our furniture was spoiled'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. WISDOM
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'wisdom' is 'stupidity'. 'Maturity' is close in meaning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. COMPLY
questions.explanation: To 'comply' is to act as asked or required: to 'obey'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'highlight'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'. I “practised for” the debate; that's why I am late.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'was practising for': the past continuous presents the practice as an activity that was going on and kept the speaker, the usual way to explain being late. The simple past 'practised' is not ungrammatical, but it reports a finished event and explains the lateness less naturally.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Dearth
questions.explanation: A 'dearth' is a scarcity or lack: a 'shortage'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Weird
questions.explanation: 'Weird' means strange or unusual; its opposite is 'normal'. 'Abnormal' is close to a synonym.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. If the test booklet seal is broken or ______ with, bring it immediately to the notice of the invigilator.
questions.explanation: To 'tamper with' something is to interfere with it so as to damage or alter it.

questions.text: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. As soon as the bus driver was seeing the child crossing the road, he applied the brakes.
options: As soon as the bus driver
questions.explanation: 'See' is not normally used in the continuous, and 'as soon as' takes the simple past here: 'As soon as the bus driver saw the child'.

questions.text: Given below are four sentences in jumbled order. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. On coming out, his skin would be shining like ebony and he would squeal with pleasure. B. First, he would lie down on the sand bank while I rubbed him clean with the sand of the river. C. Every day, I used to take the baby elephant to the river for his bath. D. After that, he would lie in the water for a long time.
questions.explanation: C introduces the daily bath, B says what he did 'First', D what he did 'After that', and A describes him 'On coming out': CBDA.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in the active or passive voice. Designer clothes were sold to the masses by Pierre Cardin.
options: The masses were sold by Pierre Cardin to the designer clothes.
Designer clothes have been sold by Pierre Cardin to the masses.
Pierre Cardin sold designer clothes to the masses.
Pierre Cardin had sold designer clothes to the masses.
questions.explanation: The simple past passive 'were sold by' becomes the simple past active 'sold', with the agent as subject: 'Pierre Cardin sold designer clothes to the masses.'

questions.text: Select the misspelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'accommodate', with double 'c' and double 'm'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. ‘SkillSet’ was founded in 2014 to collect and co-ordinate (1) ______ about educational access and quality for students with special needs and disabilities. The organisation (2) ______ thousands of enquiries every year and offers (3) ______ to students on how to apply to colleges and universities across the country and how to find out about special (4) ______ and scholarships. We ensure easy access to higher education for all students, (5) ______ those with disabilities. Your donations and suggestions will help us to improve our service to customers and you will also be helping us to continue our valuable work.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The organisation was founded to collect and co-ordinate 'information' about educational access and quality.

questions.text:

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: An organisation 'receives' enquiries; it does not pass, transmit or send them.

questions.text:

Your donations and suggestions will help us to improve our service to customers and you will also be helping us to continue our valuable work.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: It offers 'advice', that is guidance, to students on how to apply to colleges and universities.

questions.explanation: Students with special needs look for special 'facilities' (and scholarships) at colleges and universities.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.

questions.text: Select the word-pair in which the two words are related in the same way as are the two words in the following word-pair. Language : Telugu
questions.explanation: Telugu is one of the languages, as Asia is one of the continents: a class and a member of it.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given letter series will complete the series. Z H _ O R C _ _ K _ R _ Z H _ O _ C
options: Z, H, K, O, C, K, R
K, Z, H, K, R, K, R
K, Z, H, O, C, K, R
K, Z, O, R, C, K, R
questions.explanation: With K, Z, H, O, C, K, R in the blanks the block ZHKORC repeats: ZHKORC ZHKORC ZHKORC.

questions.text: In a code language, if RAFT is written as 180 and DON is written as 99, then how will SHOWER be written in the same language?
questions.explanation: The code is the sum of the letters' positions times the number of letters: RAFT = (18 + 1 + 6 + 20) × 4 = 180 and DON = (4 + 15 + 14) × 3 = 99. SHOWER = (19 + 8 + 15 + 23 + 5 + 18) × 6 = 88 × 6 = 528.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully.
