Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All trucks are cars. No wheel is a car. No car is a bus. Conclusions: I. No bus is a truck. II. No wheel is a bus. III. Some cars are trucks.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Both conclusions II and III follow.
Both conclusions I and III follow.
questions.explanation: All trucks are cars and no car is a bus, so no bus is a truck (I); and as all trucks are cars, some cars are trucks (III). Wheels and buses both lie outside the cars, but nothing relates them to each other, so II does not follow.

questions.text: Barun is the son of Chetan. Advita and Chetan are a married couple. Prakul is the brother of Chetan. Diya is the daughter of Advita. Suman is the brother of Barun. How is Diya related to Barun?
questions.explanation: Advita is Chetan's wife, so Barun (Chetan's son) and Diya (Advita's daughter) are children of the same couple: Diya is Barun's sister.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the sixth number is related to the fifth number. 3 : 65 : : 5 : ? : : 4 : 126
questions.explanation: The second number is the cube of one more than the first, plus 1: 4³ + 1 = 65 and 5³ + 1 = 126. Likewise 6³ + 1 = 217.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (42, 14, 294)
questions.explanation: The third number is half the product of the first two: 42 × 14 ÷ 2 = 294. Likewise 34 × 18 ÷ 2 = 306.

questions.text: In a certain code language, BACK is written as YEXP and MIXTURE is written as NOCGAII. How will FROGS be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each consonant is replaced by its opposite letter (B ↔ Y, C ↔ X, K ↔ P, M ↔ N) and each vowel by the next vowel (A → E, I → O, U → A, E → I). So F → U, R → I, O → U, G → T and S → H: UIUTH.

questions.text: Three of the following four letter-clusters are alike in a certain way and one is different. Select the odd one.
questions.explanation: In KPUZ, TYDI and LQVA each letter is 5 places after the one before it (wrapping round after Z). BGLP moves +5, +5, then +4, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 14, 16, 34, 104, 418, ?
Select the option that represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in an English dictionary. 1. Presume 2. Prepare 3. Priority 4. Prince 5. Prick
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Prepare (2), Presume (1), Prick (5), Prince (4), Priority (3). 'Prep' comes before 'Pres', and 'Pric' before 'Prin' and 'Prio'.

questions.text: What was the day of the week on 22 February 2012?
questions.explanation: 1 January 2012 was a Sunday. 22 February is 31 + 21 = 52 days later, and 52 = 7 × 7 + 3, so it falls three days after Sunday: Wednesday.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. Africa : Algeria : : South America : ?
questions.explanation: Algeria is a country in Africa; likewise Argentina is in South America. Canada and Mexico are in North America, Germany in Europe.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 21 + 5 – 45 × 9 ÷ 3 = 11
Four words have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the word that is different.
questions.explanation: Baht, peso and rial are currencies; Oslo is a city, the capital of Norway.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term. POSTED : TPQEFU : : COUNTS : ?
questions.explanation: Each half is moved one letter forward and reversed: POS → QPT → TPQ and TED → UFE → EFU. So COU → DPV → VPD and NTS → OUT → TUO: VPDTUO.

questions.text: Four number-pairs have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the one that is different.
questions.explanation: 289, 225 and 484 are the squares of 17, 15 and 22. 18² = 324, not 322, so 322 : 18 is the odd one.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers share the same relationship as that shared by the numbers in the given set. (4, 3, 73)
questions.explanation: The cube of the first number plus the square of the second gives the third: 4³ + 3² = 64 + 9 = 73. Likewise 5³ + 4² = 125 + 16 = 141.

questions.text: Which of the given Articles of the Constitution of India mentions the following? "There shall be a council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President who shall in the exercise of his functions, act in accordance with such advice."
questions.explanation: Article 74(1) provides for a Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister to aid and advise the President, who shall act in accordance with its advice.

questions.text: In which country was the World Snooker Championship 2020 held from 31 July to 16 August 2020?
questions.explanation: The 2020 World Snooker Championship, delayed by the pandemic, was played at the Crucible Theatre in Sheffield, England.

questions.text: In which year did India host the Commonwealth Games?
questions.explanation: India has hosted the Commonwealth Games once, in Delhi in 2010.

questions.text: What is the generic name of calcium sulphate hemihydrate?
questions.explanation: Calcium sulphate hemihydrate, CaSO₄·½H₂O, is Plaster of Paris, made by heating gypsum.

questions.text: Which of the following rivers originates from the state of Rajasthan?
questions.explanation: The Banas rises in the Aravalli hills of Rajasthan's Rajsamand district. The Chambal, the Mahi and the Narmada all rise in Madhya Pradesh.

questions.text: Who was the ruler of Delhi sultanate when Ibn Batuta came in India?
questions.explanation: Ibn Battuta reached India in 1333 and served as a qazi at Delhi under Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

questions.text: Which of the following keyboard shortcuts will you press in order to minimise all programs on a computer screen and display the desktop?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Windows + D, which Microsoft lists as 'Display and hide the desktop': it minimises the open windows and brings the desktop in front of any that cannot be minimised (pressed again, it restores them). Windows + M only minimises the windows that can be minimised and leaves the rest on screen, so it is close but less exact.

questions.text: Which has been India's most successful sport in the history of Olympic games having won medals maximum number of times till December 2020?
questions.explanation: Field hockey has won India more Olympic medals than any other sport, including 8 gold medals.

questions.text: In which of the following caves is the painting named ‘Padmapani Bodhisattva’ found?
questions.explanation: The Padmapani Bodhisattva is painted in Ajanta Cave No. 1.

questions.text: Down Syndrome, which causes learning difficulties and physical health development delays and disabilities, is a:
questions.explanation: Down syndrome is a genetic disorder, caused by an extra copy of chromosome 21 (trisomy 21).

questions.text: Who among the following became the youngest speaker of Lok Sabha till March 2021?
questions.explanation: G. M. C. Balayogi became Speaker of the Lok Sabha in 1998 at 46, the youngest so far.

questions.text: ______ launched 'Harit Path', a mobile app, in 2020.
questions.explanation: The National Highways Authority of India launched the Harit Path app in August 2020 to monitor, through geo-tagged photographs, the trees planted along national highways.

questions.text: CorelDraw is an example of a/an:
questions.explanation: CorelDRAW is a graphics design program used for drawings, layouts and print material: of these, desktop publishing software. It is not a database, accounting or spreadsheet program.

questions.text: What minimum support price per quintal of groundnut has been declared by the Government of India for the marketing season 2020-21?
questions.explanation: The minimum support price for groundnut in the 2020-21 kharif marketing season was ₹5,275 a quintal, ₹185 more than the year before.

questions.text: Mirzai and bandi (types of jackets in white or black) are popular in the ______ region/s.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Bundelkhand and Malwa: accounts of Madhya Pradesh's traditional dress describe the bandi or mirzai, a jacket in white or black, as part of men's attire in these two regions.

questions.text: What do you call the point in the orbit of the moon or a satellite at which it is nearest to Earth?
questions.explanation: The perigee is the point of an orbit nearest the Earth; the apogee is the farthest.

questions.text: Which of the following types of rocks are formed by the lithification process?
questions.explanation: Lithification is the compaction and cementation of deposited sediment into rock: it forms sedimentary rocks.

questions.text: Bhaskaravarman of the Varman dynasty ruled in the ______ region.
questions.explanation: Bhaskaravarman, a contemporary and ally of Harshavardhana, ruled Kamarupa, in present-day Assam.

questions.text: Who among the following took charge as the CEO and Managing Director of HDFC Bank in October 2020?
questions.explanation: Sashidhar Jagdishan succeeded Aditya Puri as HDFC Bank's MD and CEO in October 2020.

questions.text: Convention on the prohibition of the use of nuclear weapons and reducing nuclear danger under the nuclear weapons cluster were two resolutions sponsored by India that ______ adopted in 2020.
questions.explanation: The UN General Assembly's First Committee, on disarmament, adopted India's resolutions 'Convention on the Prohibition of the Use of Nuclear Weapons' and 'Reducing Nuclear Danger' in November 2020; India has tabled them since 1982 and 1998.

questions.text: Which of the following organisations released the ‘Global Economic Freedom Index 2020 Annual Report’?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives The Heritage Foundation, the only one of these that publishes an economic freedom index: its annual Index of Economic Freedom (India 120th in 2020). The 'Economic Freedom of the World: 2020 Annual Report', which ranked India 105th, is the Fraser Institute's, and it is not among the options.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a use of washing soda?
options: It can be used as a cleaning agent for domestic purposes.
It is used in glass, soap and paper industries.
It is used to make drinking water free from germs.
It is used for removing permanent hardness of water.
questions.explanation: Making drinking water free from germs is a use of bleaching powder. Washing soda (sodium carbonate) is used for cleaning, in the glass, soap and paper industries and to remove permanent hardness of water.

questions.text: In 2020, the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded jointly to Harvey J Alter, Michael Houghton and Charles M Rice for the discovery of:
questions.explanation: Alter, Houghton and Rice shared the 2020 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for the discovery of the hepatitis C virus.

questions.text: Which Indian actor was conferred with the ‘Most Inspiring Indian Bollywood Actor’ award in the UK in 2019?
questions.explanation: Sanjay Kapoor received the award at an event in the House of Commons, London, in 2019.

questions.text: In the given sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. I would have died if he did not dress my wound that day.
questions.explanation: An unreal condition in the past takes the past perfect in the 'if' clause: 'I would have died if he had not dressed my wound that day.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. Priya has a very ______ nature and does not accept financial help even from her own parents.
questions.explanation: Someone who will not take financial help even from her parents has an 'independent' nature.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Encroach
questions.explanation: To 'encroach' is to intrude, little by little, on another's land, rights or time.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. Cheetahs are one of the world’s most-recognisable cats, known especially for their speed. B. Their faces too are distinguished by prominent black lines that curve from the inner corner of each eye to the outer corners of the mouth, like a well-worn trail of inky tears. C. Cheetahs are covered almost entirely with small black spots on a background of pale yellow and have a white underbelly. D. They have a long, slender body measuring 1.2 metres (4 feet), with a long tail (65–85 cm [2–3 feet]) that generally ends in a white tuft.
questions.explanation: A introduces cheetahs and their speed, so it opens the paragraph ('Their' in B and 'They' in D need it before them), and ABDC is the only option that begins with A: B ('Their faces too') adds a second distinguishing feature, D describes the body and C its coat.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Pull something off
options: Take out the cover or lid
questions.explanation: To 'pull something off' is to succeed in making something difficult happen.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Go to the dogs
questions.explanation: To 'go to the dogs' is to deteriorate badly, to fall into a very poor state.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Fond of company
questions.explanation: A gregarious person is fond of company and sociable.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No improvement'. “The child is crying” because she can't find her mother.
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct: the present continuous 'is crying' describes what is happening now, and the singular 'The child' agrees with 'is' and with 'she'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'heinous'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. INDIGNANT
questions.explanation: 'Indignant' means angry at something unfair; its opposite is 'pleased'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Harrowing
questions.explanation: 'Harrowing' means extremely distressing; its opposite is 'pleasant'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech. My friends say that many young people are very active on social media now.
options: My friends say, “Many young people were very active on social media now.”
My friends said, “Many young people were very active on social media then.”
My friends say, “Many young people are very active on social media now.”
My friends are saying, “Many young people are very active on social media then.”
questions.explanation: The reporting verb 'say' is in the present tense, so nothing shifts: the direct speech keeps 'are' and 'now'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. The roof “is being held up over” two stone pillars.
questions.explanation: A roof is supported 'by' its pillars, and a lasting state takes the simple present passive: 'The roof is held up by two stone pillars.'

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order. A. He confessed that the only thing he was afraid of was snakes. B. On my second visit to West Africa I met a young man on board the ship. C. I told him that it was very unlikely that he would see any. D. He was going out to take up a job in a banana plantation.
questions.explanation: B introduces the young man on the ship, D says where he was going, A gives his confession about snakes and C the narrator's reply that he would hardly see any: BDAC.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. A person who arranges and sells cut flowers
questions.explanation: A florist arranges and sells cut flowers; a horticulturist grows plants and a botanist studies them.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. At the last moment, a fireman pulled out Manohar from the burning bus.
options: At the last moment, Manohar was pulling out of the burning bus by a fireman.
At the last moment, Manohar was pulled out of the burning bus by a fireman.
At the last moment, Manohar had been pulled out of the burning bus by a fireman.
At the last moment, a fireman was pulled out of the burning bus by Manohar.
questions.explanation: The object, Manohar, becomes the subject of the past simple passive 'was pulled out of', and the fireman becomes the agent after 'by'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank in the given sentence. The passengers waited ______ for the local train to arrive.
questions.explanation: Waiting calmly, without complaint, for the train is waiting 'patiently'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. APPARENTLY
questions.explanation: 'Apparently' means as far as one can tell: 'seemingly'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. At the workshop, / they were taught how to nail / the pieces of wood together to create toys.
options: they were taught how to nail
the pieces of wood together to create toys
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct: 'were taught how to nail the pieces of wood together' uses 'how to' with the infinitive, and 'to create toys' gives the purpose.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Equiano was born in 1745 in Nigeria. When he (1) ______ about eleven, Equiano was kidnapped and sold to slave traders headed (2) ______ the West Indies. Though he spent a brief (3) ______ in the state of Virginia, much of Equiano's time (4) ______ serving on slave ships and British navy vessels. In his service on these (5) ______, Equiano traveled extensively.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number1.
questions.explanation: 'He' is singular and the story is in the past: 'When he was about eleven'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Equiano was born in 1745 in Nigeria. When he (1) ______ about eleven, Equiano was kidnapped and sold to slave traders headed (2) ______ the West Indies. Though he spent a brief (3) ______ in the state of Virginia, much of Equiano's time (4) ______ serving on slave ships and British navy vessels. In his service on these (5) ______, Equiano traveled extensively.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The slave traders were 'headed to', that is travelling towards, the West Indies.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Equiano was born in 1745 in Nigeria. When he (1) ______ about eleven, Equiano was kidnapped and sold to slave traders headed (2) ______ the West Indies. Though he spent a brief (3) ______ in the state of Virginia, much of Equiano's time (4) ______ serving on slave ships and British navy vessels. In his service on these (5) ______, Equiano traveled extensively.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 3.
questions.explanation: He spent a brief 'period', a stretch of time, in Virginia; an 'era' or an 'age' is a long span of history.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Equiano was born in 1745 in Nigeria. When he (1) ______ about eleven, Equiano was kidnapped and sold to slave traders headed (2) ______ the West Indies. Though he spent a brief (3) ______ in the state of Virginia, much of Equiano's time (4) ______ serving on slave ships and British navy vessels. In his service on these (5) ______, Equiano traveled extensively.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'Much of Equiano's time' is the subject and the story is in the past, so the past simple passive: 'was spent' serving on ships.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Equiano was born in 1745 in Nigeria. When he (1) ______ about eleven, Equiano was kidnapped and sold to slave traders headed (2) ______ the West Indies. Though he spent a brief (3) ______ in the state of Virginia, much of Equiano's time (4) ______ serving on slave ships and British navy vessels. In his service on these (5) ______, Equiano traveled extensively.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'These ships' refers back to the slave ships and navy vessels just named.

questions.text: Nirmala introduced Rahul as the son of the sister of her mother. How is Nirmala related to Rahul?
questions.explanation: Rahul is the son of Nirmala's mother's sister, her maternal aunt, so Nirmala and Rahul are cousins.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to balance the following equation? 646 ÷ 19 – 746 + 20 × 34 = 100
Select the correct option that indicates the arrangement of the given words in a logical and meaningful order. 1. Prescription 2. Diagnosis 3. Illness 4. Follow-up 5. Recovery
questions.explanation: An illness (3) is diagnosed (2), a prescription is given (1), the patient recovers (5) and comes back for a follow-up (4).

questions.text: Four letter-clusters have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the letter-cluster that is different.
questions.explanation: In PVBH, CIOU and KQWC each letter is 6 places after the one before it, wrapping round after Z. In SYDJ, Y to D is only 5 places, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: In a certain code language, CANDIDATE is coded as 846292417 and ACTION is coded as 481936. How will DICTATION be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: From the two codes: C = 8, A = 4, N = 6, D = 2, I = 9, T = 1, E = 7 and O = 3. So DICTATION = 2 9 8 1 4 1 9 3 6: 298141936.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. Galvanometer : Electric current : : Graphometer : ?
questions.explanation: A galvanometer detects electric current; a graphometer, a surveyor's instrument, measures angles.

questions.text: In a certain code language, PROUD is written as WYJPK. How will GUILTY be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Consonants move 7 places forward and vowels 5 places back: P → W, R → Y, O → J, U → P, D → K. So G → N, U → P, I → D, L → S, T → A and Y → F: NPDSAF.

questions.text: From the given options choose the one in which the set of numbers do not follow the same Logic/Rule/Relation as the numbers given in below set. (32, 16, 96)
questions.explanation: In (32, 16, 96) the second number is half the first and the third is 3 times the first. In (22, 11, 68) the third should be 3 × 22 = 66.

questions.text: Select the option in which the words share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of words. Power : Watt
questions.explanation: The watt is the unit of power, as the ohm is of resistance. Current is measured in amperes, not volts, and force in newtons, not pascals.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 4, 5, 13, 22, 86, 111, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 1², 2³, 3², 4³ and 5², so the next is 6³ = 216: 111 + 216 = 327.

questions.text: Four numbers have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the number that is different.
questions.explanation: 231 = 7 × 33, 252 = 7 × 36 and 217 = 7 × 31 are multiples of 7; 348 is not.

questions.text: A driver increases the speed of his vehicle by 5 km/h after every one hour. If the initial speed of the vehicle was 75 km/h, then what was the average speed of the vehicle in a journey of 4 hours?
questions.explanation: The speeds in the four hours are 75, 80, 85 and 90 km/h, so the distance is 330 km and the average speed 330 ÷ 4 = 82.5 km/h.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term. AMIDST : AIMDST : : SYNTAX : ?
questions.explanation: Each half of the word is put in alphabetical order: AMI → AIM, and DST stays DST. So SYN → NSY and TAX → ATX: NSYATX.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given letter series will complete the series. p l _ p p _ s p _ l s p p l _ p
questions.explanation: With s, l, p, s in the blanks the block 'plsp' repeats: plsp plsp plsp plsp.

questions.text: Four words have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the word that is different.
questions.explanation: To fluster, confound or agitate someone is to disturb them; to calm them is the opposite.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (2194, 1328, 726)
questions.explanation: Each number is a cube minus 3, the bases falling by 2: 2194 = 13³ − 3, 1328 = 11³ − 3 and 726 = 9³ − 3. Likewise 1725 = 12³ − 3, 997 = 10³ − 3 and 509 = 8³ − 3.

questions.text: According to which of the following Schedules to the Constitution provides for allocation of seats to the states and union territories in Rajya Sabha?
questions.explanation: The Fourth Schedule allocates the seats of the Rajya Sabha among the states and union territories.

questions.text: Which of the following rivers rises in the west of Rohtang Pass in the Kullu hills of Himachal Pradesh and flows through the Chamba valley of the state?
questions.explanation: The Ravi rises in the Kullu hills and drains the Chamba valley before flowing into Pakistan, where it joins the Chenab.

questions.text: How many Rajya Sabha seats come from the state of Assam?
questions.explanation: Under the Fourth Schedule, Assam has 7 seats in the Rajya Sabha.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which of the following years was the Cornwallis Code enacted?
questions.explanation: The Cornwallis Code, a body of regulations issued under Governor-General Lord Cornwallis in 1793, separated revenue collection from the administration of justice in British India.

questions.text: Which of the following is the full form of EBCDIC?
questions.explanation: EBCDIC, IBM's 8-bit character code, stands for Extended Binary Coded Decimal Interchange Code.

questions.text: Which of the following factors is NOT responsible for the loss of fertility of agricultural land?
options: Higher cation exchange capacity of soil
questions.explanation: Cation exchange capacity is the soil's ability to hold nutrient cations such as potassium, calcium and magnesium, so a higher capacity makes soil more fertile. Salinisation, alkalisation and waterlogging all reduce fertility.

questions.text: Which of the following banks has signed a loan of $40 million to Northern Arc Capital to support the microfinance borrowers and the MSME sectors in India?
questions.explanation: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) signed the $40 million loan to Northern Arc Capital in December 2020, to support microfinance borrowers and small businesses hit by the pandemic.

questions.text: Which of the following devices accepts the results produced by the computer in a machine-readable form?
questions.explanation: A printer is an output device: it takes the computer's results, in machine-readable form, and prints them in human-readable form. The microphone, graphics tablet and mouse are input devices.

questions.text: Kuldeep Handoo has won the Dronacharya Award in 2020. He belongs to which of the following sports?
questions.explanation: Kuldeep Handoo, a wushu coach, received the Dronacharya Award, India's award for sports coaches, in 2020.

questions.text: Which of the following is one of the basic plant nutrients of fertilizers that are commonly used in agriculture?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium (NPK) are the basic plant nutrients in common fertilisers; mercury and arsenic are poisons.

questions.text: Who among the following has written the novel ‘The Awasthis of Aamnagri’?
questions.explanation: 'The Awasthis of Aamnagri' (2020) is the second book of Shubha Sarma, an IAS officer; the paper spells her name 'Sharma'.

questions.text: The 'SAKSHAM' campaign launched by the Government of India in January 2021 aims to spread awareness about ______.
questions.explanation: SAKSHAM (Sanrakshan Kshamata Mahotsav), the Petroleum Conservation Research Association's month-long campaign under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, began in January 2021 to promote fuel conservation and a shift to cleaner fuels.

questions.text: Who among the following footballers won the ‘Best FIFA Men's Player Award’ 2020?
questions.explanation: Robert Lewandowski of Poland and Bayern Munich won The Best FIFA Men's Player award for 2020.

questions.text: Shigmotsav is essentially a festival of the masses, celebrated on the full moon day in the month of Phalguna (March). Which state celebrates this festival?
questions.explanation: Shigmo (Shigmotsav), Goa's spring festival, is celebrated in Phalguna with folk dances and processions.

questions.text: India has engaged actively in the multilateral negotiations in the UNFCCC. What is the full form of UNFCCC?
options: United Nations Framework of Central Climate Change
United Nations Fellowship of Central Climate Change
United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
United Nations Fellowship Convention on Climate Change
questions.explanation: UNFCCC stands for the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, opened for signature at the Rio Earth Summit in 1992.

questions.text: Suryadhar lake is located in which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Suryadhar Lake, at Doiwala in Dehradun district, Uttarakhand, was opened in November 2020.

questions.text: Which of the followings sports was added to the Asian Beach Games Program 2021 as of December 2020?
questions.explanation: Athletics (beach athletics) was among the new disciplines added to the programme of the 6th Asian Beach Games at Sanya, China, then planned for 2021.

questions.text: In which of the following states is Buxa National Park situated?
questions.explanation: Buxa National Park and Tiger Reserve lies in Alipurduar district, in northern West Bengal.

questions.text: Which of the following states Government has unveiled the ‘Farmer Registration and Unified beneficiary Information System’ (FRUITS), an e-governance portal, to create a repository of farmland information and farm loan details on a single platform?
questions.explanation: FRUITS is the Karnataka government's portal that brings farmers' land records and farm-loan details onto one platform.

questions.text: In which of the following cities was India's first indigenously designed and developed driverless metro car unveiled in January 2021?
questions.explanation: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh unveiled the car, built by BEML for the Mumbai Metro, at BEML's plant in Bengaluru on 15 January 2021.

questions.text: Who among the following were awarded the Nobel Prize 2020 in Economics Sciences?
options: James J Heckman and Daniel L McFadden
Paul R Milgrom and Robert B Wilson
William Vickrey and James A Mirrlees
Robert W Fogel and Douglass C North
questions.explanation: Paul Milgrom and Robert Wilson won the 2020 prize in Economic Sciences for improvements to auction theory and inventions of new auction formats.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following battles did Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah fight, defeating the forces under Henry Lawrence?
questions.explanation: At Chinhat, near Lucknow, on 30 June 1857, rebel forces that included Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah's men defeated Sir Henry Lawrence's troops, who fell back to the Residency.

questions.text: Which of the following is used as a primary means of implementing the monetary policy of the Reserve Bank of India?
questions.explanation: The repo rate, at which the RBI lends to banks against government securities, is the policy rate set by its Monetary Policy Committee.

questions.text: In which of the following states is Sri Bhramaramba Mallikarjuna Temple located?
questions.explanation: The Sri Bhramaramba Mallikarjuna Temple at Srisailam, Andhra Pradesh, is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas.

questions.text: Which of the following diseases is caused by Helicobacter pyroli?
questions.explanation: Helicobacter pylori (printed 'pyroli') infects the stomach lining and causes gastritis and peptic ulcers.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'suspense'.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. The other aspect touches upon certain issues that have arisen in recent years, such as brain-death, mercy killing and cloning. B. There are two major aspects relating to the medical profession and its practice the world over. C. These issues must be discussed and debated in the public domain in terms of our cultures and value systems. D. One of these is the ethics of medical practitioners in their day-to-day relationship with their patients and with one another.
questions.explanation: B introduces the two aspects, D gives the first (the ethics of practitioners), A the other (new issues) and C says how those issues must be debated: BDAC.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in the active or passive voice. Celebrate the New Year with amazing offers.
options: The New Year should be celebrated with amazing offers.
The New Year will be celebrated with amazing offers.
Amazing offers will be celebrate in the New Year.
Let the New Year be celebrated with amazing offers.
questions.explanation: A command becomes passive with 'let … be' and the past participle: 'Let the New Year be celebrated with amazing offers.'

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Public speaking / is one of / the most feared form / of communication.
questions.explanation: 'One of' is followed by a plural noun: 'one of the most feared forms'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech. He said to his sister, “Please help me with my homework.”
options: His sister told him that he should help her with her homework.
He requested his sister to help him with his homework.
His sister was asked by her brother that she should help him with his homework.
He told his sister that she should help him with his homework.
questions.explanation: A request is reported with 'requested … to', and 'me' and 'my' become 'him' and 'his': 'He requested his sister to help him with his homework.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Mandatory
questions.explanation: 'Mandatory' means required: 'imperative'. 'Optional' is its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Abode
questions.explanation: An 'abode' is the place where one lives: a 'dwelling'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To drag one’s feet
questions.explanation: To 'drag one's feet' is to be slow or reluctant to act: to put off doing something or deciding it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'. Fermented vegetables can be stored for about a year “without going bad”.
questions.explanation: 'Without' is followed by the -ing form, and 'going bad' means spoiling: the sentence is correct as it stands.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. We admit students with ______ academic backgrounds like life sciences, physical sciences, and business and commerce.
questions.explanation: Life sciences, physical sciences and commerce are very different backgrounds: 'diverse'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Malicious
questions.explanation: 'Malicious' means intending harm; of the options only 'decent' (good and kind) is its opposite. 'Culpable', 'perverted' and 'biased' are all unfavourable.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. After a long gap, / we went shopping / last Sunday and bought / that we wanted.
questions.explanation: 'Bought' needs an object, and 'that we wanted' cannot be one: 'bought what we wanted' (or 'all that we wanted').

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. Please complete the short questionnaire ______ and return it to us.
questions.explanation: The questionnaire is 'attached' (enclosed with the letter) to be filled in and returned.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'. I cannot help you “if you tell me” your problem.
questions.explanation: The sense is 'if you do not tell me': 'unless you tell me'. 'Unless' already carries the negative, so 'unless you don't' is wrong.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Withdraw from a forward position in battle
questions.explanation: To 'retreat' is to withdraw from a forward position in battle.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To make both ends meet
options: To have just enough money to live
To try to do two different things at the same time
To try to bring two parties together
To try to solve a problem between friends
questions.explanation: To 'make (both) ends meet' is to earn just enough money to live on.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Relating to the present time
questions.explanation: 'Contemporary' means belonging to the present time (or to the same time as something else).

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. But he has reached out to millions of people the world over and helped to improve their lives. B. Born in downtown Los Angeles in 1960, Tony Robins came from very humble beginnings. C. Now he travels by private jet and owns properties in many parts of the world. D. His family had been fed by others when they did not have enough money for food.
questions.explanation: B introduces Tony Robins and his humble start, D describes his poor family, C his wealth now and A, opening with 'But', what he has done for others: BDCA.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Resign
questions.explanation: To 'resign' is to leave a job or post; its opposite is to 'join' one.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. All of us know that the American astronaut Neil Armstrong was the first (1) _____ to set foot on the Moon in July 1969. Human footprints on the lunar (2) ______ won’t disappear for millions of years. That is because there is no rain or wind to (3) ______ them. The surface area of the Moon is 25% larger than that of Africa. Astronauts have so far brought back hundreds of kilos of rock and dust from the Moon to (4) ______. It takes the Moon 27.3 days to travel around the Earth. As it does so, we see different amounts of its side (5) ______ by the Sun. That is why it appears to get larger and then smaller.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Armstrong was the first 'human' to set foot on the Moon, as the next sentence's 'human footprints' confirms.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. All of us know that the American astronaut Neil Armstrong was the first (1) _____ to set foot on the Moon in July 1969. Human footprints on the lunar (2) ______ won’t disappear for millions of years. That is because there is no rain or wind to (3) ______ them. The surface area of the Moon is 25% larger than that of Africa. Astronauts have so far brought back hundreds of kilos of rock and dust from the Moon to (4) ______. It takes the Moon 27.3 days to travel around the Earth. As it does so, we see different amounts of its side (5) ______ by the Sun. That is why it appears to get larger and then smaller.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The footprints lie on the lunar 'surface', the ground of the Moon.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. All of us know that the American astronaut Neil Armstrong was the first (1) _____ to set foot on the Moon in July 1969. Human footprints on the lunar (2) ______ won’t disappear for millions of years. That is because there is no rain or wind to (3) ______ them. The surface area of the Moon is 25% larger than that of Africa. Astronauts have so far brought back hundreds of kilos of rock and dust from the Moon to (4) ______. It takes the Moon 27.3 days to travel around the Earth. As it does so, we see different amounts of its side (5) ______ by the Sun. That is why it appears to get larger and then smaller.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: With no rain or wind to 'erode' (wear away) them, the footprints stay.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. All of us know that the American astronaut Neil Armstrong was the first (1) _____ to set foot on the Moon in July 1969. Human footprints on the lunar (2) ______ won’t disappear for millions of years. That is because there is no rain or wind to (3) ______ them. The surface area of the Moon is 25% larger than that of Africa. Astronauts have so far brought back hundreds of kilos of rock and dust from the Moon to (4) ______. It takes the Moon 27.3 days to travel around the Earth. As it does so, we see different amounts of its side (5) ______ by the Sun. That is why it appears to get larger and then smaller.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: Rock and dust were brought back to 'study'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. All of us know that the American astronaut Neil Armstrong was the first (1) _____ to set foot on the Moon in July 1969. Human footprints on the lunar (2) ______ won’t disappear for millions of years. That is because there is no rain or wind to (3) ______ them. The surface area of the Moon is 25% larger than that of Africa. Astronauts have so far brought back hundreds of kilos of rock and dust from the Moon to (4) ______. It takes the Moon 27.3 days to travel around the Earth. As it does so, we see different amounts of its side (5) ______ by the Sun. That is why it appears to get larger and then smaller.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: We see different amounts of the side 'lit' by the Sun.

questions.text: Four number-pairs have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the one that is different.
questions.explanation: In 14 : 112, 21 : 168 and 18 : 144 the second number is 8 times the first. 11 × 8 = 88, not 122.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. France : Euro : : Myanmar : ?
questions.explanation: The euro is the currency of France and the kyat that of Myanmar. (The ringgit is Malaysia's and the yen Japan's.)

questions.text: Select the correct option that indicates the arrangement of the following words in a logical and meaningful order. 1. Restaurant 2. Eating 3. Cooking 4. Order food 5. Serve food
questions.explanation: First the restaurant, then ordering the food, cooking it, serving it and eating it: 1, 4, 3, 5, 2.

questions.text: In a code language, if VISION is written as 176, then how will SEEING be written in the same language?
questions.explanation: Each code is twice the sum of the letters' places in the alphabet: VISION = 22 + 9 + 19 + 9 + 15 + 14 = 88, and 2 × 88 = 176. SEEING = 19 + 5 + 5 + 9 + 14 + 7 = 59, so 118.

questions.text: Four words have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the word that is different.
questions.explanation: Amicability, consensus and rapport all describe agreement or good relations between people; dislike is the opposite.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series. _ _ c f b _ c _ b d _ f
questions.explanation: With b, d, d, f, c in the blanks the block bdcf repeats: bdcf bdcf bdcf.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 33, 34, 30, 39, 23, 48, 12, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are +1, −4, +9, −16, +25, −36: the squares with alternating signs. The next is +49: 12 + 49 = 61.

questions.text: Select the word-pair in which the two words are related in the same way as are the two words in the following word-pair. Litre : Millilitre
questions.explanation: A millilitre is a thousandth of a litre, as a gram is a thousandth of a kilogram.

questions.text: In a certain code language, THICK is written as FELHW. How will RAISE be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters are put in alphabetical order and then moved +3, −3, +3, −3, +3: THICK → C H I K T → F E L H W. So RAISE → A E I R S → D B L O V.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs that can sequentially replace the * signs and balance the given equation. 25 * 48 * 6 * 12 * 2 = 41

Select the option that is related to the fourth number in the same way as the first number is related to the second number and the fifth number is related to the sixth number. 19 : 362 : : ? : 442 : : 17 : 290
questions.explanation: The second number is the square of the first plus 1: 19² + 1 = 362 and 17² + 1 = 290. Likewise 21² + 1 = 442.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers share the same relationship as that shared by the numbers in the given set. (12, 18, 225)
questions.explanation: The third number is the square of the average of the first two: ((12 + 18)/2)² = 15² = 225. Likewise ((25 + 15)/2)² = 20² = 400.

questions.text: Three of the following four letter-cluster pairs are alike in a certain way and one is different. Select the odd one.
questions.explanation: PORT, MODE and LIMB are written backwards: TROP, EDOM, BMIL. FIST backwards is TSIF, not IFTS.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term. SEVERAL : MZSDWDT : : HEADING : ?
questions.explanation: SEVERAL is written backwards (LAREVES) and its letters moved +1, −1 alternately: MZSDWDT. HEADING backwards is GNIDAEH, which becomes HMJCBDI.

questions.text: A total of 1012 candies are to be distributed among Virat, Ketan and Rohan in the ratio of 6 : 9 : 8, respectively. How many candies will Rohan get?
questions.explanation: Rohan gets 8 of every 6 + 9 + 8 = 23 candies: 1012 × 8/23 = 44 × 8 = 352.

questions.text: Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it. 14 22 5 18 42 11 22 35 ?
questions.explanation: In each row the third number is the sum of the digits of the first two minus 4: 1 + 4 + 2 + 2 − 4 = 5 and 1 + 8 + 4 + 2 − 4 = 11. So 2 + 2 + 3 + 5 − 4 = 8.

questions.text: In which of the following states/union territories is India’s highest Meteorological Centre situated?
questions.explanation: The Meteorological Centre at Leh, Ladakh, opened in December 2020 at about 3,500 m, is the highest in India.

questions.text: Who among the following is the brand ambassador of Entri, a local learning app for jobs?
questions.explanation: In September 2020 Entri, an app that prepares job seekers for exams in local languages, signed the cricketer Robin Uthappa as its brand ambassador.

questions.text: The polity of a country is designed according to its ______ and any change to the polity is possible only when an amendment is made.
questions.explanation: A country's polity is laid down by its Constitution, which can be changed only by an amendment.

questions.text: Which of the following is the only state in India that produces diamonds?
questions.explanation: Today India's diamonds come only from the Panna diamond belt of Madhya Pradesh.

questions.text: Who among the following is the Regional Ambassador for India for UNEP (United Nations Environment Programme) as of December 2020?
questions.explanation: In September 2020 Khushi Chindaliya, a 17-year-old from Surat, was named India's Regional Ambassador for UNEP's Tunza Eco-Generation programme.

questions.text: When was the Jal Jeewan Mission launched by the Prime Minister, with the goal of ‘Har Ghar Jal’?
questions.explanation: The Jal Jeevan Mission, to bring tap water to every rural household, was announced by the Prime Minister on Independence Day 2019.

questions.text: New Development Bank (NDB) is a multilateral development bank established in 2014. How many countries are members of NDB?
questions.explanation: The New Development Bank was set up by the five BRICS countries: Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa. They were still its only members in April 2021, when this paper was held; the bank admitted its first new members (the UAE, Uruguay and Bangladesh) in September 2021.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which of the following years was the Supreme Court set up in Calcutta by the East India Company?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 1773, the year of the Regulating Act, which provided for a Supreme Court at Fort William in Calcutta; the court itself was set up under it in 1774.

questions.text: With which of the following banks has the Government of India signed a $500 million project to build safe and green national highway corridors in Rajasthan, Himachal Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh?
questions.explanation: In December 2020 India and the World Bank signed the $500 million Green National Highway Corridors Project for highways in these four states.

questions.text: Who has been nominated as a member on the GAVI Board by the Global Alliance for Vaccines and Immunisation in December 2020?
questions.explanation: Health Minister Harsh Vardhan was nominated to the GAVI Board in December 2020, for the South-East Asia and Western Pacific seat, from January 2021 to December 2023.

questions.text: In which of the following cities was the International Gita Mahotsav held in November-December 2020?
questions.explanation: The International Gita Mahotsav is held every year at Kurukshetra in Haryana, the setting of the Bhagavad Gita.

questions.text: In which of the following states is the Losoong festival celebrated?
questions.explanation: Losoong, the Sikkimese new year, is celebrated in Sikkim at the end of the harvest season.

questions.text: BWF (Badminton World Federation) has imposed a 5-year ban on shuttler Nikita Khakimov on the charges of betting, wagering and irregular match results. He represents which of the following countries?
questions.explanation: In December 2020 the BWF banned the Russian doubles player Nikita Khakimov for five years for betting and match-result offences. (The Court of Arbitration for Sport set the ban aside in November 2021.)

questions.text: Infrared optical ______ can be used for measuring and monitoring temperatures and hot spots of jet engine rotor blades.
questions.explanation: A pyrometer measures high temperatures; an infrared one does so from the heat a body radiates, without touching it. An ammeter measures current, a hygrometer humidity and a machmeter speed relative to that of sound.

questions.text: Which of the following is the full form of ASCII?
options: American Standard Code for Information Interchange
Asian Standard Code for Information Interchange
Analytical Scientific Code for Information Interchange
Analytical Standard Code for Intermitted Information
questions.explanation: ASCII stands for American Standard Code for Information Interchange.

questions.text: Linganamakki Dam is built across which of the following rivers?
questions.explanation: Linganamakki Dam, in Karnataka's Shivamogga district, is built across the Sharavathi river.

questions.text: Trachoma is a preventable disease that results from poor hygiene and sanitation. Which of the following body parts does it affect?
questions.explanation: Trachoma, a bacterial infection spread where hygiene is poor, affects the eyes and can cause blindness.

questions.text: Kolhapur city is located on the banks of which of the following rivers?
questions.explanation: Kolhapur stands on the Panchganga river, a tributary of the Krishna.

questions.text: Who among the following cricketers has won the ’Sir Garfield Sobers Award’ for the ICC Male Cricketer of the Decade and ICC Men’s ODI Cricketer of the Decade Award in December 2020?
questions.explanation: Virat Kohli won both awards in the ICC Awards of the Decade, announced in December 2020.

questions.text: Which of the following state’s government has launched the flagship programme ‘Pedalandariki Illu’ (housing for the poor) scheme in December 2020?
questions.explanation: Navaratnalu-Pedalandariki Illu, Andhra Pradesh's scheme giving house sites and houses to the poor, was launched in December 2020.

questions.text: In which of the following states will the 4th edition of Khelo India Youth Games be held?
questions.explanation: The fourth Khelo India Youth Games were given to Haryana and held there in June 2022, with Panchkula as the main venue.

questions.text: An/A ______ is a finite set of instructions which, when followed, accomplish a particular task.
questions.explanation: An algorithm is a finite sequence of well-defined steps that solves a problem or performs a task.

questions.text: Who among the following rulers inscribed his messages to his subjects and officials on stone surfaces?
questions.explanation: Ashoka had his messages to his subjects and officials inscribed on rocks and pillars across his empire.

questions.text: In which of the following years did the Supreme Court of India come into existence after Independence?
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court of India came into being in January 1950, when the Constitution came into force, replacing the Federal Court.

questions.text: Who among the following has assumed the charge of Director General of the Armed Forces Medical Services on 1 January 2021?
questions.explanation: Surgeon Vice Admiral Rajat Datta took over as Director General Armed Forces Medical Services on 1 January 2021.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Getting butterflies in one's stomach
options: To be very angry with someone
questions.explanation: To have 'butterflies in one's stomach' is to feel nervous and anxious, as before an exam or a performance.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A Herculean task
questions.explanation: A 'Herculean task' needs enormous strength or effort, like the labours of the Greek hero Hercules.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. Dr. Chanda said, “I will definitely write about this case in the medical journal.”
options: Dr. Chanda said that I will definitely write about this case in the medical journal.
Dr. Chanda said that she will definitely write about this case in the medical journal.
Dr. Chanda said that she would definitely write about that case in the medical journal.
Dr. Chanda said that she would definitely be writing about this case in the medical journal.
questions.explanation: In reported speech after 'said', 'I' becomes 'she', 'will' becomes 'would' and 'this' becomes 'that'.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, pick the one that gives their correct order. A. Jody went to the kitchen. B. A pan of milk stood on the kitchen shelf. C. Jody poured some milk into a bowl and held it out to the fawn. D. The fawn followed him.
questions.explanation: Jody goes to the kitchen (A) and the fawn follows 'him' (D); the pan of milk on the shelf (B) comes before Jody pours some of it out for the fawn (C): ADBC.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. HASTE
questions.explanation: 'Haste' is excessive speed or hurry; its opposite is 'delay'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. It was a second hand car but it “hasn't been use” much.
questions.explanation: 'It was' places the sentence in the past, so the passive needs the past perfect and the past participle: 'it hadn't been used much'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. PLUNGE
questions.explanation: To 'plunge' is to fall or drop suddenly; its opposite is to 'rise'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. The medicines have arrived, “isn't it”?
questions.explanation: A positive statement with 'have' takes a negative tag with 'have' and a pronoun for the subject: 'The medicines have arrived, haven't they?'

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'segregate'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Of all the emotions that ______ through me as I stood on the summit of Everest, the dominant one, I think, was humility.
questions.explanation: Emotions 'surge' through a person: they rise and sweep through suddenly and powerfully.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. We had our time of peace and goodwill, a time I will ______ as long as I live.
questions.explanation: To 'cherish' a time is to hold its memory dear, which fits 'as long as I live'.

questions.text: Select the option which means the same as the group of words given. A person who composes the sequence of steps and moves for a dance performance
questions.explanation: A choreographer designs the steps and movements of a dance; a cartographer makes maps and a calligrapher practises decorative handwriting.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. I spotted this clock in a junk shop.
options: This clock has been spotted by me in a junk shop.
A junk shop was spotted in this clock by me.
This clock was spotted by me in a junk shop.
This clock has spotted me in a junk shop.
questions.explanation: The simple past 'spotted' becomes 'was spotted', with 'this clock' as the subject: 'This clock was spotted by me in a junk shop.'

questions.text: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. He part the grass at the place where he had seen the deer.
questions.explanation: The sentence is in the past, as 'had seen' shows, so 'part' must be 'parted': 'He parted the grass at the place where he had seen the deer.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. PROBE
questions.explanation: To 'probe' is to examine or inquire into something closely: to 'investigate' it.

questions.text: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. Bags and purses were thoroughly checking at the entrance to the theatre.
questions.explanation: Bags and purses do not check; they are checked. The passive is needed: 'were thoroughly checked'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. BRACE
questions.explanation: To 'brace' something is to support or strengthen it: to 'fortify' it.

questions.text: Select the option which means the same as the group of words given. Animals that live in water
questions.explanation: 'Aquatic' animals live in water; terrestrial ones live on land, arboreal ones in trees and aerial ones largely in the air.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, pick the one that gives their correct order. A. But Romulous said it should be built on another. B. Remus said the city should be built on one hill. C. However, they quarreled on where to make the city. D. Romulous and Remus went to the hills to build the city of Rome.
questions.explanation: D introduces the brothers and their plan, C says that 'however' they quarrelled over where to build, and B and A give the two sides, with 'But' bringing in the second: DCBA.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Many people believe that animals possess a sixth sense and know (1) ______ the earth is going to shake. Some experts (2) ______ that animals' more acute hearing helps (3) ______ to hear or feel the earth's vibrations. (4) ______ can sense an approaching disaster long before humans (5) ______ what's going on.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 1.
questions.explanation: Animals are said to know 'when' the earth is going to shake: the time of the earthquake.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Many people believe that animals possess a sixth sense and know (1) ______ the earth is going to shake. Some experts (2) ______ that animals' more acute hearing helps (3) ______ to hear or feel the earth's vibrations. (4) ______ can sense an approaching disaster long before humans (5) ______ what's going on.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 2.
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'some experts' takes the simple present 'believe', matching 'Many people believe' earlier.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Many people believe that animals possess a sixth sense and know (1) ______ the earth is going to shake. Some experts (2) ______ that animals' more acute hearing helps (3) ______ to hear or feel the earth's vibrations. (4) ______ can sense an approaching disaster long before humans (5) ______ what's going on.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 3.
questions.explanation: Their hearing helps the animals, so the object pronoun 'them' is needed.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Many people believe that animals possess a sixth sense and know (1) ______ the earth is going to shake. Some experts (2) ______ that animals' more acute hearing helps (3) ______ to hear or feel the earth's vibrations. (4) ______ can sense an approaching disaster long before humans (5) ______ what's going on.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 4.
questions.explanation: The subject pronoun 'They' refers back to the animals.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Many people believe that animals possess a sixth sense and know (1) ______ the earth is going to shake. Some experts (2) ______ that animals' more acute hearing helps (3) ______ to hear or feel the earth's vibrations. (4) ______ can sense an approaching disaster long before humans (5) ______ what's going on.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 5.
questions.explanation: Animals sense the disaster long before humans 'realise', that is become aware of, what is going on.

questions.text: Select the option in which the words share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of words. Butcher : Knife
questions.explanation: A butcher works with a knife, as a teacher works with chalk. A hairdresser uses scissors, not a hammer, and a carpenter a chisel, not scissors.

questions.text: In a certain code language, IMPUDENT is written as PFXMHAWK. How will ABNORMAL be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters are taken in pairs, each pair is swapped, and then the first letter moves 3 forward and the second 3 back: IM → MI → PF, PU → UP → XM, DE → ED → HA, NT → TN → WK. So AB → BA → EX, NO → ON → RK, RM → MR → PO and AL → LA → OX: EXRKPOOX.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term. MONKEY : XDJMNL : : TIGER : ?
questions.explanation: MONKEY is written backwards (YEKNOM) with each letter moved one place back: XDJMNL. TIGER backwards is REGIT, which becomes QDFHS.

questions.text: Four letter-clusters have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the letter-cluster that is different.
questions.explanation: In SWDZ, FJQM and GKPL the second and third letters are opposites in the alphabet (W and D, J and Q, K and P: their places add up to 27). In RVGC, V and G are not (the opposite of V is E), so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Select the correct option that indicates the arrangement of the given words in the order in which they appear in an English dictionary. 1. Misappropriate 2. Misbehave 3. Microorganism 4. Miscellaneous 5. Mineralize
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Microorganism (3), Mineralize (5), Misappropriate (1), Misbehave (2), Miscellaneous (4). 'Mic' comes before 'Min' and 'Mis', and 'Misa' before 'Misb' and 'Misc'.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. Death : Accident : : Starvation : ?
questions.explanation: An accident can cause death, as a hunger strike can cause starvation.

questions.text: Four words have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the word that is different.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'Slavery': choice, autonomy and convenience all let people act as they wish, and slavery takes that away. ('Convenience', the only word not directly about freedom, could also be argued.)

questions.text: Four numbers have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the number that is different.
questions.explanation: The digits of 3437, 7415 and 5453 add up to 17 (3 + 4 + 3 + 7, 7 + 4 + 1 + 5, 5 + 4 + 5 + 3). Those of 7437 add up to 21, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 3, 7, 13, 25, 47, 83, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 4, 6, 12, 22, 36, and they grow by 2, 6, 10, 14, each 4 more than the last. The next growth is 18, so the next difference is 54: 83 + 54 = 137.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All balls are fans. No fan is a player. Some players are wickets. Conclusions: I. Some players are fans. II. Some wickets are balls. III. Some fans are balls.
options: Both conclusions II and III follow
questions.explanation: All balls are fans, so some fans are balls (III). No fan is a player, so I is false. Wickets that are players cannot be balls, and nothing links the other wickets to balls, so II need not follow.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the following equation correct? 13 × 2 − (8 ÷ 4) + (4 × 1) = 24
questions.explanation: After interchanging + and −: 13 × 2 + (8 ÷ 4) − (4 × 1) = 26 + 2 − 4 = 24.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (7, 12, 18)
questions.explanation: The third number is the sum of the first two minus 1: 7 + 12 − 1 = 18. Likewise 8 + 14 − 1 = 21; the other sets fail (6 + 12 − 1 = 17, 4 + 6 − 1 = 9, 5 + 9 − 1 = 13).

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number. 8 : 69 : : 7 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is the square of the first plus 5: 8² + 5 = 69. Likewise 7² + 5 = 54.

questions.text: Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it. 4 10 16; 6 4 13; 8 ? 26
questions.explanation: In each row the third number is the first, plus half the first, plus the second: 4 + 2 + 10 = 16 and 6 + 3 + 4 = 13. So 8 + 4 + ? = 26 gives ? = 14.

questions.text: 2 train tickets from Mohali to Delhi and 3 tickets from Mohali to Jammu cost ₹800. But 3 tickets from Mohali to Delhi and 2 tickets from Mohali to Jammu cost ₹700. What are the ticket prices for Delhi and Jammu, respectively, from Mohali?
questions.explanation: With D and J the fares to Delhi and Jammu: 2D + 3J = 800 and 3D + 2J = 700. Adding, 5(D + J) = 1500, so D + J = 300; subtracting, J − D = 100. So D = ₹100 and J = ₹200.

questions.text: U's daughter, X, is the daughter-in-law of V. W is the son of V's daughter. How is W related to X?
questions.explanation: X, U's daughter, is married to V's son. W is the son of V's daughter, that is of X's husband's sister, so W is X's nephew.

questions.text: In a certain code language, INHALE is coded as 110 and DELAY is coded as 86. How will IGNORE be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Taking A = 25, B = 24, … Z = 0, the letter values are added and 3 is added to the total: INHALE gives 107 + 3 = 110 and DELAY 83 + 3 = 86. IGNORE gives 17 + 19 + 12 + 11 + 8 + 21 = 88, and 88 + 3 = 91.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series. h _ c g _ h k _ g l _ k c _ l
questions.explanation: With k, l, c, h, g in the blanks the block hkcgl repeats: hkcgl hkcgl hkcgl.

questions.text: A ______ is a computer programme which can self-replicate and propagate over the network with or without human intervention and has malicious intent.
questions.explanation: A worm copies itself and spreads across a network on its own, without attaching to a host program; a virus needs a host file and usually a user's action to spread.

questions.text: A government budget is an annual financial statement which outlines estimated government expenditures and expected government receipts or revenues for the forthcoming fiscal year. Depending on the feasibility of these estimates which of the following is NOT the budget type?
questions.explanation: A budget is balanced (receipts equal expenditure), surplus (receipts exceed expenditure) or deficit (expenditure exceeds receipts). There is no 'economy budget'.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: When did the peasant movement in Bardoli begin?
questions.explanation: The Bardoli Satyagraha, a no-tax campaign by the peasants of Bardoli in Gujarat against a steep rise in land revenue, began in 1928 under Vallabhbhai Patel, who earned the title 'Sardar' there.

questions.text: On which of the following dates is the Good Governance Day observed in India every year?
questions.explanation: Good Governance Day is observed on 25 December, the birthday of former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee.

questions.text: ICAR is an autonomous body responsible for coordinating agriculture and research in India. What is the full form of ICAR?
options: Indian Centre of Agriculture and Research
questions.explanation: ICAR is the Indian Council of Agricultural Research, set up in 1929, with its headquarters in New Delhi.

questions.text: Where has Kiren Rijiju, Union Minister for Youth and Sports, launched the Assam Rifles Public School as the first sports school announced under Khelo India Scheme?
questions.explanation: In January 2021 Kiren Rijiju launched the Assam Rifles Public School in Shillong, Meghalaya, as a Khelo India sports school, the first in the North East.

questions.text: Where did Union Minister of Earth Sciences Dr. Harsh Vardhan virtually inaugurate India’s highest Meteorological Centre?
questions.explanation: On 29 December 2020 Dr Harsh Vardhan virtually inaugurated the Meteorological Centre at Leh, Ladakh: at about 3,500 m, India's highest.

questions.text: ______ is a set of norms and guidelines to be followed by the political parties and contesting candidates during election time.
questions.explanation: The Model Code of Conduct, issued by the Election Commission, sets out the norms that parties and candidates must follow during elections.

questions.text: Pt. Satish Vyas was conferred upon the prestigious Tansen Samman in December 2020. He was associated with which of the following musical instruments?
questions.explanation: Pandit Satish Vyas, a santoor player and disciple of Pandit Shivkumar Sharma, received Madhya Pradesh's Tansen Samman for 2020 at Gwalior in December 2020.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a good conductor of electricity?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives diamond, an insulator: all its carbon atoms' outer electrons are held in bonds, whereas graphite, another form of carbon, and gold conduct well. (Soil conducts far less well than a metal, but moist soil conducts enough to be used for earthing.)

questions.text: Who among the following Sikh Gurus laid the foundation of ‘Khalsa Panth’?
questions.explanation: Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Sikh Guru, founded the Khalsa at Anandpur Sahib on Baisakhi day in 1699.

questions.text: Who among the following has been awarded the Bharathi award 2020?
questions.explanation: Seeni Viswanathan, a scholar who has collected and published the complete works of the Tamil poet Subramania Bharati, received the Bharathi Award 2020 from the Vanavil Cultural Centre in December 2020.

questions.text: Who among the following has become the Chief Justice of Orissa High Court in January 2021?
questions.explanation: Justice S Muralidhar, earlier of the Punjab and Haryana High Court, was sworn in as Chief Justice of the Orissa High Court on 4 January 2021.

questions.text: Which of the following rivers does NOT culminate in the Arabian Sea?
questions.explanation: The Godavari flows east across the Deccan into the Bay of Bengal. The Sabarmati, the Tapti and the Indus empty into the Arabian Sea.

questions.text: Big Bang theory explains:
questions.explanation: The Big Bang theory explains how the universe began, expanding from an extremely hot, dense state; stars, galaxies and the solar system formed much later within it.

questions.text: Who among the following is the brand ambassador of Equitas Small Finance Bank (ESFB)?
questions.explanation: Equitas Small Finance Bank named the India cricketer Smriti Mandhana its brand ambassador in November 2020.

questions.text: Who among the following women cricketers has won the ICC Associate Player of the Decade award in 2020?
questions.explanation: Scotland's Kathryn Bryce was named the ICC Women's Associate Cricketer of the Decade in December 2020; her sister Sarah was also shortlisted.

questions.text: ______ are built up by the liquid and solid rock erupting from the earth’s interior.
questions.explanation: Volcanoes are built up from lava and fragments of rock thrown out from the earth's interior. Fault-block mountains are raised by faulting, and erosional mountains are what erosion leaves behind.

questions.text: Amino acids are often referred to as the building blocks of ______.
questions.explanation: Proteins are long chains of amino acids joined by peptide bonds.

questions.text: Hampi was declared as a World Heritage Site by UNESCO in which of the following years?
questions.explanation: The Group of Monuments at Hampi, the Vijayanagara capital in Karnataka, was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.

questions.text: Who has become the new chief of the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) in January 2021?
questions.explanation: Subodh Kumar Jaiswal, earlier Maharashtra's Director General of Police, took charge as Director General of the CISF in January 2021.

questions.text: A User Interface is the part of ______ that allows the user to enter and receive information.
questions.explanation: The operating system provides the user interface, command-line or graphical, through which a user gives commands and receives output.

questions.text: The world’s oldest first-class cricketer and World War II veteran, Alan Burgess passed away in January 2021. He represented which of the following countries?
questions.explanation: Alan Burgess, who played first-class cricket for Canterbury in New Zealand and served in Egypt and Italy in the Second World War, died on 6 January 2021 aged 100.

questions.text: On which of the following idols of Hindu mythology has Italian screenwriter-film producer Alfredo Covelli authored ‘Vahana Masterclass’, a book for kids?
questions.explanation: Alfredo Covelli's 'Vahana Masterclass' tells of four young mice trained to succeed Mooshika as the vahana, or mount, of Lord Ganesha.

questions.text: Which type of dam is a temporary dam constructed to exclude water from the specific area?
questions.explanation: A cofferdam is a temporary enclosure built to keep water out of an area, so that work such as laying a dam's or a bridge's foundations can be done in the dry.
