Mother told Megha to leave for your office now.
questions.explanation: An order is reported with 'told' + object + 'to'-infinitive; 'your' becomes 'her' and 'now' becomes 'then'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. I have always enjoyed flying. I wasn't afraid (1) ______my mother and I boarded LANSA Airlines flight 508. Some people had (2) ______ flying LANSA because of a recent crash. But (3) ______and I had a good reason for flying: I had just (4) ______secondary school in Lima, and we wanted to (5) ______Christmas with my father in our jungle hut.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 1.
questions.explanation: 'I wasn't afraid when my mother and I boarded': 'when' marks the time.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. I have always enjoyed flying. I wasn't afraid (1) ______my mother and I boarded LANSA Airlines flight 508. Some people had (2) ______ flying LANSA because of a recent crash. But (3) ______and I had a good reason for flying: I had just (4) ______secondary school in Lima, and we wanted to (5) ______Christmas with my father in our jungle hut.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 2.
questions.explanation: To 'give up' something is to stop doing it: some people had stopped flying LANSA after a recent crash.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. I have always enjoyed flying. I wasn't afraid (1) ______my mother and I boarded LANSA Airlines flight 508. Some people had (2) ______ flying LANSA because of a recent crash. But (3) ______and I had a good reason for flying: I had just (4) ______secondary school in Lima, and we wanted to (5) ______Christmas with my father in our jungle hut.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 3.
questions.explanation: The narrator is flying with her mother: 'But mother and I had a good reason for flying'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. I have always enjoyed flying. I wasn't afraid (1) ______my mother and I boarded LANSA Airlines flight 508. Some people had (2) ______ flying LANSA because of a recent crash. But (3) ______and I had a good reason for flying: I had just (4) ______secondary school in Lima, and we wanted to (5) ______Christmas with my father in our jungle hut.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 4.
questions.explanation: 'Had just finished secondary school': the past perfect needs the past participle 'finished'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. I have always enjoyed flying. I wasn't afraid (1) ______my mother and I boarded LANSA Airlines flight 508. Some people had (2) ______ flying LANSA because of a recent crash. But (3) ______and I had a good reason for flying: I had just (4) ______secondary school in Lima, and we wanted to (5) ______Christmas with my father in our jungle hut.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 5.
questions.explanation: To 'spend Christmas' with someone is to pass the holiday with them.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (23, 4, 92)
Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term. Indonesia : Jakarta : : Canada : ?
questions.explanation: Jakarta is the capital of Indonesia; Ottawa is the capital of Canada.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that, when placed from left to right in the blanks below, will complete the letter sequence correctly. Q _ _ R R K Z _ _ K Z R T _ _ R
options: K Z R S K Z
Q Z R S P R
K Z R P R Z
K Z R S Z T
questions.explanation: With K Z R S K Z in the blanks the series reads QKZR RKZR SKZR TKZR: the first letter runs Q, R, S, T and KZR follows each.

questions.text: In a certain code language, PROFANE is written as KOLCZKV. How will DISOBEY be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Letters in odd places are replaced by their opposites in the alphabet (P → K, O → L, A → Z, E → V) and letters in even places move 3 back (R → O, F → C, N → K). DISOBEY: D → W, I → F, S → H, O → L, B → Y, E → B, Y → B: WFHLYBB.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of numbers. 18 : 42
Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. {5, 15, 20}
questions.explanation: The three numbers add up to 40: 5 + 15 + 20 = 40 and 10 + 13 + 17 = 40. The other sets add up to 50, 42 and 42.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All combs are scales. Some routers are combs. All gloves are routers. Conclusions: I. All gloves are scales. II. Some gloves are scales. III. Some scales are routers. IV. All routers are scales.
options: Both conclusions I and III follow.
questions.explanation: Some routers are combs and all combs are scales, so some routers are scales, that is, some scales are routers (III). The gloves are routers, but not necessarily ones that are combs, so neither I nor II follows; nor does IV.

questions.text: Select the correct option that indicates the arrangement of the given places in a logical and meaningful order. 1. Hyderabad 2. Nagpur 3. Dehradun 4. Bhopal 5. Madurai 6. Agra
questions.explanation: From north to south: Dehradun, Agra, Bhopal, Nagpur, Hyderabad, Madurai (3, 6, 4, 2, 1, 5).

questions.text: Four letter-clusters have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the letter-cluster that is different.
questions.explanation: In DJWQ, CGXT and HDSW the first and third letters are opposites in the alphabet (their positions add up to 27), as are the second and fourth: D/W and J/Q, C/X and G/T, H/S and D/W. In GBTV, G and T are opposites but B (2) and V (22) are not.

questions.text: Select the option in which the words share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of words. Car : Truck
questions.explanation: A car and a truck are both road vehicles, the truck the larger, built to carry more; a chair and a bench are both seats, the bench the larger, seating several people.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs that can sequentially replace the * signs and balance the given equation. 216 * 6 * 8 * 64 * 48 = 500
Four words have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the word that is different.
questions.explanation: 'Gorgeous', 'exalted' and 'august' are words of praise (beautiful, high in rank, inspiring respect); 'ridiculous', deserving mockery, is not.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 4, 7, 11, 17, 27, 45, ?
questions.explanation: The differences 3, 4, 6, 10, 18 themselves grow by 1, 2, 4, 8, so the next difference is 18 + 16 = 34: 45 + 34 = 79.

questions.text: Pointing to the photograph of a lady, Sukanya said, "Her son's son is the brother of my daughter's sister." How is the lady related to Sukanya?
questions.explanation: The brother of Sukanya's daughter's sister is Sukanya's son. He is the lady's son's son, so the lady's son is Sukanya's husband and the lady is her mother-in-law.

questions.text: Krishna gave 1/9 of his savings to his son, 3/4 of the remaining to his first daughter, and the rest to his second daughter. If the first daughter received ₹880 more than the second one, how much did the son get?
questions.explanation: The first daughter gets 3/4 × 8/9 = 2/3 of the savings and the second 1/4 × 8/9 = 2/9. The difference, 4/9 of the savings, is ₹880, so the savings are ₹1,980 and the son's 1/9 is ₹220.

questions.text: In a certain code language, MACHINE is coded as 5861944. How will STORK be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite in the alphabet, whose position is then added up to a single digit: M → N (14) → 5, A → Z (26) → 8, C → X (24) → 6, H → S (19 → 10) → 1, I → R (18) → 9, N → M (13) → 4, E → V (22) → 4. STORK: H (8), G (7), L (12) → 3, I (9), P (16) → 7: 87397.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term. SACRED : VXEPIZ : : WINTER : ?
questions.explanation: The letters move +3, −3, +2, −2, +4, −4, wrapping round: S → V, A → X, C → E, R → P, E → I, D → Z. WINTER: W → Z, I → F, N → P, T → R, E → I, R → N: ZFPRIN.

questions.text: Four numbers have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the number that is different.
questions.explanation: 678, 234 and 345 are three consecutive digits; 589 is not.

questions.text: The Innovation Festival 2020 was celebrated in which of the following Indian cities?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Itanagar, where Arunachal Pradesh held its first Innovation Festival in January 2020.

questions.text: Laokhowa Wildlife Sanctuary lies on the southern bank of which river in the north-eastern states of India?
questions.explanation: Laokhowa Wildlife Sanctuary, in Assam's Nagaon district, lies on the southern bank of the Brahmaputra.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The second Round Table Conference was held in 1931 in which of the following countries?
questions.explanation: The Second Round Table Conference was held in London in 1931; Gandhi attended it for the Congress.

questions.text: A ______ is an ordered list in which all insertions and deletions are made at one end.
questions.explanation: A stack is a last-in, first-out list in which items are added and removed only at one end, the top; a queue adds at the rear and removes at the front.

questions.text: Which of the following animals is made to race in the traditional sport called 'Kambala' in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Kambala is a buffalo race run in slushy paddy fields in coastal Karnataka.

questions.text: Who among the following is the Chief Election Commissioner of India as of January 2021?
questions.explanation: Sunil Arora was Chief Election Commissioner from December 2018 to April 2021.

questions.text: Who among the following cricketers has won the ICC Spirit of Cricket Award 2020?
questions.explanation: MS Dhoni received the ICC Spirit of Cricket Award of the Decade, announced in December 2020, for recalling Ian Bell after a run-out at Trent Bridge in 2011.

questions.text: Lionel Messi, one of the winners of the ‘Laurel Sportsman of the Year 2020’, plays football for:
questions.explanation: Lionel Messi, who shared the Laureus World Sportsman of the Year award for 2020 with Lewis Hamilton, plays for Argentina.

questions.text: In February 2020, the Kerala Chief Minister launched a mobile application named 'Yodhavu' (Warrior). The purpose of this application is combating:
questions.explanation: Kerala's 'Yodhavu' app, launched in Kochi in February 2020, lets the public tell the police about drug abuse and drug dealing, with the informer's identity kept secret.

questions.text: Which of the following satellites is India’s first Earth imaging satellite in a geostationary orbit?
questions.explanation: ISRO's GISAT-1 (Geo Imaging Satellite-1) was built as India's first Earth-observation satellite for geostationary orbit, to watch the country continuously.

questions.text: As of 30 April 2020, the annual entitlement to eligible farmers under the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) scheme was:
questions.explanation: PM-KISAN pays eligible farmers ₹6,000 a year in three instalments of ₹2,000.

questions.text: Indian athlete Joshna Chinappa represents the country in:
questions.explanation: Joshna Chinappa is one of India's leading squash players.

questions.text: Which scientific instrument is used to measure the height of an aircraft above a fixed level?
questions.explanation: An altimeter measures altitude, the height above a fixed level such as the sea; a fathometer measures the depth of water and a barometer air pressure.

questions.text: Who among the following has become the youngest Mayor of Thiruvananthapuram Corporation, Kerala, in December 2020?
questions.explanation: Arya Rajendran became Mayor of Thiruvananthapuram in December 2020 at 21, the youngest mayor in India.

questions.text: In which of the following years was ADB (Asian Development Bank) established?
questions.explanation: The Asian Development Bank was established in 1966, with its headquarters in Manila.

questions.text: Who among the following won the ‘EY Entrepreneur of the Year 2019’ award?
questions.explanation: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw, founder of Biocon, was named EY Entrepreneur of the Year India 2019 in February 2020.

questions.text: ______ is the application of plant and soil science to crop production.
questions.explanation: Agronomy is the science of soil management and crop production; agrostology is the study of grasses and bryology that of mosses.

questions.text: Who among the following sultans of the Delhi Sultanate appointed Ghiyasuddin Balban as his/her Prime Minister?
questions.explanation: Nasiruddin Mahmud (1246-1266) made Balban his naib, the deputy who ran the government; Balban succeeded him as sultan.

questions.text: As of 30 April 2020, who among the following was the Chairman of the Eastern Zonal Council?
questions.explanation: The Union Home Minister chairs each Zonal Council; on 30 April 2020 that was Amit Shah.

questions.text: Which of the following Indian cities hosted the 13th Session of the Conference of Parties to the Convention on the Conservation of Migratory Species of Wild Animals (CMS COP 13)?
questions.explanation: The 13th Conference of the Parties to the CMS (COP 13) was held at Gandhinagar, Gujarat, in February 2020.

questions.text: Which of the following chemicals is responsible for the yellow colour in urine?
questions.explanation: Urobilin (urochrome), formed from the breakdown of bilirubin, gives urine its yellow colour.

questions.text: Which of the following species was among the species classified as ‘endangered migratory species’ by the UN's Convention on Conservation of Migratory Species in February 2020?
questions.explanation: At CMS COP 13 in February 2020 the Bengal Florican, the Great Indian Bustard and the Asian Elephant were added to Appendix I, the list of endangered migratory species.

questions.text: Who among the following is the author of the book ‘40 years with Abdul Kalam - Untold Stories’?
questions.explanation: '40 Years with Abdul Kalam: Untold Stories' (2020) is by A. Sivathanu Pillai, who worked with Kalam at ISRO and DRDO and was the founding chief of BrahMos Aerospace.

questions.text: Which of the following states has a marine sanctuary called Gahirmatha Marine Sanctuary?
questions.explanation: Gahirmatha Marine Sanctuary, on the Odisha coast, is a major nesting ground of olive ridley turtles.

questions.text: While working in MS Office software, which of the following commands will you give on a US keyboard layout to undo the previous action?
questions.explanation: Ctrl + Z undoes the last action; Ctrl + N opens a new document, Ctrl + U underlines and Ctrl + C copies.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. A place where coins are manufactured
questions.explanation: A mint is a place where a country's coins are made.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To run around like a headless chicken
options: To do things methodically one by one
To be lazy and unwilling to work
To do many things in a disorganised manner
To be unable to catch escaping chicken
questions.explanation: To 'run around like a headless chicken' is to rush about frantically, doing many things without order or purpose.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. He was not ready at first to come with us for the picnic but we ______him.
questions.explanation: He was not ready at first, but we 'persuaded' him: we talked him into coming.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. CONDESCENSION
questions.explanation: 'Condescension' is a patronising air of superiority; of the options, 'disdain' is closest.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'maintenance'.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. The Indian government has introduced a ban on spitting in public.
options: A ban on spitting in public has been introduced by the Indian government.
The ban on spitting had been introduced by the Indian government.
The ban on spitting was being introduced by the Indian government.
The Indian government had introduced a ban on spitting in public places.
questions.explanation: The present perfect 'has introduced' becomes 'has been introduced', with the object 'a ban on spitting in public' as the new subject.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. The policeman said to the Inspector, "I arrested a man who broke the window of a car."
options: The policeman told the inspector that he had arrested a man who broke the window of a car.
The policeman told the inspector that he arrested a man who broke the window of a car.
The policeman told the inspector that he had arrested a man who had broken the window of a car.
The policeman told the inspector that I arrested a man who broke the window of a car.
questions.explanation: 'Said to' becomes 'told', 'I' becomes 'he', and both past-tense verbs move back to the past perfect: 'arrested' to 'had arrested' and 'broke' to 'had broken'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Courts help in the resolution of ______ issues.
questions.explanation: 'Contentious' issues are those that cause disagreement, which courts settle. 'Conscientious' (careful) and 'contemptuous' (scornful) only look alike.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. INNOCUOUS
questions.explanation: 'Innocuous' means harmless; its opposite is 'harmful'.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order. A.They made fruit mash for me. B. They extracted 30 worms from my wounds on my legs and arms. C. But I was unable to eat. D. They washed me with salt water and bandaged my wounds after putting a lotion on them.
questions.explanation: First the worms were removed (B), then the wounds were washed and bandaged (D); the fruit mash came next (A), 'but' the writer could not eat it (C): BDAC.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. “I wrote a novel” for the last two years but it is not finished yet.
options: I have been writing a novel
questions.explanation: An action that began in the past and is still going on ('for the last two years', 'not finished yet') takes the present perfect continuous: 'I have been writing a novel'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. SEVERE
questions.explanation: 'Severe' means harsh or extreme; its opposite is 'mild'.

questions.text: Examine the four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, pick the one that gives their correct order. A. Some Europeans demand that Europe slam its gates. B. Today more and more humans are crossing more and more borders in search of a job. C. Nowhere is it more apparent than in Europe. D. But others call for opening the gates wider.
questions.explanation: B states the general trend, C says it is most apparent in Europe, and A and D give the two opposite European responses, 'some' and 'but others': BCAD.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To leave no stone unturned
options: To try everything possible to solve a problem
To become accustomed to routine things
questions.explanation: To 'leave no stone unturned' is to try every possible means to find or achieve something.

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. Participating in the Republic Day Parade are considered an honour by many people.
questions.explanation: A gerund phrase as subject takes a singular verb: 'Participating in the Republic Day Parade is considered an honour'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined segment in the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement' How much does it cost to “travels” from the airport to Noida?
questions.explanation: 'To' before a verb takes its base form: 'to travel'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. ATTRACT
questions.explanation: To 'attract' is to draw someone's interest: to 'fascinate'.

questions.text: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. I think someone has been picked my pocket while I was travelling in the metro.
options: someone has been picked my pocket
questions.explanation: 'Someone' is the doer, so the verb must be active, not the passive 'has been picked': 'someone picked my pocket while I was travelling'.

questions.text: Select the option which means the same as the group of words given. A person authorised to examine and verify accounts
questions.explanation: An auditor examines and verifies an organisation's accounts.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Graduation Day was at hand. Primary school graduation (1) ______ in those days followed a prescribed order-conventional, courteous and (2) ______. First the school principal made a long speech (3) ______ encouragement and blessing for the future of the graduates. (4) ______ one of the representatives of the graduating class (5) ______ with a vote of thanks.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 1.
questions.explanation: The events are graduation 'ceremonies', the plural subject of 'followed'; 'ceremonials' are formal rites rather than the occasions, 'ceremonially' is an adverb and 'ceremonious' an adjective.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Graduation Day was at hand. Primary school graduation (1) ______ in those days followed a prescribed order-conventional, courteous and (2) ______. First the school principal made a long speech (3) ______ encouragement and blessing for the future of the graduates. (4) ______ one of the representatives of the graduating class (5) ______ with a vote of thanks.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 2.
questions.explanation: An adjective completes the list 'conventional, courteous and ...': 'sentimental'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Graduation Day was at hand. Primary school graduation (1) ______ in those days followed a prescribed order-conventional, courteous and (2) ______. First the school principal made a long speech (3) ______ encouragement and blessing for the future of the graduates. (4) ______ one of the representatives of the graduating class (5) ______ with a vote of thanks.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 3.
questions.explanation: A speech 'of' encouragement and blessing: 'of' links the speech to what it contains.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Graduation Day was at hand. Primary school graduation (1) ______ in those days followed a prescribed order-conventional, courteous and (2) ______. First the school principal made a long speech (3) ______ encouragement and blessing for the future of the graduates. (4) ______ one of the representatives of the graduating class (5) ______ with a vote of thanks.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 4.
questions.explanation: 'Then' moves the account on to the next part of the ceremony, after the principal's speech.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Graduation Day was at hand. Primary school graduation (1) ______ in those days followed a prescribed order-conventional, courteous and (2) ______. First the school principal made a long speech (3) ______ encouragement and blessing for the future of the graduates. (4) ______ one of the representatives of the graduating class (5) ______ with a vote of thanks.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 5.
questions.explanation: The passage is in the past tense: the representative 'responded' with a vote of thanks.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number. 256 : 13 : : 676 : ?
Select the option in which the words share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of words. Pullover : Wool
questions.explanation: A pullover is made of wool, as a prism is made of glass.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some men are athletes. No athlete is a singer. All singers are dancers. Conclusions: I. No dancer is an athlete. II. Some singers are men. III. Some men are dancers.
options: Only conclusions II and III follow .
questions.explanation: All singers are dancers, but nothing links singers or dancers to men, so II and III need not follow. Dancers who are not singers may still be athletes, so I need not follow either.

questions.text: Select the correct option that indicates the arrangement of the given words in the order in which they appear in an English dictionary. 1. Certificate 2. Cerebellum 3. Cervical 4. Ceremonious 5. Certainty
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Cerebellum (2), Ceremonious (4), Certainty (5), Certificate (1), Cervical (3). 'Cereb' comes before 'Cerem', 'Cere' before 'Cert', 'Certa' before 'Certi', and 'Cert' before 'Cerv'.

questions.text: Four words have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the word that is different.
questions.explanation: A minister, a mayor and a speaker hold political offices, in a government, a city corporation and a legislature. A director runs a company or makes a film, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Four letter-clusters have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the letter-cluster that is different.
questions.explanation: In FBDX, HDFZ and TPRL the letters move −4, +2, −6 (F → B → D → X, wrapping round from A to Z). SNPJ moves −5, +2, −6, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. {22, 17, 31}
questions.explanation: The second number is the first minus 5 and the third is the first plus 9: 22 − 5 = 17 and 22 + 9 = 31. Likewise 31 − 5 = 26 and 31 + 9 = 40.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the following equation correct? 14 + 12 × 18 ÷ 6 – 12 = 6

‘A + B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’. ‘A – B’ means ‘A is the daughter of B’. ‘A × B’ means ‘A is the sister of B’. ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’. If P ÷ M × R – Z + Q, then how is P related to Q?
questions.explanation: P is the brother of M, M is the sister of R, R is the daughter of Z and Z is the wife of Q. So P, M and R are children of Q, and P, being male, is Q's son.

questions.text: From the given options choose the one in which the set of numbers do not follow the same Logic/Rule/Relation as the numbers given in below set. (12, 36, 132)
questions.explanation: In each set the second number is 3 times the first and the third 11 times the first: 12 × 3 = 36 and 12 × 11 = 132. In (18, 54, 196) the third should be 18 × 11 = 198.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. MORV : NJGE : : DGKP : ?
questions.explanation: The positions of matching letters add up to 27, 25, 25, 27: M (13) + N (14), O (15) + J (10), R (18) + G (7), V (22) + E (5). Likewise D (4) → W (23), G (7) → R (18), K (11) → N (14) and P (16) → K (11): WRNK.

questions.text: Four numbers have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the number that is different.
questions.explanation: 4095 = 2¹² − 1, 255 = 2⁸ − 1 and 127 = 2⁷ − 1: each is one less than a power of 2. 1049 is not (2¹⁰ − 1 = 1023).

questions.text: In a certain code language, ROCKET is written as BNQSDJ. How will NOTICE be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each half of the word is written backwards with every letter moved one place back: ROC → QNB → BNQ and KET → JDS → SDJ. So NOT → MNS → SNM and ICE → HBD → DBH: SNMDBH.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series. K O _ M C L _ Q M C M O _ M _ N O Q _ C
questions.explanation: With Q, O, Q, C, M in the blanks the series reads KOQMC LOQMC MOQMC NOQMC: the first letter moves K, L, M, N and OQMC repeats.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 1, 2, 6, 21, ?, 445
questions.explanation: Each term is the one before times n, plus n, for n = 1, 2, 3, …: 1 × 1 + 1 = 2, 2 × 2 + 2 = 6, 6 × 3 + 3 = 21, 21 × 4 + 4 = 88 and 88 × 5 + 5 = 445.

questions.text: In a certain code language, REFUSAL is coded as 100 and SHORTEN is coded as 83. How will INERTIA be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is worth 26 minus its place in the alphabet (A = 25, … Z = 0) and the values are added. REFUSAL's places add to 82, so 7 × 26 − 82 = 100; SHORTEN's add to 99, giving 182 − 99 = 83. INERTIA's add to 76, so it is 182 − 76 = 106.

questions.text: An online entrance exam was conducted in 250 centres all over a country. The average number of applicants per centre was found to be 1250. However, it was later realised that in one centre, the number of applicants was counted as 1758 instead of 1658. What was the correct average number of applicants per centre?
questions.explanation: The total was overstated by 1758 − 1658 = 100, so the average falls by 100 ÷ 250 = 0.4: 1250 − 0.4 = 1249.6.

questions.text: ‘War’ is related to ‘Destruction’ in the same way as ‘Cyclone’ is related to ‘______’.
questions.explanation: War causes destruction, as a cyclone causes devastation. Storm, wind and hurricane are kinds of weather, not results of a cyclone.

questions.text: On which river is the Peacock Island located?
questions.explanation: Umananda, called Peacock Island by the British, lies in the Brahmaputra at Guwahati, Assam.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following was a leader who led a revolt against the British rule from North East India?
questions.explanation: Rani Gaidinliu, a Naga leader from Manipur, led a revolt against British rule as a young woman and was imprisoned in 1932. Pritilata Waddedar, Matangini Hazra and Durgawati Devi were freedom fighters from outside the North East.

questions.text: In which state is India’s least densely populated district Dibang Valley located as per Census 2011?
questions.explanation: Dibang Valley in Arunachal Pradesh had the lowest population density of any district in Census 2011, about 1 person per km².

questions.text: Which Indian actor got the Best Actor Award at Indo-German Film Week in 2020?
questions.explanation: Adil Hussain won the Best Actor award at the Indo-German Film Week in Berlin in 2020.

questions.text: In which of the following cities is the headquarters of All India Chess Federation situated?
questions.explanation: The All India Chess Federation has its headquarters in Chennai.

questions.text: Who among the following is the President of FICCI (Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry) for the year 2020-21?
questions.explanation: Uday Shankar took over as FICCI President for 2020-21 in December 2020, succeeding Sangita Reddy.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which of the following years was the Diwani of Bengal transferred to the East India Company?
questions.explanation: By the Treaty of Allahabad in 1765 Shah Alam II granted the East India Company the Diwani (the right to collect revenue) of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.

questions.text: Wavel Ramkalawan, an Indian origin has been elected as the President of which of the following countries?
questions.explanation: Wavel Ramkalawan, of Indian origin, was elected President of Seychelles in October 2020.

questions.text: ______ is the easy way to check your favourite websites for updates without having to visit them all.
questions.explanation: RSS (Really Simple Syndication) feeds let a feed reader collect new posts from the websites a user follows, so they can be checked in one place without visiting each site.

questions.text: Alaknanda river originates from ______ and Bhagirathi Kharak glacier.
questions.explanation: The Alaknanda rises from the Satopanth and Bhagirath Kharak glaciers in Uttarakhand.

questions.text: Who among the following was the winner of the Senior National Billiards Championship 2020?
questions.explanation: Pankaj Advani won the Senior National Billiards title in January 2020, beating Sourav Kothari 5-2 in the final at Pune.

questions.text: How many members are nominated by the President in the Rajya Sabha?
questions.explanation: Under Article 80 the President nominates 12 members of the Rajya Sabha for their special knowledge of literature, science, art and social service.

questions.text: In which of the following Tiger Reserves of India, is its first hot air balloon wildlife safari launched in December 2020?
questions.explanation: India's first hot air balloon safari in a tiger reserve was launched at Bandhavgarh, Madhya Pradesh, on 25 December 2020.

questions.text: Indian-origin global health expert ______ was appointed as the first Chief Executive Officer of The WHO Foundation in 2020.
questions.explanation: Anil Soni was named the WHO Foundation's first chief executive in December 2020, taking up the post in January 2021.

questions.text: As of May 2020, who among the following has become the world’s highest paid female athlete according to Forbes magazine report?
questions.explanation: Forbes's list of May 2020 put Naomi Osaka at the top of the highest-paid female athletes, ahead of Serena Williams.

questions.text: How many bones are there in the human hand?
questions.explanation: Each human hand has 27 bones: 8 carpals in the wrist, 5 metacarpals in the palm and 14 phalanges in the fingers.

questions.text: Which of the following is a pointing device used to move an object on the screen of a computer in any direction?
questions.explanation: A joystick is a pointing device: a lever that moves a cursor or object on screen in any direction, used mostly in games. A modem and a server are not input devices, and a floptical is a disk drive.

questions.text: Hoysaleswara Temple is located in which of the following states?
questions.explanation: The Hoysaleswara Temple at Halebidu, Karnataka, was built under the Hoysala kings in the 12th century.

questions.text: Which economic thought talks about methodological individualism, or the idea that people will act in meaningful ways which can be analysed?
questions.explanation: Methodological individualism, explaining economic events through the purposeful actions of individuals, is a founding idea of the Austrian school of Carl Menger and Ludwig von Mises.

questions.text: Which of the following is responsible for producing green light in fireworks?
questions.explanation: Barium compounds burn with a green flame and colour fireworks green; sodium gives yellow.

questions.text: What is another name for the disorder called 'parasomnia'?
questions.explanation: Parasomnias are sleep disorders marked by unusual behaviour during sleep; sleepwalking (somnambulism) is the best known of them, and the only one among the options.

questions.text: Which of the following is a dance form in Mizoram participated exclusively by 'village guests'?
questions.explanation: Khuallam, 'the dance of the guests' (khual means guest, lam dance), is performed by guests invited to the Khuangchawi feast in Mizoram. Cheraw is the bamboo dance.

questions.text: Who among the following has launched the Global Pravasi Rishta portal and mobile app, to connect with Indian Diaspora across the world?
questions.explanation: V Muraleedharan, Minister of State for External Affairs, launched the Global Pravasi Rishta portal in December 2020 to connect the ministry and Indian missions with the diaspora.

questions.text: Tso Kar wetland has been included in Ramsar Site in December 2020. In which of the following states or union territories is it located?
questions.explanation: The Tso Kar wetland complex in Ladakh became India's 42nd Ramsar site; its listing was announced in December 2020.

questions.text: In which of the following years was the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) first constituted?
questions.explanation: The Rajya Sabha was first constituted on 3 April 1952 and held its first sitting on 13 May 1952.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. Mawsmai Cave is one of the most alluring tourist destinations near Cherrapunji in the northeast Indian state of Meghalaya. B. Other sections of the cave are off the limits for tourists. C. The cave is quite big. However, the tourists can visit it up to a distance of 150 metres only. D. The limestone cave has spellbinding beauty and is the only cave which is naturally illuminated to let the tourists cherish natural formations.
questions.explanation: A introduces Mawsmai Cave, D describes 'the limestone cave', C says it is big but tourists may go only 150 metres in, and B adds that the other sections are off limits: ADCB.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. CORROBORATE
questions.explanation: To 'corroborate' is to confirm or support; of the options only 'oppose' is opposite in sense. 'Validate', 'confirm' and 'verify' are synonyms.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Thousands of people / in Telangana are employed on / the granite companies.
questions.explanation: People are employed 'in' (or 'by') a company, not 'on' it: 'are employed in the granite companies'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. During the tsunami, my family took ______ in a guest house on the hill.
questions.explanation: To 'take refuge' is to shelter from danger: 'my family took refuge in a guest house'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. RECKLESS
questions.explanation: 'Reckless' means acting without thinking of the consequences: 'thoughtless'. 'Cautious' is its opposite.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, pick the one that gives their correct order. A. When John was five years old, a circus came to the village. B. John saw the circus people and slipped out of the house. C. After a long search, his father found him among the trained goats and dogs. D. It put up its tents in front of the Town Hall.
questions.explanation: A sets the scene (a circus came to the village), D says where 'it' put up its tents, B tells how John slipped out to see it, and C ends with his father finding him: ADBC.

questions.text: Select the option which means the same as the group of words given. One who is easily deceived
questions.explanation: A 'gullible' person is easily deceived or tricked.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'manipulation'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Deviate
questions.explanation: To 'deviate' is to turn aside from a course: to 'veer'. 'Conform' is its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. Who “is responsible for” the disorderly state of this room?
questions.explanation: 'Who' takes a singular verb here, and one is 'responsible for' something, so the underlined part is already correct.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. Can you please ______ me in sorting out these files on my computer?
questions.explanation: To 'assist' is to help. 'Abet' means to help someone do wrong and 'connive' to conspire or secretly allow wrongdoing, while 'hinder' is the opposite.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. His father said to him, "I cannot allow you to waste my hard-earned money.'
options: His father told him that he cannot allow you to waste his hard-earned money.
His father told him that I cannot allow you to waste my hard-earned money.
His father told him that he could not allow him to waste his hard-earned money.
His father told him that he could not allow you to waste his hard-earned money.
questions.explanation: In indirect speech 'I' becomes 'he', 'you' becomes 'him' and 'my' becomes 'his', and 'cannot' moves back to 'could not' after the past 'told'.

questions.text: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. The guards in the colony always keep an eye in things going on around.
questions.explanation: The idiom is 'keep an eye on' something: 'always keep an eye on things going on around'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. In exactly the same words as were used originally
questions.explanation: 'Verbatim' means in exactly the same words as the original.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. In hot water
questions.explanation: To be 'in hot water' is to be in trouble.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Intrepid
questions.explanation: 'Intrepid' means fearless; its opposite is 'cowardly'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. The maid was dusting the hall when the door-bell rang.
options: The door-bell rang when the hall was being dusted by the maid.
The door-bell rang by the maid when the hall was dusted.
The door-bell rang when the maid was dusting the hall.
The door-bell rang when the maid is dusting the hall.
questions.explanation: The past continuous 'was dusting' becomes 'was being dusted', with the maid as the agent; 'the door-bell rang' has no object and stays as it is.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Make big time
questions.explanation: To 'make the big time' (or 'make it big') is to become famous and successful.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Bhojeshwar Temple is an incomplete Hindu temple in Bhojpur village of Madhya Pradesh, India. The temple's construction is (1) ______ to have started in the 11th century, (2) ______ the reign of the Paramara king, Bhoja. The (3) ______ was abandoned for unknown reasons, with the architectural plans (4) ______ on the surrounding rocks. To understand the construction (5) ______ of 11th-century India, the unfinished materials and the masons’ marks have been studied by scholars.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.explanation: The construction 'is believed to have started' in the 11th century: that is the general view of historians. 'Alleged' is used of wrongdoing.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Bhojeshwar Temple is an incomplete Hindu temple in Bhojpur village of Madhya Pradesh, India. The temple's construction is (1) ______ to have started in the 11th century, (2) ______ the reign of the Paramara king, Bhoja. The (3) ______ was abandoned for unknown reasons, with the architectural plans (4) ______ on the surrounding rocks. To understand the construction (5) ______ of 11th-century India, the unfinished materials and the masons’ marks have been studied by scholars.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
questions.explanation: Construction began 'during the reign of' Bhoja: at some point within that period.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Bhojeshwar Temple is an incomplete Hindu temple in Bhojpur village of Madhya Pradesh, India. The temple's construction is (1) ______ to have started in the 11th century, (2) ______ the reign of the Paramara king, Bhoja. The (3) ______ was abandoned for unknown reasons, with the architectural plans (4) ______ on the surrounding rocks. To understand the construction (5) ______ of 11th-century India, the unfinished materials and the masons’ marks have been studied by scholars.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
questions.explanation: The 'construction' of the temple was abandoned, which is why it is incomplete.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Bhojeshwar Temple is an incomplete Hindu temple in Bhojpur village of Madhya Pradesh, India. The temple's construction is (1) ______ to have started in the 11th century, (2) ______ the reign of the Paramara king, Bhoja. The (3) ______ was abandoned for unknown reasons, with the architectural plans (4) ______ on the surrounding rocks. To understand the construction (5) ______ of 11th-century India, the unfinished materials and the masons’ marks have been studied by scholars.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
questions.explanation: The architectural plans were 'engraved', that is cut, on the surrounding rocks.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Bhojeshwar Temple is an incomplete Hindu temple in Bhojpur village of Madhya Pradesh, India. The temple's construction is (1) ______ to have started in the 11th century, (2) ______ the reign of the Paramara king, Bhoja. The (3) ______ was abandoned for unknown reasons, with the architectural plans (4) ______ on the surrounding rocks. To understand the construction (5) ______ of 11th-century India, the unfinished materials and the masons’ marks have been studied by scholars.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
questions.explanation: 'Construction techniques': the building methods that the unfinished materials and masons' marks reveal.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (11, 12, 264)
questions.explanation: The third number is twice the product of the first two: 11 × 12 × 2 = 264. Likewise 16 × 18 × 2 = 576.

questions.text: In a certain code language, SUPER is written as IVKFH. How will LOFTY be written in that language?
questions.explanation: SUPER is written backwards (REPUS) and each letter replaced by its opposite in the alphabet (A ↔ Z, B ↔ Y, ...): R → I, E → V, P → K, U → F, S → H. LOFTY backwards is YTFOL: Y → B, T → G, F → U, O → L, L → O, so BGULO.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs that can sequentially replace the * signs and balance the given equation. 64 * 16 * 22 * 11 * 5 * 70

Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All cartoons are boxes. No box is a pen. Some cartoons are locks. Conclusions: I. Some boxes are locks. II. No pen is a cartoon. III. No pen is a lock.
options: Both conclusions I and III follow.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: The cartoons that are locks are also boxes, so some boxes are locks (I). All cartoons are boxes and no box is a pen, so no pen is a cartoon (II). The locks that are not cartoons may or may not be pens, so III does not follow.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. Allow : Forbid :: Bragging : ?
questions.explanation: 'Allow' and 'forbid' are opposites; the opposite of 'bragging' is 'modesty'.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series. Y _ B P _ _ A _ P K _ A B _ K Y _ B P K
options: Y A K B Y P A
A K Y B Y P K
A K Y B Y P A
A K A Y K P A
questions.explanation: With A, K, Y, B, Y, P, A in the blanks the block YABPK repeats: YABPK YABPK YABPK YABPK.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers in the set share the same relationship as that shared by the numbers of the given set. (5, 8, 338)
questions.explanation: The third number is twice the square of the sum of the first two: 2 × (5 + 8)² = 2 × 169 = 338. Likewise 2 × (11 + 8)² = 2 × 361 = 722.

questions.text: In a code language, if TERMINAL is written as 401036261828224, then how will AUDITORY be written in the same language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is written as twice its place in the alphabet: T = 20 → 40, E = 5 → 10, R = 18 → 36 and so on. AUDITORY gives 2, 42, 8, 18, 40, 30, 36, 50: 24281840303650.

questions.text: Introducing Raveena, Nitish said, "She is the maternal grandmother of my sister’s son". How is Raveena related to Nitish?
questions.explanation: The maternal grandmother of Nitish's sister's son is his sister's mother, who is Nitish's own mother.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term. PLASTIC : ALPSCIT :: FESTIVE : ?
questions.explanation: The first three letters are reversed, the middle letter stays and the last three are reversed: PLA S TIC → ALP S CIT. So FES T IVE → SEF T EVI: SEFTEVI.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the sixth number is related to the fifth number. 5 : 50 : : 6 : ? : : 12 : 288
questions.explanation: Each second number is twice the square of the first: 2 × 5² = 50 and 2 × 12² = 288. So 2 × 6² = 72.

questions.text: Select the word-pair in which the two words are related in the same way as are the two words in the following word-pair. Doctor : Cardiologist
questions.explanation: A cardiologist is a specialised kind of doctor, as a chemical engineer is a specialised kind of engineer.

questions.text: Four words have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the odd one.
questions.explanation: The kelvin, ampere and candela are SI base units (of temperature, electric current and luminous intensity). Luminosity is a quantity, not a unit.

questions.text: Three of the following four letter-clusters are alike in a certain way and one is different. Select the odd one.
questions.explanation: In ZGN, TAH and LSZ each letter is 7 places after the one before it (counting on from Z to A). In OUD the steps are +6 and +9, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Kritika had ₹21,450 with her. She spent 16% of this amount on conveyance. Then, she spent 50% of the remaining amount on ration. Then, she spent ₹991 on internet expenses. How many rupees is left with her now?
questions.explanation: After 16% on conveyance: 21,450 × 0.84 = ₹18,018. Half of that, ₹9,009, is left after ration, and ₹9,009 − ₹991 = ₹8,018.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in an English dictionary. 1. Peripheral 2. Presence 3. Peninsula 4. Produce 5. Prevent
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Peninsula (3), Peripheral (1), Presence (2), Prevent (5), Produce (4). 'Pen' comes before 'Per', 'Pres' before 'Prev', and both before 'Pro'.

questions.text: Four number-pairs have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the one that is different.
questions.explanation: In 18 : 288, 12 : 120 and 13 : 143 the second number is the first times two less than itself (18 × 16, 12 × 10, 13 × 11). 11 × 9 = 99, not 111, so 11 : 111 is the odd one.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 12, 15, 75, ?, 738, 749
questions.explanation: The steps alternate between adding and multiplying by the odd numbers: 12 + 3 = 15, 15 × 5 = 75, 75 + 7 = 82, 82 × 9 = 738, 738 + 11 = 749.

questions.text: Who has become the first Woman DGP of Kerala?
questions.explanation: R. Sreelekha, the first woman IPS officer of the Kerala cadre, became Kerala's first woman Director General of Police.

questions.text: Where is the Kudremukh iron ore mine located?
questions.explanation: Kudremukh, in Chikkamagaluru district of Karnataka, is known for its iron ore deposits.

questions.text: Which of the following nations ‘unintentionally’ shot down a Ukrainian Boeing 737-800 passenger aircraft in January 2020?
questions.explanation: Iran's forces shot down Ukraine International Airlines Flight 752 near Tehran on 8 January 2020, killing all 176 people on board; Iran later admitted it had done so unintentionally.

questions.text: What is a leaf-shaped flap of cartilage located behind the tongue, at the top of the larynx or voice box called?
questions.explanation: The epiglottis is the leaf-shaped flap of cartilage that closes over the windpipe during swallowing. The gallbladder, ileum and jejunum are parts of the digestive system.

questions.text: Which of the following channels or straits is located between the Great Nicobar Island and Indonesia's Sumatra Island?
questions.explanation: The Great Channel (printed here as 'Grand channel'), also called the Six Degree Channel, separates Great Nicobar from Sumatra. The Ten Degree Channel separates the Andamans from the Nicobars, and the Palk Strait lies between India and Sri Lanka.

questions.text: India’s first gold medal at Commonwealth Games 2018 was won by:
questions.explanation: Mirabai Chanu won India's first gold of the 2018 Gold Coast Commonwealth Games, in women's 48 kg weightlifting.

questions.text: Who among the following won Poland’s Presidential Election held on 12 July 2020?
questions.explanation: Andrzej Duda won the run-off of 12 July 2020 against Rafał Trzaskowski, securing a second term as President of Poland.

questions.text: Tiny pores present on the surface of leaves are known as:
questions.explanation: Stomata are the tiny pores on leaves through which gases are exchanged and water vapour is lost.

questions.text: As of January 2021, how many Olympic medals did India win in the sport of weightlifting?
questions.explanation: Karnam Malleswari's bronze at Sydney 2000 was India's only Olympic weightlifting medal until Mirabai Chanu's silver at Tokyo in July 2021.

questions.text: Which type of malware is a program or piece of code that is loaded onto a person’s computer without his knowledge and runs against his wishes?
questions.explanation: That is the standard definition of a computer virus, which copies itself into other programs and spreads. A trojan horse is disguised as useful software that the user installs, adware shows unwanted advertisements, and phishing is a fraudulent attempt to obtain information, not a program.

questions.text: Which of the following languages is an example of fourth generation language in computer programming?
questions.explanation: SQL is a fourth-generation language: it states what result is wanted rather than how to compute it. ALGOL, SNOBOL and Pascal are third-generation languages.

questions.text: Who among the following was NOT a Nayanar saint?
questions.explanation: Sundarar, Appar and Sambandar were Nayanars, the Shaiva saints of the Tamil country. Andal was one of the Alvars, the Vaishnava saints.

questions.text: Cytology is related to the study of:
questions.explanation: Cytology is the study of cells.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: What was the outcome of the Gandhi-Irwin Pact of 1931?
options: Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev were to be given a fair trial.
Indian National Congress agreed on a peaceful partition of Bengal.
Indian National Congress agreed to end the Civil Disobedience Movement.
questions.explanation: Under the Gandhi-Irwin Pact of March 1931 the Congress agreed to suspend the Civil Disobedience Movement and attend the Second Round Table Conference; the government agreed to release political prisoners not charged with violence.

questions.text: Who among the following was awarded the 55th Jnanpith Award?
questions.explanation: The Malayalam poet Akkitham Achuthan Namboothiri received the 55th Jnanpith Award (for 2019). Amitav Ghosh received the 54th.

questions.text: Who is the author of the book ‘Hit Refresh’?
questions.explanation: 'Hit Refresh' (2017) is by Satya Nadella, chief executive of Microsoft.

questions.text: Which of the following government schemes was launched with the objective of achieving inclusive growth, by developing the skills and productive capacity of the rural youth from poor families?
options: Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay Shramev Jayate Yojana (PDUSJY)
Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDUGKY)
Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY)
questions.explanation: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana, the Ministry of Rural Development's placement-linked skilling scheme, trains rural youth from poor families.

questions.text: Prabhavati Gupta, the Queen Regent of the Vakataka empire, was the daughter of Kuberanaga and ______.
questions.explanation: Prabhavatigupta was the daughter of the Gupta king Chandragupta II and his queen Kuberanaga; she married the Vakataka king Rudrasena II.

questions.text: With which of the following musical instruments was the musician Bismillah Khan associated?
questions.explanation: Ustad Bismillah Khan was the great master of the shehnai; he received the Bharat Ratna in 2001.

questions.text: In which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India is right to property mentioned?
questions.explanation: The 44th Amendment (1978) removed the right to property from the Fundamental Rights and made it a constitutional right under Article 300A.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding the functioning of Rajya Sabha is correct?
options: Rajya Sabha is dissolved every second year.
Rajya Sabha is dissolved after the dissolution of the Lok Sabha.
Rajya Sabha is dissolved after the assent of the President of India.
Rajya Sabha is not subject to dissolution.
questions.explanation: The Rajya Sabha is a permanent body: it is never dissolved, and one-third of its members retire every second year.

questions.text: Which of the following states has accorded industry status to sports?
questions.explanation: In May 2020 Mizoram's cabinet granted sports the status of an industry, so that industrial benefits such as subsidies apply to sports ventures.

questions.text: As of the financial year 2017-18, which of the following was the largest jowar producing state in India?
questions.explanation: Maharashtra is India's largest producer of jowar (sorghum).

questions.text: What was the estimation for the fiscal deficit in the financial year 2019-20?
questions.explanation: The Union Budget of July 2019 put the fiscal deficit for 2019-20 at 3.3% of GDP.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, pick the one that gives their correct order. A. There he brought them up as his own children. B. He took them away to his hut. C. He found the two children and the basket. D. One day an old man came to the jungle.
questions.explanation: D brings in the old man, C has him find the children, B has him take them to his hut and A says he raised them there: DCBA.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. The eradication of corona virus is still “a far cry”.
questions.explanation: 'A far cry' means a long way off: the eradication is still very distant.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'instance'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. The house “has been auction” before we reached there.
questions.explanation: The auction came before another past action, 'we reached', so the past perfect passive: 'had been auctioned'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. RESOLVE
questions.explanation: To 'resolve' is to decide firmly to do something; its opposite here is 'refuse', to decline to do it. 'Decide' is a synonym.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. PRECIOUS
questions.explanation: 'Precious' means of great value; its opposite is 'cheap'. 'Costly' and 'rare' are close to synonyms.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given words. speed greater than that of sound
questions.explanation: 'Supersonic' means faster than sound; 'subsonic' means slower than sound.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. PRUDENT
questions.explanation: 'Prudent' means acting with care and good judgement: 'cautious'.

questions.text: Select the option which means the same as the group of words given. A place where Buddhist monks live
questions.explanation: A monastery is a place where monks live together; stupas, pagodas and temples are monuments or places of worship.

questions.text: Given below are four sentences in jumbled order. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. This flight takes place on a hot summer day. B. It has a pair of wings but bites them off after its ‘wedding’ flight. C. In the heat, the queen leaves the nest and goes out to meet a drone, high up in the air. D. The queen is the mother of the entire population of a colony of ants.
questions.explanation: D introduces the queen, B mentions her wings and her 'wedding' flight, A says when this flight takes place and C describes it: DBAC.

questions.text: Fill in the blank with most appropriate word. ______ of adulterated food stuff being sold in the market.
questions.explanation: 'Beware of' is a warning on its own; 'wary', 'aware' and 'cautious' are adjectives and would need 'Be' before them.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. The prisoners of this jail have woven these carpets.
options: The prisoners have been woven by these carpets of this jail.
These carpets have been woven by the prisoners of this jail.
These carpets were woven by the prisoners of this jail.
These carpets wove the prisoners of this jail.
questions.explanation: The present perfect active 'have woven' becomes the present perfect passive 'have been woven', with the carpets as subject.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. The gardener said to the children, “Please do not pluck any flowers.”
options: The gardener requested the children not to pluck any flowers.
The gardener told to the children to kindly not pluck any flowers.
The gardener ordered the children to not pluck any flowers.
The gardener requested to the children please do not pluck any flowers.
questions.explanation: A polite request with 'please' is reported with 'requested' and the infinitive: 'requested the children not to pluck any flowers'.

questions.text: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. Why didn’t you submitted your project on time?
questions.explanation: After 'did' (here 'didn't') the verb takes its base form: 'Why didn't you submit your project on time?'

questions.text: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. Electric heaters were providing to all the officers at the guest house.
questions.explanation: The heaters were given to the officers, so the verb must be passive: 'Electric heaters were provided to all the officers'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. STRETCH
questions.explanation: To 'stretch' something is to 'extend' it; 'compress' is the opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Living in a fool’s paradise
options: To believe wrongly that your situation is good
To live in luxuriously after fooling someone
To live in a world of imagination
questions.explanation: To live in a fool's paradise is to be content because you wrongly believe your situation is good.

questions.text: Select the misspelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'tariff'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. Supriya as well as her friends “have gone of” a trekking expedition.
questions.explanation: With 'as well as' the verb agrees with the first subject, 'Supriya', so it is singular; and one goes 'on' an expedition: 'has gone on'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I should have stopped them then and there. But it never even ______ to me that I should.
questions.explanation: An idea 'occurs to' someone: 'it never even occurred to me that I should'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Before the giant waves slammed into the coast in India and Sri Lanka, wild and domestic animals (1) ______ to know what was about to happen. (2) ______ fled to safety. According to eyewitness (3) ______, elephants screamed and ran for (4) ______ grounds, dogs refused to go outdoors, flamingoes abandoned (5) ______ low-lying breeding areas and zoo animals rushed into their shelters.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 1.
questions.explanation: The animals 'seemed' to know: the simple past, like the rest of the passage.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Before the giant waves slammed into the coast in India and Sri Lanka, wild and domestic animals (1) ______ to know what was about to happen. (2) ______ fled to safety. According to eyewitness (3) ______, elephants screamed and ran for (4) ______ grounds, dogs refused to go outdoors, flamingoes abandoned (5) ______ low-lying breeding areas and zoo animals rushed into their shelters.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 2.
questions.explanation: 'They', the subject of 'fled', refers back to the animals.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Before the giant waves slammed into the coast in India and Sri Lanka, wild and domestic animals (1) ______ to know what was about to happen. (2) ______ fled to safety. According to eyewitness (3) ______, elephants screamed and ran for (4) ______ grounds, dogs refused to go outdoors, flamingoes abandoned (5) ______ low-lying breeding areas and zoo animals rushed into their shelters.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 3.
questions.explanation: 'Eyewitness accounts' are the reports of people who saw what happened.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Before the giant waves slammed into the coast in India and Sri Lanka, wild and domestic animals (1) ______ to know what was about to happen. (2) ______ fled to safety. According to eyewitness (3) ______, elephants screamed and ran for (4) ______ grounds, dogs refused to go outdoors, flamingoes abandoned (5) ______ low-lying breeding areas and zoo animals rushed into their shelters.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 4.
questions.explanation: The elephants ran for 'higher' grounds, away from the low coast the waves struck.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Before the giant waves slammed into the coast in India and Sri Lanka, wild and domestic animals (1) ______ to know what was about to happen. (2) ______ fled to safety. According to eyewitness (3) ______, elephants screamed and ran for (4) ______ grounds, dogs refused to go outdoors, flamingoes abandoned (5) ______ low-lying breeding areas and zoo animals rushed into their shelters.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 5.
questions.explanation: The breeding areas were the flamingoes' own, so the plural possessive 'their'.

questions.text: P and Q are husband and wife. P's father-in-law is R's wife's father. Q is the brother of T. How is P related to R's wife?
questions.explanation: Q is T's brother, so Q is the husband and P the wife. P's father-in-law, Q's father, is also the father of R's wife, so R's wife is Q's sister, and P, her brother's wife, is her sister-in-law.

questions.text: Select the word-pair in which the two words are related in the same way as are the two words in the following word-pair. Spoon : Utensil
questions.explanation: A spoon is a kind of utensil, as a scooter is a kind of vehicle.

questions.text: Vijay is 8 years younger than Amit. The sum of the current ages of Vijay and Amit is 42 years. What is the current age of Vijay?
questions.explanation: Vijay + (Vijay + 8) = 42, so 2 × Vijay = 34 and Vijay is 17 years old.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number. 25 : 750 : : 30 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is the first times 5 more than itself: 25 × 30 = 750. Likewise 30 × 35 = 1050.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given letter series will complete the series. a _ _ gb _ _ acegb _ _ aceg _ _ _
questions.explanation: With c, e, d, f, d, f, b, d, f in the blanks the block acegbdf repeats: acegbdf acegbdf acegbdf.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 2, 4, 5, 19, 71, ?
Four number-pairs have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the one that is different.
questions.explanation: In 5 : 65, 8 : 104 and 11 : 143 the second number is 13 times the first. 12 × 13 = 156, not 146, so 12 : 146 is the odd one.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in an English dictionary. 1. Rubric 2. Ruminate 3. Rose 4. Reader 5. Reap
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Reader (4), Reap (5), Rose (3), Rubric (1), Ruminate (2). 'Read' comes before 'Reap', and 'Rub' before 'Rum'.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers share the same relationship as that shared by the numbers of the given set. (8, 44, 224)
questions.explanation: Each number is 5 times the one before it plus 4: 8 × 5 + 4 = 44 and 44 × 5 + 4 = 224. Likewise 11 × 5 + 4 = 59 and 59 × 5 + 4 = 299.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term. SLIM : MHQO : : COLD : ?
questions.explanation: The letters are put in alphabetical order and then moved +4, −4, +4, −4: SLIM → I L M S → M H Q O. So COLD → C D L O → G Z P K (D moved back 4 wraps round to Z).

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (57, 126, 199)
questions.explanation: In each set the second number is 69 more than the first and the third 73 more than the second: 57 → 126 → 199. Likewise 63 → 132 → 205.

questions.text: In a code language, if SEND is written as 168, then how will PURSE be written in the same language?
questions.explanation: Each code is the sum of the letters' places in the alphabet times the number of letters: SEND = (19 + 5 + 14 + 4) × 4 = 168. So PURSE = (16 + 21 + 18 + 19 + 5) × 5 = 79 × 5 = 395.

questions.text: In a certain code language, BEYOND is written as BDFNPY. How will PROMISE be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters are put in alphabetical order and each vowel then moves one place forward: BEYOND → B D E N O Y → B D F N P Y. So PROMISE → E I M O P R S → F J M P P R S.

questions.text: Three of the following four letter-clusters are alike in a certain way and one is different. Select the odd one.
questions.explanation: In LPT, GKO and QUY each letter is 4 places after the one before it. HLQ moves +4 then +5, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Four words have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the word that is different.
questions.explanation: 'Equivocal', 'hesitant' and 'ambivalent' all describe uncertainty or indecision; 'certain' is their opposite.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. Ohmmeter : Resistance : : Zymometer : ?
questions.explanation: An ohmmeter measures electrical resistance; a zymometer measures fermentation.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs that can sequentially replace the * signs and balance the given equation. 14 * 11 * 552 * 23 * 29 = 159
Who among the following has been appointed as the Deputy Election Commissioner in the Election Commission of India?
questions.explanation: In December 2020 the government kept Umesh Sinha on as Deputy Election Commissioner until June 2021. Ashok Lavasa and Rajiv Kumar were Election Commissioners, members of the Commission itself.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Swami Vivekananda established Ramakrishna Mission in the year ______.
questions.explanation: Swami Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission in Calcutta on 1 May 1897.

questions.text: Which of the following is an extension of a temporary file?
questions.explanation: Temporary files usually carry the extension '.tmp'; '.txt' marks a plain text file and '.tar' an archive.

questions.text: Birdie, eagle and albatross are all terms used in ______.
questions.explanation: In golf a birdie is one stroke under par on a hole, an eagle two under and an albatross three under.

questions.text: ______ holds the Indian record for the most test matches as captain as of December 2020.
questions.explanation: MS Dhoni captained India in 60 Tests, the Indian record as of December 2020.

questions.text: Which of the following planets has the most number of moons?
questions.explanation: Saturn had the most known moons: with 20 more announced in October 2019 its count reached 82, against Jupiter's 79.

questions.text: Which of the following festivals of Tamil Nadu is dedicated to Lord Muruga?
questions.explanation: Thaipusam, held in the Tamil month of Thai, honours Lord Murugan (Muruga). Pongal is a harvest festival, Aadi Perukku honours the rivers and Onam is Kerala's festival.

questions.text: In 2020, India co-sponsored a security council resolution that calls for full, effective and meaningful participation of ______ personnel in peacekeeping operations.
questions.explanation: Security Council Resolution 2538, adopted on 28 August 2020 with India among its co-sponsors, is on women in peacekeeping, both uniformed and civilian.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Champaran Satyagraha was launched in which of the following years?
questions.explanation: Gandhi led the Champaran Satyagraha for the indigo farmers of Bihar in 1917, his first satyagraha in India.

questions.text: In how many countries, Union Cabinet approved the opening of Indian Missions in 2021?
questions.explanation: In December 2020 the Union Cabinet approved opening Indian Missions in three countries in 2021: Estonia, Paraguay and the Dominican Republic.

questions.text: AMR occurs when bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites change over time and no longer respond to medicines making infections harder to treat and increasing the risk of disease spread, severe illness and death. What is the full form of AMR?
questions.explanation: AMR stands for antimicrobial resistance: microbes stop responding to the medicines meant to kill them.

questions.text: What kind of soil is most suitable for growing cashew nuts?
questions.explanation: NCERT notes that the red laterite soils of Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Kerala suit crops like cashew nuts.

questions.text: Who among the following is the first female Chief Justice of Telangana?
questions.explanation: Justice Hima Kohli became Chief Justice of the Telangana High Court in January 2021, the first woman to hold the post.

questions.text: Hakki, Pikki and Siddi are ______ from Karnataka.
questions.explanation: The Hakki Pikki and the Siddi are tribal communities of Karnataka; the People's Linguistic Survey of India listed their languages (the Hakki Pikki speak Vaagri) as critically endangered.

questions.text: Who is the author of the book 'Pathway to God'?
