markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: Two trains of lengths 110 m and 100 m are running towards each other on parallel lines at the speed of 50 km/h and 58 km/h, respectively. How long will they take to cross each other after they meet?
questions.explanation: Running towards each other, the trains close at 50 + 58 = 108 km/h = 30 m/s. To pass each other completely they cover 110 + 100 = 210 m: 210/30 = 7 seconds.

questions.text: What is the HCF of 513,1134 and 1215?
If a semi-circular plot has radius 100 m, find its perimeter. (Use π = 3.14)
questions.explanation: The perimeter is the curved edge plus the diameter: πr + 2r = 3.14 × 100 + 200 = 514 m.

questions.text: A train increases its regular speed by 12.5% and reaches its destination 20 minutes earlier. What is the actual time taken by the train on the journey?
questions.explanation: At 9/8 of its speed the train takes 8/9 of its usual time, saving 1/9 of it. 1/9 of the time is 20 minutes, so the usual time is 180 minutes.

questions.text: A shop has two promotional offers: buy three shirts, get one shirt free, or a 25% discount on the marked price. If a customer buys five using both offers, what discount will he get all together?
questions.explanation: Four shirts under the first offer cost the price of three, and the fifth costs 75% of its price under the second. He pays 3 + 0.75 = 3.75 shirts' price for 5: a discount of 1.25/5 = 25%.

questions.text: The quantity of milk ordered on the first, second, third and fourth day of a four day ceremony is in the proportion of 30 litres, 24 litres, 35 litres and ‘x’ litres, respectively. Find the quantity of milk (in litres) ordered on the fourth day.
questions.explanation: In proportion, 30 : 24 = 35 : x, so x = 24 × 35/30 = 28.

questions.text: For a sum of ₹15,000 the rate of interest of 8.5% per annum simple interest, find the interest earned (in ₹) in 5 years 3 months.
The average weight of Rakesh and his five friends is 62 kg. If Rakesh is 6 kg heavier than the average weight of his five friends, then find the weight of Rakesh.
questions.explanation: The six weigh 6 × 62 = 372 kg. If the five friends average a kg, 5a + (a + 6) = 372, so a = 61 and Rakesh weighs 67 kg.

questions.text: A solid hemisphere of radius 12 cm is melted into N identical cones, each of radius 6 cm and height 8 cm. What is the value of N?
questions.explanation: The hemisphere holds (2/3)π × 12³ = 1,152π cm³ and each cone (1/3)π × 6² × 8 = 96π cm³, so N = 1,152π ÷ 96π = 12.

questions.text: The average weight of a family of five members (in kg) whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 68 kg and 38 kg is:
Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3500 as a sum borrowed at 7% per year rate of interest for 4 years.
What sum (in ₹) will earn a simple interest of ₹360 in 3 years at 12% per year rate of interest?
‘RJ 17’ is related to ‘QL 19’ in a certain way. In the same way, ‘CP 12’ is related to ‘BR 14’. To which of the following is ‘OJ 22’ related following the same logic?
questions.explanation: The first letter moves back one, the second forward two and the number up two: R → Q, J → L, 17 → 19 and C → B, P → R, 12 → 14. So O → N, J → L, 22 → 24: NL 24.

questions.text: What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘×’ are interchanged and ‘−’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 78 − 6 ÷ 6 + 2 × 8 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 78 ÷ 6 − 6 × 2 + 8 = 13 − 12 + 8 = 9.

questions.text: A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H are sitting around a circular table facing out to the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). D is sitting to the immediate left of A and third to the right of H. B is sitting third to the right of F. F is the immediate neighbour of C and G. C is sitting third to the right of A. Who is sitting fourth to the right of A?
questions.explanation: D sits on A's immediate left, and H is third to D's left (D is third to H's right), so H is four seats from A: directly opposite in a circle of eight. Fourth to the right of A is that opposite seat, whichever way the people face.

questions.text: What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 24 × 576 ÷ 72 – 108 + 91 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 24 ÷ 576 × 72 + 108 − 91 = 3 + 108 − 91 = 20.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘GOES’ is coded as ‘4268’ and ‘OILY’ is coded as ‘3457’. What is the code for ‘O’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: O is the only letter in both words and 4 the only digit in both codes, so O = 4.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘you read book’ is written as ‘hm rn op’ and ‘book is good’ is written as ‘cf am rn’. What is the code for ‘book’ in that language?
questions.explanation: 'book' is the only word in both sentences and 'rn' the only code in both, so book = rn.

questions.text: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). B sits to the immediate left of E. C sits to the immediate left of F. F sits second to the left of G. D sits third to the left of E. Who sits third to the left of A?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, each person's left is clockwise. The clues fit only one order, clockwise: E, B, G, D, F, C, A. Counting three to the left of A: E, B, G.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All papayas are oranges. Some oranges are apples. Conclusions: (I) At least some apples are oranges. (II) Some papayas are apples.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: Some oranges are apples, so at least some apples are oranges (I). All papayas are oranges, but nothing says any of them are among the apples, so II need not follow.

questions.text: In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/ subtracting /multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 8, 72; 11, 99
questions.explanation: The second number is 9 times the first: 8 × 9 = 72 and 11 × 9 = 99. Likewise 17 × 9 = 153.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘MONKEY’ is coded as ‘BHNQRP’ and ‘NAP’ is coded as ‘SDQ’. What is the code for ‘JUTEBAG’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: The word is reversed and each letter moved 3 places forward: MONKEY → YEKNOM → BHNQRP and NAP → PAN → SDQ. So JUTEBAG → GABETUJ → JDEHWXM.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? XCW, UGS, RKO ,?, LSG
questions.explanation: First letters move back 3 (X, U, R, O, L), second letters forward 4 (C, G, K, O, S) and third letters back 4 (W, S, O, K, G): OOK.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some tomatoes are potatoes. No potato is an onion. Conclusions: (I) Some potatoes are not tomatoes. (II) No tomato is an onion.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: The statements allow every potato to be a tomato, so I need not follow. The tomatoes that are potatoes are not onions, but the other tomatoes may be, so II need not follow either.

questions.text: CDFG is related to FGIJ in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, MNPQ is related to PQST. To which of the following is HIKL related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places forward: CDFG → FGIJ and MNPQ → PQST. So HIKL → KLNO.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 10, ?, 46, 94, 190, 382, 766
questions.explanation: Each term is twice the one before plus 2: 10 × 2 + 2 = 22, 22 × 2 + 2 = 46, 46 × 2 + 2 = 94, and so on to 766.

questions.text: 3 is related to 40 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 5 is related to 66. To which of the following is 10 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding / subtracting / multiplying, etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is 13 times the first plus 1: 3 × 13 + 1 = 40 and 5 × 13 + 1 = 66. Likewise 10 × 13 + 1 = 131.

questions.text: Limestone is composed of:
questions.explanation: Limestone is a sedimentary rock made mainly of calcium carbonate, as the mineral calcite.

questions.text: What is the term for the gradual, sequential changes in species composition in an ecosystem over time?
questions.explanation: Ecological succession is the gradual, orderly change in the species of a community over time, from pioneer species to a climax community.

questions.text: Which edition of 'Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana' has been announced in union budget 2023?
questions.explanation: The Union Budget 2023-24, presented on 1 February 2023, announced Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana 4.0.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a drawback of the barter system?
options: Surplus goods are replaced with other goods
Lack of a common unit of value
questions.explanation: Barter is the direct exchange of goods for goods, so swapping surplus goods for others is simply how it works. Its drawbacks are the need for a double coincidence of wants, the lack of a common measure of value and the difficulty of deferred (contractual) payments.

questions.text: As per Census 2011, what is the average female literacy rate in India?
questions.explanation: Census 2011 put female literacy at 65.46%, against 82.14% for males.

questions.text: Which brick-made minaret holds the record for being the world's tallest tower at 73 metres?
questions.explanation: The Qutb Minar in Delhi, 72.5 m tall, is the tallest brick minaret in the world.

questions.text: Which state hosted the 6th edition of Khelo India Youth Games in 2024?
questions.explanation: The 6th Khelo India Youth Games were held in Tamil Nadu in January 2024.

questions.text: The Aatmanirbhar Bharat Rojgar Yojana was implemented through which organisation?
questions.explanation: The Aatmanirbhar Bharat Rojgar Yojana (2020), which paid the provident fund contributions for new employees, was implemented through the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO).

questions.text: Identify the tributary of the Brahmaputra River from the following.
questions.explanation: The Burhi Dihing is a south-bank tributary of the Brahmaputra in Assam. The Barakar joins the Damodar and the Hindan the Yamuna.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Jallianwala Bagh is located in which city?
questions.explanation: Jallianwala Bagh, scene of the massacre of 13 April 1919, is in Amritsar, Punjab.

questions.text: Children’s Day in India is celebrated to commemorate the birth anniversary of _________.
questions.explanation: Children's Day, 14 November, marks the birth anniversary of Jawaharlal Nehru.

questions.text: Which Article of the Constitution of India describes a key feature of ‘Universal Adult Franchise’ that grants the right to vote to citizens, above the age of 18 years in India?
questions.explanation: Article 326 provides that elections to the Lok Sabha and the State Legislative Assemblies are held on the basis of adult suffrage: every citizen aged 18 or over may vote.

questions.text: The Hugli industrial region is located in which state?
questions.explanation: The Hugli industrial region grew up along the Hugli river around Kolkata, in West Bengal.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following social reformers ruled out the practice of Sati on the basis of Hindu religious texts?
questions.explanation: Raja Ram Mohan Roy argued from the Hindu scriptures that they did not require Sati, and campaigned until it was banned in 1829.

questions.text: Both, Rajesh Prasanna and Rishabh Prasanna are associated with which musical instrument?
questions.explanation: Rajesh Prasanna and Rishab Prasanna, of the Prasanna family of the Banaras gharana, play the bansuri, the bamboo flute.

questions.text: Which of the following was the mascot of the 37th National Games?
questions.explanation: Moga, an Indian bison (gaur), was the mascot of the 37th National Games, held in Goa in 2023. Savaj was the mascot of the 36th Games, in Gujarat.

questions.text: How many covalent bonds are present between the constituent atoms in the molecules of Butane and Hexane, respectively?
questions.explanation: An alkane CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ has n − 1 C–C bonds and 2n + 2 C–H bonds, 3n + 1 in all. Butane (n = 4) has 13 and hexane (n = 6) 19.

questions.text: Which among the following dynasties originated from the Yueh-chih tribe of China?
questions.explanation: The Kushanas were a branch of the Yuezhi (Yueh-chih), a people of north-western China who migrated west into Central Asia.

questions.text: Vinod Kevin Bachan has been selected for the Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar 2021, for his contribution to which Indian dance form?
questions.explanation: Vinod Kevin Bachan is an Odissi dancer; SSC's key gives Odissi as the form for which he received the Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar 2021.

questions.text: The First Battle of Panipat (1526) marked the beginning of:
options: French East India Company's rule in India
British East India company's rule in India
questions.explanation: At the First Battle of Panipat (1526) Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi, the last Delhi Sultan, and began Mughal rule in India.

questions.text: Which of the following classical dance styles manifests the element of sky?
questions.explanation: SSC's key follows the popular pairing of five classical dances with the five elements, in which Kathakali stands for the sky (ether), Bharatanatyam for fire, Mohiniyattam for air, Odissi for water and Kuchipudi for earth.

questions.text: How many fundamental duties were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act 1976?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment (1976) added ten Fundamental Duties in Article 51A; the 86th Amendment (2002) added an eleventh.

questions.text: The novel ‘Pinjar’ that was later converted into a motion picture was written by:
questions.explanation: 'Pinjar' (1950), Amrita Pritam's Punjabi novel set during Partition, was made into a film in 2003.

questions.text: Chili peppers produce a burning sensation in any tissue with which they come into contact. What is the compound responsible for this?
questions.explanation: Capsaicin is the compound that makes chilli peppers hot; it acts on the nerve receptors for heat and pain.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Naviggetion' is misspelt: the word is 'navigation'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. It was an insight / and determination of the lady doctor / that people were / able to lead a normal life.
options: and determination of the lady doctor
able to lead a normal life
questions.explanation: 'Insight and determination' are made particular by 'of the lady doctor', so they take the definite article: 'It was the insight and determination of the lady doctor that...'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks. I did not _______ that he would ______ the offer.
questions.explanation: 'Expect' means to think likely and 'accept' to agree to take: 'I did not expect that he would accept the offer.' 'Except' means leaving out.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. A majority of Indians prefer to use the Internet for ______________ booking and other financial services.
questions.explanation: One uses the Internet for 'accessing' (getting the use of) booking and other financial services; one does not attend, disperse or improve them.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. Radha stepped “backward” to avoid the incoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'backward' is 'forward'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Pull someone’s leg
options: To physically pull the legs of a person
To take a situation seriously or earnestly
To tease or play a joke on someone
questions.explanation: To 'pull someone's leg' is to tease them, usually by telling them something untrue as a joke.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. My cousin thinks that / English is difficult / than other subjects.
questions.explanation: A comparison with 'than' needs the comparative: 'English is more difficult than other subjects'.

questions.text: Select the option that correctly rectifies the underlined spelling error. Thank you for this jar of “asorted” cookies.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'assorted', with a double 's'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in future continuous tense form I shall come again in the afternoon for lunch.
options: I will be coming again in the afternoon for lunch.
I will come again in the afternoon for lunch.
I shall have come again in the afternoon for lunch
I shall be coming again in the afternoon for lunch.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'I shall be coming', the future continuous ('shall/will be' + '-ing') that keeps the sentence's own 'shall'. 'I will be coming' is also future continuous, so it is arguable too.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Only when the floods get _________ will world governments begin to act.
questions.explanation: 'Get worse' means become more severe: only when the floods get 'worse' will governments act. 'Frequently' is an adverb, and 'lucky' and 'gullible' do not describe floods.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Attract
questions.explanation: To 'attract' is to draw towards; its opposite is to 'repel', to drive away.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Please pass _________ the salt.
questions.explanation: 'Pass' takes the object pronoun as its indirect object: 'Please pass me the salt.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Mountaineering requires a combination of physical strength,“endurance”, technical skill and mental fortitude.
questions.explanation: 'Endurance' is the strength to keep going through hardship. Of the options, 'timidity', a lack of courage and boldness, is the nearest opposite; 'persistence' is close in meaning, and 'excitement' and 'enthusiasm' are unrelated.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank to complete the idiom and make the sentence meaningful. Her company's new product launch was a real ___________________ squib.
questions.explanation: A 'damp squib' is something that fails to live up to expectations, like a firework that fizzles because it is damp.

questions.text: The given sentence is divided into three segments. One of them may contain a grammatical error. Select the option that has the segment with the error. If there is no error, select ‘No error’ as your answer. Meenu looks/ much better/ today.
questions.explanation: 'Looks' is a linking verb followed by the comparative adjective 'better', strengthened by 'much': the sentence is correct.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Ramesh is fond “at” playing guitar in his free time.
questions.explanation: 'Fond' takes 'of': 'Ramesh is fond of playing guitar in his free time.'

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. I thought of this idea / just when you called / me yesterday.
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct: one thinks 'of' an idea, and the simple past suits both actions ('thought', 'called') on the same occasion.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the highlighted word. The man had committed a “grave” offence so he was granted bail.
questions.explanation: 'Grave' means serious; its opposite is 'trivial'. 'Serious' and 'solemn' are synonyms.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Fish live in aquariums and pigs live in _________.
questions.explanation: A sty, or pigsty, is a pen for pigs; kennels are for dogs, stables for horses and dens for wild animals.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. To forgive an injury is often (1)_______ to be a sign of weakness; it is really a sign of (2)___ . It is easy to allow oneself to be carried away by resentment and hate into an act of (3)______; but it takes a strong character to restrain those natural passions. The man who (4)______ an injury proves himself to be the superior of the man who wronged him, and puts the wrong-doer to shame. (5)___ may even turn a foe into a friend.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Forgiving an injury is often 'considered', that is thought to be, a sign of weakness; the sentence goes on to say it is really the opposite.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. To forgive an injury is often (1)_______ to be a sign of weakness; it is really a sign of (2)___ . It is easy to allow oneself to be carried away by resentment and hate into an act of (3)______; but it takes a strong character to restrain those natural passions. The man who (4)______ an injury proves himself to be the superior of the man who wronged him, and puts the wrong-doer to shame. (5)___ may even turn a foe into a friend.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The contrast with 'weakness' calls for 'strength', which the passage confirms: 'it takes a strong character'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. To forgive an injury is often (1)_______ to be a sign of weakness; it is really a sign of (2)___ . It is easy to allow oneself to be carried away by resentment and hate into an act of (3)______; but it takes a strong character to restrain those natural passions. The man who (4)______ an injury proves himself to be the superior of the man who wronged him, and puts the wrong-doer to shame. (5)___ may even turn a foe into a friend.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Resentment and hate carry one away into an act of 'vengeance', that is revenge.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. To forgive an injury is often (1)_______ to be a sign of weakness; it is really a sign of (2)___ . It is easy to allow oneself to be carried away by resentment and hate into an act of (3)______; but it takes a strong character to restrain those natural passions. The man who (4)______ an injury proves himself to be the superior of the man who wronged him, and puts the wrong-doer to shame. (5)___ may even turn a foe into a friend.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: The man who 'forgives' an injury proves himself superior to the man who wronged him.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. To forgive an injury is often (1)_______ to be a sign of weakness; it is really a sign of (2)___ . It is easy to allow oneself to be carried away by resentment and hate into an act of (3)______; but it takes a strong character to restrain those natural passions. The man who (4)______ an injury proves himself to be the superior of the man who wronged him, and puts the wrong-doer to shame. (5)___ may even turn a foe into a friend.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'Forgiveness', the passage's subject, may even turn a foe into a friend.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: If the number of working staff in the company is increased by 20% and the salary per head is decreased by 20%, then the percentage of change in the total salary is:
questions.explanation: Total salary = staff × salary per head, so it becomes 1.2 × 0.8 = 0.96 of what it was: a decrease of 4%.

questions.text: Pankaj bought a watch at a price range from ₹1,500 to ₹3,000 which are sold at prices ranging from ₹2,500 to ₹3,500. If Pankaj sells such 10 watches, then the greatest possible profit (in ₹) he made with the transaction is:
questions.explanation: The profit is greatest when each watch is bought at the lowest price and sold at the highest: (3,500 − 1,500) × 10 = ₹20,000.

questions.text: A 250-metre-long train running at a speed of 100 km/h crosses another train coming from the opposite direction at a speed of 62 km/h in 10 seconds. What is the length of the second train?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 100 + 62 = 162 km/h = 45 m/s, so in 10 seconds the trains cover 450 m between them. The second train is 450 − 250 = 200 metres long.

questions.text: A sum of ₹12,000 becomes double at simple interest in 7 years at a certain rate of simple interest. Find the time (in years) it takes for the amount to become ₹60,000 at the same rate of interest.
questions.explanation: The interest equals the sum in 7 years. To become ₹60,000 the sum must earn 4 times itself, ₹48,000, which takes 4 × 7 = 28 years.

questions.text: A spherical metal ball is melted into a shape of cylinder mounted by a cone such that the base of cone exactly overlaps the top base of cylinder. The diameter of the cylinder and sphere is 4.2 m each. What is the height (in m) of the cone if the height of cylinder is 1.4 m?
questions.explanation: The volumes are equal, with radius 2.1 m throughout: (4/3)π × 2.1³ = π × 2.1² × 1.4 + (1/3)π × 2.1² × h. Dividing by π × 2.1²: 2.8 = 1.4 + h/3, so h = 4.2 m.

questions.text: The average of 7 numbers is 55. If the first 4 numbers are 48, 62, 135 and 74, then what will be the average of the remaining numbers?
questions.explanation: The 7 numbers total 7 × 55 = 385 and the first four 48 + 62 + 135 + 74 = 319, so the other three total 66: an average of 22.

questions.text: Two trains of lengths 310 m and 340 m, respectively, are 285 m apart. They start moving towards each other on parallel tracks, at the speeds of 151 km/h and 155 km/h, respectively. In how much time will the trains cross each other completely?
questions.explanation: To cross completely the trains must close the gap and pass each other: 285 + 310 + 340 = 935 m. Relative speed = 151 + 155 = 306 km/h = 85 m/s, and 935 ÷ 85 = 11 s.

questions.text: Find the number that must be added to the terms of the ratio 11 : 29 to make it equal to 11 : 20.

A right circular solid metallic cone is 7.2 cm high and radius of its base 3.5 cm. It is melted and recast into two right circular solid metallic cones equal in all respects, each with base radius 2.1 cm and height ‘h’. What is the value of ‘h’ (in cm)?
questions.explanation: The volume is unchanged: (1/3)π × 3.5² × 7.2 = 2 × (1/3)π × 2.1² × h, so 88.2 = 8.82h and h = 10 cm.

questions.text: A shopkeeper of a subsidised canteen mixed three varieties of rice, X, Y and Z, in the ratio of 4 : 1 : 3 to make a packet of 4 kg of rice. The cost prices per kg of X, Y and Z varieties of rice are ₹2, ₹4 and ₹6, respectively. What is the cost price (in ₹) of the packet of rice?
questions.explanation: 4 kg in the ratio 4 : 1 : 3 is 2 kg of X, 0.5 kg of Y and 1.5 kg of Z: 2 × 2 + 0.5 × 4 + 1.5 × 6 = 4 + 2 + 9 = ₹15.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2500 as a sum borrowed at 7% per year rate of interest for 2 years.
The average weight of 6 children increases by 1.5 kg when a new child comes in place of one of them weighing 12 kg. The weight of the new child is:
questions.explanation: The total weight rises by 6 × 1.5 = 9 kg, so the new child weighs 12 + 9 = 21 kg.

questions.text: The average height of a group of 10 students is 172 cm. Two more students of height 178 cm and 165 cm joined the group and 3 students of average height 160 cm leave the group. What is the new average height (in cm, rounded off to 1 decimal place) of the group after the changes?
Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2500 as a sum borrowed at 7% per year rate of interest for 4 years.
Which of the following equations is correct by interchanging the ‘+’ and ‘×’ signs and the ‘4’ and ‘5’ numbers?
questions.explanation: Interchanging '+' and '×' and the numbers 4 and 5 turns 20 + 5 × 4 into 20 × 4 + 5 = 80 + 5 = 85. The other three give 65, 54 and 30.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 392 × 7 − 2 ÷ 12 + 80 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 392 ÷ 7 + 2 × 12 − 80 = 56 + 24 − 80 = 0.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘DAYS’ is coded as ‘3917’ and ‘YOLK’ is coded as ‘2496’.What is the code for ‘Y’ in that language?
questions.explanation: Y is the only letter in both words and 9 the only digit in both codes, so Y = 9.

questions.text: 4 is related to 70 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 8 is related to 518. To which ofthe following is 6 related, following the same logic?(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbersinto its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: The second number is the cube of the first plus 6: 4³ + 6 = 70 and 8³ + 6 = 518. Likewise 6³ + 6 = 222.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘YATCH’ is coded as ‘RTMVA’ and ‘CAT’ is coded as ‘VTM’. What is the code for ‘ANAMOLIES’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 7 places back, wrapping round from A to Z: Y → R, A → T, T → M, C → V, H → A. So ANAMOLIES → TGTFHEBXL.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 118 122 130 142 158 ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 4, 8, 12, 16, rising by 4, so the next is 20: 158 + 20 = 178.

questions.text: LO15 is related to OR30 in a certain way. In the same way, SV25 is related to VY50. To which of the following is TW35 related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places forward and the number is doubled: L → O, O → R, 15 → 30. So TW35 → WZ70.

questions.text: This question has two statements followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the given statements. Statements: All arrows are swords. Some swords are dragons. Conclusions (I) Some swords are arrows. (II) Some dragons are not swords.
questions.explanation: As all arrows are swords, some swords are arrows: I follows. Nothing is said about dragons outside the swords, so II does not follow.

questions.text: Seven people A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Exactly three people are sitting between E and B when counted from the right of E. Both G and D are immediate neighbours of F. C is sitting to the immediate left of A. D and E are not sitting next to each other. The position of how many persons will remain unchanged, excluding A, if all the persons are arranged in the English alphabetical order, in clockwise direction, starting from A?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, a person's right is anticlockwise and left clockwise. Clockwise the seats are E, A, C, B, D, F, G: G, F and D sit between E and B on E's right, C is on A's left, F sits between G and D, and D is not next to E. Seated alphabetically clockwise from A they would be A, B, C, D, E, F, G, so only D keeps his seat.

questions.text: Three statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered 1, and 2. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: No Doctor is a Nurse; Some Nurses are Patients; Some Patients are Medicines Conclusions: 1. Some Patients are not Doctors 2. Some Nurses are Medicines
questions.explanation: The nurses who are patients cannot be doctors, so some patients are not doctors: 1 follows. The patients who are medicines need not be nurses, so 2 does not follow.

questions.text: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). G sits second to the left of F, who is third to the left of D. C sits third to the right of B, who is not an immediate neighbour of E. A sits second to the right of B. Who is immediate right of E?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, a person's left is clockwise and right anticlockwise. Clockwise the seats are F, B, G, E, D, C, A: G is second to F's left, F third to D's left, C third and A second to B's right, and E, in the one seat left, is not next to B. E's immediate right is G.

questions.text: NLRP is related to USYW in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, KIOM is related to RPVT. To which of the following is GEKI related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 7 places forward: N → U, L → S, R → Y, P → W, and K → R, I → P, O → V, M → T. So GEKI → NLRP.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? RJK, PMI, NPG, LSE, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move back 2 (R, P, N, L, J), second letters forward 3 (J, M, P, S, V) and third letters back 2 (K, I, G, E, C): JVC.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'MINT' is coded as '9735' and 'NEAR' is coded as '4568'. What is the code for 'N' in the given code language?
questions.explanation: N is the only letter in both words and 5 the only digit in both codes, so N = 5.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘FISH’ is coded as ‘6482’ and ‘SANE’ is coded as ‘7691’. What is the code for ‘S’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: S is the only letter in both words and 6 the only digit in both codes, so S = 6.

questions.text: 19 is related to 39 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 1 is related to 3. To which of the following is 3 related following the same logic?(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbersinto its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: The second number is twice the first plus 1: 2 × 19 + 1 = 39 and 2 × 1 + 1 = 3. Likewise 2 × 3 + 1 = 7.

questions.text: Which is the jet stream that brings Western disturbances in India?
questions.explanation: In winter the westerly jet stream, blowing south of the Himalayas, brings the western disturbances from the Mediterranean region to north and north-west India.

questions.text: Aparna Satheesan, a recipient of 2021 Abhinandan Saroja National award by National Institute of Classical Dance, is an exponent of ________ and Kuchipudi.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Bharatanatyam. Aparna Satheesan, who received the Abhinandan Saroja National Award for 2021, began with Bharatanatyam as a child and performs both it and Kuchipudi; profiles of her also name Mohiniyattam among her other forms.

questions.text: According to Census of India 2011, which pair of states recorded the highest population density (persons/km²) in India?
questions.explanation: In the 2011 census Bihar, at 1,106 persons per km², was the most densely populated state, followed by West Bengal.

questions.text: Identify the place where the West Central Railway Zone headquarters is located.
questions.explanation: The West Central Railway zone has its headquarters at Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh.

questions.text: Which of the following Rashtrakuta rulers performed the ceremony called ‘Hiranya Garbha’?
questions.explanation: The Rashtrakuta founder Dantidurga performed the 'hiranya-garbha' (golden womb) ritual, which was thought to make the performer a Kshatriya by rebirth.

questions.text: Who can exercise a casting vote in the case of an equality of votes in Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: Under Article 100 the Speaker (or whoever presides) does not vote in the first instance, but has a casting vote when the votes are equal.

questions.text: The autobiography of Sam Pitroda is called:
options: Dreaming Big: My Journey to Connect India
questions.explanation: Sam Pitroda's autobiography is 'Dreaming Big: My Journey to Connect India' (2015). The others are the autobiographies of Harivansh Rai Bachchan, Dilip Kumar and Kuldip Nayar.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: On which of the following dates did the British Empire transfer its powers to the Constituent Assembly in India?
questions.explanation: Under the Indian Independence Act, 1947, power passed on 15 August 1947, when the Constituent Assembly also became the legislature of the new Dominion.

questions.text: The Right to Freedom of Religion is covered under which Articles of the Constitution of India?
questions.explanation: Articles 25 to 28 make up the Right to Freedom of Religion.

questions.text: A little child is a very picky eater and hates drinking milk and milk products. When he lost his baby tooth, permanent teeth took a very long time to come up in its place. What could be the probable reason behind this?
questions.explanation: Teeth are built largely of calcium phosphate, and milk is a chief source of calcium; a child who avoids milk may have too little calcium for the new teeth to form.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The 'Quit India Movement' was launched under the leadership of __________________________.
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi launched the Quit India Movement in August 1942 with the call 'Do or Die'.

questions.text: On May 23, 2023, who assumed the position of Chairperson at the Competition Commission of India?
questions.explanation: Ravneet Kaur, a 1988-batch IAS officer, took charge as Chairperson of the Competition Commission of India on 23 May 2023.

questions.text: Which of the following Indian philosophical systems and its widely acknowledged proponents is INCORRECTLY paired?
questions.explanation: The Vaisheshika system is ascribed to Kanada; Vyasa (Badarayana) is linked with the Vedanta. The other three pairs are right.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is/are true about public goods? I. Rivalrous in consumption II. Non-excludability III. Positive marginal cost
questions.explanation: Public goods are non-rivalrous and non-excludable, and serving one more user adds nothing to the cost (zero marginal cost). So only II is true.

questions.text: Which of the following folk dances of Jharkhand, Odisha and West Bengal region is on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity?
questions.explanation: Chhau, the masked dance of Jharkhand, Odisha and West Bengal, was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List in 2010.

questions.text: Where did the IBA Women's World Boxing Championships 2023 take place in India?
questions.explanation: The 2023 IBA Women's World Boxing Championships were held in New Delhi in March 2023.

questions.text: The rifle (in the shooting sport) is single-loaded in _________-millimetre calibre (the inner diameter of a gun barrel), which is used across all events.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 5.6 mm, the .22 calibre of the single-loaded small-bore rifles used in the 50 m rifle events. It is not strictly used in every event: the 10 m air rifle fires 4.5 mm pellets.

questions.text: In Harappan civilisation, which material was NOT used in the construction of buildings?
questions.explanation: The Harappans did not know iron. They built with burnt bricks, used wood, and set the bricks of structures such as the Great Bath in gypsum mortar.

questions.text: The National Food Security Act (NFSA) was enacted in which year by the Government of India?
questions.explanation: The National Food Security Act was enacted in 2013.

questions.text: As of July 2023, how many products were notified under the 'One District, One Product' scheme as per the information provided by the Ministry of Food Processing Industries, Government of India?
questions.explanation: Under the PM Formalisation of Micro food processing Enterprises (PMFME) scheme, the Ministry of Food Processing Industries has approved One District One Product for over 700 districts, covering 137 unique products.

questions.text: Vibration or wave caused by the sudden movement of tectonic plates within the earth that can travel through and around the earth is called:
questions.explanation: The energy of an earthquake travels through and around the earth as seismic waves. A main shock is the largest quake of a sequence and a foreshock a smaller one before it.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following agreements led Mahatma Gandhi to attend the Second Round Table Conference?
questions.explanation: Under the Gandhi-Irwin Pact of March 1931 the Congress called off civil disobedience and agreed to attend the Second Round Table Conference, where Gandhi was its sole representative.

questions.text: What is the primary source of energy for most ecosystems on Earth?
questions.explanation: Plants capture sunlight in photosynthesis, and that energy passes along the food chains to the rest of the ecosystem.

questions.text: Who was the progenitor of the prolific Jaipur-Atrauli gharana?
questions.explanation: Ustad Alladiya Khan founded the Jaipur-Atrauli gharana of Hindustani vocal music.

questions.text: 0.25 g of an organic compound gave 0.20 g of CO₂ after complete combustion. The percentage composition of carbon is _____.
questions.explanation: Carbon in the CO₂ = (12/44) × 0.20 ≈ 0.0545 g, which is (12/44) × (0.20/0.25) × 100 ≈ 21.82% of the compound.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The philanthropist's __________ donations significantly improved the quality of life in the community.
questions.explanation: Donations that improved the community's quality of life were large: 'substantial'. 'Meagre' and 'parsimonious' mean scanty or stingy.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word..
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'faithful': the suffix '-ful' has one 'l'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. She is ___________ of spiders.
questions.explanation: Fear of something is expressed with the adjective 'afraid of': 'She is afraid of spiders.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Dig up dirt
options: To uncover negative information about someone or something.
questions.explanation: To 'dig up dirt' on someone is to search out damaging information about them.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Following weeks of intense training, the athlete ____________________ in the championship.
questions.explanation: A completed past event takes the simple past: 'the athlete competed'. 'Were' and 'have' do not agree with the singular 'the athlete'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'obedience'.

questions.text: Select the grammatically correct sentence from the given options. These are the works of a great poet Tagore.
options: These are the works of that great poet Tagore.
These are the works of an great poet Tagore.
These are the works of this great poet Tagore.
These are the works of the great poet Tagore.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'the great poet Tagore': a well-known person named with a descriptive title takes 'the'. 'An' is wrong before the consonant sound of 'great' and 'this' needs an earlier mention; 'that great poet' is an emphatic use also heard.

questions.text: Select the option that is OPPOSITE in meaning to the underlined word in the given sentence. The state played only a “modest” part in the outstanding advancement of modern morality.
questions.explanation: Of the options only 'boastful' is opposite to 'modest', in its sense of unassuming. 'Humble', 'moderate' and 'unimpressive' are close to its senses, including the 'small' sense it has in 'a modest part'.

questions.text: Select the correct spelling of the incorrectly spelt word in the given sentence. She is an indepandent writer.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'independent'.

questions.text: Select the option that best expresses the meaning of the given idiom. When pigs fly
questions.explanation: 'When pigs fly' describes something that will never happen.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate homophone to fill in the blank.While learning to drive, Shivani met with an accident because she couldn't hit the _________________.
questions.explanation: A car is stopped with its 'brake'; 'break', which sounds the same, means to smash or a pause.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined word. "He was notorious for his “avaricious” behaviour, always seeking ways to accumulate more wealth."
questions.explanation: 'Avaricious' means having an excessive desire for wealth: 'greedy'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The residents of Rameswaram / about the 1940s were quite / orthodox, but were also / tolerant of other communities.
questions.explanation: A period of time takes 'in': 'The residents of Rameswaram in the 1940s were quite orthodox'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. We are planning to see an _________________ perform a symphony.
questions.explanation: A symphony is performed by an orchestra, and 'an' fits the vowel sound of 'orchestra'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The cat likes to _________ in the sun during the afternoon.
questions.explanation: 'Lie' (to rest in a flat position) takes no object; 'lay' needs one, and 'lye' and 'lei' are nouns.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The movie was so boring that I fell _________.
questions.explanation: To 'fall asleep' is to begin sleeping; the adjective 'asleep' follows 'fell'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. After months of / meticulous planning and hard work, / a team successfully launched / their innovative product to the market.
options: their innovative product to the market.
questions.explanation: The team is a particular one, the one that did the planning and whose product it was, so 'the team successfully launched'.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Dr. Oppenheimer is the exceptional movie of all the movies in recent times.
questions.explanation: 'Of all the movies' calls for a superlative: 'the most exceptional movie'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Cacophony
questions.explanation: 'Cacophony' is a harsh mixture of sounds; its opposite is 'harmony'. 'Discord', 'noise' and 'dissonance' are close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Select the grammatically correct sentence from the given options.
options: A salesman insisted that the payment against an purchase should be done by using the bank card.
The salesman insisted that the payment against the purchase should be done by using a bank card.
The salesman insisted that a payment against the purchase should be done by using an bank card.
A salesman insisted that a payment against a purchase should be done by using a bank card.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the version with 'the salesman', 'the payment' and 'the purchase', all particular ones, and 'a bank card', any card. Two versions use 'an' before a consonant sound ('an purchase', 'an bank card'); the all-'a' version is grammatical too, but speaks of no particular salesman or purchase.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In terms of technical difficulty, Nanga Parbat, the world's ninth (1)_____ peak, competes with K2. The first (2)_____ to the summit follows a narrow ridge. The 15,000-foot Rupal Face, a single wall of rock and ice, is located on the mountain's southern side. Climbers have dubbed the Nanga Parbat, which (3)______ as ‘naked mountain’, ‘Killer Mountain’. This gives Annapurna a (4)______ of 32%, making it the most statistically dangerous of the world’s 8,000-metre peaks. It is an avalanche-prone area with some technical difficulty. Climbers’ misery is (5)_______ by insufficient local support, in addition to unpredictable weather and inaccessibility.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Peaks are ranked by height: the world's ninth 'highest' peak.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In terms of technical difficulty, Nanga Parbat, the world's ninth (1)_____ peak, competes with K2. The first (2)_____ to the summit follows a narrow ridge. The 15,000-foot Rupal Face, a single wall of rock and ice, is located on the mountain's southern side. Climbers have dubbed the Nanga Parbat, which (3)______ as ‘naked mountain’, ‘Killer Mountain’. Climbers’ misery is (5)_______ by insufficient local support, in addition to unpredictable weather and inaccessibility.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: An 'ascent' is a climb, here the route by which the summit was first climbed.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In terms of technical difficulty, Nanga Parbat, the world's ninth (1)_____ peak, competes with K2. The first (2)_____ to the summit follows a narrow ridge. Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: A name 'translates as' its meaning in another language: Nanga Parbat means 'naked mountain'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: The share of climbers who die is the 'fatality rate'; 'mortal rate' and 'frailty rate' are not used for this.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In terms of technical difficulty, Nanga Parbat, the world's ninth (1)_____ peak, competes with K2. The first (2)_____ to the summit follows a narrow ridge. The 15,000-foot Rupal Face, a single wall of rock and ice, is located on the mountain's southern side. Climbers have dubbed the Nanga Parbat, which (3)______ as ‘naked mountain’, ‘Killer Mountain’. Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'Exacerbated' means made worse: the climbers' misery is worsened by poor local support. The other options do not fit after 'is' and before 'by'.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: The average weight of a family of five members (in kg) whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 71 kg and 36 kg is:
questions.explanation: The weights add up to 40 + 49 + 56 + 71 + 36 = 252 kg, so the average is 252/5 = 50.4 kg.

questions.text: What sum (in ₹) will earn a simple interest of ₹240 in 4 years at 4% per year rate of interest?
The ratio of two numbers is 15 : 26. If the difference between the numbers is 352, then find the smallest number.
questions.explanation: The difference is 26 − 15 = 11 parts = 352, so one part is 32 and the smaller number is 15 × 32 = 480.

questions.text: A certain shopping site gave successive discounts of 20% and 30% on purses during a new year sale. What is the actual discount received by the customer?
questions.explanation: After 20% and then 30% off, 0.8 × 0.7 = 0.56 of the price is paid: a single discount of 44%.

questions.text: Find the greatest possible length which can be used to measure exactly the lengths 2 m 25 cm, 2 m 70 cm, 3 m 15 cm.
questions.explanation: In centimetres the lengths are 225, 270 and 315. Their HCF is 45 (45 × 5, 45 × 6 and 45 × 7), so the longest measure is 45 cm.

questions.text: Two trains start at the same time from Agra and Meerut and proceed towards each other at speeds of 16 km/h and 32 km/h, respectively. When they meet, it is found that one train has travelled 64 km more than the other. The distance between the two stations is:
questions.explanation: Each hour the faster train covers 32 − 16 = 16 km more than the slower, so the 64 km difference builds up in 4 hours. In 4 hours they cover (16 + 32) × 4 = 192 km between them.

questions.text: The average weight of a family of five members (in kg) whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 71 kg and 35 kg is:
questions.explanation: The weights add up to 40 + 49 + 56 + 71 + 35 = 251 kg, so the average is 251/5 = 50.2 kg.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2000 as a sum borrowed at 6% per year rate of interest for 4 years.
The radius of a circle is equal to the side of a square. The perimeters of the square and circle are in the ratio 7 : 11, then the ratio of the areas will be:(Use π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: With side = radius = r, the perimeters are 4r : 2πr = 7 : 11, as given. The areas are r² : πr² = 1 : 22/7 = 7 : 22.

questions.text: Annu buys a dress from an online designer portal during a festival sale, marked at a price of ₹9,600. She gets a 15% festive discount and a further 10% discount on checkout as it is her first order from the site. How much did she actually pay for the dress?
A shopkeeper mixes three types of pulses costing ₹88/kg, ₹72/kg and ₹62/kg in the ratio of 5 : 2 : 3. The average cost (in ₹) of the mixture per kg is:
A shopkeeper sells one-fourth of his items at a loss of 12%, one-third of the remaining items at a profit of 44%, and the rest at a loss of 7%. What is his overall profit/loss percentage?
questions.explanation: Take 12 items costing ₹1 each. 3 are sold at a 12% loss (−0.36), 3 of the remaining 9 at a 44% profit (+1.32) and the other 6 at a 7% loss (−0.42): a net gain of 0.54 on 12, or 4.5%.

questions.text: A thief Rohan is spotted by a policeman Ramesh from a distance of 250 m. When they see each other, they start running. How much distance is covered by Rohan, who is running at the speed of 20 km/h, before being caught by Ramesh, who is running at the speed of 25 km/h?
questions.explanation: Ramesh gains 25 − 20 = 5 km/h on Rohan, so he closes the 250 m (0.25 km) in 0.25/5 = 1/20 hour. In that time Rohan runs 20 × 1/20 = 1 km.

questions.text: Find the missing term in the below series: F, I, K, N, P, ?, U.
questions.explanation: The letters move +3 and +2 in turn: F (+3) I (+2) K (+3) N (+2) P (+3) S (+2) U.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: A. Some dogs are frogs. B. Some swans are dogs. Conclusions: I. Some frogs are swans. II. No dogs are swans.
questions.explanation: The dogs that are frogs and the dogs that are swans need not be the same, so I does not follow; and as some swans are dogs, 'No dogs are swans' is false. Neither follows.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘FISH’ is coded as ‘8426’ and ‘SAND’ is coded as ‘5749’.What is the code for ‘S’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: S is the only letter in both words and 4 the only digit in both codes, so S = 4.

questions.text: Six players Jadeja, Ashwin, Karthik, Murli, Sarfaraz and Virat are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Virat is sitting to the immediate right of Jadeja. Only Sarfaraz is sitting between Virat and Murli. Jadeja is an immediate neighbour of Ashwin. Who is immediate neighbour of both Sarfaraz and Jadeja?
questions.explanation: Jadeja, Virat, Sarfaraz and Murli sit in that order (Virat beside Jadeja, only Sarfaraz between Virat and Murli), with Ashwin on Jadeja's other side. Virat is the only one next to both Sarfaraz and Jadeja.

questions.text: KL42 is related to PQ50 in a certain way. In the same way, RS52 is related to WX60. To which of the following is DE62 related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Both letters move 5 places forward and the number rises by 8: KL42 → PQ50 and RS52 → WX60. So DE62 → IJ70.

questions.text: UMSO is related to RJPL in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, QIOK is related to NFLH. To which of the following is MEKG related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places back: UMSO → RJPL and QIOK → NFLH. So MEKG → JBHD.

questions.text: M, N, O, P, Q, R and S are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Q sits second to the right of M. P sits third to the left of M. N is an immediate neighbour of S and P. R is not an immediate neighbour of P. Who sits third to the left of R ?
questions.explanation: Clockwise, which is each person's left when facing the centre, the seats run M, S, N, P, O, Q, R: P is third to M's left, Q second to M's right, N between S and P, and R, kept away from P, next to Q. Counting three to R's left gives M, S, N.

questions.text: Three statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered 1 and 2. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All Mangoes are Kiwis; All Kiwis are Guavas; No Guava is an Apple Conclusions: 1. All Apples are Mangoes 2. Some Guavas are Apples
questions.explanation: Every mango is a guava and no guava is an apple, so no apple is a mango: 1 is false. 'Some Guavas are Apples' contradicts the third statement, so 2 does not follow either.

questions.text: 146 is related to 208.4 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 112 is related to 174.4. To which of the following is 135 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbersinto its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is 62.4 more than the first: 146 + 62.4 = 208.4 and 112 + 62.4 = 174.4. Likewise 135 + 62.4 = 197.4.

questions.text: What should come in place of ‘?’ in the given series? 13, 24, 75, 296, 1485, ?
questions.explanation: Multiply by 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and subtract or add the same number in turn: 13 × 2 − 2 = 24, 24 × 3 + 3 = 75, 75 × 4 − 4 = 296, 296 × 5 + 5 = 1485, so 1485 × 6 − 6 = 8904.

questions.text: What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 75 ÷ 27 × 27 + 93 − 20 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 75 × 27 ÷ 27 − 93 + 20 = 75 − 93 + 20 = 2.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘GAVE’ is coded as ‘7485’ and ‘CAGE’ is coded as ‘4589’. What is the code for ‘C’ in that language?
questions.explanation: G, A and E are in both words, and 4, 5 and 8 in both codes. The letter left in CAGE is C and the digit left in its code is 9, so C = 9.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (10, 8, 65) (16, 6, 81) (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The third number is the product of the first two minus 15: 10 × 8 − 15 = 65 and 16 × 6 − 15 = 81. Likewise 7 × 5 − 15 = 20.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘GAME’ is coded as ‘5279’ and ‘META’ is coded as ‘7942’. What is the code for ‘T’ in that language?
questions.explanation: M, E and A are in both words, and 2, 7 and 9 in both codes. The letter left in META is T and the digit left in its code is 4, so T = 4.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 24 ÷ 6 + 18 × 9 – 2 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 24 × 6 − 18 ÷ 9 + 2 = 144 − 2 + 2 = 144.

questions.text: Why will a person weigh more at the north or south pole?
options: Due to variation in centripetal force of earth with altitude
Due to Earth’s distance from the sun
Due to variation in centripetal force of earth with latitude
Due to variation in centrifugal force of earth with latitude
questions.explanation: Earth's rotation produces a centrifugal effect that is greatest at the equator and nil at the poles, so at the poles nothing is taken off a body's weight. The poles are also nearer Earth's centre, which adds to the difference.

questions.text: Which festival is celebrated as the birth anniversary of Prophet Muhammad?
questions.explanation: Milad-un-Nabi marks the birth of the Prophet Muhammad, in the Islamic month of Rabi-ul-Awwal.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is/are true about the Cholas? 1 The capital of the Chola kingdom was Tanjore. 2 Vikram Chola had in his veins the blood of the Cholas and Eastern Chalukyas. 3 Rajendra I Chola is known as Gangaikonda Chola.
questions.explanation: Thanjavur (Tanjore) was the Chola capital from Vijayalaya's time until Rajendra I built Gangaikondacholapuram. Vikrama Chola was the son of Kulottunga I, himself the son of an Eastern Chalukya king of Vengi and a Chola princess, and Rajendra I took the title Gangaikonda Chola after his campaign to the Ganga. All three are true.

questions.text: Which Indian state's cabinet approved the proposal for recommending the inclusion of the Kui language in the eighth schedule in July 2023?
questions.explanation: In July 2023 Odisha's cabinet approved recommending Kui, the language of the Kandha (Kondh) tribe, for inclusion in the Eighth Schedule.

questions.text: In which of the following dance performance is the main percussion instrument Edakka used?
questions.explanation: The edakka, an hourglass-shaped drum of Kerala, accompanies Mohiniyattam, one of the state's classical dances.

questions.text: According to the census of India 2011, which union territory of India has the highest literacy rate?
questions.explanation: Census 2011 put Lakshadweep's literacy rate at about 92%, the highest of the union territories; Delhi, Chandigarh and Puducherry were near 86%.

questions.text: For most of the ecosystem, what is the primary source of energy?
questions.explanation: Almost every ecosystem runs on sunlight, which green plants capture by photosynthesis and pass up the food chain.

questions.text: Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award is given for the spectacular and most outstanding performance in the field of sports by a sportsperson over a period of the previous four years. In 2021, the awardee for para shooting was:
questions.explanation: Avani Lekhara, who won shooting gold at the Tokyo Paralympics, received the Khel Ratna in 2021. Neeraj Chopra was honoured the same year, for athletics.

questions.text: In which year did India host the FIFA U 17 Women's Football World Cup?
questions.explanation: India hosted the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup in October 2022.

questions.text: Which local storm is also known as 'Kalbaisakhi'?
questions.explanation: Kalbaisakhi, 'the calamity of the month of Baisakh', is West Bengal's name for the nor'westers, violent evening thunderstorms of the hot season.

questions.text: Which poet composed the Allahabad Prashasti of Samudragupta?
questions.explanation: Harisena, Samudragupta's court poet, composed the Allahabad (Prayaga) Prashasti, inscribed on the Ashokan pillar at Allahabad.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following sessions of the Indian National Congress was headed by Sarojini Naidu?
questions.explanation: Sarojini Naidu presided over the Kanpur session of 1925, the first Indian woman to be Congress president.

questions.text: In which of the following types of regions, is the maximum temperature variation observed between a day and the same night?
questions.explanation: Deserts have the widest daily range of temperature: dry air and clear skies let the ground heat up fast by day and lose the heat fast at night.

questions.text: The Government of India in collaboration with ___________ has launched the Skills on Wheels mission in Oct 2023 for equipping rural youth with employable skills.
questions.explanation: Skills on Wheels, a bus that takes digital-skills training and news of free courses to rural youth, was launched in 2023 with the National Skill Development Corporation and IndusInd Bank.

questions.text: During the framing of the Indian Constitution, the Constituent Assembly held a total of eleven sessions, with sittings spread over for how many days?
questions.explanation: The Constituent Assembly met in eleven sessions over 2 years, 11 months and 18 days, sitting on 165 days in all.

questions.text: What is the tenure of a Governor?
questions.explanation: Under Article 156 a Governor holds office for five years, though at the pleasure of the President.

questions.text: Which of the following sectors engaged the largest percentage of women workers in the year 2019-2020?
questions.explanation: The Periodic Labour Force Survey for 2019-20 found more than half of India's women workers engaged in agriculture, far more than in any other sector.

questions.text: Which substance is commonly added to tap water to make it safe for drinking by killing harmful microorganisms?
questions.explanation: Chlorine is added to drinking water to kill bacteria and other germs; fluoride, added in some places, protects teeth rather than disinfecting.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who appointed the ‘Hunter Commission’ for Educational Reforms in 1882?
questions.explanation: Lord Ripon set up the Hunter Commission in 1882, under Sir William Hunter, to review the progress of education since Wood's Despatch of 1854.

questions.text: Which famous monument of Vijayapura has a Whispering Gallery, where subtle sounds can be heard clearly even from a distance of 37 metres?
questions.explanation: The Gol Gumbaz, the tomb of Mohammed Adil Shah at Vijayapura (Bijapur), has a gallery under its dome where a whisper carries right across.

questions.text: The concept of the Self-Help Group Bank Linkage Program was introduced by:
questions.explanation: NABARD launched the SHG-Bank Linkage Programme in 1992, linking self-help groups to banks for savings and credit.

questions.text: The title of the autobiography of famous cricketer of Pakistan Imran Khan is:
questions.explanation: Imran Khan's autobiography is 'All Round View' (1988). 'Game Changer' is Shahid Afridi's.

questions.text: ___________ was an Indian mandolinist who was a master composer of the Carnatic style of classical music.
questions.explanation: U. Srinivas (Uppalapu Srinivas) brought the mandolin into Carnatic music. Ravikiran plays the chitravina, Prasanna the guitar, and Kunnakudi Vaidyanathan was a violinist.

questions.text: Which region in India has the highest concentration of Iron and Steel Industry?
questions.explanation: Most of India's iron and steel plants are in the Chotanagpur plateau region, where iron ore, coal and other raw materials lie close together.

questions.text: In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative. Poverty is the “urgent” concern in India today.
questions.explanation: Poverty is compared with all other concerns, so the superlative is needed: 'the most urgent concern'. 'Urgent' takes 'more' and 'most', not '-er' and '-est'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word..
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'perseverance'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Manoj has a bigger / farmhouse of one hundred / hectares near the city.
questions.explanation: Nothing is being compared, so the comparative 'bigger' does not fit: 'Manoj has a big farmhouse'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Destroy
questions.explanation: To 'destroy' something is to 'ruin' it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. My hands are full
questions.explanation: 'My hands are full' means that I am very busy.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'secrecy'.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word to fill in the blank and make the sentence meaningful. Before retiring, Kaul had been teaching physics at the university for three __________________.
questions.explanation: 'Three decades' is thirty years of teaching; 'decimals' and 'decadents' do not fit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word segment that can replace the underlined part in the sentence. The two thieves divided the looted money “with themselves”.
questions.explanation: 'Between' is used of two: the two thieves divided the money 'between themselves'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and complete the given idiom. That’s great! You keep everything under your _________________.
questions.explanation: To have something 'under your thumb' is to have it completely under your control.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Autumn leaves “shuffled beneath him” as he wandered through the quiet forest.
questions.explanation: Dry leaves 'rustle underfoot' as one walks over them; to 'shuffle' is to walk dragging one's feet.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. They worked / very hardly / on their project / for several weeks.
questions.explanation: 'Hardly' means scarcely; the adverb for working with effort is 'hard': 'They worked very hard'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. His artwork is / more intricate / than any artist / in the gallery.
questions.explanation: Like must be compared with like: 'more intricate than that of any other artist', not than an artist.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The land that is best suitable for growing crops
questions.explanation: 'Arable' land is fit for ploughing and growing crops.

questions.text: In the following sentence the underlined part contains as error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative. The water near the coast was “shallower” and clean.
questions.explanation: Nothing is compared, and 'clean' is in the positive degree, so 'shallow and clean'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Appease
questions.explanation: To 'appease' someone is to calm them by giving in to their demands: to 'pacify' them.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Whim
questions.explanation: A 'whim' is a sudden 'fancy' or impulse.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The ___________ of the novel kept me hooked from the beginning to the end.
questions.explanation: A novel's 'plot', its sequence of events, is what keeps a reader hooked.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I am not going to pay a ________ for this broken CD.
questions.explanation: A 'cent' is a coin of very little value; 'send', 'sent' and 'scent' only sound similar.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Benevolent
questions.explanation: 'Benevolent' means kind and well-meaning; its opposite is 'malevolent', wishing harm to others.

questions.text: The given sentence is divided into four segments. Select the option that has the segment with a grammatical error. He has / no / influence about / me.
questions.explanation: One has 'influence on' (or 'over') someone, not 'influence about'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The eye of an ostrich is larger than its brain. Of all birds, ostriches have the 1.________ eyes. Their eyes are the size of a pool ball, measuring around 2 inches in diameter. Their size is five times greater than that of human eyes. Ostriches have excellent vision, so their enormous eyes aren't just for show. Because of their height and keen 2.________, the birds can see well over great distances, enabling them to identify potential 3._________ before they approach. In general, compared to mammals of comparable size, birds often have smaller brains. Ostrich brains are approximately 1.5 inches in width, the study found. Additionally, their average brain weight is almost 17 times lower than that of the three other 4._____. When comparing the brain-to-body weight ratio of the other birds, the ostrich's brain was lighter than their body weight. Some other facts concerning these birds are what set them apart. All other birds have three or four toes; this magnificent creature has only two. Ostriches bend their knees in a forward orientation; thus, they kick forward rather than backward. Furthermore, ostriches do not require water because they produce some of it internally and obtain the 5._______ from the plants they consume.

Select the most appropriate option for blank 1.
questions.explanation: 'Of all birds' calls for the superlative: 'the biggest eyes'.
