markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: The average weight of a family of five members (in kg) whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 69 kg and 39 kg is:
The average weight of a family of five members (in kg) whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 68 kg and 37 kg is:

In a group of sports persons, 20 wrestlers have an average weight of 90 kg, while some athletes have an average weight of 68 kg. If the average weight of all sports persons is 78 kg, then the number of athletes is:
A man covers 30 km by car at a speed of 60 km/h and another 20 km by cycle. His whole journey is completed in 3 hours. What is the speed (in km/h) of the cycle?
questions.explanation: The car takes 30/60 = 0.5 hour, leaving 2.5 hours for the 20 km by cycle: 20/2.5 = 8 km/h.

questions.text: What sum (in ₹) will earn a simple interest of ₹240 in 3 years at 20% per year rate of interest?
What sum (in ₹) will earn a simple interest of ₹360 in 2 years at 20% per year rate of interest?
If the length and breadth of a rectangle are 7cm and 5cm, respectively, the area of the rectangle is:
questions.explanation: Area = length × breadth = 7 × 5 = 35 cm².

questions.text: The average score of boys in an examination in a school is 71 and that of the girls is 73. The average score of the school is 71.8. The ratio of the number of boys to that of the girls that appeared in the examination is:
questions.explanation: With b boys and g girls: 71b + 73g = 71.8(b + g), so 1.2g = 0.8b and b : g = 1.2 : 0.8 = 3 : 2.

questions.text: The product of LCM and HCF of two numbers is 24. If the difference between the two numbers is 2, then find the numbers.
questions.explanation: LCM × HCF equals the product of the two numbers, so they multiply to 24 and differ by 2: 6 and 4.

questions.text: If 49 : x :: x : 81 and 64 : y :: y : 169, where x and y are both natural numbers, then find the value of 2x + 3y.
questions.explanation: x is the mean proportional of 49 and 81: x² = 49 × 81, so x = 63. Likewise y² = 64 × 169, so y = 104. 2x + 3y = 126 + 312 = 438.

questions.text: The height of Aaryan was 120 cm. After 1 year,his height increased by 15%, and in the next 1 year, his height increased by 16%. What will be the height (in cm) of Aaryan after the second years?
questions.explanation: 120 × 1.15 = 138 cm after the first year, and 138 × 1.16 = 160.08 cm after the second.

questions.text: A person can complete a journey in 21 hours. He covers the first one-third of the journey at the speed of 40 km/h and the remaining distance at the speed of 60 km/h. What is the total distance of his journey?
questions.explanation: With distance D: (D/3)/40 + (2D/3)/60 = D/120 + D/90 = 7D/360 = 21 hours, so D = 1080 km.

questions.text: Ramesh bought a watch for Rs.460 and sold it for Rs.414. Find his percentage of loss
By selling a book for ₹480 at marked price, a shopkeeper gains 20%. During a clearance sale, the shopkeeper allows a discount of 10% on the marked price. What is his gain per cent during the sale?
questions.explanation: Cost price = 480/1.2 = ₹400. In the sale the book goes for 90% of ₹480 = ₹432, a gain of ₹32 on ₹400: 8%.

questions.text: The difference between simple interests on a certain sum at the annual rate of 6% for 6 years and 8% for 8 years is ₹1,176. What is the sum?
questions.explanation: The two interest amounts differ by (8 × 8 − 6 × 6)% = 28% of the sum, so the sum = 1,176/0.28 = ₹4,200.

questions.text: CMGW is related to XHDT in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, SCAQ is related to NXXN. To which of the following is ISUK related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: The first two letters move 5 places back and the last two 3 places back: C → X, M → H, G → D, W → T. So I → D, S → N, U → R, K → H: DNRH.

questions.text: 12 is related to 61 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 15 is related to 76. To which of the following is 18 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is 5 times the first plus 1: 12 × 5 + 1 = 61 and 15 × 5 + 1 = 76. Likewise 18 × 5 + 1 = 91.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the statement(s). Statements: Some salaries are bonus. All wages are bonus. Conclusions: (I) Some salaries are wages. (II) All bonus are wages.
questions.explanation: Salaries and wages can both overlap with bonus without overlapping each other, so I does not follow. All wages being bonus does not make all bonus wages, so II does not follow.

questions.text: 2 is related to 15 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 6 is related to 43. To which of the following is 9 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 - Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is 7 times the first plus 1: 2 × 7 + 1 = 15 and 6 × 7 + 1 = 43. Likewise 9 × 7 + 1 = 64.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘–’ and ‘÷‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘+’ are interchanged? 70 ÷ 90 – 10 + 20 × 80 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 70 − 90 ÷ 10 × 20 + 80 = 70 − 180 + 80 = −30.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 36, 39, 44, 51, 60, 71, 84, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, so the next is 15: 84 + 15 = 99.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if '+' and '-' are interchanged and '×' and '÷' are interchanged? 81 × 3 - 9 ÷ 3 + 2 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 81 ÷ 3 + 9 × 3 − 2 = 27 + 27 − 2 = 52.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘black dark night’ is coded as ‘ck th lp’ and ‘dark cloudy sky’ is coded as ‘eg lp sc’. How is ‘dark’ coded in the given language?
questions.explanation: 'dark' is the only word in both phrases and 'lp' the only code in both, so dark = lp.

questions.text: Seven people A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). D is sitting second to the left of F. A is sitting third to the right of B. C is sitting to the immediate right of D. Only two people are sitting between F and G. How many people are sitting between C and G when counted from the left of G?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, a person's left is clockwise. With D second to F's left and C at D's right, A third to the right of B fits only when G is three seats to F's right; clockwise the order is F, C, D, A, G, E, B. Going round from G to its left, E, B and F come before C: three.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? AGK, FLP, KQU, PVZ, ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 5 places forward, wrapping round after Z: P → U, V → A, Z → E. So UAE.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some doors are rocks. All rocks are woods. Conclusions: (I) At least some woods are doors. (II) All woods are rocks.
questions.explanation: The doors that are rocks are also woods, so some woods are doors (I). All rocks being woods does not make all woods rocks, so II does not follow.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘WEAR’ is coded as ‘PI1O’ and ‘EARS’ is coded as ‘I4OP’. What is the code for ‘S’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: E, A and R are in both words, as are I, O and P in both codes. The letter left in WEAR is W and the code left is 1; in EARS they are S and 4. So S = 4.

questions.text: A, E, I, O, U, S and K are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). K is to the immediate right of O. E is the immediate neighbour of both O and S. I is neither an immediate neighbour of S nor A. Who sits to the immediate right of U?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, a person's right is anticlockwise. O has K on its right and E on its other side, with S beyond E. I may sit next to neither S nor A, so I takes the seat beside K, A the seat beside S and U the one between them. Clockwise: O, E, S, A, U, I, K, so A is to U's immediate right.

questions.text: In a certain code language,‘shirt pant coat’ is coded as ‘ek ph bq’,‘coat jacket sweater’ is coded as ‘ek lh to’,‘jacket shirt watch’ is coded as ‘fd bq lh’. What is the code for‘coat’ in that language?(Note: All the codes are two-letter coded only.)
questions.explanation: 'coat' is the only word in the first two phrases and 'ek' the only code in both, so coat = ek.

questions.text: GNEE is related to JQHH in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, BHYY is related to EKBB. To which of the following is QXOO related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places forward: G → J, N → Q, E → H; B → E, H → K, Y → B. So Q → T, X → A, O → R: TARR.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘JUMP’ is coded as ‘4682’ and ‘MIND’ is coded as ‘3741’.What is the code for ‘M’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: M is the only letter in both words and 4 the only digit in both codes, so M = 4.

questions.text: Anuradhapura, the old capital of Sri Lanka, was destroyed by which of the following dynasties of South India in the 10th century AD?
questions.explanation: The Chola king Rajaraja I invaded Sri Lanka in 993 AD and sacked Anuradhapura; the Cholas then ruled the north of the island from Polonnaruwa.

questions.text: What is the atomic number of uranium (U)?
questions.explanation: A uranium atom has 92 protons, so its atomic number is 92.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: When was the Jallianwala Bagh massacre brought into action by the Britishers in Amritsar?
questions.explanation: General Dyer's troops fired on an unarmed crowd at Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar, on 13 April 1919, the day of Baisakhi.

questions.text: Kanaka Raju, who kept the tribal folk dance Gussadi alive, was honoured with which of the following civilian awards of India in 2021?
questions.explanation: Kanaka Raju, a Gond dancer from Telangana who kept Gussadi alive, received the Padma Shri in 2021.

questions.text: The Citadel area has a huge mud ________ platform, which is 6 m high and underlies all the construction.
questions.explanation: Harappan citadels were raised on platforms of mud brick, which lifted their buildings above the rest of the town.

questions.text: The Indus Water Treaty took place in ________ between India and Pakistan.
questions.explanation: The Indus Waters Treaty, brokered by the World Bank, was signed at Karachi in September 1960 by Jawaharlal Nehru and Ayub Khan.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The planned large-scale disruption of rail communications and the seizure of arms in Bengal were undertaken under the leadership of ________.
questions.explanation: During the First World War the Jugantar revolutionaries under Jatin Mukherjee (Bagha Jatin) planned a rising in Bengal, with German arms, that was to cut rail links and seize arms; he was killed in a fight with the police near Balasore in 1915.

questions.text: The revival of the art form in the late 1940s was spearheaded by maestros such as Kelucharan Mohapatra and Raghunath Dutta in the field of ____________.
questions.explanation: Gurus such as Kelucharan Mohapatra led the revival of Odissi, Odisha's classical dance, from the late 1940s.

questions.text: A child is a picky eater. He does not consume milk at all and barely eats other kinds of food. When he started losing his baby teeth, they were not getting replaced with new teeth. This can be solved by giving him ___________.
questions.explanation: Teeth and bones need calcium, and milk is its main source in a child's diet; calcium supplements make up the lack.

questions.text: Which of the following is included in the estimation of Gross National Product?
questions.explanation: GNP counts the goods and services produced in the year, such as new shirts. Second-hand sales (used cars), transfer payments (pensions) and financial transactions (securities) add nothing to current output.

questions.text: Which of the following Indian cities was the host of the ICC Men's World Cup final cricket match in 2023?
questions.explanation: The final of the 2023 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup was played at the Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad, on 19 November 2023.

questions.text: Kala Ramnath belonged to which of the following gharanas?
questions.explanation: The violinist Kala Ramnath, a disciple of Pandit Jasraj, belongs to the Mewati gharana.

questions.text: The 9th Asian Games was hosted by which of the following countries?
questions.explanation: New Delhi hosted the 9th Asian Games in 1982.

questions.text: In January 2023, the Chief Minister's Residential Land Rights Scheme (Mukhyamantri Awasiya Bhu Adhikar Yojana) was launched in which Indian state?
questions.explanation: The Mukhyamantri Awasiya Bhu Adhikar Yojana is Madhya Pradesh's scheme giving free residential plots to rural families who have no home of their own.

questions.text: As per Census 2011, which of the following states has the lowest child sex ratio?
questions.explanation: In the 2011 Census Haryana had the lowest child sex ratio (0-6 years) of any state, 834 girls per 1,000 boys.

questions.text: Every year, Karthik Purnima marks the end of a livestock fair in Pushkar, where the main animal on display is:
questions.explanation: The Pushkar fair in Rajasthan, which ends on Kartik Purnima, is famous as a camel fair.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECT statement regarding Ozone.
options: Ozone is formed from oxygen in the presence of ultraviolet radiation.
Ozone (O₃), like oxygen, is a life-supporting gas.
questions.explanation: NCERT calls ozone a deadly poison: its value lies in the upper atmosphere, where it absorbs the sun's ultraviolet radiation. Unlike oxygen, it does not support life.

questions.text: Who is the author of the English novel ‘Voting at Fosterganj’?
questions.explanation: 'Voting at Fosterganj', about an election coming to a small hill town near Mussoorie, is by Ruskin Bond.

questions.text: Which writ is issued by the High Court or Supreme Court when a lower court considers a case going beyond its jurisdiction?
questions.explanation: A writ of prohibition is issued by a higher court to a lower court or tribunal to stop it from exceeding its jurisdiction.

questions.text: Tsunami is a natural disaster that originates from the ocean. The cause of Tsunami in the ocean is:
options: The movement of tectonic plates under the ocean
The presence of excessive carbon dioxide in the water
The alarmingly increasing amount of acid in water
The accumulation of high amount of radioactive pollutants in the ocean
questions.explanation: Tsunamis are mostly set off by undersea earthquakes, when tectonic plates shift suddenly and displace the water above them.

questions.text: Which of the following organisations in India provides facilities for acquisition of satellite data and its processing?
questions.explanation: The National Remote Sensing Centre, Hyderabad, an ISRO centre, acquires, processes and distributes remote-sensing satellite data; IIRS, Dehradun, trains people in remote sensing.

questions.text: Which of the following periods in India is also associated with the Iron Age?
questions.explanation: Iron came into wide use in the Later Vedic period (about 1000-600 BC), whose texts call it 'shyama ayas' or 'krishna ayas'.

questions.text: What was the unemployment rate of Gujarat in November 2021?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 1.4%. CMIE's monthly surveys put Gujarat among the states with the lowest unemployment at the time (1.6% in December 2021), far below the all-India rate of about 7% in November 2021.

questions.text: An Indian Parliamentary delegation led by Minister of Parliamentary Affairs, Coal and Mines ______________________ visited Brazil from 11 to 13 June 2023.
questions.explanation: Pralhad Joshi, Minister of Parliamentary Affairs, Coal and Mines, led Parliament's goodwill delegation to Brazil in June 2023.

questions.text: As per Article 157 of the Constitution of India, a person needs to complete the age of ____________ years to be appointed as Governor.
questions.explanation: Under Article 157 a person must be a citizen of India and have completed 35 years of age to be appointed Governor.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Whoever got the “few” answers correct has to leave the room.
questions.explanation: Among more than two people the superlative of 'few' is needed: 'Whoever got the fewest answers correct'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. The vegetation in this area of the forest is very “dense”.
questions.explanation: 'Dense' means thick or closely packed; its opposite is 'sparse', thinly scattered.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence. Adi had “not only assisted her by” giving evidence in the case but also provided many examples to prove her point in the court.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'assisted her not only by', which puts 'not only' directly before the phrase it limits, 'by giving evidence'. The sentence as printed ('had not only assisted ... but also provided') is arguably already balanced, and the keyed version pairs 'by giving' with 'provided', but no option keeps the original.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. My aunt came from Switzerland by the flight which was landing at 5:00 a.m. yesterday.
questions.explanation: A single completed action at a stated past time takes the simple past: 'the flight which landed at 5:00 a.m. yesterday'.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. The car which I bought last year was cheap than my bike.
questions.explanation: 'Than' needs the comparative: 'was cheaper than my bike'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom/phrase. Throw in the towel
options: To cause an activity or process to continue
To take responsibility for a situation while another person is temporarily absent
questions.explanation: To 'throw in the towel' is to give up or admit defeat.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The plan was very ____________ and took a lot of time to develop.
questions.explanation: After 'was very' the complement is an adjective: 'The plan was very elaborate'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A serpent having many heads in Greek mythology
questions.explanation: The Hydra was the many-headed serpent of Greek myth that Heracles killed.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'infinite'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. (1) We knocked across (2) early on Saturday (3) to enjoy (4) the beautiful weather.
questions.explanation: 'Knock across' is not an English phrasal verb; 'knock off' (stop work) fits the sense: 'We knocked off early on Saturday to enjoy the beautiful weather.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate antonym for the word provided in the bracket to fill in the blank. The professor delivered a ___________________ lecture on quantum physics. (simplified)
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'simplified' is 'complex': 'a complex lecture on quantum physics'.

questions.text: Select the appropriate option that can substitute the underlined idiom in the given sentence. The interns explained the whole issue to the coordinator “in a nutshell”.
questions.explanation: 'In a nutshell' means briefly, in a few words.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Please hang with for two minutes while I finish cleaning the utensils.
questions.explanation: Asking someone to wait is 'hang on': 'Please hang on for two minutes'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Hamper
questions.explanation: To 'hamper' is to hinder or obstruct.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks. A buzzing ______ can ____ dangerous.
questions.explanation: A 'bee' is the insect and 'be' the verb: 'A buzzing bee can be dangerous.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. With the increasing reliance on digital systems, ensuring robust cybersecurity measures is _______________ to protect against online threats.
questions.explanation: 'Paramount' means of supreme importance; 'superfluous' means unnecessary, 'extraneous' irrelevant and 'impartial' unbiased.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelled sentence.
options: The sceintist discovered a new palnet in the galaxy.
The scienetist discovered a new planet in the galaxy.
The scientist discovered a new planet in the galaxy.
The scientist discovred a new planet in the galexy.
questions.explanation: Only this sentence spells 'scientist', 'discovered', 'planet' and 'galaxy' correctly.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM for the underlined word in the given sentence. Her profile was “complete” on the company website.
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'complete' is 'incomplete'.

questions.text: Identify the error in the usage of the future tense in the given sentence and choose the correct sentence from the following options. Parvati finish the painting in one hour.
options: Parvati will finish the painting in one hour.
Parvati was finished the painting in one hour.
Parvati has been finishing the painting in one hour.
Parvati had been finishing the painting in one hour.
questions.explanation: The simple future is 'will' with the base verb: 'Parvati will finish the painting in one hour.'

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Until that moment, every director in Hollywood had accepted as gospel (1)_______ that the audience should not be taxed too much. Welles struck a (2)_______ at these beliefs, without displaying the slightest of qualms. Visually, 'Citizen Kane' was shot with a harsh sharpness which (3)_____ every scene. Traditionally, every make-up man and cameraman in Hollywood had to keep a careful (4)_______ on the appearance of the heroine. Welles refused to follow this (5)_____ in the case of his own heroine. For the first time, dialogue was presented in its realistic form.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1
questions.explanation: To accept something 'as gospel truth' is to accept it as unquestionably true.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2
questions.explanation: To 'strike a blow at' something is to attack it; 'blew' is only the past tense of 'blow'.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3

Until that moment, every director in Hollywood had accepted as gospel (1)_______ that the audience should not be taxed too much. For the first time, dialogue was presented in its realistic form.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4
questions.explanation: To 'keep an eye on' something is to watch it carefully.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Until that moment, every director in Hollywood had accepted as gospel (1)_______ that the audience should not be taxed too much. Welles struck a (2)_______ at these beliefs, without displaying the slightest of qualms. Visually, 'Citizen Kane' was shot with a harsh sharpness which (3)_____ every scene. Traditionally, every make-up man and cameraman in Hollywood had to keep a careful (4)_______ on the appearance of the heroine. Welles refused to follow this (5)_____ in the case of his own heroine. For the first time, dialogue was presented in its realistic form.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5
questions.explanation: 'Follow this practice' needs the noun 'practice', a custom; 'practise' is the British spelling of the verb.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: The average score of 12 girls in a test was 16.5 and that of 18 boys in the same test was 16. The average score of girls and boys taken together in the same test was:
I walk at a speed of 10 km/h and reach the destination in 2 hours. If I increase my speed by 5 km/h, how early would I reach my destination?
questions.explanation: The distance is 10 × 2 = 20 km. At 15 km/h it takes 20/15 = 4/3 hours = 80 minutes, 40 minutes less than 2 hours.

questions.text: In an office having 160 staff members, 40% are females and the remaining are males. The average weight of females is 58 kg and that of males is 63 kg. Find the average weight of all staff members.
Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2500 as a sum borrowed at 4% per year rate of interest for 6 years.
A man buys 15 identical articles for a total of ₹15. If he sells each of them for ₹1.32, then his profit percentage is:
questions.explanation: Each article costs ₹15/15 = ₹1 and sells for ₹1.32, a profit of ₹0.32 on ₹1: 32%.

questions.text: A person lent a sum of ₹30,000 on simple interest for 12 years, with an interest rate of 8% per annum for the first 4 years, 10% per annum for the next 3 years, and 15% per annum for last 5 years. How much interest (in ₹) will he earn at the end of 12 years?
The average age of a man and his son is 48 years. The ratio of their ages is 5 : 3. What is the son's age?
questions.explanation: Their ages total 2 × 48 = 96 years, so the son is 3/8 × 96 = 36.

questions.text: When a number is first increased by 18% and then decreased by 18%, the change in the number is ____________.
questions.explanation: 1.18 × 0.82 = 0.9676 of the number is left: a fall of 3.24% (x²/100 = 18²/100).

questions.text: A vehicle moves at 65 km/h for 4 hours before slowing down to 52 km/h for the next 2.5 hours. Calculate the average speed.
What is the radius of the largest right circular cone that can be cut out from a cube of edge 8.4 cm ?
questions.explanation: The largest cone stands on one face, its base the circle inscribed in that face: radius 8.4/2 = 4.2 cm (height 8.4 cm).

questions.text: A printer with a marked price of ₹9,000 is offered on successive discounts of 30%, 20%, and 15%. Identify the printer's selling price.
The average of seven consecutive natural numbers is 56. The greatest number among them is:
questions.explanation: The average of consecutive numbers is the middle one, so the seven are 53 to 59; the greatest is 59.

questions.text: What sum (in ₹) will earn a simple interest of ₹240 in 4 years at 20% per year rate of interest?

Which two numbers should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? (12÷ 3) × 18 - 2× 4 + 42÷ 6 = 69 (Note: Interchange should be done of entire number and not individual digits of a given number)

Read the given statement(s) and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement(s). Statements: No lizard is a snake. All lizards are reptiles. Conclusions: (I) At least some reptiles are snakes. (II) All reptiles are lizards.
questions.explanation: Nothing links reptiles to snakes beyond the lizards, which are not snakes, so I does not follow; and all lizards being reptiles does not make all reptiles lizards, so II does not follow either.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘you are a good friend’ is coded as ‘es an pz fd mq’ and ‘his friend is very kind’ is coded as ‘ck mq pn ag sb’. How is ‘friend’ coded in the given language?
questions.explanation: 'friend' is the only word in both sentences and 'mq' the only code in both, so friend = mq.

questions.text: 13 is related to 103 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 9 is related to 71. To which of the following is 15 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding / subtracting / multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each number is multiplied by 8 and 1 subtracted: 13 × 8 − 1 = 103 and 9 × 8 − 1 = 71. Likewise 15 × 8 − 1 = 119.

questions.text: JQMT is related to PWSZ in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, HOKR is related to NUQX. To which of the following is FMIP related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 6 places forward: J → P, Q → W, M → S, T → Z, and HOKR → NUQX the same way. So F → L, M → S, I → O, P → V: LSOV.

questions.text: Seven people A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). B is sitting second to the left of C. Only two people are sitting between B and D. D is an immediate neighbour of C. A is sitting third to the right of F. E is sitting to the immediate left of G. What is the position of E with respect to B?
questions.explanation: With B second to C's left, D on C's other side (C and F between D and B), A third to F's right and E on G's left, the order going round to each person's left is C, F, B, G, E, A, D. E is second to the left of B.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? AEH, DHK, GKN, JNQ, ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places forward each time: A, D, G, J, M; E, H, K, N, Q; H, K, N, Q, T. So MQT.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘MOTH’ is coded as ‘2514’ and ‘TOME’ is coded as ‘1453’. What is the code for ‘E’ in that language?
questions.explanation: M, O and T are in both words and 1, 4 and 5 in both codes. H, left in MOTH, is 2, and E, left in TOME, is 3.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the following series? 3, 7, 15, 31, 63, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is twice the one before plus 1: 63 × 2 + 1 = 127.

questions.text: In a code language, 'ROASTER' is coded as '96' and 'GUM' is coded as '41'. How will 'ARTIST' be coded in the same language?
questions.explanation: The code is the sum of the letters' places in the alphabet: ROASTER = 18 + 15 + 1 + 19 + 20 + 5 + 18 = 96 and GUM = 7 + 21 + 13 = 41. ARTIST = 1 + 18 + 20 + 9 + 19 + 20 = 87.

questions.text: What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 29 × 841 ÷ 87 + 37 – 59 = ?

The second number in the given number pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. Select the pair in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the given pairs. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 11, 88; 14, 112
questions.explanation: The second number is 8 times the first: 11 × 8 = 88 and 14 × 8 = 112. Likewise 16 × 8 = 128.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: No soap is a lotion. No lotion is a conditioner. Conclusions: (I) No soap is a conditioner. (II) Some conditioners are lotions.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusion I and II follow
questions.explanation: Soaps and conditioners are both kept apart from lotions, which says nothing about soaps and conditioners, so I does not follow. As no lotion is a conditioner, no conditioner is a lotion, so II is false.

questions.text: Six persons – L, M, N, O, P and Q – are sitting around a circular table facing the centre, but not necessarily in the same order. O is sitting second to the left of Q. P is not an immediate neighbour of Q. M is sitting second to the right of L. N is sitting to the immediate right of Q. Who is an immediate neighbour of both, L and N?
questions.explanation: O is second to Q's left and N on Q's right; with P not beside Q and M second to L's right, the order going round to each person's left is Q, M, O, L, P, N. P sits between L and N.

questions.text: Which of the following vitamins includes cobalt as an essential component?
questions.explanation: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) has a cobalt atom at the centre of its molecule.

questions.text: The construction of Mehrangarh fort of Jodhpur was initiated during the reign of which ruler?
questions.explanation: Rao Jodha, the Rathore ruler who founded Jodhpur, began building Mehrangarh Fort in 1459.

questions.text: ________ was awarded, Padma Shri in 1970 for his contribution to the field of Kuchipudi dance.
questions.explanation: Vedantam Satyanarayana Sarma, a Kuchipudi dancer famous for female roles such as Satyabhama, received the Padma Shri in 1970.

questions.text: The 11th Fundamental Duty to the Indian Constitution was added in the year ____________ by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act.
questions.explanation: The 86th Amendment Act, 2002, added Article 51A(k): parents and guardians are to provide opportunities for education to their children aged 6 to 14.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who became the Nawab of Bengal after the death of Alivardi Khan in the year 1756?
questions.explanation: Siraj-ud-Daulah, Alivardi Khan's grandson, succeeded him in 1756; he lost Bengal to the East India Company at Plassey in 1757.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following was the first woman President of the Indian National Congress?
questions.explanation: Annie Besant presided over the Calcutta session of 1917; Sarojini Naidu, in 1925, was the first Indian woman President.

questions.text: What is a 'double fault' in tennis?
options: A serve that hits the net and goes into the correct service box
A serve that goes out of bounds
A fault called by the linesman
Serving two faults in a row
questions.explanation: A double fault is failing with both serves on a point, which loses the server the point.

questions.text: Birju Maharaj is related to which of the following classical dance forms?
questions.explanation: Pandit Birju Maharaj, of the Lucknow gharana, was a leading exponent of Kathak.

questions.text: Kharavela was an important ruler of which dynasty?
questions.explanation: Kharavela, the Kalinga king known from the Hathigumpha inscription, belonged to the Chedi (Mahameghavahana) dynasty.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is/are true for the Religious Festivals in India? 1.Losar festival is majorly celebrated by Buddhist community of India. 2.Navroz festival is majorly celebrated by the Parsi community of India. 3.Saga Dawa is majorly celebrated by the Muslim community of India.
questions.explanation: Losar, the Tibetan new year, is a Buddhist festival and Navroz the Parsi new year. Saga Dawa is also Buddhist, not Muslim, so 3 is false.

questions.text: Which of the following iron and steel plants is located in Jharkhand?
questions.explanation: Bokaro Steel Plant is in Jharkhand; Durgapur is in West Bengal, Salem in Tamil Nadu and Vijayanagar in Karnataka.

questions.text: Which of the following peaks is NOT located in India?
questions.explanation: Dhaulagiri is in Nepal. Nanda Devi is in Uttarakhand, Guru Shikhar in Rajasthan and Mahendragiri in Odisha.

questions.text: With reference to medieval history, consider the following statements. 1. The founder of the Chola dynasty called the ‘Imperial Cholas’ was Vijayalaya (9th century AD). 2. One of the important dynasties which ruled in northern India was Gurjara-Pratiharas. 3. Palas ruled in western India and Rashtrakutas ruled in southern India in the early years (750 -1000). Which of the given statement(s) is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Vijayalaya founded the Imperial Chola line in the 9th century, and the Gurjara-Pratiharas ruled in northern India. The Palas ruled in eastern India (Bengal and Bihar), not western, so 3 is wrong.

questions.text: Which of the following is an informal group consisting of 4 to 10 individuals who seek loans against mutual guarantee?
questions.explanation: NABARD describes a joint liability group as an informal group of 4 to 10 people who borrow from a bank against a mutual guarantee.

questions.text: Who has been appointed as the new Chief of the Special Protection Group (SPG) by the centre in November 2023?
questions.explanation: Alok Sharma, a 1991-batch IPS officer already serving in the SPG, was named its Director in November 2023, after the death of Arun Kumar Sinha.

questions.text: Who among the following elect(s) the presiding officer of the Vidhan Sabha in India?
questions.explanation: Under Article 178 the Legislative Assembly chooses its Speaker from among its own members.

questions.text: The major carbohydrate of milk is
questions.explanation: Lactose, a disaccharide of glucose and galactose, is the sugar of milk.

questions.text: The national animal of Nepal is:
questions.explanation: The cow is Nepal's national animal.

questions.text: Which of these state governments has implemented PESA act in November 2022?
questions.explanation: Madhya Pradesh brought its PESA rules into force on 15 November 2022, Janjatiya Gaurav Divas.

questions.text: Which of the following Census recorded negative population growth in India?
questions.explanation: 1921 is the only census to record a fall in India's population, after the influenza epidemic of 1918 and famines; it is called the year of the great divide.

questions.text: Which state in India hosted the 77th edition of the Santosh Trophy?
questions.explanation: The final round of the 77th Santosh Trophy (2023-24) was played at Yupia in Arunachal Pradesh; Services won it.

questions.text: Who is the author of the historical fiction novel ‘The Mauryan: The Legend of Ashoka’?
questions.explanation: 'The Mauryan: The Legend of Ashoka' (2017) is a historical novel by Komal Bhanver.

questions.text: Padma Bhushan awardee Mogubai Kurdikar was associated with which of the following music styles?
questions.explanation: Mogubai Kurdikar was a Hindustani classical singer of the Jaipur-Atrauli gharana.

questions.text: In which year did John Dalton present his atomic theory, the second part of which states that all atoms of a particular element are equal?
questions.explanation: Dalton set out his atomic theory in 'A New System of Chemical Philosophy' in 1808: matter is made of atoms, and the atoms of one element are identical in mass and properties.

questions.text: The cold subarctic climate region possesses forest lands having conifers as main vegetation. These forest lands are known as:
questions.explanation: The taiga, or boreal forest, is the belt of coniferous forest in the cold subarctic climate; the tundra north of it is largely treeless.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Whenever she is coming / here, she brings / many gifts for everyone.
questions.explanation: A repeated, habitual action takes the simple present: 'Whenever she comes here'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. The pineapple dessert was “so delicious that we couldn’t help eat it”.
options: so that delicious we couldn’t help eating it
so delicious that we couldn’t helping eat it
so delicious that we couldn’t help eating it
questions.explanation: 'Can't help' is followed by a gerund: 'couldn't help eating it'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the following sentence. Don’t fight over such a “trivial” issue.
questions.explanation: 'Trivial' means of little importance: 'insignificant'.

questions.text: Rectify the sentence by selecting the correct spelling from the options. After the storm passed, the sun emarged from behind the clouds.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'emerged'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'Lieutenant'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. My sister performed / brilliant / in the competition / yesterday.
questions.explanation: A verb is modified by an adverb: 'My sister performed brilliantly'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. My brother plays the guitar _________ than I do.
questions.explanation: 'Than' calls for the comparative, and the comparative of the adverb 'well' is 'better'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. He is an intelligent person who always thinks before he ______________.
questions.explanation: The habitual present 'always thinks' is matched by the simple present with 'he': 'before he acts'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Ravi said that / his red jacket is / the cheaper than all other jackets.
options: the cheaper than all other jackets.
questions.explanation: A comparative with 'than' takes no 'the': 'cheaper than all other jackets'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM for the underlined word. They want to “bifurcate” the states.
questions.explanation: To 'bifurcate' is to divide into two; its opposite is 'combine'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Straight from the horse's mouth
questions.explanation: Information 'straight from the horse's mouth' comes directly from the person involved, the most reliable source.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The assignment was _________ early in the morning.
questions.explanation: An assignment that is 'due' at a time must be handed in then; 'dew' (moisture), 'do' and 'doe' (a female deer) make no sense here.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The author's use of vivid imagery ___________ the reader's senses, making the story come alive.
questions.explanation: Imagery that makes a story come alive 'heightens', or sharpens, the reader's senses.

questions.text: Select the appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the following sentence to make it grammatically correct. Smart watches are “the last” gadgets used by younger generations.
questions.explanation: 'The latest' means the newest; 'the last' means the final one: 'Smart watches are the latest gadgets'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word: Grapple
questions.explanation: To 'grapple' is to seize and hold, or struggle with; its opposite is 'release'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The way Sonam performs live on stage can be called the _________ one.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'most perfect': 'the … one', comparing her way of performing with all others, calls for the superlative, and 'more perfect' is a comparative while 'perfectable' and 'mostly perfect' do not fit. Strictly, 'perfect' is an absolute adjective that takes no degrees, though 'most perfect' is common in use.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. He is a complete “novice” when it comes to driving a car.
questions.explanation: A 'novice' is a beginner without experience: an 'amateur'.

questions.text: Select the meaningful and correctly spelt word from the given options to fill in the blank. The oceans cover more than 70% of the Earth's surface, making them the largest _______________ on the planet.
questions.explanation: A 'habitat' is the natural home of living things; 'habitude' means a habit, and 'hybrid' a cross.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank: In the realm of literature, words are the (1) ____________ of creation, and authors are the (2) ____________ of meaning. They skillfully weave stories with (3) ____________ narratives that can (4) ____________ the depths of human emotion. A well-crafted novel can (5) ____________ readers into its world, making them forget the passage of time.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Words are the 'tools', the instruments, with which literature is created.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank: In the realm of literature, words are the (1) ____________ of creation, and authors are the (2) ____________ of meaning. They skillfully weave stories with (3) ____________ narratives that can (4) ____________ the depths of human emotion. A well-crafted novel can (5) ____________ readers into its world, making them forget the passage of time.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Authors are the 'keepers' of meaning, those who hold and shape it.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank: In the realm of literature, words are the (1) ____________ of creation, and authors are the (2) ____________ of meaning. They skillfully weave stories with (3) ____________ narratives that can (4) ____________ the depths of human emotion. A well-crafted novel can (5) ____________ readers into its world, making them forget the passage of time.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Before 'narratives' the blank needs an adjective: 'vivid', lively and clear. 'Mundane' (dull) would contradict the praise, and 'defrost' and 'convey' are verbs.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank: In the realm of literature, words are the (1) ____________ of creation, and authors are the (2) ____________ of meaning. They skillfully weave stories with (3) ____________ narratives that can (4) ____________ the depths of human emotion. A well-crafted novel can (5) ____________ readers into its world, making them forget the passage of time.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: After 'can' the blank needs a verb, and of the options only 'pilot' is one: to steer or navigate through the depths of emotion.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank: In the realm of literature, words are the (1) ____________ of creation, and authors are the (2) ____________ of meaning. They skillfully weave stories with (3) ____________ narratives that can (4) ____________ the depths of human emotion. A well-crafted novel can (5) ____________ readers into its world, making them forget the passage of time.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: A novel can 'immerse', or absorb, readers in its world, so that they forget the passage of time.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: A man rows downstream 27 km and upstream 18 km, taking one hour each time. What is the speed of the current?
questions.explanation: Downstream the speed is 27 km/h and upstream 18 km/h. Current = (27 − 18)/2 = 4.5 km/h.

questions.text: The HCF of 28,35 and 42 is:
questions.explanation: 28 = 2² × 7, 35 = 5 × 7 and 42 = 2 × 3 × 7; 7 is the only prime factor common to all three, so the HCF is 7.

questions.text: If 5 litres of vinegar containing 20% of water is mixed with 10 litres of vinegar containing 5% of water, then what percentage of the new vinegar mixture is water?
questions.explanation: Water = 20% of 5 + 5% of 10 = 1 + 0.5 = 1.5 litres in 15 litres: 1.5/15 = 10%.

questions.text: A shopkeeper marked the price of a commodity at ₹37,000 more than the actual cost. If the shopkeeper allowed a 15% discount, it would fetch ₹ 7,500 more than if he allowed a 20% discount. Find the cost price.
questions.explanation: The two discounts differ by 5% of the marked price, so 0.05 × MP = ₹7,500 and MP = ₹1,50,000. Cost price = 1,50,000 − 37,000 = ₹1,13,000.

questions.text: Find the number of lead balls of diameter 4 cm each that can be made from a sphere of diameter 24 cm.
questions.explanation: Volume goes with the cube of the diameter: (24/4)³ = 6³ = 216 balls.

questions.text: A’s income and expenditure are in the ratio 5 : 4. If his total savings are ₹56,000, what is his expenditure in ₹?
questions.explanation: Savings are 5 − 4 = 1 part = ₹56,000, so expenditure is 4 parts = ₹2,24,000.

questions.text: The average age of a mother and her daughter is 42 years. The ratio of their ages is 9 : 5, respectively. Find the daughter's age (in years).
questions.explanation: Their ages add up to 2 × 42 = 84 years; the daughter's share is 5/14 × 84 = 30 years.

questions.text: 16 women can finish a task in 20 days and 20 men take 32 days to finish the same task. How many days will 8 women and 16 men take to finish the same task?
questions.explanation: The task takes 16 × 20 = 320 woman-days or 20 × 32 = 640 man-days, so 1 woman = 2 men. 8 women and 16 men equal 32 men, who take 640/32 = 20 days.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3000 as a sum borrowed at 6% per year rate of interest for 6 years.
Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2500 as a sum borrowed at 3% per year rate of interest for 2 years.

A start from X at 9:00 A.M. and reaches Y at 1:00 P.M., on the same day, B also starts from Y at 9:00 A.M. and reaches X at 3:00 P.M. on the same day, following the same route as A. At what time do the two meet?
questions.explanation: A covers the route in 4 hours and B in 6, so together they close 1/4 + 1/6 = 5/12 of it an hour and meet after 12/5 hours = 2 hours 24 minutes: 11:24 A.M.

questions.text: A solid sphere of radius 12 cm is melted and cast into small spherical balls, each of diameter 2.4 cm. Find the number of balls thus obtained.
questions.explanation: Radius 12 cm against 1.2 cm: (12/1.2)³ = 10³ = 1000 balls.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘COAT’ is coded as ‘3571’ and ‘PAIN’ is coded as ‘4238’.What is the code for ‘A’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: A is the only letter in both words and 3 the only digit in both codes, so A = 3.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: No bed is a chair. No chair is table. Conclusions: (I) No bed is a table. (II) Some tables may be chairs.
options: Both conclusion I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: Beds and tables are each kept apart from chairs, which says nothing about beds and tables, so I does not follow. If no chair is a table, no table can be a chair, so II does not follow either.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘KIDS’ is coded as ‘97&5’ and ‘DESK’ is coded as ‘R759’. What is the code for ‘E’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: K, D and S are in both words and 9, 7 and 5 in both codes. The letter left in DESK is E and the symbol left in its code is R, so E = R.

questions.text: WGQA Is related to XHRB in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, HRBL is related to ISCM. To which of the following is GQAK related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one place forward: WGQA → XHRB and HRBL → ISCM. So GQAK → HRBL.

questions.text: Which two numbers should be interchanged to make the following equation correct? (16÷ 4) × 6 + 26 −48 + 9× 8 = 154 (Note: Interchange should be done of the entire number and not individual digits of a given number.)
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? AAA, BCD, CEG, DGJ, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move +1 (A, B, C, D, E), second letters +2 (A, C, E, G, I) and third letters +3 (A, D, G, J, M): EIM.

questions.text: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). A sits second to the left of D, who is third to the left of E. C sits third to the right of G, who is not an immediate neighbour of E. B sits second to the right of G. What is the position of B with respect to C?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, left is clockwise. A sits 2 and E 4 places clockwise from D; G, not beside E, sits next to D, and only on D's left do C and B find free seats. Clockwise from D: D, G, A, F, E, C, B, so B is on C's immediate left.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 13, 26, 39, 52, 65, ?
questions.explanation: The series is the multiples of 13: 13 × 6 = 78.

questions.text: What will come in the place of the question mark (‘?’) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘×’ are interchanged and ‘÷′ and ‘–‘ are interchanged? 18 × 72 – 3 ÷ 2 + 11 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 18 + 72 ÷ 3 − 2 × 11 = 18 + 24 − 22 = 20.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘BLAME’ is coded as ‘YOZNV’ and ‘GLAZE’ is coded as ‘TOZAV’. What is the code for ‘PRAKASH’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite in the alphabet (A ↔ Z, B ↔ Y, L ↔ O, M ↔ N, E ↔ V): BLAME → YOZNV. So PRAKASH → KIZPZHS.

questions.text: Seven people A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). B is sitting third to the right of D. G is sitting second to the left of A. E is sitting to the immediate right of G. Only three people are sitting between E and C when counted from the left of E. C is not an immediate neighbour of A. The position of how many persons will remain unchanged except A if all the persons are arranged in the English alphabetical order in anti-clockwise direction, starting from A and keeping the position of A unchanged?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, left is clockwise. G sits 2 and E 1 place clockwise from A, C 4 places clockwise from E, and B, third to D's right, fits only with D next to A: clockwise A, E, G, B, F, C, D. Seated alphabetically anti-clockwise from A, the clockwise order becomes A, G, F, E, D, C, B, so only C keeps its seat.

questions.text: 45 is related to 85 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 63 is related to 121. To which ofthe following is 58 related, following the same logic?(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbersinto its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: Double the first number and subtract 5: 45 × 2 − 5 = 85 and 63 × 2 − 5 = 121. So 58 × 2 − 5 = 111.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All cats are dogs. No cat is a horse. Conclusions: (I): No dog is a horse. (II): No horse is a cat.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
questions.explanation: 'No cat is a horse' can be read the other way round: no horse is a cat (II). Dogs that are not cats may or may not be horses, so I does not follow.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘please fill this’ is written as ‘km tu dk’ and ‘this is book’ is written as ‘dk pu sy’. How is ‘this’ written in the given language?
questions.explanation: 'this' is the only word in both sentences and 'dk' the only code in both, so this = dk.

questions.text: 9 is related to 37 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 3 is related to 13. To which of the following is 8 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 - Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Multiply by 4 and add 1: 9 × 4 + 1 = 37 and 3 × 4 + 1 = 13. So 8 × 4 + 1 = 33.

questions.text: Indian classical singer, Kesarbai Kerkar belonged to which of the following gharanas?
questions.explanation: Kesarbai Kerkar was a leading singer of the Jaipur-Atrauli gharana, a disciple of its founder, Ustad Alladiya Khan.

questions.text: Which of the following autobiographies is written by the former Indian Judge Leila Seth?
options: Justice for the Judge: An Autobiography
Challenges of Governance: An Insider’s View
In Pursuit of Justice: An Autobiography
questions.explanation: 'On Balance' (2003) is the autobiography of Leila Seth, the first woman to be Chief Justice of a state High Court (Himachal Pradesh).

questions.text: In which Indian city is the DY Patil Cricket Stadium located?
questions.explanation: The DY Patil Stadium is at Nerul in Navi Mumbai.

questions.text: The Talcher Thermal Power Station is located in which state?
questions.explanation: NTPC's Talcher Thermal Power Station is in Angul district, Odisha, by the Talcher coalfield.

questions.text: In which city was the 141st session of the International Olympic Committee (IOC) inaugurated in India?
questions.explanation: The 141st IOC Session was held in Mumbai in October 2023, the first in India since 1983.

questions.text: The Kamakshi Saunsthan temple of Goa is crowned with the ________ two-storied tower and with a golden Kalash perched on its Shikhar.
questions.explanation: The Kamakshi temple at Shiroda, built in the late 16th century, has an octagonal two-storied tower topped by a golden kalash.

questions.text: The SEWA Cooperative Bank was first initiated in ________ in the year ________.
questions.explanation: The Shri Mahila SEWA Sahakari Bank was set up in Ahmedabad in 1974 by members of the Self Employed Women's Association, led by Ela Bhatt.

questions.text: The Ananda Pagoda is a famous festival of which neighbouring country of India?
questions.explanation: The Ananda Pagoda festival is held at the Ananda Temple in Bagan, Myanmar.

questions.text: Which of the following groups of organisms are more vulnerable to the acidification of ocean?
questions.explanation: More acidic seawater holds fewer carbonate ions, which corals, molluscs and other calcifying organisms need to build their calcium carbonate shells and skeletons.

questions.text: The president of which country was the chief guest at the Indian Republic Day Ceremony of 2023?
questions.explanation: Egypt's President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi was the chief guest at India's Republic Day in 2023.

questions.text: Which of the following is the zonal headquarter of North Eastern Railway?
questions.explanation: North Eastern Railway has its headquarters at Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh.

questions.text: During which of the following Prime Minsters' leadership were Fundamental Duties incorporated in the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The Fundamental Duties (Article 51A) were added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976, when Indira Gandhi was Prime Minister.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following Indian leaders was the first member to be elected to the British Parliament?
questions.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji won Finsbury Central for the Liberal Party in 1892 and sat in the British House of Commons until 1895.

questions.text: Which Article of the Constitution of India deals with the composition of the Legislative Council?
questions.explanation: Article 171 sets the composition of a state's Legislative Council; Article 169 provides for creating or abolishing one.

questions.text: At which of the following places the written form of teachings of Jainism in which they are presently available, were written around 1500 years ago?
questions.explanation: Jain teachings were passed down orally for centuries; they were written down, in the form available today, at Valabhi in Gujarat about 1500 years ago.

questions.text: The title of ‘Chief of the Merchants’ or ‘Malikut-Tujjar’ was conferred on Mahmud Gawan by which of the following Bahamani kings?
questions.explanation: On taking the throne in 1458, Humayun Shah made Mahmud Gawan his chief minister with the title Malik-ut-Tujjar.

questions.text: Which element is located in Group 18 of the periodic table and is known for its lack of chemical reactivity?
questions.explanation: Helium is a noble gas in Group 18; its filled outer shell makes it almost unreactive. Oxygen is in Group 16, and fluorine and chlorine in Group 17.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following signed the Treaty of Allahabad in August 1765 with the Nawab of Awadh and Shah Alam II, the Mughal Emperor?
questions.explanation: Robert Clive signed the Treaties of Allahabad in 1765, which gave the East India Company the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.

questions.text: To remain healthy and disease free, taking a balanced diet is very important. A balanced diet is:
options: a diet that contains sufficient amount of all the nutrients that the human body needs to grow properly
a diet that contains appreciable number of vitamins and minerals
a diet that contains adequate amount of carbohydrates
a diet that contains adequate amount of protein and fat
questions.explanation: A balanced diet gives the body all the nutrients it needs (carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins and minerals) in the right amounts, with roughage and water.

questions.text: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY) is a scheme launched in 2015 for providing loans up to ________ lakh to the non-corporate, non-farm small/micro enterprises.
questions.explanation: At launch, MUDRA loans went up to ₹10 lakh in three tiers: Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishore (up to ₹5 lakh) and Tarun (up to ₹10 lakh).

questions.text: National Sickle Cell Anaemia Elimination Programme, introduced in the Union Budget 2023, aims to eliminate sickle cell genetic transmission by the year _____________.
questions.explanation: The Union Budget 2023-24 announced a mission to eliminate sickle cell anaemia as a public health problem by 2047.

questions.text: In which year did Guru Indira PP Bora receive the Padma Shri Award?
questions.explanation: Indira P. P. Bora, a Sattriya dancer from Assam, received the Padma Shri in 2020.

questions.text: Which of the following Indian classical dance forms was developed by Siddhendra Yogi?
questions.explanation: Siddhendra Yogi, a Vaishnava poet-saint, is credited with giving Kuchipudi, named after its village in Andhra Pradesh, its classical form.

questions.text: In February 2023, which Indian-American was appointed as the CEO of YouTube?
questions.explanation: Neal Mohan succeeded Susan Wojcicki as YouTube's CEO in February 2023.

questions.text: Select the meaningful and correctly spelt word from the given options to fill in the blank. Regular physical exercise improves cardiovascular health, reducing the risk of heart disease and ________________.
questions.explanation: Exercise lowers the risk of heart disease and 'stroke'; 'struck' and 'strike' are forms of a verb and 'stock' makes no sense here.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. After the long and tedious project, Sarah felt like she was at the “limit of her patience”.
questions.explanation: To be at 'the end of one's rope' is to have no patience or strength left.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate expression that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence. The watchman “tried every possible way” to catch the thief of the hostel.
questions.explanation: To 'explore every avenue' is to try every possible way of doing something.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. She speaks / so soft that / hardly anyone / can hear her.
questions.explanation: The verb 'speaks' needs an adverb: 'so softly that'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. My manager thanked the staff “for there continued” dedication and support.
questions.explanation: The possessive is 'their'; 'there' is an adverb of place and 'they're' means 'they are'.

questions.text: Select the correct spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence. Sometimes, the nicknames of children, given to them by their loved ones in childhood, give them a true sense of “embarresment”, especially when they are called by those names in front of others.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'embarrassment', with a double 'r' and a double 's'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. After school, we / went home and / told our respective parents / off the incident.
questions.explanation: One tells someone 'of' (about) an incident: 'told our respective parents of the incident'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. While the stock market experiences volatility, financial analysts ___________________ market trends and provide investment advice.
questions.explanation: The sentence states a general fact in the simple present ('experiences', 'provide'), so 'monitor'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Entangle
questions.explanation: To 'entangle' is to catch in something that is hard to escape: to 'trap'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I am thinking about colouring my ___________.
questions.explanation: One colours one's 'hair'; 'hare', 'heir' and 'air' only sound alike.

questions.text: Select the grammatically correct sentence from the given options.
options: Since yesterday, the policeman had been waiting for the woman to take a details of a case.
Since yesterday, the policeman had been waiting for a woman to take a details of the case.
Since yesterday, the policeman had been waiting for the woman to take the details of the case.
Since yesterday, a policeman had been waiting for a woman to take the details of the case.
questions.explanation: 'Details' is plural, so it cannot take 'a', which rules out the first two sentences. SSC's key gives the one with 'the' throughout, for a particular policeman, woman and case; the version with 'a policeman' and 'a woman' is grammatical too, though less natural with 'the details of the case'.

questions.text: In the following sentence the underlined part contains as error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative. We never expected “most” from her.
questions.explanation: After a negative, a large amount is 'much': 'We never expected much from her.' 'Many' needs a plural noun, and 'more' implies a comparison the sentence does not make.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word..
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'stubble'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. I “concur” with the decision of our principal, when he says that students who display indiscipline should be dismissed from the institute irrespective of their academic achievements.
questions.explanation: To 'concur' is to agree; its opposite is to 'differ'. 'Coincide' is close in meaning.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. Ritu was still standing in the queue when the “film was starting.”
questions.explanation: A completed action that comes in the middle of one in progress takes the simple past: 'was still standing in the queue when the film started'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. spontaneous
questions.explanation: 'Spontaneous' means done on impulse, without planning; its opposite is 'deliberate'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To look black
questions.explanation: Things 'look black' when the outlook is bad: they seem unfavourable.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Westminster Abbey's 1._________ was one of Edward the Confessor's greatest accomplishments as king of England from 1042 to 1066. Edward was King Ethelred's son and he had a lot of pressure as his father was known to be an incompetent ruler. The Danes drove Edward from England, and he lived in exile in Normandy. According to legend, Edward promised that if he could make it back to his realm in safety, he would travel to St. Peter's in Rome. Upon his return and 2.______ in Winchester in 1042, he discovered that he could not abandon his subjects. He was freed from his pledge by the Pope, but only if he established or 3.___________ a monastery dedicated to St. Peter. As a result, Westminster Abbey was constructed in the Norman 4._________. He believed that London was not the 5._________ place to built the Minster. Hence, a location known as 'Westminster' was discovered to be to the west of the metropolis.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The abbey's 'construction' (building) was one of Edward's great accomplishments, as the passage goes on to describe.

He believed that London was not the 5._________ place to built the Minster. Hence, a location known as 'Westminster' was discovered to be to the west of the metropolis.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: On his return Edward was crowned: his 'coronation' at Winchester.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
