questions.explanation: London was not the 'appropriate' (suitable) place; the blank needs an adjective, and the other options are verbs.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: The average score of 30 students (boys and girls only) in a class test was 16.2 and that of 18 boys in the same test was 16. The average score of girls in the same test was:
questions.explanation: All 30 scored 30 × 16.2 = 486 and the 18 boys 18 × 16 = 288. The 12 girls scored 198, an average of 198/12 = 16.5.

questions.text: Mihir buys a toy for ₹70 and sells it for ₹90. What is his gain percentage?

Two trains start at the same time from two stations and proceed towards each other at speeds of 120 km/hr and 80 km/hr, respectively. When they meet, it is found that one train has travelled 60 km more than the other. What is the distance (in km) between the two stations?
questions.explanation: Each hour the faster train covers 120 − 80 = 40 km more than the other, so they meet after 60/40 = 1.5 hours. Together they cover (120 + 80) × 1.5 = 300 km.

questions.text: The average salary of all 50 employees including 5 officers of a company is ₹855. If the average salary of the officers is ₹2,550, find the average salary of the remaining staff of the company. (Rounded to the nearest integer.)
questions.explanation: All 50 earn 50 × 855 = ₹42,750 and the officers 5 × 2,550 = ₹12,750. The other 45 earn ₹30,000, an average of ₹666.67 ≈ ₹667.

questions.text: Using the factor method of HCF, which of the following is the HCF of 160 and 256?
questions.explanation: 160 = 2⁵ × 5 and 256 = 2⁸, so the HCF is 2⁵ = 32.

questions.text: The marked price of a mobile phone at a showroom is ₹25,000 and is sold at successive discounts of 20%, 15% and 10%. Find its selling price.
Harsha obtained 72, 63 and 81 marks (out of 100) in Maths, Physics and Chemistry, respectively. What is the average of his marks?
A sum of money at simple interest amounts to ₹2,500 in three years and ₹3,000 in five years. What is the rate of interest (correct up to two decimal places)?
questions.explanation: The two extra years earn 3,000 − 2,500 = ₹500, so ₹250 a year. The principal is 2,500 − 3 × 250 = ₹1,750 and the rate 250/1,750 × 100 = 14.29%.

questions.text: In an election there were only two candidates, Geeta and Shyama. Geeta received 15% of the total votes and Shyama received 8700 votes. 60% of the voters did not cast their vote to either of the two candidates. Find the total percentage of votes that Shyama received, assuming that all the votes cast were valid.
questions.explanation: Geeta got 15% and 60% voted for neither, so Shyama got 100 − 15 − 60 = 25%.

questions.text: In a hospital, 60% of the patients are men, 25% of the patients are women, and 15% of the patients are children. If the average age of the men is 40 years, that of the women is 36 years, and that of the children is 8 years. What is the average age of all the patients?
A policeman travelling at a speed of 120 km/h chases a thief 5000 m away from him, and travelling at a speed of 100 km/h. What is the time taken by the policeman to catch the thief?
questions.explanation: The policeman gains 120 − 100 = 20 km/h on the thief, so he closes the 5 km in 5/20 hour = 15 minutes.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3500 as a sum borrowed at 6% per year rate of interest for 6 years.
Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2500 as a sum borrowed at 3% per year rate of interest for 3 years.
TW21 is related to ZC66 in a certain way. In the same way, UX33 is related to AD78. To which of the following is MP45 related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 6 places forward and the number rises by 45: T → Z, W → C, 21 + 45 = 66; U → A, X → D, 33 + 45 = 78. So M → S, P → V, 45 + 45 = 90: SV90.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? TCU, UFP ,VIK, WLF ,?
questions.explanation: First letters move forward 1 (T, U, V, W, so next X); second letters forward 3 (C, F, I, L, so O); third letters back 5 (U, P, K, F, so A): XOA.

questions.text: 11 is related to 78 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 6 is related to 43. To which of the following is 31 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding / subtracting / multiplying, etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is 7 times the first plus 1: 11 × 7 + 1 = 78 and 6 × 7 + 1 = 43. Likewise 31 × 7 + 1 = 218.

questions.text: In a code language, 'VGAL' is coded as ‘BEGJ’ and 'XQEB' is coded as ‘DOKZ’. How will 'HTSO' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +6, −2, +6, −2: VGAL → BEGJ and XQEB → DOKZ. So H → N, T → R, S → Y, O → M: NRYM.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed) (18, 108, 12) (33, 198, 22)
questions.explanation: In each set the first number × 6 and the third × 9 both give the second: 18 × 6 = 108 = 12 × 9 and 33 × 6 = 198 = 22 × 9. Likewise 42 × 6 = 252 = 28 × 9.

questions.text: BZ7 is related to GE15 in a certain way. In the same way, PN13 is related to US21. To which of the following is IG12 related following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 5 places forward and the number rises by 8: B → G, Z → E, 7 + 8 = 15; P → U, N → S, 13 + 8 = 21. So I → N, G → L, 12 + 8 = 20: NL20.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 6 16 27 39 52 ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 10, 11, 12, 13, so the next is 14: 52 + 14 = 66.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘let us go’ is coded as ‘ck ru tb’ and ‘please go away’ is coded as ‘tb mg du’. How is ‘go’ coded in that code language?
questions.explanation: 'go' is the only word in both phrases and 'tb' the only code in both, so go = tb.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘−’ and ‘ + ‘ are interchanged and ‘÷’ and ‘×’ are interchanged? 15 − 4 + 9 × 3 ÷ 6 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 15 + 4 − 9 ÷ 3 × 6 = 15 + 4 − 18 = 1.

questions.text: Seven executives of a law firm (P, Q, R, S, T, U and V) are sitting at a circular table for a meeting, everyone facing towards the center(but not necessarily in the same order); P is an immediate neighbor of both U and S; Q is sitting to the immediate right of S, and is one of the immediate neighbors of T; V is sitting second to the right of T. Who is sitting second to the left of U?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, a person's left is the clockwise side. Clockwise the seats run S, P, U, V, R, T, Q: P between U and S, Q on S's right next to T, and V second to T's right. Second to the left of U is R.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘gre pul sep’ means ‘eat the sofa’, ‘pul pra sem’ means ‘clear my sofa’ and ‘gre boi nad’ means ‘the great river’. What is the code for ‘the’ in the same code language?
questions.explanation: 'sofa' is in the first two sentences and 'pul' in both their codes, so sofa = pul. 'the' is in the first and third, whose only shared code is 'gre': the = gre.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: No sunflower is a lily. No lily is a rose. Conclusions: (I) No sunflower is a rose. (II) No rose is a lily.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusion I and II follow
questions.explanation: 'No lily is a rose' can be reversed: no rose is a lily (II). Sunflowers and roses are each kept apart from lilies, which says nothing about whether any sunflower is a rose, so I does not follow.

questions.text: In a code language, 'KITE' is written as 'PRGV' and 'MARBLE' is written as 'NZIYOV'. How will 'DOLPHIN' be written in the same language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite in the alphabet (A ↔ Z, B ↔ Y, ...): K → P, I → R, T → G, E → V. So DOLPHIN → WLOKSRM.

questions.text: E, F, G, H, P, S, and T are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). F sits second to the right of T. P sits to the immediate left of S. Only one person sits between P and G when counted from the left of P. H sits third to the right of E.How many people are sitting between H and P when counted from the right of H?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, a person's left is the clockwise side. Clockwise the seats run S, P, H, G, F, E, T: P on S's left, G second to P's left, F second to T's right and H third to E's right. P sits immediately to H's right, so no one sits between them.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) of the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 7 + 8 – 24 × 6 ÷ 3 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 7 − 8 + 24 ÷ 6 × 3 = 7 − 8 + 12 = 11.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All schools are colleges. No college is a university. Conclusions: (I): No school is a university. (II): All colleges are schools.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: Every school is a college and no college is a university, so no school is a university (I). 'All schools are colleges' cannot be reversed into 'all colleges are schools', so II does not follow.

questions.text: The rock-cut caves in Karnataka, mainly at Badami and Aihole, were built under the patronage of the ______.
questions.explanation: The cave temples at Badami and Aihole were cut under the Chalukyas of Badami in the sixth and seventh centuries.

questions.text: Bharatanatyam dancer ________ received the Natya Kala Sarathy award from Sri Parthasarathy Swami Sabha in 2023 at Chennai.
questions.explanation: Srekala Bharath, a Bharatanatyam dancer and teacher, received the sabha's Natya Kala Sarathy award on 20 March 2023.

questions.text: The Kakrapar Atomic Power Plant is located in which state?
questions.explanation: The Kakrapar Atomic Power Station stands on the Tapi river in south Gujarat.

questions.text: What is the term 'ace' commonly associated within sports?
options: A high jump technique in athletics
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the tennis serve: an ace is a serve the receiver cannot touch, usually a fast one, and it is the sense the word most commonly has in sport. (Golfers also call a hole in one an ace, which 'a perfect shot in golf' could describe.)

questions.text: A factory set up in my area is causing huge deforestation. Which of the following can we expect to see in the near future? A) Lowering of ground water B) Lower temperatures C) Frequent rain D) Arrival of new animals
questions.explanation: Without trees, rainwater runs off instead of soaking in, so ground water is not recharged and its level falls. Deforestation tends to raise local temperatures and reduce rainfall, and it drives animals away.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the Ozone layer are true? Statement A: It is found in the stratosphere. Statement B: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) are responsible for ozone hole. Statement C: Ozone layer is found around 15–30 km above the earth’s surface. Statement D: Ozone layer is expected not to recover anymore now.
options: Only statements A, B and C
Only statement B, C and D
questions.explanation: The ozone layer lies in the stratosphere, roughly 15–30 km up, and CFCs caused the ozone hole. D is false: since the Montreal Protocol the layer is expected to recover over the coming decades.

questions.text: Which of the following types of volcanic eruptions of Earth’s volcanoes are most explosive?
questions.explanation: Calderas are the most explosive of Earth's volcanoes: they erupt so violently that they collapse on themselves instead of building a tall cone. Dykes and lopoliths are intrusive forms, and flood basalts are outpourings of very fluid lava.

questions.text: Which book has been authored by Shovana Narayan and Geetika Kalha?
questions.explanation: Kathak dancer Shovana Narayan and Geetika Kalha wrote 'Indian Mythology through Classical Dance' (2023).

questions.text: How many Pillar Edicts or Major Pillar Edicts (PEs) of Ashoka are found?
questions.explanation: Ashoka issued seven Major Pillar Edicts; all seven appear together only on the Delhi-Topra pillar.

questions.text: A famous organisation Self-Employed Women’s Association (SEWA) is related with which of the following states?
questions.explanation: SEWA, a trade union of self-employed women, was founded by Ela Bhatt in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, in 1972.

questions.text: At the ____________, Neeraj Chopra became the first Indian to win a gold medal in javelin throw.
questions.explanation: Neeraj Chopra won the javelin gold at the 2018 Asian Games in Jakarta, India's first in the event; he won it again at the 2022 Games, held in 2023.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following is the author of the book, 'A History of British India'?
questions.explanation: James Mill's 'The History of British India' (1817) divided India's past into Hindu, Muslim and British periods.

questions.text: According to Article 280 of the Indian Constitution, the Finance Commission needs to be appointed for every ________________.
questions.explanation: Under Article 280 the President constitutes a Finance Commission every fifth year, or earlier if the President considers it necessary.

questions.text: Lokrang, a five-day festival organised by the Madhya Pradesh Adivasi Lok Kala Academy, begins on ________________ every year.
questions.explanation: Lokrang, held in Bhopal by the Madhya Pradesh Adivasi Lok Kala Academy, opens on Republic Day, 26 January, every year.

questions.text: A four-carbon chain with a triple bond is called _________.
questions.explanation: The ending '-yne' marks a carbon-carbon triple bond, so four carbons give butyne. Butene has a double bond, butanol an -OH group and butanal an aldehyde group.

questions.text: In May 2023, who was sworn in as Central Vigilance Commissioner?
questions.explanation: Praveen Kumar Srivastava took the oath as Central Vigilance Commissioner before President Droupadi Murmu in May 2023.

questions.text: Oak and chestnut trees are found in which type of forest in India?
questions.explanation: In the montane forests, between about 1,000 and 2,000 m, wet temperate forests of evergreen broad-leaved trees such as oak and chestnut predominate.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which of the following sessions of Congress did the Party issue a call to celebrate 26th January as ‘Purna Swaraj Day’?
questions.explanation: The Lahore session of December 1929, under Jawaharlal Nehru, made Purna Swaraj Congress's goal and called for 26 January 1930 to be celebrated as Independence Day.

questions.text: Vani Jairam, who won Padma Bhushan 2023, belongs to which state?
questions.explanation: Playback singer Vani Jairam, awarded the Padma Bhushan in 2023, was born in Vellore, Tamil Nadu.

questions.text: Which Article of the Constitution of India directs the State to provide public assistance to its citizens in case of unemployment, old age, sickness and disablement, within the limits of its economic capacity and development?
questions.explanation: Article 41, a Directive Principle, asks the State to secure the right to work, to education and to public assistance in unemployment, old age, sickness and disablement.

questions.text: At the time of its adoption, the Constitution contained 395 Articles and ________ Schedules.
questions.explanation: As adopted in 1949 the Constitution had 395 Articles in 22 Parts, and 8 Schedules.

questions.text: The last Mughal emperor of India was:
questions.explanation: Bahadur Shah II (Bahadur Shah Zafar) was the last Mughal emperor; the British exiled him to Rangoon after the revolt of 1857.

questions.text: In which year was the first Socio Economic and Caste Census (SECC) conducted in India?
questions.explanation: The first Socio Economic and Caste Census was begun in 2011.

questions.text: In 2023, Government of India has announced to set up a/an ______________ DigiLocker for use by MSMEs, large businesses and charitable trusts to store and share documents online securely.
questions.explanation: The Union Budget 2023-24 announced an Entity DigiLocker for MSMEs, large businesses and charitable trusts to store and share documents online securely.

questions.text: Padma Subrahmanyam is associated with which dance form?
questions.explanation: Padma Subrahmanyam is a Bharatanatyam dancer and scholar, who developed the Bharata Nrithyam style from the karanas of the Natya Shastra.

questions.text: Choose the correctly spelt word to fill in the blank meaningfully. The citizens of Iraq wanted _______________ after years of war.
questions.explanation: 'Peace', the absence of war, is the word, correctly spelt; 'piece' means a part.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word. The Prime Minister will “address” the nation tomorrow.
options: A postal code for sending letters
questions.explanation: As a verb, to 'address' a group is to speak formally to it: the Prime Minister will deliver a speech to the nation.

questions.text: In the following sentence the underlined part contains as error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative. Their chance of winning is “slimmest”.
questions.explanation: Nothing is being compared, so the positive degree is needed: 'Their chance of winning is slim.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Shirin “came off with a brilliant idea” to solve the problem.
options: came off to a brilliant idea
came up with a brilliant idea
came up in a brilliant idea
came off on a brilliant idea
questions.explanation: To 'come up with' an idea is to think of it: 'Shirin came up with a brilliant idea'. To 'come off' is to succeed or to become detached.

questions.text: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks. Martin Luther King Jr. started a crusade for discrimination ________ African Americans. He relied on peaceful demonstrations and demonstrators. His most famous march was a powerful rally of about 250,000 people in Washington in 1963, where he ________ one of the most famous speeches in history.
questions.explanation: Discrimination is 'against' a group, and a speech is 'delivered'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks. The teacher asked the students to remain ____, but the noise continued to ____. She finally had to raise her voice to gain control.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'quit; rise', evidently 'quiet; rise' with 'quiet' misprinted: the teacher asked for quiet, but the noise kept rising. ('Calm; escalate' also reads naturally, though 'calm' speaks of composure rather than of the silence the noise is set against.)

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiom from the options given below. To accept the gauntlet
questions.explanation: To accept (or take up) the gauntlet is to accept a challenge; a knight threw down his gauntlet to issue one.

questions.text: In the following sentence the underlined part contains as error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative. Pankaj is a “better” cook.
questions.explanation: Nothing is being compared, so the positive degree is needed: 'Pankaj is a good cook.'

questions.text: Select the correct spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence. Is he ready to risk his “acredation” for the greater good?
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'accreditation'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. I still / do not understand / why he did not / reply my email.
questions.explanation: 'Reply' takes 'to' before its object: 'why he did not reply to my email'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. You need to rest the ________ before baking the bread.
questions.explanation: Bread is baked from 'dough', which is left to rest before baking; 'doe' is a female deer.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The team captain inquired of his teammates _________ they preferred to choose batting as their initial option.
questions.explanation: 'Whether' introduces an indirect question between alternatives; 'whither' means to where, 'wither' to shrivel, and 'weather' is the state of the atmosphere.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word from the given sentence. The teacher's encouragment motivated the students to excel in their studies.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'encouragement'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Inferior
questions.explanation: 'Inferior' means lower in quality or rank; its opposite is 'superior'.

questions.text: Read the following sentence and select its future tense form from the options given below: Rachel and Rahul joined forces on a project and successfully completed it within a month.
options: Rachel and Rahul will join forces on a project and successfully complete it within a month.
Rachel and Rahul have joined forces on a project and successfully completed it within a month.
Rachel and Rahul should join forces on a project and successfully complete it within a month.
Rachel and Rahul are joining forces on a project and successfully completing it within a month.
questions.explanation: The simple future uses 'will' with the base form of each verb: 'will join ... and successfully complete'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Hire
questions.explanation: To 'hire' someone is to 'engage' them: to employ them for a job.

questions.text: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
options: A secondary section of the school is located at an end of the street.
The secondary section of a school is located at the end of a street.
The secondary section of a school is located at an end of the street.
The secondary section of the school is located at the end of the street.
questions.explanation: The section, the school and the end of the street are all particular ones the reader can identify, so each takes 'the'.

questions.text: Select the grammatically correct sentence from the given options.
options: She was not allowed to enter the hotel as her clothes were dirty.
She was not allowed to enter the hotel as her clothes were dirtier.
She was not allowed to enter the hotel as her clothes was dirtier.
She was not allow to enter the hotel as her clothes were dirty.
questions.explanation: Nothing is compared, so the positive 'dirty' is needed, with the plural 'clothes were' and the passive 'was not allowed'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Employers, nowadays, are (1)_______ on team-building as it proves to be useful in being more productive. So, they create occasions for the employees to spend time together. Some employees are sick (2) ________ office festival parties with mandatory dress codes and fun competitions. Some others (3)____ of having to forcibly bond with colleagues during after-work happy hours when they would rather be at home. A French court (4)____ recently that one very much has the right to be boring at the workplace. Seven years after Mr. T was fired from his company for not participating in fun activities, which included going out for drinks after work once a week, the court said that Mr. T was merely exercising his ‘freedom of expression’. It added that the company’s culture of fun (5)________ Mr. T ‘s fundamental right to ‘dignity and respect of private life’. However, employers and HR personnel insist that team-bonding initiatives are crucial to the workplace and the employees too feel the same if they want promotions.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'Employers, nowadays, are focusing on team-building': the present continuous, for what is going on now.

However, employers and HR personnel insist that team-bonding initiatives are crucial to the workplace and the employees too feel the same if they want promotions.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: One is 'sick of' something one has had too much of.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: A sum of ₹717 becomes ₹874.74 in 5 years at a certain rate of simple interest. If the rate of interest is increased by 3.1%, then what will be the simple interest (in ₹) of ₹717 in 5 years?
The average of 11 numbers is 17. If the average of the first five numbers is 16 and the average of the last five numbers is 19, then the sixth number is:
questions.explanation: The 11 numbers total 11 × 17 = 187, the first five 5 × 16 = 80 and the last five 5 × 19 = 95, so the sixth is 187 − 80 − 95 = 12.

questions.text: Find the HCF of 10, 35 and 55.
questions.explanation: 10 = 2 × 5, 35 = 5 × 7 and 55 = 5 × 11; the only common factor is 5.

questions.text: The average of 5 consecutive natural numbers is 7. Which is the largest number among these?
questions.explanation: Five consecutive numbers averaging 7 are 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9, so the largest is 9.

questions.text: A thief saw a policeman from a distance of 300 m and started running. At the same time, the policeman started chasing the thief. If the speed of the thief is 12 km/h and that of the policeman 15 km/h, then the distance (in km) covered by the policeman to catch the thief is:
questions.explanation: The policeman gains 15 − 12 = 3 km/h on the 0.3 km gap, so he catches the thief in 0.3/3 = 0.1 hour, having run 15 × 0.1 = 1.5 km.

questions.text: What sum (in ₹) will earn a simple interest of ₹360 in 3 years at 16% per year rate of interest?

There are 20 cricket balls in the showroom. Among these 20 balls, some are yellow and some are white. The average cost of all the balls is ₹75. If the average cost of yellow balls is ₹80 and that of white is ₹60, then the number of yellow balls is:
questions.explanation: With y yellow balls: 80y + 60(20 − y) = 20 × 75 = 1,500, so 20y = 300 and y = 15.

questions.text: The average of 10 numbers is 29. The average of the first 6 numbers is 22 and that of the last 6 numbers is 32. What is the average of the 5th number and the 6th number?
questions.explanation: The 10 numbers total 290, the first six 6 × 22 = 132 and the last six 6 × 32 = 192. The 5th and 6th numbers are counted in both, so they total 132 + 192 − 290 = 34 and average 17.

questions.text: The difference between successive discounts of 25% followed by 12% and 20% followed by 15% on the marked price of a saree is ₹50. The marked price of the saree is:
questions.explanation: 25% then 12% leaves 0.75 × 0.88 = 66% of the marked price (34% off); 20% then 15% leaves 0.8 × 0.85 = 68% (32% off). The 2% difference is ₹50, so the marked price is ₹2,500.

questions.text: A, B and C start running around a circular track and complete one round in 16, 20 and 28 seconds, respectively. In how much time will they meet again at the starting point?
questions.explanation: They are next together at the start after the LCM of 16, 20 and 28: 2⁴ × 5 × 7 = 560 seconds.

questions.text: The rate of oil is increased by 12% every year. The rate in the next year would be ₹125.44 per litre. What is the difference between the prices (in ₹) per litre of the oil in the last year and this year?
questions.explanation: This year's rate is 125.44 ÷ 1.12 = ₹112 and last year's 112 ÷ 1.12 = ₹100, so the difference is ₹12.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3000 as a sum borrowed at 6% per year rate of interest for 3 years.
Find the total surface area of a cone having base radius 49 cm and slant height 61 cm.
In a certain code language, ‘FROM’ is coded as ‘7519’ and ‘MADE’ is coded as ‘2146’.What is the code for ‘M’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: M is the only letter in both words and 1 the only digit in both codes, so M = 1.

questions.text: Seven friends - L, M, N, O, D, E, and F - are seated around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). O is sitting fifth to the right of L. M has F and O as immediate neighbours. N and L are immediate neighbours of E. Who is sitting to the immediate left of D?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, a person's right is anticlockwise and left clockwise. Clockwise from L the seats are L, D, O, M, F, N, E: O is fifth to L's right, E sits between L and N, M between F and O, and D takes the seat left between L and O. D's immediate left is O.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘SLAM’ is coded as ‘4918’ and ‘LAME’ is coded as ‘2184’. What is the code for ‘S’ in the given language?
questions.explanation: L, A and M are in both words, as are 1, 4 and 8 in both codes. The letter left in SLAM is S and the digit left in its code is 9, so S = 9.

questions.text: Which two numbers should be interchanged to make the following equation correct? (54 ÷ 18)× 5 + 9 × 2 −45 + 12 × 3 = 57 (Note: Interchange should be done of the entire number and not individual digits of a given number.)
When the signs + and ÷ as well as the numbers 5 and 10 are interchanged, which option will be the correct one?
questions.explanation: After the interchanges 5 + 10 ÷ 2 = 4 reads 10 ÷ 5 + 2 = 2 + 2 = 4. The others give 6 + 5 ÷ 10 = 6.5, 10 + 1 ÷ 5 = 10.2 and 3 ÷ 10 + 5 = 5.3.

questions.text: In a code language, 'PORTER' is written as 'RVYALP' and 'REMOTE' is written as 'ELTVAR'. How will 'CLOUDY' be written in the same language?
questions.explanation: The first and last letters swap places and each letter between them moves 7 places forward (T wraps round to A): PORTER → R VYAL P and REMOTE → E LTVA R. So CLOUDY → Y SVBK C: YSVBKC.

questions.text: JHMK is related to PNSQ in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, NLQO is related to TRWU . To which of the following is QOTR related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 6 places forward: J → P, H → N, M → S, K → Q, and N → T, L → R, Q → W, O → U. So QOTR → WUZX.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g., 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding / subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (15, 14, 13) (12, 10, 8)
questions.explanation: In each set the middle number is the average of the other two: 15 + 13 = 2 × 14 and 12 + 8 = 2 × 10. Only (15, 15, 15) fits: 15 + 15 = 2 × 15.

questions.text: Read the given statement(s) and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement(s). Statements: All shirts are pants. Some shirts are watches. Conclusions: (I) Some pants are watches. (II) Some watches are not shirts.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: The shirts that are watches are also pants, so some pants are watches (I). Every watch could be a shirt, so II need not follow.

questions.text: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). E sits second to the right of A. B sits fourth to the right of D. F is an immediate neighbour of E and G. Who sits third to the right of C?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, a person's right is anticlockwise. Clockwise from A the seats are A, C, B, G, F, E, D: E is second to A's right, F sits between E and G, and only D in the seat on A's right puts B fourth to D's right. Third to the right of C is E.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? HCJ, JGL, LKN, ? , PSR
questions.explanation: First letters move 2 forward (H, J, L, N, P), second letters 4 forward (C, G, K, O, S) and third letters 2 forward (J, L, N, P, R): NOP.

questions.text: 4 is related to 34 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 7 is related to 61. To which of the following is 11 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding / subtracting / multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is 9 times the first minus 2: 9 × 4 − 2 = 34 and 9 × 7 − 2 = 61. Likewise 9 × 11 − 2 = 97.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 28, 31, 36, 43, 54, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 3, 5, 7, 11, successive prime numbers, so the next is 13: 54 + 13 = 67.

questions.text: DA2 is related to GD10 in a certain way. In the same way, SP7 is related to VS35. To which of the following is JG10 related following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Both letters move 3 places forward and the number is multiplied by 5: DA2 → GD10 and SP7 → VS35. So JG10 → MJ50.

questions.text: Drains exiting from Mohenjo-Daro had ________ doors that were probably closed at night to prevent vagrants or negative elements from entering the city through that access.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives wooden doors. The Harappans did not use iron, and a door of mud or sandstone could not easily be opened and shut every night.

questions.text: Which of the following was the capital of Vatsa Mahajanapada?
questions.explanation: Kausambi, on the Yamuna, was the capital of Vatsa. Ujjayini was the capital of Avanti, Vaishali of the Vajji confederacy and Ahichchhatra of northern Panchala.

questions.text: In Kerala and coastal area of Karnataka the pre-monsoon shower is known as ______.
questions.explanation: The pre-monsoon showers of Kerala and coastal Karnataka are called mango showers, as they help mangoes ripen early. Blossom showers make coffee flowers bloom, and Kalbaisakhi (Bardoisila in Assam) are the evening thunderstorms of Bengal and Assam.

questions.text: Former Indian actress Vyjayanthimala was trained in which classical dance form?
questions.explanation: Vyjayanthimala trained in Bharatanatyam, which she performed alongside her film career.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a commercial bank?
options: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development
The Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India Bank
questions.explanation: NABARD, set up in 1982, is an apex development finance institution for agriculture and rural development, not a commercial bank. DBS, SBI and ICICI Bank are commercial banks.

questions.text: According to the Human Development Index 2023-24, what is the rank of India?
questions.explanation: UNDP's Human Development Report 2023-24 ranks India 134th of 193 countries.

questions.text: The institution like Lokpal or Lokayukta (Ombudsman) was first created in which of the following countries?
questions.explanation: The ombudsman was first created in Sweden, in 1809; the Lokpal and Lokayuktas are India's version of it.

questions.text: According to Article ____, no religious instruction shall be provided in any educational institution wholly maintained out of State funds.
questions.explanation: Article 28(1) bars religious instruction in any educational institution wholly maintained out of State funds.

questions.text: In which year was Pt. Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (Scheme) announced by the Government of India?
questions.explanation: DDU-GKY, the Ministry of Rural Development's placement-linked skilling scheme for rural youth, was announced on 25 September 2014, Deen Dayal Upadhyaya's birth anniversary.

questions.text: In june 2023, which state government among the following has announced the 'Shakti' scheme for free bus travel for women and trans people within the state?
questions.explanation: Karnataka's Shakti scheme, launched on 11 June 2023, lets women and transgender persons travel free in the state's government buses within Karnataka.

questions.text: Bhamidipati Srivalli Rashmika is associated with which game?
questions.explanation: Shrivalli Rashmikaa Bhamidipaty, from Hyderabad, is a tennis player.

questions.text: In which weight category did Nitu Ghanghas win the IBA Women's World Boxing Championship event, 2023?
questions.explanation: Nitu Ghanghas won gold in the 48 kg category at the 2023 IBA Women's World Boxing Championships in New Delhi.

questions.text: Who among the following received the Nritya Kalanidhi for the year 2022?
questions.explanation: The Music Academy, Madras, named the Bharatanatyam dancer and guru Bragha Bessell its Nritya Kalanidhi for 2022.

questions.text: Vitamin D is synthesised using sunshine, by the:
questions.explanation: The skin makes vitamin D when it is exposed to the ultraviolet rays in sunlight.

questions.text: Which festival is celebrated at Sabarimala temple, on the occassion of Makar Sakranti?
questions.explanation: Makaravilakku is the festival held at Sabarimala on Makar Sankranti. Vishu is the Malayali new year, Onam Kerala's harvest festival and Ugadi the Telugu and Kannada new year.

questions.text: Which structure within the nucleus contains genetic information in the form of DNA?
questions.explanation: Chromosomes, made of DNA and proteins, carry the genetic information. The nucleolus makes ribosomes, which build proteins in the cytoplasm.

questions.text: What is the title of Sania Mirza's autobiography?
questions.explanation: Sania Mirza's autobiography is 'Ace Against Odds' (2016). 'Wings of Fire' is A. P. J. Abdul Kalam's, 'The Test of My Life' Yuvraj Singh's and 'Changing India' Manmohan Singh's.

questions.text: As on 31st October 2023, the youngest member of parliament (in terms of age) in the 17th Lok Sabha, Chandrani Murmu, represents which political party?
questions.explanation: Chandrani Murmu, elected from Keonjhar, Odisha, in 2019 at the age of 25, was the youngest member of the 17th Lok Sabha; she belongs to the Biju Janata Dal.

questions.text: Plutonic rocks are formed when lava cools ______.
questions.explanation: Plutonic (intrusive) igneous rocks such as granite form when molten rock cools slowly deep inside the crust, where it is strictly called magma. Lava that cools at the surface forms volcanic rocks such as basalt.

questions.text: Who among the following was the first sultan of Delhi Sultanate to visit the Ajmer shrine of Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti?
questions.explanation: Muhammad bin Tughlaq (ruled 1324-51) was the first Sultan to visit the shrine of Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti at Ajmer.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Where was the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association established in the year 1928?
questions.explanation: The Hindustan Socialist Republican Association was founded in September 1928 at Feroz Shah Kotla in Delhi, by Chandrashekhar Azad, Bhagat Singh and others.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which of the following years was a Hindu College in Benaras established to impart education from the ancient Sanskrit texts?
questions.explanation: Jonathan Duncan set up the Hindu College at Benaras in 1791 to encourage the study of ancient Sanskrit texts; the Calcutta Madrasa had been set up in 1781.

questions.text: In 2017, who became the first Indian singer to make it to Delhi's Madame Tussauds Museum?
questions.explanation: In 2017 Shreya Ghoshal became the first Indian singer to have a wax figure at Madame Tussauds, Delhi.

questions.text: Which of the following is the first planned industrial city in India?
questions.explanation: Jamshedpur, built around the Tata iron and steel works founded in 1907, is regarded as India's first planned industrial city.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. “This was not only exciting but rewarding” because I was able to experience adventure for the first time in my life.
options: This was not only excited but also rewarding
This was not only exciting but also rewarded
This was not only exciting but also rewarding
questions.explanation: 'Not only' pairs with 'but also': 'not only exciting but also rewarding'.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word to fill in the blank. Macbeth believed the witches’ _________ about his future.
questions.explanation: 'Prophecy' (a prediction) is spelt correctly and fits; the others should be 'questionnaire', 'surprise' and 'tyranny'.

questions.text: Select the appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the following sentence to make it grammatically correct. She is the most active and “the more” energetic social worker in our team.
questions.explanation: Both adjectives single her out in the team, so both take the superlative: 'the most active and the most energetic'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence. We rely on Hiren because he is “most intelligent” than many other boys in our school quiz team.
questions.explanation: 'Than' needs a comparative: 'more intelligent than many other boys'. 'Less intelligent' would give no reason to rely on him.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Boisterous
questions.explanation: 'Boisterous' means noisy and lively; its opposite is 'quiet'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The Lal Chowk is a large open square surrounded by mansions of the “wealthiest” classes than educated ones.
questions.explanation: 'Than' needs a comparative: 'the wealthier classes than educated ones'. 'More wealthier' is a double comparative.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Insist
questions.explanation: To 'insist' is to demand or press for something firmly; 'urge' is closest.

questions.text: Select the word segment that can substitute the bracketed words correctly and complete the sentence meaningfully. (My husband and I) are from Varanasi.
questions.explanation: Two people with the plural verb 'are' make 'both of us'; 'either of us', 'each one of us' and 'everyone of us' take a singular verb.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'succulent'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The teacher __________ the students to think critically about the topic.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'advised': one advises someone to do something. 'Acquiesced' and 'assented' mean agreed and cannot take 'the students' as an object; 'admonished' can mean 'urged firmly', but it carries a reproof the sentence does not suggest.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical/spelling error. She has taken / nothing from yesterday / and is feeling / nauseatic now.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'nothing from yesterday': with the present perfect, the starting point takes 'since', 'has taken nothing since yesterday'. 'Nauseous' or 'nauseated' is the usual word for 'nauseatic', so the last segment is arguable too.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. The strongest suit of documentary theatre lies not only in political insight and “ignorance”, but also in the variety of aesthetic approaches it makes possible.
questions.explanation: 'Ignorance' is lack of knowledge or understanding; its opposite is 'acumen', keen insight and judgement. 'Perspicuity' means clarity of expression.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. She often goes for a walk / with her dog / in the night.
options: She often goes for a walk
questions.explanation: Something done regularly after dark is done 'at night': 'goes for a walk with her dog at night'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. Army officers are given training to “decipher” the secret messages sent during war time.
questions.explanation: To 'decipher' a message is to 'decode' it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Excessive
questions.explanation: 'Excessive' means more than is reasonable: 'exorbitant'.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelled sentence.
options: The gardner planted colorfull flowers in the garden.
The gardner planted colorful flowers in the gardin.
The gardener planted colourfull flowers in the gardin.
The gardener planted colourful flowers in the garden.
questions.explanation: The correct spellings are 'gardener', 'colourful' (with one 'l' at the end) and 'garden'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and complete the given phrase. She was on cloud ________ after receiving the scholarship.
questions.explanation: To be 'on cloud nine' is to be extremely happy.

questions.text: Select the option that has used the correct tense.

questions.text: In a stationary shop, a pen is marked as ₹80 and it is sold at a discount of 15%. The shopkeeper also offers a special discount of ₹8 on the pen. Find the cost price of the pen if the shopkeeper earns a profit of 20%.
questions.explanation: ₹80 less 15% is ₹68, and the special discount brings it to ₹60. A 20% profit means CP × 1.2 = ₹60, so CP = ₹50.

questions.text: I walk at a speed of 10 km/h and reach my destination in 2 hrs. If I increase my speed by 2 km/h, how early would I reach my destination?
questions.explanation: The distance is 10 × 2 = 20 km. At 12 km/h it takes 20/12 hours = 1 hour 40 minutes: 20 minutes less.

questions.text: Rahul and Rohit start running on a circular track (of length 360 m) from the same point simultaneously with a speed of 3 m/s and 4 m/s. After how much time from the start, they will meet again at the starting point?
questions.explanation: Rahul takes 360/3 = 120 s a lap and Rohit 360/4 = 90 s. They are next at the start together after LCM(120, 90) = 360 s = 6 minutes.

questions.text: The sum of the radii of spheres A and B is 14 cm, the radius of A being larger than that of B. The difference between their surface areas is 112 π cm² . What is the ratio of the volumes of B to A?
questions.explanation: 4π(R² − r²) = 112π, so R² − r² = 28; with R + r = 14, R − r = 2. So R = 8 and r = 6, and the volumes go as the cubes: 6³ : 8³ = 216 : 512 = 27 : 64.

questions.text: The HCF of 204 and 1547 is:
Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2500 as a sum borrowed at 5% per year rate of interest for 2 years.
Manoj buys 1 kg tomato for ₹80 and sells it for ₹90. He also uses a weight of 800 gm in place of 1 kg. What is Manoj’s actual profit percentage on the sale of 1 kg tomato?
questions.explanation: For ₹90 he gives only 800 g, which cost him 0.8 × ₹80 = ₹64. Profit = 26/64 × 100 = 40.625%.

questions.text: In a class of 40 students the ratio of boys to girls is 3 : 5. If the average marks scored by the boys in Science is 70 and the average marks scored by the whole class in Science is 60, then find the average marks scored by the girls in Science.
questions.explanation: There are 15 boys and 25 girls. The class total is 40 × 60 = 2,400 and the boys' 15 × 70 = 1,050, so the girls average 1,350/25 = 54.

questions.text: ₹7,000 becomes ₹7,567 in 2 years at simple interest at a certain rate percentage. Find the principal amount (in ₹) that will become ₹24,050 in 5 years at the same rate of interest.
questions.explanation: The interest for 2 years is ₹567, so the rate is 567/(7,000 × 2) × 100 = 4.05% a year. In 5 years the amount is P × 1.2025 = ₹24,050, so P = ₹20,000.

questions.text: The average marks obtained by 75 students in a certain examination is 38. Find the total marks.
In an examination, the average marks obtained by 15 students was 96, by 12 other students was 84 and by 13 other students was 68. Find the average marks of all 40 students.
The average weight of a family of five members (in kg) whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 69 kg and 36 kg is:

What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order ? CEH, FHK, IKN, LNQ, ?
questions.explanation: Every letter moves 3 places forward each time: C, F, I, L, O; E, H, K, N, Q; H, K, N, Q, T. The next cluster is OQT.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the following series? 12, 18, 36, 90, 252, ?
questions.explanation: The differences 6, 18, 54, 162 are each three times the one before, so the next is 486: 252 + 486 = 738.

questions.text: What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 15 ÷ 15 – 30 + 225 × 25 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 15 × 15 + 30 − 225 ÷ 25 = 225 + 30 − 9 = 246.

questions.text: This question has two statements followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the given statements. Statements: All apricots are buns. All buns are sweet. Conclusions (I) Some apricots are sweet. (II) Some buns are apricots.
questions.explanation: All apricots are buns and all buns are sweet, so all apricots are sweet, and some apricots are sweet (I). As all apricots are buns, some buns are apricots (II). Both follow.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (6, 24, 36) (8, 11, 25)
questions.explanation: In each set the third number is the sum of the first two plus 6: 6 + 24 + 6 = 36 and 8 + 11 + 6 = 25. Likewise 5 + 19 + 6 = 30.

questions.text: Seven friends - M, N, O, P, Q, R, and S - are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). O is sitting third to the right of S. N is sitting second to the right of O. Q is an immediate neighbour of both M and S. P is an immediate neighbour of both O and N. Who is sitting to the immediate right of R?
questions.explanation: Counting to the right of S: O is 3rd, N 5th and P, between them, 4th. Q sits next to S with M beside it, so Q is 1st and M 2nd (with Q 6th, M would need N's seat), leaving R 6th, just to the left of S. So S is to R's immediate right.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘EVIL’ is coded as ‘5731’ and ‘BEAD’ is coded as ‘4816’.What is the code for ‘E’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: E is the only letter in both words and 1 the only digit in both codes, so E = 1.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘FEEDING’ is coded as ‘ECBDJPJ’ and ‘SURFACE’ is coded as ‘RSOFBEH’. How will ‘MIGRATE’ be coded in the same language?
questions.explanation: The letters move −1, −2, −3, 0, +1, +2, +3 in turn: FEEDING → ECBDJPJ and SURFACE → RSOFBEH. So MIGRATE → LGDRBVH.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘GOAT’ is coded as ‘2684’ and ‘OPEN’ is coded as ‘3598’.What is the code for ‘O’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: O is the only letter in both words and 8 the only digit in both codes, so O = 8.

questions.text: KRAV is related to GNWR in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, UBKF is related to QXGB. To which of the following is IPYT related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 4 places back (A wraps round to W): KRAV → GNWR and UBKF → QXGB. So IPYT → ELUP.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 111 – 1 + 36 ÷ 2 × 12 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 111 + 1 − 36 × 2 ÷ 12 = 112 − 6 = 106.

questions.text: Adesh, Rinki, Narendra, Priya, Kiara, Sahil, and Lakshmi are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Kiara sits third to the left of Sahil. Rinki sits to the immediate right of Priya, who sits with Sahil. Adesh sits second to the right of Lakshmi. Who is sitting to the immediate left of Adesh?
questions.explanation: Counting to the right of Sahil: Kiara, third to his left, is 4th. Priya sits next to Sahil with Rinki on her right, so Priya is 1st and Rinki 2nd (on Sahil's left, Priya would put Rinki in Sahil's seat). Adesh, second to the right of Lakshmi, fits only as 5th with Lakshmi 3rd, so Kiara (4th) is to Adesh's immediate left.

questions.text: 12 is related to 139 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 17 is related to 284. To which ofthe following is 18 related, following the same logic?(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbersinto its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: Each number is squared and 5 taken away: 12² − 5 = 139 and 17² − 5 = 284. So 18² − 5 = 319.

questions.text: FH 61 is related to JL 69 in a certain way. In the same way, QS 76 is related to UW 84. To which of the following is LN 46 related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 4 places forward and the number rises by 8: FH 61 → JL 69 and QS 76 → UW 84. So LN 46 → PR 54.

questions.text: Which of the following neighbouring countries of India is most populous?
questions.explanation: Pakistan, with about 24 crore people by its 2023 census, is more populous than Bangladesh (about 17 crore); Afghanistan and Bhutan are far smaller.

questions.text: In the year 1940, the national games were hosted by which of the following cities?
questions.explanation: The 1940 edition, held in Bombay, was the first under the name National Games; until then the event was the Indian Olympic Games.

questions.text: The Mayurbhanj District in Odisha is a part of which Biosphere Reserve from the following?
questions.explanation: The Similipal Biosphere Reserve lies in Odisha's Mayurbhanj district.

questions.text: In which of the following years was the state of Golconda finally annexed into the Mughal empire?
questions.explanation: Aurangzeb took Golconda after a long siege in 1687 and annexed the Qutb Shahi kingdom to the Mughal empire.

questions.text: Which of the following is/are the highest judiciary in India?
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court is the highest court of India; Parliament is the legislature, not a court.

questions.text: Which of the following gases is generally used to flush bags of chips by the manufacturers?
questions.explanation: Bags of chips are flushed with nitrogen, an unreactive gas, so that the oil in them is not oxidised and does not turn rancid.

questions.explanation: Guru Ghasidas founded the Satnami movement in the Chhattisgarh region in the early nineteenth century, preaching equality and rejecting caste.

questions.text: In which of the following states is the groundnut fair, ’Kadalekayi Parishe’ celebrated on the last Monday of the Karthika month of the Hindu calendar?
questions.explanation: Kadalekayi Parishe, the groundnut fair, is held at the Bull Temple in Basavanagudi, Bengaluru, Karnataka.

questions.text: The Great Granary was one of the largest granaries in the _______________.
questions.explanation: The Great Granary is one of the largest buildings excavated at the cities of the Harappan Civilization.

questions.text: As on February 2024, Nitish Kumar is the 9th time Chief Minister of which state?
questions.explanation: Nitish Kumar was sworn in as Chief Minister of Bihar for the ninth time on 28 January 2024.

questions.text: Forward Bloc was founded in 1939-40 by which of the following leaders?
questions.explanation: Subhas Chandra Bose founded the All India Forward Bloc in 1939, after resigning as Congress president.

questions.text: Who among the following Indian dancers was honoured with the Padma Vibhushan in 1971, who was also known as the father of modern Indian dance?
questions.explanation: Uday Shankar, who blended Indian classical and folk forms with Western theatre, is called the father of modern Indian dance; he received the Padma Vibhushan in 1971.

questions.text: As per Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, what is the total length of National Highways in India as of November 2022?

questions.text: What does a budget deficit indicate?

The government is saving for future projects
questions.explanation: A budget deficit is the gap when a government's spending is more than its revenue.

questions.text: In December 2023, who became the first women Chief of Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) in India?
questions.explanation: Nina Singh, an IPS officer of the Rajasthan cadre, became the first woman Director General of the CISF in December 2023.

questions.text: Which of the following is the federal feature of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: A bicameral legislature, with the Rajya Sabha representing the states, is a federal feature. All India Services, single citizenship and an integrated judiciary are unitary features.

questions.explanation: Nehru's 'An Autobiography' (1936) was published in the United States as 'Toward Freedom'.

questions.text: In the 1974 edition of the Guinness Book of Records, which playback singer was mentioned as the most recorded artist in human history?
questions.explanation: The 1974 Guinness Book of Records named Lata Mangeshkar the most recorded artist in history.

questions.text: Dandiya Raas is a famous dance form of which state?

questions.text: What is the female literacy rate in India, as per the 2011 census?
questions.explanation: The 2011 census's provisional figures, the ones usually cited, put female literacy at 65.46% and male at 82.14% (74.04% overall).

questions.text: Palkigundu Minor Rock Edicts of Ashoka are located in _________.

questions.text: Based on the context of the given sentence, select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank. Siri was feeling ____________ after receiving praise from her professor for completing the project ahead of schedule.

questions.explanation: One is allergic 'to' something: 'allergic to peanuts'.

The dog is the faithful animal.
The dog is more useful than any other animal.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given phrase. A person who does not believe in the institution of marriage
