questions.text: Two trains start at the same time from two stations and travel towards each other with speeds of 72 km/h and 84 km/h, respectively. When they cross each other, it is found that one train has covered 108 km more than the other. What is the distance (in km) between the two stations, and after how many hours will they meet, respectively?
questions.explanation: Each hour the faster train covers 84 − 72 = 12 km more, so they meet after 108/12 = 9 hours. Distance = (72 + 84) × 9 = 156 × 9 = 1404 km.

questions.text: The sum of three consecutive odd numbers is 58 more than the average of these numbers. Find the largest number.
questions.explanation: With the numbers x − 2, x and x + 2, the sum is 3x and the average x: 3x = x + 58, so x = 29 and the largest is 31.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2000 as a sum borrowed at 8% per year rate of interest for 5 years.
A solid sphere of radius 9 cm is melted to form a hollow, right circular cylindrical tube of length 12 cm and external radius 15 cm. The thickness (in cm) of the tube is:
questions.explanation: The volume is unchanged: (4/3)π × 9³ = 972π = π(15² − r²) × 12, so 225 − r² = 81 and the inner radius r = 12 cm. Thickness = 15 − 12 = 3 cm.

questions.text: The ratio between the monthly incomes of P and Q is 7 : 6 and the ratio between their expenditures is 6 : 5. If they save ₹480 each, then find P’s monthly income.
questions.explanation: With incomes 7x and 6x and expenditures 6y and 5y: 7x − 6y = 480 and 6x − 5y = 480. Then 35x − 30y = 2400 and 36x − 30y = 2880, so x = 480 and P's income = 7 × 480 = ₹3,360.

questions.text: In an examination, the average marks of the student in class were 85.4. If the student had got 8 more marks in History, 12 more marks in Science, 10 more marks in Computer Science, 15 less marks in Hindi and retained the same marks in other subjects, then the average would have been 87.9. How many subjects were there in the examination?
questions.explanation: The total would rise by 8 + 12 + 10 − 15 = 15 marks and the average by 87.9 − 85.4 = 2.5, so there were 15/2.5 = 6 subjects.

questions.text: Amar buys a wall clock for ₹300 and sells it for ₹200. Find his percentage loss.
The average marks of 60 students was found to be 48. Later on, it was discovered that a score of 68 was misread as 56. Find the correct average corresponding to the correct score.
questions.explanation: The total was 68 − 56 = 12 marks short, so the average rises by 12/60 = 0.2: 48 + 0.2 = 48.2.

questions.text: There are five baskets- A, B, C, D and E. Each basket has rings in it and the average number of rings in all five baskets is 42. If basket D is removed, the average number of rings in the remaining baskets is 38. How many rings are there in basket D?
questions.explanation: All five baskets hold 5 × 42 = 210 rings and the other four 4 × 38 = 152, so D has 210 − 152 = 58.

questions.text: A sum was deposited at a certain rate of simple interest for 4 years. If it had been a 5% higher rate of interest, then it would have amounted to ₹5,200 more. The sum deposited is:
questions.explanation: 5% more a year for 4 years is 20% of the sum: 20% = ₹5,200, so the sum is ₹26,000.

questions.text: The greatest number which exactly divides the numbers 38, 95 and 171 is:
The salary of a person was reduced by 20%. By what percentage should his reduced salary be raised so as to bring it at par with his original salary?
questions.explanation: A salary of 100 falls to 80; raising 80 back to 100 needs 20/80 × 100 = 25%.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘BEND’ is written as ‘ADMC’ and ‘FISH’ is written as ‘EHRG’. How will ‘EVIL’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one place back: B → A, E → D, N → M, D → C. So EVIL → DUHK.

questions.text: E, F, G, H, I, J and K are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). I sits third to the left of J. E is an immediate neighbour of both G and H. G sits third to the right of J. F sits second to the right of I. What is the position of K with respect to H?
questions.explanation: I is third to J's left and G third to J's right, so they sit side by side; E takes G's other side, with H beyond it, and F is second to I's right. Going round to the left from J: J, F, K, I, G, E, H. Counting left from H: J, F, K, so K is third to the left of H.

questions.text: AI10 is related to YG12 in a certain way. In the same way, BJ20 is related to ZH22. To which of the following is CK30 related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Both letters move 2 places back and the number rises by 2: A → Y, I → G, 10 → 12. So C → A, K → I and 30 → 32: AI32.

questions.text: In a code language, 'MBXL' is coded as ‘OXZH’ and 'FKRG' is coded as ‘HGTC’. How will 'LUGS' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +2, −4, +2, −4: M → O, B → X, X → Z, L → H. So L → N, U → Q, G → I, S → O: NQIO.

questions.text: 6 is related to 77 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 9 is related to 116. To which of the following is 11 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The number is multiplied by 13 and 1 taken away: 6 × 13 − 1 = 77 and 9 × 13 − 1 = 116. So 11 × 13 − 1 = 142.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘KNOW’ is coded as ‘2846’ and ‘WIDE’ is coded as ‘5729’.What is the code for ‘W’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: W is the only letter in both words and 2 the only digit in both codes, so W = 2.

questions.text: Which of the following interchanges of signs would make the given equation correct? 8 − 4 + 144 ÷ 16 × 27 = 14
OM 13 is related to RP 17 in a certain way. In the same way, WU 19 is related to ZX 23. To which of the following is IG 14 related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Both letters move 3 places forward and the number rises by 4: O → R, M → P, 13 → 17. So I → L, G → J and 14 → 18: LJ 18.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 234 × 6 − 6 ÷ 66 + 60 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 234 ÷ 6 + 6 × 66 − 60 = 39 + 396 − 60 = 375.

questions.text: A, B, L, N, S, T and Z are seven candidates sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order), for a group discussion. L is sitting third to the left of N. N is sitting exactly between T and B. Z is an immediate neighbour of B and is sitting third to the left of S. Z is also an immediate neighbour of A. Who is sitting second to the left of N?
questions.explanation: With B on N's left, Z would sit beside B and S would need T's seat; so B is on N's right. Going round to the left from N: N, T, S, L, A, Z, B. Second to the left of N is S.

questions.text: In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 12, 108; 20, 180
questions.explanation: The second number is 9 times the first: 12 × 9 = 108 and 20 × 9 = 180. Likewise 25 × 9 = 225.

questions.text: Read the given statement(s) and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement(s). Statements: All belts are wallets. Some wallets are glasses. Conclusions: (I) Some belts are glasses. (II) Some glasses are not wallets.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: The wallets that are glasses need not be belts, so I does not follow; and every glass may be a wallet, so II does not follow either.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? FOM, ILJ, LIG, OFD, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move 3 forward (F, I, L, O, R), second letters 3 back (O, L, I, F, C) and third letters 3 back (M, J, G, D, A): RCA.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 86, 91, 101, 116, ?
questions.explanation: The differences grow by 5: +5, +10, +15, +20. 116 + 20 = 136.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘FITS’ is coded as ‘ULID’ and ‘GIFT’ is coded as ‘IUZD’. What is the code for ‘G’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: F, I and T are in both words, and U, I and D in both codes. The letter left in GIFT is G and the code letter left in IUZD is Z (in FITS they are S and L), so G = Z.

questions.text: Read the given statement(s) and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement(s). Statements: Some babies are humans. All babies are animals. Conclusions: (I) At least some animals are humans. (II) All animals are babies.
questions.explanation: The babies who are humans are also animals, so some animals are humans (I). Nothing says every animal is a baby, so II does not follow.

questions.text: Which of the following national leaders of India inaugurated the first Akhil Bhartiya Kalidas Samman Samaroh held in Ujjain in 1958?
questions.explanation: The first Akhil Bharatiya Kalidas Samaroh at Ujjain, in 1958, was inaugurated by President Rajendra Prasad; Jawaharlal Nehru opened the next year's.

questions.text: The famous folk dance 'Dholacha Nach' is performed in which state?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Maharashtra; 'Dholacha Nach' is Marathi for 'dance of the dhol', the drum.

questions.text: In 2023, the philanthropic organisation Carnegie Corporation of New York placed Ajay Banga, the President of ______, on its annual 'Great Immigrants' list. This list consists of honourees who have enriched and strengthened America and its democracy through their contributions and actions.
questions.explanation: Ajay Banga became President of the World Bank in June 2023, and was named on Carnegie's 'Great Immigrants' list that year.

questions.text: Which of the following is/are an example of a non-tax revenue receipt?
questions.explanation: Interest the government earns is a non-tax revenue receipt. Disinvestment and borrowings are capital receipts, and income tax is tax revenue.

questions.text: On 11th December 2022, who among the following took over as the Deputy Chief Minister of Himachal Pradesh?
questions.explanation: Mukesh Agnihotri was sworn in as Deputy Chief Minister of Himachal Pradesh on 11 December 2022, with Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu as Chief Minister.

questions.text: The position of the President in the Indian Political system is that of a ________.
questions.explanation: The President is the nominal (constitutional) head; real executive power lies with the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.

questions.text: Who was the Prime Minister when the 11th Fundamental Duty was incorporated into the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The 11th Fundamental Duty, Article 51A(k) (education for children of 6 to 14), was added by the 86th Amendment in 2002, when Atal Bihari Vajpayee was Prime Minister.

questions.text: The village servants or functionaries, who constituted of groups of families in Vijayanagar empire, were called __________.
questions.explanation: In the Vijayanagara empire the hereditary village servants and functionaries were the ayagars.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The Fourth Anglo-Mysore War was fought in the year ________.
questions.explanation: The Fourth Anglo-Mysore War was fought in 1799; Tipu Sultan was killed defending Seringapatam.

questions.text: Where is the headquarters of the West Central Railway Zone?
questions.explanation: The West Central Railway zone has its headquarters at Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh.

questions.text: Which team won the first edition of the Women's Premier League (WPL) event in the year 2023?
questions.explanation: Mumbai Indians won the first Women's Premier League in 2023, beating Delhi Capitals in the final.

questions.text: The Indian Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change maintains a log of all the endangered species of India along with their conservation status. What is the name of this book?
questions.explanation: The Red Data Book records endangered plants and animals; the IUCN keeps the global one, and India keeps its own for Indian species.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: At which of the following places was the first Singh Sabha founded in 1873?
questions.explanation: The first Singh Sabha was founded at Amritsar in 1873; the Lahore Singh Sabha followed in 1879.

questions.text: Which of the following festivals is celebrated in the month of Chaitra?
questions.explanation: Ram Navami, Rama's birthday, falls on the ninth day of the bright half of Chaitra.

questions.text: The National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) was launched by the Government of India in the year ________.
questions.explanation: The National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme was launched in August 2016 to encourage apprenticeship training.

questions.text: Which state lies in the rain shadow region of the Arabian Sea branch of the southwest monsoon?
questions.explanation: The Tamil Nadu coast stays fairly dry in the southwest monsoon: it lies in the rain shadow of the Arabian Sea branch, beyond the Western Ghats.

questions.text: For which song did Tanvi Shah become the first Indian woman to win a Grammy Award in 2010?
questions.explanation: Tanvi Shah shared the 2010 Grammy for 'Jai Ho' from 'Slumdog Millionaire', the first Indian woman to win one.

questions.text: What approach did Dadabhai Naoroji use to calculate the Poverty Line?
questions.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji based his poverty line on the cost of the subsistence diet given to prisoners in jails, the 'jail cost of living'.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is/are correct temples of Khajuraho? a) Equal importance is given to human experience and spiritual pursuit. b) Jain and Hindu temples are also found at Khajuraho. c) Chausanth Yogini temple is one of the important temples here.
questions.explanation: Khajuraho's Chandela temples include both Hindu and Jain temples, among them the Chausath Yogini temple, and their sculpture gives worldly life a place beside the spiritual. All three statements are correct.

questions.text: In rat-hole mining, which of the following minerals is mined?
questions.explanation: Rat-hole mining digs narrow tunnels to reach thin coal seams, as in Meghalaya.

questions.text: Literal meaning of 'megalith' is _____________________.
questions.explanation: 'Megalith' comes from the Greek 'megas' (big) and 'lithos' (stone): a big stone, as used to mark burials.

questions.text: Which of the following Hindi novels is written by Vishnu Prabhakar?
questions.explanation: Vishnu Prabhakar's novel 'Ardhnarishwar' won him the Sahitya Akademi Award. 'Kyapa' ('Kyap') is Manohar Shyam Joshi's and 'Mujhe Chand Chahiye' Surendra Verma's.

questions.text: Gluten formation is observed in various foods like pasta, noodles, pizzas, and bread. Gluten occurs when two specific proteins are mixed with water. Name the two proteins responsible for gluten formation.
questions.explanation: Gluten forms when the wheat proteins glutenin and gliadin are mixed with water.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Effective “responses of climate change” are imperative to protect the world’s children and fulfil their rights.
questions.explanation: A 'response' is made 'to' something: 'responses to climate change'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank . The company's decision to relocate had a negative ___________ on its employees.
questions.explanation: A decision has an 'effect on' people: 'a negative effect on its employees'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Always keep in mind leaner bodies need more calories than “fattest” ones.
questions.explanation: A comparison with 'than' takes the comparative: 'more calories than fatter ones'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. We often go camping, but I have never been to that “particular part of town or country” before.
questions.explanation: One's 'neck of the woods' is a particular area or neighbourhood.

questions.text: Select the sentence that has a grammatical error.
options: They have an information about the event.
She is an artist at a local gallery.
Can you bring me the keys to the car?
The cat is sleeping on a mat.
questions.explanation: 'Information' is uncountable and takes no 'an': 'They have information about the event.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined word. The old library had a “musty” smell from years of neglect.
questions.explanation: A 'musty' smell is a damp, 'stale' one.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence. I have “never had” and never will be dependent on him.
questions.explanation: Each verb must fit 'dependent on him': 'I have never been and never will be dependent on him.' 'Have never had ... dependent' does not work.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Brave
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'brave' is 'cowardly'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. I did not like his “bossy” attitude.
questions.explanation: 'Bossy' means fond of giving orders: 'controlling'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word from the given sentence. The kitten's playful behaivor brought joy to the entire family.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'behaviour' ('behavior' in American English).

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom from the alternatives. Rajiv will understand some day that all his friends are “fair weather friends”.
options: A friend who stays only when times are convenient
A friend who meets you only during pleasant weather
True friends help you when you need them
questions.explanation: A 'fair-weather friend' stays only while things go well and leaves in hard times.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. When we _____________ ourselves, we activate a variety of psychological processes that help us achieve our objectives and improve our overall well-being.
questions.explanation: To 'believe in' ourselves, to have self-confidence, is what helps us achieve our objectives; the other words do not fit.

questions.text: Select the option that rectifies the INCORRECT spelling in the given sentence. If you try to conwince people that money is not very important, then you are barking up the wrong tree.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'convince'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Collapse
questions.explanation: To 'collapse' is to fall down suddenly: 'fall'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. If the players don’t wear sunscreen, / their faces will / get reddest.
options: If the players don’t wear sunscreen,
questions.explanation: Nothing is being compared, so the superlative 'reddest' is wrong: 'their faces will get red'.

questions.text: Select the correct spelling from the given options to fill in the blank. We ________ to keep you informed of any delay to your expected delivery date.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'endeavour' ('endeavor' in American English).

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. compassionate
questions.explanation: 'Compassionate' means feeling for others' suffering; its opposite is 'cruel'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If I wrote an email / to my boss now, / he will react / by yelling at me tomorrow in the morning.
options: by yelling at me tomorrow in the morning.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'If I wrote an email': with 'he will react' in the main clause, the first conditional needs the present, 'If I write an email to my boss now, he will react ...'. (Keeping 'wrote' and changing 'will' to 'would' would also make the sentence correct, so 'he will react' is arguable.)

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Rahul was angry “of” his brother as he broke his pen.
questions.explanation: One is 'angry at' (or 'with') a person, not 'angry of'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Sports further demand continuous practice, hard work and ___2___ training. One must understand that sport not only has physical benefits but also ___3___ concentration and inner strength. Not only this, one who plays feels that ____4___ overall personality has undergone a change for better. Besides, social connectivity or networking, games develop ___5___ spirit in players.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Sport is expected to 'operate', that is to work, at a very high moral plane.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Continuous practice, hard work and 'relentless', that is unceasing, training; 'paltry', 'abated' and 'faltering' would weaken it.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: A class of 42 students took a Physics test. 18 students had an average score of 95. The other students had an average score of 73. What is the average score (rounded off to one decimal place) of the whole class?
questions.explanation: 18 × 95 = 1,710 and 24 × 73 = 1,752, so the class totals 3,462 and averages 3,462/42 ≈ 82.4.

questions.text: Three numbers are in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5 and their LCM is 2400. Their HCF is:
questions.explanation: The numbers are 3k, 4k and 5k, with LCM 60k = 2400, so k = 40. As 3, 4 and 5 have no common factor, the HCF is k = 40.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3500 as a sum borrowed at 6% per year rate of interest for 5 years.
Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3000 as a sum borrowed at 3% per year rate of interest for 2 years.

The average of 8 numbers 127, 432, p, 89, q, 99, 842 and 76 is 221 and the numbers p and q are two-digit numbers. If the units digit of p is one less than that of q and tens digit of q is one less than that of p, then the sum of the digits of p is:
questions.explanation: The eight numbers total 8 × 221 = 1,768 and the six known ones 1,665, so p + q = 103. With p = 10a + b and q = 10(a − 1) + (b + 1), p + q = 20a + 2b − 9 = 103, so 10a + b = 56: p = 56 (and q = 47), whose digits add up to 11.

questions.text: Arman leaves ₹2,17,600 to be divided among four sons, three daughters and five nephews. If each daughter receives 3 times as much as each nephew and each son receives 5 times as much as each nephew, how much does each son receive?
questions.explanation: If each nephew gets x, the sons get 4 × 5x = 20x, the daughters 3 × 3x = 9x and the nephews 5x. 34x = ₹2,17,600, so x = ₹6,400 and each son gets 5x = ₹32,000.

questions.text: When the price of an article was reduced by 10% its sale increased by 60%. What was the net effect on the revenue?
questions.explanation: Revenue = price × sales: 0.9 × 1.6 = 1.44, an increase of 44%.

questions.text: A person marks his goods x% above the cost price and allows a discount of 28% on the marked price. If his profit is 22.4%, then the value of x is:
questions.explanation: 0.72 × marked price = 1.224 × cost price, so the marked price is 1.7 times the cost: x = 70.

questions.text: If the radius of a cylinder is decreased by 25% and the height is increased by 25% to form a new cylinder, what is the percentage decrease in new volume (rounded off to two digits after the decimal)?
questions.explanation: V = πr²h, so the new volume is 0.75² × 1.25 = 0.703125 of the old one: a decrease of 29.6875% ≈ 29.69%.

questions.text: Kumar took a loan from a bank at the rate of 9.5% per annum at simple interest. After 6 years he had to pay ₹3,705 as interest only for the period. The principal amount borrowed by him was:

The milk and water in two buckets P and Q are in the ratio 5 : 3 and 1 : 4, respectively. In what ratio are the liquids in both the buckets mixed to obtain a new mixture in a third bucket R containing 50% milk and 50% water?
questions.explanation: Milk is 5/8 of bucket P and 1/5 of bucket Q. For a half-milk mixture, by alligation P : Q = (1/2 − 1/5) : (5/8 − 1/2) = 3/10 : 1/8 = 12 : 5.

questions.text: In a certain language, ‘this college bag is expensive’ is coded as ‘br od hy jh pb’ and ‘your bag looks very heavy’ is coded as ‘mh sa tn dl od’. How is ‘bag’ coded in the given language?
questions.explanation: 'bag' is the only word in both sentences and 'od' the only code in both, so bag = od.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 6 ÷ 3 × 2 + 1 – 2 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 6 × 3 ÷ 2 − 1 + 2 = 9 − 1 + 2 = 10.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘sold the painting’ is written as ‘ju ri gi’ and ‘directors sold business’ is coded as ‘hu fe ju’. How is ‘sold’ coded in that language?
questions.explanation: 'sold' is the only word in both phrases and 'ju' the only code in both, so sold = ju.

questions.text: 11 is related to 127 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 8 is related to 70. To which ofthe following is 14 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbersinto its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc., to 13 canbe performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each number is squared and 6 added: 11² + 6 = 127 and 8² + 6 = 70. So 14² + 6 = 202.

questions.text: In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 18, 37; 22, 45
questions.explanation: The second number is twice the first plus 1: 2 × 18 + 1 = 37 and 2 × 22 + 1 = 45. Likewise 2 × 26 + 1 = 53.

questions.text: E, F, G, H, I and J are sitting around a round table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). F is sitting to the immediate left of G and immediate right of E. J is sitting to the immediate right of H and immediate left of I. H is sitting to the immediate right of G. Who is sitting to the immediate left of E?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, a person's immediate left is the next seat clockwise. The clues give the clockwise order I, J, H, G, F, E, which closes the circle, so I sits to the immediate left of E.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: •Some mats are yolks. •Some toys are mats. Conclusions: (I)Some mats are jute. (II)Toy is a yolk.
questions.explanation: Jute is not mentioned in the statements, so I cannot follow; and the toys that are mats need not be among the mats that are yolks, so II does not follow either.

questions.text: MKQO is related to TRXV in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, KIOM is related to RPVT. To which of the following is HFLJ related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 7 places forward: M → T, K → R, Q → X, O → V and K → R, I → P, O → V, M → T. So H → O, F → M, L → S and J → Q: OMSQ.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘listen to music’ is written as ‘fd si lr’ and ‘you should listen’ is writtenas ‘lr ep wi’. How is ‘listen’ writtenin the given language?
questions.explanation: 'listen' is the only word in both sentences and 'lr' the only code in both, so listen = lr.

questions.text: Read the given statement(s) and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement(s). Statements: Some pillows are curtains. No curtain is a bedsheet. Conclusions: (I) All pillows can never be bedsheets. (II) Some curtains are not pillows.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
questions.explanation: The pillows that are curtains cannot be bedsheets, so it is impossible for all pillows to be bedsheets (I). The curtains may all be pillows, so II does not follow.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘quip area flash’ is coded as 'er to pg' and ‘bacon quip bonus’ is coded as ‘to my te’. How is ‘quip’ coded in the given language?
questions.explanation: 'quip' is the only word in both phrases and 'to' the only code in both, so quip = to.

questions.text: What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 31 × 961 ÷ 155 – 73 + 54 = ?
Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 6 ,7, 9, 13, 21, ?
questions.explanation: The differences double each time: +1, +2, +4, +8, so the next is +16: 21 + 16 = 37.

questions.text: JK 3 is related to MH 6 in a certain way. In the same way, OD 11 is related to RA 14. To which of the following is RD 14 related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: The first letter moves 3 places forward, the second 3 places back and the number rises by 3: J → M, K → H, 3 → 6 and O → R, D → A, 11 → 14. So RD 14 → UA 17.

questions.text: A, C, F, E, B, U and P are sitting around a circular table facing away from the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). F is sitting third to the right of E. P is sitting third to the left of A. U is sitting third to the right of C. E is an immediate neighbour to the left of P. C is not an immediate neighbour of P. Who among the following is sitting third to the right of U?
questions.explanation: Facing away from the centre, a person's right is the next seat clockwise. Numbering the seats clockwise with P at 0: E is at 6 (P's immediate left), F at 2 (third to the right of E) and A at 3 (P is third to its left). C may not sit next to P and U is third to its right, so C is at 5 and U at 1, leaving B at 4. Third to the right of U is seat 4: B.

questions.text: Find the missing term in the following series: MM, LO, KQ, __, IU, HW.
questions.explanation: The first letters go back one at a time (M, L, K, J, I, H) and the second letters forward two (M, O, Q, S, U, W): JS.

questions.text: Indian classical vocalist and Padma Vibhushan awardee Kishori Amonkar belongs to which of the following gharanas?
questions.explanation: Kishori Amonkar sang in the Jaipur (Jaipur-Atrauli) gharana, which she learned from her mother, Mogubai Kurdikar.

questions.text: Kathakali, one of the classical dance forms, is performed primarily in which state of India?
questions.explanation: Kathakali, the dance-drama known for its elaborate make-up and costumes, is a classical dance form of Kerala.

questions.text: Who was appointed as the governor of Bengal by Sultan Balban after the revolt and subsequent death of Tughril Beg?
questions.explanation: After crushing Tughril Beg's revolt in Bengal, Balban made his son Bughra Khan its governor.

questions.text: In which year did Roshan Mistry become the first Indian woman to win an Asian Games medal when she took the silver in the 100-m sprint?
questions.explanation: Roshan Mistry took silver in the women's 100 m at the 1951 Asian Games in New Delhi, the first Asian Games medal won by an Indian woman.

questions.text: In 1973, the first female high court judge of India Anna Chandy published her autobiography ____________________ in Malayalam.
questions.explanation: Anna Chandy's autobiography is 'Atmakatha' (1973). 'The Race of My Life' is Milkha Singh's, 'The Test of My Life' Yuvraj Singh's and 'Playing It My Way' Sachin Tendulkar's.

questions.text: Which of the following languages was used by the Sangam poets for composing the texts?
questions.explanation: The Sangam poems, the earliest literature of south India, were composed in Tamil.

questions.text: According to the National Multidimensional Poverty Index of India: A Progress Review 2023, which of the following states has the LOWEST percentage of population being multidimensionally poor?
questions.explanation: In the 2023 review Sikkim had a far smaller share of its people multidimensionally poor in 2019-21 than Manipur (8.10%), West Bengal (11.89%) or Rajasthan.

questions.text: The religious festival, 'Easter' is celebrated by which community?
questions.explanation: Easter, which celebrates the resurrection of Jesus Christ, is a Christian festival.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following organisations was established in Bombay by Atmaram Pandurang?
questions.explanation: The Prarthana Samaj, a reform society inspired by the Brahmo Samaj, was founded in Bombay in 1867 by Atmaram Pandurang.

questions.text: Which of the following location has NOT been selected for setting up the seven PM Mega Integrated Textile Region and Apparel (PM MITRA) Park for the textile sector announced by the Government of India in March 2023?
questions.explanation: The seven PM MITRA parks announced in March 2023 are in Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh; none is in West Bengal.

questions.text: Sedimentary rocks are formed by the process of deposition and compaction of fragments of rocks of various sizes. This process is called:
questions.explanation: Lithification is the compaction and cementation of deposited sediment into sedimentary rock. Weathering breaks rocks down, and laccoliths are bodies of intrusive igneous rock.

questions.text: Who received 'Sangeet Natak Akademi' award 2022 for his/her contribution in the field of Kathak?
questions.explanation: The Sangeet Natak Akademi Awards for 2022, announced in February 2024, gave the Kathak award jointly to the sisters Nalini and Kamalini Asthana. (Jagdish Gangani received it for 2023.)

questions.text: Which of the following features of the Indian Constitution is added by the 97th Constitutional Amendment Act?
questions.explanation: The 97th Amendment (2011) gave cooperative societies constitutional status: the right to form them in Article 19(1)(c), Article 43B and Part IXB.

questions.text: Who among the following assumed the position of Central Vigilance Commissioner (CVC) in May 2023?
questions.explanation: Praveen Kumar Srivastava, who had been acting Central Vigilance Commissioner, was sworn in as CVC in May 2023.

questions.text: Which of the following is a NOT a natural fibre crop grown in India?
questions.explanation: Polyester is a synthetic fibre made from petrochemicals; hemp, cotton and jute are natural fibre crops.

questions.text: As per National Multidimensional Poverty Index report 2023, what is the poverty rate of India (2019-21)?
questions.explanation: The 2023 review put India's multidimensionally poor at 14.96% of the population in 2019-21, down from 24.85% in 2015-16.

questions.text: Select the correct order of the following metals in terms of their increasing reactivities.
questions.explanation: In the reactivity series potassium is above magnesium, magnesium above copper and copper above gold, so in increasing order: Au, Cu, Mg, K.

questions.text: The elliptical shapes in temple architecture in Dravidian style are known by which of the given terms?
questions.explanation: In Dravidian temple architecture the elliptical (apsidal) shape is called gajaprishta, 'elephant-backed'; ayatasra is the rectangular shape and vritta the circular one.

questions.text: Which of the following groups of plants are categorised as cryptogams?
questions.explanation: Cryptogams are plants without flowers or seeds: the thallophytes, bryophytes and pteridophytes. Gymnosperms and angiosperms bear seeds.

questions.text: In which year was the Shri Mahila SEWA Sahakari Bank established?
questions.explanation: The Shri Mahila SEWA Sahakari Bank was set up in Ahmedabad in 1974 by self-employed women members of SEWA.

questions.text: What is denatured alcohol?
questions.explanation: Denatured alcohol is ethanol made unfit to drink by adding a little methanol (often with other substances such as dyes).

questions.text: What is the meaning of the term 'drop shot' in tennis?
options: A shot played softly and close to the net
A shot that hits the lines on the court
questions.explanation: A drop shot is played softly so that the ball just clears the net and falls close to it.

questions.text: Which physical feature of India is known for its lateritic soil which supports plantation crops?
questions.explanation: Laterite soils form under heavy rain and high temperatures; in the hilly Western Ghats areas of Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu they are used for plantation crops such as tea and coffee.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Where was the India House established to work for India’s liberation from British possession?
questions.explanation: India House was set up in London in 1905 by Shyamji Krishna Varma as a base for Indian students and revolutionaries.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. I regret / in notify that / the model you want/ is out of stock.
questions.explanation: 'In notify' is ungrammatical; to announce bad news, 'regret' takes the to-infinitive: 'I regret to notify that'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’. When Shina reached the bus stand, she realised that “she has left her wallet” at home.
options: she had been left her wallet
questions.explanation: The leaving happened before the realising, so it takes the past perfect: 'she had left her wallet'.

questions.text: Select the option that correctly rectifies the underlined spelling error. He received an “honarary” degree for his contributions.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'honorary'.

questions.text: From the given options, identify the sentence which is in the positive degree.
options: They are playing hockey with longer sticks.
She is the most beautiful girl of the class.
His brother is an intelligent boy.
I have a greater idea in this regard.
questions.explanation: 'An intelligent boy' uses the plain adjective, the positive degree; 'longer' and 'greater' are comparatives and 'the most beautiful' a superlative.

questions.text: Select the option that has an error in the usage of the present perfect tense.
questions.explanation: The present perfect is 'has' + past participle: 'Ravi has completed his homework', not 'has complete'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Through thick and thin
options: To possess both thick and thin clothes
To travel through thick and thin clouds
To pass through thick and thin air
To be supportive in both good and bad times
questions.explanation: To stand by someone 'through thick and thin' is to support them in good times and bad.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'sculptor'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. From contacting our loved ones to buying groceries for our daily needs, mobile phones fulfilled our every requirement during the COVID-19 pandemic. Not only during the pandemic, but mobile phones have also ________ our needs since the time of their invention.
questions.explanation: Phones have 'served', that is met, our needs; the other words are about annoying someone.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Mary appeared for the test. She was “waiting anxiously” for the test result.
options: hitting the nail on the head
questions.explanation: To be 'on pins and needles' is to be anxious while waiting for something: 'She was on pins and needles for the test result.'

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. As he is not satisfied / with the jury’s decision, / he appeal / in the higher court.
questions.explanation: The subject 'he' needs a verb that agrees with it, here the future: 'he will appeal' (or 'he appeals'), not 'he appeal'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains grammatical error(s). At the zoo, a curious child / fed an elephant some peanuts, / while enthusiastic group of the visitors / watched in amazement.
options: while enthusiastic group of the visitors
At the zoo, a curious child
questions.explanation: The singular noun 'group' needs an article: 'while an enthusiastic group of visitors watched'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word It is a “betterment” of his work.
questions.explanation: 'Betterment' is improvement; its opposite is 'worsening'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Contaminate
questions.explanation: To 'contaminate' is to make impure: to 'pollute'. 'Clean' and 'purify' are its opposites.

questions.text: Select the grammatically correct sentence from the given options.
options: He is famous for all his contributions for weekly magazines.
He is famous for all his contributions to weekly magazines.
He is more famous for all his contributions to weekly magazines.
He is more famous for all his contributions for weekly magazines.
questions.explanation: One contributes 'to' a magazine, and 'more famous' needs something to compare with: 'He is famous for all his contributions to weekly magazines.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Sarah said that she hates it when people ______ at her.
questions.explanation: To 'stare' is to look at someone fixedly; 'stair', 'star' and 'steer' only sound or look similar.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Skeleton in the cupboard
questions.explanation: A 'skeleton in the cupboard' is an embarrassing secret kept hidden.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. The corporator gathered heaps of curses, and his “misdeeds” can never be forgiven by the people.
questions.explanation: 'Misdeeds' are wrongful acts: 'transgressions'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. The “ambiguous” statement of the leader raised criticism among the public.
questions.explanation: 'Ambiguous' means open to more than one meaning; its opposite is 'clear'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. It was Saturday evening last week. My parents and younger sister had (1)_______ to my uncle's house to (2)______the day. I had stayed back to prepare for a class test. At 5:00 p.m, someone (3)_____the door bell. To my shock and dismay, one of my distant relatives, Mr. Sinha (4)______ standing with his suitcase. I had to call him in most unwillingly. He was a big bore and nothing less than a chatterbox. I asked his preference (5)____ coffee and tea.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The past perfect 'had' takes the past participle: 'had gone to my uncle's house'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. It was Saturday evening last week. My parents and younger sister had (1)_______ to my uncle's house to (2)______the day. I had stayed back to prepare for a class test. At 5:00 p.m, someone (3)_____the door bell. To my shock and dismay, one of my distant relatives, Mr. Sinha (4)______ standing with his suitcase. I had to call him in most unwillingly. He was a big bore and nothing less than a chatterbox. I asked his preference (5)____ coffee and tea.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: 'To' is followed by the base form of the verb: 'to spend the day'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. It was Saturday evening last week. My parents and younger sister had (1)_______ to my uncle's house to (2)______the day. I had stayed back to prepare for a class test. At 5:00 p.m, someone (3)_____the door bell. To my shock and dismay, one of my distant relatives, Mr. Sinha (4)______ standing with his suitcase. I had to call him in most unwillingly. He was a big bore and nothing less than a chatterbox. I asked his preference (5)____ coffee and tea.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: The story is told in the simple past: 'someone rang the door bell'; 'rung' is the past participle.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. It was Saturday evening last week. My parents and younger sister had (1)_______ to my uncle's house to (2)______the day. I had stayed back to prepare for a class test. At 5:00 p.m, someone (3)_____the door bell. To my shock and dismay, one of my distant relatives, Mr. Sinha (4)______ standing with his suitcase. I had to call him in most unwillingly. He was a big bore and nothing less than a chatterbox. I asked his preference (5)____ coffee and tea.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: A singular subject in a past narrative takes 'was': 'Mr. Sinha was standing with his suitcase'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. It was Saturday evening last week. My parents and younger sister had (1)_______ to my uncle's house to (2)______the day. I had stayed back to prepare for a class test. At 5:00 p.m, someone (3)_____the door bell. To my shock and dismay, one of my distant relatives, Mr. Sinha (4)______ standing with his suitcase. I had to call him in most unwillingly. He was a big bore and nothing less than a chatterbox. I asked his preference (5)____ coffee and tea.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: A choice of two takes 'between': 'his preference between coffee and tea'; 'among' is for more than two.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: Ram borrows a sum of ₹24,000 from his friend Soham on 31December 2021 on the condition that he will return the same after one year with simple interest at 18% per annum. However, Ram is able to return the money on 1August 2022. What amount does Ram have to return to Soham?
questions.explanation: The loan from 31 December 2021 to 1 August 2022 is taken as 7 months (January to July): SI = 24,000 × 18/100 × 7/12 = ₹2,520, so Ram returns 24,000 + 2,520 = ₹26,520. Counting the exact 213 days (213/365 of a year) gives ₹2,520.99, practically the same.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3000 as a sum borrowed at 9% per year rate of interest for 5 years.
The average weight of 5 persons sitting in a boat is 28 kg. If the average weight of the boat and the persons sitting in the boat is 56 kg, what is the weight of the boat?
questions.explanation: The 5 persons weigh 5 × 28 = 140 kg, and the boat and the persons together 6 × 56 = 336 kg, so the boat weighs 336 − 140 = 196 kg.

questions.text: If the numbers X + 2, X + 5, 2X − 3 and 3X − 5 are in proportion, then which of the following pairs of values is possible for X?
A number is increased by 24% and then decreased by 25%. What is the net increase or decrease percentage?
questions.explanation: 1.24 × 0.75 = 0.93, so the number falls by 7%.

questions.text: The area (in cm²) of circle that can be inscribed in a square of side 12 cm is:
questions.explanation: The inscribed circle's diameter equals the side, 12 cm, so its radius is 6 cm and its area π × 6² = 36π cm².

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2500 as a sum borrowed at 8% per year rate of interest for 5 years.
The average of all the numbers between 8 and 68 that are divisible by 9 is:
questions.explanation: The multiples of 9 between 8 and 68 are 9, 18, 27, 36, 45, 54 and 63; their average is the middle term, 36.

questions.text: A policeman notices a thief from a distance of 220 m. He chases the thief when he started running the moment he saw the police. The thief and policeman run at the rate of 9 km/h and 11 km/h respectively. How much distance policeman has to cover for catching the thief?
questions.explanation: The policeman gains 11 − 9 = 2 km/h on the thief, so he closes the 220 m = 0.22 km in 0.11 hour, in which he runs 11 × 0.11 = 1.21 km.

questions.text: What is the difference between the average of prime numbers between 30 and 50 and the average of multiples of 3 between 20 and 50?
questions.explanation: The primes between 30 and 50 are 31, 37, 41, 43 and 47, averaging 199/5 = 39.8. The multiples of 3 from 21 to 48 average (21 + 48)/2 = 34.5. 39.8 − 34.5 = 5.3.

questions.text: A and B start running on a circular race track whose length is 3240 m. A and B start from the same point and at the same time, but in opposite directions. If A runs at a speed of 10 m/s and they cross each other 3 minutes after they start running, then what is B’s speed (in m/s)?
questions.explanation: Running in opposite directions, they cross when together they have covered one lap: 10 + B = 3,240/180 = 18 m/s, so B runs at 8 m/s.

questions.text: The monthly incomes of Selva for 3 months of a year are ₹19,500, ₹21,500 and ₹22,000. What is Selva’s average income per month for these 3 months?
By selling an article for ₹20, a dealer makes a profit of 20%. By how much should he increase his selling price (in ₹, rounded off to two decimal place) so as to make a profit of 30%?
questions.explanation: The cost price is 20/1.2 = ₹50/3. For a 30% profit the price must be 1.3 × 50/3 = ₹65/3 (₹21.67), so the increase is ₹5/3, about ₹1.67.

questions.text: The LCM of 16,20 and 24 is:
What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 25 + 20 × 10 ÷ 2 − 5 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 25 − 20 ÷ 10 × 2 + 5 = 25 − 4 + 5 = 26.

questions.text: U, V, W, X, Y, Z and A are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Only one person sits between Y and X when counted from the left of X. A sits third to the right of U. V sits third to the left of W. A sits to the immediate right of V. Z is not an immediate neighbour of V. How many people sit between Z and X when counted from the right of Z?
questions.explanation: Going round to the right from U the order is U, X, V, A, Z, W, Y: A third to U's right with V just to its left, W third to V's right, Z not beside V, and Y two places to X's left. Counting to the right from Z, W, Y and U come before X: three people.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some cameras are radios. All radios are routers. Conclusions: (I): Some cameras are routers. (II): No camera is a router.
questions.explanation: The cameras that are radios are also routers, so some cameras are routers (I). II contradicts this, so only I follows.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some cameras are phones. No phone is a laptop. Conclusions: (I) Some phones are cameras. (II) Some laptops are phones.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusion I and II follow
questions.explanation: 'Some cameras are phones' converts to 'some phones are cameras', so I follows. 'No phone is a laptop' means no laptop is a phone, so II does not follow.

questions.text: PS 41 is related to KN 47 in a certain way. In the same way, TW 30 is related to OR 36. To which of the following is VY 27 related following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 5 places back and the number rises by 6: PS 41 → KN 47 and TW 30 → OR 36. So VY 27 → QT 33.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 310 × 2 − 3 ÷ 40 + 170 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 310 ÷ 2 + 3 × 40 − 170 = 155 + 120 − 170 = 105.

questions.text: 22 is related to 43 following a certain logic. Following the same logic,35 is related to 69. To which of the following is 81 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding / subtracting / multiplying, etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is twice the first minus 1: 22 × 2 − 1 = 43 and 35 × 2 − 1 = 69. Likewise 81 × 2 − 1 = 161.

questions.text: In a code language, 'JASMINE' is coded as '213' and 'TULIP' is coded as '234'. How will 'CHAMELI' be coded in the same language?
questions.explanation: The code is three times the sum of the letters' places in the alphabet: JASMINE = 10 + 1 + 19 + 13 + 9 + 14 + 5 = 71, and 71 × 3 = 213; TULIP = 78, and 78 × 3 = 234. CHAMELI = 3 + 8 + 1 + 13 + 5 + 12 + 9 = 51, and 51 × 3 = 153.

questions.text: EHJD is related to LOQK in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, GJLF is related to NQSM. To which of the following is ILNH related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 7 places forward: EHJD → LOQK and GJLF → NQSM. So ILNH → PSUO.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘do it correctly’ is written as ‘nq sd fo’ and ‘Please do this’ is written as ‘rt fo in’. How is ‘do’ written in the given code language?
questions.explanation: 'do' is the only word in both sentences and 'fo' the only code in both, so do = fo.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘I Love biryani’ is written as ‘qs vx pg’ and ‘biryani was good’ is written as ‘vx pm ed’. How is ‘biryani’ written in the given code language?
questions.explanation: 'biryani' is the only word in both sentences and 'vx' the only code in both, so biryani = vx.

questions.text: In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 10, 49; 14, 69
questions.explanation: The second number is five times the first minus 1: 10 × 5 − 1 = 49 and 14 × 5 − 1 = 69. Likewise 18 × 5 − 1 = 89.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 736, 689, 642, 595, 548 ?
questions.explanation: Each term is 47 less than the one before: 548 − 47 = 501.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? JBM, MEJ, PHG, SKD, ?
questions.explanation: The first letters move +3 (J, M, P, S, V), the second +3 (B, E, H, K, N) and the third −3 (M, J, G, D, A): VNA.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘POST’ is coded as ‘3854’ and ‘TIPS’ is coded as ‘5648’. What is the code for ‘O’ in that language?
questions.explanation: P, S and T are in both words, as are 8, 5 and 4 in both codes. The letter left in POST is O and the digit left in its code is 3, so O = 3.

questions.text: Which volume of the ‘Akbar-Nama’ is known as Ain-i-Akbari and deals with Akbar’s administration, household, army and the revenues and geography of his empire?
questions.explanation: Abul Fazl's 'Akbar-Nama' has three volumes; the third, the Ain-i-Akbari, describes Akbar's administration, household, army, revenues and the geography of his empire.

questions.text: In which athletics event did Eldhose Paul win a gold medal at the Commonwealth Games 2022?
questions.explanation: Eldhose Paul won the triple jump at the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham, with India's Abdulla Aboobacker second.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a private sector industry in India?
questions.explanation: BHEL is a public sector undertaking owned by the Government of India; Dabur, Bajaj Auto and TISCO (now Tata Steel) are private companies.

questions.text: Who among the following was appointed as the Director of the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) in May 2023?
questions.explanation: Praveen Sood, then Karnataka's Director General of Police, was appointed Director of the CBI in May 2023 for a two-year term.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Brahmo Samaj, the theistic movement within Hinduism, was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in the year ________.
questions.explanation: Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Sabha in Calcutta in 1828; it later became the Brahmo Samaj.

questions.text: How does salt contribute to the preservation of food?
options: By reducing the pH of the food.
By inhibiting the growth of microorganisms through osmosis.
questions.explanation: Salt draws water out of the food and out of microbial cells by osmosis, so bacteria and moulds cannot grow.

questions.text: Which of the following is the main objective of the DWCRA model of SHGs?
options: To provide education opportunities for rural children
To provide self-employment opportunities for rural women
To provide housing support for rural families
To provide healthcare services to rural women
questions.explanation: DWCRA (Development of Women and Children in Rural Areas), begun in 1982 under the IRDP, organised poor rural women into groups for self-employment and income-generating activities.

questions.text: The English novel ‘Morning Face’ is written by:
questions.explanation: 'Morning Face' (1968), an autobiographical novel by Mulk Raj Anand, won the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1971.

questions.text: Under Article 165, the Governor appoints a person who is qualified to be appointed a Judge of a High Court to be the _________ for the State.
questions.explanation: Article 165 provides for the Advocate-General for the State, appointed by the Governor; the Attorney General (Article 76) is the Union's counterpart.

questions.text: Which of the following Articles is automatically suspended when an emergency is declared on the grounds of external aggression?
questions.explanation: Under Article 358 the freedoms of Article 19 are suspended automatically when a national emergency is proclaimed on the ground of war or external aggression, but not of armed rebellion.

questions.text: The 'Mahawat' term is associated with which season in North-West India?
questions.explanation: Mahawat is the winter rain that western disturbances bring to north-west India; it is valuable for the rabi crops.

questions.text: Rita Mustaphi who is honoured with Mcknight Fellowship of 2023 for her excellent innovation in which of the following Indian Dance Forms?
questions.explanation: Rita Mustaphi, a disciple of Pandit Birju Maharaj and founder of the Katha Dance Theatre in Minnesota, is a Kathak dancer and choreographer; her 2023 McKnight Fellowship was for choreography.

questions.text: Which of the following Census decades in India recorded the highest crude death rate?
questions.explanation: The death rate was highest in 1911-1921, the decade of the 1918 influenza pandemic; it is the only census decade in which India's population fell.

questions.text: Kelucharan Mohapatra is associated with which of the following dances?
questions.explanation: Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra was a leading Odissi dancer and teacher, central to the dance's revival in the twentieth century.

questions.text: Padma Shri Pandit Rajeev Tharanath, the famous ________________ player is from the state of Karnataka.
questions.explanation: Pandit Rajeev Taranath, a disciple of Ustad Ali Akbar Khan, was a sarod player from Karnataka.

questions.text: Which day is celebrated as International Day of Non-Violence?
questions.explanation: The UN observes 2 October, Mahatma Gandhi's birthday, as the International Day of Non-Violence, under a General Assembly resolution of 2007.

questions.text: The Anusandhan National Research Foundation Bill, 2023 was introduced in Lok Sabha on 4 August 2023, which repeals the _____________________________.
options: Science and Engineering Research Board Act, 2008
Science and Engineering Research Board Act, 2006
Science and Engineering Research Board Act, 2009
Science and Engineering Research Board Act, 2007
questions.explanation: The Anusandhan National Research Foundation Bill, 2023 repeals the Science and Engineering Research Board Act, 2008, bringing SERB into the new foundation.

questions.text: At 1 bar pressure, the volume of a fixed amount of hydrogen gas is 2.27 litre. What will be the volume if the pressure is kept at 0.2 bar?
questions.explanation: By Boyle's law p₁V₁ = p₂V₂: V₂ = 1 × 2.27/0.2 = 11.35 litres = 11,350 cm³.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Hanging by a thread.
options: To be perilously close to failing, dying, or resulting in a bad outcome
questions.explanation: To be 'hanging by a thread' is to be in a precarious state, very close to failure or disaster.

questions.text: select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in brackets. Despite facing numerous challenges, her [tenacious] determination never faded one bit.
questions.explanation: 'Tenacious' means holding firmly to a purpose: persistent, unyielding, 'stubborn'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. John’s coffee is “hot” than Jack’s.
questions.explanation: 'Than' compares two things, so the comparative is needed: 'hotter than Jack's'. 'More hotter' is a double comparative.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. We all ____________ at the sky as it was full of stars that night.
questions.explanation: To 'gaze' is to look steadily, and it takes 'at': 'We all gazed at the sky'. 'Saw at' is not idiomatic.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence. After the heavy rains last Thursday, the water in the river “raised another three feet”.
questions.explanation: 'Rise' (rose, risen) needs no object, while 'raise' does; the simple past fits 'last Thursday': 'the water in the river rose another three feet'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. The politician's speech was an attempt to “mitigate” the concerns of the citizens.
questions.explanation: To 'mitigate' is to make less severe: 'lessen'. 'Aggravate' is its opposite.

questions.text: Select the word segment that substitutes the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. The movie was (mostly over) when we entered the hall.
questions.explanation: 'Almost over' means nearly finished; 'mostly' means for the most part and does not fit with 'over' here.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Yesterday, / my surgeon / operate on my knee.
questions.explanation: 'Yesterday' calls for the simple past: 'my surgeon operated on my knee'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. The news of her promotion left her feeling “buoyant”, with a sense of accomplishment and pride in her work.
questions.explanation: 'Buoyant' here means cheerful and optimistic. 'Dour' (stern, gloomy) is nearly its opposite.

questions.text: Select the option that has an error in the use of present tense.
options: I have performed all my duties with utmost sincerity.
The mother cooks delicious food for her children.
I am observing your mischievous activities for half an hour.
The painter is painting the wall right now.
questions.explanation: An action that began in the past and is still going on takes the present perfect continuous: 'I have been observing your mischievous activities for half an hour.'

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'indulgent'.

questions.text: In the following sentence the underlined part contains as error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative. He looked extremely smart and “handsomest” in the black suit.
questions.explanation: 'Extremely smart and ...' calls for the positive degree, like 'smart': 'smart and handsome'. The superlative 'handsomest' does not fit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks. An adventurer packed _____ backpack and _____ assortment of survival gear for the challenging trek through the wilderness.
questions.explanation: 'Backpack' begins with a consonant sound, so 'a backpack'; 'assortment' begins with a vowel sound, so 'an assortment'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined phrase. Can you please stop “continuously complaining about” the student's shortcomings?
questions.explanation: To 'whine' is to complain continually in a peevish way.

questions.text: Select the option that does NOT contain an adverb.
options: She ran swiftly to catch the thief.
Maya was quite absent-minded during class today.
questions.explanation: 'Swiftly', 'quite' and 'never' are adverbs; 'Rohit loves chocolate' has only nouns and a verb.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I need to ________ my shoelaces before going out.
questions.explanation: To 'tie' shoelaces is to fasten them; 'tye' is a misspelling, and 'thigh' and 'thai' are other words.

questions.text: Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word from the given sentence. Comprehensiveness constitues wisdom and many examples from history illustrate this fact.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'constitutes'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM to substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. How would you describe your “ideal” vacation destination?
questions.explanation: 'Ideal' means perfect; its opposite is 'faulty'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To throw caution to the wind
options: To give answer with utmost attention
To roam here and there aimlessly
To do something with care and attention
To do something without worrying about risk
questions.explanation: To 'throw caution to the wind' is to act boldly, without worrying about the risk.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In the realm of literature, metaphors and similes are like (1) ________ tools for writers. They serve to (2) ________ the reader's understanding and make the text more (3) ________. However, it's crucial for writers to (4) ________ use them, as excessive figurative language can (5) ________ the clarity of the writing.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Metaphors and similes are 'indispensable', that is essential, tools for writers.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In the realm of literature, metaphors and similes are like (1) ________ tools for writers. They serve to (2) ________ the reader's understanding and make the text more (3) ________. However, it's crucial for writers to (4) ________ use them, as excessive figurative language can (5) ________ the clarity of the writing.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: They 'illuminate', or throw light on, the reader's understanding.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In the realm of literature, metaphors and similes are like (1) ________ tools for writers. They serve to (2) ________ the reader's understanding and make the text more (3) ________. However, it's crucial for writers to (4) ________ use them, as excessive figurative language can (5) ________ the clarity of the writing.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: They make the text more 'vivid'; 'more' needs an adjective here, and 'substantiality', 'meaning' and 'ambiguity' are nouns.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In the realm of literature, metaphors and similes are like (1) ________ tools for writers. They serve to (2) ________ the reader's understanding and make the text more (3) ________. However, it's crucial for writers to (4) ________ use them, as excessive figurative language can (5) ________ the clarity of the writing.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: As too much figurative language harms clarity, writers must use them 'judiciously', that is with good judgement.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In the realm of literature, metaphors and similes are like (1) ________ tools for writers. They serve to (2) ________ the reader's understanding and make the text more (3) ________. However, it's crucial for writers to (4) ________ use them, as excessive figurative language can (5) ________ the clarity of the writing.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Excessive figurative language can 'detract from', that is reduce, the clarity of the writing.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: A thief is 150 metres away from a policeman. If the speed of the thief is 93 km/h and the speed of the policeman is 108 km/h, then the time taken by the policeman to catch the thief is:
questions.explanation: The policeman gains 108 − 93 = 15 km/h = 15 × 5/18 = 25/6 m/s on the thief, so he closes the 150 m in 150 ÷ 25/6 = 36 seconds.

questions.text: The length of a rectangle is four-fifths of the side of the square, whose area is 1225 units². What is the area (in units²) of the rectangle if the breadth is 12 units?
questions.explanation: The square's side is √1225 = 35 units, so the rectangle's length is 4/5 × 35 = 28 units. Area = 28 × 12 = 336 units².

questions.text: A shopkeeper sells an article for ₹450.30 with a loss of 21%. What is the cost price (in ₹)of the article?
questions.explanation: At a 21% loss the selling price is 0.79 of the cost, so cost price = 450.30/0.79 = ₹570.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2500 as a sum borrowed at 9% per year rate of interest for 5 years.

A supermarket gives two successive discounts on a mobile phone marked ₹19,000. The first discount given is 14%. If the customer pays ₹15,048 for the phone, then what was the second discount (rounded up to two decimal points)?
questions.explanation: After the first discount the phone costs 0.86 × 19,000 = ₹16,340. The second discount is 16,340 − 15,048 = ₹1,292, and 1,292/16,340 × 100 = 7.91%.

questions.text: The ratio of two numbers is 3:4 and their HCF is 4. Then, their LCM is:
questions.explanation: The numbers are 3 × 4 = 12 and 4 × 4 = 16, so their LCM is 4 × 3 × 4 = 48.

questions.text: Find the average of the first 10 natural numbers.
questions.explanation: The sum of 1 to 10 is 10 × 11/2 = 55, so the average is 55/10 = 5.5.

questions.text: The average of a non-zero number and its square is 7 times the number. The number is:
questions.explanation: (x + x²)/2 = 7x gives x² + x = 14x, so x² = 13x and, as x is not zero, x = 13.

questions.text: A dealer made some profit by selling a laptop for ₹88,000, which is equal to the amount of loss incurred on selling the same laptop for ₹72,000. If he had sold the laptop for ₹96,000, then his profit percentage would have been:
questions.explanation: The profit and the loss are equal, so the cost price lies midway: (88,000 + 72,000)/2 = ₹80,000. At ₹96,000 the profit is 16,000/80,000 × 100 = 20%.

questions.text: A 296-m long train is running at a speed of 72 km/h. In how much time will it pass a 144-m long bridge?
questions.explanation: The train covers 296 + 144 = 440 m at 72 km/h = 20 m/s, which takes 440/20 = 22 seconds.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3500 as a sum borrowed at 4% per year rate of interest for 5 years.
In a factory, the average monthly salary of 25 unskilled workers is ₹11,950, that of 20 mechanics is ₹24,000 and that of 5 supervisors is ₹35,000. The average monthly salary of all the employees is:
A library has an average number of 768 visitors on Monday, and 258 visitors on others day. Find the average number of visitors per day in a month of 30 days, beginning with Tuesday.
questions.explanation: A 30-day month beginning on a Tuesday has 4 Mondays (days 7, 14, 21 and 28). Total = 4 × 768 + 26 × 258 = 3,072 + 6,708 = 9,780 visitors, an average of 9,780/30 = 326.

questions.text: Read the given statement(s) and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement(s). Statements: Some papers are pens. All the pencils are pens. Conclusions (I): Some pens are pencils. Conclusions (II): Some pens are papers.
questions.explanation: All pencils are pens, so some pens are pencils (I). Some papers are pens, so some pens are papers (II). Both follow.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘GIRL’ is coded as ‘3571’ and ‘TAGS’ is coded as ‘4685’. What is the code for ‘G’ in that language?
questions.explanation: G is the only letter in both words and 5 the only digit in both codes, so G = 5.

questions.text: 11 is related to 65 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 16 is related to 90. To which of the following is 21 related following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is five times the first plus 10: 11 × 5 + 10 = 65 and 16 × 5 + 10 = 90. Likewise 21 × 5 + 10 = 115.

questions.text: CHUM is related to DJVO in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, NOPA is related to OQQC. To which of the following is DYIE related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: The letters move +1, +2, +1, +2: CHUM → DJVO and NOPA → OQQC. So DYIE → EAJG (Y moves 2 places, wrapping round to A).

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 12, 16, 22, 32, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 4, 6, 10, 14: twice the prime numbers 2, 3, 5, 7. So 32 + 14 = 46.

questions.text: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). B is sitting second to the right of A and to the immediate left of C. C is sitting second to the left of D. F is sitting to the immediate right of A. E is not an immediate neighbour of A. How many people are sitting between D and A when counted from the left of A?
