questions.explanation: Going round to the right from A: A, F, B, C, E, D, G. (F is on A's immediate right, B second to A's right with C on B's right, and D second to C's right; E cannot sit next to A, so G does.) Counting from A's left, G is the only person before D.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the following series based on the English alphabetical order? SWS, TUQ, USO, VQM, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move +1 (S, T, U, V, W), second letters −2 (W, U, S, Q, O) and third letters −2 (S, Q, O, M, K): WOK.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘will you go’ is coded as ‘rp zs tu’ and ‘you come here’ is written as ‘ar cm tu’. How is ‘you’ coded in that code language?
questions.explanation: 'you' is the only word in both sentences and 'tu' the only code in both, so you = tu.

questions.text: HN74 is related to TZ55 in a certain way . In the same way, XD60 is related to JP41. To which of the following is ZF55 related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 12 places forward, wrapping round after Z, and the number falls by 19: H → T, N → Z, 74 − 19 = 55; X → J, D → P, 60 − 19 = 41. So Z → L, F → R and 55 − 19 = 36: LR36.

questions.text: What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 22 × 484 ÷ 44 – 93 + 12 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 22 ÷ 484 × 44 + 93 − 12 = 2 + 93 − 12 = 83.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (10, 360, 3) (12, 720, 5) (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The middle number is 12 times the product of the other two: 10 × 3 × 12 = 360 and 12 × 5 × 12 = 720. Likewise 8 × 6 × 12 = 576.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘get a driver’ is written as ‘ki jo hu’ and ‘better get out’ is writtenas ‘ji hy ki’. How is ‘get’ writtenin the given language?
questions.explanation: 'get' is the only word in both sentences and 'ki' the only code in both, so get = ki.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All books are racks. All tables are books. Conclusions: (I) At least some racks are tables. (II) All racks are books.
questions.explanation: All tables are books and all books are racks, so all tables are racks and at least some racks are tables (I). Nothing says every rack is a book, so II does not follow.

questions.text: Six persons P1, P2, P3, P4, P5 and P6 sit around a circular table facing towards the centre (not necessarily in the same order). P2 sits second to the left of P5. One person sits between P2 and P6 when counted from the left of P2. P3 and P2 are not neighbours of P5 and P4, respectively. Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct? I. One person sits between P1 and P6 when counted from the right of P1. II. P3 is an immediate neighbour of P2.
questions.explanation: Going round to the left from P5: P5, P1, P2, P3, P6, P4. (P3 cannot sit next to P5, so it takes the seat between P2 and P6; P4 cannot sit next to P2, so it sits on P5's right, leaving P1 between P5 and P2.) P1 and P6 sit opposite, with two people between them either way, so I is false; P3 is next to P2, so II is true.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘−‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 41 ÷ 6 + 99 × 3 − 9 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 41 × 6 − 99 ÷ 3 + 9 = 246 − 33 + 9 = 222.

questions.text: A hockey ground is rectangular in shape, measuring 91.4 m in length and ______ in width.
questions.explanation: A hockey field measures 91.4 m by 55 m.

questions.text: Emani Sankara Sastry and Doraiswamy Iyengar are both associated with which musical instrument?
questions.explanation: Emani Sankara Sastry and Mysore V. Doraiswamy Iyengar were both celebrated veena players.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College in Aligarh was founded by ___________.
questions.explanation: Sir Syed Ahmed Khan founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College at Aligarh in 1875; it became Aligarh Muslim University in 1920.

questions.text: Which Bharatanatyam dancer is the recipient of one of India’s top civilian award, the Padma Vibhushan 1977?
questions.explanation: T. Balasaraswati, the Bharatanatyam dancer, received the Padma Vibhushan in 1977.

questions.text: Where was the inaugural season of Ultimate Kho-Kho League held in 2022?
questions.explanation: The first season of Ultimate Kho Kho, in 2022, was played in Pune.

questions.text: According to the census of India 2011, which of the following states is least urbanised?
questions.explanation: By the 2011 census only about 10% of Himachal Pradesh's people lived in towns, the lowest share of any state; Bihar, at about 11%, came next.

questions.text: Nishagandhi festival is celebrated in which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Kerala Tourism holds the Nishagandhi Dance Festival in Thiruvananthapuram, at the Nishagandhi open-air auditorium.

questions.text: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India emphasises the participation of workers in the management of industries?
questions.explanation: Article 43A, a Directive Principle added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976, asks the State to secure the participation of workers in the management of industries.

questions.text: In May 2023, the Supreme Court interpreted which article related to the governance structure of Delhi, which outlines the principles of federalism, participatory democracy and collective responsibility?
questions.explanation: Article 239AA sets out the special provisions for the government of Delhi. In May 2023 a Constitution Bench read it to give Delhi's elected government control over its services, except those tied to public order, police and land.

questions.text: The Indravati National Park is located in which state?
questions.explanation: Indravati National Park, a tiger reserve named after the Indravati river, is in Bijapur district, Chhattisgarh.

questions.text: As of July 2023, who was the Member of Parliament from the parliamentary constituency of Varanasi?
questions.explanation: Narendra Modi has represented Varanasi in the Lok Sabha since 2014.

questions.text: The National Population Register was created under the provisions of _______ and ______. a. the Citizenship Act, 1965 b. the Citizenship Rules, 2004 c. the Citizenship Act, 1955 d. the Citizenship Rules, 2003
questions.explanation: The National Population Register is prepared under the Citizenship Act, 1955 and the Citizenship (Registration of Citizens and Issue of National Identity Cards) Rules, 2003.

questions.text: The Jhaveri Sisters are known for keeping alive the temple tradition of which of the following classical dances of India?
questions.explanation: The Jhaveri Sisters devoted their lives to Manipuri dance, performing and teaching it and recording its traditions.

questions.text: Which virus is responsible for causing AIDS?
questions.explanation: AIDS is caused by the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), which attacks the body's immune cells.

questions.text: Which dynasty defeated the Kanva dynasty?
questions.explanation: By the Puranas' account Simuka, founder of the Satavahana dynasty, overthrew Susharman, the last Kanva king.

questions.text: The navigable portion of Barak River in India is the 121 km stretch between Lakhipur and Bhanga, which was declared as ______ in the year 2016.
questions.explanation: The National Waterways Act, 2016 declared the Lakhipur-Bhanga stretch of the Barak river National Waterway 16.

questions.text: Panch Mahal, a palace in Fatehpur Sikri, was built by the Mughal Emperor ________.
questions.explanation: Fatehpur Sikri, with its five-storeyed Panch Mahal, was built by Akbar.

questions.text: The non-metallic mineral mica is used in which of the following industries?
questions.explanation: Mica, a good insulator that withstands heat, is used mainly in the electrical and electronics industries.

questions.text: What is the quorum of the Lok Sabha at the time of the Presidential address, which is held at the opening of each session of the Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: Under Article 100(3) the quorum of either House of Parliament is one-tenth of its total membership. (Under Article 87 the President addresses both Houses together at the first session after each general election and the first session of each year, not at every session.)

questions.text: Which of the following best represents the Revenue Deficit?
questions.explanation: The revenue deficit is the excess of the government's revenue expenditure over its revenue receipts.

questions.text: The historical novel, 'Train to Pakistan' was written by:
questions.explanation: Khushwant Singh's 'Train to Pakistan' (1956) is set in a Punjab border village during the Partition of 1947.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Against which of the following were ‘Swadeshi’ and ‘Boycott’ used as the means of protest and struggle, for the first time in India?
questions.explanation: The Swadeshi movement, with its boycott of British goods, began in 1905 against Lord Curzon's partition of Bengal.

questions.text: Which of the following two properties of metals are exploited to prepare very thin sheets of silver to decorate sweets?
questions.explanation: Silver is malleable, so it can be beaten into very thin foil, and lustrous, so the foil shines on the sweets.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. The mother told the child to “erase” the extra dots from the given graph.
questions.explanation: To 'erase' is to rub out or remove; its opposite is 'create'. 'Delete' and 'efface' are synonyms.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The company “ran about of stock due to” unexpectedly high demand for the product.
options: ran around of stock due to
ran on of stock due to
ran out of stock due to
ran across of stock due to
questions.explanation: To 'run out of' something is to use it all up: the company 'ran out of stock'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The rules of behaviour which guide one in a formal situation
questions.explanation: Protocol is the set of rules of conduct for formal or official occasions.

questions.text: Select the option that rectifies the underlined spelling error. The panel “submited” the findings to the ministry.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'submitted'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word in the given sentence. “Disclaimer” on products in the markets saves manufacturer from unusual results on usage.
questions.explanation: A disclaimer is a statement, often a clause on a label or in a contract, that limits the maker's responsibility; of the options only 'clause' fits.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. He was “appointed” as the Manager.
questions.explanation: To be 'appointed' is to be given a post; the opposite is to be 'dismissed' from it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. The order will be “operational” from 1st of November.
questions.explanation: 'Operational' here means in force: the order is 'effective' from 1st of November.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. Her team played exceptionally “more well” in the competition.
questions.explanation: 'Well' is already an adverb, and 'more well' is not standard English: 'played exceptionally well'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. “No sooner had she enter her apartment than” she found a bouquet of flowers on her table.
options: No sooner did she enter her apartment than
No sooner has she enter her apartment than
No sooner did she entered her apartment than
questions.explanation: After 'No sooner' the auxiliary comes before the subject, and 'did' takes the base form of the verb: 'No sooner did she enter her apartment than'. ('Had' would need 'entered'.)

questions.text: Identify the error in the following sentence. The zoo is under the street from the temple.
questions.explanation: A place on the other side of a street is 'across the street from' another: 'The zoo is across the street from the temple.'

questions.text: Select the word that has the same meaning (SYNONYM) as the underlined word in the given sentence. The doctor made a “tentative” diagnosis as he did not have the reports of her blood tests.
questions.explanation: 'Tentative' means not yet final: 'provisional'.

questions.text: Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word from the given sentence. Enthusiasm is one of those vital elements that transforms an indivdual and his failures into victories and success.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'individual'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. She oftenly goes / shopping with / her friends / on Saturdays.
questions.explanation: 'Often' is already an adverb and 'oftenly' is not a word: 'She often goes shopping'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Clear the decks
options: To remove unnecessary things for further work
Prepare for an event or course of action by dealing with anything that might hinder progress
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the dictionary sense: to 'clear the decks', as a ship's crew did before battle, is to get ready for something by first dealing with anything that might hold it up. 'To remove unnecessary things for further work' is close, but describes only part of it.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in future continuous tense form. Shall I meet you soon?
options: Shall I be meeting you soon?
Will I be meeting you soon?
Shall I have met you soon?
questions.explanation: The future continuous is 'shall/will be' + '-ing'; keeping the question's 'Shall I': 'Shall I be meeting you soon?'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I have never _________ this kind of pain before surgery.
questions.explanation: One 'experiences' pain: 'I have never experienced this kind of pain'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate degree to fill in the blank. Doctors should never be ___________ than others when patients come for their treatment.
questions.explanation: 'Than' calls for the comparative, and the sense needs 'less caring': doctors should never care less than others.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'cautious'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment. Despite the difficulties, Sarah “started her business with great energy and hard work,”and performed remarkably well in the industry.
questions.explanation: To 'hit the ground running' is to start something with great energy and make quick progress.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Indian villages showcase the country's rich culture and customs. Most Indians live in villages, (1)_______ agriculture, modest living and close-knit communities are the norms. Villagers wake up to roosters crowing and farm (2)_____ day. Farming is the main employment, and generations labour (3)____ the same land. Traditions, communal events and a slower pace (4)_____ village life from metropolitan life. Villagers' togetherness and shared duty make it part of India's identity, (5)_____ the lack of contemporary conveniences.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'Villages, where agriculture, modest living and close-knit communities are the norms': 'where' introduces a clause about a place.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Indian villages showcase the country's rich culture and customs. Most Indians live in villages, (1)_______ agriculture, modest living and close-knit communities are the norms. Villagers wake up to roosters crowing and farm (2)_____ day. Farming is the main employment, and generations labour (3)____ the same land. Traditions, communal events and a slower pace (4)_____ village life from metropolitan life. Villagers' togetherness and shared duty make it part of India's identity, (5)_____ the lack of contemporary conveniences.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Villagers farm 'all day', the whole day long.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Indian villages showcase the country's rich culture and customs. Most Indians live in villages, (1)_______ agriculture, modest living and close-knit communities are the norms. Villagers wake up to roosters crowing and farm (2)_____ day. Farming is the main employment, and generations labour (3)____ the same land. Traditions, communal events and a slower pace (4)_____ village life from metropolitan life. Villagers' togetherness and shared duty make it part of India's identity, (5)_____ the lack of contemporary conveniences.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Generations labour 'on' the same land.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Indian villages showcase the country's rich culture and customs. Most Indians live in villages, (1)_______ agriculture, modest living and close-knit communities are the norms. Villagers wake up to roosters crowing and farm (2)_____ day. Farming is the main employment, and generations labour (3)____ the same land. Traditions, communal events and a slower pace (4)_____ village life from metropolitan life. Villagers' togetherness and shared duty make it part of India's identity, (5)_____ the lack of contemporary conveniences.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: Traditions and a slower pace 'distinguish' village life from metropolitan life: 'distinguish ... from'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Indian villages showcase the country's rich culture and customs. Most Indians live in villages, (1)_______ agriculture, modest living and close-knit communities are the norms. Villagers wake up to roosters crowing and farm (2)_____ day. Farming is the main employment, and generations labour (3)____ the same land. Traditions, communal events and a slower pace (4)_____ village life from metropolitan life. Villagers' togetherness and shared duty make it part of India's identity, (5)_____ the lack of contemporary conveniences.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'Despite' takes a noun phrase directly: 'despite the lack of contemporary conveniences'. 'In spite' would need 'of'.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2000 as a sum borrowed at 8% per year rate of interest for 4 years.
The average weight of a family of five members (in kg) whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 67 kg and 35 kg is:

A shopkeeper offered following four different discount schemes for buyers on an item. A. Two successive discounts of 8%. B. A discount of 11% followed by a discount of 5%. C. Successive discounts of 13% and 3% D. A discount of 16%. Which discount scheme should be opted for getting the item at minimum price?
questions.explanation: The share of the price left: A 0.92 × 0.92 = 0.8464; B 0.89 × 0.95 = 0.8455; C 0.87 × 0.97 = 0.8439; D 0.84. D leaves the least, so the price is lowest.

questions.text: The perimeter of a rhombus is 68 cm and one of its diagonals is 30 cm. Its area is:
questions.explanation: Each side is 68/4 = 17 cm and half the given diagonal 15 cm, so half the other is √(17² − 15²) = 8 cm and the diagonals are 30 and 16 cm. Area = ½ × 30 × 16 = 240 cm².

questions.text: The rate of nickel plating on a metal is ₹50 / m². If the cost of nickel plating on a curved surface area of a solid hemisphere is ₹600, find the cost of nickel coating on the total surface area of this hemisphere.
questions.explanation: ₹600 at ₹50/m² means a curved surface of 2πr² = 12 m². The total surface, 3πr², is 1.5 times that, 18 m², and costs 18 × 50 = ₹900.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3500 as a sum borrowed at 5% per year rate of interest for 4 years.
The average weight of a family of five members (in kg) whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 66 kg and 39 kg is:

A person has to cover a distance of 8 km in 1 hour. If he covers one-fourth of the distance in one-third of the total time, then what should his speed (in km/h) be to cover the remaining distance in the remaining time so that the person reaches the destination exactly on time?
questions.explanation: A quarter of the distance, 2 km, takes a third of the hour, 20 minutes. The other 6 km must take the remaining 40 minutes (2/3 hour): 6 ÷ 2/3 = 9 km/h.

questions.text: A shopkeeper claims that he sells rock salt at ₹23 per kg, which costs him ₹25 per kg. But he gives 800 g instead of 1,000 g. What is his percentage profit or loss?
questions.explanation: The 800 g he hands over costs him 0.8 × ₹25 = ₹20, and he charges ₹23 for it: a profit of 3/20 = 15%.

questions.text: How many seconds does Tiwari take to cover a distance of 600 m if he runs at a speed of 10 km/h?
The ratio of the number of boys to that of girls in a school is 7 : 9. If the number of girls in the school is 189, then the number of boys in that school is:
Ramesh sold a watch to Rahul at a gain of 10%, and Rahul sold it to Arun at a loss of 10%. If Arun paid ₹1,800 to Rahul, then for how much did Ramesh sell it to Rahul?
questions.explanation: Rahul sold it at a 10% loss for ₹1,800, so he had bought it for 1,800/0.9 = ₹2,000: the price Ramesh sold it to him for.

questions.text: The average of nine numbers is 6. When three new numbers are included, the average of the twelve numbers becomes 7.5. The average of three new numbers is:
questions.explanation: The nine numbers total 9 × 6 = 54 and the twelve 12 × 7.5 = 90, so the three new numbers total 36: an average of 12.

questions.text: The salary of T in January, February and March is ₹15,000 per month. His salary in July, August, September, October, November and December is ₹30,000 per month. His average salary per month for the year is ₹27,000. What is his salary (in ₹) in April, May and June per month?
questions.explanation: The year's total is 12 × 27,000 = ₹3,24,000. January to March give 3 × 15,000 = ₹45,000 and July to December 6 × 30,000 = ₹1,80,000, leaving ₹99,000 for April to June: ₹33,000 a month.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘eat your food’ is written as ‘wb hs lg’ and ‘food is tasty’ is writtenas ‘sw lj hs’. How is ‘food’ writtenin the given language?
questions.explanation: 'food' is the only word in both phrases and 'hs' the only code in both, so food = hs.

questions.text: Seven people C, H, A, P, T, E and R are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). T is sitting to the immediate right of E and to the immediate left of R. Only one person is sitting between E and C when counted from the left of E. Only one person is sitting between R and H when counted from the right of R. Who is sitting to the immediate left of C?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, each person's left is clockwise. Clockwise, R, T and E sit together; C is second to E's left and H second to R's right. That gives, clockwise: E, (A or P), C, H, (P or A), R, T. The person to C's immediate left is H.

questions.text: Read the given statement(s) and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement(s). Statements: All laptops are speakers. Some laptops are desktops. Conclusions: (I) Some speakers are desktops. (II) Some desktops are not laptops.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
questions.explanation: The laptops that are desktops are also speakers, so some speakers are desktops (I). Nothing says any desktop lies outside the laptops, so II does not follow.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'N E W S ' is coded as '2 @ 3 #' and 'D E W S' is coded as '4 @ 3 #". What is the code for 'D' in that language?
questions.explanation: E, W and S are in both words and @, 3 and # in both codes. The letter left in DEWS is D and the code left is 4, so D = 4.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 483 502 521 540 559 ?
questions.explanation: Each term is 19 more than the one before: 559 + 19 = 578.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 56 – 14 × 7 ÷ 22 + 63 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 56 + 14 ÷ 7 × 22 − 63 = 56 + 44 − 63 = 37.

questions.text: 9 is related to 83 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 13 is related to 171. To which ofthe following is 15 related, following the same logic?(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbersinto its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: Each number is related to its square plus 2: 9² + 2 = 83 and 13² + 2 = 171. So 15² + 2 = 227.

questions.text: WN 22 is related to AR 29 in a certain way. In the same way, MD 19 is related to QH 26. To which of the following is EV 35 related following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Both letters move 4 places forward and the number rises by 7: WN 22 → AR 29 and MD 19 → QH 26. So EV 35 → IZ 42.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? XDZ, THV, PLR, ?, HTJ
questions.explanation: First letters move 4 back (X, T, P, L, H), second letters 4 forward (D, H, L, P, T) and third letters 4 back (Z, V, R, N, J): LPN.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs that can sequentially replace the * signs and balance the given equation. 12 * 3 * 4 = 6 * 8 * 8
KGNI is related to LHOJ in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, GCJE is related to HDKF. To which of the following is OKRM related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 1 place forward: KGNI → LHOJ and GCJE → HDKF. So OKRM → PLSN.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (7, 40, 9 ) (9,71, 10) (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The middle number is the square of the first minus the third: 7² − 9 = 40 and 9² − 10 = 71. Likewise 13² − 19 = 169 − 19 = 150.

questions.text: Seven people A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table, facing away from the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Exactly three people are sitting between E and B when counted from the right of E. C is sitting second to the left of B. A is sitting to the immediate right of D. E and F are not neighbours. How many people are sitting between C and A when counted from the right of C?
questions.explanation: Facing away from the centre, each person's right is clockwise. B is fourth to E's right and C second to B's left; D and A, side by side, fit only in the two seats after B, and F cannot sit next to E. Clockwise: E, G, C, F, B, D, A. Counting right from C come F, B and D before A: three people.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All trees are branches. Some branches are leaves. Conclusions: (I) All leaves are branches. (II) All leave are trees.
questions.explanation: Some branches are leaves, but nothing says every leaf is a branch (I), and nothing links leaves to trees at all (II). Neither follows.

questions.text: According to a code language, 256 means ‘they are nice’, 637 means ‘we are rude’ and 358 means ‘rude and nice’. What is the code for ‘nice’ in the same code language?
questions.explanation: 'nice' is in the first and third phrases, and 5 is the only digit in both codes (256 and 358), so nice = 5.

questions.text: When did the Hockey wizard Major Dhyan Chand make his Olympic debut?
questions.explanation: Dhyan Chand first played at the Olympics in 1928 at Amsterdam, where India won its first Olympic hockey gold.

questions.text: Sitara Devi was a classical dancer of India who used to perform _____________.
questions.explanation: Sitara Devi was one of the best-known Kathak dancers of the twentieth century.

questions.text: To which position in the Mughal administration under Akbar does Diwan-i-Ala refer?
questions.explanation: Under Akbar the Diwan-i-Ala (also called Diwan-i-Kul) headed revenue and finance: the finance minister. The Mir Bakhshi headed the military.

questions.text: The Republic Day parade is held every year at Kartavya Path, in which of the following cities?
questions.explanation: Kartavya Path (formerly Rajpath), where the Republic Day parade is held, is in New Delhi.

questions.text: Water from melting snow or rainfall or the spring drains downwards through an area of land and finally gets mixed into a large water body like river or ocean. This area of land is called:
questions.explanation: The area drained by a river and its tributaries is its drainage basin. A delta and an estuary form where a river meets the sea, and a bay is part of the sea.

questions.text: According to Census 2011 of India, which Indian state has the highest urban population percentage?
questions.explanation: In Census 2011 about 62% of Goa's people lived in urban areas, the highest share among the states.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: What is the year of foundation of the Women’s Indian Association (WIA)?
questions.explanation: The Women's Indian Association was founded at Adyar, Madras, in 1917 by Annie Besant, Margaret Cousins and others.

questions.text: Which dance guru of Kuchipudi dance got Padma Bhushan in 1998?
questions.explanation: Vempati Chinna Satyam, the Kuchipudi guru who did much to bring the dance to the classical stage, received the Padma Bhushan in 1998. Kelucharan Mohapatra was an Odissi guru.

questions.text: In which neighbouring country of India is the Haa Summer Festival celebrated?
questions.explanation: The Haa Summer Festival is held in the Haa Valley of western Bhutan.

questions.text: In the Vedic period, education was begun with which of the following?
questions.explanation: Vedic education began with the Upanayana, the sacred-thread ceremony that marked a student's entry into study under a guru. Grihastha and Vanaprastha are stages of life.

questions.text: Who among the following is appointed as the chairman of the 16th Finance Commission?
questions.explanation: Arvind Panagariya, a former Vice-Chairman of NITI Aayog, was appointed chairman of the 16th Finance Commission in December 2023. N K Singh chaired the 15th, Y V Reddy the 14th and Vijay Kelkar the 13th.

questions.text: With which Kathak gharana was Pandit Janki Prasad affiliated?
questions.explanation: Pandit Janki Prasad is regarded as the founder of the Benaras (Banaras) gharana of Kathak.

questions.text: Mukhya Mantri Sikho Kamao Yojana was launched by which of these state governments?
questions.explanation: Madhya Pradesh launched the Mukhya Mantri Sikho Kamao Yojana in 2023: young people train on the job in industry and receive a monthly stipend.

questions.text: Australia won the Men’s T20 World Cup Cricket in 2021 defeating New Zealand by ______.
questions.explanation: In the 2021 final at Dubai, Australia chased New Zealand's 172 for 4 and won by 8 wickets.

questions.text: The memoir of which of the following actors is titled ‘Unfinished’?
questions.explanation: 'Unfinished' (2021) is Priyanka Chopra's memoir.

questions.text: Which of the following Harappan cities was found without a citadel?
questions.explanation: Chanhudaro, in Sindh, is the Harappan city found without a citadel.

questions.text: ‘Doabs’ are found in which physical feature of India?
questions.explanation: A doab is the land between two rivers that meet, such as the Ganga-Yamuna doab; doabs are typical of the Northern Plains, above all the Punjab plains.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following Acts was the first intervention by the British government in the East India Company’s territorial affairs?
questions.explanation: The Regulating Act of 1773 was the British government's first step to control and regulate the East India Company's affairs in India; it made the Governor of Bengal the Governor-General.

questions.text: In which of the following groups of States and Union Territories is ‘slash and burn’ agriculture known as ‘Dipa’?
questions.explanation: Slash-and-burn (shifting) cultivation is called 'Dipa' in the Bastar district of Chhattisgarh and in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

questions.text: What is the primary objective of Microfinance Institutions (MFIs) in India?
options: To provide financial services to large corporations
To offer financial assistance and services to low-income individuals and entrepreneurs
questions.explanation: Microfinance institutions give small loans and other financial services to low-income people and small entrepreneurs who lack access to ordinary banking.

questions.text: The Indian Constitution originally consisted of how many Articles?
questions.explanation: The original Constitution had 395 Articles in 22 Parts and 8 Schedules.

questions.text: A person with a very low count of red blood cells is medically known to have _______.
questions.explanation: Anaemia is a shortage of red blood cells or haemoglobin. Scurvy comes from lack of vitamin C and goitre from lack of iodine; jaundice is a build-up of bilirubin.

questions.text: What is the term for the maximum population size that an environment can sustain indefinitely?
questions.explanation: Carrying capacity is the largest population an environment can support indefinitely with its resources.

questions.text: The space-filling model emphasises the relative size of each atom based on its _______.
questions.explanation: A space-filling model draws each atom as a sphere sized by its van der Waals radius, so it shows the space the molecule occupies.

questions.text: On 16 February 2023, who was sworn in as the new Governor of Sikkim at Raj Bhawan, Gangtok?
questions.explanation: Lakshman Prasad Acharya succeeded Ganga Prasad as Governor of Sikkim in February 2023.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Catch someone’s eye
options: To surprise someone with unexpected behaviour
To irritate or annoy someone intentionally
To attract someone's attention or to be noticed by them
To physically capture someone's gaze and hold it, making them unable to look away
questions.explanation: To 'catch someone's eye' is to attract their attention.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. This is one of best movies I have ever seen.
questions.explanation: 'One of' takes the superlative with 'the': 'one of the best movies'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Fondness
questions.explanation: 'Fondness' is affection for someone or something: a 'liking'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate adjective to fill in the blank. Among the three little cats, the first was __________ and the second was smaller.
questions.explanation: The first cat is simply described, so the positive degree 'small'; the second is then compared with it ('smaller'). 'More small' and 'most small' are not used for one-syllable 'small', and 'most smallest' is a double superlative.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the highlighted word. Sonali uses a “soft” mattress to sleep.
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'soft' is 'hard'; 'cushiony' and 'spongy' are close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Baker's Dozen
options: One unit extra with one dozen
questions.explanation: A baker's dozen is thirteen: a dozen and one extra.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. Mohit “have appreciated” Riya for her hard work.
questions.explanation: 'Mohit' is singular, so the present perfect takes 'has': 'Mohit has appreciated Riya'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Although experts are worried / that retail inflation is rising / at a steep rate, / the crisis will soon blow away.
options: the crisis will soon blow away
questions.explanation: A crisis that passes without lasting harm 'blows over'; 'blow away' means to be carried off by the wind.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Much of the beauty and glory of life have disappeared.
questions.explanation: 'Much of' an uncountable noun takes a singular verb: 'Much of the beauty and glory of life has disappeared.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Stories are how we make ______________________ of our lives and of the world.
questions.explanation: To 'make sense of' something is to understand it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. He is the “friendly” man in the group.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'friendliest': 'the … man in the group' calls for the superlative, and 'friendly', ending in '-y', usually takes '-iest'. 'Most friendly' is also found in standard English, so it is arguable too; 'more friendly' and 'friendlier' are comparatives.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Departing or having departed from a country to settle elsewhere
questions.explanation: An emigrant leaves his or her own country to settle in another; to the country of arrival the same person is an immigrant.

questions.text: Rectify the sentence by selecting the correct spelling from the options. While threatening the integrity of Universal values, the campaign to spread democracy will not suceed.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'succeed'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank. In the absence of her parents, the little girl felt ________ (lonely).
questions.explanation: Without her parents she felt 'alone', close in meaning to 'lonely'; 'crowded' and 'sociable' mean the opposite.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A room for cleaning and storing dishes and cooking utensils and for doing messy kitchen work.
questions.explanation: A scullery is a small room next to a kitchen for washing dishes and other messy work.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANOTNYM of the word 'zest' in the given sentence. The peppy and energetic music of the DJ was able to remove the passivity and dullness present in the party.
questions.explanation: 'Zest' means energy and enthusiasm, which the sentence calls 'peppy and energetic'; its opposite there is 'dullness'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. She asked if he could recount a moment when he felt completely “serene”.
questions.explanation: 'Serene' means calm and untroubled; its opposite is 'turbulent'. 'Pacific' (peaceful) is a synonym.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'revealed'.

questions.text: Select the option that rectifies the spelling error of the underlined word. The historic “cathedrel” stood as a symbol of faith and architectural marvel, drawing visitors from around the world.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'cathedral'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Despite facing numerous challenges, the team successfully _________________ the project ahead of schedule.
questions.explanation: The sentence reports a finished action, so the simple past 'completed'. The passive forms do not fit a subject that does the completing, and 'had completed' would need a later past event.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The (1)______ life in Kashmir was drawing to its end after three (2)______ months. Miss Joan was leaving a week earlier than Mrs. Rhodes, and about two days before she left, I took her alone to the hotel for dinner. We walked to the hotel in (3)______ silence, a silence so heavy that I could (4)______ breathe. The hotel seemed to be far away and yet not far (5)______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'The romantic life in Kashmir': the other options are technical words from mathematics, medicine and phonetics that make no sense here.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Three 'glorious' months: a happy time that was drawing to its end.

questions.text:

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: During the first year, the population of a village increased by 5%, and during the second year, it reduced by 6%. At the end of the second year, its population was 35,532. What was the population at the beginning of the first year?
Determine the smallest number which when divided by 20, 15 and 30 leaves remainder 6 in each case.
questions.explanation: The LCM of 20, 15 and 30 is 60, so the smallest such number is 60 + 6 = 66.

questions.text: A car’s radiator should contain a solution of 52% antifreeze. A motorist has 8 litres of 40% antifreeze. How many litres (rounded off to 2 decimal places) of 95% antifreeze liquid should he add to his solution to produce a 52% antifreeze?
questions.explanation: The 8 litres hold 3.2 litres of antifreeze. Adding x litres of 95%: 3.2 + 0.95x = 0.52(8 + x), so 0.43x = 0.96 and x ≈ 2.23 litres.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3000 as a sum borrowed at 3% per year rate of interest for 5 years.
A cyclist covers a distance of 2.5 km in 4 minutes 10 seconds. How long will he take to cover a distance of 12 km at the same speed?
questions.explanation: 4 minutes 10 seconds is 250 seconds for 2.5 km. 12 km is 4.8 times as far: 4.8 × 250 = 1,200 seconds = 20 minutes.

questions.text: The average weight of a family of five members (in kg) whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 69 kg and 35 kg is:

The outer circumference of the top of a large hemispherical iron bowl is 565.2 cm and the bowl is y cm thick. If the total surface area of the bowl is 98,988.5 cm², then what is the value of y? (Use π = 3.14.)
questions.explanation: Outer radius R = 565.2 ÷ (2 × 3.14) = 90 cm. TSA = outer 2πR² + inner 2πr² + rim π(R² − r²) = π(3R² + r²), so 3.14(24,300 + r²) = 98,988.5, r² = 7,225 and r = 85 cm. y = 90 − 85 = 5 cm.

questions.text: If a sum doubles itself on certain rate of simple interest in 10 years, then at the same rate of interest, the sum will become 4 times itself in:
questions.explanation: Doubling means the interest equals the sum in 10 years, so the rate is 10%. To become 4 times, the interest must be 3 times the sum: 30 years.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3000 as a sum borrowed at 5% per year rate of interest for 3 years.
A man on a tour travels first 120 km at 48 km/h and the next 120 km at 80 km/h. The average speed for the first 240 km of the tour is:
A trader gains 44% after selling an item at 25% discount on the printed price. What is the ratio of the cost price and the printed price of the item?
questions.explanation: SP = 0.75 × printed price = 1.44 × CP, so CP : printed price = 0.75 : 1.44 = 25 : 48.

questions.text: In a school, class 11th has three sections A, B and C. There are 30 students in Section A, 36 students in Section B, and 40 students in Section C. The average marks scored by the students in Section A, Section B and Section C in the Mathematics annual exam are 90, 85 and 70, respectively. Find the average marks scored by the whole class, correct to two places of decimals.

The resistance of a wire is directly proportional to its length and inversely proportional to the square of its radius. Two wires of the same material have the same resistance and their radii are in the ratio of 7 : 8. The corresponding lengths of the wires are 147 cm and L cm, respectively. Find the value of L.
questions.explanation: Equal resistance means L/r² is the same for both wires: L = 147 × (8/7)² = 147 × 64/49 = 192 cm.

questions.text: A shopkeeper mixes three types of seeds worth ₹240, ₹258 and ₹252 in 3 : 1 : 2. Average cost of the mixture is:

E, F, G, H, L, K, and M are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). K sits to the immediate left of F. Only two people sit between K and L when counted from the left of K. Only two people sit between M and E when counted from the right of E. E sits to the immediate right of H. H is not an immediate neighbour of F. Who is sitting to the immediate right of G?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, a person's right is anticlockwise and left clockwise. Clockwise from F the seats are F, K, E, H, L, G, M (the other place for E and H puts H next to F). L sits to G's immediate right.

questions.text: In a code language, 'STATION' is coded as '18' and 'JOURNALS' is coded as '20'. How will 'GOLDMEDAL' be coded in the same language?
questions.explanation: Each code is twice the number of letters plus 4: STATION has 7 letters (2 × 7 + 4 = 18) and JOURNALS 8 (2 × 8 + 4 = 20). GOLDMEDAL has 9: 2 × 9 + 4 = 22.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘system is backbone’ is written as ‘sdf wer tce’ and ‘backbone is you’ is coded as ‘tce kpo wer’. What is the meaning of the code ‘sdf’ in the given language?
questions.explanation: 'is' and 'backbone' are in both sentences, as are 'wer' and 'tce' in both codes. The word left in the first sentence is 'system', and the code left is 'sdf'.

questions.text: What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘×’ are interchanged and ‘÷’ and ‘−’ are interchanged? 35 ÷ 4 + 6 − 3 × 12 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 35 − 4 × 6 ÷ 3 + 12 = 35 − 8 + 12 = 39.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts,decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All roses are lilies. No rose is a sunflower. Conclusions: (I) All lilies are roses. (II) No lily is a sunflower.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: All roses being lilies does not make all lilies roses (I). The lilies that are not roses may be sunflowers, so II does not follow either.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the statement(s). Statements: All bags are duffles. All duffles are containers. Conclusions: (I) Some containers are duffles. (II) All bags are containers.
questions.explanation: Every duffle is a container, so some containers are duffles (I); bags are duffles and duffles are containers, so all bags are containers (II). Both follow.

questions.text: What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 12 × 3 – 5 ÷ 4 + 11 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 12 ÷ 3 + 5 × 4 − 11 = 4 + 20 − 11 = 13.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘SNOW’ is written as ‘7358’ and ‘BLEW’ is written as ‘1293’. How is ‘W’ coded in the given language?
questions.explanation: W is the only letter in both words and 3 the only digit in both codes, so W = 3.

questions.text: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Only 3 people sit between C and E when counted from the right of C. Only 1 person sits between E and G when counted from the left of E. F sits immediate to the left of D. Only 2 people sit between B and F when counted from the left of B. How many people sit between G and B when counted from the left of G?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, a person's right is anticlockwise and left clockwise. Clockwise from C the seats are C, D, F, E, A, G, B, the only order that meets every condition. B sits immediately to G's left, so no one is between them.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 41, 48, 55, 62, 69, ?
questions.explanation: The numbers rise by 7 each time: 69 + 7 = 76.

questions.text: BMGC is related to GRDZ in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, LWAW is related to QBXT. To which of the following is VGUQ related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: The first two letters move 5 places forward and the last two 3 back, wrapping round the alphabet: BMGC → GRDZ and LWAW → QBXT. So VGUQ → ALRN.

questions.text: 11 is related to 106 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 15 is related to 146. To which of the following is 19 related following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is ten times the first minus 4: 11 × 10 − 4 = 106 and 15 × 10 − 4 = 146. So 19 × 10 − 4 = 186.

questions.text: MK14 is related to QO19 in a certain way. In the same way, XV31 is related to BZ36. To which of the following is RP52 related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Both letters move 4 places forward and the number rises by 5: MK14 → QO19 and XV31 → BZ36 (X wraps round to B). So RP52 → VT57.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order ? DBF, HFJ, LJN, PNR, ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 4 places forward from one group to the next: D, H, L, P, T; B, F, J, N, R; F, J, N, R, V. The next group is TRV.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the given sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (284, 238) (271, 225)
questions.explanation: The second number is 46 less than the first: 284 − 46 = 238 and 271 − 46 = 225. Likewise 212 − 46 = 166.

questions.text: At which of the following places is the tomb of Sher Shah Suri situated?
questions.explanation: Sher Shah Suri's tomb stands in an artificial lake at Sasaram, in Bihar's Rohtas district.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: After the decisive battle of Plassey of 1757, who among the following was declared as the Nawab of Bengal by the British?
questions.explanation: After Plassey the British made Mir Jafar, Siraj-ud-Daulah's commander who had gone over to them, the Nawab of Bengal.

questions.text: Which of the following countries won its 8th Men's Asian Cup cricket title in 2023?
questions.explanation: India beat Sri Lanka by ten wickets in the final at Colombo in September 2023 for its eighth Asia Cup title.

questions.text: Which of the following dance awards is organised by the National Institute of Indian Classical Dance?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the Abhinandan Saroja National Award, which the National Institute of Indian Classical Dance presents to classical dancers.

questions.text: Ranjani Hebbar was associated with which of the following fields?
questions.explanation: Ranjani Hebbar (died 2013) was a Carnatic vocalist from Udupi, Karnataka, and an A-grade artist of All India Radio.

questions.text: Which element is known for having the highest electronegativity on the periodic table?
questions.explanation: Fluorine is the most electronegative element, at 3.98 on the Pauling scale.

questions.text: What does the term 'deuce' signify in tennis?
options: The final point in a game
questions.explanation: Deuce is a score of 40-40 in a game of tennis; a player must then win two points in a row to take the game.

questions.text: Which virus is responsible for causing common cold?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives rhinovirus, the cause of most common colds. Some coronaviruses also cause colds, though far fewer; influenza viruses cause flu, and hepatitis A a liver infection.

questions.text: In which of the following years was the 11th Fundamental Duty added in the Indian Constitution through the 86th Amendment Act?
questions.explanation: The 86th Amendment Act, 2002 added Article 51A(k), the duty of parents or guardians to provide opportunities for education to their children aged 6 to 14.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In the year 1930, the Salt Satyagraha was led by who among the following?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi led the Salt Satyagraha, marching from Sabarmati to Dandi in March-April 1930 to break the salt law.

questions.text: Akbar’s first expedition towards Deccan was sent to Ahmednagar under the leadership of Prince Murad and _______________.
questions.explanation: Akbar's first Deccan campaign, against Ahmednagar, was led by Prince Murad and Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khanan; Chand Bibi defended the city.

questions.text: Which Rigvedic God is considered an intermediary between God and men?
questions.explanation: In the Rig Veda, Agni, the god of fire, carries the sacrificial offerings to the gods, and so acts as the messenger between gods and men.

questions.text: How many central banks can a country have?
questions.explanation: A country has a single central bank, which issues its currency and regulates its banks; India's is the Reserve Bank of India.

questions.text: Which of the following is written by Mulk Raj Anand?
questions.explanation: 'Untouchable' (1935) is Mulk Raj Anand's first novel. 'The Guide' is by R. K. Narayan, 'The Blue Umbrella' by Ruskin Bond and 'The White Tiger' by Aravind Adiga.

questions.text: The Uttarakhand Public Services (Horizontal Reservation for Women) Bill, 2022 provides how much reservation to women?
questions.explanation: The Uttarakhand bill of 2022 gives women of Uttarakhand domicile 30% horizontal reservation in the state's public services.

questions.text: A regal ceremony in the form of Beating Retreat ceremony on the evening of _____________ marks the end of Republic Day celebrations.
questions.explanation: The Beating Retreat ceremony at Vijay Chowk, New Delhi, on the evening of 29 January closes the Republic Day celebrations.

questions.text: What is the rate of movement of tectonic plate boundaries?
questions.explanation: Tectonic plates move only a few centimetres a year; of these options, 1-2 inches (about 2.5-5 cm) a year.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in ‘Liberty’ as per the Preamble of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The Preamble promises liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship; 'trust and hope' are not among them.

questions.text: Based on the number of chambers in the heart, select the odd one from the following.
questions.explanation: Frogs, chameleons and turtles have three-chambered hearts; the crocodile, like the other crocodilians (alone among reptiles), has four.

questions.text: Padma Subramanyam, Alarmel Valli, Yamini Krishnamurthy and Anita Ratnam are distinguished practitioners of ____________.
questions.explanation: Padma Subrahmanyam, Alarmel Valli, Yamini Krishnamurthy and Anita Ratnam are all noted Bharatanatyam dancers (Yamini Krishnamurthy was also a leading Kuchipudi dancer).

questions.text: Which of the following Biosphere reserves is located in Uttarakhand?
questions.explanation: The Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve is in Uttarakhand. Pachmarhi is in Madhya Pradesh, the Nilgiri in Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka, and Dihang-Dibang in Arunachal Pradesh.

questions.text: In February 2023, who was appointed as the CEO of NITI Aayog?
questions.explanation: BVR Subrahmanyam was appointed CEO of NITI Aayog in February 2023, succeeding Parameswaran Iyer.

questions.text: In which state is the Kaiga Nuclear Power Project located?
questions.explanation: The Kaiga nuclear power station is in Uttara Kannada district, Karnataka.

questions.text: Theravada is known as the official religion of which of the following neighbouring countries of India?
questions.explanation: Theravada Buddhism is the main religion of Sri Lanka, whose constitution gives Buddhism 'the foremost place'. Bangladesh, Afghanistan and Pakistan are Muslim-majority countries.

questions.text: Your sibling accidentally broke your favourite vase. Which of the following idioms might you use to tell them not to worry about it?
questions.explanation: 'Don't cry over spilt milk' means there is no point in worrying about something that has already happened and cannot be undone.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The humble surroundings of our company ______ creativity amongst the newly recruited employees.
questions.explanation: The surroundings 'inspired', that is encouraged, creativity; 'banished' says the opposite, and 'connected' and 'filed' do not fit.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The act of talking to oneself, often audibly
questions.explanation: A soliloquy is the act of speaking one's thoughts aloud to oneself; a monologue is a long speech by one person to others.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'obligation'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Fetid
questions.explanation: 'Fetid' means foul-smelling; its opposite is 'fragrant'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. We agree that Professor Revanth is very knowledgeable, but we do not like attending his classes because he always keeps “blowing the trumpet” .
questions.explanation: To 'blow one's own trumpet' is to boast about oneself.

questions.text: Select the option that will correct the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no correction is required, select No correction needed. Naveen is “as tall as” Rocky.
questions.explanation: Equality is shown with 'as … as' and the positive degree, so the sentence is correct as it stands.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. He hardness ever / complains about / his workload because / he enjoys his job.
questions.explanation: 'Hardly ever' means almost never: 'He hardly ever complains about his workload'. 'Hardness' is a noun.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. I have a “vague” memory of meeting her many years ago.
questions.explanation: 'Vague' means unclear or indistinct: 'hazy'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word opposite in meaning (ANTONYM) to the underlined word in the given sentence. Aunty Hema gave us her “candid” opinion on the skit we performed on Children’s Day.
questions.explanation: 'Candid' means frank and, in an older sense, free from bias; its opposite here is 'prejudiced'. 'Frank' is a synonym.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I dream of a country where even the least talented person has the ________ to earn a living.
questions.explanation: Even the least talented person should have the 'opportunity', the chance, to earn a living.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. The late secretary of our society was known for his “ruthless” treatment of all the security personnel of the society.
questions.explanation: 'Ruthless' means without pity; its opposite is 'compassionate'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word. A) Exaggerate B) Accommodate C) Exuberant D) Perservere
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'persevere'.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. An eucalyptus tree in my backyard acts as a landmark for many to reach my house.
options: acts as a landmark for many
questions.explanation: 'Eucalyptus' begins with a 'yoo' sound, a consonant sound, so it takes 'a': 'A eucalyptus tree'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. How can someone / walk this farthest / just for / peace of mind?
questions.explanation: 'This far' means to such a distance: 'walk this far'. The superlative 'farthest' does not go with 'this'.

questions.text: Select the option that corrects the error in the given sentence. She performed bad in the exam.
questions.explanation: A verb is modified by an adverb: 'She performed badly in the exam.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Show
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'show' is 'cover', to hide from view; 'exhibit' and 'display' are synonyms.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The fresh air / in the garden relaxes / the minds of children as / the environment is cleaner.
questions.explanation: Nothing is being compared, so the positive degree: 'as the environment is clean'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence. Applicants who are younger and prettier than you will continue appliying.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'applying'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The teacher asked us to _______ our essays for spelling and grammar errors.
questions.explanation: To 'revise' an essay is to read it again and correct it.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Students want (1)________ as the primary outcome of higher education. Hence, practical experience becomes (2)________ valuable to a student’s degree. Indian students are highly (3)________ at theoretical learning but lack practical training. This (4)________ an issue for decades in the Indian job market. In order to address this (5)________ issue, state governments have to take a lead. The AP government in the past three years have made efforts to bridge this long-lasting gap between theoretical and practical learning of the students.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 1.
questions.explanation: Students want 'employability', a noun, as the outcome of higher education; 'employable' is an adjective.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Students want (1)________ as the primary outcome of higher education. Hence, practical experience becomes (2)________ valuable to a student’s degree. Indian students are highly (3)________ at theoretical learning but lack practical training. This (4)________ an issue for decades in the Indian job market. In order to address this (5)________ issue, state governments have to take a lead. The AP government in the past three years have made efforts to bridge this long-lasting gap between theoretical and practical learning of the students.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 2.
questions.explanation: Practical experience becomes 'equally' valuable, as valuable as the degree itself.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Students want (1)________ as the primary outcome of higher education. Hence, practical experience becomes (2)________ valuable to a student’s degree. Indian students are highly (3)________ at theoretical learning but lack practical training. This (4)________ an issue for decades in the Indian job market. In order to address this (5)________ issue, state governments have to take a lead. The AP government in the past three years have made efforts to bridge this long-lasting gap between theoretical and practical learning of the students.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 3.
questions.explanation: Indian students are 'highly competitive' at theoretical learning, in contrast with their lack of practical training.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Students want (1)________ as the primary outcome of higher education. Hence, practical experience becomes (2)________ valuable to a student’s degree. Indian students are highly (3)________ at theoretical learning but lack practical training. This (4)________ an issue for decades in the Indian job market. In order to address this (5)________ issue, state governments have to take a lead. The AP government in the past three years have made efforts to bridge this long-lasting gap between theoretical and practical learning of the students.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 4.
questions.explanation: 'For decades' calls for the present perfect: 'This has been an issue'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Students want (1)________ as the primary outcome of higher education. Hence, practical experience becomes (2)________ valuable to a student’s degree. Indian students are highly (3)________ at theoretical learning but lack practical training. This (4)________ an issue for decades in the Indian job market. In order to address this (5)________ issue, state governments have to take a lead. The AP government in the past three years have made efforts to bridge this long-lasting gap between theoretical and practical learning of the students.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 5.
questions.explanation: A 'perennial' issue is one that lasts or keeps returning: the 'long-lasting gap' the passage goes on to describe.
