questions.text: Mr Rao purchased a laptop for ₹45,000. After a few months, as his office provided another laptop, he sold it at a loss of 12% to Mrs Sharma. After one year, she sold it to an engineering student for a profit of 12%. What is the amount the student had to pay?
Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2500 as a sum borrowed at 8% per year rate of interest for 3 years.
Two trains are running in opposite directions at the same speed. If the length of each train is 150 m and they cross each other in 15 sec, find the speed of each train (in km/hr).
questions.explanation: Running towards each other, the trains cover 150 + 150 = 300 m in 15 s, a combined 20 m/s. So each runs at 10 m/s = 10 × 18/5 = 36 km/h.

questions.text: 400 chickooes were bought at ₹1280 per hundred and were sold at a profit of ₹980. Find the selling price (in ₹) per dozen of chickooes.

What is the ratio in which product A, costing ₹70 per 100 grams, should be mixed with product B, costing ₹100 per 100 grams, so that on selling the mixture at ₹1.20 per gram, a profit of 25% is achieved?
questions.explanation: Selling at ₹1.20 a gram (₹120 per 100 g) for a 25% profit means a cost of 120/1.25 = ₹96 per 100 g. By alligation A : B = (100 − 96) : (96 − 70) = 4 : 26 = 2 : 13.

questions.text: The HCF and LCM of two numbers are 11 and 3465, respectively. If one of the two numbers is 693, what is the other number?
questions.explanation: The product of two numbers equals HCF × LCM: 11 × 3465/693 = 38,115/693 = 55.

questions.text: If Mohan’s income is 20% less than Arvind’s income, then how much per cent is Arvind’s income more than Mohan’s income?
questions.explanation: If Arvind earns 100, Mohan earns 80. Arvind's 20 more is 20/80 = 25% of Mohan's income.

questions.text: The area of a right-angled triangle is 80m². If its perpendicular is equal to 20 m, then find its base.
questions.explanation: Area = ½ × base × perpendicular: 80 = ½ × b × 20, so b = 8 m.

questions.text: A clothing store announces a discount scheme 'Buy one shirt and get 40% off on another shirt of the same price'. What is the profit percentage of the store, given that each shirt has a cost price 60% below the marked price?
questions.explanation: Take the marked price as ₹100, so each shirt costs ₹40. Two shirts sell for 100 + 60 = ₹160 against a cost of ₹80: a profit of 80/80 = 100%.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2500 as a sum borrowed at 6% per year rate of interest for 2 years.
If 80 workers took 25 days to finish a task,how many days will it take to finish the same task if 20 more workers join?
questions.explanation: The task is 80 × 25 = 2,000 worker-days; 100 workers finish it in 2,000/100 = 20 days.

questions.text: In an examination, the average score of a student was 71.9. If the student would have got 28 more marks in English, 22 more marks in Mathematics, 16 more marks in Computer Science, 14 more marks in History, 10 less marks in Hindi, and retained the same marks in other subjects, then the average score would have been 80.65. How many subjects were there in the examination?
questions.explanation: The changes add 28 + 22 + 16 + 14 − 10 = 70 marks and raise the average by 80.65 − 71.9 = 8.75, so there are 70/8.75 = 8 subjects.

questions.text: A train travelling at a speed of 36 km/h crosses a pole in 24 sec. What is the length of the train?
questions.explanation: 36 km/h = 10 m/s. Crossing a pole, the train covers its own length: 10 × 24 = 240 m.

questions.text: The average weight of X, Y and Z is 67 kg. The average weight of X and Y is 64 kg and that of Y and Z is 52 kg. The weight of Y (in kg) is:
Ram borrowed ₹20,000 at 6% per annum and ₹25,000 at 8% per annum, for the same duration. He had to pay ₹9,600 in all as interest. What is the time period?

Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All irons are heaters. Some irons are fans. Conclusions: (I) Some heaters are fans. (II) All fans are irons.
options: Both conclusion I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: The irons that are fans are also heaters, so some heaters are fans (I). Nothing says every fan is an iron, so II does not follow.

questions.text: Six persons – Rahul, Ram, Ranjan, Reena, Rohit and Rupali – are sitting around a circular table facing the centre, but not necessarily in the same order. Rupali is sitting second to the right of Ram, who is Reena’s immediate neighbour. Rohit is not an immediate neighbour of Reena. Rahul is an immediate neighbour of both, Rupali and Ram. Who is sitting second to the left of Ram?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, each person's right is anticlockwise. Rahul sits between Ram and Rupali, and Reena on Ram's other side. Rohit may not sit next to Reena, so he sits opposite Ram and Ranjan sits next to Reena: second to the left of Ram.

questions.text: 18 is related to 91 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 27 is related to 136. To which of the following is 45 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 - Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is five times the first plus 1: 18 × 5 + 1 = 91 and 27 × 5 + 1 = 136. Likewise 45 × 5 + 1 = 226.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘BIRD’ is coded as ‘6428’ and ‘DOPE’ is coded as ‘5679’.What is the code for ‘D’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: D is the only letter in both words and 6 the only digit in both codes, so D = 6.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 2, 3, 6 ,11, 18 ,?
questions.explanation: The differences are 1, 3, 5, 7, so the next is 9: 18 + 9 = 27.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘÷ ‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘−’ are interchanged? 88 ÷ 18 × 28 + 4 − 14 =?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 88 + 18 − 28 ÷ 4 × 14 = 88 + 18 − 98 = 8.

questions.text: EBHD is related to IFLH in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, JGMI is related to NKQM. To which of the following is OLRN related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 4 places forward: E → I, B → F, H → L, D → H, and the same for JGMI → NKQM. So OLRN → SPVR.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘zebra tool bean’ is coded as 'rj pi ki' and ‘bean knife army’ is coded as ‘ko jm pi’. How is ‘bean’ coded in the given language?
questions.explanation: 'bean' is the only word in both sentences and 'pi' the only code in both, so bean = pi.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'ABROAD' is coded as ‘WZLIYZ’ and 'ADVISE' is coded as ‘VHREWZ’. How will 'AGENDA' be coded in the same language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite in the alphabet (A ↔ Z, B ↔ Y, and so on) and the result is written backwards: ABROAD → ZYILZW → WZLIYZ. So AGENDA → ZTVMWZ → ZWMVTZ.

questions.text: In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/ subtracting /multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 246, 123; 448, 224
questions.explanation: The second number is half the first: 246 ÷ 2 = 123 and 448 ÷ 2 = 224. Likewise 624 ÷ 2 = 312.

questions.text: What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 2 ÷ 40 × 5 – 4 + 5 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 2 × 40 ÷ 5 + 4 − 5 = 16 + 4 − 5 = 15.

questions.text: Six people A, B, C, D, E and F are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). F is sitting third to the right of C. D is sitting second to the left of F. A and E are immediate neighbours. E is sitting second to the right of B. How many people are sitting between E and C when counted from the left of E?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, each person's right is anticlockwise. F sits opposite C and D second to F's left; E second to the right of B then puts B, E and A in the other seats, so going right from C the order is C, D, B, F, E, A. Counting leftwards from E: F, B and D come before C, three people.

questions.text: UD 1 is related to OF −6 in a certain way. In the same way, IX 6 is related to CZ −1. To which of the following is MJ 3 related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: The first letter moves 6 back, the second 2 forward and the number falls by 7: U → O, D → F, 1 → −6 and I → C, X → Z, 6 → −1. So MJ 3 → GL −4.

questions.text: Read the given statement(s) and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement(s). Statements: Some tables are plates. Some tables are spoons. Conclusions: (I) At least some spoons are plates. (II) Some plates are tables.
questions.explanation: Some tables are plates, so some plates are tables (II). The tables that are plates and those that are spoons need not overlap, so I does not follow.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? HXS, JVQ, LTO, NRM, ?
questions.explanation: The first letters move 2 forward (H, J, L, N, P), the second 2 back (X, V, T, R, P) and the third 2 back (S, Q, O, M, K): PPK.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who is the author of ‘The story of My Experiments with Truth’?
questions.explanation: 'The Story of My Experiments with Truth' is MK Gandhi's autobiography.

questions.text: At 10 × 10⁴ Pa pressure and 300 K temperature, the volume of 0.09 mol CO₂ gas is 22.4 × 10⁻³ m³. What will be the volume of the gas if the pressure is decreased to 2 × 10⁴ Pa?
questions.explanation: At constant temperature Boyle's law gives P₁V₁ = P₂V₂: V₂ = (10 × 10⁴ × 22.4 × 10⁻³)/(2 × 10⁴) = 5 × 22.4 × 10⁻³ = 112.0 × 10⁻³ m³. (The amount of gas and the temperature are not needed.)

questions.text: Which of the following Articles entails “Equality of opportunity in matters of public employment”?
questions.explanation: Article 16 guarantees equality of opportunity in matters of public employment. Article 14 is equality before the law, Article 15 bars discrimination and Article 17 abolishes untouchability.

questions.text: To control the prices, which of the following Sultans of Delhi set up three different markets for different commodities in Delhi?
questions.explanation: Alauddin Khalji's market reforms set up separate markets in Delhi for grain, for cloth and other goods, and for horses, slaves and cattle, all at fixed prices.

questions.text: The modern-day __________ was molded by the renowned Tanjore Bandhu, consisting of the four Nattuvanars: Ponnayya, Vadivelu, Sivanandam and Chinnayya.
questions.explanation: The Tanjore Quartet, four brothers at the Thanjavur court in the early 19th century, set the order of items of modern Bharatanatyam.

questions.text: Which state in India has the largest scheduled tribe population as per the 2011 Census?
questions.explanation: By the 2011 Census Madhya Pradesh has the largest scheduled tribe population of any state, about 1.53 crore.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The partition of ___________was annulled in 1911.
questions.explanation: The partition of Bengal, made in 1905, was annulled in 1911, as announced at the Delhi Durbar.

questions.text: Who became the first female armless archer to win a medal at the Para World Championship event, 2023?
questions.explanation: Sheetal Devi won silver in the women's compound event at the 2023 World Archery Para Championships in Pilsen, the first female armless archer to win a medal there.

questions.text: Which of the following options represents the correct flow of energy in an ecosystem?
questions.explanation: Energy enters an ecosystem through producers, which capture sunlight, and passes to herbivores and then to carnivores.

questions.text: In 1990, who established Nrityagram, a dance school in Bengaluru?
questions.explanation: Odissi dancer Protima Gauri Bedi set up Nrityagram, a residential dance village near Bengaluru, in 1990.

questions.text: Sawai Gandharva was associated with which of the following gharanas?
questions.explanation: Sawai Gandharva (Rambhau Kundgolkar), a disciple of Abdul Karim Khan, was a singer of the Kirana gharana and the guru of Bhimsen Joshi.

questions.text: The percentage of pore space between the particles inside a rock or soil is called:
questions.explanation: Porosity is the share of a rock's or soil's volume taken up by pore spaces; permeability is how easily water passes through it.

questions.text: Losar festival is celebrated in which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Losar, the Tibetan Buddhist new year, is celebrated in Arunachal Pradesh by communities such as the Monpas, as well as in Sikkim and Ladakh.

questions.text: In which state is the Rewa Ultra Mega Solar Power Project located?
questions.explanation: The 750 MW Rewa Ultra Mega Solar project is in Rewa district, Madhya Pradesh.

questions.text: What is the chemical name for the compound responsible for the cooling sensation in mint leaves?
questions.explanation: Menthol gives mint its cooling sensation. Capsaicin is what makes chillies hot.

questions.text: In March 2023, who was appointed as Chairperson of Pension Fund Regulatory Development Authority (PFRDA)?
questions.explanation: Deepak Mohanty, a former executive director of the RBI, was appointed Chairperson of the PFRDA in March 2023.

questions.text: In the State Legislature, _______________ is subject to dissolution.
questions.explanation: A state's Legislative Assembly can be dissolved; its Legislative Council, like the Rajya Sabha, is a permanent house. The House of the People and the Council of States are the houses of Parliament.

questions.text: For which of the following minerals are Jharia and Raniganj known?
questions.explanation: Jharia (Jharkhand) and Raniganj (West Bengal) are major coalfields of the Damodar valley.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following formed an organisation to support widow remarriage in Madras Presidency?
questions.explanation: In the Telugu-speaking areas of the Madras Presidency, Kandukuri Veeresalingam Pantulu formed an association for widow remarriage. Vidyasagar led the movement in Bengal.

questions.text: The ___________ scheme, that covers artisans related to 18 fields, was included under the 'Payments Infrastructure Development Fund' ('PIDF') scheme by the Reserve Bank of India in October 2023.
questions.explanation: In October 2023 the RBI extended its Payments Infrastructure Development Fund scheme to the beneficiaries of PM Vishwakarma, the scheme for artisans and craftspeople in 18 trades.

questions.text: What was the name of the official torch for the Khelo India University Games 2022?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'Shakti' as the name of the official torch of the Khelo India University Games 2022, which Uttar Pradesh hosted in May-June 2023.

questions.text: As per Census 2011, which of the following is the most populated city in India?
questions.explanation: By the 2011 Census Greater Mumbai, with about 1.24 crore people, was India's most populous city.

questions.text: The second largest dome in the world was built in India and is still standing strong. Which dome is being spoken about here?
questions.explanation: Gol Gumbaz, the tomb of Mohammed Adil Shah at Bijapur (Vijayapura), Karnataka, is often described as the second largest dome in the world.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: At burials in Harappan sites the dead were generally laid in pits.
Harappan culture spread only to Sindh and Punjab.
The script of the Harappan culture has been deciphered by historians.
Granaries in the Indus Valley Civilization were found in Harappa only.
questions.explanation: At Harappan burials the dead were generally laid in pits. The culture also spread to Gujarat, Rajasthan and Haryana, its script is still undeciphered, and a granary was found at Mohenjodaro too.

questions.text: Identify the correct match in the context of microfinance.
questions.explanation: Muhammad Yunus founded the Grameen Bank in Bangladesh, a pioneer of microcredit; he and the bank shared the 2006 Nobel Peace Prize.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Industrialisation gives even the least talented person a chance to ______________ his livelihood.
questions.explanation: One 'earns' a livelihood.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word to fill in the blank. We ___________________ to follow the traffic rules.
questions.explanation: 'Ought to' expresses duty: 'We ought to follow the traffic rules.' 'Aught' means anything.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Obsequious
questions.explanation: 'Obsequious' means too eager to please or obey; of these, 'obstinate', stubbornly refusing to give way, is the nearest to its opposite.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. According to Greek mythology, Sipylus is “holier” city of Lydia.
questions.explanation: Picking out one city from all the cities of Lydia calls for the superlative with 'the': 'Sipylus is the holiest city of Lydia.' 'Most holiest' is a double superlative.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word. The “sink” is clogged due to solid materials.
options: A large fixed container to wash hands or utensils
questions.explanation: A 'sink' is a fixed basin for washing hands or utensils.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'awesome'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate superlative adjective form to fill in the blanks. What’s ___ book you’ve ever read?
questions.explanation: The superlative of 'interesting' is 'the most interesting'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. A good lawyer / always looks in the / case before he / attends court.
questions.explanation: To examine a matter closely is to 'look into' it: 'always looks into the case'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. On the back foot
questions.explanation: To be 'on the back foot' is to be at a disadvantage, forced to defend oneself.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Gloomy
questions.explanation: 'Gloomy' means dark or depressing: 'dismal'. 'Buoyant' is close to its opposite.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Before the internet was available on mobile, I read often books for entertainment and information.
questions.explanation: An adverb of frequency goes before the main verb: 'I often read books'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate present tense form of the verb to fill in the blank. __________ they like sweets?
questions.explanation: With 'they', a present tense question takes 'do': 'Do they like sweets?'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Predicament
questions.explanation: A 'predicament' is a difficult situation; of these, 'solution', the way out of one, is the nearest to its opposite. 'Mess' is close in meaning.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical/spelling error. They decided to /start their journey / towards the hills / in midnight.
questions.explanation: A point of time takes 'at': 'at midnight', not 'in midnight'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Despite his initial ___________, he eventually agreed to join the team.
questions.explanation: 'Despite' signals a contrast: his initial 'reluctance', then his agreement.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The investigating team smelled a ___________________ in the suspect's defence.
questions.explanation: To 'smell a rat' is to suspect that something is wrong.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word to fill in the blank meaningfully.. The ______ on the wall was beautifully painted.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'picture'.

questions.text: S gets 78, 75, 68, 64 and 58 marks in Hindi, English, Chemistry, Physics and Mathematics, respectively. What are his average marks per subject?

In a group of 200 members, 45% are teenagers and the remaining are adults. The average weight of the whole group is 62 kg. If the average weight of teenagers is 56 kg, then the nearest integral value of the average weight of adults is ________.
questions.explanation: The whole group weighs 200 × 62 = 12,400 kg and the 90 teenagers 90 × 56 = 5,040 kg, so the 110 adults weigh 7,360 kg: 7,360 ÷ 110 = 66.9, or 67 kg.

questions.text: The average of the first twelve multiples of 11 is:
questions.explanation: The multiples 11, 22, …, 132 are evenly spaced, so their average is (11 + 132)/2 = 71.5.

questions.text: The diameter of a hollow hemisphere is 40 cm. Water is filled in it up to its brim. When spherical lead shots each of diameter 0.8 cm are dropped into the hemisphere, three-fifths of the water flows out. How many lead shots were dropped into the hemisphere?
questions.explanation: The hemisphere (radius 20 cm) holds (2/3)π × 20³ = 16,000π/3 cm³, so the shots displace three-fifths of it, 3,200π cm³. Each shot (radius 0.4 cm) has volume (4/3)π × 0.4³ = 0.256π/3 cm³, and 3,200π ÷ (0.256π/3) = 37,500.

questions.text: The HCF of 21 and 49 is:
questions.explanation: 21 = 3 × 7 and 49 = 7 × 7, so the HCF is 7.

questions.text: What will be the average of all the odd numbers from 11 to 71 (both inclusive)?
questions.explanation: The odd numbers 11, 13, …, 71 are evenly spaced, so their average is (11 + 71)/2 = 41.

questions.text: The difference between the selling prices with 19% profit and 11% loss is Rs.454.50. What is the cost price of the item?
questions.explanation: The two selling prices differ by 19% + 11% = 30% of the cost price, so the cost price is 454.50 ÷ 0.3 = ₹1,515.

questions.text: If a man takes 36 minutes to cover a certain distance at a speed of 6 km/h, then the distance covered by him is:
questions.explanation: 36 minutes is 0.6 hour, and 6 × 0.6 = 3.6 km.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2500 as a sum borrowed at 5% per year rate of interest for 4 years.
Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3000 as a sum borrowed at 5% per year rate of interest for 4 years.
A person spends 75% of his income. If his income increases by 15% and expenditure decreases by 10%, then what percentage increase will occur in his savings?
questions.explanation: On an income of 100 he spends 75 and saves 25. Afterwards he earns 115 and spends 67.5, saving 47.5: a rise of 22.5 on 25, or 90%.

questions.text: Gagandeep marks his goods 50% above the cost price and offers a discount of 25% on the marked price to his customers. What is the percentage gain of Gagandeep?
questions.explanation: Selling price = 1.5 × 0.75 = 1.125 times the cost price: a gain of 12.5%.

questions.text: A cooperative society increases the annual rate of simple interest from 10% to 16½ %, then the yearly income of a person increases by ₹1,077.70. The simple interest (in ₹) on the sum at 10% for four years will be:
questions.explanation: The rise of 16.5% − 10% = 6.5% of the sum is ₹1,077.70, so the sum is ₹16,580. SI at 10% for four years = 16,580 × 10 × 4/100 = ₹6,632.

questions.explanation: The selling price must rise from 1.1 to 1.3 times the cost price, an increase of 19.5 × 0.2/1.1 = 3.5454…, or ₹3.55 to two decimal places.

questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places forward: N → P, U → W, Q → S, M → O, and J → L, Q → S, M → O, I → K. So FMIE → HOKG.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? NRT, JNP, FJL, BFH, ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 4 places back every step (B wraps round to X): N, J, F, B, X; R, N, J, F, B; T, P, L, H, D. The next cluster is XBD.

questions.text: S, T, U, V, W, X and Y are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Only four people are sitting between S and W when counted from the right of S. Only one person is sitting between W and Y when counted from the left of W. Only two people are sitting between S and X when counted from the left of S. Only two people are sitting between U and Y when counted from the left of U . Only one person is sitting between U and V when counted from the left of V. Who is sitting to the immediate right of X ?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, a person's right is anticlockwise and left clockwise. Clockwise from S the seats are S, U, W, X, Y, T, V: four sit between S and W on S's right, one between W and Y on W's left, two between S and X on S's left, two between U and Y on U's left and one between V and U on V's left. X's immediate right is W.

questions.text: What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 12 ÷ 13 + 128 – 343 × 49 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 12 × 13 − 128 + 343 ÷ 49 = 156 − 128 + 7 = 35.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the following series? -553, -532, -511, -490, -469, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is 21 more than the one before: −469 + 21 = −448.

questions.text: 28 is related to 168 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 39 is related to 234. To which of the following is 43 related following the same logic?(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbersinto its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: The second number is six times the first: 28 × 6 = 168 and 39 × 6 = 234. Likewise 43 × 6 = 258.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘–’ are interchanged? 24 + 3 ÷ 8 × 2 – 6 =?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 24 ÷ 3 + 8 − 2 × 6 = 8 + 8 − 12 = 4.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some rhinos are birds. All penguins are birds. Conclusions: (I): Some rhinos are penguins. (II): All birds are penguins.
questions.explanation: The rhinos that are birds need not be penguins, so I does not follow; and all penguins being birds does not make all birds penguins, so II does not follow.

questions.text: U, V, W, X, Y, Z and A are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). X sits third to the left of Y. W sits second to the left of V. Only Y sits between A and W. U is not an immediate neighbour of X. Who sits fourth to the right of Z?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, a person's left is clockwise and right anticlockwise. A and W sit either side of Y; W cannot be on Y's left, since V would then need A's seat. So clockwise from Y the seats are Y, A, Z, X, V, U, W (U, not next to X, takes the seat between V and W). Four places to Z's right is U.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘RESHMA’ is coded as ‘XJEPBO’ and ‘PRITHAM’ is coded as ‘JXEQFOM’. How will ‘GOURI’ be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places back and the result is reversed: RESHMA → OBPEJX → XJEPBO and PRITHAM → MOFQEXJ → JXEQFOM. So GOURI → DLROF → FORLD.

questions.text: FLLC is related to HNNE in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, AFFW is related to CHHY. To which of the following is PVVM related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places forward: F → H, L → N, C → E, and A → C, F → H, W → Y. So PVVM → RXXO.

questions.text: In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 7, 27; 11, 43
questions.explanation: The second number is four times the first minus 1: 7 × 4 − 1 = 27 and 11 × 4 − 1 = 43. Likewise 15 × 4 − 1 = 59.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘LIME’ is coded as ‘4826’ and ‘FOLD’ is coded as ‘9378’. What is the code for ’L’ in that language?
questions.explanation: L is the only letter in both words and 8 the only digit in both codes, so L = 8.

questions.text: As per the 2011 census, which of the following union territories had the lowest population?
questions.explanation: Lakshadweep, with 64,473 people in 2011, was the least populous Union Territory; Andaman and Nicobar had about 3.8 lakh, and Chandigarh and Puducherry over 10 lakh each.

questions.text: What is the study of the interactions between living organisms and their environment called?
questions.explanation: Ecology is the study of how living organisms interact with one another and with their surroundings.

questions.text: In which of the following states is the Mamallapuram Utsav celebrated?
questions.explanation: The Mamallapuram Dance Festival is held at Mamallapuram (Mahabalipuram) in Tamil Nadu, against the backdrop of the Pallava rock monuments.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT considered as a Fundamental Duty?
options: To develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform
To value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture
To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India
questions.explanation: Article 51A asks citizens to uphold the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India, to value and preserve the heritage of our composite culture and to develop the scientific temper; protecting secularism is not among the listed duties.

questions.text: Which Kuchipudi dancer received National Nritya Shiromani Award 2022?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Aparna Satheesan. Of the others, Jatin Goswami is a Sattriya dancer and Anindita Neogy Anaam a Kathak dancer.

questions.text: Which of the following rivers flows north of the Tropic of Cancer in India?
questions.explanation: The Yamuna, which rises in Uttarakhand and joins the Ganga at Prayagraj, flows wholly north of the Tropic of Cancer (23.5° N). The Tapi, Mahanadi and Penganga flow south of it.

questions.text: In May 2023, who was sworn in as the new Central Vigilance Commissioner of India?
questions.explanation: Praveen Kumar Srivastava, acting Central Vigilance Commissioner since December 2022, was sworn in as CVC by the President on 29 May 2023. Suresh N Patel was his predecessor.

questions.text: The Huttari dance, observed as an annual tradition, is a leisurely performance that takes place during the harvesting season in _____________.
questions.explanation: Huttari is the harvest festival of the Kodavas of Kodagu (Coorg) in Karnataka, celebrated with their traditional dances.

questions.text: Scissor style and Western Roll are the techniques used in:
questions.explanation: The scissors and the western roll are ways of clearing the bar in the high jump, as is the Fosbury flop used today.

questions.text: Match the following parties with their reserved symbols and choose the INCORRECT one among the following:
questions.explanation: The All India Trinamool Congress's symbol is 'flowers and grass', not a sickle. The BSP's elephant, the NPP's book and the NCP's clock are correct.

questions.text: Large tidal waves caused by an underwater earthquake or volcanic eruption are known as a _________.
questions.explanation: A tsunami is a series of huge sea waves set off by an undersea earthquake, volcanic eruption or landslide.

questions.text: Which of the following National Waterways (NW) is associated with the Udyogamandal and the Champakkara canals?
questions.explanation: National Waterway 3, the West Coast Canal in Kerala (Kollam to Kottapuram), includes the Champakara and Udyogamandal canals.

questions.text: Most of the Harappan sites are primarily divided into _________ parts.
questions.explanation: Harappan settlements such as Mohenjodaro were divided into two parts: a smaller but higher citadel and a much larger but lower town.

questions.text: On 19 July 2023, who was appointed as the 25th Director General of the Indian Coast Guard?
questions.explanation: On 19 July 2023 the Ministry of Defence announced Rakesh Pal's appointment as the 25th Director General of the Indian Coast Guard.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: With which of the following organisations was Henry Louis Vivian Derozio, a teacher of Hindu College of Calcutta, associated?
questions.explanation: Henry Louis Vivian Derozio, who taught at Hindu College, inspired the radical Young Bengal Movement among his students.

questions.text: Meher had two large chunks of coal. She set fire to the first chunk and broke the second one into pieces. Help Meher understand what kind of changes happened to the two chunks of coal at the end of the activity by choosing all the applicable statements. A. Both chunks of coal underwent physical changes only. B. The changes were reversible for the first chunk of coal only. C. Only physical changes took place for the second chunk of coal. D. Both chunks of coal underwent chemical changes only. E. The first case is an example of chemical changes.
questions.explanation: Burning turns coal into new substances such as ash and carbon dioxide, a chemical change that cannot be reversed (E); breaking the second chunk only changes its size, a physical change (C). A, B and D are false.

questions.text: With reference to provinces under Mauryan dynasty, which of the following pairs is correct?
questions.explanation: Tosali (Toshali) was the capital of the Mauryas' eastern province, Kalinga. Taxila was the northern capital, Ujjain the western (Avanti) and Suvarnagiri the southern.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: As a part of the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1922, the angry peasants had set ablaze the police station of which place?
questions.explanation: In February 1922 a crowd at Chauri Chaura, in Gorakhpur district, set the police station on fire; Gandhi then called off the Non-Cooperation Movement.

questions.text: Gangubai Hangal, a renowned Indian music personality, is recognised for her contributions in which of the following fields?
questions.explanation: Gangubai Hangal was a Hindustani classical vocalist of the Kirana gharana.

questions.text: What do you call the body cavity that is lined by mesoderm?
questions.explanation: The coelom is the body cavity lined by mesoderm; animals that have one are called coelomates.

questions.text: The God of Small Things is a novel authored by whom among the following authors?
questions.explanation: 'The God of Small Things' (1997), Arundhati Roy's first novel, won the Booker Prize.

questions.text: In which of the following empires of South India was the Kamalapuram tank built in the 15th century?
questions.explanation: The Kamalapuram tank, built in the early fifteenth century, was one of the major waterworks of the Vijayanagara empire, near its capital at Hampi.

questions.text: If labour is employed in a job but is not actually utilised for the production of goods and services, it is known as:
questions.explanation: In disguised unemployment more people are engaged in work than it needs, so taking some away would not reduce output.

questions.text: In basketball, how many points are awarded when a basket is scored from outside the 6.25-metre line?
questions.explanation: A basket scored from beyond the three-point line counts for three points. (Under FIBA's rules the line was 6.25 m from the basket until 2010; it is now 6.75 m.)

questions.text: What is the role of a commercial bank in the economy?
options: To provide financial services, such as accepting deposits, lending money and facilitating payments
To set interest rates for the entire banking system
questions.explanation: Commercial banks accept deposits, lend money and handle payments. Issuing currency, setting policy rates and regulating the money supply are the work of the central bank (the RBI in India).

questions.text: Select the option with the correctly spelt word to fill in the blank. The delta of river ____________ looks like a bird's foot because a lot of sediment is carried into the calm sea water.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'Mississippi', whose delta is the classic bird's-foot delta.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The irrational fear of snakes
questions.explanation: Ophidiophobia is the fear of snakes; xenophobia is fear of foreigners, necrophobia of death and nomophobia of being without a mobile phone.

questions.text: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks. Cuba is known as the sugar bowl of the world. It is part of the Caribbean _____________. This country _______________ a lot of sugar in the decade of 1960s.
questions.explanation: Cuba is part of the Caribbean 'region', and as the sugar bowl of the world it 'produced' a great deal of sugar.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Despite the challenges, / the team is determined to / completed / the project on time and within budget.
options: the project on time and within budget
questions.explanation: 'To' as part of an infinitive takes the base form of the verb: 'determined to complete the project'.

questions.text: Select the option that correctly rectifies the underlined spelling error in the given sentence. In the first half century after U.S. independence, a major “preportion” of the nation's labour force shifted from the agricultural to the manufacturing sector.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'proportion', a part or share of a whole.

questions.text: Select the grammatically correct sentence from the given options.
options: The responsibility was given to each student to keep quiet during the seminar.
The responsibility was given to each student to keep quieter during the seminar.
The responsibility is given to each student to keep quieter during the seminar.
The responsibility was give to each student to keep quieter during the seminar.
questions.explanation: 'Keep quiet' takes the plain adjective, since nothing is being compared; the other sentences use 'quieter', and one also has 'was give' for 'was given'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word in the context of the following sentence. We should go to the Himalayas this “spring”.
questions.explanation: Going to the Himalayas 'this spring' refers to the season; the other meanings of 'spring' do not fit.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'Assessment'.

questions.text: The given sentence is divided into four segments. Select the segment with the grammatical error. I was surprised / to see my / daughter, Manya, riding her / new bicycle confident.
questions.explanation: An adverb is needed to describe how she was riding: 'riding her new bicycle confidently'.

questions.text: Select the sentence that has a grammatical error.
options: We came in the meeting room quietly.
He came across an interesting article while researching.
The company came up with a brilliant marketing strategy.
She always comes down with a cold in winter.
questions.explanation: Movement to the inside of a place is 'into': 'We came into the meeting room quietly.' The others use 'come across', 'come up with' and 'come down with' correctly.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. How long have you been _________ these contact lenses?
questions.explanation: Contact lenses are worn: 'How long have you been wearing these contact lenses?'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The _________ model who can be selected for this advertisement is Meera Narayan.
questions.explanation: 'Best' is already the superlative of 'good'; 'most best', 'more better' and 'most good' are wrong forms.

questions.text: Identify the preposition that needs to be omitted to correct the sentence. They live near to the park.
questions.explanation: 'Near' is itself the preposition, so 'to' is redundant: 'They live near the park.'

questions.text: select the most appropriate idiom/phrase to fill in the blank and complete the sentence. It was all _________________. He did not really mean what he said.
options: a storm in a tea cup
questions.explanation: Something said 'tongue in cheek' is said ironically or as a joke, not meant seriously.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Ally
questions.explanation: An 'ally' is a friend or supporter; its opposite is an 'enemy'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. Ritu is a “diligent” girl who looks after her aged parents.
questions.explanation: 'Diligent' means careful and hardworking.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. Manisha “set apart” with her friends to explore the countryside.
questions.explanation: To 'set out' is to begin a journey; to 'set apart' is to make different from others.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word in the given sentence. The military operation was part of a “conspiracy” against national security.
questions.explanation: A 'conspiracy' is a secret plan to do harm: a 'plot'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word in the given sentence. I “agreed” with your assessment.
questions.explanation: To have 'agreed with' an assessment is to have shared and backed it: 'supported' it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom to replace the underlined segment in the given sentence. We were asked to vote for the candidates by “raising our hands to indicate voting for or against a proposition”.
questions.explanation: A 'show of hands' is a vote taken by raising hands.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A weed is an untamed plant that (1)______ where it is not wanted, usually among gardens or crops. The majority of weeds are (2)________. While some are toxic to horses and cattle, others harm mature crops by (3)________them of water, sunlight, soil and minerals. There are various ways that weeds (4)______. They are (5)_______ transported from one location to another as trash, dust or fodder.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: A weed 'spreads' where it is not wanted.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A weed is an untamed plant that (1)______ where it is not wanted, usually among gardens or crops. The majority of weeds are (2)________. While some are toxic to horses and cattle, others harm mature crops by (3)________them of water, sunlight, soil and minerals. There are various ways that weeds (4)______. They are (5)_______ transported from one location to another as trash, dust or fodder.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Most weeds are 'dangerous', that is harmful, as the next sentence shows: toxic to animals and harmful to crops. The other options are nouns.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A weed is an untamed plant that (1)______ where it is not wanted, usually among gardens or crops. The majority of weeds are (2)________. While some are toxic to horses and cattle, others harm mature crops by (3)________them of water, sunlight, soil and minerals. There are various ways that weeds (4)______. They are (5)_______ transported from one location to another as trash, dust or fodder.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: To 'deprive' something of a thing is to take it away: weeds harm crops by 'depriving them of water'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A weed is an untamed plant that (1)______ where it is not wanted, usually among gardens or crops. The majority of weeds are (2)________. While some are toxic to horses and cattle, others harm mature crops by (3)________them of water, sunlight, soil and minerals. There are various ways that weeds (4)______. They are (5)_______ transported from one location to another as trash, dust or fodder.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: Weeds 'propagate', that is spread and multiply, in various ways; 'extension' is a noun, and 'entertain' and 'breach' make no sense here.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A weed is an untamed plant that (1)______ where it is not wanted, usually among gardens or crops. The majority of weeds are (2)________. While some are toxic to horses and cattle, others harm mature crops by (3)________them of water, sunlight, soil and minerals. There are various ways that weeds (4)______. They are (5)_______ transported from one location to another as trash, dust or fodder.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: The adverb 'frequently' modifies 'transported': weeds are often carried from place to place.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: What sum (in ₹) will earn a simple interest of ₹360 in 2 years at 16% per year rate of interest?
A shopkeeper sold an article at a profit of 4%. If he had bought the article at 5% less and sold it at ₹30 more, then he would have made a profit of 12%. What is the cost price (in ₹) of the article?
questions.explanation: With cost price x, the selling price is 1.04x. Bought at 0.95x and sold at 1.04x + 30 for a 12% profit: 1.04x + 30 = 1.12 × 0.95x = 1.064x, so 0.024x = 30 and x = ₹1,250.

questions.text: The average weight of 14 persons out of 16 persons is 75 kg. The total weight of the remaining two persons is 48 kg more than the average weight of all 16 persons. Find the average weight of the remaining two persons.
questions.explanation: The 14 weigh 14 × 75 = 1,050 kg. If the average of all 16 is A, the other two weigh A + 48, so 16A = 1,050 + A + 48 and A = 73.2. The two weigh 121.2 kg, an average of 60.6 kg.

questions.text: What will be the average of the odd numbers from 1 to 51, both inclusive?
questions.explanation: The odd numbers from 1 to 51 are evenly spaced, so their average is (1 + 51)/2 = 26.

questions.text: Raghu lends ₹9,600 and ₹11,800 at simple interest to two different persons for the same time at the rate of 7% per annum and 8% per annum, respectively. If he had received ₹9,696 as total interest from both, find the time period for which the amounts were lent.
Find the ratio in which rice worth ₹7.20/kg should be mixed with rice worth ₹5.70/kg to produce a mixture worth ₹6.30/kg.

A man travelled from Tirupati to Tirumala at the speed of 20 km/h and walked back at the speed of 4 km/h. If the whole journey took 24 hours, then find the distance (in km) between Tirumala and Tirupati.
Aman, Bheema and Rehman play cricket, the ratio of Aman's runs to Bheema's runs and Bheema's runs to Rehman's runs is 5 : 4. They make together 549 runs. How many runs did Rehman make?
questions.explanation: A : B = 5 : 4 and B : C = 5 : 4, so A : B : C = 25 : 20 : 16, which sums to 61. 549/61 = 9, so Rehman made 16 × 9 = 144 runs.

questions.text: A spherical ball of iron is to be produced. If the radius of the ball is 3 cm and weight of iron per cm³ is 30g,what would be the weight of the ball?
questions.explanation: Volume = (4/3)π × 3³ = 36π cm³, so the ball weighs 36π × 30 = 1080π g.

questions.text: A policeman sees a thief at a distance of 50 m and starts chasing him at a speed of 7 m/s, while the thief runs at a speed of 5 m/s. What is the distance (in m) covered by the thief when he is caught?
questions.explanation: The policeman gains 7 − 5 = 2 m/s, so he closes the 50 m in 25 s. In that time the thief runs 5 × 25 = 125 m.

questions.text: A vendor bought a certain number of bananas at 6 for ₹5 and sold them at 4 for ₹3. Find his loss percentage.
questions.explanation: 12 bananas cost ₹10 and sell for ₹9: a loss of ₹1 on ₹10, or 10%.

questions.text: The salary of a worker is first increased by 30% and later reduced by 28.5%. What is the net change in his salary?
Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2500 as a sum borrowed at 8% per year rate of interest for 4 years.
The average of first 9 whole numbers is:
questions.explanation: The first 9 whole numbers are 0 to 8; their average is (0 + 8)/2 = 4.

questions.text: A banner at a garment shop advertises 'Buy 2 and get 5'. The shopkeeper has marked all the shirts at the same amount. Gaurav was his relative and the shopkeeper gave him an additional discount of 2% on the total bill. Gaurav purchased 5 shirts and paid ₹1,274. What is the marked price of each shirt?
questions.explanation: 'Buy 2 and get 5' means paying for 2 shirts and getting 5. With the extra 2% off, 2M × 0.98 = 1,274, so 2M = 1,300 and M = ₹650.

questions.text: 20 is related to 401 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 15 is related to 226. To which of the following is 18 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 - Operations on 13 such as adding / subtracting / multiplying, etc.. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each number is related to its square plus 1: 20² + 1 = 401 and 15² + 1 = 226. Likewise 18² + 1 = 325.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘JUGS’ is coded as ‘3715’ and ‘GOLD’ is coded as ‘6524’. What is the code for ‘G’ in that language?
questions.explanation: G is the only letter in both words and 5 the only digit in both codes, so G = 5.

questions.text: What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 2 ÷ 90 × 5 – 4 + 10 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 2 × 90 ÷ 5 + 4 − 10 = 36 + 4 − 10 = 30.

questions.text: What should come in place of question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? CEB, GHE, KKH, ONK, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move 4 places forward (C, G, K, O, so next S); second and third letters move 3 forward (E, H, K, N, so Q; B, E, H, K, so N): SQN.

questions.text: In a code language, 'PINK' is coded as ‘WFUH’ and 'DORM' is coded as ‘KLYJ’. How will 'BUGI' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +7, −3, +7, −3: PINK → WFUH and DORM → KLYJ. So BUGI → IRNF.

questions.text: Three statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered 1 and 2. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some Jeans are Pants; No Pant is a Shirt; Some Shirts are T-shirts Conclusions: 1. Some T-shirts are Shirts 2. Some T-shirts are Jeans
questions.explanation: 'Some Shirts are T-shirts' converts to 'some T-shirts are Shirts', so 1 follows. Nothing links T-shirts to Jeans, so 2 does not follow.

questions.text: HLTE is related to DHPA in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, VBNW is related to RXJS. To which of the following is MUXK related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 4 places back, wrapping round before A: HLTE → DHPA and VBNW → RXJS. So MUXK → IQTG.

questions.text: AFKO is related to CHMQ in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, ILRS is related to KNTU. To which of the following is BDGI related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places forward: AFKO → CHMQ and ILRS → KNTU. So BDGI → DFIK.

questions.text: Which of the following interchanges of signs would make the given equation correct? 96 × 8 − 15 ÷ 5 + 100 = 37
In a certain code language, ‘HOME’ is coded as ‘5317’ and ‘EAST’ is coded as ‘6528’.What is the code for ‘E’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: E is the only letter in both words and 5 the only digit in both codes, so E = 5.

questions.text: Seven people A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table, facing the center (but not necessarily in the same order). F is sitting second to the left of C. E is the immediate neighbour of A and C. G is sitting third to the right of D. What is the position of B with respect to G?
questions.explanation: Going round to each person's left (clockwise, as they face the centre) the order is C, G, F, B, D, A, E: F second to C's left, E between A and C, and G third to D's right. B is second to the left of G.

questions.text: 79 is related to 164 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 98 is related to 183. To which ofthe following is 112 related, following the same logic?(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbersinto its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: The second number is the first plus 85: 79 + 85 = 164 and 98 + 85 = 183. Likewise 112 + 85 = 197.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the following series? 4, 10, ?, 82, 244, 730, 2188
questions.explanation: Each term is 3 times the one before minus 2: 4 × 3 − 2 = 10, 10 × 3 − 2 = 28, 28 × 3 − 2 = 82, and so on to 2188.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All apples are mangoes. No mango is a kiwi. Conclusions: (I) No apple is a kiwi. (II) No kiwi is a mango.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusion I and II follow
questions.explanation: Every apple is a mango and no mango is a kiwi, so no apple is a kiwi (I). 'No mango is a kiwi' converts to 'no kiwi is a mango' (II). Both follow.

questions.text: A, B, C, D, E, F, and G, are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Only 3 people sit between E and F when counted from the right of E. A and D are both immediate neighbours of G. B sits immediate to the right of C. Only 1 person sits between B and D. How many people sit between A and E when counted from the right of A?
questions.explanation: Going round to each person's right (anticlockwise, as they face the centre) from E the order is E, D, G, A, F, C, B: three people between E and F, G between A and D, B to C's right and one person, E, between B and D. To the right of A come F, C and B before E: three.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a salient feature of Fundamental Duties of the Indian Constitution?
options: There is clear difference between Fundamental Rights and Fundamental Duties.
Fundamental Duties are both civic and moral in nature.
They are enforceable by law and can be challenged in court.
questions.explanation: The Fundamental Duties (Article 51A) are non-justiciable: no court can enforce them directly, so being enforceable and open to challenge in court is not one of their features.

questions.text: The oceanic trenches or the narrow depressions on the seafloor are formed by reason of:
questions.explanation: Oceanic trenches form where one tectonic plate sinks beneath another (subduction), as at the Mariana Trench.

questions.text: What are the three components of the empowerment model in SAPAP of SHGs?
options: Public resource allocation, capacity building, and microfinance
Social mobilisation, capital formation, and capacity building of the poor
Collective empowerment, capital formation, and poverty eradication
Social mobilisation, economic development, and education
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives social mobilisation, capital formation and capacity building of the poor. SAPAP, the UNDP-backed South Asia Poverty Alleviation Programme, organised the poor into self-help groups that build up their own savings and are trained to run them.

questions.text: According Census 2011 of India, which of the following union territories has the second highest literacy rate?
questions.explanation: In the 2011 Census Lakshadweep had the highest literacy rate among the union territories, and Daman and Diu (about 87%) the second highest.

questions.text: The Hindi novel 'Jhutha Sach' is written by:
questions.explanation: 'Jhutha Sach', a two-part Hindi novel about the Partition, was written by Yashpal.

questions.text: Harappa, one of the sites of the Harappan culture, was found in which of the following states of pre-independent India?
questions.explanation: Harappa, on the Ravi, lies in the old Montgomery district of Punjab (now Sahiwal, in Pakistan); Daya Ram Sahni excavated it in 1921.

questions.text: What is the term used for the line that a raider must cross to score points in Kabaddi?
questions.explanation: A raider must cross the baulk line in the opponents' half for the raid to count; the bonus line, further in, earns an extra point.

questions.text: Which of the following states has bicameral (two houses) state legislature?
questions.explanation: Six states have a Legislative Council as well as an Assembly: Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana and Uttar Pradesh. Punjab, Goa and West Bengal have only an Assembly.

questions.text: In the number 0.002609, the number of significant figures is ______.
questions.explanation: Leading zeros only place the decimal point and are not significant; 2, 6, 0 and 9 are, so there are four.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The Indian reformer Jyotirao Phule was primarily critical of which social evil of the Indian society?
questions.explanation: Jyotirao Phule fought caste discrimination above all: his 'Gulamgiri' (1873) attacked the caste system, and his Satyashodhak Samaj, founded the same year, worked for the lower castes.

questions.text: Which treatise of Indian classical music was composed by Pandit Sharanga Deva?
questions.explanation: Sharngadeva's 'Sangita Ratnakara', written in the 13th century, is a classic treatise on Indian music and dance.

questions.text: 'Attolu Eidu' is the cultural festival of which of the following union territories?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Lakshadweep, the union territory whose islanders, almost all of them Muslim, keep the Eid festivals as their chief celebrations.

questions.text: In which year did Rohan Bopanna become world number one in the Men's Doubles category of Lawn Tennis?
questions.explanation: Rohan Bopanna reached world No. 1 in men's doubles in January 2024, at 43 the oldest player to get there for the first time, and won the Australian Open with Matthew Ebden that month.

questions.text: Chand Minar at Daulatabad is a 210-feet-high tapering tower divided into _____ storeys.
questions.explanation: The Chand Minar, a 15th-century Bahmani victory tower at Daulatabad, rises in four storeys.

questions.text: Identify the personality on the basis of the given clues: i) She is an acclaimed Bharatanatyam dancer. ii) She is the recipient of Padma Shri 2016 award.
questions.explanation: Pratibha Prahlad, a Bharatanatyam dancer from Karnataka, received the Padma Shri in 2016.

questions.text: Which of the following folk dances is conducted during the Bwisagu Festival?
questions.explanation: Bagurumba is the Bodo dance performed at Bwisagu, the Bodo new-year festival in Assam.

questions.text: Which of the following rivers flows through Madhya Pradesh?
questions.explanation: The Betwa rises in Madhya Pradesh and flows into Uttar Pradesh to join the Yamuna. The Sharda runs along the India-Nepal border, the Bhima through Maharashtra and Karnataka, and the Shyok through Ladakh.

questions.text: On 10 April 2023, the Government of India launched tourism infrastructure and amenities in the __________________ villages through the ‘Vibrant Villages Programme’.
questions.explanation: The Vibrant Villages Programme, launched by Home Minister Amit Shah at Kibithoo in Arunachal Pradesh on 10 April 2023, develops villages along India's northern border.

questions.text: Who is National Security Advisor of India as of July 2023?
questions.explanation: Ajit Doval has been India's National Security Advisor since 2014.

questions.text: Which of the following is a natural indicator for acid and base?
questions.explanation: An indicator made from China rose (hibiscus) petals turns acids dark pink (magenta) and bases green.

questions.text: Which port situated at the head of Gulf of Kutch has helped to reduce the pressure at Mumbai port?
questions.explanation: Kandla, at the head of the Gulf of Kutch, was developed after Partition, when Karachi went to Pakistan, to ease the load on Mumbai port.

questions.text: Cyanobacteria belong to the domain of:
questions.explanation: Cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) photosynthesise and make their own food, so they are producers.

questions.text: According to National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2023 (A Progress Review), what is the percentage of the total population who are multidimensionally poor (Headcount Ratio) in Bihar state?
questions.explanation: NITI Aayog's National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2023 puts 33.76% of Bihar's population in multidimensional poverty in 2019-21, down from 51.89% in 2015-16.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM for the underlined word in the given sentence. He is a “lazy” person.
questions.explanation: 'Lazy' means unwilling to work; its opposite is 'hardworking'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word from the given sentence. The explorer's adventuros spirit led to the discovery of an ancient civilisation.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'adventurous'.

questions.text: In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative. Wolfia is the “tiny” plant in the world.
questions.explanation: 'The … in the world' compares one thing with all others, so the superlative is needed: 'the tiniest plant in the world'.

questions.text: Identify the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in brackets. Her candid remarks were a (refreshing) change from the usual diplomatic responses.
questions.explanation: 'Refreshing' means pleasantly new and different; its opposite is 'stale'. The other three are near-synonyms.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'abdomen'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. I started feeling tired as I had been working for a long time and so I decided to “call the day”.
questions.explanation: The idiom is 'call it a day': to stop working for the day.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error in phrasal verb. Gita got onto / the book / she was reading / this morning.
questions.explanation: 'Get onto' means to climb onto something or to contact someone; reading a book through is 'getting through' it (or, becoming absorbed in it, 'getting into' it).

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment without changing its meaning in the given sentence. Entrepreneurial “endeavours drive economic growth” and innovation, empowering individuals to bring their ideas to fruition.
questions.explanation: 'Ventures' are 'endeavours', to 'contribute to' something is near to 'driving' it, and 'flourishing' matches 'growth', so the meaning is kept; the others reverse it ('recession', 'discourage') or break the grammar ('pursuits manipulates').

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The farmer stood by the roadside stand to sell his _________.
questions.explanation: A farmer's 'produce' is what he grows, here sold at a roadside stand.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. I had to choose the “best of” the two options available.
questions.explanation: Between two, the comparative is used: 'the better of the two options'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Sree did not go to work today, as she was “feeling a bit under the weather.”
questions.explanation: To be 'under the weather' is to feel slightly ill.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. My mother said / that the thief / Ramesh will learnt / his lesson soon.
questions.explanation: 'Will' is followed by the base form of the verb: 'will learn', not 'will learnt'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Please turn off the lights _________ leaving the house.
questions.explanation: The lights go off ahead of leaving: 'before leaving the house'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The family members described their dream home's architectural “elegance”.
questions.explanation: 'Elegance' is refined grace; its opposite is 'coarseness'. 'Fortitude' is courage, and 'grandiosity' and 'gleam' are not opposites.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. After the match, / the stadium was the messiest / it’s ever been.
questions.explanation: 'It's' here stands for 'it has': 'the messiest it has ever been' is correct, so there is no error.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks. He is going to _________ the campaign against excessive use of _________ in local production units.
questions.explanation: 'Lead' fits both blanks: to 'lead' (head) the campaign, against the excessive use of 'lead', the toxic metal.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate adjective to fill in the blank. According to the chairman, his proposal was ___________ than Mr. Jackson’s.
questions.explanation: With 'than' the comparative is needed, and the comparative of 'bad' is 'worse'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. James is just an old “eccentric.”
questions.explanation: An 'eccentric' is an odd, unconventional person; 'cranky', in its sense of strange or odd, is the closest of the options.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Enlightenment, sometimes known as the ‘Age of Reason’, is described as the period of (1)________ scientific, political, and philosophical debate that characterised European culture (2) ________ the ‘long’ 18th century: from the late 17th century until the end of the Napoleonic Wars in 1815. This was an era of an enormous (3) ________ in thinking and reason, which historian Roy Porter describes as ‘decisive in the formation of modernity’. Centuries of custom and tradition were (4) ________ in favour of exploration, individuality, tolerance, and scientific (5) ________, all of which contributed to the formation of the ‘modern world’.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1..
questions.explanation: A period of 'rigorous', that is thorough and demanding, scientific, political and philosophical debate.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Enlightenment, sometimes known as the ‘Age of Reason’, is described as the period of (1)________ scientific, political, and philosophical debate that characterised European culture (2) ________ the ‘long’ 18th century: from the late 17th century until the end of the Napoleonic Wars in 1815. This was an era of an enormous (3) ________ in thinking and reason, which historian Roy Porter describes as ‘decisive in the formation of modernity’. Centuries of custom and tradition were (4) ________ in favour of exploration, individuality, tolerance, and scientific (5) ________, all of which contributed to the formation of the ‘modern world’.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2..
questions.explanation: The debate ran 'throughout' the long 18th century, from the late 17th century to 1815.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Enlightenment, sometimes known as the ‘Age of Reason’, is described as the period of (1)________ scientific, political, and philosophical debate that characterised European culture (2) ________ the ‘long’ 18th century: from the late 17th century until the end of the Napoleonic Wars in 1815. This was an era of an enormous (3) ________ in thinking and reason, which historian Roy Porter describes as ‘decisive in the formation of modernity’. Centuries of custom and tradition were (4) ________ in favour of exploration, individuality, tolerance, and scientific (5) ________, all of which contributed to the formation of the ‘modern world’.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3..
questions.explanation: The era saw an enormous 'shift', or change, in thinking and reason, which shaped modernity.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Enlightenment, sometimes known as the ‘Age of Reason’, is described as the period of (1)________ scientific, political, and philosophical debate that characterised European culture (2) ________ the ‘long’ 18th century: from the late 17th century until the end of the Napoleonic Wars in 1815. This was an era of an enormous (3) ________ in thinking and reason, which historian Roy Porter describes as ‘decisive in the formation of modernity’. Centuries of custom and tradition were (4) ________ in favour of exploration, individuality, tolerance, and scientific (5) ________, all of which contributed to the formation of the ‘modern world’.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4..
questions.explanation: Centuries of custom and tradition were 'discarded', thrown aside, in favour of exploration and tolerance.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Enlightenment, sometimes known as the ‘Age of Reason’, is described as the period of (1)________ scientific, political, and philosophical debate that characterised European culture (2) ________ the ‘long’ 18th century: from the late 17th century until the end of the Napoleonic Wars in 1815. This was an era of an enormous (3) ________ in thinking and reason, which historian Roy Porter describes as ‘decisive in the formation of modernity’. Centuries of custom and tradition were (4) ________ in favour of exploration, individuality, tolerance, and scientific (5) ________, all of which contributed to the formation of the ‘modern world’.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5..
questions.explanation: 'Scientific endeavour', that is scientific effort and inquiry, goes with exploration, individuality and tolerance.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: If the average of nine numbers is 360, then what is the sum of the nine numbers?
questions.explanation: Sum = average × count = 360 × 9 = 3,240.

questions.text: A money lender lent out ₹40,000 in two parts, one at 7% p.a. and the other at 6% p.a.. If the total annual simple interest on the amount is ₹2,550, what is the amount of money lent at 7%?

A bag contains coins of 1 rupee, 0.5 rupee and 0.25 rupee in the ratio of 5: 6: 8. If the total amount of money in the bag is ₹420, find the number of coins of type1 rupee, 0.5 rupee and 0.25 rupee are:
questions.explanation: Each set of 5, 6 and 8 coins is worth 5 × 1 + 6 × 0.5 + 8 × 0.25 = ₹10, so there are 420/10 = 42 sets: 5 × 42 = 210, 6 × 42 = 252 and 8 × 42 = 336 coins.

questions.text: If the price of a commodity is increased by 10% and 20% successively, what is the net percentage increase/decrease in its price, if it is further decreased by 25%?
questions.explanation: 1.1 × 1.2 × 0.75 = 0.99 of the original price: a net decrease of 1%.

questions.text: By selling an article for ₹19.5, a dealer makes a profit of 25%. By how much should he increase his selling price (in ₹) so as to make a profit of 50%?
questions.explanation: Cost price = 19.5/1.25 = ₹15.6. A 50% profit needs 15.6 × 1.5 = ₹23.4, so the price must rise by 23.4 − 19.5 = ₹3.9.

questions.text: Rahul sells an article at 8% above its cost price. If he had bought it at 5% less than what he had paid for it and sold it at ₹8 less, he would have gained 12%. Find the cost price of the article.
The average monthly pocket money of Ram and Shyam is ₹2,460, Shyam and Manohar is ₹2,380 and Manohar and Ram is ₹2,760. Find the monthly pocket money of Ram alone.
questions.explanation: The three pairs total ₹4,920, ₹4,760 and ₹5,520, which together count each person twice: 15,200/2 = ₹7,600 for all three. Ram = 7,600 − 4,760 (Shyam and Manohar) = ₹2,840.

questions.text: A thief is noticed by a policeman from a distance of 400 m. The thief starts running at a speed of 8 km/h and the policeman chases him at a speed of 9 km/h. What is the distance between them after 18 minutes?
questions.explanation: The policeman gains 9 − 8 = 1 km/h, so in 18 minutes (0.3 hour) he closes 0.3 km = 300 m of the 400 m gap, leaving 100 m.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2000 as a sum borrowed at 8% per year rate of interest for 6 years.
In Class I there are 12 students of average age 20 years, and in Class II there are 16 students of average age 23 years. What is the average age (approximately) of both the classes?
Two sections A and B of class VIII consist of 42 and 38 students, respectively. If the average marks of section A is 400 and that of section B is 320, find the average marks of the whole class.
What sum (in ₹) will earn a simple interest of ₹240 in 2 years at 4% per year rate of interest?
Three bells toll at intervals of 12, 15 and 18 minutes, respectively. If all the three bells toll together at 8 a.m., when will they toll together next?
questions.explanation: The bells toll together every LCM(12, 15, 18) = 180 minutes, that is 3 hours, so next at 11 a.m.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘−‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 102 − 36 + 59 ÷ 4 × 2 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 102 + 36 − 59 × 4 ÷ 2 = 102 + 36 − 118 = 20.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All doors are locks. Some doors are keys. Conclusions: (I) Some locks are keys. (II) Some keys are doors.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: The doors that are keys are also locks, so some locks are keys (I); 'some doors are keys' converts to 'some keys are doors' (II). Both follow.

questions.text: LJPN is related to SQWU in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, JHNL is related to QOUS. To which of the following is OMSQ related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 7 places forward: LJPN → SQWU and JHNL → QOUS. So OMSQ → VTZX.

questions.text: In a code language, 'XCMY' is coded as ‘AHPD’ and 'PGVK' is coded as ‘SLYP’. How will 'JOCH' be coded in that language?
