Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
questions.explanation: 'We have records of attacks': written accounts from the early 20th century to the 1950s.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Saltwater crocodiles are also known as estuarine crocodiles, as they (1)_____________ to live in mangrove-lined rivers. They’re the (2)_________________ living reptile, reaching up to seven metres in length: far larger than Indonesia’s famous Komodo dragon, which tops out at three metres. (3)______________________, crocodiles lived throughout the Indonesian archipelago. We have (4)_________________ of attacks on humans in Bali from the early 20th century and across much of Java until the 1950s. Even Indonesia’s capital, Jakarta, had crocodile’s (5)____________________in many rivers running through the city.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
questions.explanation: Jakarta had crocodiles in 'residence', that is living, in many of the rivers running through the city.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: The LCM of 3,4 and 5 is:
questions.explanation: 3, 4 and 5 have no common factor, so their LCM is their product: 3 × 4 × 5 = 60.

questions.text: A motor car starts with a speed of 60 km/h and increases its speed after every two hours by 15 km/h. In how much time will it cover a distance of 450 km?
questions.explanation: In the first two hours the car covers 2 × 60 = 120 km, in the next two 2 × 75 = 150 km and in the two after that 2 × 90 = 180 km: 450 km in 6 hours.

questions.text: In an election between two candidates, one person got 35% of the votes and lost by 6 votes. Assuming that there were no invalid votes, what was the total number of votes?
questions.explanation: The loser got 35% and the winner 65%, so the margin of 30% of the votes is 6 votes and the total is 6/0.3 = 20.

questions.text: By selling an article for ₹19.5, a dealer makes a profit of 30%. By how much should he increase his selling price (in ₹) so as to make a profit of 35%?
questions.explanation: Cost price = 19.5/1.3 = ₹15. At 35% profit the price is 15 × 1.35 = ₹20.25, an increase of ₹0.75.

questions.text: A chair was sold for ₹8,601 after giving two successive discounts of 8.5% and 6%. Find the marked price.
questions.explanation: The two discounts leave 0.915 × 0.94 = 0.8601 of the marked price, so the marked price is 8,601/0.8601 = ₹10,000.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3500 as a sum borrowed at 4% per year rate of interest for 3 years.

In a circular race of 1100 m, P and Q start from the same point, at the same time and at speeds of 36 km/h and 63 km/h, respectively. When will they meet again for the first time on the track if they are running in the opposite direction?
questions.explanation: 36 km/h = 10 m/s and 63 km/h = 17.5 m/s. Running in opposite directions they close the 1,100 m track at 27.5 m/s, so they first meet after 1,100/27.5 = 40 s.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3500 as a sum borrowed at 7% per year rate of interest for 5 years.

Sunita borrows ₹5,500 for 3 years at 6.5% per annum simple interest. She immediately lends it to Vedanshi at 9.3% per annum simple interest for 3 years. Find her gain (in ₹) in the transaction per year.
questions.explanation: She pays 6.5% and earns 9.3% on ₹5,500, a gain of 2.8% a year: 5,500 × 2.8/100 = ₹154.

questions.text: If the total surface area of a hemisphere is 192π cm², then the radius of the base of the hemisphere is:
questions.explanation: A hemisphere's total surface area is 2πr² + πr² = 3πr² = 192π, so r² = 64 and r = 8 cm.

questions.text: How much water should be added to a 30 l mixture of milk and water, which currently has a ratio of 7 : 3, so that the resultant mixture contains 40% water?
questions.explanation: The 30 l holds 21 l of milk and 9 l of water. For water to be 40%, the 21 l of milk must be 60% of the mixture, which is then 35 l: add 35 − 30 = 5 l of water.

questions.text: In a ration shop, there is a certain amount of cereals to distribute to 42 families for 15 days. If 48 kg of cereals can be distributed to 30 families for 7 days, then the quantity of cereals already in the shop was:
questions.explanation: 48 kg feeds 30 × 7 = 210 family-days, so 42 × 15 = 630 family-days need 48 × 630/210 = 144 kg.

questions.text: The average weight of a family of five members (in kg) whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 72 kg and 35 kg is:
The mean of five numbers is 55. If one of the numbers is excluded, the mean gets reduced by 5. Which of the following is the excluded number?
questions.explanation: The five numbers add up to 5 × 55 = 275 and the remaining four to 4 × 50 = 200, so the excluded number is 75.

questions.text: The average weight of a family of five members (in kg) whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 68 kg and 39 kg is:

A cylindrical glass with a diameter of 20 cm is having the juice to a height of 9 cm. An ice cube of size 8 cm is amerced in it completely. How much will the juice level rise in the glass? (Use π = 3.142 and answer correctly up to the nearest mm)
questions.explanation: The cube's volume, 8³ = 512 cm³, spreads over the glass's base of π × 10² = 314.2 cm², raising the juice by 512/314.2 = 1.63 cm: about 16 mm.

questions.text: In a code language, 'PRETTY' is written as 'BIVGGK' and 'JOYFUL' is written as 'OLBUFQ'. How will 'EXOTIC' be written in the same language?
questions.explanation: The first and last letters swap, then each letter is replaced by its opposite in the alphabet (A ↔ Z, B ↔ Y, ...): PRETTY → YRETTP → BIVGGK and JOYFUL → LOYFUJ → OLBUFQ. So EXOTIC → CXOTIE → XCLGRV.

questions.text: EJIA is related to FKJB in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, ZDCU is related to AEDV. To which of the following is OTSK related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 1 place forward (Z wraps round to A): EJIA → FKJB and ZDCU → AEDV. So OTSK → PUTL.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 110 + 54 × 9 − 13 ÷ 2 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 110 − 54 ÷ 9 + 13 × 2 = 110 − 6 + 26 = 130.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 9, 45, 225, 1125, 5625, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is 5 times the one before: 5,625 × 5 = 28,125.

questions.text: Seven friends - Asha, Sreeja, Mamata, Ramya, Hema, Jaya, and Mohini - are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Ramya is sitting fourth to the right of Asha. Mamata sits third to the left of Ramya. Jaya has Sreeja and Mamata as immediate neighbours. Hema is sitting to the immediate right of Ramya. Who is sitting second to the left of Mohini?
questions.explanation: Going round to the left from Asha the order is Asha, Mohini, Hema, Ramya, Sreeja, Jaya, Mamata: Ramya is fourth to Asha's right, Mamata third to Ramya's left, Hema to Ramya's immediate right, and Jaya sits between Sreeja and Mamata. Second to the left of Mohini is Ramya.

questions.text: MIPL is related to OKRN in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, PLSO is related to RNUQ. To which of the following is HDKG related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places forward: MIPL → OKRN and PLSO → RNUQ. So HDKG → JFMI.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 62 − 36 + 18 ÷ 6 × 3 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 62 + 36 − 18 × 6 ÷ 3 = 62 + 36 − 36 = 62.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the following series based on the English alphabetical order? RJX, PNV, NRT, LVR ,?
questions.explanation: First letters move back 2 (R, P, N, L, so J), second letters forward 4 (J, N, R, V, so Z) and third letters back 2 (X, V, T, R, so P): JZP.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All Excels are Words. All Words are PowerPoints. Conclusions: (I) All PowerPoints are Excels. (II) At least some Words are Excels.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusion I and II follow
questions.explanation: 'All Excels are Words' converts to 'some Words are Excels', so II follows. All Excels being PowerPoints does not make every PowerPoint an Excel, so I does not follow.

questions.text: D, E, F, L, R, S and T are sitting around a circular table facing the centre(but not necessarily in the same order). R sits second to the right of D. L sits to the immediate left of D. T sits third to the left of L. F sits third to the left of S. Neither E nor S is an immediate neighbour of R. What is the position of S with respect to R?
questions.explanation: Going round to the left from D the order is D, L, E, S, T, R, F. R is second to D's right, L to D's immediate left and T third to L's left; F, third to the left of S, must take the seat next to R, since neither E nor S may, which puts S between E and T. S is second to the right of R.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘LINK’ is coded as ‘4175’ and ‘NICK’ is coded as ‘7419’. What is the code for ‘C’ in the given language?
questions.explanation: I, N and K are in both words, as are 4, 7 and 1 in both codes. The letter left in NICK is C and the digit left in its code is 9, so C = 9.

questions.text: 35 is related to 105 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 51 is related to 153. To which of the following is 72 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding / subtracting / multiplying, etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each number is related to 3 times itself: 35 × 3 = 105 and 51 × 3 = 153. Likewise 72 × 3 = 216.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the statement(s). Statements: All bats are mammals. No mammal is a fish. Conclusions: (I) No bat is a fish. (II) Some fishes are mammals.
questions.explanation: All bats are mammals and no mammal is a fish, so no bat is a fish (I). 'No mammal is a fish' rules out II.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘VOLT’ is coded as ‘5731’ and ‘LEAD’ is coded as ‘4186’. What is the code for ‘L’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: L is the only letter in both words and 1 the only digit in both codes, so L = 1.

questions.text: In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 25, 77; 28, 86
questions.explanation: The second number is 3 times the first plus 2: 25 × 3 + 2 = 77 and 28 × 3 + 2 = 86. Likewise 34 × 3 + 2 = 104.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: When was the first-round table Conference started by the British Government in London?
questions.explanation: The First Round Table Conference opened in London on 12 November 1930 and ran until January 1931; the Congress stayed away.

questions.text: Who is literate according to the Census of India?
options: A person above 5 years of age, who can read and write with understanding in any language.
A person above 7 years of age, who can read and write with understanding in any language.
A person above 18 years of age, who can read and write with understanding in any language.
A person above 14 years of age, who can read and write with understanding in any language.
questions.explanation: The Census counts a person aged seven or above who can both read and write with understanding in any language as literate.

questions.text: Rank the following states in ascending order, based on their population density, as per Census 2011. Tripura, Meghalaya, Manipur, Nagaland
questions.explanation: SSC's key follows the Census 2011 densities (persons per km²) of Nagaland 119, Manipur 128, Meghalaya 132 and Tripura 350. (Some tables give Manipur 115, leaving out three subdivisions of Senapati district, which would put it first, an order no option offers.)

questions.text: Who does NOT fall under the executive of the Indian Union?
questions.explanation: The Union executive includes the President and the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister. The Chief Justice of India heads the judiciary.

questions.text: 'Rajatarangini', a vivid account of the kings of Kashmir, was composed by Kalhana in the ______ language.
questions.explanation: Kalhana wrote the 'Rajatarangini' in Sanskrit verse in the 12th century.

questions.text: 'The Climate Smart Cities Assessment Framework 2.0' is to evaluate how many cities across India?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 100: the framework was set up under the Smart Cities Mission to benchmark the climate actions of its 100 Smart Cities, and the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs launched version 2.0 in September 2020. (Its 2020 assessment in fact covered 126 cities, the 100 Smart Cities among them.)

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The East India Company lost all its administrative powers with the enforcement of ___________.
questions.explanation: The Government of India Act, 1858, passed after the revolt of 1857, ended the Company's rule and transferred the government of India to the Crown.

questions.text: In which state of India is the Telaiya dam located?
questions.explanation: The Tilaiya (Telaiya) dam, the first dam of the Damodar Valley Corporation, is on the Barakar river in Koderma district, Jharkhand.

questions.text: When a river reaches a low lying plain, it continues erosion of soil as well as deposition and as a result of both these factors another river channel develops and later it is detached from the main river forming a U-shaped lake; this is called:
questions.explanation: A meander cut off from the main channel by erosion and deposition forms an oxbow lake.

questions.text: Which of the following awards and recognitions was NOT received by Vempati Chinna Satyam?
questions.explanation: The Kuchipudi guru Vempati Chinna Satyam received the Padma Bhushan (1998), not the Padma Shri; the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, the Kalidas Samman and an honorary doctorate were among his other honours.

questions.text: As of February 2023, who is the Union Minister of Road Transport and Highways?
questions.explanation: Nitin Gadkari has been Union Minister of Road Transport and Highways since 2014.

questions.text: The autobiography of which of the following famous Indian musicians is titled ‘My Life, My Music’?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Ravi Shankar, the sitar maestro, whose 1968 autobiography is 'My Music, My Life' (the question has the title the other way round).

questions.text: Which of the following dances is performed in Goa during the festival Ganesh Chaturthi?
questions.explanation: Fugdi, danced by Goan women in circles or rows to singing and clapping, is traditionally performed during Ganesh Chaturthi.

questions.text: Sultan Ghari tomb is situated to west of the Qutub in Delhi is like a fortress within a walled enclosure with bastions on the comers, with its ____________ grave chamber underground.
questions.explanation: Sultan Ghari, built by Iltutmish in 1231-32 for his son Nasiruddin Mahmud, has an octagonal grave chamber below ground, whose roof forms an octagonal platform in the courtyard.

questions.text: The official journey of 'Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav' commenced on:
questions.explanation: Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav began on 12 March 2021, the anniversary of the Dandi March, starting a 75-week countdown to the 75th anniversary of independence on 15 August 2022.

questions.text: Which of the following is the role of fibre in the diet?
questions.explanation: Dietary fibre (roughage) adds bulk to food, helping digestion and the regular passage of stools.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the contingency fund of India?
options: Allowances and emoluments of the President are charged under it.
It is issued on behalf of the President of India.
questions.explanation: The President's emoluments and allowances are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India (Article 112), not the Contingency Fund. The Contingency Fund, set up under Article 267 for unforeseen expenditure, is held at the President's disposal.

questions.text: Which of the following is a unitary feature of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: Single citizenship is a unitary feature; the division of powers, bicameralism and a written constitution are federal ones.

questions.text: A three-time Olympian, PT Usha broke the Asian Games record in four events (200 m, 400 m, 400 m hurdles and 4 × 400 m relay) in ____________.
questions.explanation: At the 1986 Asian Games in Seoul PT Usha won gold in the 200 m, 400 m, 400 m hurdles and 4 × 400 m relay, setting Games records in each, and silver in the 100 m.

questions.text: Fa-Hsien, a Chinese Buddhist Pilgrim, began his journey back home (China) from ________.
questions.explanation: Fa-Hien sailed home from Tamralipti, the port in Bengal, by way of Sri Lanka.

questions.text: In which of the following states can the 'Loo' phenomenon be observed?
questions.explanation: The loo is the hot, dry wind that blows over north and north-western India, Rajasthan among them, in May and June.

questions.text: At which Olympic games did India receive its first Olympic medal in a shooting event?
questions.explanation: Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore won silver in the men's double trap at Athens 2004, India's first Olympic medal in shooting.

questions.text: Lalita J Rao is associated with which of the following gharanas?
questions.explanation: Lalith (Lalita) J. Rao was a Hindustani vocalist of the Agra gharana, a disciple of Ustad Khadim Hussain Khan.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Frugal
questions.explanation: 'Frugal' means sparing with money; its opposite is 'profligate', recklessly extravagant. 'Thrifty' is a synonym.

questions.text: Select the sentence that has a grammatical error.
options: It was a huge zoo with an elephant enclosure.
Suhas has a younger brother and an elder sister.
He was an honest engineer by profession.
Alka bought new pair of shoes for the party.
questions.explanation: 'Pair' is a singular countable noun and needs an article: 'Alka bought a new pair of shoes for the party.'

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'admitted': the 't' is doubled before '-ed'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The athletes / trained tirelessness / to prepare for / the upcoming competition.
questions.explanation: The verb 'trained' needs an adverb, 'tirelessly', not the noun 'tirelessness'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The storm caused extensive damage to homes, ___________ many families homeless.
questions.explanation: A present participle introduces the result: 'caused extensive damage to homes, leaving many families homeless'.

questions.text: Select the correct spelling of the incorrectly spelt word in the given sentence. He was suspended from the party due to his suspiscious activities.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'suspicious'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The elusive moon peeked from behind the clouds, “illuminating the earth with” its gentle glow.
questions.explanation: 'Illuminating' means 'lighting up', so 'lighting up the earth with its gentle glow' keeps the meaning; the other options change it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Grease someone's palm
questions.explanation: To 'grease someone's palm' is to bribe them.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Hermetic
questions.explanation: Besides 'airtight', 'hermetic' means obscure and understood only by a few: 'esoteric'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. She is learning / to play the guitar / to pursue her passion / for the music.
questions.explanation: Music in general takes no article: 'her passion for music'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Ambrosial
questions.explanation: 'Ambrosial' means exceptionally pleasing in taste or smell; its opposite is 'malodorous', foul-smelling.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical/spelling error. He was lying at / his bed when he / saw the snake entering / through the window.
questions.explanation: One lies 'in' or 'on' a bed, not 'at' it: 'He was lying in his bed'. (The sheet prints this option as 'He way lying at'.)

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. she had “garnered” the information from various books.
questions.explanation: To 'garner' is to gather or collect; its opposite is 'dispersed', scattered.

questions.text: Select the correct idiom to substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence. His remarks “made the matter worse.”
options: Killed two birds with one stone
questions.explanation: To 'add fuel to the fire' is to make a bad situation worse.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. He is / an expert / in / an English literature.
questions.explanation: Names of languages and subjects take no article: 'an expert in English literature'.

questions.text: Select the option that rectifies the INCORRECT spelling in the given sentence. Pleasee allow me to start.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'please'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Do you know the purpose of a fire extinguisher? It helps to “put up with” an engulfing fire, in case of an emergency.
questions.explanation: To 'put out' a fire is to extinguish it; to 'put up with' something is to tolerate it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined phrase. Those who have died cannot be “brought back to life”.
questions.explanation: To 'resurrect' is to bring back to life.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. A raven, which you know is black as coal, was envious of the swan, because her “feathers are as white as” the purest snow.
questions.explanation: The plural 'feathers' needs a plural verb, and the past 'was envious' calls for the past tense: 'her feathers were as white as'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Vivid
questions.explanation: 'Vivid' means intensely bright or clear: 'bright'. 'Dull' is its opposite.

Khashaba Jadhav was the independent India's first individual olympic medallist. There (1) _________ some firsts that stay in history forever. The one held by Khashaba Jadhav is one such first. He might have been referred to as the Pocket Dynamo, but his deeds dwarfed those of far (2) _________ athletes in his sport. markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: The average of 41 numbers is 62. The average of the first 18 numbers is 65.5, and the average of the last 24 numbers is 61.5. If the 18th number from the beginning is excluded, then what is the average of the remaining numbers?
questions.explanation: The 41 numbers total 41 × 62 = 2,542. The first 18 total 18 × 65.5 = 1,179 and the last 24 total 24 × 61.5 = 1,476; together they count the 18th number twice, so it is 1,179 + 1,476 − 2,542 = 113. The other 40 average (2,542 − 113)/40 = 60.725.

questions.text: A girl spends 76% of her income. If her income increases by 18% and her expenditure increases by 25%, then what is the percentage increase or decrease in her savings? (Correct to one decimal place)
questions.explanation: On an income of 100 she spends 76 and saves 24. Now her income is 118 and her spending 76 × 1.25 = 95, so she saves 23: a fall of 1/24 ≈ 4.2%.

questions.text: An ice-cream cone with a lid has a total surface area equal to the area of another circle of certain radius. If the radius of the circle is equal to average of the slant height and the radius of the cone, then the ratio of the slant height of the cone to the radius of the circle is:
questions.explanation: With a lid the cone's total surface area is πr(l + r). Setting it equal to πR² with R = (l + r)/2 gives (l + r)²/4 = r(l + r), so l + r = 4r: l = 3r and R = 2r. l : R = 3 : 2.

questions.text: The difference between successive discounts of 28% followed by 25% and 10% followed by 5% on the marked price of a pen is ₹63. The marked price of the pen is:
questions.explanation: 28% then 25% leaves 0.72 × 0.75 = 0.54 of the price (46% off); 10% then 5% leaves 0.9 × 0.95 = 0.855 (14.5% off). The difference, 31.5% of the marked price, is ₹63, so the price is ₹200.

questions.text: Find the LCM of 120, 200 and 225.
A boat is rowed down along a river 21km in 3 hours and against a river 14km in 7 hours. Find the speed of the boat and the river.
questions.explanation: Downstream speed = 21/3 = 7 km/h and upstream speed = 14/7 = 2 km/h. Boat = (7 + 2)/2 = 4.5 km/h and river = (7 − 2)/2 = 2.5 km/h.

questions.text: A train moving at the same speed passes two bridges of length 900 m and 486 m in 110 seconds and 70 seconds, respectively. The length of the train (in m) is:
Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3500 as a sum borrowed at 4% per year rate of interest for 2 years.

A hemispherical bowl with an internal radius of 27 cm is full of liquid. The liquid is to be filled into cylindrical shaped bottles of diameter 12 cm and height 13.5 cm. The number of bottles required to empty the bowl is:
questions.explanation: The bowl holds (2/3)π × 27³ = 13,122π cm³ and each bottle (radius 6 cm) π × 6² × 13.5 = 486π cm³. 13,122 ÷ 486 = 27.

questions.text: The average weight of 11 persons is increased by 4.5 kg when one of them, whose weight is 50.5 kg, is replaced by a new person. The weight of the new person is:
questions.explanation: The total rises by 11 × 4.5 = 49.5 kg, so the new person weighs 50.5 + 49.5 = 100 kg.

questions.text: The average of five numbers is 62. The average of the first two numbers is 48 and that of the last two numbers is 52. What is the third number?
questions.explanation: The five total 5 × 62 = 310; the first two total 96 and the last two 104, so the third is 310 − 96 − 104 = 110.

questions.text: What sum (in ₹) will earn a simple interest of ₹240 in 2 years at 8% per year rate of interest?
What should be added to each of the four numbers 5, 19, 7 and 25 to make them proportional?

A, B, C, D, E, F, and G are sitting around a circular table, facing away from the centre (but not necessarily in the same order).Only 2 people sit between A and D when counted from the right of D.B and C are both immediate neighbours of G.F sits to the immediate left of E.Only 1 person sits between C and E when counted from the left of C. How many people are sitting between G and D when counted from the right of G?
questions.explanation: Facing outwards, each person's right is clockwise. The clues fit only one order, clockwise: D, F, E, A, C, G, B. Counting from G to the right comes B and then D, so one person sits between them.

questions.text: RXPL is related to OUMI in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, TZRN is related to QWOK. To which of the following is PVNJ related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places back: R → O, X → U, P → M, L → I, and likewise TZRN → QWOK. So PVNJ → MSKG.

questions.text: 4 is related to 17 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 5 is related to 26. To which of the following is 10 related following the same logic?(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbersinto its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: Each number is related to its square plus 1: 4² + 1 = 17 and 5² + 1 = 26. So 10² + 1 = 101.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 69 – 24 ÷ 4 × 6 + 13 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 69 + 24 × 4 ÷ 6 − 13 = 69 + 16 − 13 = 72.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘have good food’ is coded as ‘ti ma ka’ and ‘nutritious food healthy’ is coded as ‘ka lu pe’. How is ‘food’ coded in the given language?
questions.explanation: 'food' is the only word in both phrases and 'ka' the only code in both, so food = ka.

questions.text: ‘4KC2’ is related to ‘6MA4’ in a certain way. In the same way, ‘3MN4’ is related to ‘5OL6’. To which of the following is ‘5NO3’ related following the same logic?
questions.explanation: The digits rise by 2, the first letter moves 2 places forward and the second 2 places back: 4KC2 → 6MA4 and 3MN4 → 5OL6. So 5NO3 → 7PM5.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the following series? 800, 700, 600, 500, 400, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is 100 less than the one before: 400 − 100 = 300.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘LIVE’ is coded as ‘2648’ and ‘EAST’ is coded as ‘3215’. What is the code for ‘E’ in that language?
questions.explanation: E is the only letter in both words and 2 the only digit in both codes, so E = 2.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts,decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All gardens are museums. All museums are parks. Conclusions: (I) Some museums are gardens. (II) All gardens are parks.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: All gardens are museums, so some museums are gardens (I). All gardens are museums and all museums are parks, so all gardens are parks (II). Both follow.

questions.text: Four number triads have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the number triad that is different from the rest. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In the other triads the second number is twice the first and the third is the square of the second: 16² = 256, 6² = 36, 10² = 100. But 18² = 324, not 320.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the statement(s). Statements: Some desktops are monitors. No monitor is a television. Conclusions: (I) Some desktops are televisions. (II) Some monitors are desktops.
questions.explanation: 'Some desktops are monitors' means some monitors are desktops (II). The desktops that are monitors cannot be televisions, and nothing says any other desktop is one, so I does not follow.

questions.text: Sunita, Lokesh, Babita, Isha, Akram, Alok and Kiran are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Sunita is an immediate neighbour of Babita. Lokesh sits 2nd to the right of Babita. Isha sits 4th to the right of Akram. Alok sits 3rd to the right of Lokesh. Isha sits 2nd to the left of Alok. Who sits third to the right of Babita?
questions.explanation: Counting places to the right from Babita: Lokesh is 2nd, Alok 5th (3rd to Lokesh's right), Isha 3rd (2nd to Alok's left) and Akram 6th (Isha is 4th to his right). Sunita, Babita's neighbour, takes the 1st place and Kiran the 4th. Third to Babita's right is Isha.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the following series based on the English alphabetical order? ISC, GPF, EMI, CJL, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move 2 back (I, G, E, C, A), second letters 3 back (S, P, M, J, G) and third letters 3 forward (C, F, I, L, O): AGO.

questions.text: iGOT Karmayogi is an integrated online training platform to provide continuous learning opportunities to ______________ in order to upgrade their skills.
questions.explanation: iGOT (Integrated Government Online Training) Karmayogi, under Mission Karmayogi, is the online learning platform for building the capacity of civil servants.

questions.text: ‘Dashain’ and ‘Tihar’ are popular festivals of which neighbouring country of India?
questions.explanation: Dashain and Tihar (the Nepali festival of lights) are the main Hindu festivals of Nepal.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a private sector Industry?
questions.explanation: TISCO (now Tata Steel), a Tata Group company, is privately owned. SAIL, LIC and BHEL are owned by the Government of India.

questions.text: Which of the following countries won the maximum number of T20 Women's Cricket World Cup titles?
questions.explanation: By 2024 Australia had won the Women's T20 World Cup six times (2010, 2012, 2014, 2018, 2020 and 2023), more than any other side.

questions.text: All natural earthquakes take place in the:
questions.explanation: All natural earthquakes take place in the lithosphere, the rigid outer layer of the Earth made up of the crust and the uppermost mantle.

questions.text: In February 2024, who was sworn in as the first woman Chief Justice of the Uttarakhand High Court?
questions.explanation: Justice Ritu Bahri, earlier of the Punjab and Haryana High Court, became the first woman Chief Justice of the Uttarakhand High Court.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following Acts provided for a system of tribunals and a ban on strikes?
questions.explanation: The Trade Disputes Act, 1929 set up courts of inquiry and boards of conciliation to settle industrial disputes and made strikes in public utility services illegal without advance notice.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT the principle laid down by the OECD about budgetary governance?
options: Design the capital budgeting framework to meet national development needs.
Alignment of budgets with medium-term strategic priorities of the government.
It does not allow the citizen to participate in budgetary debates.
The execution of the budget must be proactively planned, managed, and monitored.
questions.explanation: The OECD's 2015 Recommendation on Budgetary Governance calls for an inclusive, participative and realistic debate on budget choices, so shutting citizens out of budget debates goes against it. The other three are among its principles.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Epic Poem, Savitri, described by its author as ‘A Legend and a Symbol’, was written by _____.
questions.explanation: Sri Aurobindo (Aurobindo Ghosh) wrote 'Savitri: A Legend and a Symbol', an epic poem in blank verse on the story of Savitri and Satyavan.

questions.text: Which chronicler of the medieval age recognised that Raziyya was more able and qualified than all her brothers?
questions.explanation: Minhaj-i-Siraj, a chronicler of the Delhi Sultanate, recognised Raziyya's ability, though he was uneasy at having a queen as ruler.

questions.text: Which of the following fields is NOT covered by the National Eminence Award?
options: Music of all forms and origin
questions.explanation: The National Eminence Award of the Sri Shanmukhananda Fine Arts and Sangeetha Sabha, Mumbai, set up in 2002, honours music of all forms and origin, dance, theatre and fine arts administrators. Literature is not one of its fields.

questions.text: Which specific chemical can be applied to achieve staining of chromosomes?
questions.explanation: Acetocarmine stains chromosomes, which is why it is used to study cell division, for example in onion root tips.

questions.text: Which track and field event has a water jump?
questions.explanation: The steeplechase (usually over 3000 m) has barriers and a water jump on each full lap.

questions.text: According to the Census of India 2011, what is the population density of India?
questions.explanation: The 2011 Census put India's population density at 382 persons per km².

questions.text: Which of the following Indian tribal dances is prevalent in the Araku Valley near Visakhapatnam?
questions.explanation: Dhimsa is a dance of the tribal communities of the Araku Valley in Andhra Pradesh; Bardo Chham belongs to Arunachal Pradesh and Bagurumba to the Bodos of Assam.

questions.text: Which Article of the Indian Constitution has provisions for the appointment of High Court Judges?
questions.explanation: Article 217 deals with the appointment and conditions of office of a Judge of a High Court.

questions.text: In which of the following years did Alexander invade Punjab and in which of the following years did he die?
questions.explanation: Alexander crossed into Punjab in 326 BC, defeating Porus at the Hydaspes (Jhelum), and died at Babylon in 323 BC.

questions.text: Carnatic singer Bombay Jayashri has been selected for which music award in 2023?
questions.explanation: The Music Academy, Madras chose Bombay Jayashri for its Sangita Kalanidhi, the highest honour in Carnatic music, in 2023.

questions.text: JJ Thomson is known for developing which model in 1898?
questions.explanation: Thomson pictured the atom as a sphere of positive charge with electrons embedded in it, like plums in a pudding. The gold foil experiment was Rutherford's and the oil drop experiment Millikan's.

questions.text: Right of a prisoner to speedy trial will be categorised in which of the following Fundamental Rights?
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court has held the right to a speedy trial to be part of the right to life and personal liberty under Article 21 (Hussainara Khatoon v. State of Bihar).

questions.text: The Zaskar and the Nubra are tributaries of which river?
questions.explanation: The Zaskar and the Nubra are tributaries of the Indus, as are the Shyok, the Gilgit, the Hunza and the Dras.

questions.text: In which of the following states is Aoleang Monyü celebrated, which is an ancient spring festival celebrated by all Konyaks in the month of April?
questions.explanation: Aoleang Monyü, the spring festival of the Konyak Nagas, is celebrated in Nagaland's Mon district in the first week of April.

questions.text: ‘Once a Dancer’ is the autobiography of ________________.
questions.explanation: 'Once a Dancer' (1997) is the autobiography of Allegra Kent, a ballerina of the New York City Ballet.

questions.text: If after being bitten by a mosquito, the person is detected as being malaria positive, which of the following will hold true? A. The person did not have a balanced diet. B. The mosquito was carrying plasmodium. C. The mosquito was suffering from malaria. D. The person was not vaccinated as a child.
questions.explanation: Malaria is caused by the Plasmodium parasite, which the female Anopheles mosquito carries, so B must hold. The mosquito does not itself suffer from the disease, and a positive test says nothing about the person's diet or childhood vaccinations.

questions.text: Who excavated the Chira Tope stupa at Taxila?
questions.explanation: Sir John Marshall, Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India, excavated Taxila, including the Dharmarajika stupa known as Chir Tope.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The teacher encouraged students to cultivate a __________ attitude towards learning, embracing challenges as opportunities for growth.
questions.explanation: 'Resilient' means able to recover from difficulties, which fits treating challenges as chances to grow; the other options are negative.

questions.text: In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative. When they left for Mexico, their house was in “good” condition than it is now.
questions.explanation: 'Than' calls for the comparative: 'in better condition than it is now'.

questions.text: In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Below are given alternatives to the underlined part. Select the correct alternative. Kanha National Park in MP is the “dense” forest in India.
questions.explanation: 'The … forest in India' calls for the superlative, and one-syllable 'dense' takes '-est': 'the densest forest'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate adjective to fill in the blank. The Nile is the _________ river in the world.
questions.explanation: Comparison with every river in the world calls for the superlative: 'the longest river'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The government is developing a new test “in the recruitment and training of teachers” in the upcoming session.
options: of the recruitment and training of teachers
for the recruitment and training of teachers
in recruitment and training on teachers
for recruitment or training of teachers
questions.explanation: A test is developed 'for' a purpose: 'a new test for the recruitment and training of teachers'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate phrase that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The question paper was “very easy to complete”.
questions.explanation: 'A piece of cake' is something very easy.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word in the context of the following sentence. The “palm” is a native of Malaysia. We can find them in groves.
questions.explanation: Here 'palm' is the tree: palms grow in groves. The palm of the hand is another meaning.

questions.text: Select the option that rectifies the spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence. How can one justify sending sound waves into space when they cannot travel through a “vacum”?
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'vacuum'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. The car, with all “its features, were meticulously” designed.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'The car'; 'with all its features' does not make it plural, so 'was meticulously designed'. 'It's' means 'it is'.

questions.text: Select the appropriate synonym of the underlined word. The bride has an “exquisite” face.
questions.explanation: 'Exquisite' means extremely beautiful.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Preserve
questions.explanation: To 'preserve' something is to keep it as it is: to 'maintain' it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank. We hear the judges from their ________ that only CNG buses should run in Delhi.
questions.explanation: An 'ivory tower' is a place of privileged seclusion, cut off from everyday realities, from which such a pronouncement is made.

questions.text: Identify the sentence with an error in the use of simple present tense.
options: He go to school every day.
questions.explanation: With 'he' the simple present takes the third-person singular form: 'He goes to school every day.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word. He took the “right” decision at that time.
questions.explanation: Here 'right' means correct: he made the correct decision.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. She received / an award / for her work / in a engineering field.
questions.explanation: 'An' comes before a vowel sound: 'in an engineering field'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. Her fear of public speaking was a major “hurdle” in her career.
questions.explanation: A 'hurdle' is a difficulty to be overcome: an 'obstacle'.

questions.text: In the given sentence, one of the four underlined words is incorrectly spelt. Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word. The scientific “community” gave “credance” to the new research findings after “rigorous” testing and “validation”.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'credence' (belief or acceptance).

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. There is only one way / to have a happier marred life / and I will learn it soon.
options: to have a happier marred life
and I will learn it soon.
questions.explanation: 'Marred' means spoiled; the sense calls for 'married': 'a happier married life'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the following sentence. The restaurant's specialtiy is seafood.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'specialty' (or 'speciality').

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. How environmental problems ____1_____ different groups is a function of social inequality. Social status and power determine the _______2____ to which people can insulate themselves from environmental crises or overcome them. In some cases, their ‘solutions’ may actually worsen environmental disparities. In Kutch, Gujarat, where water is scarce, richer farmers have ____3____ in deep bore tubewells to tap groundwater to irrigate their fields and grow cash crops. When the rains fail, the earthen wells of the poorer villagers run dry and they do not even have water to drink. At such times, the moist green fields of the rich farmers seem to mock them. Certain environmental concerns sometimes appear to be universal concerns, not particular to ____4_____ social groups. For instance, ______5_______ air pollution or protecting biodiversity seems to be in the public interest. A sociological analysis shows, however, that how public priorities are set and how they are pursued may not be universally beneficial.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: How environmental problems 'affect' different groups: 'affect' is the verb, 'effect' usually a noun.
