markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2500 as a sum borrowed at 6% per year rate of interest for 6 years.
There are five persons with weights 58 kg, 38 kg, 45 kg, 34 kg and 55 kg. What is the average weight (in kg) of those persons whose weight is less than the average weight of the five persons?
questions.explanation: The five weigh 230 kg in all, an average of 46 kg. Those below it weigh 38, 45 and 34 kg: 117/3 = 39 kg.

questions.text: The average of five numbers is 206. The average of two of them is 205. The average of another two of those numbers is 207.5. How many numbers can be accurately identified with this information?
questions.explanation: The five total 5 × 206 = 1,030 and the two pairs 2 × 205 = 410 and 2 × 207.5 = 415. Only the fifth number can be found: 1,030 − 410 − 415 = 205.

questions.text: The average of some natural numbers is 27. If 69 is added to the first number and 12 is subtracted from the last number, the average becomes 32.7, then the number of natural numbers is:
questions.explanation: The total rises by 69 − 12 = 57, which raises the average by 32.7 − 27 = 5.7. So there are 57/5.7 = 10 numbers.

questions.text: The price of a product increased by 20%. After some time, it decreased by 15%. What is the overall percentage change in the price?
questions.explanation: 1.2 × 0.85 = 1.02, so the price rises by 2% overall.

questions.text: What is the mean proportional between 9 and 25?
questions.explanation: The mean proportional of a and b is √(ab): √(9 × 25) = √225 = 15.

questions.text: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 400 metres. When the policeman starts to chase the thief also starts running. If the speed of the thief is18km/h and that of the policeman 20 km/h, then how far would the thief have run before he is overtaken?
questions.explanation: The policeman gains 20 − 18 = 2 km/h, so he closes the 0.4 km in 0.2 hours. In that time the thief runs 18 × 0.2 = 3.6 km.

questions.text: The average weight of a family of five members (in kg) whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 67 kg and 39 kg is:

A shopkeeper sells a notebook that has a marked price of ₹80 at a discount of 8% and gives a pen costing ₹8.60 free with each notebook. Even then he makes a profit of 17%. Find the cost price of each note book correct to two places of decimals.
questions.explanation: The selling price is 0.92 × 80 = ₹73.60. Less the ₹8.60 pen, he gets ₹65 for the notebook, which is 117% of its cost: 65/1.17 = ₹55.56.

questions.text: An iron ball of radius 20 cm is melted and recast into 64 spherical balls of same radius. Find the radius of each spherical ball.
questions.explanation: The volume is unchanged: 20³ = 64r³, so r³ = 8,000/64 = 125 and r = 5 cm.

questions.text: By selling an article for ₹19.5, a dealer makes a profit of 30%. By how much should he increase his selling price (in ₹) so as to make a profit of 50%?
questions.explanation: Cost price = 19.5/1.3 = ₹15. A 50% profit needs 1.5 × 15 = ₹22.50, an increase of ₹3.

questions.text: x,y and z are divisible by 2,3 and 4, respectively. What is the highest common factor (HCF) of 6x,4y and 3z?
questions.explanation: With x = 2a, y = 3b and z = 4c, 6x = 12a, 4y = 12b and 3z = 12c. All three are multiples of 12, so their HCF is at least 12.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3500 as a sum borrowed at 7% per year rate of interest for 2 years.

Two bicycle riders started at a speed of 7 m/sec and 8 m/sec on a circular path in opposite directions at the same point. If the circumference of the circle is 300 m, then in what time will they first meet?
questions.explanation: Riding in opposite directions they close the 300 m together at 7 + 8 = 15 m/s: 300/15 = 20 seconds.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 135 × 5 – 12 ÷ 11 + 8 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 135 ÷ 5 + 12 × 11 − 8 = 27 + 132 − 8 = 151.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 4 ÷ 8 × 2 − 7 +3 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 4 × 8 ÷ 2 + 7 − 3 = 16 + 7 − 3 = 20.

questions.text: HOJF is related to IPKG in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, KRMI is related to LSNJ. To which of the following is MTOK related following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one place forward: H → I, O → P, J → K, F → G. So MTOK → NUPL.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: No child is a man. No man is an adult. Conclusions: (I) Some men are child. (II) No child is an adult.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follow
questions.explanation: No child is a man, so no man is a child and I is false. Two negative statements say nothing about children and adults, so II does not follow either.

questions.text: KPMI is related to LQNJ in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, NSPL is related to OTQM. To which of the following is RWTP related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one place forward: K → L, P → Q, M → N, I → J. So RWTP → SXUQ.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'SAND' is coded as '2468' and 'WEST' is coded as '3574'. What is the code for 'S' in the given code language?
questions.explanation: S is the only letter in both words and 4 the only digit in both codes, so S = 4.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘does she hear’ is written as ‘mt sp dt’ and ‘hear the music’ is written as ‘rb mt ch’. What is the code for ‘hear’ in that language?
questions.explanation: 'hear' is the only word in both sentences and 'mt' the only code in both, so hear = mt.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? DXZ, HTV ,LPR ,PLN, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move 4 places forward (D, H, L, P, T), second letters 4 back (X, T, P, L, H) and third letters 4 back (Z, V, R, N, J): THJ.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13, can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (8, 38, 11) (3, 20, 7)
questions.explanation: The middle number is twice the sum of the other two: 2 × (8 + 11) = 38 and 2 × (3 + 7) = 20. Likewise 2 × (1 + 12) = 26.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘BOAT’ is coded as ‘5197’ and ‘AIRS’ is coded as ‘2418’. What is the code for ‘A’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: A is the only letter in both words and 1 the only digit in both codes, so A = 1.

questions.text: Six boys A, B, C, D, E and F sit around a circular table facing towards the centre (not necessarily in the same order). Two boys sit between B and F when counted either from the right or left of B. One boy sits between A and B when counted from the right of A. E sits second to the left of A. D sits second to the left of C. Which of the following statement(s) is/are not correct? I. A is an immediate neighbour of D. II. C is an immediate neighbour of F.
questions.explanation: B and F sit opposite. B is second to A's right, so A is second to B's left; E is second to A's left, and D second to C's left puts C and D in the last two seats. Going round to each boy's left: B, D, A, F, E, C. A sits next to D, so I is correct; C sits between E and B, not next to F, so II is not.

questions.text: 15 is related to 92 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 18 is related to 110. To which of the following is 7 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each number is multiplied by 6 and 2 added: 15 × 6 + 2 = 92 and 18 × 6 + 2 = 110. So 7 × 6 + 2 = 44.

questions.text: U, V, W, X, Y, Z and A are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Only three people sit between X and Y when counted from the left of X. Only three people sit between Z and U when counted from the right of U. V sits to the immediate right of Z. W is an immediate neighbour of U as well as Y. Who sits to the second to the left of A?
questions.explanation: Y is fourth to X's left and W sits between U and Y. With U and W on Y's right, Z (fourth to U's right) would have Y on its immediate right, V's seat, so W and U are on Y's left. Going round to each person's left from X: X, V, Z, A, Y, W, U. Second to the left of A is W.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All bowling are billiards. Some billiards are not chess. Conclusions: [1] All chess are bowling. [2] All billiards are chess.
questions.explanation: Nothing makes every chess a bowling, so [1] does not follow; some billiards are not chess, so [2], 'all billiards are chess', is false.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the following series? 4, 10 ,28, 82, 244, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is three times the one before minus 2: 82 × 3 − 2 = 244 and 244 × 3 − 2 = 730.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘will you go’ is written as ‘ht dt gt’ and ‘you can go’ is written as ‘gt st dt’. How will ‘can’ be written in the given code language?
questions.explanation: 'you' and 'go' are in both sentences and 'dt' and 'gt' in both codes, so 'can' is the code left in the second: st.

questions.text: In May 2023, the Union Housing and Urban Affairs Ministry has extended the deadline of its Smart Cities Mission to ________.
questions.explanation: In May 2023 the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs extended the Smart Cities Mission's deadline to June 2024.

questions.text: Which of the following cultural festivals of Himachal Pradesh is organised on the auspicious occasion of Basant Panchami at Hadimba Temple?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Doongri, the festival of the Hadimba Devi temple in Manali, which stands in the Doongri forest. Mopin and the Ziro music festival belong to Arunachal Pradesh.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: At which of the following places was the Indian Civil Service Examination held for the first time in India?
questions.explanation: The ICS examination was first held in India, alongside London, at Allahabad in 1922.

questions.text: ‘Ace Against Odds’ is the autobiography of a sports personality playing the game of ___________.
questions.explanation: 'Ace Against Odds' (2016) is the autobiography of the tennis player Sania Mirza.

questions.text: Which inorganic compound is known to undergo solid state reaction to form urea?
questions.explanation: Ammonium cyanate rearranges into urea, its isomer, when heated: Friedrich Wöhler's synthesis of urea in 1828.

questions.text: The Pitti Bird Sanctuary is located in which Union Territory/State of India?
questions.explanation: Pitti, an uninhabited islet of Lakshadweep, is a sanctuary for nesting sea birds such as terns.

questions.text: Sunil Chhetri made history by becoming the first Indian to score a hat-trick in the Hero ISL, which came in the ________ edition.
questions.explanation: On 28 October 2015, in Mumbai City FC's 5–1 win over NorthEast United, Sunil Chhetri scored the first ISL hat-trick by an Indian.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which of the following years was the Child Marriage Restraint Act passed?
questions.explanation: The Child Marriage Restraint Act, known as the Sarda Act, was passed in 1929.

questions.text: The classical dance form ‘Kathakali’ traces its origin to which of the following states of India?
questions.explanation: Kathakali, the dance drama known for its elaborate make-up and costumes, comes from Kerala.

questions.text: Which of the following is the first event in a triathlon?
questions.explanation: A triathlon is swimming, cycling and running, in that order.

questions.text: Article 157 of the Constitution of India mentions the qualifications required for appointment of the _________________ of a State.
questions.explanation: Under Article 157 a Governor must be a citizen of India who has completed 35 years of age.

questions.text: The excavated ruins of the Nalanda University indicate that bright red _____ was/were used in its construction.
questions.explanation: The excavated monasteries and temples of Nalanda are built of red brick.

questions.text: Where was the Hindustani classical singer Kumar Gandharva born?
questions.explanation: Kumar Gandharva (Shivaputra Komkalimath) was born in 1924 at Sulebhavi near Belgaum (Belagavi), Karnataka.

questions.text: What is the primary function of the excretory system in animals?
questions.explanation: The excretory system removes the body's nitrogenous wastes, with excess water and salts.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an example of public goods?
questions.explanation: Public goods are open to all, and one person's use does not reduce another's: clean air, law enforcement, national defence. A driveway at one's home is private.

questions.text: With reference to agriculture in India, the term 'penda' is the name given to ________________.
questions.explanation: NCERT lists 'Podu' or 'Penda' as the names for slash and burn (shifting) agriculture in Andhra Pradesh.

questions.text: Who among the following scholars gave reference to the history of Kashmir?
questions.explanation: Kalhana's 'Rajatarangini' (12th century) is a chronicle of the kings of Kashmir.

questions.text: The author of ‘Arthashastra’ was a contemporary of which of the following rulers?
questions.explanation: The 'Arthashastra' is attributed to Kautilya (Chanakya), Chandragupta Maurya's minister.

questions.text: Despite being eligible for the job of a Legal Officer, Mr. X was not called for an interview for the aforementioned post. Which of his rights was Mr. X unable to exercise?
questions.explanation: Article 16 guarantees equality of opportunity in public employment, which an eligible candidate kept from the interview is denied.

questions.text: Which of the following factors is primarily responsible for soil formation?
questions.explanation: Soil forms from rock broken down by weathering, physical, chemical and biological.

questions.text: Shovana Narayan, a Padma Shri recipient, is an exponent of ________.
questions.explanation: Shovana Narayan is a leading Kathak dancer.

questions.text: According to sympatric speciation, the rising of a new species occurs when:
options: organisms from the same species start to show different behavioural characteristics
one species is separated into different groups due to geologic events like mountain formation
the two groups of organisms from the same species would phenotypically look different
two groups of the same species cannot interbreed among themselves despite living in the same geographic location
questions.explanation: In sympatric speciation groups living in the same area become reproductively isolated, without any geographic barrier. Separation by mountains or other barriers is allopatric speciation.

questions.text: Which of the following states has the lowest child sex ratio according to Census of India, 2001?
questions.explanation: In Census 2001 Haryana's child sex ratio, 819 girls per 1,000 boys, was the lowest in India after Punjab's (798).

questions.text: In January 2023, three Indian-origin researchers were among nine scientists named recipients of the Blavatnik Awardsfor Young Scientists in the UK. Which of the following is NOT one of these three scientists?
questions.explanation: Rahul R Nair (laureate), Mehul Malik and Tanmay Bharat (finalists) were the three Indian-origin scientists among the nine honoured; the awards were in fact announced in January 2024, for 2024. Gagandeep Kang is an Indian virologist.

questions.text: As per Census 2011, which of the following states recorded negative growth in child sex ratio?
questions.explanation: Between Census 2001 and 2011 Maharashtra's child sex ratio fell, while those of Punjab, Haryana and Himachal Pradesh rose.

questions.text: Which of the following sentences contains an adverbial error?
options: The teacher spoke clear and concise.
They danced gracefully across the stage.
He sang beautifully at the talent show.
questions.explanation: Verbs are modified by adverbs: 'spoke clearly and concisely', not 'clear and concise'.

questions.text: Read the following sentence and select its future tense form from the options given below: Ramya finished her dissertation early.
options: Ramya is finishing her dissertation early.
Ramya had finished her dissertation early.
Ramya has finished her dissertation early.
Ramya will finish her dissertation early.
questions.explanation: The simple future of 'finished' is 'will finish'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. David decided to __________ his old boat to get a new one.
questions.explanation: To 'sell' the boat is to part with it for money; 'sale' is the noun, and 'cell' only sounds the same.

questions.text: In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative. Yesterday was the “worse” day of my life.
questions.explanation: Comparing one day with all the others needs the superlative: 'the worst day of my life'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'Celebrate'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The branches of the tree “is” very long.
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'branches' takes the plural verb 'are'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. He received the best employee award because he was the “more hardworking”.
questions.explanation: Being the best of all the employees needs the superlative: 'the most hardworking'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The Chinese government has accepted slower economic development as the ‘new normal’, recognising the need for China to adopt a new growth model that depends less on fixed investment and exports and more on private consumption, services, and innovation to _____________ economic growth.
questions.explanation: Consumption, services and innovation are to 'drive', that is power, economic growth.

questions.text: Select the correct option of the given sentence. Smt. Savithri is wisest than all others in the group.
options: Smt. Savithri is wise than all others in the group.
Smt. Savithri is the wise than all others in the group.
Smt. Savithri is wiser than all others in the group.
Smt. Savithri is the wiser than all others in the group.
questions.explanation: A comparison with 'than' takes the comparative: 'wiser than all others'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. He possesses one of the “slimmer” handsets in the world.
questions.explanation: 'One of the' is followed by a superlative: 'one of the slimmest handsets'.

questions.text: Select the word that has the same meaning (SYNONYM) as the underlined word in the given sentence. The teacher made “judicious” use of technology to explain a sensitive topic.
questions.explanation: 'Judicious' means showing good judgement: 'prudent'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word provided in the brackets to fill in the blank. The painting exhibited a __________________ blend of colours. (harmonious)
questions.explanation: 'Harmonious' means pleasingly combined; its opposite is 'discordant', clashing.

questions.text: Select the appropriate meaning of the given idiom. At the drop of a hat
questions.explanation: To do something 'at the drop of a hat' is to do it at once, without hesitation.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The teacher asked the students to stay _________ during the exam.
questions.explanation: 'Quiet' means silent; 'quite', 'quit' and 'quote' only look or sound similar.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Due to _________ 'eve teasing', parents conclude that it is not worth the danger of sending their daughters to school.
questions.explanation: It is eve teasing that is 'widespread', found everywhere, that makes parents think school not worth the danger.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word..
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'tendency'.

questions.text: select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank to complete the idiom and make the sentence meaningful. During the interview, the candidate was challenged to provide chapter and ___________ on his proposed plan.
questions.explanation: 'Chapter and verse' means the exact details or authority for something.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The place where soldiers live
questions.explanation: Barracks are the buildings in which soldiers live.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. It is the mad (1)_______ for speed that is responsible for many motor accidents. Only last year, I (2)_______ what might have been a (3)_______ accident on Kashmir Road. I was motoring down (4)________ Srinagar; and as I was nearing Kohala, I came upon the (5)_______ of two cars on the road.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: A 'craze' is a passion or obsession: the mad craze for speed.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. It is the mad (1)_______ for speed that is responsible for many motor accidents. Only last year, I (2)_______ what might have been a (3)_______ accident on Kashmir Road. I was motoring down (4)________ Srinagar; and as I was nearing Kohala, I came upon the (5)_______ of two cars on the road.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The writer 'witnessed', that is saw, what might have been an accident.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. It is the mad (1)_______ for speed that is responsible for many motor accidents. Only last year, I (2)_______ what might have been a (3)_______ accident on Kashmir Road. I was motoring down (4)________ Srinagar; and as I was nearing Kohala, I came upon the (5)_______ of two cars on the road.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: What 'might have been a fatal accident' is one that could have killed.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. It is the mad (1)_______ for speed that is responsible for many motor accidents. Only last year, I (2)_______ what might have been a (3)_______ accident on Kashmir Road. I was motoring down (4)________ Srinagar; and as I was nearing Kohala, I came upon the (5)_______ of two cars on the road.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: The writer was motoring down 'from' Srinagar, the starting point, and was nearing Kohala.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. It is the mad (1)_______ for speed that is responsible for many motor accidents. Only last year, I (2)_______ what might have been a (3)_______ accident on Kashmir Road. I was motoring down (4)________ Srinagar; and as I was nearing Kohala, I came upon the (5)_______ of two cars on the road.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: He came upon the 'collision', the crash, of two cars.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3000 as a sum borrowed at 3% per year rate of interest for 6 years.
A sold an article to B at 40% profit and B sold it to C at 15% profit. If C paid ₹4,914 for the article, how much (in ₹, rounded off to the nearest integer) did A pay for it?

A chef has two cans of acids and water mixture. He combines the contents of both cans in a beaker. The resulting mixture has half water and half acid. What is the quantity in which he mixed the contents of can 1 and can 2, given that can 2 has an acid-to-water ratio of 2 : 3 and can 1 has an acid-to-water ratio of 5 : 3?
questions.explanation: Acid is 5/8 of can 1 and 2/5 of can 2. For a mixture that is 1/2 acid, by alligation can 1 : can 2 = (1/2 − 2/5) : (5/8 − 1/2) = 1/10 : 1/8 = 4 : 5.

questions.text: In an election, 750 votes were cast for the two contestants, Bharti and Manya. Bharti defeated Manya by 16% votes. If there were no invalid vote, then how many votes did Manya get?
questions.explanation: Bharti's margin is 16% of 750 = 120 votes, so Manya got (750 − 120)/2 = 315.

questions.text: In an office, the average salary of 22 staff members was ₹81,400. If the average salary of staff and the Vice Chairman was ₹89,600, then how much is the salary of the Vice Chairman (in ₹)?
questions.explanation: With the Vice Chairman the total is 23 × 89,600 = ₹20,60,800; the staff's alone is 22 × 81,400 = ₹17,90,800. The difference, ₹2,70,000, is his salary.

questions.text: A and B start running simultaneously, around a circular track of 1200 m, in the same direction, at a speed of 8 m/s and 12 m/s, respectively. A and B will meet at the starting point for the first time after:
questions.explanation: A takes 1,200/8 = 150 s a lap and B 1,200/12 = 100 s. They are first at the start together after LCM(150, 100) = 300 s.

questions.text: Anand wanted to make a cylindrical kaleidoscope of length 30 cm and radius 7 cm. If he is using handmade sheets to make it, then how much sheet will be required for this?
questions.explanation: The sheet forms the curved surface: 2πrh = 2 × 22/7 × 7 × 30 = 1,320 cm².

questions.text: A thief is running away on a straight road on a bike moving at the speed of 28 m/s. A policeman chases him in a car moving at the speed of 30 m/s. if the instantaneous separation of the bike from the car is 400 m, how long will it take for the policeman to catch the thief?
questions.explanation: The car gains 30 − 28 = 2 m/s on the bike, so it closes the 400 m in 400/2 = 200 seconds.

questions.text: A shopkeeper offers buy three, get one free; what is the percentage discount being offered by the shopkeeper in this scheme?
questions.explanation: The customer pays for 3 articles and gets 4, so 1 article in 4 is free: a discount of 25%.

questions.text: P sold an article to Q at 11% profit and Q sold it to R at 11% loss. If R paid ₹19,758 for it, then at what price (in ₹) was the article purchased by P?
The average weight of a family of five members (in kg) whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 72 kg and 36 kg is:
In a class, there are 30 boys and 20 girls. The average score of boys in Physics is 92, whereas the average score of girls in Physics is 83. Find the average score of the whole class in Physics.
The simple interest on a sum of ₹4,200 at the end of 3 years is ₹756. What will be the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹5,400 at the same rate and for the same time period?
Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹4000 as a sum borrowed at 4% per year rate of interest for 6 years.
Find the HCF of 36 and 84.
questions.explanation: 36 = 2² × 3² and 84 = 2² × 3 × 7, so the HCF is 2² × 3 = 12.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some trees are blue. All blue is green. Conclusions: (I) All trees are blue. (II) Some trees are green.
questions.explanation: The trees that are blue are also green, so some trees are green (II). Only some trees are said to be blue, so I does not follow.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘×‘ are interchanged and ‘−’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 41 × 1 + 390 − 10 ÷ 15 =?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 41 + 1 × 390 ÷ 10 − 15 = 41 + 39 − 15 = 65.

questions.text: P, Q, R, S, T, U and V are sitting around a circular table facing out to the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). P is sitting second to the left of U. R is sitting third to the right of S. S is an immediate neighbour of V. V is sitting to the immediate left of P. T is not an immediate neighbour of U. How many people are sitting between P and Q when counted from the right of P?
questions.explanation: Going round to the left from U: R, P, V, S, T, Q (P second to U's left, V on P's left, S beside V, R third to S's right, and T away from U). Counting rightwards from P, R and U come before Q: two people.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13, can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (4, 9, 26) (2, 8, 20)

37 is related to 89 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 43 is related to 101. To which of the following is 28 related, following the same logic?(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbersinto its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1and 3 is not allowed)
FLRX is related to KQWC in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, GMSY is related to LRXD. To which of the following is HNTZ related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 5 places forward (Y wraps round to D): FLRX → KQWC and GMSY → LRXD. So HNTZ → MSYE.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘GAME’ is coded as ‘8536’ and ‘MEAN’ is coded as ‘5983’. What is the code for ‘N’ in that language?
questions.explanation: M, E and A are in both words, as are 3, 5 and 8 in both codes. The letter left in MEAN is N and the digit left in its code is 9, so N = 9.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some bulls are rocks. Some rocks are stones. Conclusions: (I): Some bulls are stones. (II): All stones are rocks.
questions.explanation: The rocks that are bulls need not be the rocks that are stones, so I does not follow; and 'some rocks are stones' does not make every stone a rock, so II does not follow either.

questions.text: TGKP is related to QDHM in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, XBWL is related to UYTI. To which of the following is VEAH related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places back (A wraps round to X): TGKP → QDHM and XBWL → UYTI. So VEAH → SBXE.

questions.text: What will come in the place of the question mark (‘?’)in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘×’ are interchanged and ‘÷′ and ‘–‘ are interchanged? 19 × 7 ÷ 8 × 306 – 17 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 19 + 7 − 8 + 306 ÷ 17 = 19 + 7 − 8 + 18 = 36.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘derive the formula’ is written as ‘le ro da’ and ‘formula to win’ is writtenas ‘ka wb ro’. How will ‘formula’ be writtenin the given language?
questions.explanation: 'formula' is the only word in both sentences and 'ro' the only code in both, so formula = ro.

questions.text: In a certain code, ‘pen pencil eraser’ is coded as ‘dy ph mt’, ‘pencil box crayon’ is coded as ‘lp ph st’ and ‘box pen board’ is coded as ‘st bq dy’. All the codes are two-letter codes only. What is 'board' coded as?
questions.explanation: 'pencil' is in the first two and 'ph' in both their codes; 'pen' is in the first and third, coded 'dy'; 'box' is in the second and third, coded 'st'. That leaves 'bq' for 'board'.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 3, ?, 13, 18, 23, 28, 33
questions.explanation: The terms rise by 5: 3, 8, 13, 18, 23, 28, 33.

questions.text: R, S, T, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Only three people are sitting between E and T when counted from the right of E. Only two people are sitting between R and G. S is sitting to the immediate left of D. Only two people are sitting between T and R. How many people are sitting between F and S when counted from the left of F?
questions.explanation: T is fourth to E's right; R, with two people between it and T, sits on E's right, and G, with two between it and R the other way round, on T's right. S and D take the seats between R and T, S on D's left: going right from E, R, S, D, T, G, F. Counting leftwards from F, G, T and D come before S: three people.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘RENT’ is coded as ‘1957’ and ‘GRIM’ is coded as ‘2469’.What is the code for ‘R’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: R is the only letter in both words and 9 the only digit in both codes, so R = 9.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? OSM, LPJ ,IMG, FJD ,?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places back: O, L, I, F, C; S, P, M, J, G; M, J, G, D, A. The next cluster is CGA.

questions.text: Select the correct order of processes used for water purification in waterworks. 1. Filtration 2. Chlorination 3. Suspended impurity sedimentation 4. Solid impurity sedimentation
questions.explanation: Waterworks first let the heavy solid impurities settle, then make the fine suspended ones settle (with alum, for instance), then filter the water and finally chlorinate it to kill germs.

questions.text: Which of the following groups of ports are located on the bank of the Bay of Bengal?
questions.explanation: Haldia (West Bengal) and Paradip (Odisha) are on the Bay of Bengal. New Mangalore, Cochin and Kandla are on the Arabian Sea, and Tuticorin on the Gulf of Mannar.

questions.text: Mysore Brothers are known for playing which musical instrument?
questions.explanation: The Mysore Brothers, Mysore Nagaraj and Mysore Manjunath, are Carnatic violinists.

questions.text: The Betul, Hoshangabad and Chhindwara districts of Madhya Pradesh is a part of which of the following Biosphere Reserves?
questions.explanation: The Pachmarhi Biosphere Reserve, in the Satpura range, spreads over parts of the Betul, Hoshangabad and Chhindwara districts.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which of the places was Arya Samaj founded?
questions.explanation: Swami Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in Bombay in 1875.

questions.text: The Kalidas Samman award is presented by which of the following governments?
questions.explanation: The Kalidas Samman, a national award for the arts, was instituted by the Government of Madhya Pradesh in 1980.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: 'Waiting for a Visa' is the autobiography of:
questions.explanation: 'Waiting for a Visa' is B. R. Ambedkar's short autobiographical account of the untouchability he faced.

questions.text: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution has a provision that ‘all executive actions of the Government of India shall be expressed to be taken in the name of the President’?
questions.explanation: Article 77, on the conduct of business of the Government of India, says this in clause (1).

questions.text: Which of the following is observed on the birthday of Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan?
questions.explanation: Dr Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan's birthday, 5 September, is Teachers' Day in India.

questions.text: Which financial products are commonly offered by Microfinance Institutions in India?
options: Savings, credit and insurance services tailored for low-income individuals
questions.explanation: Microfinance institutions give small loans, savings and insurance to low-income households that ordinary banking does not reach.

questions.text: What is the standard length of a cricket pitch?
questions.explanation: A cricket pitch is 22 yards (20.12 m) long between the wickets.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of anaerobic activity?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives jumping: anaerobic activity is a short, intense burst, such as a jump, in which the muscles need energy faster than oxygen can supply it. Walking and swimming at a steady pace are aerobic, and so, as a rule, is skipping, though fast skipping can be anaerobic too.

questions.text: What is the name of the scheme launched by the Government of India in 2023 to effectively resolve pending contractual disputes?
questions.explanation: Vivad se Vishwas II (Contractual Disputes), announced in the Union Budget 2023-24, is a voluntary settlement scheme for the pending contractual disputes of the government and its undertakings.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Shuddhi movement was initiated by which of the following organisations?
questions.explanation: The Arya Samaj ran the Shuddhi movement to bring back into Hinduism those who had converted to other faiths.

questions.text: Which of the following programmes is taken up by the Government of India for improvement of female literacy rates in India?
questions.explanation: Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao, launched in 2015, aims to protect the girl child and see her educated.

questions.text: In the year of the coronation of Akbar, who among the following was designated as the Wakil of the Mughal kingdom with the title of ‘Khan-i-Khanan’?
questions.explanation: At Akbar's accession in 1556 Bairam Khan became his regent, the vakil, with the title Khan-i-Khanan.

questions.text: The basic structure of the Indian Constitution stands on the Government of India Act, ___________.
questions.explanation: Much of the Constitution's structure, including the federal scheme and the office of Governor, was taken from the Government of India Act, 1935.

questions.text: Which of the following is the oldest dated forts in India, as first mentioned in Alexander the Great’s war records, bringing it to the 4th century BCE?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Kangra Fort in Himachal Pradesh, which heritage and tourism accounts describe as mentioned in Alexander the Great's war records. Kumbhalgarh and Mehrangarh were built in the 15th century.

questions.text: As per the National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2021, which of the following groups of states is the poorest?
questions.explanation: NITI Aayog's National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2021 found the highest shares of poor people in Bihar, Jharkhand and Uttar Pradesh.

questions.text: Which edition of the ODI Cricket World Cup was held in India in 2023?
questions.explanation: The 2023 ODI World Cup, held in India, was the 13th edition of the tournament.

questions.text: In November 2023, who was appointed as the President-elect of the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI)?
questions.explanation: Anish Shah, Group CEO of the Mahindra Group, was named FICCI's President-elect in November 2023 and took over as President in December 2023.

questions.text: Which of the following is a precious mineral?
questions.explanation: Platinum is a precious metal. Mica is a non-metallic mineral, and bauxite and hematite are ores of aluminium and iron.

questions.text: Which folk dance has its roots in Maharashtra?
questions.explanation: Lavani is a folk dance of Maharashtra, performed to the beat of the dholki. Garba and Dandiya are from Gujarat, Bihu from Assam.

questions.text: Foods containing fats and carbohydrates are also called ____________.
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates and fats are the body's main sources of energy, so they are called energy-giving foods; proteins are the body-building foods.

questions.text: Ravikirti was the court poet of which ruler?
questions.explanation: Ravikirti, court poet of the Chalukya king Pulakeshin II, composed the Aihole inscription.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate form of comparative degree that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Rohit Sharma “is better than more other batsman” in the world.
options: as good as the most other batsmen
questions.explanation: Comparing one player with the rest of a group takes 'better than most other' and a plural noun. The sheet underlines 'is' as well, but no option repeats it, so the verb stays: 'Rohit Sharma is better than most other batsmen in the world.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The analysis of a person's handwriting to determine his/her personality
questions.explanation: Graphology is the study of handwriting as a guide to character. Calligraphy is the art of fine handwriting, numismatics the study of coins and philology the study of the history of languages.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The happy and cheerful girls / is always running towards / the ice cream cart in / front of the garden.
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'girls' takes a plural verb: 'are always running towards'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The branch of geography that studies mountains and their formation
questions.explanation: Orography is the study of mountains. Orthography is spelling and palaeography the study of ancient writing.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'beginner'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom to replace the underlined segment. He thinks his new plan will undoubtedly “produce the desired result” .
questions.explanation: To 'bear fruit' is to produce the desired result. To 'go pear-shaped' is to go wrong, and 'sour grapes' is pretending not to want what one cannot have.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence. Losing my job turned out to be “an unexpected benefit” because it pushed me to start my own business, which has been more successful than I ever imagined.
questions.explanation: A 'blessing in disguise' is something that seems bad at first but turns out to be good: an unexpected benefit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. Anupama was a very “industrious” child and submitted all her assignments on time.
questions.explanation: 'Industrious' means hard-working; its opposite is 'lazy'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Antique
questions.explanation: 'Antique' means very old: 'ancient'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks. I bought a _____ but it is ______.
questions.explanation: 'A' needs a noun and 'it is' an adjective: 'I bought a chip but it is cheap.' 'Cheap' is not a noun, and 'cain' is not a common English word.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate form of comparative degree that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Maheshwari is three years “junior than me.”
options: junior than any other to me
questions.explanation: 'Junior' and 'senior' take 'to', not 'than': 'three years junior to me'.

questions.text: Select the grammatically correct sentence..
options: Rukmini put a book on an table and sat down.
Rukmini put the book on the table and sat down.
Rukmini put the book on an table and sat down.
Rukmini put an book on the table and sat down.
questions.explanation: 'An' goes only before a vowel sound, so 'an table' and 'an book' are wrong; only 'Rukmini put the book on the table and sat down' avoids both.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. He was very “inquisitive” and wanted to know each and every detail.
questions.explanation: 'Inquisitive' means eager to know; its opposite is 'indifferent', not interested.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank. Many orthodox people have a ____(hostile) attitude towards the idea of women getting educated and employed.
questions.explanation: 'Hostile' means unfriendly and aggressive: 'belligerent'.

questions.text: Identify the error in the given sentence. Ajit got to work earliest than everyone else today.
questions.explanation: 'Than' follows a comparative, so 'earlier than', not the superlative 'earliest'.

questions.text: Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence. Are you sure that you can’t even write a single sentnce properly?
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'sentence'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word..
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'scary'.

questions.text: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
options: Rahul is very naughty as he is the most young sibling between Rama’s three brothers.
Rahul is very naughty as he is the most young sibling among Rama’s three brothers.
Rahul is very naughty as he is the youngest sibling among Rama’s three brothers.
Rahul is very naughty as he is the youngest sibling between Rama’s three brothers.
questions.explanation: The superlative of 'young' is 'youngest', and a choice from three or more takes 'among', not 'between'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The computer can become a threat to man. It can (1)______________ his survival and privacy. It also offers excellent encouragement for unethical or criminal activities. It can (2)_______________ the unemployment problem as employers prefer the computer and the 'computer- controlled robots' to humans for obvious reasons. The information storage facility the computer provides has (3)___________ to collection of personal information about individuals and storage of this information in data banks by several employing agencies. If care is not exercised (4)__________ data gathering, data integrity may suffer. That is, questionable or imperfect methods may be employed; as a result, incorrect or incomplete data may be stored, and this (5)____________ become a permanent source and used for any given purpose.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.explanation: A computer that is a 'threat' to man can 'endanger' his survival and privacy.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: The population of a village is increased by 3%. Had there been 122 less, there would have been a decrease of 1%. Find the original population.
How many seconds will a boy take to run one complete round around a square field of side 38 metres, if he runs at a speed of 6 km/h?
questions.explanation: One round is 4 × 38 = 152 m, and 6 km/h = 6 × 5/18 = 5/3 m/s. Time = 152 × 3/5 = 91.2 seconds.

questions.text: A tradesman marks his goods at 45% above the cost price but allows a discount of 20% at the time of sale. His gain is:
questions.explanation: Selling price = 1.45 × 0.8 = 1.16 times the cost price: a gain of 16%.

questions.text: A solid sphere of iron having radius 15 cm is to be melted and recast in the shape of a cylindrical pipe having internal and external radii 4 cm and 6 cm, respectively. Find the length (in m) of the pipe thus formed.
questions.explanation: Volume of the sphere = (4/3)π × 15³ = 4500π cm³. The pipe's cross-section is π(6² − 4²) = 20π cm², so its length is 4500π/20π = 225 cm = 2.25 m.

questions.text: Three different types of pulses costing ₹180, ₹240 and ₹200 per kg, respectively, are mixed in the ratio 1 : 5 : 4. What will be the cost for 1 kg of the mixture?
Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2500 as a sum borrowed at 9% per year rate of interest for 3 years.
Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3000 as a sum borrowed at 5% per year rate of interest for 5 years.
What is the average of the first 40 natural numbers?
questions.explanation: The sum of 1 to 40 is 40 × 41/2 = 820, so the average is 820/40 = 20.5.

questions.text: Eight persons went to a restaurant for lunch. Seven of them spent ₹80 each on their meals, while the eighth person spent ₹70 more than the average expenditure of all eight persons. What was the total amount spent by all the individuals?
questions.explanation: If the average is A, the total 8A = 7 × 80 + (A + 70), so 7A = 630 and A = 90. The total is 8 × 90 = ₹720.

questions.text: In what ratio must tea at ₹82/kg be mixed with tea at ₹92/kg so that the mixture be worth ₹84.50/kg?

A person walks alonga rectangular field, whose dimensions are 6 km long and 3 km wide. For the first 1 hour, he walks at a speed of 2 km/hr. After 1 hour, he increases his speed to 4 km/hr. Next 1 hour, his speed is decreased to 2 km/hr. For the next 1 hour, he increases his speed to 4 km/hr. Find his average speed (in km/hr).
questions.explanation: In the 4 hours he covers 2 + 4 + 2 + 4 = 12 km, so his average speed is 12/4 = 3 km/h.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the following series? 11, 18, 25, 32, 39, ?
questions.explanation: The numbers rise by 7 each time: 39 + 7 = 46.

questions.text: Which two numbers should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 7 × 4− 8 × 2 + 3 × 14 × 5− 9 = 133 (Note: Interchange should be done of entire number and not individual digits of a given number)
GN76 is related to UB53 in a certain way. In the same way, KR34 is related to YF11. To which of the following is OV98 related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 14 places forward (wrapping round after Z) and the number falls by 23: G → U, N → B, 76 − 23 = 53. So O → C, V → J and 98 − 23 = 75: CJ75.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the given sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/ subtracting /multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (444, 74, 6) (666, 37, 18)
questions.explanation: In each set the first number divided by the second gives the third: 444 ÷ 74 = 6 and 666 ÷ 37 = 18. Likewise 256 ÷ 32 = 8.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All horses are donkeys. All donkeys are mules. Conclusions: (I) All donkeys are horses. (II) Some mules are donkeys.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusion I and II follow
questions.explanation: All donkeys are mules, so some mules are donkeys (II). That all horses are donkeys does not make all donkeys horses, so I does not follow.

questions.text: 46 is related to 414 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 52 is related to 468. To which ofthe following is 67 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbersinto its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: The second number is 9 times the first: 46 × 9 = 414 and 52 × 9 = 468. Likewise 67 × 9 = 603.

questions.text: Which two numbers should be interchanged to make the following equation correct? 12 × 2 −6 × 7 + 3× 5× 4 + 10 = 46 (Note: Interchange should be done of the entire number and not individual digits of a given number.)

Six people A, B, C, D, E and F are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). F is sitting second to right of D. C is sitting third to left of F. B is sitting to the immediate right of D. A is not an immediate neighbour of C. How many people are sitting between E and B when counted from right of E?
questions.explanation: Seated clockwise from D (each person's left, as all face the centre): D, C, E, A, F, B. Going to E's right you pass C and D before reaching B: two people.

questions.text: In this question, two statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusion(s) logically follows/follow from the statements. Statements: All cows are goats. Some goats are lions. Conclusions: I. All lions are goats. II. Some cows are lions.
options: Neither Conclusion I nor II follow.
Both Conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: That some goats are lions does not make all lions goats (I), and the cows, all of them goats, need not include any of the goats that are lions (II). Neither follows.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘FINE’ is coded as ‘9632’ and ‘LINE’ is coded as ‘2946’. What is the code for ‘F’ in that language?
questions.explanation: I, N and E are in both words, and 9, 6 and 2 in both codes. The letter left in FINE is F and the digit left in its code is 3, so F = 3.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark(?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? ABA, BDB, CFC, DHD, ?
questions.explanation: The first and last letters run A, B, C, D, so next E; the middle letters skip one each time, B, D, F, H, so next J: EJE.

questions.text: Six people—A, B, C, D, E, and F—are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). A is an immediate neighbour of both E and C. B is an immediate neighbour of both D and C. F is to the immediate right of D. Who among the following is an immediate neighbour of both F and A?
questions.explanation: A sits between E and C, and B between C and D, so five of them sit E, A, C, B, D and F takes the seat between D and E. F's neighbours are D and E, and A's are E and C: E is next to both.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘FISH’ is coded as ‘4268’ and ‘RATS’ is coded as ‘2357’.What is the code for ‘S’ in that language?
questions.explanation: S is the only letter in both words and 2 the only digit in both codes, so S = 2.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘cake is delicious’ is written as ‘kg fv bu’ and ‘you like cake’ is coded as ‘bu wl ma’. How is ‘cake’ coded in the given language?
questions.explanation: 'cake' is the only word in both sentences and 'bu' the only code in both, so cake = bu.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘Try to act’ is coded as ‘ZX MN HO’ and ‘act your age’ is coded as ‘CO MB ZX’. How is ‘act’ coded in that code language?
questions.explanation: 'act' is the only word in both sentences and 'ZX' the only code in both, so act = ZX.

questions.text: NQRP is related to TWXV in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, EHIG is related to KNOM. To which of the following is LOPN related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 6 places forward: N → T, Q → W, R → X, P → V and E → K, H → N, I → O, G → M. So LOPN → RUVT.

questions.text: Which edition of the Santosh Trophy event did Karnataka win in the 2022-23 season?
questions.explanation: Karnataka won the 76th Santosh Trophy (2022-23), beating Meghalaya in the final played in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

questions.text: Which percussionist from Maharashtra received Padma Vibhushan 2023?
questions.explanation: Tabla maestro Zakir Hussain, listed from Maharashtra, received the Padma Vibhushan in 2023.

questions.text: Ortho-sulphobenzimide is one of the artificial sweeteners. It is also known as ________.
questions.explanation: Ortho-sulphobenzimide is saccharin, the first popular artificial sweetener, about 550 times as sweet as cane sugar.

questions.text: The founders of Vijayanagar empire, Harihara and Bukka Raya were the ministers of:
questions.explanation: Harihara and Bukka served as ministers of the kingdom of Kampili before founding the Vijayanagara empire in 1336.

questions.text: By which of the following Amendments was the right to property removed from Part III of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The 44th Amendment (1978) removed the right to property from the Fundamental Rights in Part III and made it a legal right under Article 300A.

questions.text: Which of the following is referred to as ‘Near Money’?
questions.explanation: Near money is an asset that can quickly be turned into cash but is not itself used to pay, such as savings deposits and government savings schemes. Currency notes, coins and bank (demand) deposits are money itself.

questions.text: Identify the group of states that is a part of Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyaan (As of June 2022).
questions.explanation: The Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyaan, launched in June 2020 for migrant workers who had returned home, covered 116 districts in six states: Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Jharkhand and Odisha.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following is an autobiography of Abul Kalam Azad, the first education minister of India?
options: The Story of My Experiments with Truth
questions.explanation: 'India Wins Freedom' is Maulana Abul Kalam Azad's autobiographical account. 'Long Walk to Freedom' is Nelson Mandela's, 'The Story of My Experiments with Truth' Gandhi's and 'My Country My Life' L. K. Advani's.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following pacts suspended the Civil Disobedience Movement?
questions.explanation: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact of March 1931 suspended the Civil Disobedience Movement, and Gandhi agreed to attend the Second Round Table Conference.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an iron-ore producing belt of India?
questions.explanation: India's iron-ore belts are Odisha-Jharkhand, Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur, Ballari-Chitradurga-Chikkamagaluru-Tumakuru and Maharashtra-Goa. There is no Bilaspur-Panipat belt.

questions.text: Which state has the highest population in India as per the projected data of 2024?
questions.explanation: Uttar Pradesh, India's most populous state in the 2011 census, remains so in the population projections for 2024.

questions.text: ICC Women's T-20 Cricket World Cup is a/an ________ event.
questions.explanation: The ICC Women's T20 World Cup is planned as a biennial event, held every two years.

questions.text: Bokaro, Burnpur, Rourkela, etc., are famous for development of which of the following industries?
questions.explanation: Bokaro (Jharkhand), Burnpur (West Bengal) and Rourkela (Odisha) are home to major steel plants of the Steel Authority of India (SAIL).

questions.text: What is the chemical formula for potassium permanganate?
questions.explanation: Potassium permanganate is KMnO₄: one potassium ion (K⁺) and one permanganate ion (MnO₄⁻).

questions.text: Hareli festival is celebrated in which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Hareli, a farmers' festival at which ploughs and other tools are worshipped, is celebrated in Chhattisgarh in the month of Sawan.

questions.text: Kamalini Asthana is associated with which of the following dance forms?
questions.explanation: Kamalini Asthana is a Kathak dancer; with her sister Nalini she received the Padma Shri in 2022.

questions.text: Which of the following was the capital of the Pallava Dynasty?
questions.explanation: Kanchipuram (Kanchi) was the Pallava capital. Aihole and Badami (Vatapi) were Chalukya centres, and Madurai was the Pandya capital.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about pteridophytes are correct? Statements: A. They include horsetails and ferns. B. Pteridophytes are used for medicinal purposes and as soil-binders. C. They are very advanced type of plants on earth, which evolved very recently. D. Evolutionarily, they are the first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues – xylem and phloem.
questions.explanation: Pteridophytes, such as horsetails and ferns, are used medicinally and as soil-binders, and were the first land plants with vascular tissues, xylem and phloem. They are an ancient group, not a recent one, so C is false.

questions.text: Which Article of the Constitution of India states that the Parliament consists of the President of India and the two Houses of Parliament known as Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and House of the People (Lok Sabha)?
questions.explanation: Article 79 says Parliament consists of the President and the two Houses, the Council of States and the House of the People.

questions.text: In May 2023, which Chief Minister was honoured with the Bharat Ratna Dr. Ambedkar award for creating a fear-free state?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Yogi Adityanath, Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following formed a group of non-violent revolutionaries, the Khudai Khidmatgars (known as Red Shirts)?
questions.explanation: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, the 'Frontier Gandhi', founded the Khudai Khidmatgars (the 'Red Shirts') in 1929.

questions.text: Divergent plate boundary is a boundary that occurs between two tectonic plates:
options: that are sliding horizontally past each other
that are moving towards one another
where one plate slides beneath the other
that are moving away from one another
questions.explanation: At a divergent boundary two plates move apart and new crust forms between them, as along the mid-ocean ridges.

questions.text: Which of the following statements with reference to Padma Subrahmanyam is/are correct? 1) Padma Subrahmanyam is a famous Bharatanatyam dancer. 2) She received the Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan awards. 3) She was also honoured with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Dance.
questions.explanation: Padma Subrahmanyam is a Bharatanatyam dancer and scholar who has received the Padma Shri, the Padma Bhushan and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, so all three statements are correct.

questions.text: Who discovered the Bharhut stupa?
questions.explanation: Alexander Cunningham, the first head of the Archaeological Survey of India, discovered the Bharhut stupa in Madhya Pradesh in 1873.

questions.text: In July 2023, the District Rural Development Agency (DRDA) in Tirupathur district, Tamil Nadu, achieved a monumental achievement by constructing 1546 farm ponds in just 30 days, setting a new world record. This remarkable initiative was carried out under which government scheme?
options: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme, under which farm ponds are dug on farmers' land as water-conservation works.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Congenial
questions.explanation: 'Congenial' means pleasant or agreeable.

questions.text: Based on the context of the given sentence, select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank. After spending hours working non-stop on the project, the team decided to ___________ and go home.
questions.explanation: To 'call it a day' is to stop working for the day.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. It is a fact that / girls' hair is usually / long than the boys' hair.
questions.explanation: A comparison with 'than' needs the comparative: 'longer than the boys' hair'.

questions.text: Select the sentence that has a grammatical error.
options: The train leaves the station at 8:00 a.m. every day.
They play chess together on weekends.
She usually walks her dog in the park every morning.
questions.explanation: A singular subject takes 'doesn't': 'He doesn't like spicy food.'

questions.text: Change the following sentence into positive degree. Ramesh is not stronger than Mahesh.
options: Mahesh is as strong as Ramesh.
Ramesh is as strong than Mahesh.
questions.explanation: 'Ramesh is not stronger than Mahesh' means Mahesh is at least as strong as Ramesh; in the positive degree, 'Mahesh is as strong as Ramesh'. 'Strongest than' and 'as strong than' are ungrammatical, and 'stronger than' is still comparative.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word..
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'occasionally'.

questions.text: Select the correct spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence. “Scince” explores and explains the natural world through observation and experimentation.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'science'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank. In an _____(endeavour) to improve the environment of their society, they planted many trees surrounding the parking area.
questions.explanation: An 'endeavour' is an attempt to achieve something; of the options, 'aim' is closest.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Gandhi’s ways of life, if followed in their entirety, will aid us in the creation of a society of peace and _______.
questions.explanation: A society of peace and 'harmony': agreement and goodwill, the opposite of discord.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'perseverance'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks. Chocolate can be ______ without milk; mix cocoa butter, sugar and a puree of fermented, roasted cocoa beans, and you _______ a perfectly respectable dark chocolate.
questions.explanation: 'Can be made' is the passive after the modal, and 'you have' goes with the subject 'you'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM for the underlined word. My teacher is very “diligent”.
questions.explanation: 'Diligent' means hard-working; its opposite is 'idle'.

questions.text: Select the option that changes the degree of comparison in the given sentence from superlative to positive without changing the meaning of the sentence. Kalpana Ahuja is the tallest girl in the colony.
options: Kalpana Ahuja is as tallest as other girls of the colony.
Many girls in the colony are taller than Kalpana Ahuja.
No other girl in the colony is as tall as Kalpana Ahuja.
No other girl in the colony is as taller as Kalpana Ahuja.
questions.explanation: In the positive degree, 'the tallest girl in the colony' becomes 'No other girl in the colony is as tall as Kalpana Ahuja'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. Swati came here with the intent “of insulting me”.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'to insult me': 'intent' is most often followed by a to-infinitive ('with intent to deceive'). The sentence's own 'of insulting me' is also used, but there is no 'no improvement' option, and 'off', 'from' and 'for' are wrong.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Elevation
questions.explanation: 'Elevation' is raising to a higher rank; its opposite is 'demotion'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate form of comparative degree that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Neha’s house is “far from the city than” everyone else’s.
options: more far from the city to
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'farther from the city than': for physical distance the comparative of 'far' is traditionally 'farther', with 'further' kept for extent ('further details'), though 'further' is also widely used for distance, especially in British English. 'More far' and 'to' are wrong.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Don’t be such an ________; we have plenty of time to complete the task.
questions.explanation: An 'eager beaver' is someone over-keen to get on with work; with plenty of time, there is no need to be one.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. When I was studying Economics in Delhi University, Ritu was senior than me.
questions.explanation: 'Senior' takes 'to', not 'than': 'Ritu was senior to me'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Abundant
questions.explanation: 'Abundant' means plentiful: 'ample'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. That was a jolly story _____1_____ Arthur Ransome told the other day in one of his messages from Petrograd, a place in Russia. A stout old lady was walking __2___ her basket down the middle of a street to the _____3_____ confusion of the traffic and with no small peril to herself. It was pointed _____4_____ to her that the _____5_____ was the place for the foot passengers, but she replied, “I’m going to walk where I like. We’ve got liberty now.”

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun 'which' introduces the clause: 'a jolly story which Arthur Ransome told'.

questions.text:

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
