markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: Pure ghee costs ₹100 per kg. After adulterating it with vegetable oil costing ₹50 per kg, a shopkeeper sells the mixture at the rate of ₹96 per kg, thereby making a profit of 20%. In what ratio does he mix the two?
questions.explanation: At 20% profit, ₹96 is 1.2 times the cost, so the mixture costs ₹80 a kg. By alligation, ghee : oil = (80 − 50) : (100 − 80) = 30 : 20 = 3 : 2.

questions.text: A cone of radius 16 cm and height 12 cm is cut, parallel to the base, at some height closer to the top. If the ratio of the heights of the solids is 1∶3, then the ratio of the total surface areas of the two solids formed is approximately given by:
questions.explanation: Slant height = √(16² + 12²) = 20 cm. The small cone on top has height 3 cm, radius 4 cm and slant 5 cm: TSA = π × 4 × (4 + 5) = 36π. The frustum has radii 16 and 4 cm and slant 15 cm: TSA = π(16 + 4) × 15 + π × 16² + π × 4² = 572π. 36 : 572 = 9 : 143.

questions.text: A student's overall grade is determined by their scores in three subjects: Mathematics, English, and Science, with weights of 40%, 30%, and 30%, respectively. If the student scores 80, 90, and 75 in these subjects, respectively, the overall grade of the student is:

A man’s average driving speed for 9 hours is 88 km/hr. During the first five hours of his journey, he drove at 74 km/hr, and last two hours he drove at 82 km/hr. What was his average speed (in km/hr) for the sixth and the seventh hour?
questions.explanation: Total distance = 9 × 88 = 792 km. The first five hours cover 5 × 74 = 370 km and the last two 2 × 82 = 164 km, leaving 258 km for the sixth and seventh hours: 258 ÷ 2 = 129 km/hr.

questions.text: By selling an article for ₹20, a dealer makes a profit of 10%. By how much should he increase his selling price (in ₹, rounded off to two decimal place) so as to make a profit of 45%?
questions.explanation: Cost price = 20 ÷ 1.1 = ₹18.18. For a 45% profit the price must be 18.18 × 1.45 = ₹26.36, an increase of ₹6.36.

questions.text: A shopkeeper offers two schemes, the first being a single discount of 30%, and the second being two successive discounts of 25% and 5%. What is the difference (in ₹) in the discounts of both the schemes if the customer did the shopping of ₹5,000 each in both the schemes?
questions.explanation: A single 30% discount on ₹5,000 is ₹1,500. The successive discounts leave 5,000 × 0.75 × 0.95 = ₹3,562.50 to pay, a discount of ₹1,437.50. The difference is ₹62.50.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2500 as a sum borrowed at 8% per year rate of interest for 2 years.

The length and the breadth of the floor of a rectangular hall are 98 feet and 70 feet, respectively. If all persons in the hall are allotted equal square spaces as workstations, what will be the area of the largest such workstation that can be allotted to any user, assuming no space in the hall is left unoccupied?
questions.explanation: The largest square that fills the floor exactly has a side equal to the HCF of 98 and 70, which is 14 feet: 14² = 196 sq. ft.

questions.text: A policeman saw a thief at a distance of 800m. When the policeman started chasing the thief, the thief started running. If the ratio of the speeds of the policeman to the thief is 3:2, then the distance travelled by the policeman to catch the thief is
questions.explanation: While the policeman runs 3 units the thief runs 2, so he gains 1 unit for every 3 he runs. To gain 800 m he runs 3 × 800 = 2,400 m = 2.4 km.

questions.text: Which of the following options is equal to the radius of the new sphere, if three spheres of radii 5cm, 3cm and 4cm are melted into form a new sphere?
questions.explanation: The volume is unchanged, so R³ = 5³ + 3³ + 4³ = 125 + 27 + 64 = 216 and R = 6 cm.

questions.text: A batsman scored the following runs in the last 5 innings. Find his score in the 4th innings if the average score is 43. Innings Score (in runs): 1st - 92; 2nd - 53; 3rd - 35; 4th - X; 5th - 27
questions.explanation: The five innings total 5 × 43 = 215 runs. The other four total 92 + 53 + 35 + 27 = 207, so X = 215 − 207 = 8.

questions.text: The average weight of a family of five members (in kg) whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 72 kg and 37 kg is:
The average weight of 20 boys is 60 kg. Together with 30 girls, the average weight of all boys and girls is 54 kg. What is the average weight of 30 girls in kg?
questions.explanation: All 50 together weigh 50 × 54 = 2,700 kg and the boys 20 × 60 = 1,200 kg, so the 30 girls weigh 1,500 kg: 1,500/30 = 50 kg.

questions.text: The ratio of prices of coffee and tea is 5 : 7 and the ratio of their quantities consumed by a family is 7 : 9. Find the ratio of expenditures on coffee and tea.
questions.explanation: Expenditure = price × quantity: (5 × 7) : (7 × 9) = 35 : 63 = 5 : 9.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2000 as a sum borrowed at 6% per year rate of interest for 5 years.

Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts,decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All parrots are eagles. Some parrots are ostriches. Conclusions: (I) Some eagles are parrots. (II) Some eagles are ostriches.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: All parrots are eagles, so some eagles are parrots (I). The parrots that are ostriches are also eagles, so some eagles are ostriches (II). Both follow.

questions.text: Which two numbers should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? (24 ÷ 6) + (18 × 4) – 54 + 42 = 99 (Note: Interchange should be done of entire number and not individual digits of a given number)

A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a round table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). C is sitting to the immediate left of A and immediate right of E. E is sitting to the immediate right of B. D is sitting to the immediate left of B and immediate right of F. A is sitting to the immediate left of G. Who is sitting to the immediate right of G?
questions.explanation: Going round the table to each person's right: F, D, B, E, C, A, G, and back to F (D is right of F, B right of D, E right of B, C right of E, A right of C, G right of A). So F sits to G's immediate right.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘TURF’ is coded as ‘5691’ and ‘RAFT’ is coded as ‘6935’. What is the code for ‘A’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: T, R and F are in both words, as are 5, 6 and 9 in both codes. The letter left in RAFT is A and the digit left in its code is 3, so A = 3.

questions.text: NUQM is related to PWSO in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, JQMI is related to LSOK. To which of the following is QXTP related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places forward: N → P, U → W, Q → S, M → O and J → L, Q → S, M → O, I → K. So QXTP → SZVR.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order ? BDG, HJM, NPS, TVY, ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 6 places forward from one cluster to the next, wrapping round after Z: B, H, N, T, Z; D, J, P, V, B; G, M, S, Y, E. The next cluster is ZBE.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 5 + 3 – 10 × 2 ÷ 2 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 5 − 3 + 10 ÷ 2 × 2 = 5 − 3 + 10 = 12.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (8, 64, 2) (12, 12, 1)
questions.explanation: The second number is the first raised to the power of the third: 8² = 64 and 12¹ = 12. Likewise 4⁴ = 256.

questions.text: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order).Only two people sit between E and F when counted from the right of E. Only two people sit between F and C. Only three people sit between E and B. D sits to the immediate left of A. How many people sit between A and G when counted from the left of A?
questions.explanation: Number the seats 1 to 7 going to E's right, with E in seat 1. F is then in seat 4, C (two people from F) in seat 7 and B (three people from E) in seat 5. D is immediately to A's left, which leaves A in seat 3, D in seat 2 and G in seat 6. Counting to A's left come D, E and C, then G: three people.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 115 117 123 125 131 ?
questions.explanation: The differences alternate +2 and +6: 115, 117, 123, 125, 131, so the next term is 131 + 2 = 133.

questions.text: In a certain language, 'INCH' is coded as '9631', and 'THIN' is coded as '3269'. What is the code for ‘T’ in 'THIN'?
questions.explanation: I, N and H are in both words, as are 9, 6 and 3 in both codes. The letter left in THIN is T and the digit left in its code is 2, so T = 2.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some ants are flies. All flies are bees. Conclusions: (I): No ant is a bee. (II): Some ants are bees.
questions.explanation: The ants that are flies are bees, since all flies are bees, so some ants are bees (II). That contradicts I, which does not follow.

questions.text: ODGM is related to NBFK in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, TAYP is related to SYXN. To which of the following is RJFB related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: The letters move −1, −2, −1, −2: ODGM → NBFK and TAYP → SYXN. So RJFB → QHEZ (B moved back 2 wraps round to Z).

questions.text: 12 is related to 81 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 24 is related to 153. To which ofthe following is 19 related, following the same logic?(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbersinto its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: The second number is six times the first plus 9: 12 × 6 + 9 = 81 and 24 × 6 + 9 = 153. Likewise 19 × 6 + 9 = 123.

questions.text: In a certain code language,‘legs hands ears’ is coded as ‘du ph bq’,‘hands eyes hearts’ is coded as ‘ak fd du’,‘ears hearts arms’ is coded as ‘fd bq dy’. What is the code for‘eyes’ in that language?(Note: All the codes are two-letter coded only.)
questions.explanation: 'hands' is in the first two sentences and 'du' in both their codes, so hands = du; likewise hearts = fd (sentences 2 and 3) and ears = bq (1 and 3). In the second sentence that leaves eyes = ak.

questions.text: It is observed that a child's heart rate is 135 times per minute. The beat frequency of heart is ____.
questions.explanation: Frequency is beats per second: 135 ÷ 60 = 2.25 Hz.

questions.text: Who first postulated that cells are generated from pre-existing cells?
questions.explanation: Rudolf Virchow (1855) proposed that new cells arise only from pre-existing cells: 'omnis cellula e cellula'.

questions.text: The Ebony, Mahogany, Cinchona etc. are trees found in which type of forests in India?
questions.explanation: NCERT names ebony, mahogany, rosewood, rubber and cinchona as important trees of India's tropical evergreen forests.

questions.text: In October 2023, Raghubar Das has been appointed the Governor of which of the following states of India?
questions.explanation: Raghubar Das, a former Chief Minister of Jharkhand, was appointed Governor of Odisha in October 2023.

questions.text: What kind of structures are generally used by Buddhists for containing remains of their monks and nuns?
questions.explanation: Stupas are mounds built over relics of the Buddha or of revered monks and nuns. Viharas were monasteries where monks lived, and the garbha griha is a temple's sanctum.

questions.text: Jaiminiya and Kausitaki dances are mentioned in which of the following?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the Brahmanas: the Jaiminiya and the Kausitaki are Brahmanas, prose texts attached to the Sama Veda and the Rig Veda, and are said to mention dance together with music.

questions.text: Geeta Chandran received the Padma Shri in 2007 who is an acclaimed ________ dancer.
questions.explanation: Geeta Chandran, an acclaimed Bharatanatyam dancer, received the Padma Shri in 2007.

questions.text: Analgesic medicines are used for _________________.
options: correcting deficiencies due to vitamins and nutrients
killing or weakening microbes and infections
questions.explanation: Analgesics reduce or abolish pain; many, such as aspirin and paracetamol, also bring down fever. Antimicrobials act against microbes, and supplements make up deficiencies.

questions.text: Ustad Ghagge Khuda Baksh was associated with which of the following gharanas?
questions.explanation: Ghagge Khuda Baksh is credited with bringing khayal singing into the Agra gharana and is often called its founder.

questions.text: Who was the first feudatory of Pallavas?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Vijayalaya, the only one of the four linked to the Pallavas: he is generally held to have been their feudatory when he took Thanjavur in the mid-ninth century and founded the imperial Chola line. Harshavardhana and Ashoka ruled in the north, and Rajendra was a later Chola emperor.

questions.text: As per the National Multidimensional Poverty Index Report 2021, which of the following states has the least population under poverty?
questions.explanation: In NITI Aayog's National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2021 (based on NFHS-4, 2015-16), Sikkim's share of poor people (3.82%) was lower than Tamil Nadu's (4.89%), Punjab's (5.59%) and Himachal Pradesh's (7.62%).

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following was the Viceroy of India during the announcement of the Partition of Bengal in 1905?
questions.explanation: Lord Curzon was Viceroy when the Partition of Bengal was announced in 1905; it took effect on 16 October 1905.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an important function of the Supreme Court?
options: It is the protector and guarantor of fundamental rights
It acts to check on executive authorities and enforce the rule of law
It maintains of land records and revenue collection
questions.explanation: Land records and revenue collection are the work of state revenue departments. The Supreme Court guards Fundamental Rights, settles disputes between the Union and the states, and checks the executive through judicial review.

questions.text: Which of the following is considered as a day of mourning among the Muslim community?
questions.explanation: Muharram, above all its tenth day, Ashura, is observed as a time of mourning for Imam Husain, killed at Karbala in 680 AD.

questions.text: In which of the following states is shifting agriculture locally called Penda?
questions.explanation: NCERT lists the local names of slash-and-burn (shifting) agriculture: 'Podu' or 'Penda' in Andhra Pradesh, 'Bewar' or 'Dahiya' in Madhya Pradesh, and 'Pama Dabi', 'Koman' or 'Bringa' in Odisha.

questions.text: In January 2023, the Warehouse Development Regulation Authority (WDRA) signed a memorandum of understanding with _________________ of India to help farmers get low interest rate loans.
questions.explanation: In January 2023 the WDRA and the State Bank of India signed an MoU to promote SBI's Produce Marketing Loan, lent to farmers against electronic negotiable warehouse receipts (e-NWRs) at low interest.

questions.text: What is the standard length of an Olympic-size swimming pool?
questions.explanation: An Olympic-size swimming pool is 50 metres long.

questions.text: Who among the following was the captain of the Indian cricket team during the 1983 Cricket World Cup event?
questions.explanation: Kapil Dev captained India to its first World Cup title in 1983, beating the West Indies in the final at Lord's.

questions.text: All living organisms on the Earth are made up of carbon compounds. Many years ago, dead and buried plants started slowly modifying into coal under high temperature and high pressure. This process is called:
questions.explanation: The slow conversion of buried dead vegetation into coal under high temperature and pressure is called carbonisation.

questions.text: Which Article of the Constitution of India lays down qualifications for the membership of the Parliament?
questions.explanation: Article 84 sets out the qualifications for membership of Parliament. Article 80 deals with the composition of the Rajya Sabha, Article 85 with the sessions of Parliament and Article 105 with members' privileges.

questions.text: Who among the following has written the famous novels (originally in Bangla) ‘Devdas’ and ‘Parineeta’?
questions.explanation: Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay wrote both 'Devdas' and 'Parineeta'.

questions.text: Recreation services are an example of _________.
questions.explanation: Recreation services are bought by households for their own final use, so they count as consumer goods (consumer services). Capital and intermediate goods are used in further production, and 'inferior' goods are those whose demand falls as income rises.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Maria was unhappy / because she terribly performed / in the examination / conducted last month.
questions.explanation: The adverb belongs after the verb: 'because she performed terribly'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. Ritesh remarked, "Honesty is a great “virtue”."
questions.explanation: 'Virtue' is moral goodness; its opposite is 'wickedness'. 'Probity', 'integrity' and 'rectitude' are synonyms.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and complete the expression. I begin to pronounce the sequence of words and numbers that will prevent her from giving him a piece of her ____________.
questions.explanation: To give someone 'a piece of one's mind' is to tell them angrily what one thinks of them.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. She was amazed by / the unique architecture of / the Sydney Opera House.
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct: 'amazed by' takes what causes the amazement, here 'the unique architecture of the Sydney Opera House'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. There was no one left in the world whom they could call _______.
questions.explanation: The possessive pronoun 'theirs' stands without a noun: someone they could call their own. 'Their' needs a noun after it, 'there's' means 'there is', and 'their's' is not a word.

questions.text: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
options: It is the obvious that child needs love and attention of parents.
It is obvious that a child needs love and attention of parents.
It is a obvious that child needs love and attention of parents.
It is an obvious that child needs love and attention of parents.
questions.explanation: The predicative adjective 'obvious' takes no article ('It is obvious that'), while the singular countable noun 'child' needs one: 'a child needs'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in brackets to fill in the blank. He spoke softly and ____________ (tensely), trying to diffuse the tense situation.
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'tensely' is 'calmly', which fits speaking softly to ease a tense situation.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Exemplary
questions.explanation: 'Exemplary' means good enough to serve as an example: 'excellent'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. He told / his senior, "I / will sung a song / at the party tonight."
questions.explanation: 'Will' takes the base form of the verb: 'I will sing a song'. 'Sung' is the past participle.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given word. Improbable
questions.explanation: 'Improbable' means unlikely to be true or to happen: 'implausible'. 'Plausible' is its opposite.

questions.text: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks. The touch-sensitive surface is one of the reasons why tablets and smart phones are so smart. All touchscreens generate an electric field ______________ the screen. Your finger interferes with the field, and the device's operating system ______________ your touch or swipe.
questions.explanation: The field spreads 'across' the screen, and the operating system 'follows', that is tracks, the touch or swipe. 'Escorts', 'chases' and 'attends' do not describe how a device registers a touch.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word to fill in the blank and make the sentence meaningful. Anuradha travelled to Italy last summer and _____________________ the historic ruins of Rome.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'explored'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A room in a hospital used especially for sunbathing or therapeutic exposure to light
questions.explanation: A solarium is a room built to let in sunlight, for sunbathing or light therapy. A sanatorium treats long-term illness, a planetarium shows the night sky, and a podium is a raised platform.

questions.text: In the following sentence the underlined part contains as error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative. It is very “hottest” over here.
questions.explanation: 'Very' goes with the positive degree, not the superlative: 'It is very hot over here.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. He is “reluctant” to do the work.
questions.explanation: 'Reluctant' means unwilling: 'hesitant'. 'Eager' and 'disposed' are near opposites.

questions.text: Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'deliverance'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The students were captivated by the __________ story told by their teacher.
questions.explanation: A story that captivated the students was 'compelling', one that holds attention. 'Mundane' (dull), 'superfluous' (unnecessary) and 'obsolete' (outdated) do not fit.

questions.text: Correct the underlined part of the sentence. The rabbit runs “fastly”.
questions.explanation: 'Fast' is both an adjective and an adverb, and 'fastly' is not standard English: 'The rabbit runs fast.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. It's raining cats and dogs.
options: There are cats and dogs in the rain.
It's a perfect day for a picnic.
questions.explanation: 'It's raining cats and dogs' means it is raining very heavily.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'conscientious'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. As community-minded creatures who want (1)_________________ to belong, we often mirror others, including on social media, where we adopt phrasing, tone and expressions of emotion. In the past few years, social media has had a (2)________________ on hyper positivity: think cheery emojis and (3)____________________ quotes plastered over sunsets. Some put this 'good vibes only' trend down to the pandemic and a (4)______________ to avoid painful feelings when (5)____________________ on difficult realities. However, attempting to convey constant happiness is not only difficult but impossible.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Creatures who want 'deeply' to belong: the adverb fits the strong human need to belong.

questions.text:

questions.text: Five athletes are weighed consecutively, and after each measurement, their average weight is calculated. If the average weight increases by 1.5 kg each time, then how much heavier is the last player than the first player?
questions.explanation: If the first athlete weighs w, the averages are w, w + 1.5, w + 3, w + 4.5 and w + 6, so the totals are w, 2w + 3, 3w + 9, 4w + 18 and 5w + 30. The last athlete weighs (5w + 30) − (4w + 18) = w + 12: 12 kg more than the first.

questions.text: It takes15 seconds for a 375-m long train to pass a pole. How long will it take to pass a 975-m long platform?
questions.explanation: Speed = 375/15 = 25 m/s. To pass the platform the train covers 375 + 975 = 1,350 m: 1,350/25 = 54 seconds.

questions.text: What is the cost of a tadpole required to make a conical tent with slant height 15 m and height 9 m, when one square meter tadpole costs ₹147?
questions.explanation: The radius is √(15² − 9²) = 12 m, so the canvas (the 'tadpole', i.e. tarpaulin) covers πrl = (22/7) × 12 × 15 = 3,960/7 m². At ₹147 a square metre: 3,960/7 × 147 = ₹83,160.

questions.text: A thief steels a bike at 10:30 am and drives it at 50 km/hr. But the thief is found after half an hour. The bike owner started to chase him by another bike at 60 km/hr. The time at which the thief is caught is:
questions.explanation: By 11:00 am, when the chase begins, the thief is 50 × ½ = 25 km ahead. The owner gains 60 − 50 = 10 km/h, so he takes 25/10 = 2.5 hours: 1:30 pm.

questions.text: The greatest number of four digits which is divisible by each one of the numbers 15, 25, 40 and 75 is:
questions.explanation: LCM of 15, 25, 40 and 75 = 2³ × 3 × 5² = 600. The greatest four-digit multiple of 600 is 600 × 16 = 9600.

questions.text: Rakesh obtained a simple interest of ₹3,195 on a certain principal in 6 years at the rate of 15% per annum. What amount of simple interest would he get if he invested ₹1,250 more than the previous principal for 3 years at the same rate of interest?
questions.explanation: Principal = 3,195 × 100/(15 × 6) = ₹3,550. The new principal is 3,550 + 1,250 = ₹4,800, and its interest for 3 years is 4,800 × 15 × 3/100 = ₹2,160.

questions.text: A conical cavity is drilled in a solid circular cylinder of 7 cm height and 48 cm base diameter. The height and base diameter of the cone are the same as those of the cylinder. What is the total surface area of the remaining solid?
questions.explanation: Radius 24 cm; the cavity's slant height is √(24² + 7²) = 25 cm. The remaining solid's surface is the cylinder's curved surface, its base and the cone's curved surface: 2π × 24 × 7 + π × 24² + π × 24 × 25 = 336π + 576π + 600π = 1512π cm².

questions.text: When the price of a laptop was reduced by 15%, its sales increased by 10%. What was the net effect on the sale?
questions.explanation: Sales value = price × quantity: 0.85 × 1.10 = 0.935 of the old value, a 6.5% decrease.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2000 as a sum borrowed at 7% per year rate of interest for 6 years.
The average age of a class of 39 students is 20 years. If the age of the teacher is included, then the average increases by 6 months. Find the age of the teacher (in years).
questions.explanation: The 39 students' ages total 39 × 20 = 780 years. With the teacher, 40 people average 20.5 years, a total of 820, so the teacher is 820 − 780 = 40.

questions.text: In what proportion must a man mix milk worth ₹3.3/litre with milk worth ₹1.8/litre so that the mixture may be worth ₹2.4/litre?
questions.explanation: By alligation, milk at ₹3.3 and at ₹1.8 is mixed in the ratio (2.4 − 1.8) : (3.3 − 2.4) = 0.6 : 0.9 = 2 : 3.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2500 as a sum borrowed at 5% per year rate of interest for 3 years.
The average weight of a family of five members (in kg) whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 71 kg and 38 kg is:
Ramesh purchased a piano, marked at ₹18,000 at a successive discounts of 12% and 15%, respectively. Ramesh gave ₹536 as transportation charge and sold it at ₹21,000. What is his gain percentage?

17 is related to 119 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 31 is related to 217. To which of the following is 32 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding / subtracting / multiplying, etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each number is multiplied by 7: 17 × 7 = 119 and 31 × 7 = 217. Likewise 32 × 7 = 224.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 14 ÷ 6 + 9 × 3 − 2 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 14 × 6 − 9 ÷ 3 + 2 = 84 − 3 + 2 = 83.

questions.text: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Only one person sits between D and A when counted from the right of D. Only one person sits between A and B. Only one person sits between D and G. Only two people sit between E and B, when counted from the right of E. Only one person sits between F and G. Who sits third to the right of C ?
questions.explanation: Seated clockwise (each person's left, facing the centre): D, C, G, B, F, A, E, which meets every condition. Going from C to its right (anticlockwise): D, E, A, so A is third to the right of C.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (37, 58, 100) (35, 70, 110)
questions.explanation: The third number is the sum of the first two plus 5: 37 + 58 + 5 = 100 and 35 + 70 + 5 = 110. Likewise 8 + 13 + 5 = 26.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which conclusion/s logically follow/s from the given statements. Statements: All boxes are glasses. All glasses are cups. Some cups are bottles. Conclusions: (I): All boxes are cups. (II): Some glasses are bottles.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
questions.explanation: All boxes are glasses and all glasses are cups, so all boxes are cups (I). The cups that are bottles need not be glasses, so II does not follow.

questions.text: IOZU is related to HNYT in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, PDYC is related to OCXB. To which of the following is EJSW related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 1 place back: IOZU → HNYT and PDYC → OCXB. So EJSW → DIRV.

questions.text: In a certain code,‘curtain door window’ is coded as ‘la ph ba’,‘lock window key’ is coded as ‘ep zm la’,‘key curtain handle’ is coded as ‘fd ba zm’. What is the code for ‘curtain’ in that language?(Note: All the codes are two-letter coded only.)
questions.explanation: 'window' is in the first two phrases and 'la' in both their codes, so window = la; 'key' is in the last two and 'zm' in both their codes, so key = zm. 'curtain' is in the first and the last, and the code they share is 'ba'.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘−‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 66 × 6 − 15 ÷ 3 + 9 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 66 ÷ 6 + 15 × 3 − 9 = 11 + 45 − 9 = 47.

questions.text: A, D, K, N, Y and Z are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Z is sitting third to the right of D. K is not the immediate neighbour of Z. A is sitting second to the left of Z. N is not the immediate neighbour of A. Who is the immediate neighbour of both between A and K?
questions.explanation: Seated clockwise (each person's left, facing the centre): D, K, N, Z, Y, A. Z is opposite D, A is second to Z's left, and K and N then take the only seats that keep them away from Z and A. D sits between A and K.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some books are wood. All wood is fire. Conclusions: (I) Some fire is wood. (II) All books are fire.
questions.explanation: Some books are wood and all wood is fire, so some fire is wood (I). The books that are not wood need not be fire, so II does not follow.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 219 222 227 234 ? 254
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? GJD ,IHH, KFL, MDP, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move 2 forward (G, I, K, M, so O), second letters 2 back (J, H, F, D, so B) and third letters 4 forward (D, H, L, P, so T): OBT.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘complete the task’ is written as ‘je tc xo’ and ‘work is complete’ is coded as ‘xo ig lx’. How is ‘complete’ coded in the given language?
questions.explanation: 'complete' is the only word in both sentences and 'xo' the only code in both, so complete = xo.

questions.text: OT11 is related to PU15 in a certain way. In the same way, WB21 is related to XC25. To which of the following is DI31 related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 1 place forward and the number rises by 4: OT11 → PU15 and WB21 → XC25. So DI31 → EJ35.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘this is book’ is written as ‘lo mo ro’ and ‘this is me’ is written as ‘mo lo po’. How is ‘me’ written in the given code language?
questions.explanation: 'this' and 'is' are in both sentences, as are 'lo' and 'mo' in both codes. The word left in the second sentence is 'me' and the code left is 'po', so me = po.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘FITCH’ is coded as ‘47601’ and ‘DITCH’ is coded as ‘70619’. What is the code for ‘D’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: I, T, C and H are in both words, as are 7, 6, 0 and 1 in both codes. The letter left in DITCH is D and the digit left in its code is 9, so D = 9.

questions.text: ‘Bayalata’ is a famous folk dance of which of the following Indian states?
questions.explanation: Bayalata, literally 'open-field play', is a folk dance-drama of Karnataka performed in the open air.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which year was the first session of the Indian National Congress held?
questions.explanation: The first session of the Indian National Congress met in Bombay in December 1885, presided over by W.C. Bonnerjee.

questions.text: In a laterite soil profile, which of the following elements is present in an excessive amount?
questions.explanation: Laterite soils form under heavy rain and high heat, which leach away lime and silica; what remains is rich in iron oxide and aluminium compounds.

questions.text: What is the chemical reaction that occurs when sugar is heated and turns into a caramel syrup?
questions.explanation: Heated on its own, sugar breaks down into the brown, flavourful compounds of caramel: caramelisation. The Maillard reaction needs amino acids (proteins) as well as sugars.

questions.text: Who among the following is known as the 'Mozart of Madras'?
questions.explanation: The composer A.R. Rahman, born in Madras (Chennai), is called the 'Mozart of Madras'.

questions.text: Devendra Fadnavis became the ___________ of the state of Maharashtra on 30th June 2022.
questions.explanation: Devendra Fadnavis was sworn in as Deputy Chief Minister of Maharashtra on 30 June 2022, when Eknath Shinde became Chief Minister.

questions.text: Which of the following States/Union Territories is NOT a part of Indus River Basin?
questions.explanation: Sikkim is drained by the Teesta, part of the Brahmaputra system. Ladakh, Jammu and Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh are drained mainly by the Indus and its tributaries.

questions.text: The Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee of the Constituent Assembly was headed by ____________.
questions.explanation: The Constituent Assembly's sub-committee on Fundamental Rights was chaired by J.B. Kripalani, under the Advisory Committee headed by Sardar Patel.

questions.text: In which of the following months is the Konark Dance festival organised in Odisha?
questions.explanation: The Konark Dance Festival is held every year from 1 to 5 December at the open-air auditorium near the Sun Temple.

questions.text: The Hathigumpha Inscription was inscribed in which of the following historical regions of India?
questions.explanation: The Hathigumpha inscription, in the Udayagiri caves near Bhubaneswar, records the reign of Kharavela, king of Kalinga.

questions.text: The transportation mechanism in cells by which food or other useful molecules from the outside are carried inside the cell is known as _______________.
questions.explanation: In endocytosis the cell membrane folds round material outside the cell and takes it in; exocytosis is the reverse, and osmosis is the movement of water across a membrane.

questions.text: Where does the cash grants in aid from foreign countries are classified?
questions.explanation: In the government budget, cash grants-in-aid from foreign countries and international organisations are counted as non-tax revenue, along with interest, dividends, profits and fees.

questions.text: Sachin Tendulkar scored his 100th international century against which country?
questions.explanation: Sachin Tendulkar's 100th international century came against Bangladesh at Mirpur, in the 2012 Asia Cup.

questions.text: Which of the following para athletes is associated with the javelin throw event?
questions.explanation: Devendra Jhajharia won Paralympic gold in the javelin throw in 2004 and 2016. Sharad Kumar is a high jumper and Pramod Bhagat a badminton player.

questions.text: When was ‘Nai Chetna-Pahal Badlav Ki’ campaign launched?
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Rural Development (DAY-NRLM) launched 'Nai Chetna', a national campaign against gender-based violence, on 25 November 2022.

questions.text: What is the full form of INSAT?
questions.explanation: INSAT is the Indian National Satellite System, ISRO's series of geostationary satellites for communication, broadcasting and weather services.

questions.text: Under the influence of the Greeks, which of the following art styles flourished in India?
questions.explanation: Gandhara art, which grew up in the north-west under Greek (Hellenistic) influence, shows the Buddha in a Greco-Roman style. The Mathura and Amaravati schools were largely indigenous.

questions.text: National Urban Livelihood Mission (NULM) was launched in which of the following Five Year plans?
questions.explanation: The National Urban Livelihoods Mission was launched in September 2013, during the Twelfth Five Year Plan (2012-17), replacing the Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rozgar Yojana.

questions.text: According to Census 2011 of India, which Union Territory has the second highest percentage of urban population?
questions.explanation: In the 2011 census Delhi (97.5%) had the highest share of urban population among the Union Territories, followed by Chandigarh (97.25%).

questions.text: 'Unbreakable' is an autobiography of _________________ published in 2013.
questions.explanation: 'Unbreakable' (2013) is the autobiography of the boxer M.C. Mary Kom.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following events took place in the year 1928?
questions.explanation: The Bardoli Satyagraha, led by Vallabhbhai Patel against a rise in land revenue, took place in 1928. The Kakori incident was in 1925, the Kheda Satyagraha in 1918 and the Dandi March in 1930.

questions.text: As per the treaty of Purandar, how many forts were surrendered by Shivaji to Mughals?
questions.explanation: By the Treaty of Purandar (1665) with Raja Jai Singh, Shivaji surrendered 23 forts to the Mughals and kept 12.

questions.text: The number of Rajya Sabha members to be elected from each State of India has been fixed by the _________ Schedule of the Constitution.
questions.explanation: The Fourth Schedule allocates the seats in the Rajya Sabha to the States and Union Territories.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. In order to maintain good governance, every government servant must be held ______ for his/her decisions.
questions.explanation: Good governance needs servants who answer for their decisions: 'held accountable'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The team was gradually realising that the social gatherings were “draining”.
questions.explanation: 'Draining' means tiring and wearing; its opposite here is 'absorbing', holding one's interest.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence. Many biologists have stated the fact that most of the herbs are perinnial and have healing qualities with added flavour.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'perennial'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. In addition with / the existing crisis in economy, / the rise of hunger index / is another cause of worry.
questions.explanation: The phrase is 'in addition to': 'In addition to the existing crisis in economy'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The inclusion of Durga Puja in the UNESCO's list of Intangible Cultural Heritage was only possible due to the arduous ________ of all stakeholders.
questions.explanation: The inclusion was possible due to the 'arduous efforts', the hard work, of all stakeholders; 'affects' is a verb.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. My sister Mona / never drinks coffee; / she prefer tea / in the morning.
questions.explanation: A third-person singular subject takes 'prefers': 'she prefers tea in the morning'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'machinery'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Most probably, / he come / to office / next Tuesday.
questions.explanation: 'Next Tuesday' is in the future, so 'he will come'; 'he come' also lacks the singular verb form.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. The bishop sadly declared that the poor gentleman who was dead was “quieter” of the community.
questions.explanation: 'Of the community' compares him with everyone in it, so the superlative: 'the quietest of the community'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence. The neighbour came in disgoise and attacked her children.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'disguise'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. Reduced price of cooking gas brought “happy” to the face of every citizen.
questions.explanation: 'Brought' needs a noun as its object: 'brought happiness to the face of every citizen'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'. Rishi Sunak, the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom and Leader of the Conservative Party, “was born into” Southampton to parents of Indian descent who immigrated to Britain from East Africa in the 1960s.
questions.explanation: One is born 'in' a place: 'was born in Southampton'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. The moment James saw Regena, he fell “head on to his heels” in love with her.
questions.explanation: To fall 'head over heels' in love is to fall deeply in love.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Beat around the bush
options: To avoid getting to the point of an issue
questions.explanation: To 'beat around the bush' is to avoid coming to the point.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the bracketed word to fill in the blank. The rainbow arched gracefully across the sky, painting it in __________ (lifeless) hues.
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'lifeless' is 'vibrant', full of life and colour; 'muted' is close to lifeless.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Pacify
questions.explanation: To 'pacify' is to calm someone; its opposite is 'enrage'.

questions.text: Read the following sentence and select its future tense form from the following options. The food company promoted newly launched products at affordable prices.
options: The food company is promoting newly launched products at affordable prices.
The food company will be promoting newly launched products at affordable prices.
The food company promotes newly launched products at affordable prices.
The food company had promoted newly launched products at affordable prices.
questions.explanation: 'Will be promoting' (the future continuous) is the only future form offered; the others are the present continuous, the simple present and the past perfect.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate adverb to fill in the blank. The explorers trekked __________ through the dense jungle.
questions.explanation: The blank needs an adverb of manner saying how they trekked: 'bravely'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Delay
questions.explanation: To 'delay' is to put off or slow down; its opposite is 'hasten'.

questions.text: Amithab has scored an average of 72 runs in his six interschool matches. In the next match, he scored 96 runs. What is his revised average score?
questions.explanation: Six matches at 72 make 6 × 72 = 432 runs; with 96 more the total is 528 over 7 matches: 528/7 = 75.428...

The average weight of a group of 8 people is 70 kg. After a new person joins the group, the average weight becomes 72 kg. What is the weight (in kg) of the new person?
questions.explanation: The total rises from 8 × 70 = 560 kg to 9 × 72 = 648 kg, so the new person weighs 648 − 560 = 88 kg.

questions.text: A person invested a certain sum of money at 6% per annum simple interest and another sum at 8% per annum simple interest at the same time. After 4 years, he received interest ₹1,560 from both sums. One-fifth of the first sum is equal to one-sixth of the second sum. Find the total sum invested.
questions.explanation: One-fifth of the first sum equals one-sixth of the second, so the sums are 5k and 6k. A year's interest is 0.06 × 5k + 0.08 × 6k = 0.78k, and 4 × 0.78k = 1,560 gives k = 500. Total = 11k = ₹5,500.

questions.text: The side of a square exceeds the side of another square by 3 cm and the sum of the areas of the two squares is 225 cm² . Find the sum of the perimeter (in cm) of both squares.
questions.explanation: With sides x + 3 and x: (x + 3)² + x² = 225, so x² + 3x − 108 = 0 and x = 9. The sides are 12 cm and 9 cm, and the perimeters add up to 4 × (12 + 9) = 84 cm.

questions.text: A well with an internal diameter 10 m is dug to a depth of 10 m. Earth taken out of it is spread all around the well to a width of 12 m to form an embankment. What is the height (in m, rounded off to 2 decimal places) of the embankment?
questions.explanation: Earth dug out = π × 5² × 10 = 250π m³. The embankment is a ring from radius 5 m to 5 + 12 = 17 m, of area π(17² − 5²) = 264π m². Height = 250π/264π = 0.947 ≈ 0.95 m.

questions.text: What sum (in ₹) will earn a simple interest of ₹360 in 2 years at 8% per year rate of interest?
Raima saves 14% from her income of ₹35,000. How much is her expenditure (in ₹)?

A thief is noticed by a policeman from a distance of 150 m. The thief starts running, and the policeman chases him. The thief and the policeman run at the rate of 8 m/s and 10 m/s, respectively. Find the distance travelled by the thief before being caught.
questions.explanation: The policeman gains 10 − 8 = 2 m/s on the thief, so he closes the 150 m gap in 75 seconds. In that time the thief runs 8 × 75 = 600 m.

questions.text: A dealer marked the price of an item 30% above the cost price. He allowed two successive discounts of 15% and 20% to a particular customer. As a result, he incurred a loss of ₹696. At what price did he sell the item to the customer?
questions.explanation: With cost price C, the selling price is 1.3C × 0.85 × 0.8 = 0.884C, a loss of 0.116C = ₹696. So C = ₹6,000 and the selling price is 0.884 × 6,000 = ₹5,304.

questions.text: The average of 70 values is 40. If each value is multiplied by 20, what will be the changed average?
questions.explanation: Multiplying every value by 20 multiplies the average by 20: 40 × 20 = 800.

questions.text: If the radius of the base of a right circular cylinder is reduced to one-third, keeping the height same, what is the ratio of the volume of the reduced cylinder to that of the original?
questions.explanation: V = πr²h, so with the height unchanged the volume varies as r²: (1/3)² = 1/9, a ratio of 1 : 9.

questions.text: If two kinds of resins costing ₹160 per kg and ₹210 per kg are mixed in the ratio of 2 : 3, then find the cost (in ₹) of the mixture per kg.

A length of a violin string varies inversely with respect to the frequency of its vibrations. The frequency of a 14-inch-long violin string is 450 cycles per second. Find the frequency of a 12-inch violin string.
questions.explanation: Length × frequency stays the same: 14 × 450 = 6,300, so a 12-inch string vibrates at 6,300/12 = 525 cycles per second.

questions.text: KB 9 is related to ED 2 in a certain way. In the same way, XF 11 is related to RH 4. To which of the following is UH 8 related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: The first letter moves 6 back, the second 2 forward and the number falls by 7: K → E, B → D, 9 → 2 and X → R, F → H, 11 → 4. So U → O, H → J and 8 → 1: OJ 1.

questions.text: 326 is related to 335 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 419 is related to 428. To which of the following is 566 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding / subtracting / multiplying, etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is the first plus 9: 326 + 9 = 335 and 419 + 9 = 428. Likewise 566 + 9 = 575.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘TREE’ is coded as ‘POCD’ and ‘FOOT’ is coded as ‘BLMS’. How will ‘MIND’ be coded in the same language?
questions.explanation: The letters move back 4, 3, 2 and 1 places: TREE → POCD and FOOT → BLMS. So M → I, I → F, N → L and D → C: IFLC.

questions.text: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre(but not necessarily in the same order). F is sitting third to the left of A. A is sitting second to the left of G. G is sitting to the immediate right of E. B is sitting to the immediate left of D. What is the position of F with respect to E?
questions.explanation: Going round the table to each person's left from E: E, A, D, B, F, C, G. This fits every clue (G to E's immediate right, A second to G's left, F third to A's left, B to D's immediate left), and F is three places to E's right.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘apple pen card’ is coded as ‘136’, ‘doctor no apple’ is coded as ‘243’ and ‘card is blocked’ is coded as ‘695’. How is ‘apple’ coded in the given code language?
questions.explanation: 'apple' is the only word in both the first and second sentences and 3 the only digit in both their codes, so apple = 3.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? PKQ ,OJP, NIO ,MHN, ?
questions.explanation: Every letter moves one place back each time: P, O, N, M, L; K, J, I, H, G; Q, P, O, N, M. The next cluster is LGM.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) of the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 45 × 3 + 9 – 18 ÷ 1 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 45 ÷ 3 − 9 + 18 × 1 = 15 − 9 + 18 = 24.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the following series? 255, 248, 241, 234 ,227, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is 7 less than the one before: 227 − 7 = 220.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All doors are locks. Some locks are handles, Conclusions: (I) All handles are locks. (II) No door is a handle.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: Only some locks are said to be handles, and nothing is said of handles that are not locks, so I does not follow. The doors may or may not be among the locks that are handles, so II does not follow either.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement(s). Statements: All cabbages are roses. All cabbages are tulips. Conclusions: (I) At least some tulips are roses. (II) All roses are cabbages.
questions.explanation: Every cabbage is both a rose and a tulip, so some tulips are roses (I). Nothing says every rose is a cabbage, so II does not follow.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 11 × 7 − 48 + 6 ÷ 37 = 106
In a certain code language, ‘LIKE’ is coded as ‘4682’ and ‘BEAM’ is coded as ‘1358’.What is the code for ‘E’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: E is the only letter in both words and 8 the only digit in both codes, so E = 8.

questions.text: LQ87 is related to VA55 in a certain way. In the same way, QV59 is related to AF27. To which of the following is BG49 related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Both letters move 10 places forward (wrapping round after Z) and the number falls by 32: L → V, Q → A, 87 → 55 and Q → A, V → F, 59 → 27. So B → L, G → Q and 49 → 17: LQ17.

questions.text: In a code language, ‘I want food’ is written as ' sickota dongre dujubu’, ‘I want drink’ is written as ‘bluto sickota dujubu', ‘food and drink’ is written as ‘dongre peppin bluto’, then what is the code for the word 'peppin' in this language?
questions.explanation: 'I want' is in the first two sentences, so 'sickota' and 'dujubu' stand for 'I' and 'want'; that leaves food = dongre and drink = bluto. The code left over in the third sentence, 'peppin', is 'and'.

questions.text: T, N, S, P, R and M are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). S is sitting second to the left of T. Only two people are sitting between S and R. M is not the immediate neighbour of S. P is sitting second to the right of R. How many people are sitting between N and M, when counted from the right of N?
questions.explanation: Going round the table to each person's left from T: T, N, S, P, M, R (S second to T's left, R opposite S, P second to R's right, M not beside S). Counting from N to the right, T and R come before M: two people.

questions.text: In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 11, 66; 26, 156
questions.explanation: The second number is 6 times the first: 11 × 6 = 66 and 26 × 6 = 156. Likewise 18 × 6 = 108.

questions.text: The weaker warm storms that grow stronger over time are finally converted into huge storms or hurricanes. Which of the following climate regions is the origin of such hurricanes?
questions.explanation: Hurricanes are tropical cyclones: they form over warm tropical seas, whose surface water above about 27 °C supplies the heat and moisture that let a weak storm grow.

questions.text: Which type of loan is supported by MUDRA?
questions.explanation: MUDRA (Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency), set up in 2015, supports loans to non-corporate, non-farm small and micro enterprises under the Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana.

questions.text: India launched the ‘National Social Assistance Programme’ in:
questions.explanation: The National Social Assistance Programme, with old-age pension, family benefit and maternity benefit schemes, was launched on 15 August 1995.

questions.text: The Iron Age site named Tekwada is located in _________.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Maharashtra, where Tekwada is one of the excavated sites with Iron Age remains.

questions.text: In which of the following states is the Bissu Mela organised to thank Santoora Devi for the good harvest?
questions.explanation: The Bissu Mela of the Jaunsari people, held in the Jaunsar-Bawar area (Chakrata) of Uttarakhand's Dehradun district, honours the goddess Santoora Devi at harvest time.

questions.text: In Union Budget 2023, a sub-scheme of which of the following Yojanas has been proposed with the investment of ₹6,000 crore to enable activities of fishermen, fish vendors and micro and small enterprises?
questions.explanation: The Union Budget 2023-24 announced a new sub-scheme of the PM Matsya Sampada Yojana, with a targeted investment of ₹6,000 crore, for fishermen, fish vendors and micro and small enterprises.

questions.text: How many chances does a high jumper get for overcoming a certain height?
questions.explanation: A high jumper has three attempts at a height; three failures in a row put the athlete out of the competition.

questions.text: In Harappan civilisation, cities were planned with the streets generally oriented along the __________ directions.
questions.explanation: Harappan streets ran roughly north-south and east-west, the cardinal directions, crossing at right angles in a grid.

questions.text: In june 2022, Eknath Sambhaji Shinde became the Chief Minister of which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Eknath Shinde was sworn in as Chief Minister of Maharashtra on 30 June 2022.

questions.text: Which Census decade recorded the highest population growth rate (in terms of percentage) in India?
questions.explanation: India's population grew fastest in the 1961-1971 decade, by 24.80%, slightly more than in 1971-1981.

questions.text: To which of the following groups do whales belong?
questions.explanation: Whales breathe air through lungs, are warm-blooded and suckle their young: they are mammals, not fish.

questions.text: Who among the following received the Padma Shri 2021 for Panthi folk dance?
questions.explanation: Radhe Shyam Barle of Chhattisgarh received the Padma Shri in 2021 for Panthi, the folk dance of the Satnami community.

questions.text: The term 'Aus', 'Aman' and 'Boro' are associated with which crop in India?
questions.explanation: In West Bengal farmers grow three crops of rice (paddy) a year, called 'aus', 'aman' and 'boro'.

questions.text: What is the percentage of 's' character in the carbon atom of acetylene?
questions.explanation: Each carbon in acetylene (HC≡CH) is sp hybridised, one s and one p orbital, so it has 50% s character (sp² has 33.33%, sp³ 25%).

questions.text: Which of the following is the correct statement about the Rajya Sabha?
options: It is known as the Council of the States.
It is known as the lower house of the parliament.
All the members are directly elected by the people.
The term of the members is for 5 years.
questions.explanation: The Rajya Sabha is the Council of States, Parliament's upper house. Most of its members are elected indirectly by the state legislative assemblies, for six years.

questions.text: Anorexia Nervosa is an eating disorder characterised by _________. a) an abnormally heavy body weight b) an intense fear of losing weight c) a distorted perception of weight d) trying to lose weight by exercising excessively
questions.explanation: Anorexia nervosa involves a distorted perception of one's weight and efforts such as excessive exercise to lose weight. Sufferers have an abnormally low (not heavy) body weight and an intense fear of gaining (not losing) weight.

questions.text: Buddhadev Dasgupta was a famous instrumentalist of which of the following instrument?
questions.explanation: Pandit Buddhadev Dasgupta, a disciple of Radhika Mohan Maitra, was one of the leading sarod players of his time.

questions.text: Which of the following Mughal emperors issued silver coins in the honour of his wife Mehrunnisa?
questions.explanation: Mehrunnisa became Jahangir's queen, Nur Jahan, in 1611; Jahangir had coins struck in her name, a rare honour for a Mughal queen.

questions.text: The author of the Hindi novel ‘Kohre Mein Kaid Rang’ is:
questions.explanation: Govind Mishra won the 2008 Sahitya Akademi Award for his Hindi novel 'Kohre Mein Kaid Rang'.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following founded the 'Satyashodhak Samaj' in 1873?
questions.explanation: Jyotirao (Jyotiba) Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in Pune on 24 September 1873 to fight caste discrimination.

questions.text: Rabindranath Tagore referred to ____________ as Nritya Samragini, which translates to 'the empress of dance'.
questions.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore gave the Kathak dancer Sitara Devi the title 'Nritya Samragini' after seeing her dance as a girl.

questions.text: Which of the following Fundamental Rights entails trafficking of human beings and forced labour?
questions.explanation: The Right against Exploitation (Articles 23 and 24) bans trafficking in human beings and forced labour (Article 23) and the employment of children in hazardous work (Article 24).

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following founded the Asiatic Society of Bengal?
questions.explanation: Sir William Jones founded the Asiatic Society in Calcutta on 15 January 1784.

questions.text: Ujjwala was the mascot of which national sports event held in 2023?
questions.explanation: Ujjwala, a sparrow standing for Delhi, was the mascot of the first Khelo India Para Games, held in New Delhi in December 2023.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a physiographic division of India?
questions.explanation: NCERT divides India into six physiographic divisions: the Himalayan Mountains, the Northern Plains, the Peninsular Plateau, the Indian Desert, the Coastal Plains and the Islands. The Tibetan Plateau lies beyond the Himalayas, in Tibet.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate to substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. Rohit asked Nita what was the most “intriguing” book she has read recently.
questions.explanation: The instruction, as SSC printed it, is missing a word (most likely 'ANTONYM'). SSC's key gives 'tedious', dull and tiresome, the opposite of 'intriguing', fascinating; it is also the only option that makes sense in the sentence, and none of the options means the same as 'intriguing'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word..
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'occurrence'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The ancient Greeks and pagans used to worship natural _________ as Gods and Goddesses.
questions.explanation: The ancients worshipped natural 'elements', such as the sun, wind, water and fire, as gods and goddesses.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Most women are “facing the same problem” when it comes to job satisfaction because of the pay parity in institutions.
questions.explanation: To be 'in the same boat' is to share the same difficult situation with others.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Rose painted the most beautifullest picture ever at the art class today!
questions.explanation: 'Beautiful' takes 'most' for its superlative: 'the most beautiful picture'. 'Most beautifullest' is a double superlative, and 'beautifullest' is not a word.

questions.text: Correct the underlined part of the sentence. This mango is “bitterer”.
questions.explanation: Nothing is compared with the mango, so the positive degree is needed: 'This mango is bitter.'

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Inflamous' is not a word; the spelling is 'infamous', well known for something bad. 'Kerbstone' is the British spelling of 'curbstone'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. one who does something for pleasure
questions.explanation: A hedonist is one who lives for and pursues pleasure. (One who takes up an activity for pleasure rather than pay is an 'amateur', which is not among the options.)

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. Raju is “lazy” and smart, but he does not attend the classes.
questions.explanation: 'Lazy' means unwilling to work; its opposite is 'industrious', hard-working. 'Lax' is close to a synonym.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. He pressed the _________ just in time to avoid the accident.
questions.explanation: A vehicle is stopped with its 'brake'; 'break' sounds the same but means something else.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. Even if an unlaced shoe is spotless, it is not “neat”.
questions.explanation: 'Neat' means clean and tidy; its opposite is 'soiled', made dirty.

questions.text: Select the grammatically correct sentence..
options: The traffic on the highway was heavy during an evening.
A traffic on the highway was heavy during an evening.
The traffic on a highway was heavy during an evening.
The traffic on the highway was heavy during the evening.
questions.explanation: The highway and the evening are particular ones, so both take 'the': 'The traffic on the highway was heavy during the evening.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. My brother asked me, "Can I exchange “my phone from you”?"
questions.explanation: Of the options only 'with' goes with 'exchange': 'Can I exchange my phone with yours?' 'Since', 'off' and 'within' do not.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. Any declarations or practices of religious “antipathy” against ethnic minorities in a democratic country should not be tolerated.
questions.explanation: 'Antipathy' is a deep-seated dislike or hostility: 'enmity'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in future perfect tense form. I hope you wash all the clothes before you come into the house again.
options: I hope you will have wash all the clothes before you come into the house again.
I hope you shall wash all the clothes before you come into the house again
I hope you will have washed all the clothes before you come into the house again.
I hope you will be washing all the clothes before you come into the house again.
questions.explanation: The future perfect is 'will have' + past participle: 'will have washed'. 'Will have wash' uses the wrong form of the verb, and 'will be washing' is the future continuous.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word...
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'depressed'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Everyone disliked the new CEO, Kushal, but nobody is ready to “put themselves in dangerous situation” by telling him their feelings.
questions.explanation: To 'bell the cat' is to take on a dangerous task for the good of all: here, telling the disliked CEO what everyone feels.

questions.text: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
options: The intrepid explorer stumbled upon the uncharted cavern deep within the heart of the rainforest.
An intrepid explorer stumbled upon an uncharted cavern deep within the heart of the rainforest.
The intrepid explorer stumbled upon an uncharted cavern deep within a heart of the rainforest.
An intrepid explorer stumbled upon the uncharted cavern deep within a heart of the rainforest.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the sentence with 'an' for the explorer and the cavern, both met here for the first time, and 'the heart of the rainforest' (it has only one). The version with 'the' throughout is not ungrammatical, but it presumes an explorer and a cavern already known to the reader; 'a heart of the rainforest' is wrong.

questions.text: Read the sentence given below and identify if there is an error in it. The error can be in any segment of the sentence which are marked A, B, C, and D. Select option D if there is 'No error'. (A) She sings / (B) the song / (C) beautiful in the party / (D) No error.
questions.explanation: A verb is modified by an adverb: 'She sings the song beautifully', so the error is in C.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I am calling to thank you _________ the present you sent.
questions.explanation: One thanks someone 'for' something: 'thank you for the present'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Newspapers are like mirrors (1)___________ the diverse facets of society, capturing the voices, stories, and events that define our shared human experience. They serve as a forum (2)___________ dialogue, debate, and discussion, amplifying voices from all walks of life and fostering (3)___________ sense of community. Beyond reporting news, newspapers also celebrate achievements, highlight cultural (4)___________, and showcase human resilience in the face of adversity. They are archives of history, chronicling the triumphs and trials of generations, and serving as a reminder of how far we have come and how much further we can go. In an age of digital transformation, newspapers continue to (5)___________, adapting to new mediums while upholding the core values of journalism: accuracy, integrity, and accountability.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'Mirrors reflecting the diverse facets of society': the '-ing' participle describes the mirrors.
