markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: The average weight of 20 boys in a class is 65 kg and that of remaining 35 boys is 32 kg. What is the average weight of all the boys in the class?
The LCM of 140,180 and 240 is:
The average of five numbers, where the difference between any two consecutive numbers is 5, is 215. Find the least number.
questions.explanation: Five numbers 5 apart have their average in the middle, so they are 205, 210, 215, 220 and 225; the least is 205.

questions.text: A policeman sees a thief at a distance of 100 m and starts chasing him at a speed of 6 m/s while the thief runs at a speed of 5 m/s. What is the distance (in m) covered by the thief when he is caught?
questions.explanation: The policeman gains 6 − 5 = 1 m every second, so he closes the 100 m in 100 seconds. In that time the thief runs 5 × 100 = 500 m.

questions.text: Two stations A and B are 1800 km apart. A train starts from A towards B at 7 A.M. at a speed of 100 km/h. Another train starts from B towards A at 8 A.M. on the same day at a speed of 325 km/h. At what time will they cross each other?
questions.explanation: By 8 A.M. the first train has run 100 km, leaving 1700 km. The trains close it at 100 + 325 = 425 km/h, taking 1700/425 = 4 hours: they cross at 12 noon.

questions.text: A sum of money invested at simple interest becomes 5 times in 12 years. How many times will it become in 27 years?
questions.explanation: Becoming 5 times means the interest is 4 times the sum in 12 years, so 1/3 of the sum a year. In 27 years the interest is 9 times the sum, so the amount is 10 times.

questions.text: Due to a fault in the voting machine, the invalid votes are counted in votes of the candidate B, who gets 5 times the invalid votes. A gets the votes 8 times the invalid votes and wins the election by 28. What is the total number of votes polled?
questions.explanation: Let the invalid votes be x. B's own votes are 5x, and with the invalid ones counted in he has 6x; A has 8x. So 8x − 6x = 28 gives x = 14, and the votes polled are 8x + 5x + x = 14x = 196.

questions.text: What sum (in ₹) will earn a simple interest of ₹240 in 3 years at 4% per year rate of interest?
What sum (in ₹) will earn a simple interest of ₹240 in 3 years at 8% per year rate of interest?
The length and breadth of a rectangular field are in the ratio 3 : 2. If the area of the field is 3456 m², then the cost of fencing the field at ₹3.50 per metre is:
questions.explanation: With sides 3k and 2k, 6k² = 3456, so k = 24 and the field is 72 m by 48 m. Perimeter = 2(72 + 48) = 240 m, and 240 × ₹3.50 = ₹840.

questions.text: If x : 6 :: 6 : y and x : y :: y : 6, then which of the options below gives the correct values of x and y in that order?
questions.explanation: x : 6 :: 6 : y gives xy = 36, and x : y :: y : 6 gives y² = 6x. Substituting x = 36/y: y³ = 216, so y = 6 and x = 6.

questions.text: Out of 8 lecturers of a college, one lecturer retires and at his place a new lecturer of age 32 years joins. As a result, the average age of lecturers is reduced by 4 years. The age of the retired lecturer is:
questions.explanation: The total age of the 8 lecturers falls by 8 × 4 = 32 years, so the retired lecturer was 32 years older than the new one: 32 + 32 = 64 years.

questions.text: In what ratio must a shopkeeper mix two types of rice worth ₹60/kg and ₹80/kg, respectively, so that, the average cost of the mixture is ₹75/kg?
By selling an article for ₹19, a dealer makes a profit of 10%. By how much should he increase his selling price (in ₹, rounded off to two decimal place) so as to make a profit of 50%?
questions.explanation: Cost price = 19/1.1 = ₹190/11. For a 50% profit the selling price must be 1.5 × 190/11 = ₹285/11, an increase of (285 − 209)/11 = 76/11 ≈ ₹6.91.

questions.text: BI 2 is related to EF 5 in a certain way. In the same way, KR 8 is related to NO 11. To which of the following is TI 3 related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: The first letter moves 3 forward, the second 3 back and the number goes up by 3: B → E, I → F, 2 → 5 and K → N, R → O, 8 → 11. So T → W, I → F, 3 → 6: WF 6.

questions.text: What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘−’ are interchanged? 18 ÷ 6 + 2 − 3 × 4 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 18 + 6 ÷ 2 × 3 − 4 = 18 + 9 − 4 = 23.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? ESG, GTK, IUO, KVS, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move +2 (E, G, I, K, M), second letters +1 (S, T, U, V, W) and third letters +4 (G, K, O, S, W): MWW.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 2 ÷ 8 − 25 × 5 + 9 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 2 × 8 + 25 ÷ 5 − 9 = 16 + 5 − 9 = 12.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘INTO’ is coded as ‘2684’ and ‘OPEN’ is coded as ‘3567’. What is the code for ‘O’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: O is in both words, so its digit must be in both codes, and 6 is the only digit they share: O = 6. (N is in both words too, so strictly the codes should share two digits; the question is imperfect, but only 6 fits O.)

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘BALE’ is coded as ‘2496’ and ‘LORD’ is coded as ‘3759’. What is the code for ‘L’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: L is the only letter in both words and 9 the only digit in both codes, so L = 9.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘TIME’ is coded as 61 and ‘POND’ is coded as 59. How will ‘BLUE’ be coded in the same language?
questions.explanation: Each word is the sum of its letters' positions counted from Z (Z = 1, A = 26): TIME = 7 + 18 + 14 + 22 = 61 and POND = 11 + 12 + 13 + 23 = 59. So BLUE = 25 + 15 + 6 + 22 = 68.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘HEAP’ is coded as ‘7395’ and ‘PEAS’ is coded as ‘9571’. What is the code for ‘S’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: E, A and P are in both words, and 9, 5 and 7 in both codes. The letter left in PEAS is S and the digit left in its code is 1, so S = 1.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: A. Some guns are swords. B. All swords are onions. Conclusions: I. All guns are onions. II. Some guns are swords.
questions.explanation: Statement A itself says some guns are swords (II). Only the guns that are swords are known to be onions, so 'all guns are onions' (I) does not follow.

questions.text: Read the given statement(s) and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement(s). Statements: All bars are clubs. Some bars are gyms. Conclusions: (I) Some clubs are gyms. (II) Some gyms are not bars.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: The bars that are gyms are also clubs, so some clubs are gyms (I). Nothing says any gym lies outside the bars, so II does not follow.

questions.text: 18 is related to 60 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 42 is related to 140. To which ofthe following is 33 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbersinto its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding / subtracting / multiplying etc., to 13 canbe performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each number is multiplied by 10/3: 18 × 10/3 = 60 and 42 × 10/3 = 140. So 33 × 10/3 = 110.

questions.text: 21 is related to 73 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 28 is related to 94. To which ofthe following is 35 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbersinto its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: Each number is multiplied by 3 and 10 added: 21 × 3 + 10 = 73 and 28 × 3 + 10 = 94. So 35 × 3 + 10 = 115.

questions.text: Seven people A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table, facing the center (but not necessarily in the same order). C is sitting to the immediate right of B. E is sitting third to the left of B. D is the immediate neighbour of E and F. A is sitting to the immediate right of C. What is the position of G with respect to B?
questions.explanation: Going round to B's right: C, then A, and E is fourth (third to B's left). D must sit between E and F, so the order is C, A, G, E, D, F: G is third to the right of B.

questions.text: WY 13 is related to UW 16 in a certain way. In the same way, SU 19 is related to QS 22. To which of the following is OQ 17 related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Both letters move 2 places back and the number goes up by 3: W → U, Y → W, 13 → 16 and S → Q, U → S, 19 → 22. So O → M, Q → O, 17 → 20: MO 20.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 6, ?, 7, 10, 8, 11
questions.explanation: Two series alternate: 6, 7, 8 and 9, 10, 11.

questions.text: Six teachers are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). C is an immediate neighbour of both A and F. E is sitting second to the left of F. D is sitting fourth to the left of C. A is sitting second to the right of F. Which of the following statements is true?
options: B is immediate right of F.
F and D are immediate neighbours.
B is immediate left of F.
D is to the immediate right of E.
questions.explanation: A is second to the right of F, and C, next to both, sits between them. E is second to F's left and D fourth to C's left, between A and E. B takes the seat left over, immediately to F's left.

questions.text: Identify the primary characteristic of the Cooperative Development Foundation (CDF) model of SHGs regarding its focus on membership from the following.
options: It includes both poor and non-poor members.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives that the Cooperative Development Foundation's model of self-help groups takes in both poor and non-poor members.

questions.text: In Jain Basti temple of Karnataka, over the garbhagriha is raised a __________ storied nirandhara vimana with a square griva and sikhara.
questions.explanation: This is the Jaina basti (Brahma Jinalaya) at Lakkundi, an 11th-century temple; the Archaeological Survey of India describes the vimana over its garbhagriha as five-storeyed.

questions.text: The zone where the earthquake waves are not observed is called:
questions.explanation: Seismic waves are not recorded between about 105° and 145° from the epicentre; this belt is the shadow zone.

questions.text: Which of the following dance forms is inspired by the sculptures of the ancient temple of Chidambaram?
questions.explanation: The gopurams of the Nataraja temple at Chidambaram are carved with the 108 karanas (dance poses) of the Natya Shastra, on which Bharatanatyam draws.

questions.text: 'Straight from the Heart' is an autobiography of the famous cricketer ______________.
questions.explanation: 'Straight from the Heart' is the autobiography of Kapil Dev, India's 1983 World Cup-winning captain.

questions.text: Who among the following dancers won the prestigious Padma Shree award in the year 2021, for her contribution to folk dance?
questions.explanation: Matha B. Manjamma Jogathi, a transgender Jogati folk dancer from Karnataka, received the Padma Shri in 2021.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECT statement from the following.
options: Both boiling and evaporation are bulk phenomena.
questions.explanation: Evaporation takes place only at the surface of a liquid; boiling takes place throughout its bulk.

questions.text: In 1974, MS Subbulakshmi became the first Indian musician to win _____________.
questions.explanation: M. S. Subbulakshmi received the Ramon Magsaysay Award for Public Service in 1974; in 1998 she became the first musician to receive the Bharat Ratna.

questions.text: Which state government of India launched the 'Swanirbhar Nari' aimed at making the weavers of the state self-reliant?
questions.explanation: Swanirbhar Nari is the Assam government's scheme for the state's handloom weavers, under which their products are bought directly from them.

questions.text: As per Census of India 2011, which of the following states has the highest percentage of urban population in India?
questions.explanation: In Census 2011 about 52% of Mizoram's people lived in towns, against about 48% in Tamil Nadu, 45% in Maharashtra and 43% in Gujarat. (Goa, at about 62%, led all states.)

questions.text: The iodine value of oil and fat indicates:
questions.explanation: The iodine value is the grams of iodine taken up by 100 g of a fat or oil. Iodine adds across C=C double bonds, so the value measures how unsaturated it is.

questions.text: The number of organisms in the population divided by a regular unit of area or volume is called _______.
questions.explanation: Population density is the number of individuals per unit area or volume; population size is only the total number.

questions.text: In November 2023, who was re-appointed as the Chairman of the Armed Forces Tribunal?
questions.explanation: Justice Rajendra Menon, a former Chief Justice of the Delhi High Court, became Chairperson of the Armed Forces Tribunal in 2019 and was re-appointed in November 2023. Ramana and Bobde were Chief Justices of India, and Nariman a Supreme Court judge.

questions.text: Seleucus Nicator was a contemporary of ______________.
questions.explanation: Seleucus Nicator, Alexander's general, was defeated by Chandragupta Maurya around 305 BC, and Chanakya was Chandragupta's minister. Kalashoka ruled before them; Ashoka and Kanishka came later.

questions.text: Neville Steven Joseph D'Souza is associated with which game?
questions.explanation: Neville D'Souza was an Indian footballer; his hat-trick against Australia at the 1956 Melbourne Olympics was the first by an Asian player at the Olympics.

questions.text: According to the advancing of monsoon in India, which of the following cities receives rainfall after 15 June every year?
questions.explanation: On the normal onset dates the monsoon reaches Bengaluru, Imphal and Hyderabad in the first half of June; Jaipur, in the north-west, gets it only towards the end of June.

questions.text: Which of the following sultans of Delhi set up three different markets for different commodities in Delhi?
questions.explanation: Alauddin Khalji's market reforms set up separate markets, with fixed prices, for grain, for cloth and other costly goods, and for horses, cattle and slaves.

questions.text: With which of the following festivals does the five-day long festival of Diwali end?
questions.explanation: Diwali runs from Dhanteras through Narak Chaturdashi, Lakshmi Puja and Govardhan Puja to Bhai Dooj on the fifth day.

questions.text: Bhakra Dam is built on which of the following rivers?
questions.explanation: The Bhakra Dam stands on the Satluj in Bilaspur district, Himachal Pradesh.

questions.text: What is the stump height of a cricket wicket as per international standards?
questions.explanation: Under the Laws of Cricket the stumps stand 28 inches (71.12 cm) above the ground.

questions.text: Which Chapter of Part VI of the Indian Constitution is concerned with the State Legislatures?
questions.explanation: Part VI deals with the States: Chapter II with the Executive, Chapter III with the State Legislature (Articles 168 to 212) and Chapter V with the High Courts.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The Permanent Settlement introduced by Cornwallis was NOT prevalent in which of the following regions of India?
questions.explanation: The Permanent Settlement of 1793 covered Bengal, Bihar and Odisha; Punjab, annexed only in 1849, never came under it.

questions.text: Which Article of the Constitution of India governs the Population Census?
questions.explanation: The census is entry 69 of the Union List, so under Article 246 only Parliament can make laws on it (the Census Act, 1948).

questions.text: With which of the following Amendment Acts of the Indian Constitution was 11th Fundamental Duty added?
questions.explanation: The 86th Amendment Act, 2002 added Article 51A(k): the duty of a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to a child aged 6 to 14.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the two following countries were formed as a result of the partition of India?
questions.explanation: The partition of August 1947 divided British India into India and Pakistan; Bangladesh broke away from Pakistan only in 1971.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as one-word substitute for the given group of words. Detailed examination of something complex
questions.explanation: 'Analysis' is the detailed examination of something complex; 'synthesis' is the opposite, combining parts into a whole.

questions.text: Identify the spelling error in the given sentence. The restaurant offered a diverse menu with a wide renge of culinary options.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'range'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The Kumbh Mela (the festival of the sacred Pitcher) is the world's biggest peaceful gathering of pilgrims, with participants bathing or taking the dip in the _____ river.
questions.explanation: The pilgrims bathe in a river they hold holy: a 'sacred' river.

questions.text: Which of the following sentences contains an error in the use of a phrasal verb?
options: Clean out the backyard this weekend.
The old lady broke down when she heard her son lost his job.
Make over the bed daily. It is a good habit.
Try your level best before you decide to give up.
questions.explanation: One simply 'makes' the bed; 'make over' means to transform something or to hand it over to someone. 'Clean out', 'break down' and 'give up' are used correctly.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word to fill in the blank. Averted Rohit ______ looking at Sheena’s face while we were talking about domestic violence.
questions.explanation: To 'avert' one's eyes is to turn them away: Rohit 'avoided' looking at her face.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Illicit
questions.explanation: 'Illicit' means forbidden by law: 'illegal'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. The author's writing was so captivating that readers were “enthralled” by every word.
questions.explanation: To be 'enthralled' is to be held spellbound: 'fascinated'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A dime a dozen
options: To be in a difficult situation
questions.explanation: 'A dime a dozen' describes something so common that it has little value.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Brought to light
questions.explanation: 'Brought to light' means revealed or made known: disclosed.

questions.text: The following sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error. Along with his friend, he walked till the end of the street and came back immediately.
questions.explanation: 'Till' marks a point in time; for a distance or place it is 'to': 'he walked to the end of the street'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in present perfect continuous tense form Rama is working on this project.
options: Rama has worked on this project for six months
Rama has been working on this project since six months.
Rama is working on this project for six months.
Rama has been working on this project for six months.
questions.explanation: The present perfect continuous is 'has been' + '-ing', and a period of time takes 'for': 'Rama has been working on this project for six months.'

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. He climbed of / the steep mountain trail, / his backpack heavy / with supplies for the journey.
questions.explanation: 'Climb' takes its object directly: 'He climbed the steep mountain trail'; 'of' must go.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word. "The architekture of the building is marvellous", said the spectators.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'architecture'.

questions.text: Select the option that rectifies the given sentence. She runs very quick in marathons.
options: She run very quick in marathons.
She runs very quickly in marathons.
She run much quickly in marathons.
She runs much quickly in marathons.
questions.explanation: A verb is modified by an adverb, so 'runs very quickly'; 'run' would not agree with 'she'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Lisa was very excited about her promotion; she was “very happy and delighted”.
questions.explanation: To be 'on cloud nine' is to be extremely happy.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Odious
questions.explanation: 'Odious' means extremely unpleasant: 'repugnant'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given word. Fragile
questions.explanation: 'Fragile' means easily broken: 'brittle'.

questions.text: In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative. The table looks “proper” in the centre than in the corner.
questions.explanation: A comparison with 'than' needs the comparative, and 'proper' forms it with 'more': 'The table looks more proper in the centre than in the corner.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The charismatic leader's speeches were known for their __________ impact on motivating people to take positive actions.
questions.explanation: A deep and far-reaching impact is a 'profound' one; 'frugal' means sparing, and 'impenitence' and 'doldrums' are nouns.

questions.text: Select the correct spelling from the given options to fill in the blank. They may vary and seem very different, but they are not ________.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'irreconcilable'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Hyojeng, a twenty-five-year-old South Korean Youtuber (1)_________since the age of 16. She (2)_______around twenty-five countries so far. (3)________ India was high on her wish list. She is currently soaking in the energy of Mumbai and planning to (4)________ more of this beautiful city. Unfortunately, her experience of the city turned sour recently. She was filming on the streets of Mumbai and two men tried to hug and kiss her, which was captured in her video. The video (5)_________ viral and the Mumbai police swung into action.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The travelling began at 16 and is still going on ('since the age of 16'), and the subject is singular: 'has been travelling'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Hyojeng, a twenty-five-year-old South Korean Youtuber (1)_________since the age of 16. She (2)_______around twenty-five countries so far. (3)________ India was high on her wish list. She is currently soaking in the energy of Mumbai and planning to (4)________ more of this beautiful city. Unfortunately, her experience of the city turned sour recently. She was filming on the streets of Mumbai and two men tried to hug and kiss her, which was captured in her video. The video (5)_________ viral and the Mumbai police swung into action.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: 'So far' marks an action that runs up to the present, which takes the present perfect: 'She has covered around twenty-five countries so far.'

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Hyojeng, a twenty-five-year-old South Korean Youtuber (1)_________since the age of 16. She (2)_______around twenty-five countries so far. (3)________ India was high on her wish list. She is currently soaking in the energy of Mumbai and planning to (4)________ more of this beautiful city. Unfortunately, her experience of the city turned sour recently. She was filming on the streets of Mumbai and two men tried to hug and kiss her, which was captured in her video. The video (5)_________ viral and the Mumbai police swung into action.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: A gerund can be the subject of a sentence: 'Visiting India was high on her wish list.'

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Hyojeng, a twenty-five-year-old South Korean Youtuber (1)_________since the age of 16. She (2)_______around twenty-five countries so far. (3)________ India was high on her wish list. She is currently soaking in the energy of Mumbai and planning to (4)________ more of this beautiful city. Unfortunately, her experience of the city turned sour recently. She was filming on the streets of Mumbai and two men tried to hug and kiss her, which was captured in her video. The video (5)_________ viral and the Mumbai police swung into action.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'Planning to' is followed by the base form of the verb: 'planning to explore more of this beautiful city'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Hyojeng, a twenty-five-year-old South Korean Youtuber (1)_________since the age of 16. She (2)_______around twenty-five countries so far. (3)________ India was high on her wish list. She is currently soaking in the energy of Mumbai and planning to (4)________ more of this beautiful city. Unfortunately, her experience of the city turned sour recently. She was filming on the streets of Mumbai and two men tried to hug and kiss her, which was captured in her video. The video (5)_________ viral and the Mumbai police swung into action.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: The passage narrates a past event, and the expression is 'go viral': 'The video went viral'.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: The outer circumference of the top of a large hemispherical iron bowl is 565.2 cm and the bowl is 6 cm thick. What will be the volume (in cm³) of the iron required to make this bowl? (Use π = 3.14.)
questions.explanation: Outer radius = 565.2 ÷ (2 × 3.14) = 90 cm, so the inner radius is 84 cm. Volume of iron = (2/3)π(90³ − 84³) = (2/3) × 3.14 × 1,36,296 = 2,85,312.96 cm³.

questions.text: A shop keeper allows a 25% discount and gains 20%. How much of the percentage is above the Marked Price on the Cost Price?
questions.explanation: Selling price = 1.2 × CP = 0.75 × MP, so MP = (1.2/0.75) × CP = 1.6 × CP: the marked price is 60% above the cost price.

questions.text: Two trains are running in opposite directions at the same speed. The length of each train is 180 m. If they cross each other in 12 seconds, what is the speed of each train (in km/h)?
questions.explanation: Crossing each other, the trains cover 180 + 180 = 360 m in 12 seconds at their combined speed of 30 m/s. Each runs at 15 m/s = 15 × 18/5 = 54 km/h.

questions.text: If the volume of a sphere is divided by its surface area, the result is 54 cm. The radius of the sphere is:

Three candidates contested an election and obtained 1136, 7636 and 11628 votes, respectively. What percentage of the total votes did the losing candidate (last one) get? (Correct to two decimal places)
questions.explanation: The losing candidate, the one who came last, got 1,136 of the 1,136 + 7,636 + 11,628 = 20,400 votes: 1,136/20,400 × 100 = 5.57%.

questions.text: The average age of a class of 65 boys is 14 years. The average age of 20 of them is 14 years, and the average age of another 15 boys is 12 years. What will be the average age (in years) of the remaining boys?
questions.explanation: The class's total age is 65 × 14 = 910 years. The two groups account for 20 × 14 + 15 × 12 = 460, leaving 450 years for the other 30 boys: 450/30 = 15.

questions.text: A thief steals a bike at 12.40 p.m. and drives it at 45 km/h. The theft is discovered at 1 p.m. and the owner sets off in a car at 65 km/h in the direction the thief was heading. The time at which the owner can catch the thief is:
questions.explanation: By 1 p.m. the thief is 20 minutes ahead: 45 × 1/3 = 15 km. The owner gains 65 − 45 = 20 km/h, so he needs 15/20 hour = 45 minutes: 1:45 p.m.

questions.text: Find the simple interest on ₹550 for 8 months at 3 paise per rupee per month?
questions.explanation: 3 paise per rupee per month is 3% a month: 550 × 3/100 × 8 = ₹132.

questions.text: A man purchased 3 bags of cement at the rate of ₹2,200 each, 4 bags of cement at ₹2,550 each and 5 bags of cement at the rate of ₹3,120 each. What is the average cost of one bag of cement?

The average height of a group of 50 students is 175 cm. If another group of 40 students with average height of 180 cm is included, what is the average (in cm, to the nearest cm) of the combined group?
Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2000 as a sum borrowed at 6% per year rate of interest for 3 years.
A shopkeeper sells goods at the same price rate for which he has bought them, but gives 20% less quantity to the customer. Find the profit percentage.
questions.explanation: He charges for 100 units but hands over 80, which cost him the price of 80: profit = 20/80 × 100 = 25%.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3500 as a sum borrowed at 7% per year rate of interest for 3 years.
In what ratio wheat at ₹38 per kg should be mixed with wheat at ₹26 per kg so that on selling the mixture at ₹39 per kg, there would be a profit of 30%?
questions.explanation: For a 30% profit at ₹39, the mixture must cost 39/1.3 = ₹30 a kg. By alligation, ₹38 wheat : ₹26 wheat = (30 − 26) : (38 − 30) = 4 : 8 = 1 : 2.

questions.text: What is the HCF of 512 and 296?
questions.explanation: 512 = 2⁹ and 296 = 2³ × 37, so the HCF is 2³ = 8.

questions.text: A group of 9 people can survive on ₹8,100 for 30 days. How long can a group of 7 people survive on ₹8,400?
questions.explanation: ₹8,100 lasts 9 people 30 days, so one person needs 8,100/(9 × 30) = ₹30 a day. ₹8,400 then lasts 7 people 8,400/(7 × 30) = 40 days.

questions.text: Seven friends, Monu, Abhay, Vicky, Chitti, Deva, Hamza and Sanjay, are attending Hamza’s birthday party and sitting in a circular arrangement facing the centre(but not necessarily in the same order). Monu is an immediate neighbour of Abhay and Deva. Abhay is second to the left of Hamza. Sanjay is one of the immediate neighbours of Hamza. Chitti is an immediate neighbour of both Deva and Vicky. Who is sitting third to the left of Monu?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, left is clockwise. Abhay is second to Hamza's left, Monu sits between Abhay and Deva, Chitti between Deva and Vicky, and Sanjay beside Hamza, so clockwise they run Hamza, Sanjay, Abhay, Monu, Deva, Chitti, Vicky. Third to Monu's left is Vicky.

questions.text: MAZE is related to QEDI in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, YMLQ is related to CQPU. To which of the following is OCBG related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 4 places forward (Z wraps round to D): MAZE → QEDI and YMLQ → CQPU. So OCBG → SGFK.

questions.text: 181 is related to 417 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 149 is related to 385. To which ofthe following is 262 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbersinto its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is the first plus 236: 181 + 236 = 417 and 149 + 236 = 385. Likewise 262 + 236 = 498.

questions.text: In a code language, 'RAMESH' is written as 'UAPEVK' and 'TOM' is written as 'WOP'. How will 'MEGHANA' be written in the same language?
questions.explanation: Consonants move 3 places forward and vowels stay: R → U, M → P, S → V, H → K in RAMESH → UAPEVK. So MEGHANA → PEJKAQA.

questions.text: EKQW is related to JPVA in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, BHNT is related to GMSX. To which of the following is PVBH related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: The first three letters move 5 places forward and the last one 4 (wrapping round after Z): EKQW → JPVA and BHNT → GMSX. So PVBH → UAGL.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 89 92 98 107 119 ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 3, 6, 9 and 12, rising by 3, so the next is 15: 119 + 15 = 134.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 13 + 4 × 2 ÷ 5 – 2 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 13 − 4 ÷ 2 × 5 + 2 = 13 − 10 + 2 = 5.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g., 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (25, 8, 400) (12, 14, 336)
questions.explanation: In each set the third number is twice the product of the first two: 25 × 8 × 2 = 400 and 12 × 14 × 2 = 336. Likewise 16 × 21 × 2 = 672.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All hens are chickens. All chickens are eggs. Conclusions: (I) All hens are eggs. (II) All eggs are chickens.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: All hens are chickens and all chickens are eggs, so all hens are eggs (I). Nothing says every egg is a chicken, so II does not follow.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) of the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 22 × 11 + 13 − 12 ÷ 2 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 22 ÷ 11 − 13 + 12 × 2 = 2 − 13 + 24 = 13.

questions.text: In a code language, 'ARVL' is coded as ‘FOAI’ and 'DOXY' is coded as ‘ILCV’. How will 'MPSB' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +5, −3, +5, −3, wrapping round the alphabet: ARVL → FOAI and DOXY → ILCV. So MPSB → RMXY.

questions.text: Six players Jadeja, Ashwin, Karthik, Murli, Sarfaraz and Virat are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order) . Virat is sitting to the immediate right of Jadeja. Only Sarfaraz is sitting between Virat and Murli. Jadeja is an immediate neighbour of Ashwin. Who is immediate neighbour of both Sarfaraz and Karthik?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, right is anticlockwise. Virat is on Jadeja's right, Sarfaraz between Virat and Murli, and Ashwin beside Jadeja, so clockwise they run Jadeja, Ashwin, Karthik, Murli, Sarfaraz, Virat. Murli sits between Karthik and Sarfaraz.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘barks a lot’ is written as ‘qw er ui’ and ‘the dog barks’ is writtenas ‘op ji er’. How is ‘barks’ writtenin that language?
questions.explanation: 'barks' is the only word in both sentences and 'er' the only code in both, so barks = er.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? SDW, OHS, KLO, GPK ,?
questions.explanation: First letters move back 4 (S, O, K, G, so C), second letters forward 4 (D, H, L, P, so T) and third letters back 4 (W, S, O, K, so G): CTG.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘BEAM’ is coded as ‘5791’ and ‘MINT’ is coded as ‘2467’. What is the code for ‘M’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: M is the only letter in both words and 7 the only digit in both codes, so M = 7.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some possums are bisons. No possum is a wolf. Conclusions: [1] All wolves can be bisons. [2] All bisons are wolves.
questions.explanation: Wolves are kept apart only from possums, so all wolves could be bisons: [1] follows as a possibility. Some bisons are possums and no possum is a wolf, so not every bison is a wolf: [2] does not follow.

questions.text: Which of the following is an autobiography of LK Advani?
questions.explanation: 'My Country My Life' (2008) is L. K. Advani's autobiography. 'Wings of Fire' is A. P. J. Abdul Kalam's, and 'Exam Warriors' is by Narendra Modi.

questions.text: According to Global Multidimensional Poverty Index 2022, what was the population of the poor in India in 2020?
questions.explanation: The 2022 global Multidimensional Poverty Index (UNDP and OPHI) put India's poor at 228.9 million in 2020, the largest number of any country.

questions.text: The strength of Supreme Court has increased to how many judges as of 13 Feb 2023?
questions.explanation: With two new judges sworn in on 13 February 2023, the Supreme Court reached its full sanctioned strength of 34, including the Chief Justice.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following social reformers wrote Brahmo Covenant which was a statement of the creed of the Brahmo Samaj?
questions.explanation: Debendranath Tagore, who revived the Brahmo Samaj after Raja Ram Mohan Roy's death, wrote the Brahmo Covenant.

questions.text: Which sector uses the groundwater maximally?
questions.explanation: Irrigation takes most of India's groundwater: close to 90% of what is drawn goes to agriculture.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following Governor Generals of India wrote about the predicament of Indian weavers, “The bones of the cotton weavers are scattered on the plains of India”?
questions.explanation: Lord William Bentinck, Governor-General in the 1830s, wrote these words about the ruin of India's hand-weavers, undercut by machine-made British cloth.

questions.text: Who became the first woman to win two gold medals in a single Para Asian Games event in 2023?
questions.explanation: Archer Sheetal Devi won two golds at the Hangzhou Asian Para Games in October 2023, in the women's individual compound and the mixed team compound.

questions.text: Which of the following crops takes almost a year to grow?
questions.explanation: Sugarcane takes about a year, 10 to 18 months, to mature; ragi, groundnut and soyabean are harvested within a few months of sowing.

questions.text: Wasifuddin Dagar was associated with which of the following classical music genres?
questions.explanation: Ustad Wasifuddin Dagar is a dhrupad singer of the Dagar family, the best-known lineage of dhrupad.

questions.text: In which of the following states is the famous International Sand Art Festival organised, where artists get enthralled by the diverse thoughts and their elucidation on sand?
questions.explanation: The International Sand Art Festival is held on Chandrabhaga beach near Konark, Odisha.

questions.text: Which of the following options is an example of a decomposer in an ecosystem?
questions.explanation: Fungi and bacteria are decomposers: they break down dead matter and return its nutrients to the soil.

questions.text: Sama Chakeva is a folk dance based on the mythological story of the siblings Sama and Chakeva, in which the brother goes to an extreme extent to save his sister. With which State of India is this folk dance associated?
questions.explanation: Sama-Chakeva is a folk festival and dance of the Mithila region of Bihar.

questions.text: In the periodic table, what is the trend for atomic radius as you move from left to right across a period (horizontal row)?
questions.explanation: Across a period the nuclear charge rises while electrons enter the same shell, so they are pulled closer and the atomic radius decreases.

questions.text: Which state received the Sportstar ACES Best State for the Promotion of Sport award in 2024?
questions.explanation: Tamil Nadu received the Sportstar ACES award for the best state for the promotion of sport in February 2024; it had hosted the men's hockey Asian Champions Trophy and the Khelo India Youth Games.

questions.text: Who amongst the following said that the government fiscal policy should be used to stabilise the level of output and employment?
questions.explanation: John Maynard Keynes argued that government spending and taxation should be used to stabilise output and employment.

questions.text: The Megalithic site __________ is a site on the river Ghod, a tributary of the Bhima.
questions.explanation: Inamgaon, in Pune district of Maharashtra, lies on the Ghod, a tributary of the Bhima.

questions.text: The part of a temple wherein the main deity of the temple is housed is known as the _______.
questions.explanation: The garbhagriha, the 'womb chamber', is the sanctum that houses the main deity; the mandapa is the hall before it and the shikhara the tower above it.

questions.text: The black coating formed on silver jewellery is:
questions.explanation: Silver reacts with sulphur compounds in the air to form black silver sulphide, Ag₂S: the tarnish on silver jewellery.

questions.text: Which of the following white papers, released by NITI Aayog, is related to Public Health Surveillance in India?
questions.explanation: NITI Aayog's white paper 'Vision 2035: Public Health Surveillance in India' sets out how India's disease surveillance should develop.

questions.text: The ‘Rule of Law’ is a key feature of the Indian Constitution which is a doctrine ascribed to ____________________.
questions.explanation: The rule of law was set out by the British jurist A. V. Dicey: no one is above the law, and all are equal before it.

questions.text: The Dudhsagar waterfall is a major tourist place of ________ State.
questions.explanation: Dudhsagar Falls, on the Mandovi at Goa's border with Karnataka, is one of India's tallest waterfalls.

questions.text: When was the Lahore declaration signed between India and Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Nawaz Sharif signed the Lahore Declaration on 21 February 1999, after Vajpayee's bus journey to Lahore.

questions.text: Which of following silver coins was introduced by Sultan Shamsuddin Iltutmish?
questions.explanation: Iltutmish introduced the silver tanka and the copper jital, the standard coins of the Delhi Sultanate.

questions.text: Gulabo Sapera, a legendry folk dancer from Kalbeliya tribe, Rajasthan, received Padma Shri in the year ________.
questions.explanation: Gulabo Sapera, who took the Kalbeliya dance to the world, received the Padma Shri in 2016.

questions.text: The legislative powers in India are divided into three lists, which are the Union List, the State List and the _____________.
questions.explanation: The Seventh Schedule divides legislative powers among the Union List, the State List and the Concurrent List, on which both Parliament and the states may legislate.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. Commodity prices are the “dearer” in the present economic scenario.
questions.explanation: 'The' before the adjective calls for the superlative: 'Commodity prices are the dearest'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A person who abstains from any sort of alcoholic drinks
questions.explanation: A teetotaller never drinks alcohol. A termagant is a quarrelsome woman and a Samaritan a helpful stranger.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. The students were diligently / studying for their exams / for weeks before you arrived.
questions.explanation: An action that went on for weeks up to a point in the past takes the past perfect continuous: 'The students had been diligently studying'.

questions.text: Select the option with the correct spelling to replace the underlined word in the given sentence. Polluted air can be “dangeros”, even if the pollutants are invisible.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'dangerous'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Alaska in the USA / is the colder / of all the states.
questions.explanation: Comparing one with all the states needs the superlative: 'is the coldest of all the states'.

questions.text: The following sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error. His aunt who lives at America brought a lot of gifts for him and his sister.
questions.explanation: A country takes 'in', not 'at': 'His aunt who lives in America'.

questions.text: In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative. Which flower do you like “best”?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'the best', treating the superlative as needing 'the': 'Which flower do you like the best?' 'Like best' without 'the' is also standard English, so the sentence as printed is arguably correct already.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank. After the floods, Uttarakhand was in a _______(ravaged) condition.
questions.explanation: 'Ravaged' means badly damaged; its opposite here is 'restored', brought back to a good condition.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The artist believes that this new collection of paintings / has being / a masterpiece that / will redefine contemporary art.
options: The artist believes that this new collection of paintings
questions.explanation: 'Has being' is not a verb form; the sentence needs 'is' (or 'has been'): 'this new collection of paintings is a masterpiece'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Something that is so extraordinary or unbelievable that it's hard to believe it
questions.explanation: 'Incredible' means impossible or hard to believe; 'exquisite' means extremely beautiful.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined phrase. I should “look into my past” and decide what the next course of action should be.
questions.explanation: To look back on one's past is to 'retrospect'; to 'introspect' is to examine one's own thoughts and feelings, and a 'prospect' looks ahead.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. Sushant looked “blue in the face” after the marathon.
questions.explanation: Someone 'blue in the face' is worn out by effort, as after a long run. 'Feeling blue', a different idiom, means sad.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'arrest'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'. If she “had gone to the party”, she could have met Amit.
questions.explanation: An unreal past condition takes the past perfect in the 'if' clause and 'could have' in the main clause, so the sentence is correct as it stands.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. The team worked together to “execute” the challenging task.
questions.explanation: To 'execute' a task is to carry it out: to 'accomplish' it.

questions.text: Identify the ANTONYM pair.
questions.explanation: To 'dissuade' is to persuade someone not to do something, the opposite of 'encourage'. The other pairs are near-synonyms.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Timid
questions.explanation: 'Timid' means lacking courage; its opposite is 'bold'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. She finally “spilled the beans” about the surprise party.
options: Revealed a secret or disclosed information
questions.explanation: To 'spill the beans' is to reveal a secret.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. The students demonstrated their “excitement” by volunteering for community service.
questions.explanation: 'Excitement' here is eager interest: 'enthusiasm'.

questions.text: Select the correct spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence. We do not “expet” Reema to follow all the rules from the first day of work.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'expect'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A brigantine is a two-masted sailing vessel (1)_____ fore-and-aft rigging on the mainmast and square rigging on the foremast. The pirates that (2)______ the Mediterranean in the sixteenth century loved it for its speed and ease of handling. The brigantine (3)_________ into a true sailing vessel in the waters of northern Europe. Although the words began to be used interchangeably, it was (4)_______ from the fully square-rigged brig by its gaff-rigged mainsail. True brigantines, for (5)_____, were defined as having square topsails above a gaffed mainsail.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: A brigantine is a vessel 'featuring', that is having, fore-and-aft rigging on the mainmast.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A brigantine is a two-masted sailing vessel (1)_____ fore-and-aft rigging on the mainmast and square rigging on the foremast. The pirates that (2)______ the Mediterranean in the sixteenth century loved it for its speed and ease of handling. The brigantine (3)_________ into a true sailing vessel in the waters of northern Europe. Although the words began to be used interchangeably, it was (4)_______ from the fully square-rigged brig by its gaff-rigged mainsail. True brigantines, for (5)_____, were defined as having square topsails above a gaffed mainsail.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Pirates 'ravaged', or plundered, the Mediterranean.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A brigantine is a two-masted sailing vessel (1)_____ fore-and-aft rigging on the mainmast and square rigging on the foremast. The pirates that (2)______ the Mediterranean in the sixteenth century loved it for its speed and ease of handling. The brigantine (3)_________ into a true sailing vessel in the waters of northern Europe. Although the words began to be used interchangeably, it was (4)_______ from the fully square-rigged brig by its gaff-rigged mainsail. True brigantines, for (5)_____, were defined as having square topsails above a gaffed mainsail.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: The brigantine 'evolved into' a true sailing vessel: it developed gradually.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A brigantine is a two-masted sailing vessel (1)_____ fore-and-aft rigging on the mainmast and square rigging on the foremast. The pirates that (2)______ the Mediterranean in the sixteenth century loved it for its speed and ease of handling. The brigantine (3)_________ into a true sailing vessel in the waters of northern Europe. Although the words began to be used interchangeably, it was (4)_______ from the fully square-rigged brig by its gaff-rigged mainsail. True brigantines, for (5)_____, were defined as having square topsails above a gaffed mainsail.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'For instance' introduces an example; 'for case' is not an English phrase.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: In 2016, the price of a refrigerator increased by 5%, and in 2017, it decreased by 5%. At the end of the year 2017, its price was ₹47,880. What was its price at the beginning of the year 2016?
questions.explanation: The two changes multiply the price by 1.05 × 0.95 = 0.9975, so the price at the start of 2016 was 47,880 ÷ 0.9975 = ₹48,000.

questions.text: In a company, if 40 workers can make 50 bags in 4 days, then how many bags will 24 workers will make in 8 days?
questions.explanation: 40 workers × 4 days = 160 worker-days make 50 bags. 24 workers × 8 days = 192 worker-days make 50 × 192/160 = 60 bags.

questions.text: At a certain rate of simple interest, a sum becomes ₹9,430 in 3 years and ₹11,070 in 7 years. Find the sum.
questions.explanation: The 4 years from year 3 to year 7 add ₹11,070 − ₹9,430 = ₹1,640 of interest, ₹410 a year. The sum is ₹9,430 − 3 × ₹410 = ₹8,200.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2500 as a sum borrowed at 9% per year rate of interest for 4 years.
A commodity is made of two metals, A and B, which cost ₹35 per kg and ₹40 per kg, respectively, in the ratio of 2 : 3. What is the cost (in ₹) of 12 kilograms of this commodity?
questions.explanation: In the ratio 2 : 3 the commodity costs (2 × 35 + 3 × 40)/5 = ₹38 a kg, so 12 kg cost 12 × 38 = ₹456.

questions.text: A cyclist covers a distance of 2.5 km in 4 minutes 10 seconds. How long will he take to cover a distance of 6 km at the same speed?
questions.explanation: 4 minutes 10 seconds is 250 seconds for 2.5 km, or 100 seconds a km. 6 km take 600 seconds: 10 minutes.

questions.text: A person sold an article and got a loss of 9%. If he sold it for ₹51 more he would gain 8%. Find the C.P.
questions.explanation: From a 9% loss to an 8% gain is 17% of the cost price, which is ₹51. C.P. = 51 × 100/17 = ₹300.

questions.text: The cost price of an article is 76% of its marked price. Find the gain percentage after allowing a discount of 5%.
questions.explanation: Take the marked price as 100: C.P. = 76 and S.P. = 95 after the 5% discount. Gain = 19/76 × 100 = 25%.

questions.text: The average weight of a family of five members (in kg) whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 71 kg and 39 kg is:

A chemist prepares 100 grams of medicine by mixing two ingredients X and Y. The rate of X is ₹1,500 per 100 grams and that of Y is ₹50 per 10 grams. X and Y are mixed in such a way that the cost of the resulting medicine is ₹13 per gram. What is the quantity of X (in grams) in the medicine?
questions.explanation: X costs ₹15 a gram and Y ₹5 a gram. With x grams of X: 15x + 5(100 − x) = 13 × 100, so 10x = 800 and x = 80.

questions.text: The area of a rectangular park of length 15 m and breadth 12 m is:
questions.explanation: Area = length × breadth = 15 × 12 = 180 m².

questions.text: Two vendors calculate their profit percentage on the cost price and selling price, respectively. What will be the difference between the profits (in ₹) if both the vendors declare a profit of 28% on the goods sold for ₹3,200?
questions.explanation: On cost price: ₹3,200 = 1.28 × C.P., so C.P. = ₹2,500 and the profit is ₹700. On selling price: 28% of ₹3,200 = ₹896. Difference = 896 − 700 = ₹196.

questions.text: The average of four girls' age is 12 years. The ages of three of them are 7, 12 and 13 years. Find the age of the fourth girl.
questions.explanation: The four ages total 4 × 12 = 48 years, so the fourth girl is 48 − (7 + 12 + 13) = 16 years old.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2500 as a sum borrowed at 7% per year rate of interest for 3 years.
A car can cover 275 km in 5 hours. If its speed is reduced by 5 km/h, then how much time will the car take to cover a distance of 300 km?
questions.explanation: The car's speed is 275 ÷ 5 = 55 km/h; 5 km/h less is 50 km/h, and 300 km then take 300 ÷ 50 = 6 hours.

questions.text: What should come in place of question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? AYF, FUI, KQL, PMO, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move 5 forward (A, F, K, P, U), second letters 4 back (Y, U, Q, M, I) and third letters 3 forward (F, I, L, O, R): UIR.

questions.text: Five girls P, Q, R, S and T sit around a circular table facing towards the centre (not necessarily in the same order). Only one girl sits between S and T. P sits to the immediate left of R. P is not an immediate neighbour of S. Who sits third to the right of T?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, a girl's left is the next seat clockwise. P sits just left of R and S is not next to P, so with one girl between S and T the seats run clockwise R, P, T, Q, S. Three places to T's right (anticlockwise) are P, R and then S.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 12 ÷ 3 – 8 + 16 × 4 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 12 × 3 + 8 − 16 ÷ 4 = 36 + 8 − 4 = 40.

questions.text: AE10 is related to CG20 in a certain way. In the same way, KO20 is related to MQ30. To which of the following is CG30 related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places forward and the number rises by 10: AE10 → CG20 and KO20 → MQ30. So CG30 → EI40.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 23, ?, 89, 177, 353, 705
questions.explanation: Each term is twice the one before minus 1: 89 × 2 − 1 = 177 and 177 × 2 − 1 = 353. So the missing term is 23 × 2 − 1 = 45, and 45 × 2 − 1 = 89.

questions.text: DKNF is related to YFIA in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, QYCR is related to LTXM. To which of the following is PEVM related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 5 places back, wrapping round from A to Z: D → Y, K → F, N → I, F → A. So P → K, E → Z, V → Q, M → H: KZQH.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘HAVE’ is coded as ‘2648’ and ‘VOLT’ is coded as ‘3961’.What is the code for ‘V’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: V is the only letter in both words and 6 the only digit in both codes, so V = 6.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘BEST’ is coded as ‘4982’ and ‘STEM’ is coded as ‘6489’. What is the code for ‘B’ in that language?
questions.explanation: S, T and E are in both words, as are 4, 8 and 9 in both codes. The letter left in BEST is B and the digit left in its code is 2, so B = 2.

questions.text: In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/ subtracting /multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 16, 80; 22, 110
questions.explanation: In each pair the second number is five times the first: 16 × 5 = 80 and 22 × 5 = 110. Likewise 25 × 5 = 125.

questions.text: 122 is related to 145 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 37 is related to 50. To which of the following is 82 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding / subtracting / multiplying, etc.. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each number is n² + 1 and goes with (n + 1)² + 1: 122 = 11² + 1 → 12² + 1 = 145 and 37 = 6² + 1 → 7² + 1 = 50. So 82 = 9² + 1 → 10² + 1 = 101.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement(s). Statements: All planets are stars. All stars are galaxies. Conclusion (I): All stars are planets. Conclusion (II): All planets are galaxies.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: All planets are stars and all stars are galaxies, so all planets are galaxies (II). That all planets are stars does not make all stars planets, so I does not follow.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘nothing to hide’ is written as ‘tg mk sa’ and ‘hide and seek’ is writtenas ‘mk wd lq’. How will ‘hide’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: 'hide' is the only word in both sentences and 'mk' the only code in both, so hide = mk.

questions.text: A, B, C, P, X, Y and Z are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Y sits third to the left of A. B sits second to the left of C. Z sits to the immediate left of B. P sits third to the left of Z. A is not an immediate neighbour of C. Who sits third to the left of Y?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, a person's left is the next seat clockwise. Clockwise from C come a seat, B, Z, two seats and P. Y three seats left of A, with A not next to C, puts Y between C and B and A just before P: C, Y, B, Z, X, A, P. Third to the left of Y is X.

questions.text: Which two numbers should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? (24 + 14− 6) ÷ 2 + 18 × 3 − 20 = 40 (Note: Interchange should be done of entire number and not individual digits of a given number)

Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All kurtas are sarees. All sarees are blouse. Conclusions: (I) All kurtas are blouse. (II) No blouse is a saree.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follow
Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: All kurtas are sarees and all sarees are blouse, so all kurtas are blouse (I). As every saree is a blouse, some blouse are sarees, so II is false.

questions.text: Who among the following was the top run-scorer for India at the 1983 Cricket World Cup final with 38 runs?
questions.explanation: Krishnamachari Srikkanth top-scored for India in the 1983 World Cup final with 38 of their 183 runs; India beat the West Indies by 43 runs.

questions.text: In which of the following religions was the agriculture prohibited for its followers?
questions.explanation: Jainism's strict non-violence rules out harming even insects and worms, which ploughing does, so its followers kept away from agriculture and took mainly to trade.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Due to the popularity of Indian clothes in Britain, a law was passed to ban Indian clothes. Which of the following was that law?
questions.explanation: Worried by the popularity of Indian printed cottons, the British government passed the Calico Act in 1720, banning the use of printed cotton textiles (chintz) in England.

questions.text: In 1974, classical singer Naina Devi was awarded the Padma Shri for her contribution to which of the following singing styles?
questions.explanation: Naina Devi (Nilina Sen) was one of the best-known thumri singers of Hindustani music.

questions.text: According to National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2023 (A Progress Review), which state has the highest proportion of multidimensionally poor people (Headcount Ratio)?
questions.explanation: NITI Aayog's National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2023 found Bihar with the highest share of multidimensionally poor people, about a third of its population in 2019-21.

questions.text: Amer Fort was built with red sandstone and white marble by which ruler in the 16th century?
questions.explanation: Amer Fort near Jaipur was built by Raja Man Singh I, Akbar's general, from the late 16th century.

questions.text: Who among the following is known for his/her books ‘The Algebra of Infinite Justice’, ‘Kashmir: The Case for Freedom’ and ‘Capitalism: A Ghost Story’?
questions.explanation: 'The Algebra of Infinite Justice' and 'Capitalism: A Ghost Story' are essay collections by Arundhati Roy, the author of 'The God of Small Things', who is also one of the contributors to 'Kashmir: The Case for Freedom'.

questions.text: Moti Masjid in Agra fort was constructed by which of the following Mughal Emperors?
questions.explanation: The white-marble Moti Masjid inside Agra Fort was built by Shah Jahan.

questions.text: The Indian Constitution has adopted the parliamentary form of Government from ___________.
questions.explanation: The parliamentary form of government, with a cabinet answerable to the legislature, was borrowed from Britain.

questions.text: Carbon dioxide plays a vital role in changing the earth's climate, leading to a critical condition known as ________.
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide is a greenhouse gas: it traps heat given off by the earth, so a rising level of it strengthens the greenhouse effect and warms the climate.

questions.text: What is the chemical formula for the compound commonly known as 'laughing gas'?
questions.explanation: Laughing gas is nitrous oxide, N₂O.

questions.text: Few renowned artists of __________ dance style in India are Roshan Kumari, Shovana Narayan, Maya Rao and Kumudini Lakhia.
questions.explanation: Roshan Kumari, Shovana Narayan, Maya Rao and Kumudini Lakhia are all noted Kathak dancers.

questions.text: To mark the 75 years of Indo-Lanka Diplomatic Relations, External Affairs Minister Jaishankar inaugurated the 'Geoffrey Bawa: It is Essential To be There' Exhibition in March 2023. Who was Geoffrey Bawa?
questions.explanation: Geoffrey Bawa (1919-2003) was a Sri Lankan architect, a pioneer of the style known as tropical modernism.

questions.text: ‘Navroz’ is celebrated as the new year by which of the following communities?
questions.explanation: Navroz, the Persian new year, is celebrated in India by the Parsi community.

questions.text: To get relief from constipation, which of the following is prescribed to be eaten in large amount?
questions.explanation: Dietary fibre (roughage) adds bulk to the stool and helps it pass, relieving constipation.

questions.text: Odissi Guru, ________, received the first Utkal Pratibha Samman 2023 at Bhubaneswar.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Ratikant Mohapatra, an Odissi guru and the son of the Odissi maestro Kelucharan Mohapatra.

questions.text: Based on the Tendulkar committee, the National poverty line was defined as which of the following? i. ₹816 per capita per month for rural areas ii. ₹1,000 per capita per month for urban areas.
options: Both i and ii are incorrect
Both i and ii are correct
questions.explanation: Using the Tendulkar committee's method, the Planning Commission set the 2011-12 poverty line at ₹816 per capita per month in rural areas and ₹1,000 in urban areas.

questions.text: Which of the followings is NOT one of the government accounts of India?
questions.explanation: The government's accounts are the Consolidated Fund of India, the Contingency Fund of India and the Public Account of India. The General Provident Fund is a savings scheme whose deposits are held in the Public Account, not an account of its own.

questions.text: Which Article deals with the provisions in case of failure of the constitutional machinery in the State?
questions.explanation: Article 356 provides for President's Rule in a State where the constitutional machinery has failed.

questions.text: Anorexia nervosa is an eating disorder in teenagers. Here body weight:
questions.explanation: In anorexia nervosa a person eats too little out of an intense fear of gaining weight, and body weight falls drastically.

questions.text: According to average rainfall in India, the Ladakh Union Territory is located in ___________.
questions.explanation: Ladakh, a cold desert in the rain shadow of the Himalayas, gets far less than 50 cm of rain a year, which puts it among the areas of inadequate rainfall.

questions.text: Where was the Intercontinental Football Cup 2023 organised?
questions.explanation: The 2023 Intercontinental Cup was played at the Kalinga Stadium, Bhubaneswar, in June 2023; India won it.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who was the Viceroy of India when the Indian Arms Act, 1878, was passed?
questions.explanation: The Arms Act of 1878, which barred Indians from keeping arms without a licence, was passed under Lord Lytton (Viceroy 1876-80), as was the Vernacular Press Act.

questions.text: According to Economic Survey 2023-24, which of the following states is the largest wheat producing state of India?
questions.explanation: Uttar Pradesh is India's largest wheat producer, ahead of Madhya Pradesh and Punjab.

questions.text: In 2023, Congress MP Shashi Tharoor has been named as the chairperson of the Parliamentary Committee on _______________.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Chemicals and Fertilisers: Shashi Tharoor chaired the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Chemicals and Fertilisers in 2023, having been moved to it from the Committee on Information Technology (reported in October 2022). He took over the External Affairs committee in 2024.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four parts. Identify the part that contains a grammatical error. Jack probably/ strained his back/ as the box was/ too heavier.
questions.explanation: 'Too' takes the positive degree: 'the box was too heavy', not 'too heavier'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word in the given sentence. “Exclusion” of someone from a common group harms the human society.
questions.explanation: 'Exclusion' is keeping someone out: 'prohibition', barring them, is the closest. 'Admission' is its opposite.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. Because the politician's speech was “high-flown and pretentious”, it gained popularity.
questions.explanation: 'Bombastic' describes speech or writing that is high-flown and pretentious.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Hollow
questions.explanation: 'Hollow' in its figurative sense means without real worth (a hollow promise); its opposite is 'worthwhile'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Knuckle down
options: To crush someone to the extent that they cannot get up
To start working or studying hard
To make others do their share of hard work using power
questions.explanation: To 'knuckle down' is to start working or studying hard.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. My son, who is a cricketer too, is a M.A. from Delhi University.
questions.explanation: 'M.A.' begins with a vowel sound ('em'), so it takes 'an': 'is an M.A.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word. There are so many “flies” on the food.
options: To move from one place to another
To hover up in the sky
questions.explanation: Here 'flies' is the plural noun, the winged insects, not the verb 'to fly'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A person who eats too much
questions.explanation: A glutton is a person who eats too much. A sycophant flatters, a fatalist accepts fate and a misogamist hates marriage.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'peculiar'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Personally, Ramesh was ____________ to his villagers than his elder brother.
questions.explanation: 'Than' calls for the comparative: 'more helpful'. 'Helpfuller' is not standard.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks. Kiara was born in India but she went to ______ university in ________ United Kingdom.
questions.explanation: 'University' begins with a 'yoo' sound, so 'a university'; a country name with 'Kingdom' takes 'the': 'the United Kingdom'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word ‘Plain’ from the given sentence. Mr. Das believes and follows the principle of simple living and high thinking.
questions.explanation: 'Simple living' is plain living, without luxury: 'simple' means 'plain'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Inanimate
questions.explanation: 'Inanimate' means not alive: 'lifeless'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. As technology evolves, consumers increasingly _______________________ products with enhanced features and greater efficiency.
questions.explanation: A general, ongoing truth alongside the present 'evolves' takes the simple present, and the plural 'consumers' takes 'demand'.

questions.text: The given sentence is divided into four segments. Select the option that has the segment with a grammatical error. She forbade / him not / to enter that / room.
questions.explanation: 'Forbid' already carries the negative, so 'not' is wrong: 'She forbade him to enter that room.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. The gift of the gab
options: The ability to speak easily and confidently
questions.explanation: 'The gift of the gab' is the ability to speak easily and confidently.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The comedian's jokes were so funny that the audience was “laughing uncontrollably”.
questions.explanation: To be 'in stitches' is to laugh uncontrollably.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as one-word substitute for the given group of words. One who performs daring gymnastic feats
questions.explanation: An acrobat performs daring gymnastic feats. An Adonis is a very handsome young man.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The standard of living of any country means the average (1)________ share of the goods and services which the country produces. A country’s standard of living, therefore, (2)________ first and foremost on its capacity to produce wealth. ‘Wealth’, in this sense, is not money, for we do not live (3)________ money but on things that money (4)________ buy; ‘goods’ such as food and clothing and ‘services’ such as transport and entertainment. A country’s capacity to produce wealth depends upon many factors, most of which have an effect on one another. Wealth depends to a great extent (5)________ a country’s natural resources, such as coal, gold and other minerals, water supply and so on.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.explanation: 'The average person's share': the singular possessive, one typical person's share of what the country produces.

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The standard of living of any country means the average (1)________ share of the goods and services which the country produces. A country’s standard of living, therefore, (2)________ first and foremost on its capacity to produce wealth. ‘Wealth’, in this sense, is not money, for we do not live (3)________ money but on things that money (4)________ buy; ‘goods’ such as food and clothing and ‘services’ such as transport and entertainment.
