markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: How much sugar at ₹68/kg should be added to 20 kg of tea worth ₹440/kg so that the mixture be worth ₹130/kg?
questions.explanation: By alligation, sugar : tea = (440 − 130) : (130 − 68) = 310 : 62 = 5 : 1, so 5 × 20 = 100 kg of sugar.

questions.text: A shopkeeper buys two varieties of sugar at ₹120 and ₹80 per kg, respectively, and mixes them in the ratio 2 : 3. He then sets the marked price of each kg of the blended sugar at 50% above the cost he incurred per kg of the same, and then sold it after offering a 25% discount on the marked price. At what price (in ₹) did the shopkeeper sell each kg of the blended sugar?
questions.explanation: Cost per kg of the blend = (2 × 120 + 3 × 80)/5 = ₹96. Marked price = 1.5 × 96 = ₹144, and after 25% off: 0.75 × 144 = ₹108.

questions.text: What sum (in ₹) will earn a simple interest of ₹240 in 3 years at 16% per year rate of interest?
Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3000 as a sum borrowed at 9% per year rate of interest for 2 years.
The average weight of a family of five members (in kg) whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 69 kg and 37 kg is:
Find the selling price of an article (in ₹) if the cost price is ₹4,500 and gain is 5%.

Akash, Ajay, Sonia, Anju and Rohit are in a group. The average marks scored by their group is 27. Akash left the group and now the average of the remaining students is 24. How many marks did Akash score?
questions.explanation: The five scored 5 × 27 = 135 in all and the other four 4 × 24 = 96, so Akash scored 135 − 96 = 39.

questions.text: The average age of a family consisting of parents and a child five years ago was 27 years. Three years ago, the average age of parents was 41. The child was born ______ years ago.
questions.explanation: Five years ago the three totalled 3 × 27 = 81 years, so 81 + 15 = 96 now. The parents totalled 2 × 41 = 82 three years ago, so 88 now. The child is 96 − 88 = 8: born 8 years ago.

questions.text: Find the simple interest on ₹36,000 at an annual rate of 22% over an 8 month period.

The average weight of a family of 8 members is 56 kg. The grandfather and the grandmother came to visit the family. Now, the average weight of 10 members of the family is 64 kg. Find the average weight (in kg) of the grandparents.
questions.explanation: The 10 weigh 10 × 64 = 640 kg and the 8 weigh 8 × 56 = 448 kg, so the grandparents weigh 192 kg together: 96 kg on average.

questions.text: Two numbers are in the ratio 3 : 7. Their L.C.M. is 126. Find the sum of the numbers.
questions.explanation: The numbers are 3k and 7k, whose LCM is 21k = 126, so k = 6. The numbers are 18 and 42, and their sum is 60.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘RISK’ is coded as ‘2369’ and ‘CRAP’ is coded as ‘1876’. What is the code for ‘R’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: R is the only letter in both words and 6 the only digit in both codes, so R = 6.

questions.text: KQNT is related to QWTZ in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, IOLR is related to OURX. To which of the following is DJGM related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 6 places forward: K → Q, Q → W, N → T, T → Z and I → O, O → U, L → R, R → X. So D → J, J → P, G → M, M → S: JPMS.

questions.text: Seven people A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). G is sitting second to the right of B. Only two people are sitting between E and C when counted from the left of E. G is an immediate neighbour of E. A is sitting second to the left of C. D is not an immediate neighbour of B. What is the position of F with respect to G?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, a person's right runs anticlockwise. G is second to B's right; E must sit between them (on G's other side, C would land on B's seat), then C is third to E's left, A second to C's left, and D, not beside B, sits between A and C. Going right from B: B, E, G, A, D, C, F, so F is third to G's left.

questions.text: What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 60 + 9 ÷ 63 − 72 × 12 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 60 − 9 × 63 + 72 ÷ 12 = 60 − 567 + 6 = −501.

questions.text: Two statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: I. All strawberries are fruits. II. Some berries are strawberries. Conclusions: I. All berries are fruits. II. Some fruits are strawberries. III. No berry is a fruit.
options: Both conclusions II and III follow.
Either conclusion I or III follows.
questions.explanation: All strawberries are fruits, so some fruits are strawberries (II). The berries that are strawberries are fruits, so III is false; I need not be true, as the other berries may not be fruits.

questions.text: EO 19 is related to AK 13 in a certain way. In the same way, UD 17 is related to QZ 11. To which of the following is VH 23 related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 4 places back (D wraps round to Z) and the number falls by 6: EO 19 → AK 13 and UD 17 → QZ 11. So VH 23 → RD 17.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 8796, 4392, 1092, 176, ?, −4.4

Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (6, 17, 41) (3, 20, 32)
questions.explanation: In each set, 4 × first + second = third: 4 × 6 + 17 = 41 and 4 × 3 + 20 = 32. Likewise 4 × 23 + 4 = 96.

questions.text: What should come in place of question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? ZWT, WUQ, TSN, QQK, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move back 3 (Z, W, T, Q, so N), second letters back 2 (W, U, S, Q, so O) and third letters back 3 (T, Q, N, K, so H): NOH.

questions.text: This question has two statements followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the given statements. Statements: No motor is a yak. Some yaks are wipes. Conclusions: (I) No wipe is a yak. (II) Some wipes are yaks.
questions.explanation: 'Some yaks are wipes' converts to 'some wipes are yaks' (II), which flatly contradicts I. The first statement says nothing about wipes.

questions.text: Seven people P, Q, R, S, T, U and V are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). U is sitting second to the right of S. Q is sitting third to the left of U. R is sitting fifth to the right of P. T is sitting third to the left of V. What is the position of S with respect to V?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, a person's right runs anticlockwise. U is second to S's right and Q third to U's left; R fifth to P's right and T third to V's left then fit only one way. Going right from S: S, T, U, R, V, P, Q. From V to the right come P, Q and then S: third to the right.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘FOAM’ is coded as ‘9618’ and ‘MUST’ is coded as ‘4536’. What is the code for ‘M’ in that language?
questions.explanation: M is the only letter in both words and 6 the only digit in both codes, so M = 6.

questions.text: Which of the following interchanges of signs would make the given equation correct? 8 − 42 + 104 ÷ 13 × 4 = 18

425 is related to 85 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 265 is related to 53. To which of the following is 655 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding / subtracting / multiplying, etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each number is five times the one it is related to: 425 ÷ 5 = 85 and 265 ÷ 5 = 53. Likewise 655 ÷ 5 = 131.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘PINK’ is coded as 15 and ‘PAINT’ is coded as 24. How will ‘WILDNESS’ be coded in the same language?
questions.explanation: The code is the square of the number of letters, less 1: PINK has 4 (4² − 1 = 15) and PAINT 5 (5² − 1 = 24). WILDNESS has 8: 8² − 1 = 63.

questions.text: In a Parliamentary system, who among the following is known as the head of the Government?
questions.explanation: In a parliamentary system the Prime Minister heads the government; the President (or monarch) is the head of state.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In the year 1946, a three-tiered confederation for transfer of power to India was proposed by the ________.
questions.explanation: The Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946 proposed a three-tier structure: a Union at the top, groups of provinces, and the provinces.

questions.text: Which of the following features of the Indian Constitution is taken from the USA's constitution?
questions.explanation: The removal of Supreme Court and High Court judges, like judicial review and the Fundamental Rights, comes from the US Constitution. Parliamentary privileges, the cabinet system and prerogative writs come from Britain.

questions.text: Pellagra is a deficiency disease that usually occurs due to lack of which of the following nutrients?
questions.explanation: Pellagra is caused by a lack of niacin (vitamin B3); it shows as dermatitis, diarrhoea and dementia.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT related to Macaulay?
options: He strongly advocated giving English language education to Indians.
He considered Indian and Arab literature inferior to the Western literature.
He believed that India is an uncivilised country which needs to be taught the lessons of civilisation.
questions.explanation: Macaulay was an Anglicist, not an Orientalist: his Minute on Indian Education (1835) dismissed Indian and Arabic learning and argued for teaching Indians in English.

questions.text: When was the National Digital Communications Policy launched in India?
questions.explanation: The National Digital Communications Policy, approved by the Union Cabinet in September 2018, replaced the National Telecom Policy of 2012.

questions.text: Pakhu Itu dance is performed by the Apatani tribe of which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Pakhu Itu is a traditional dance of the Apatani people of the Ziro valley, Arunachal Pradesh.

questions.text: Pandit Shiv Kumar Sharma is credited with single-handedly popularising which musical instrument?
questions.explanation: Pandit Shivkumar Sharma made the santoor, a Kashmiri folk instrument, a concert instrument of Hindustani classical music.

questions.text: The layer made up of unconsolidated rock, dust, soil, etc. that is deposited on a bed rock surface like a blanket is known as:
questions.explanation: Regolith is the blanket of loose, unconsolidated material (broken rock, dust and soil) that covers solid bedrock.

questions.text: According to Census 2011 of India, what was the percentage of Christian communities of the total population in India?
questions.explanation: Census 2011 counted about 2.78 crore Christians, 2.3% of India's population.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: What monumental site in India houses Magan Niwas, Hriday Kunj and Vinoba-Mira Kutir?
questions.explanation: Hriday Kunj (Gandhi's own cottage), Magan Niwas and Vinoba-Mira Kutir all stand in the Sabarmati Ashram, Ahmedabad.

questions.text: Which of the following places in India receive the highest rainfall?
questions.explanation: Mawsynram in Meghalaya, on the southern slopes of the Khasi Hills, receives the highest average rainfall in India.

questions.text: Who among the following rulers introduced the ‘jharokha darshan’ in the Mughal dynasty?
questions.explanation: Akbar began jharokha darshan, appearing to his subjects at a palace balcony every morning; Aurangzeb discontinued it.

questions.text: The duration of bouts in each round of the International Boxing Association (AIBA Open Boxing) match for Elite and Youth Men’s and Women’s Competitions should be __________.
questions.explanation: Under AIBA's competition rules, Elite and Youth bouts for men and women are three rounds of three minutes each, with one minute's rest between rounds.

questions.text: India played its first test match cricket against which of the following countries?
questions.explanation: India played its first Test match against England at Lord's in June 1932.

questions.text: In which of the following states is the Alpasi Festival celebrated annually, where a holy bath of the deities in the sea is the primary attraction?
questions.explanation: The Alpashi festival of the Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple, Thiruvananthapuram, ends with the Aarattu, when the deities are taken in procession for a holy bath in the sea at Shanghumukham beach.

questions.text: Who is a famous Kuchipudi Dancer to receive Padma Shri in 2001?
questions.explanation: Sobha Naidu, a Kuchipudi dancer and disciple of Vempati Chinna Satyam, received the Padma Shri in 2001.

questions.text: In December 2022, the Parliament passed the Energy Conservation (Amendment) Bill, 2022. This bill aims to make use of _____.
questions.explanation: The Energy Conservation (Amendment) Act, 2022 lets the government require designated consumers to meet part of their energy needs from non-fossil sources, and provides for a carbon credit trading scheme.

questions.text: In which year did the Government of India pass the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act?
questions.explanation: The National Rural Employment Guarantee Act was passed in 2005; it was renamed after Mahatma Gandhi in 2009.

questions.text: Find the odd one out. Vacuoles, Nucleus, Ribosomes, Lysosomes
questions.explanation: Ribosomes have no membrane; vacuoles, the nucleus and lysosomes are membrane-bound.

questions.text: What is the main objective of zero-based budgeting?
options: Examining the objectives for which funds are provided
Re-evaluation of all the activities every year when budget provisions are made
Establishing a relationship between inputs and outputs
To assess the effectiveness of each programme and activity with the output
questions.explanation: Zero-based budgeting starts each year's budget from zero, so every activity must be re-evaluated and justified afresh rather than carried over.

questions.text: What is the maximum amount of home loan the eligible beneficiaries can get under the ‘Mo Ghara’ scheme launched by the Government of Odisha in May 2023?
questions.explanation: Odisha's Mo Ghara rural housing scheme, approved in May 2023, offers eligible households home loans in slabs of ₹1 lakh, ₹1.5 lakh, ₹2 lakh and ₹3 lakh, repayable over 10 years.

questions.text: The famous autobiography ‘Lessons life taught me unknowingly’ is related to:
questions.explanation: 'Lessons Life Taught Me Unknowingly' is the autobiography of the actor Anupam Kher.

questions.text: Which property of an element is inversely related to its ionisation energy?
questions.explanation: The larger an atom's radius, the farther its outer electrons are from the nucleus and the more loosely they are held, so the less energy it takes to remove one.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. His skills in programming / are more superior than / most developers / in the company.
questions.explanation: 'Superior' is already comparative and takes 'to': 'are superior to', not 'are more superior than'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. Suman will be fired “if she did not complete the delegated target” set by her boss.
options: if she had not complete the delegated target
if she does not complete the delegated target
if she do not complete the delegated target
questions.explanation: A first conditional pairs 'will' in the main clause with the simple present in the 'if' clause: 'will be fired if she does not complete'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. Mithya's remarkable “generosity” extended to everyone she knew.
questions.explanation: 'Generosity' is readiness to give to others; its opposite is 'selfishness'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. I cannot call him directly as I “have lost his support”.
options: am out of favour with him
am quite at sea with him
questions.explanation: To be 'out of favour with' someone is to have lost their approval or support.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. (1) Malini’s family (2) doesn’t know (3) how she bears out (4) the work pressure.
questions.explanation: 'Bear out' means to confirm a claim; coping with something is 'bearing' it or 'bearing up' under it: 'how she bears the work pressure'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Vacant
questions.explanation: 'Vacant' means unoccupied: 'empty'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option with the correct usage of the preposition to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) “was born during 16 November 1945”.
questions.explanation: Dates take 'on': 'was born on 16 November 1945'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Sycophant
questions.explanation: A sycophant flatters the powerful to win favour: a 'fawner'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word 'Flash' from the given sentence. My cousin Zara, who loves to explore outer space in her free time, once noticed or observed a disc-shaped object blinking in the sky.
questions.explanation: To 'flash' is to shine on and off briefly, as a light does when 'blinking'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical/spelling error. Jack along with / his family visited / his aunt living / at America.
questions.explanation: Countries take 'in', not 'at': 'living in America'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks. ____ architect designed ____ modern office building and ____ traditional residential home, showcasing ____ blend of contemporary and classic architectural styles.
questions.explanation: 'An' goes before the vowel sound of 'architect'; 'modern', 'traditional' and 'blend' begin with consonant sounds, so they take 'a'.

questions.text: Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the following sentence and select its correct spelling from the given options. The teacher assessed the student’s flyer for writing.
questions.explanation: A natural talent is a 'flair'; a 'flyer' is a leaflet, or something that flies.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A short stay at a place.
questions.explanation: A sojourn is a temporary stay. An embargo is a trade ban, a xenophobe fears foreigners and topiary is the art of clipping shrubs into shapes.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence. The restaurent's atmosphere was pleasant and inviting.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'restaurant's'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. A famous economist / says that / the government should do more / for create enough jobs.
questions.explanation: Purpose is expressed with the to-infinitive: 'to create enough jobs', not 'for create'.

questions.text: Select the correct spelling from the given options to fill in the blank. I hope you will excuse me for doing what is only my duty, although it may appear ________.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'impertinent' (rude, lacking proper respect).

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Fast
questions.explanation: 'Fast' means 'quick'; 'tardy' and 'languid' mean slow.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The Indian Government has launched the National Rural Livelihoods Mission, a _________ programme aimed at reducing rural poverty.
questions.explanation: A 'flagship' programme is a government's leading or most important one in its field.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Burn the midnight oil
options: To work late into the night
questions.explanation: To 'burn the midnight oil' is to work or study late into the night.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. One day we saw Kala Nag. The monsoons had burst with all their fury, and it had rained in the night. The earth, which had lain parched and dry under the withering heat of the summer sun, was teeming ____1___ life. In little pools, frogs croaked. The muddy ground was littered with ____2___ worms, centipedes and velvety lady-birds. Grass ____3____ begun to show and the banana leaves glistened bright and glossy green. The _____4___ had flooded Kala Nag’s hole. He sat in an open patch on the lawn. His shiny black hood glistened in the sunlight. He was big, almost six feet in _____5____ and rounded and fleshy, as my wrist. “Looks like a King Cobra. Let’s get him."

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'Teem with' means to be full of: the earth 'was teeming with life'.

In little pools, frogs croaked. The muddy ground was littered with ____2___ worms, centipedes and velvety lady-birds. Grass ____3____ begun to show and the banana leaves glistened bright and glossy green. The _____4___ had flooded Kala Nag’s hole. He sat in an open patch on the lawn. His shiny black hood glistened in the sunlight. He was big, almost six feet in _____5____ and rounded and fleshy, as my wrist. “Looks like a King Cobra. Let’s get him."

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: After the rain the ground was littered with 'crawling' worms, centipedes and lady-birds.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: For 8 innings, a cricketer has an average of 68 runs. In the ninth inning, he scores 220 runs. His average score increased by (rounded off to the nearest whole number):
questions.explanation: The total rises from 8 × 68 = 544 to 544 + 220 = 764, an average of 764/9 ≈ 84.89. The increase is 84.89 − 68 ≈ 17.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3000 as a sum borrowed at 9% per year rate of interest for 6 years.
Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2000 as a sum borrowed at 8% per year rate of interest for 2 years.
A dozen oranges cost ₹96, 2 dozen apples cost ₹240 and 4 pineapples costs ₹180. What is the average cost (in ₹) per piece?
questions.explanation: 12 oranges, 24 apples and 4 pineapples (40 pieces) cost 96 + 240 + 180 = ₹516, so the average is 516/40 = ₹12.9 a piece.

questions.text: A specific amount of money is loaned out at a simple interest rate, resulting in ₹15,000 in 2 years and ₹20,000 in 4 years. The rate percentage per annum is:
questions.explanation: The interest for years 3 and 4 is 20,000 − 15,000 = ₹5,000, or ₹2,500 a year. So the principal is 15,000 − 5,000 = ₹10,000 and the rate is 2,500/10,000 = 25%.

questions.text: A shopkeeper bought 10 dozen eggs at the rate of ₹5 per egg. 12 eggs broke in transit. He sold the remaining eggs at the rate of ₹6 per egg. Find his profit percentage.
questions.explanation: Cost: 120 × ₹5 = ₹600. The remaining 108 eggs sell for 108 × ₹6 = ₹648, a profit of ₹48: 48/600 = 8%.

questions.text: The speed of a boat in still water is 8 km/h, while it takes 2 hours for the boat to cover a distance of 20 km downstream. What is the speed (in km/h) of the stream?
questions.explanation: Downstream speed = 20/2 = 10 km/h, so the stream's speed is 10 − 8 = 2 km/h.

questions.text: A merchant gives 800 g instead of 1000 g to a customer. What is the merchant’s percentage profit?
questions.explanation: He gains 200 g on every 800 g he actually gives: 200/800 = 25%.

questions.text: A rectangular sheet of length 28 cm and breadth 16 cm is folded to meet the edges so that it is made into a cylindrical pipe in two possible ways – one along the length and the other along the breadth. The larger volume is how much percentage of smaller volume?
questions.explanation: If side a becomes the circumference and side b the height, r = a/(2π) and V = πr²b = a²b/(4π). The volumes are in the ratio 28² × 16 : 16² × 28 = 28 : 16, so the larger is 175% of the smaller.

questions.text: A train is moving in from north to south direction. It overtakes Raj and Madhur who are walking in the same direction at the rate of 2 km/h and 4 km/h in 9 sec and 10 sec, respectively. If the train is x metres long, find the value of x.
questions.explanation: With the train's speed v km/h, its length is the relative distance covered: (v − 2) × 5/18 × 9 = (v − 4) × 5/18 × 10, so 9v − 18 = 10v − 40 and v = 22. Then x = 20 × 5/18 × 9 = 50.

questions.text: The average weight of a family of five members (in kg) whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 65 kg and 37 kg is:

A solution of phenyl and water is 28 litres, with phenyl and water in ratio 4 : 3. 21 litres phenyl-water solution which has phenyl to water ratio as 2 : 1 is added to the 28 litres phenyl-water solution. Again 51 litres phenyl-water solution that has phenyl to water ratio as 9 : 8 is added to this. What is ratio of water to phenyl in the final mixture?
questions.explanation: Phenyl and water in the three lots are 16 and 12, 14 and 7, and 27 and 24 litres, so the final mixture has 57 litres of phenyl and 43 of water: water : phenyl = 43 : 57.

questions.text: The dimensions of a room are 1650 cm × 1350 cm × 900 cm. What should be the size of the longest tape with which the three dimensions can be measured exactly?
questions.explanation: The longest such tape is the HCF: 1650 = 2 × 3 × 5² × 11, 1350 = 2 × 3³ × 5² and 900 = 2² × 3² × 5², so the HCF is 2 × 3 × 5² = 150 cm.

questions.text: Each of the two merchants sell an article for ₹1,000. If Merchant A computes his profit on the cost price, while Merchant B computes his profit on the selling price, then they both end up making profits of 25%. By how much is the profit made by Merchant B more than that of Merchant A?
questions.explanation: A: 25% on cost means cost = 1,000/1.25 = ₹800 and a profit of ₹200. B: 25% of the selling price is ₹250. B makes ₹50 more.

questions.text: A conical tent is to accommodate 12 persons. Each person must have 5 m² of the space on the ground and 20 m³ of air to breathe. The height of the tent should be:
questions.explanation: The base must be 12 × 5 = 60 m² and the volume 12 × 20 = 240 m³. (1/3) × 60 × h = 240, so h = 12 m.

questions.text: The cost of a raw material increased with equal percentage in two years. The price increased to ₹145.20 from ₹120. What is the equal annual percentage increase?
questions.explanation: 145.20/120 = 1.21 = 1.1², so the price rose 10% each year.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? CVF, GTJ, KRN, ?, SNV
questions.explanation: First letters move +4 (C, G, K, O, S), second letters −2 (V, T, R, P, N) and third letters +4 (F, J, N, R, V): OPR.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 12 ÷ 2 × 6 – 11 + 12 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 12 × 2 ÷ 6 + 11 − 12 = 4 + 11 − 12 = 3.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'DEVICE' is coded as ‘EDWHDD’ and 'DENIAL' is coded as ‘EDOHBK’. How will 'DEMAND' be coded in the same language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +1 and −1 in turn: DEVICE → EDWHDD and DENIAL → EDOHBK. So DEMAND → E D N Z O C (A − 1 wraps round to Z): EDNZOC.

questions.text: 7 is related to 33 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 9 is related to 41. To which of the following is 14 related following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is 4 times the first plus 5: 4 × 7 + 5 = 33 and 4 × 9 + 5 = 41. So 4 × 14 + 5 = 61.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘×’ and ‘−‘ are interchanged and ‘+’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 16 – 66 + 6 × 26 ÷ 36 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 16 × 66 ÷ 6 − 26 + 36 = 176 − 26 + 36 = 186.

questions.text: In a code language, 'RAM' is written as ‘Q14’ and ‘CAR’ is written as ‘B19’. How will 'MARK' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The first letter moves back one and the number is the sum of the other letters' positions: RAM → Q, 1 + 13 = 14; CAR → B, 1 + 18 = 19. So MARK → L, 1 + 18 + 11 = 30: L30.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the given sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (29, 77) (24, 62)
questions.explanation: The second number is 3 times the first minus 10: 3 × 29 − 10 = 77 and 3 × 24 − 10 = 62. Likewise 3 × 19 − 10 = 47.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 1, 2, 5, 12, ?, 58, 121
questions.explanation: Each term is twice the one before plus 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 in turn: 12 × 2 + 3 = 27, then 27 × 2 + 4 = 58 and 58 × 2 + 5 = 121.

questions.text: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order) . Only two people sit between F and C when counted from the right of F. Only three people sit between B and G when counted from the right of G. C sits to the immediate right of G. D sits to the immediate right of A. Who sits fourth to the right of E?
questions.explanation: Number the seats by places to the right of G. C is 1 (immediately right of G), B is 4 (three people between) and F is 5 (C is third to F's right). A and D then take 2 and 3, with D immediately right of A, so E is 6. Fourth to the right of E is seat 3: D.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the statement(s). Statements: All sharks are whales. No whale is a dolphin. Conclusions: (I) No shark is a dolphin. (II) No dolphin is a whale.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: All sharks are whales and no whale is a dolphin, so no shark is a dolphin (I). 'No whale is a dolphin' also means no dolphin is a whale (II). Both follow.

questions.text: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing away from the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Only 3 people sit between D and F when counted from the right of D. E and G are both immediate neighbours of A. B sits immediately to the left of C. Only 1 person sits between B and G when counted from the right of G. What is the position of E with respect to B?
questions.explanation: Number the seats by places to the right of G. B is 2 (one person between) and C, immediately right of B, is 3. A sits next to G but not at 1, where its other neighbour would be B instead of E; so A is 6 and E is 5. D and F take 1 and 4 with F fourth to D's right: D is 4 and F is 1. E (5) is third to the right of B (2).

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘GIRL’ is coded as ‘3618’ and ‘ROAD’ is coded as ‘7462’.What is the code for ‘R’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: R is the only letter in both words and 6 the only digit in both codes, so R = 6.

questions.text: AB10 is related to CD29 in a certain way. In the same way, KL65 is related to MN84. To which of the following is UV25 related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Both letters move 2 places forward and the number rises by 19: AB10 → CD29 and KL65 → MN84. So UV25 → WX44.

questions.text: SK −1 is related to OO 3 in a certain way. In the same way, IA 2 is related to EE 6. To which of the following is EO 5 related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: The first letter moves back 4, the second forward 4 and the number rises by 4: SK −1 → OO 3 and IA 2 → EE 6. So EO 5 → AS 9.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘can you swim’ is coded as ‘MQ TO LO’ and ‘He can drive’ is coded as ‘LO AB PQ’. How is ‘can’ coded in that code language?
questions.explanation: 'can' is the only word in both sentences and 'LO' the only code in both, so can = LO.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some herbs are trees. Some trees are plants. Conclusions: (I) Some herbs are plants. (II) At least some trees are herbs.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusion I and II follow
questions.explanation: Herbs and plants are linked only through trees, by two 'some' statements, so I need not be true. 'Some herbs are trees' means some trees are herbs, so II follows.

questions.text: As of February 2024, who among the following is the Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha?
questions.explanation: Harivansh Narayan Singh has been Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha since 2018, re-elected in 2020.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECT statement.
options: The chromatin material gets organised into rod-shaped chromosomes only when the cell is about to divide.
Chromosomes are composed of DNA and carbohydrates.
DNA molecules contain the information necessary for constructing and organising cells.
Functional segments of DNA are called genes.
questions.explanation: Chromosomes are made of DNA and proteins, not carbohydrates; the other three statements are correct.

questions.text: Which Fundamental Right guarantees protection of interests of the minorities in the matter of their language, script or culture?
questions.explanation: Article 29, one of the Cultural and Educational Rights, protects any section of citizens with a distinct language, script or culture of its own.

questions.text: The Irani Cup is a first-class cricket competition played between the winner of the Ranji Trophy and which other team?
questions.explanation: The Irani Cup is played between the Ranji Trophy champions and a Rest of India team.

questions.text: Which of the following is the National waterway no. 4 in India?
options: Mahanadi and Brahmani rivers and East Coast Canal
Godavari and Krishna rivers along with Kakinada Puducherry
The Brahmaputra river between Sadiya and Dhubri
questions.explanation: National Waterway 4 covers the Godavari and Krishna rivers with the Kakinada-Puducherry canal stretch. NW-1 is the Ganga from Allahabad to Haldia, NW-2 the Brahmaputra from Sadiya to Dhubri and NW-5 the East Coast Canal with the Brahmani and Mahanadi.

questions.text: Vinod Mankara’s documentary 'Mohinyattathinte Amma' is based on which of the following world renowned Mohiniyattam dancers?
questions.explanation: The title means 'Mohiniyattam's mother': Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma, who did much to revive the dance, is known as the mother of Mohiniyattam.

questions.text: According to Newland’s Law of Octaves, every eighth element has properties similar to those of the first element. Which of the following elements has properties similar to those of N?
questions.explanation: Counting N as the first, the eighth element in Newlands' arrangement is P (N, O, F, Na, Mg, Al, Si, P); both are in group 15 today.

questions.text: Which state finished second in the first edition of the Khelo India Para Games?
questions.explanation: Haryana topped the first Khelo India Para Games (New Delhi, December 2023), with Uttar Pradesh second and Tamil Nadu third.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following was the founder of Indian Association in Bengal?
questions.explanation: Surendranath Banerjee founded the Indian Association in Calcutta in 1876, with Ananda Mohan Bose.

questions.text: Tax, known as bhaga, was levied on which of the following during Mahajanapada period of Ancient India?
questions.explanation: In the mahajanapadas the tax on crops, usually a sixth of the produce, was called bhaga, a share.

questions.text: A 5% decrease in poverty by 2007 was one of main objectives of the ________ plan.
questions.explanation: The Tenth Plan (2002-2007) aimed to cut the poverty ratio by 5 percentage points by 2007, and by 15 points by 2012.

questions.text: Identify the INCORRECT pair (State and Iron-ore producing region) from the following.
questions.explanation: Ratnagiri is in Maharashtra, not Madhya Pradesh. Badampahar (Odisha), Bailadila (Chhattisgarh) and Kudremukh (Karnataka) are iron-ore regions of those states.

questions.text: Usain Bolt shared the journey of his life in which of the following autobiographies?
questions.explanation: Usain Bolt's autobiography 'Faster than Lightning' was published in 2013.

questions.text: The Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque was constructed in around 1197 AD by the sultan of which of the following dynasties of Delhi Sultanate?
questions.explanation: Qutb-ud-din Aibak, founder of the Mamluk (Slave) dynasty, built the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque in Delhi in the 1190s.

questions.text: Select the odd one from the following saltwater lakes on the basis of their formation?
questions.explanation: NCERT lists Chilika, Pulicat and Kolleru as lagoons of the coastal areas; Sambhar in Rajasthan is a salt lake in a region of inland drainage, so it formed differently.

questions.text: In 2022, Arjun Singh Dhurve was honoured with the Padma Shri Award for his contribution in which of the following Indian folk-dance forms?
questions.explanation: Arjun Singh Dhurve of Madhya Pradesh received the Padma Shri in 2022 for the Baiga tribal dance.

questions.text: Who among the following was sent by Akbar to lead the Mughal army in the Battle of Haldighati which was fought in 1576?
questions.explanation: Raja Man Singh of Amber commanded Akbar's army against Maharana Pratap at Haldighati in 1576.

questions.text: In October 2023, Indrasena Reddy Nallu has been appointed the Governor of which of the following states in India?
questions.explanation: Indrasena Reddy Nallu became Governor of Tripura in October 2023.

questions.text: Which executive system is present in India?
questions.explanation: India has a parliamentary system: the President is the nominal head, and the Council of Ministers, led by the Prime Minister, is responsible to the Lok Sabha.

questions.text: If the tax rate increases with the taxable base, then this type of taxation is called:
questions.explanation: A progressive tax charges a higher rate as the taxable base grows; a proportional tax keeps one rate and a regressive tax's rate falls.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following launched the Home Rule League in September 1916 at Madras?
questions.explanation: Annie Besant launched her Home Rule League at Madras in September 1916; Tilak had started his at Belgaum in April 1916.

questions.text: ___________ is mainly celebrated by Maharashtrians as New Year's Day.
questions.explanation: Gudi Padwa, on the first day of Chaitra, is the Marathi New Year; Ugadi is the New Year of Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

questions.text: Krishnarao Shankar Pandit belonged to which of the following music gharanas?
questions.explanation: Krishnarao Shankar Pandit was a leading vocalist of the Gwalior gharana.

questions.text: According to the Census of India 2011, which states of India have population density more than 1000 persons per sq. km?
questions.explanation: By the 2011 Census only two states had more than 1,000 persons per sq. km: Bihar (1,106) and West Bengal (1,028).

questions.text: The microscopic channels, which traverse the cell walls of plant cells and some algal cells, enabling transport and communication between them is called:
questions.explanation: Plasmodesmata are fine channels through plant cell walls that link the cytoplasm of neighbouring cells; desmosomes are junctions between animal cells.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'. The keys were “lies on the table”.
questions.explanation: 'Were' needs the '-ing' form of 'lie' (to rest): 'The keys were lying on the table.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. He is habituated to using words spoken with an unusual amount of “venom” when it comes to his in-laws.
questions.explanation: 'Venom' here is spite or malice; its opposite is 'benevolence', goodwill.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The pencil has a tip made of _______.
questions.explanation: A pencil's tip is its 'lead' (in fact graphite); 'led', the past of the verb 'lead', only sounds the same.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The manager swiftly overtook him, ____________ effortlessly past the skinny Englishman, with a practiced ease.
questions.explanation: Overtaking swiftly and 'effortlessly' fits 'sliding' past him; 'dawdling' means moving slowly.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Gracious
questions.explanation: 'Gracious' means courteous and kind; its opposite is 'rude'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate verb form to fill in the blank in the given sentence. She ________ her keys on the kitchen counter.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'laid', the past tense of 'lay' (to put down), which takes an object: 'She laid her keys on the kitchen counter.' 'Lays' would also be grammatical for a habit; 'lying' and 'lain', forms of 'lie', would need a helping verb and take no object.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The brave and courageous soldiers / of our motherland / fell into the enemy / and won the battle.
questions.explanation: To attack the enemy is to 'fall upon' (or 'fall on') it; 'fall into' means to drop into something or into a state.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks. Whenever addressed, she comes ____ and performs her ____ in a great way.
questions.explanation: To 'come forth' is to come forward, and the part one plays is a 'role'; 'fourth' and 'roll' only sound the same.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. All in the same boat
options: When everyone is dealing with the same situation
When everybody is travelling in the same vehicle
When everyone has to start all over again
When a task can be accomplished together
questions.explanation: To be 'all in the same boat' is for everyone to be facing the same situation, usually a difficult one.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. jeopardy
questions.explanation: 'Jeopardy' means danger; its opposite is 'safety'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'entertainment'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The success and achievements of a school mostly _________ on its experience and resourcefulness.
questions.explanation: Success 'depends on' something; the plural subject 'success and achievements' takes 'depend'.

questions.text: Select the option that rectifies the spelling error in the following sentence. The poet was able to compose the long poem in a tranquill atmosphere.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'tranquil'.

questions.text: Based on the situation in the given sentence, select the most appropriate idiom for the underlined segment. There are several people who find themselves “a dominating person in a group”
questions.explanation: The 'cock of the walk' is someone who dominates a group.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Manish has being applying / for colleges / ever since he passed / his entrance test in March.
questions.explanation: The present perfect continuous is 'has been applying', not 'has being applying'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate degree of comparison to fill in the blank. The underground railway network, ‘The Tube’ in London is said to be __________ transport in London.
questions.explanation: Compared with all the transport in London, the Tube needs the superlative: 'the most expensive'.

questions.text: Select the option with the correct spelling to replace the underlined word in the given sentence. Self-esteem is an important “aspekt” of one's self.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'aspect'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined phrase. Jared “deliberately set fire to a property” and got arrested by the police.
questions.explanation: Arson is the crime of deliberately setting fire to property. Dystrophy is the wasting away of a body part, dementia a loss of memory and reasoning, and insomnia an inability to sleep.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. He will be / waiting for me when / I reaches his home.
questions.explanation: The subject 'I' takes 'reach', not 'reaches': 'when I reach his home'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The new/ smartphone is/absolutely best than/ the latest model.
questions.explanation: 'Than' needs the comparative: 'better than', not 'best than'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. He knew everyone on the island. Whenever his car stopped, half a dozen voices ____ 1 _____ shout out his name. Policemen, agricultural labourers of low social status and priests waved and smiled ____ 2 ____ he passed; everyone greeted him as a brother. Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'Would' describes something that happened again and again in the past: whenever his car stopped, voices 'would shout out' his name.

questions.text: A thief saw a policeman and he started running at a speed of 12 m/s. After a certain time, the policeman starts running behind the thief at a speed of 18 m/s. If the policeman covered a 540 m distance to catch the thief, the time (in seconds) after which the policeman started running is:
questions.explanation: The policeman ran 540 m in 540 ÷ 18 = 30 seconds, in which the thief ran 12 × 30 = 360 m. The thief's start of 540 − 360 = 180 m took him 180 ÷ 12 = 15 seconds.

questions.text: A flat worth ₹9,50,000 is sold by Lakshman to Bharath at 8% profit. If Bharath sells it back to Lakshman at 3% loss, then find the gain/loss (in ₹) of Lakshman in the entire transaction?
Find the HCF of 70 and 90.
questions.explanation: 70 = 2 × 5 × 7 and 90 = 2 × 3² × 5; the common factors give 2 × 5 = 10.

questions.text: The average of the first six multiples of 7 is:
questions.explanation: The multiples 7, 14, …, 42 are evenly spaced, so their average is (7 + 42)/2 = 24.5.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3000 as a sum borrowed at 3% per year rate of interest for 4 years.
A man riding his bicycle covers 75 metres in 12.5 seconds. What is his speed (in km/hr)?
The average weight of a family of five members (in kg) whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 70 kg and 39 kg is:
The area of a rectangular field is 396 m², whose sides are in the ratio of 11 : 9. What is The perimeter of the rectangular field?
questions.explanation: With sides 11x and 9x, 99x² = 396, so x = 2 and the sides are 22 m and 18 m. Perimeter = 2 × (22 + 18) = 80 m.

questions.text: There is a 21 litres mixture of milk and water. The ratio of milk and water in the mixture is 4 : 3. Find the amount of water (in litres) that should be added to this mixture so that the resulting mixture has 50% of water in it.
questions.explanation: The mixture holds 12 litres of milk and 9 of water. For 50% water the water must equal the milk, 12 litres, so 3 litres must be added.

questions.text: The price of a computer increases by 10% in the first year, decreases by 5% in the second year, and increases by 8% in the third year. If the original price was ₹50,000, then the final price (in₹) is:

A hemispherical bowl of internal radius 15 cm contains a liquid. The liquid is to be filled into cylindrical shaped bottles of diameter 5 cm and height 6 cm. The number of bottles required to empty the bowl is:
questions.explanation: Bowl: (2/3)π × 15³ = 2,250π cm³. Bottle: π × 2.5² × 6 = 37.5π cm³. 2,250π ÷ 37.5π = 60 bottles.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2500 as a sum borrowed at 3% per year rate of interest for 6 years.
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 7 12 16 30 34 66 70 ?
questions.explanation: The steps alternate ×2 − 2 and +4: 7 → 12 → 16 → 30 → 34 → 66 → 70. The next is 70 × 2 − 2 = 138.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘WORD’ is coded as ‘7135’ and ‘RISE’ is coded as ‘4658’. What is the code for ‘R’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: R is the only letter in both words and 5 the only digit in both codes, so R = 5.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? BXL, DVN, FTP, ?, JPT
questions.explanation: First letters move +2 (B, D, F, H, J), second letters −2 (X, V, T, R, P) and third letters +2 (L, N, P, R, T): HRR.

questions.text: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Only 3 people are sitting between E and A when counted from the right of E. B is sitting 2nd to the left of A. G is sitting to the immediate left of F. Only 2 people are sitting between B and G when counted from the right of B. C is the immediate neighbour of E. What is the position of D with respect to E?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, a person's right is anticlockwise. Going right from E the order is E, C, B, D, A, G, F: A is 4th to the right of E, B is 2nd to the left of A, G is 3rd to the right of B with F on G's right, and C is E's other neighbour. D is 3rd to the right of E.

questions.text: EF26 is related to JK33 in a certain way. In the same way, TU27 is related to YZ34. To which of the following is JK28 related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Both letters move 5 places forward and the number rises by 7: E, F → J, K and 26 → 33. So J, K → O, P and 28 → 35: OP35.

questions.text: Which two numbers should be interchanged to make the following equation correct? (28 × 2) −16 × 6 + 8 × 3 + 5 × 7 = 39 (Note: Interchange should be done of the entire number and not individual digits of a given number.)

Read the given statement(s) and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statement(s) is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement(s). Statements: All pumpkin is mutton. All mutton are fishes. Conclusions: (I) Some fishes are mutton. (II) All pumpkins are fishes.
questions.explanation: All pumpkins are mutton and all mutton are fishes, so all pumpkins are fishes (II); and as all mutton are fishes, some fishes are mutton (I). Both follow.

questions.text: 3 is related to 15 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 12 is related to 60. To which of the following is 5 related to, following the same logic? (Note: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 - Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each number is multiplied by 5: 3 × 5 = 15 and 12 × 5 = 60. So 5 × 5 = 25.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘BENT’ is coded as ‘4628’ and ‘EARS’ is coded as ‘5471’.What is the code for ‘E’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: E is the only letter in both words and 4 the only digit in both codes, so E = 4.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘I play football’ is coded as ‘ku ch ta’ and ‘he play cricket’ is coded as ‘al bi ta’. How is ‘play’ coded in the given language?
questions.explanation: 'play' is the only word in both sentences and 'ta' the only code in both, so play = ta.

questions.text: Seven people S, E, C, T, I, O and N are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre(but not necessarily in the same order). E is sitting second to the left of N, while N is sitting second to the left of S. Only one person is sitting between S and O when counted from the right of S. C is sitting to the immediate right of E, whereas T is sitting to the immediate left of O. Who is sitting to the immediate right of I?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, a person's right is anticlockwise. Going right from S the order is S, T, O, E, C, N, I: N is 2nd to the left of S and E 2nd to the left of N, O is 2nd to the right of S with T on its left, C is on E's right and I takes the last seat. To I's right sits S.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘×’ and ‘ ÷ ‘ are interchanged and ‘–’ and ‘+’ are interchanged? 23 ÷ 18 + 150 × 50 – 44 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 23 × 18 − 150 ÷ 50 + 44 = 414 − 3 + 44 = 455.

questions.text: 14 is related to 68 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 17 is related to 83. To which of the following is 21 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each number is multiplied by 5 and 2 subtracted: 14 × 5 − 2 = 68 and 17 × 5 − 2 = 83. So 21 × 5 − 2 = 103.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some plants are rocks. No vegetable is a plant. Conclusions: I) No vegetable is a rock (II) Some rocks are plants.
questions.explanation: Some plants are rocks, so some rocks are plants (II). No vegetable is a plant, but vegetables may still be rocks that are not plants, so I does not follow.

questions.text: JT79 is related to DN71 in a certain way. In the same way, KU22 is related to EO14. To which of the following is LV71 related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Both letters move 6 places back and the number falls by 8: J, T → D, N and 79 → 71. So L, V → F, P and 71 → 63: FP63.

questions.text: The liquid water present in oceans, lakes and rivers gets converted to the gaseous form in the presence of sunlight in the water cycle. This step is called:
questions.explanation: Evaporation turns liquid water into water vapour with the sun's heat; condensation and precipitation follow later in the cycle.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about nutrients are correct? Statement A: C, H, O, N, P and K are macro nutrients. Statement B: Fe, Mn, Ni, Co and Mo are micronutrients. Statement C: Micronutrients are not essential for our body.
options: All statements A, B and C
questions.explanation: Micronutrients are needed only in small amounts but are essential all the same, so statement C is false. A names elements needed in large amounts and B ones needed in traces.

questions.text: What is the usual treatment on repo rates by the Reserve Bank of India in case of a hawkish monetary policy stance?
options: Reduced sharply by more than 100 bps
questions.explanation: A hawkish stance puts controlling inflation first, so the RBI tends to raise the repo rate, making borrowing dearer.

questions.text: Who is revered as ‘Karnataka Sangeeta Pitamaha’?
questions.explanation: Purandara Dasa, the 16th-century composer who laid down the graded lessons still used to teach Carnatic music, is revered as its 'pitamaha'.

questions.text: In cycling, what is a 'peloton'?
options: A cycling technique for climbing hills
The finish line of a race
The starting line of a race
A group of riders in a tight pack during a race
questions.explanation: The peloton is the main bunch of riders in a road race, who ride close together to save energy in each other's slipstream.

questions.text: As per Census of India 2011, which of the following states has the highest percentage of Hindu population in India?
questions.explanation: Census 2011 counted Hindus as about 95% of Himachal Pradesh's population, the highest share of any state.

questions.text: Which of the following articles of the Constitution of India mentions that every Minister and the Attorney-General of India shall have the right to speak in and participate in the proceedings of either House of Parliament?
questions.explanation: Article 88 gives every Minister and the Attorney-General the right to speak in, and take part in the proceedings of, either House, but not to vote.

questions.text: Below are two chemical equations: Zn (s) + CuSO₄ (aq) → ZnSO₄ (aq) + Cu (s); Pb (s) + CuCl₂ (aq) → PbCl₂ (aq) + Cu (s) Why does copper get separated from its compound form in both the cases?
options: Copper compounds break down under high pressure.
Copper is more reactive than Zinc and Lead.
Zinc and Lead are unstable in element form.
Zinc and Lead are more reactive than Copper.
questions.explanation: These are displacement reactions: a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive one from its salt, and zinc and lead stand above copper in the reactivity series.

questions.text: Who among the following is/was a famous proponent of Bharatanatyam?
questions.explanation: Rukmini Devi Arundale did much to revive Bharatanatyam and founded Kalakshetra in Madras in 1936.

questions.text: As of July 2023, 137 unique products under 'One District, One Product' scheme has been notified from how many districts?
questions.explanation: Under the PM Formalisation of Micro food processing Enterprises (PMFME) scheme, the Ministry of Food Processing Industries approved One District One Product for 713 districts, covering 137 unique products.

questions.text: What is the height of the Kanchenjunga peak of Himalaya?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 8,598 m, the height in NCERT's Class 9 table of Himalayan peaks; the figure most widely cited today is 8,586 m. None of the other options is close to either.

questions.text: Who among the following was India's first cricket team captain?
questions.explanation: C K Nayudu captained India in its first Test match, against England at Lord's in 1932.

questions.text: Swachh Bharat Mission was launched on the birth anniversary of which of the following freedom fighters?
questions.explanation: The Swachh Bharat Mission was launched on 2 October 2014, Mahatma Gandhi's birth anniversary.

questions.text: Who were the first foreign rulers of northwest India in the post-Mauryan period?
questions.explanation: After the Mauryas, the Greeks who ruled Bactria were the first to cross the Hindu Kush and rule north-west India, before the Sakas, Parthians and Kushanas.

questions.text: Bharatanatyam Guru ________ received the Nrithya Seva Ratna award from Indian Fine Arts Akademi, San Diego in 2023.
questions.explanation: Hema Rajagopalan, the Chicago-based Bharatanatyam guru who founded Natya Dance Theatre, received the Nrithya Seva Ratna from the Indian Fine Arts Academy, San Diego, on 1 April 2023.

questions.text: As of 2023, what is the number of major public seaports in India?
questions.explanation: In 2023 India had 12 major ports, under the Union Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways; the others are non-major ports under the state governments.

questions.text: Which of the following cell organelles possesses their own DNA and can synthesise protein for their functions?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts, like mitochondria, have their own DNA and ribosomes and make some of their own proteins.

questions.text: Which author wrote the Hindi novel 'Tamas'?
questions.explanation: 'Tamas', set during the riots of Partition, is by Bhisham Sahni; it won the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1975.

questions.text: 'Promotion of educational and economic interests of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and other weaker sections' comes under which Article of Indian constitution?
questions.explanation: Article 46, a Directive Principle, asks the State to promote the educational and economic interests of the weaker sections, especially the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

questions.text: The training academy for Indian Police Service officers has been named after:
questions.explanation: IPS officers are trained at the Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel National Police Academy in Hyderabad.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which social reformer from South India founded the Self Respect Movement?
questions.explanation: E V Ramasamy, 'Periyar', started the Self-Respect Movement in Tamil Nadu in 1925.

questions.text: In the Great Stupa at Sanchi there are ________ gateways known as ‘Toranas’ at the cardinal points to the compass.
questions.explanation: The Great Stupa has four toranas, one at each cardinal point: north, south, east and west.

questions.text: In which of the following years was the Census Act enacted and extended to the whole of India?
questions.explanation: The Census Act, 1948 provides for taking the census and extends to the whole of India.

questions.text: The campaign 'Ek Tareekh, Ek Ghanta, Ek Sath' is associated with which occasion?
questions.explanation: 'Ek Tareekh, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath' was an hour of nationwide cleaning on 1 October 2023, a tribute to Mahatma Gandhi on the eve of Gandhi Jayanti.

questions.text: Who among the following has written ‘Gita Govinda’, a Sanskrit epic?
questions.explanation: The 'Gita Govinda', on Krishna and Radha, was written by Jayadeva in the 12th century.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Bulging
questions.explanation: 'Bulging' means swelling outwards; its opposite is 'contracting'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Never ________ ever seen a more disgusting sight.
questions.explanation: When a sentence opens with the negative 'never', the auxiliary comes before the subject: 'Never have I ever seen ...'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Roger applied the __________ in advance as he anticipated an accident.
questions.explanation: A vehicle is slowed with its 'brake'; 'break' sounds the same but means something else.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Blend
questions.explanation: To 'blend' is to 'mix'.

questions.text: The sentence below contains errors. Select the option with the correct use of tenses. Your father will waiting for you when you reach home.
options: Your father would waiting for you when you reach home.
Your father waiting for you when you reach home.
Your father will be waiting for you when you reach home.
Your father should waiting for you when you reach home.
questions.explanation: An action that will be in progress at a future time takes the future continuous: 'will be waiting'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. She was barking up the wrong _______ when she filed a complaint against ragging with the students' union instead of the university administration.
questions.explanation: To 'bark up the wrong tree' is to look for something, or complain, in the wrong place.

questions.text: In the following sentence the underlined part contains as error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative. The sky appeared to be “greyest” after the storm.
questions.explanation: Nothing is being compared, so the positive degree: 'appeared to be grey after the storm'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Living within our environmental limits is one of the central _________________ of sustainable development.
questions.explanation: Living within environmental limits is one of the central 'principles', the basic ideas, of sustainable development. 'Illuminates' and 'demonstrates' are verbs.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'spectacular'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom/phrase to fill in the blank. My car _______ on the way to college yesterday.
questions.explanation: A car that 'breaks down' stops working. To 'break out' is to start suddenly, to 'break in' to enter by force and to 'break up' to come to an end.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Good nutrition is the “bedrock at child survival”, health and development.
questions.explanation: 'Bedrock' takes 'of': 'the bedrock of child survival'.

questions.text: Select the appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the following sentence to make it grammatically correct. This almirah is made up of “heavier” metal.
questions.explanation: Nothing is being compared, so the positive degree: 'made up of heavy metal'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains anerror in phrasal verb. Tara was late for the meeting / but somehow managed / to catch out with / everything she had missed.
options: Tara was late for the meeting
questions.explanation: To make up for what one has missed is to 'catch up with' it; to 'catch out' is to trap someone in a mistake.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word from the given options that can substitute the word ‘courage’ and make a meaningful sentence. I am not courage enough to take this risk.
questions.explanation: 'Am not ... enough' needs an adjective: 'I am not courageous enough to take this risk.'

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. “Monika said to her mother that, "I have passed” the examination."
options: Monika said to her mother, "I have passed
Monika said to her mother that, "I am passed
Monika said to her mother that, "she has passed
questions.explanation: Direct speech, the speaker's exact words in quotation marks, is not introduced with 'that'; 'that' belongs to reported speech ('Monika told her mother that she had passed').

questions.text: In the following sentence the underlined part contains as error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative. Playing in the field, the young “gayer” students were laughing and giggling.
questions.explanation: Nothing is being compared, so the positive degree: 'the young gay students', 'gay' here meaning cheerful.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. I don't prefer to remain alone at home in the evenings because loneliness evokes a sense of “melancholy” and grief within me.
questions.explanation: 'Melancholy' is a deep sadness; its opposite is 'cheerfulness'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence. Uluru is the world's largest monolith and Australia's recognisable natural icon with an elliptical shape and a circumfarence of around 94 kilometers.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'circumference'. 'Kilometers' is the American spelling, not a mistake.

questions.text: In a mixture of 60 litres, milk and water are in the ratio 7 : 3. If 3 litres of water be added, find the ratio of milk and water in the new mixture.
questions.explanation: The mixture has 42 litres of milk and 18 of water. With 3 more litres of water it is 42 : 21 = 2 : 1.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3000 as a sum borrowed at 8% per year rate of interest for 5 years.

Three red lights on the same road start blinking at the same time and blink repeatedly after every 4, 6 and 8 minutes, respectively. How many times will they blink together in an interval of 3 hours, excluding blinking together at the starting moment?
questions.explanation: They blink together every LCM(4, 6, 8) = 24 minutes. 180 ÷ 24 = 7.5, so 7 times in 3 hours after the start.
